screen.project_title: SynPETic: a PETosome for enzymatic PET recycling in space
screen.what_they_built: Expressed and purified a dockerin-tagged PETase (ICCG-DoT), a dockerin-tagged MHET-hydrolysing esterase (TfCa-DoG) and a trimeric cohesin scaffold (ScafGVT) in E. coli, then measured APET film breakdown by HPLC. A clinostat for microgravity testing was designed but never achieved driven motion.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5-alpha and BL21; pET28a constructs pelB-ICCG-DoT, TfCa-DoG, TfCaWA-DoG (I69W/V376A) and pelB-ScafGVT. No BBa part IDs anywhere on the wiki; sequences appear only on a non-standard Composite Part page.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /model: a 16-row HPLC table of TPA, MHET and BHET at 24, 48, 72 and 96 h across four Dock+/- x Scaf+/- conditions on APET film, with model curves overlaid. Single series, no replicates or error bars, and the TPA standard curve was still outstanding so TPA values are flagged provisional.
screen.hp_integration: Partly: eight expert interviews (NASA operations, Equivalent System Mass, TRL, orbital debris) moved the stated value from cost saving to mission autonomy and produced a sealed-containment concept, and the team states HP guidelines fixed the wet-lab scope, but no specific construct or assay change is traced to a stakeholder.
screen.reason: Real HPLC data and unusually honest failure reporting, but the central scaffold claim is contradicted by the team's own table (the Dock+/Scaf+ condition releases the least product), no parts are registered, an adult (Nico) directed the key assembly and left without documenting it, the bench work was carried out under Christian and the decisive statistics were done by an external advisor, and the wiki is sprawling (59k-word home page, 59k-word prior-art page).
screen.field_notes: AEI Prep-Taiwan (Space village, Taiwan) built SynPETic, a cellulosome-inspired PETosome that docks an ICCG leaf-branch compost cutinase and a Thermobifida fusca carboxylesterase (TfCa) onto a trimeric cohesin scaffold to depolymerise PET at 37-50 C aboard spacecraft. All three proteins were expressed in E. coli from pET28a, purified by Ni-NTA and confirmed by SDS-PAGE and anti-His Western blot; activity was shown by PET agar plate clearing and by HPLC product profiling of APET film, giving 67% MHET / 32% TPA / 1% BHET at 96 h and identifying MHET to TPA as the rate-limiting step. The headline 16-row HPLC dataset across four dockerin/scaffold conditions in fact shows the scaffolded fusion releasing less product than unfused enzyme, and the two-enzyme BHET synergy p-value came from a re-analysis by advisor Qi Jia. A mechanistic parallel-release and erosion ODE model was fitted to the measured curves; two ESM2/ESMFold notebooks scanned linkers and TfCa pocket residues but the team documents a bug (identical pocket-volume term, two hardcoded scores) making the rankings unreliable. Hardware was a hand-cranked clinostat whose Neo 550 motors never drove it, so no microgravity data exist; human practices ran to eight interviews including NASA operations and orbital-debris experts. No BBa parts are registered and attributions are an embedded iGEM form only.

screen.project_title: UVitis: a fusion protein acting as molecular double-sided tape to keep kaolin sunscreen on grape berries
screen.what_they_built: Three fusion proteins sharing an sfGFP core with (GGGGS)2 linkers, a 6xHis tag and TEV site, a MacHis plant-wax-binding domain at one end and one of three silica/kaolin-binding peptides (Car9, SB7, R5) at the other, designed to make kaolin rainfast on vines. The work reached transformation only.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli (pET-24(+), kanamycin). Three new basic parts: BBa_26NGR0FX (Car9), BBa_26N5H14X (SB7), BBa_26GUOFAV (R5), plus two designed negative controls (GFP only, GFP+MacHis).
screen.best_evidence: /results: all three constructs transformed, with SB7 at roughly 45,750-46,665 CFU/ug and Car9 lowest - and the team says plainly that this is three to four orders of magnitude below the published 10^6-10^8 range and attributes it to manual technique. The AlphaFold screen that cut seven candidates to three is a prediction, not a result. The page itself lists expression, purification, kaolin binding, grape binding and retention after washing as still open.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and it is the best part of the project: the Les Vins de Rene Dubois interview revealed that UV is not their problem - they apply kaolin against Drosophila suzukii and the real cost is reapplication after 20 mm of rain - which changed the project's headline claim and its decisive metric from binding strength to rainfastness.
screen.reason: No functional data at all. The only bench result is that three plasmids transformed, at efficiencies the team itself calls far below standard; the IPTG expression check is described as run but 'needs documenting'. Everything the project turns on - expression, purification, kaolin binding, wax binding, retention after washing - is listed as open on their own Results page. The honesty and the single grower interview that redirected the project are creditable at medal level, and the pLDDT-reading guidance is a real small contribution, but this is nowhere near top-2 calibre.
screen.field_notes: Aiglon College (Agriculture, CHE) designed UVitis, a fusion protein intended to glue kaolin particle film to grape berry wax so it survives rain, for Chasselas vineyards in canton Vaud. The architecture is 6xHis-TEV-[Car9 or SB7 or R5]-(GGGGS)2-sfGFP-(GGGGS)2-MacHis in pET-24(+), with MacHis taken from published adhesion-peptide microgel work on grapevine leaves; two negative controls (GFP alone, GFP+MacHis) were designed in from the start, which is good practice. AlphaFold screened seven candidate kaolin-binding peptides down to three on the criterion that the sfGFP core folds confidently while the binding ends stay flexible and accessible; the team's insight that low pLDDT in deliberately flexible regions is the design working, not a failure, is offered as their contribution and would otherwise have eliminated all three candidates. Bench work stopped at heat-shock transformation: all three gave colonies on kanamycin, SB7 highest at roughly 45,750-46,665 CFU/ug, which they correctly flag as orders of magnitude below published competent-cell efficiency and attribute to manual losses. No expression, purification, binding or wash-retention data are shown. The Hardware page honestly states no hardware was built and names the rainfall simulator they would need. The vineyard interview is the project's strongest element, having replaced the UV-damage premise with rainfastness after Drosophila suzukii treatment; the growers also raised GMO labelling concerns and legal uncertainty under Swiss agricultural rules.

screen.project_title: C.L.E.A.R. - a synthetic-biology toolkit for engineering Cutibacterium acnes
screen.what_they_built: A genetic toolkit for the skin commensal C. acnes: a methylation-matched E. coli intermediate host (EC24), an E. coli/C. acnes shuttle vector, a characterised reporter and promoter library, functional modules (glycerol uptake, oxidative stress) and layered kill switches, plus two in-house software tools, aimed at rebalancing the skin microbiome in acne rather than killing it.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli JM110-derived EC24 (dam-/dcm-, hsdMS deleted, IIIBM cassette at tnaA by CRISPR-Cas9), E. coli DH5a, C. acnes; pCa dual-origin shuttle vector (p545 + E. coli ori, AmpR + ermE); ~30 new BBa parts plus many reused Registry parts; codon-optimisation and promoter-prediction web tools.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering: quantitative reporter characterisation in DH5a and EC24 (sfGFP ~600,000 RFU, mRFP1 ~200,000 RFU, eforRed and YukonOFP below 1000 RFU) with growth curves, leading to a reasoned choice of mCherry for dynamic range; constitutive promoter screen with motif-disrupting mutants, matched negative and literature positive controls, where Pos2 gave ~10-fold higher expression in EC24 than DH5a; CFU-based kill-switch characterisation and a Biofuse time-switch time course (~1500 RFU/OD600 plateau).
screen.hp_integration: Extensive HP (over 15,000 words) and entrepreneurship work frame the product and safety design; the pack does not pin a single interview to a specific construct change as crisply as the top teams do.
screen.reason: Scope and standards are finalist-shaped: a chassis built by CRISPR editing, a dual-host shuttle vector, a promoter library screened with mutant and negative controls, biocontainment characterised by CFU, two reusable software tools and a large parts contribution. Two things need a full read - almost all data sit in the E. coli surrogate rather than C. acnes, and the wiki has no Results page while the Experiments page is only an embedded PDF and the Attribution page is ~104 words, so aspect 6 is unverifiable from the wiki.
screen.field_notes: AIS-China (Shenzhen, Therapeutics) built C.L.E.A.R., a toolkit for engineering the skin commensal Cutibacterium acnes instead of eradicating it. They CRISPR-edited E. coli JM110 (naturally dam-/dcm-) to delete hsdMS and integrate an IIIBM cassette at tnaA, giving EC24, a host whose methylation pattern mimics C. acnes so plasmids survive transfer; verification is colony PCR plus whole-genome sequencing, and they explicitly decline to claim off-target exclusion. A dual-origin pCa shuttle vector (p545/ermE for C. acnes, E. coli ori/AmpR) carries a six-reporter library characterised quantitatively in both DH5a and EC24, with mCherry chosen for dynamic range despite a 24 h growth lag. The constitutive promoter screen is the methodological high point: candidates from their own promoter-prediction framework tested alongside motif-disrupting mutants, a matched negative, a literature positive and BBa_J23119, with host-dependent effects (Pos2 ~10-fold higher in EC24) that support the methylation rationale. Further cycles cover inducible promoters, glycerol-uptake and oxidative-stress modules, and three kill-switch classes (inducible, temperature, Biofuse time switch) characterised by fluorescence and CFU; they report leaky expression and too-fast activation honestly. A Measurement page documents fluorescence, CFU and enzyme-activity assays with controls, and two software tools (codon optimisation, promoter prediction) are published as separate pages. Weaknesses: no Results page, an Experiments page that is only an embedded PDF, a ~104-word Attribution page, and most functional data obtained in the E. coli surrogate rather than in C. acnes itself.

screen.project_title: BioQuests: GGP overexpression in Chlorella vulgaris for vitamin C and iron bioavailability
screen.what_they_built: A proposed, unbuilt design: a GGP expression cassette for Chlorella vulgaris intended to raise vitamin C and so improve non-heme iron absorption. The only work done is computational iron-speciation modelling in Visual MINTEQ plus a literature 4PL ferritin dose-response curve.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Chlorella vulgaris proposed (electroporation strategy only, never performed); no constructs built, no BBa parts registered, parts page empty.
screen.best_evidence: /results: modelled soluble Fe2+ of 49.24 uM (wild-type, Eh +150 mV) versus 49.88 uM (proposed transformed, Eh +100 mV) out of 50 uM input, i.e. a 0.64 uM difference under assumed redox potentials. The page itself states these are model outputs, not measurements, and that the 4PL ferritin values (8.2 and 36.4 ng/mg) do not reconcile with the stated equation.
screen.hp_integration: Minimal: human practices is a short page of outreach and expert conversation with no traceable change to a design that was never built.
screen.reason: No wet lab at all: no construct, no transformation, no measurement. The only quantitative outputs are thermodynamic simulations whose difference (0.64 uM of 50 uM) is negligible, and the team openly reports an unresolved numerical inconsistency in its own ferritin model. Commendably honest and the gamified wiki is pleasant, but nowhere near finalist calibre.
screen.field_notes: Anatolia College-GR (Food and Nutrition, Greece) proposed BioQuests, overexpressing GDP-L-galactose phosphorylase (GGP) in Chlorella vulgaris to raise vitamin C and thereby improve non-heme iron bioavailability from algal biomass. The project is entirely dry lab: Visual MINTEQ iron speciation at pH 3 and pH 7 under assigned Eh values, with the proposed transformed scenario giving 49.88 uM soluble Fe2+ against 49.24 uM for wild type, plus a literature-parameterised four-parameter logistic ferritin response for Caco-2 cells (Ymin 4.2, Ymax 45.0, EC50 28.5 uM, nH 1.85). Two computational DBTL iterations are documented, the useful one being the discovery that an early spreadsheet wrongly summed ferric and precipitated species into a soluble-ferrous total. The team repeatedly and clearly labels everything as modelled rather than measured and flags that its own illustrative 4.44-fold ferritin comparison does not reproduce from the stated equation. No genetic construct was assembled, no transformation attempted, no parts registered and the parts page is empty; contributions are a high-schooler's guide to synthetic biology, an iGEM Corner recruitment page and documented modelling assumptions. The wiki is a polished quest-themed site with an unusually candid limitations section.

screen.project_title: 茶(Sa)kure-it-all — plant specialised metabolites (sakuranetin, quercetin, EGCG, L-theanine) in yeast coculture
screen.what_they_built: Twelve plasmids giving six S. cerevisiae strains and five modules that split flavonoid pathways across cocultured strains (upstream naringenin producer feeding downstream converters), plus a DIY Arduino 2 L bioreactor. Four DBTL iterations across two seasons, 34 parts submitted.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. cerevisiae BY4741 with pRS316 (URA3) / pRS315 (LEU2) dual-plasmid strains; earlier E. coli BL21 Duet attempt. 12 BBa_26* parts visible in the pack, 34 claimed submitted (TAL, 4CL, CHS, CHI, F3H, F3'H, F3'5'H, ANR, SCPL galloyltransferases, AtATR1, theanine synthetase).
screen.best_evidence: /results: TLC co-migration of naringenin, sakuranetin, EGCG and L-theanine with their own standards on the same plate (Rf within 0.05; EGCG lanes within 0.035). The quantification table (apparent 2,350 mg/L naringenin etc.) is explicitly retracted by the team as bulk-aromatic absorbance, not titre; quercetin band at Rf 0.85 is called 'not confirmed' and attributed to kaempferol.
screen.hp_integration: Four interviews and a tea-farm visit (Okutomi, Kawahito, Adams, Maruichi Mizuno) informed sourcing and product framing, but /human-practices (1,068 words) does not show a specific design change traceable to stakeholder input.
screen.reason: Exceptional engineering record and near-unique scientific honesty (eight claims retracted/withdrawn with causes, a self-diagnosed measurement failure, explicit bounds: no sequencing, no HPLC, no titres), plus a built-and-benchmarked bioreactor. Against that, nothing is quantitatively shown to work and HP is thin, so it is a borderline rather than clear finalist — worth a full read because aspects 4, 6 and 8 and the whole Wiki section are at or near finalist level.
screen.field_notes: ASIJ-Tokyo (Japan, Biomanufacturing) engineered S. cerevisiae to make four plant specialised metabolites — sakuranetin, quercetin, EGCG and L-theanine — splitting the pathways across cocultured strains rather than one super-strain, with twelve pRS316/pRS315 plasmids across six strains and 34 Registry parts. Best experimental evidence is TLC co-migration with own standards for four of five routes; HPLC was never run, so all identity calls are presence calls, and no construct was sequence- or cPCR-verified. The team's headline dry-lab/measurement work is a self-diagnosis that their 280 nm crude-lysate quantification was reading bulk aromatics — naringenin apparently 16x an optimised published strain — so they retracted the titres, five model conclusions and two coculture orderings, and published the broken arithmetic as a contribution. They also built a 2 L Arduino bioreactor (±0.35 C, 1.5 L/min aeration, SD logging) run against two incubator controls, with build, development and operating manuals embedded on an Appendix page. Human Practices is the weak section: four stakeholder conversations and a tea-farm visit, with no documented design change; measurement, safety, attributions and parts pages are empty on the wiki.

screen.project_title: Neurofilux: AI-designed antibodies for blood NfL detection
screen.what_they_built: A sandwich ELISA for neurofilament light chain (NfL), an early blood biomarker of neurodegeneration, in which the antibodies were generated computationally with RFantibody against a modelled NfL fragment, then expressed and tested experimentally against commercial antibodies. Nanobody conversion is virtual only.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5-alpha / BL21(DE3) for antigen expression (pPGH-GST-NfL(93-396)-6His). Eight Registry parts, all antibody VH/VL sequences (BBa_26AT1H8O, BBa_26M7D0U9, BBa_26PQL4AL, BBa_26KFQQGU, BBa_26TZQWPU, BBa_26ZS3GMP, BBa_26VOVMQF, BBa_26ZGH4Y8).
screen.best_evidence: /engineering Cycle 3-4: purified NfL rod domain at 2.3 mg/mL (Bradford); BLI showing binding (300-800 s) and slow dissociation for 4 candidates; sandwich ELISA with blank OD450 < 0.2 and epitope-competition results identifying overlapping pairs (differences -0.088, -0.041); against commercial components, capture antibody 3D9A-Epito1-2499 gave +38% net OD and detection antibody HRP-3D9A-Epito2-2834 +29%; best self-developed pair 3D9A-Epito1-2499 / 3D9A-Epito2-2834 at OD 0.459.
screen.hp_integration: Partly: a 193-respondent survey and seven structured interviews organised on a Power-Interest matrix set price (<100 yuan), privacy and post-test counselling requirements and pushed sensitivity as the technical priority, but the recorded changes are mostly to pricing, service design and future roadmap rather than to the molecular design.
screen.reason: They have the rarest thing in the HS field: a self-designed binder that out-performs a commercial reagent in a head-to-head assay (+38% capture, +29% detection net OD), backed by BLI and epitope competition. Against that, aspect 6 is the problem - the antigen gene and all eight antibody proteins were synthesised by commercial companies, the attributions page is empty, there is no results page (data is buried in /engineering), replicate counts and error bars are not shown for the ELISA numbers, and the nanobody arm is purely computational. Worth a full read mainly to settle how much of the bench work was the students'.
screen.field_notes: BAID-China (Beijing, Diagnostics village) built Neurofilux, a blood test for neurofilament light chain (NfL) aimed at pre-symptomatic screening for Alzheimer's and ALS. A hand-written cathepsin-cleavage scoring model (P4-P4' context, cysteine- and aspartyl-cathepsin scoring) plus Cys322 and SDS-PAGE mass constraints narrowed candidate NfL fragments to aa 280-377; the wider rod domain aa 93-396 was expressed in E. coli BL21 as a GST/His fusion and purified to 2.3 mg/mL. RFantibody generated candidate VH/VL sequences, multi-objective scoring picked eight, a commercial firm made the proteins, and BLI plus sandwich ELISA selected 3D9A-Epito1-2499 (capture) and 3D9A-Epito2-2834 (detection), which beat matched commercial antibodies by 38% and 29% net OD; eight sequences are registered as parts. Nanobody conversion was validated only in silico. The wiki is fully trilingual (EN/ZH/FR), has a 10k-word model page and an 8.9k-word HP page built on a 193-person survey and a Power-Interest stakeholder matrix, but the results page is empty, the attributions page is empty, and gene and protein synthesis were outsourced, leaving student-versus-vendor division of labour unclear.

screen.project_title: KeraTINT: keratin-binding-peptide chromoprotein hair dye
screen.what_they_built: Fusion proteins joining a keratin-binding peptide (KBP) to seven chromoproteins/fluorescent proteins (aeBlue, amilCP, anm2CP, mScarlet-i, mKate, amilGFP, sfGFP), intended as a non-damaging hair dye that also strengthens hair, plus two sub-$50 open-source test rigs for wash-fastness and hair tensile strength.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli NEBExpress T7 and NEB cell-free (S30-type) system; pET-style T7 constructs and a constitutive J23100 plasmid (pIDMv5K-BLUE). Only one Registry ID appears anywhere on the wiki (BBa_K2906100); no parts page.
screen.best_evidence: /results: SDS-PAGE bands at the expected ~27 kDa for KBP-aeBlue after IPTG induction and after Ni-NTA elution, but cultures stayed colourless; sequencing of blue constitutive colonies showed large deletions inside KBP while the one white colony retained it, and qPCR showed lower RNA in KBP-containing constructs - together a coherent case that the KBP is cytotoxic. Cell-free expression then gave plate-reader fluorescence for sfGFP and KBP-sfGFP above control, though with high background.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in a product sense: a cosmetics chemist and L'Oreal's North America Color Lab moved them to survey Gen Z dyers, add a semi-permanent comparison arm to the wash-fastness assay, and switch to lower-affinity keratin peptides that may fold more easily; an HP Summit review caused a rebuild of their framework graphic.
screen.reason: The core claim never worked: no coloured protein was produced in cells, no dyeing, wash-fastness or tensile measurement was performed on hair, and the two purpose-built rigs were never used to generate data. No parts are registered and there is no parts page, which caps aspects 7 and 8. The debugging is honest and genuinely well reasoned (promoter swap, SDM, temperature, sequencing that caught KBP deletions, cell-free rescue) and the sub-$50 open-source hardware is a real contribution, so this is a credible medal team, but it is far from top-2 calibre on project aspects.
screen.field_notes: Baltimore BioCrew (BUGSS, USA, Fashion & Cosmetics village) built KeraTINT, fusions of a keratin-binding peptide to seven chromoproteins/fluorescent proteins intended to dye and simultaneously strengthen bleached hair. Across five engineering iterations (T7 induction, constitutive J23100, site-directed mutagenesis, batch-growth optimisation, cell-free) they never obtained coloured protein in cells: SDS-PAGE showed ~27 kDa bands for KBP-aeBlue and Ni-NTA purification recovered it, but cultures stayed colourless, an imidazole-gradient purification recovered nothing, qPCR showed reduced transcript in KBP constructs, and sequencing of the blue constitutive colonies revealed large deletions inside KBP while the white colony kept it - good evidence that the KBP is cytotoxic. NEBExpress cell-free expression then gave above-control fluorescence for sfGFP and KBP-sfGFP, supporting the cytotoxicity hypothesis and pointing to the next design round (new KBP/linker combinations pre-screened with ColabFold Multimer, LightDock, HADDOCK, A3D and SoluProt). Their best contribution is hardware: open-sourced wash-fastness (pump, ESP32, CAD) and hair tensile-strength rigs buildable for under $50 against $1,300-$35,000 commercial equipment, though neither has produced data yet. HP engaged a cosmetics-company founder, L'Oreal's North America Color Lab and cosmetology students, and changed the assay design and peptide choice. No parts page and no registered parts; the wiki carries a GoFundMe donation appeal on every page.

screen.project_title: HEAL — engineered keratin-degrading probiotic for feline hairball management
screen.what_they_built: A four-module system in E. coli: a tri-enzyme hair-degradation module (protease P1 plus thioredoxin/thioredoxin reductase to break keratin disulfides), an AKG-producing heal module (LGOX with KatG to clear peroxide), a bile-acid-sensing suicide switch biosafety module, and a pH-responsive microcapsule delivery module for gastric transit.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3), pET28a/pET32a backbones; 8 basic plus 7 composite parts registered (keratinases P1, P2, Ker, MG1820, MG4907; Trx; TrxR; LGOX), plus Anderson promoters J23100/102/104/114. OmpA signal peptide for secretion; GST fusion for solubility.
screen.best_evidence: /results: quantitative Folin-phenol protease activity assay against a tyrosine standard curve with BCA normalisation identifies P1 as highest-activity candidate (significance letters a-d); A280 keratin-degradation assay shows P1 above heat-killed control at p<0.0001; the P1+Trx+TrxR combination gives the highest A280 signal (p<0.05 to p<0.0001) and SEM plus stereomicroscopy show cuticle disruption and fibrous tearing only in that condition. TrxR activity confirmed by DTNB/NADPH assay (p<0.0001). SDS-PAGE of culture supernatant shows P1-GST-OmpA at 62.1 kDa, i.e. secreted.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, substantially — 19 veterinarians and experts and ~300 pet owners; clinical feedback pushed the team from in-cat application to in vitro keratinase degradation plus strict safety testing first, prompted the suicide switch and delivery work, and expert interviews supplied the replacement candidate enzymes (MG1820, MG4907, P1, P2) after Ker failed.
screen.reason: The strongest evidence in this batch by a clear margin: a real screening funnel (5 candidates to 1), quantitative replicated activity assays with statistics, orthogonal SEM confirmation, a working synergy result, secretion demonstrated, and four integrated modules with 15 registered parts. Failures (Ker inactive, inclusion bodies, P2 unpurifiable) are reported and drive the next cycle. Caveats worth a full read: all constructs were commercially synthesised and sequence-verified, SEM was outsourced to Shenzhen University, and the attributions page is an empty shell pointing at a form — aspect 6 needs checking in person.
screen.field_notes: BASIS-China (Therapeutics, CHN) built HEAL, an engineered E. coli for feline hairball (trichobezoar) management across four modules. Hair degradation: five candidate keratinases screened (Ker, MG1820, MG4907, P1, P2); initial expression failed as inclusion bodies, GST fusion rescued solubility, casein halo plus BCA/Folin-phenol assays selected Protease 1 from Brevibacillus gelatini, and A280 keratin assays plus SEM showed P1 damages cat hair cuticle; adding thioredoxin and thioredoxin reductase to reduce keratin disulfides gave the highest degradation signal and visible fibre tearing, and OmpA-tagged P1 was detected in culture supernatant (62.1 kDa). Heal module expresses LGOX to make alpha-ketoglutarate with KatG clearing the H2O2 byproduct; a bile-acid-sensing suicide switch with a GFP reporter and pH-responsive microcapsules for gastric transit complete the system. 15 registered parts. Modelling covers ODE expression/secretion fitted to BCA data, pH and temperature activity surfaces, and HDOCK/AlphaFold3 docking of P1 against keratins KRT35 and KRT71. Human practices is unusually deep: 19 experts, ~300 owners, 35 documented activities on a Hear-Engage-Analyze-Learn cycle. Note for attribution: DNA was synthesised and assembled commercially, SEM imaging was done by Shenzhen University, and the attributions page carries no narrative content.

justification.a1: The results build in increasing difficulty rather than sitting side by side: five candidate proteases constructed, an expression failure diagnosed and fixed with GST fusion and milder induction, quantitative screening that selects P1, keratin and cat-hair assays, OmpA-mediated appearance of P1 in the supernatant, and then a tri-enzyme Trx/TrxR synergy test (Results, Stages 1-6 and the synergy section). A parallel LGOX/KatG track, a four-promoter bile-acid kill switch with GFP, an alginate microcapsule prototype and an ODE/docking model widen the scope further. It falls short of a 5 only because the modules are never run together and degradation of an actual hairball (mass loss, knotted mimic) is still future work, as the team's own HP page concedes.
justification.a2: Most function claims carry a figure and a control: A280 keratin hydrolysis versus heat-deactivated P1 (p < 0.0001, Results Fig 13), the four-way synergy comparison with deactivated P1 as baseline (Fig 23), casein halos with a no-enzyme control (Fig 11), LGOX AKG kit assay versus control (p < 0.01, Fig 28), KatG catalase assay (p < 0.0001, Fig 33), spot dilutions and growth curves of four promoter variants against empty vector across six TCA concentrations (Figs 36-38), and supernatant SDS-PAGE with no-signal-peptide controls (Fig 17). The honest negative in Stage 1 (no visible change in hair, with a stated limitation) is exactly what p.20 rewards. It stops at 4 because no page states replicate numbers or defines the error bars behind the asterisks, the keratin assays use crude lysate rather than purified P1, and degradation is reported as absorbance and morphology rather than hair mass lost.
justification.a3: The clinical framing is grounded and was corrected by stakeholders: Dr. Lin's interview moved the product from emergency rescue of obstructions to daily preventive management, and Dr. Mo's advice is repeated in the Entrepreneurship page with a recorded market survey of six competing Chinese products and their prices. The delivery prototype is tested in a real-world-like way, with microcapsules surviving simulated gastric acid and releasing 1.186 x 10^5 CFU/mL after sequential transit (Hardware, Fig 5). It is not a 4.5 because the benefit to a cat is never quantified from the team's own data (no dose, no hair-clearance rate) and the keratinase products already on the market in their own table are not benchmarked against P1.
justification.a4: Four degradation cycles plus two HEAL-module cycles are documented on the Engineering page, and in each the test result drives the next design rather than a repeat of the same experiment: unclear SDS-PAGE plus viscous lysate leads to the inclusion-body hypothesis and a GST fusion with 0.1 mM IPTG at 28 C; a useless visual hair inspection leads to quantitative Folin-phenol and A280 assays; selection of P1 leads to the OmpA secretion build; and the H2O2 by-product identified at the LGOX design stage leads to the KatG cycle. Design decisions are also pre-justified (promoter strength series chosen to tune CcdB before testing). Measures of success are mostly implicit rather than stated as thresholds before testing, which keeps it just under 5.
justification.a5: The iHP page records 35 activities across four mapped stakeholder groups within a declared Hear-Engage-Analyze-Learn loop, and several design changes are traceable to specific conversations: reframing to daily prevention and redesigning the in vitro assay to use knotted hairball mimics and a bile/pancreatin intestinal fluid after Dr. Lin; adopting an inducible kill switch after public concern about horizontal gene transfer; and abandoning freeze-dried powder for alginate microcapsules after cat owners, Professor Wang and the South China regional meeting (Hardware Table 1). The page is also unusually careful about what the feedback does not prove ("this feedback reflects user needs rather than providing evidence of our solution's effectiveness"). It is not a 5 because the 300-owner survey is reported as percentages without the instrument or the raw distribution.
justification.a6: The lab work reads as student-run across a 437-page scanned notebook and 14 protocols, and outsourcing is declared where it happened: gene synthesis and assembly by a commercial provider (Sangon, named on the Safety page), SEM imaging by experts at Shenzhen University, and the Folin-phenol method and TcpP/TcpH sensor adapted from BNDS-China 2025 with links. What I cannot check is task-level ownership: the Attributions page is only the embedded iGEM standardized form, which does not render as text, so the per-member split that TAS Taipei's page made obvious is not legible here. That caps it at 4 for me, and it is the first thing I would resolve in Q&A.
justification.a7: This is genuinely a standard-parts project: eight basic parts and seven composite constructs are registered with BBa_ codes, the kill-switch composite BBa_26NOEGF3 combines a prior iGEM team's TcpP/TcpH sensor with CcdA/CcdB and sfGFP, four Anderson promoters (J23100/02/04/14) are reused as a tuning series, and modular GST and OmpA elements are swapped onto a common pET28a backbone. The team also adds characterization to an existing Registry entry (KatG, BBa_K137067) that previously had none. Only the microcapsule and the ESP32 feeder sit outside the biology, and they are kept clearly subordinate.
justification.a8: The wiki side of documentation is strong, with per-figure legends, limitations boxes and cross-links from Results to Design and Engineering. The Registry side I could not verify (parts.igem.org returned 403 to me), so I score what the wiki shows, and there the part metadata is inconsistent enough to worry me: P1 is listed as 858 bp on Parts and Contribution while the Results gel reports a 1077 bp amplicon, P2's accession is WP_122903141.1 on Parts but WP_122903142.1 on Engineering, the Parts overview says "one composite part" then tabulates seven, and several composite entries carry a description copied verbatim from their basic part with the literature source in place of "this work". That is the gap between a 3.5 and a 4.5 here.
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem (swallowed hair forming trichobezoars), the approach (three modules in E. coli BL21) and the module-level mechanism within the first screens, with one schematic per idea and a link straight to Results. The Description page then gives the background in order with a clear "Our Solution" section. Half a point off because the scrolling narrative puts several atmospheric panels ("an everyday ritual", a mummy-hair aside) before the science, so the actual outcomes take a little longer to reach than Lambert_GA's concise front page.
justification.w2: Nearly every result on the Results, Safety and Hardware pages comes with a numbered figure, a legend describing the lanes or groups, a named control and, where quantitative, a significance marker; the "Result Claim / Observation / Limitations" boxes are an unusually honest device and the Stage 1 negative result is left in. Three things keep it at 4: replicate numbers and error-bar definitions are absent from the Results page (only the Model page states n = 3 with SD), the Safety page's summary overstates what was shown ("our full set of candidate enzymes ... can be actively expressed and degrade keratin fibers", "our bile-acid suicide circuit functions reliably", keratinases are "completely safe" to mucosa) when Results shows P2 unpurifiable and keratin data for P1 only, and the microcapsule group labels in Hardware Table 3 do not match the group descriptions in Results Fig 41-42.
justification.w3: Navigation follows the work (Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Engagement) with every standard URL intact, each page carries an on-page contents list and a "Related evidence" block that links Design to Engineering to Results, and the notebook and protocols are one click from the wet-lab menu. Figures open in full and the page is readable on a narrow screen. Minor friction only: there is no Proof of Concept, Implementation or Measurement page, so the measurement and prototype arguments have to be assembled from Results, Model and Hardware.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way with this: 14 protocols written to step level (buffers, volumes, g-forces, cycling tables), a 437-page scanned notebook, plasmid maps for every construct, registered parts, a parameter table for the ODE with the basis of each assumption, and failures kept in place rather than tidied away. The Contribution page deliberately packages the kill-switch characterization framework for reuse. It is not a 5 because the notebook is images only (not searchable or extractable) and no raw plate-reader or gel data files are offered for download.
justification.w5: Inline numbered citations with DOIs and back-links appear on every substantive page, prior iGEM work is credited specifically (BNDS-China 2025 for both the TcpP/TcpH sensor and the Folin-phenol method, with links), figure sources are attributed, and the footer licenses the site and credits the fonts, icon set and libraries. Small gaps rather than systematic ones: one reference lists the journal itself as the author (IJMS 2026), the Parts table attributes P2 to "Jue et al." in the source column while the description credits "Fan et al.", and a few Safety page citations (Reber and Mosley, Samanu et al.) are named in text without a resolvable entry.

J1.one_line: A broad, genuinely iterative high-school project whose main claims are backed by controlled, mostly quantitative assays, let down by unstated replicate numbers, inconsistent part metadata, and a summary page that overclaims what the data show.
strengths: Controlled function data across all four modules, not just construction checks: deactivated-enzyme controls for the keratin A280 assay, empty-vector controls for the kill-switch spot plates and GFP, and a no-signal-peptide control for the OmpA secretion gel.

A real DBTL record where failures drive redesign: the unclear SDS-PAGE and viscous lysate lead to a GST fusion and milder induction, and a useless visual hair inspection leads to quantitative Folin-phenol and A280 assays (Engineering, Cycles 1-3).

The bile-acid kill switch is characterized rather than asserted: four Anderson promoter variants, liquid growth curves, serial-dilution spots at six TCA concentrations, a stated ~0.1-0.2 mM threshold, and a comparison against published sewage and soil bile-acid levels (Safety and Security, Figs 6-8).

Human Practices that visibly changed the project, including the reframe from emergency rescue to daily prevention after Dr. Lin and the switch from freeze-dried powder to alginate microcapsules after owners and Professor Wang (iHP; Hardware Table 1).
A model fitted to the team's own measurements that reports its own failure honestly: the ODE's RMSE of 25.41 ug/mL against 2.12 for the empirical fit is stated plainly (Model, section 3).
Proactive safety conduct: the team contacted safety@igem.org before collecting shed cat hair and documented the written approval and conditions (Safety and Security).

Documentation habits a future team can use: 14 step-level protocols, a 437-page notebook, plasmid maps, limitations boxes on results, and a Contribution page that packages the kill-switch characterization framework for reuse.
weaknesses: No replicate number or error-bar definition is given anywhere on the Results page, although significance asterisks are shown throughout; only the Model page states n = 3 with sample SD.

Keratin and hair degradation are assayed with crude enzyme solution rather than the purified P1 shown on the SDS-PAGE, so the activity cannot be attributed to P1 alone, and degradation is never quantified as hair mass lost.
The four modules are never operated together, so HEAL as a system is a design, not a tested entity.

The Safety page summary outruns the data: it states that the full set of candidate enzymes can express and degrade keratin fibers (P2 could not even be purified), that the suicide circuit 'functions reliably', and that the keratinases are 'completely safe' to gut mucosa, which is argued from mucus composition with no experiment.

Part metadata is inconsistent between pages: P1 at 858 bp versus a 1077 bp amplicon, P2 accession .1 versus .2, 'one composite part' in the overview against seven in the table, and several composite entries reusing their basic part's description and literature source instead of 'this work'.
The Attributions page is only the embedded iGEM form, which does not render as readable text, so task-level ownership cannot be checked from the wiki itself.

The microcapsule experimental groups are labelled inconsistently between Hardware Table 3 and Results Figs 41-42, and the ~67% protection figure rests on a single set of plate counts with no replicates stated.

Gaussian fits reporting R-squared of 0.9999 from four pH points with three free parameters are over-fitted, and the 'optimum' pH 8.1 and 41.3 C are interpolations between measured conditions rather than measured optima.
red_flags: Overclaiming on the Safety and Security page relative to the Results page (full enzyme set degrading keratin; circuit 'functions reliably'; keratinases 'completely safe' to mucosa). Documentation issue, not an integrity concern.
Part size and accession inconsistencies between the Parts, Contribution, Results and Engineering pages; these need correcting before the Registry entries are trusted.

SEM imaging was performed by Shenzhen University staff and all constructs were synthesized and assembled commercially; both are declared, so this lowers nothing beyond the a6 discussion, but the student share of the imaging work should be clarified in Q&A.

I could not load parts.igem.org (HTTP 403 from this environment), so Registry entries were not inspected directly; a8 reflects what the wiki presents and should be revisited once the Registry is reachable.

A few citations do not resolve cleanly as written (a journal listed as its own author; Reber and Mosley, Samanu et al. named in text with no matching entry). Sloppiness rather than fabrication on the evidence I have.

Questions for Q&A: what n lies behind each error bar; was keratin-degrading activity ever confirmed with purified rather than crude P1; how much hair mass was lost; who in the team ran the kill-switch assays; and does residual fecal bile acid defeat the switch's 0.1-0.2 mM threshold.

calibrated.changed: none. a2 4.0 rather than 4.5 is consistent with how I treated unstated replicates elsewhere (Squirrel Guangzhou, ZQT): the controls and significance marks are there but no page states n or defines the error bars, and keratin activity was measured on crude lysate. w3 4.5 is the only such score on the ballot and is earned by every standard URL being intact with working cross-links.

justification.a1: Four modules carried a long way in one season: five candidate proteases screened and compared quantitatively, P1 selected and characterised, a tri-enzyme P1+Trx+TrxR system, OmpA secretion, an LGOX/KatG AKG module, a four-promoter bile-acid kill switch, and calcium-alginate microcapsules with CFU recovery after simulated gastric transit (Results; Hardware Fig 5). The chain of increasingly difficult steps and the honest reporting of dead ends (Ker visual test, P2 unpurifiable) is close to the GreatBay pattern. It falls short of 5 because the four modules were never run together and no engineered cell, as opposed to crude or purified enzyme, was ever shown to damage hair.
justification.a2: Most central claims are measured with a control: A280 keratin assay with deactivated P1 (Results Fig 13, p<0.0001), SEM with an uninduced-P1 and untreated control (Fig 14), TrxR DTNB assay (Fig 22), AKG kit assay (Fig 28), CAT assay (Fig 33), empty-vector controls and a six-point TCA spot series for the kill switch (Figs 36-38), and plate counts of 1.76x10^5 and 1.186x10^5 CFU/mL for the delivery test (Hardware). Against that, replicate numbers are given only for the BCA time course (n=3), hair degradation itself remains a proxy (A280) plus micrographs rather than mass loss, and the secretion claim rests on one supernatant SDS-PAGE lane with acknowledged extra bands (Fig 17).
justification.a3: The need is argued from real clinical literature and from their own survey of ~235 owners, and the route to use is concrete: microcapsule supplement rather than extruded feed, after Professor Wang pointed out that live cells die in high-temperature extrusion (Hardware Table 1; iHP Product section). Regulatory cost of GMO approval and the need for in vitro work before any animal study are faced openly. It is not a 4.5 because the only realistic-setting test is simulated gastric and intestinal fluid, and the specific risk vets raised (local heating of the mucosa during keratin digestion) is recorded and left unresolved.
justification.a4: There are genuine cycles where data changed the build: absent expression and viscous lysate led to GST fusions plus 0.1 mM IPTG at 28 C, which then gave bands (Engineering Cycles 1-2); screening data selected P1; the need for extracellular enzyme led to OmpA; H2O2 from the LGOX reaction led to KatG. The model is fitted to the team's own BCA measurements (ks = 0.01277 min^-1) and the page reports that the ODE fits badly (RMSE 25.41 vs 2.12 for the empirical fit) and that AlphaFold ipTM of 0.09-0.12 gives no usable interface, which is the kind of honesty I reward. The deduction is for the weighing hardware: Table 6 of the Hardware page ticks 'known masses', 'repeated placement' and 'known additions' but prints no reference values, errors or units, so by my own rule that hardware is only shown to work by measurements, the feeder is unverified; success criteria were also never quantified in advance.
justification.a5: Thirty-five documented records under a Hear-Engage-Analyze-Learn structure, with stakeholder mapping that states both influence on HEAL and HEAL's impact on each group. Several design changes are traceable to named sources: microcapsule format from Professor Wang, the bile-acid CcdA/CcdB switch from the Southern China regional meeting's HGT and kill-switch discussion, literature-based model parameters and physiological bounds from Mr. Ling, the feeder concept from JLU-NBBMS at Grand APIC, in vitro-first sequencing from the welfare organisation Xiaobabenben. The overall summary states plainly which of these changed the project rather than claiming everything did.
justification.a6: The team declares that all constructs were synthesised, assembled and sequence-verified by a commercial provider and that SEM was done by Shenzhen University, and the Results page is explicit that in-house PCR was only an additional check (Results, 'Construct verification'). That honesty is good, but it means a large part of the build was outsourced. The Attributions page carries only the standardised iGEM form in an iframe, whose contents I cannot read from the wiki, and there is no who-did-what chart of the GreatBay kind; the Team page gives Wet Lab / Dry Lab / HP tags only.
justification.a7: Fifteen parts are registered (8 basic, 7 composite), the work reuses the Anderson promoter series BBa_J23100/02/04/14 to tune CcdB, builds on BNDS-China 2025's TcpP/TcpH sensor, and adds expression and catalase-activity data to an existing Registry part, KatG BBa_K137067 (Contribution, 'Improved Part'). The GST and OmpA fusions are a modular pattern applied across five candidates, which is reusable. It is not higher because the parts are literature coding sequences placed in pET vectors with no statement of RFC10/RFC1000 compatibility or assembly standard.
justification.a8: On the wiki the documentation is good: fourteen protocols with volumes and cycling tables, a 437-page scanned notebook, full model parameter tables with sources. Registry entries themselves I could not verify (parts.igem.org returned a CAPTCHA to me), and the Parts page's own descriptions are thin and inconsistent: several composite entries repeat the basic part's text verbatim, 'Source' for OmpA-GST-P1 cites Fan et al. rather than this work, the P2 accession is WP_122903141.1 on the Parts page but WP_122903142.1 in Results Table 1, and the page subtitle says 'one composite part' where the body says seven.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the chassis (E. coli BL21) and the three modules in one screen, and the Description page gives background, current products and the gap before naming HEAL. A reader can say what the project is and what success would look like after those two pages. Marks off for a home page that is long on scroll-driven narrative before the science.
justification.w2: Claims are mostly tied to numbered figures with statistics and, unusually, to explicit 'Result Claim / Observation / Limitations' blocks that record negative results (Results, Stage 1 and Stage 2). The model page prints measured means and SDs and its own fit error. Against that, sample sizes are unstated outside the BCA series, the hardware verification table has ticks without data, and some captions are garbled (Hardware Table 3 swaps the group labels against Figure 4 and against Results Figure 42).
justification.w3: Navigation is consistent: four top sections, an on-page contents list, and 'Related evidence' links that move the reader from Description to Design to Engineering to Results. Content is findable without hunting. The deduction is that seven standard pages return 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, protocols, software, inclusivity, sustainability); the material exists under Experiments and Hardware, but a judge following the standard menu hits empty pages.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat much of this: fourteen protocols with buffers and volumes, the 437-page notebook hosted on iGEM servers, the Contribution page's candidate-screening comparison and five-step kill-switch characterisation framework, and a model page that lists every parameter with its basis. Short of 4.5 because the modelling code and the Meow Recovery application are only linked as downloadable repositories rather than described in enough detail to rebuild from the wiki.
justification.w5: Every substantive page ends with a numbered reference list carrying DOIs and back-links to the citing sentence, and the kill-switch environmental argument cites specific measured bile-acid concentrations in sewage and soil rather than asserting them. Deductions: Description Figure 5 credits '(Murphrey et al.)' with no matching list entry, the commercial-product photographs in Figure 7 are uncredited, and a few claims lean on consumer sources (PetMD, a clinic blog) where a veterinary paper exists.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineered four-module project with real controls, honest negative results and a model fitted to its own data; held back by modules never integrated, an outsourced build, and hardware ticked off without a single measurement.
strengths: Real DBTL where data changed the build: no expression on SDS-PAGE led to GST fusions and 0.1 mM IPTG at 28 C, which produced bands (Engineering Cycles 1-2)

Controls almost everywhere that matters: deactivated-P1 control for the A280 keratin assay (Results Fig 13), uninduced-P1 and untreated hair for SEM (Fig 14), empty-vector controls across the kill-switch growth and spot assays (Figs 36-38)

Kill switch characterised quantitatively across six TCA concentrations with a stated threshold near 0.1-0.2 mM, then compared against literature bile-acid levels in sewage and soil (Safety and Security)
Delivery prototype gives numbers, not adjectives: 1.76x10^5 CFU/mL intestinal-only versus 1.186x10^5 CFU/mL after acid then intestinal fluid, and no colonies from acid alone (Hardware Fig 5)

Model fitted to the team's own BCA time course and honest about failing: ODE RMSE 25.41 ug/mL against 2.12 for the empirical fit, and AlphaFold ipTM 0.09-0.12 declared unusable (Model, sections 3 and 9)
Failures reported rather than buried: the first Ker hair soak showed no visible difference, P2 could not be purified, ammonia management is left open (Results Stages 1-3; Engineering HEAL Cycle 1)
Human Practices with traceable consequences, for example Professor Wang's point about extrusion killing live cells producing the microcapsule format (Hardware Table 1; iHP Product summary)
weaknesses: The four modules were never run together; no engineered cell, as opposed to crude or purified enzyme, is shown degrading hair, and the AKG module was tested on pure L-glutamate rather than hair hydrolysate
Hardware Table 6 ticks calibration, repeatability and load tests but prints no reference values, errors or units, so the weighing device is unverified by measurement
Replicate numbers and units are missing from most wet-lab figures; only the BCA series states n=3
Constructs were synthesised and assembled commercially and the SEM was done at Shenzhen University; honestly declared, but a large share of the build was not student-executed
Attributions exist only as the embedded iGEM form, with no who-did-what breakdown visible on the wiki itself

Parts documentation is sloppy: composite entries repeating basic-part text, a source field crediting a paper rather than 'this work', the P2 accession differing between Parts and Results, and 'one composite part' versus seven in the same page
Seven standard pages (proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, protocols, software, inclusivity, sustainability) return 404
Group labels for the gastrointestinal transit experiment are inconsistent between Hardware Table 3, Hardware Fig 4 and Results Fig 42
red_flags: No integrity concern identified. One checkable internal inconsistency: the P2 accession is WP_122903141.1 on the Parts page and WP_122903142.1 in Results Table 1 - worth a question, not an allegation.

I could not open parts.igem.org (the Registry served a CAPTCHA, which I will not attempt to bypass), so aspects 7 and 8 rest on the wiki's own part tables; the Registry entries themselves are unverified by me and another judge should check them.

The Attributions page content sits inside an iframe to teams.igem.org and was not readable to me; a judge with access should confirm every field is complete, particularly the declared commercial synthesis and assembly of all constructs.

calibrated.changed: w3 4.0->3.5: seven standard pages return 404 here, which is the same or worse than plklfc (3.5), gcgs (3.0) and korea-hs (3.5). I was softer on this team for the same defect.

justification.a1: HEAL climbs through a real sequence of harder steps within one season: five candidate proteases screened, one (P1) selected on quantitative activity, GST and OmpA variants built, a three-enzyme redox-plus-protease system assembled, then a parallel AKG module, a bile-acid kill switch with four promoter strengths, an alginate delivery capsule and an ESP32 feeder with app (results.txt, engineering.txt, hardware.txt). That is wide scope carried mostly to data, not to plans. It falls short of a 5 because the four modules are never run together and the headline claim, degrading an actual hairball, is only approached indirectly.
justification.a2: Several components clearly work with controls: TrxR versus control by DTNB (Fig 22), LGOX-dependent AKG by GDH kit (Fig 28), KatG H2O2 clearance (Fig 33), P1 highest caseinolytic activity with letter-coded significance (Fig 12C), and P1+Trx+TrxR giving the highest A280 against deactivated-P1 control (Fig 23), plus kill-switch growth curves and dilution spots across 0-30 mM TCA (Figs 36-38). Hair degradation itself rests on A280 proxy and SEM/stereomicroscope morphology (Figs 14, 24) with no mass loss, no replicate counts given for the imaging, and the combined engineered strain never tested; the team says so honestly, including the failed first Ker test and unpurifiable P2. Measured components, unproven system, so 3.5.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by people, not just literature: 19 veterinarians and experts, ~300 owners, a shelter rescuer and pet-hospital interviews (human-practices.txt), and Dr Lin's input moved the product from emergency rescue to daily early management. The delivery route was tested in something closer to the real setting, with capsules surviving simulated gastric acid and releasing culturable bacteria after transit (hardware.txt Fig 5, 1.76x10^5 CFU/mL). It stops short of 4.5-5 because nothing has been tested in or on a cat, the live-GMO-in-a-pet regulatory path is acknowledged but not worked through, and benefit over existing pastes is still unmeasured.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Failures drive redesign: no visible hair change with crude Ker leads to quantitative assays and new candidates; unclear SDS-PAGE plus viscous lysate leads to an inclusion-body hypothesis, GST fusions and 0.1 mM IPTG at 28 C, after which bands appear and P2 is reported as still failing (engineering.txt Cycles 1-2); P1 selected on data then pushed to secretion with OmpA, with heterogeneous cleavage explained and cited. The model is fitted to the team's own BCA time course, and the pH/temperature Gaussian fits were used to choose pH 8 for assays (model.txt sections 3-4). The ODE is honestly reported as fitting worse than the empirical curve (RMSE 25.41 vs 2.12), which is exactly the kind of candour the handbook rewards.
justification.a5: The HEAL (Hear-Engage-Analyze-Learn) loop produces traceable changes, not a contact list: Dr Lin's clinical input reframed the product to daily management and changed the in vitro design to knotted hairball mimics plus a simulated digestion fluid; Professor Wang's advice produced both the tri-enzyme comparison and the alginate encapsulation prototype; a shelter rescuer's account of palatability and volunteer fatigue killed the forced-feeding format in favour of a self-administered jelly; peer and public worry about escape produced the bile-acid CcdA/CcdB switch and GFP reporter (human-practices.txt lines on Dr Lin, Prof Wang, Xiaobabenben, HZAU-China). Informed consent is recorded for interviews and for minor-involved events, and the team repeatedly writes that feedback guided priorities rather than validating the product. Short of 5 only because the most critical voices (regulators, a sceptic on live GMOs in pets) are thinner than the supportive ones.
justification.a6: Outside contributions are named rather than hidden: constructs were synthesised and sequence-verified by a commercial provider, SEM was performed by experts at Shenzhen University, and lab instructors are credited with the inclusion-body discussion (results.txt opening note; engineering.txt Cycle 1 Learn; team.txt lists five instructors and advisors). The Attributions page embeds the official iGEM form (teams.igem.org/wiki/6123/attributions) and the Team page tags each student Wet Lab / Dry Lab / HP, but nowhere on the wiki is there a per-experiment or per-person who-did-what chart of the GreatBay or TAS kind, so I cannot tell which student ran the Folin-phenol series or the kill-switch plating. Honest framing, incomplete granularity, so 3.5 pending the session.
justification.a7: Fifteen registered parts: eight basic (P1, P2, p-Ker, MG1820, MG4907, P-Trx, TrxR, LGOX) and seven composite, including GST solubility fusions, an OmpA-GST-P1 secretion construct and the TcpH-CadC/TcpP-ccdA/ccdB-sfGFP switch (parts.txt, contribution.txt). Several are backed by function data from this team, and the Anderson promoter series J23100/J23102/J23104/J23114 is used properly as a tuning element rather than decoration. Hardware and the Meow Recovery app add standard components in the handbook's wider sense. Not a 5 because the composite modules are characterised separately rather than as an assembled device.
justification.a8: Documentation on the wiki is genuinely good: every figure has a caption, results are written as claim / observation / limitation blocks, fourteen protocols appear on the Experiments page, and the parts and contribution tables give registry codes, sizes, sources and rationale for all fifteen parts. Registry links are present for each part, though parts.igem.org returned 403 to me, so I could not confirm how much data sits on the Registry entries themselves and I have not credited more than the wiki shows. Small defects keep it off 4.5: the parts overview says 'one composite part' in the subtitle and seven in the body, and P2's accession reads 03142.1 on Results but 03141.1 on Parts.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem (swallowed hair, trichobezoars), the gap (existing products move hair rather than degrade it) and the three modules in a few readable lines, with a labelled system schematic and direct routes into Description, Results and Team. The Description page then gives background, a case study and a comparison table of current options before the solution. A reader knows what HEAL is within a minute, which is the Lambert/Patras standard.
justification.w2: Most central claims carry a figure with a control and significance markers, and the team separates measured from modelled explicitly, labelling the ODE and docking work as prediction (model.txt sections 3 and 9). Against that, a few sentences outrun their figures, notably 'The survival of our engineered bacteria through this simulated digestive system verified the success of our prototype design' (results.txt, delivery module), and the delivery group labels are inconsistent between hardware.txt Table 3 and the Results text, so a reader must guess which group is which. Replicate numbers are given for the BCA series and bead sizing but not for the SEM or halo assays.
justification.w3: Navigation is organised as Project / Wet Lab / Dry Lab / Engagement with per-page contents and 'Related evidence' links that lead a judge from Description to Design, Engineering, Results and Safety. Six standard page URLs return 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, software, inclusivity, sustainability); the material largely exists under Hardware, Results and Model, but the handbook asks teams not to make judges hunt, and a judge checking the standard list will hit blanks. Otherwise it is complete rather than sprawling, with the one long page (iHP, ~20k words) kept usable by its activity index.
justification.w4: A future team gets fourteen step-by-step protocols, a 437-page scanned notebook, plasmid maps, parameter tables with sources for the model, a safety page with waste and chemical handling, and a contribution page that offers a five-step framework for characterising environmentally responsive kill switches. What is missing for full reproducibility: the notebook is page images rather than searchable text, no raw numerical data tables accompany the plots, and the model code is referred to but not shown on the wiki.
justification.w5: References are numbered with DOIs and back-links on every major page, prior iGEM work is credited (Folin-phenol method adapted from BNDS-China 2025, TcpP/TcpH adapted from BNDS-China 2025, exchanges with HZAU-China and JLU-NBBMS), and fonts, icons and the site libraries are licensed and credited in the footer. Two lapses pull it off 4.5: the parts and contribution tables credit 'Fan et al., Int. J. Biol. Macromol., 2024' in descriptions of keratinases whose Source column names Jue et al. 2025 or Zhang et al., and several background claims lean on commercial or veterinary-blog pages (PetMD, Vetexchange) where a primary source exists.

J3.one_line: A broad, honestly reported four-module project whose real strengths are failure-driven engineering, a model fitted to the team's own data, and human practices that visibly redirected the design; the core hair-degradation claim remains indirect and the system was never assembled.
strengths: Failure-driven DBTL: the first Ker hair test showed nothing, and instead of burying it the team wrote it up with limitations and switched to quantitative screening (results.txt Stage 1); unclear SDS-PAGE led to a GST-fusion and induction-condition redesign, with P2's continued failure reported (engineering.txt Cycles 1-2).

Controls where function is claimed: deactivated-P1 controls for A280 keratin assays, empty-vector controls on purification gels, 0 vs 30 mM TCA plus dilution series for the kill switch, and letter-coded statistics in the candidate comparison (Figs 12, 13, 22, 23, 28, 33, 36-38).

Modelling tied to the team's own measurements and then used for design: BCA time course fitted for the export rate, pH and temperature Gaussian fits used to set pH 8 for assays, and a frank statement that the ODE fits worse than the empirical curve (RMSE 25.41 vs 2.12).

Human practices with consequences: reframing from emergency rescue to daily management after Dr Lin, the tri-enzyme comparison and alginate encapsulation after Professor Wang, abandoning forced feeding after the shelter rescuer, and the bile-acid kill switch after peer and public concern, all with informed consent recorded.

Careful hedging throughout: 'potential intestinal-support metabolite', 'this does not validate the effectiveness of our enzyme system', and a Safety page section headed 'What remains before real-world use'.
weaknesses: Hair degradation itself is shown only by an A280 proxy and surface morphology; no mass loss, no hairball mimic result on the wiki despite the plan announced after the Dr Lin interview, and no test of an engineered strain degrading hair as a whole system.
The four modules are validated separately and never combined, so the integrated HEAL device remains a design rather than a demonstrated system.
No per-person or per-experiment attribution on the wiki: the Team page gives subteam tags and the Attributions page is only the embedded iGEM form, so which student ran which assay is not visible.
Six standard page URLs return 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, software, inclusivity, sustainability), forcing a judge to find that material under Hardware, Results and Model.

Editing slips that a careful read-through would have caught: template or drafting instructions left in engineering.txt captions ('Each map should identify...', 'The final reporting unit must reflect the normalization actually used'), swapped delivery group labels between Hardware Table 3 and Results, 'one composite part' versus seven on the Parts page, and the P2 accession differing by one digit between pages.
red_flags: Drafting-instruction remnants left in the published text on the Engineering page ('The maps show the Ker construct... Each map should identify the candidate coding sequence, promoter...'; 'The final reporting unit must reflect the normalization actually used'). This reads as an uncleaned AI or template draft rather than misconduct; it is a question for the session about whose voice the page is in, not an accusation, and I have let it weigh only lightly on w5.

Source attribution confusion in the parts tables: descriptions of P2, Keratinase 4907 and Keratinase 1820 credit 'Fan et al.' while the Source column names Jue et al. 2025 or Zhang et al. Likely copy-paste, but it misstates who identified the sequences and should be corrected.
Internal inconsistency in the delivery-module group labels between hardware.txt Table 3 and the Results narrative, which makes the survival result harder to verify than it should be.

I could not reach parts.igem.org (HTTP 403 via CloudFront), so the depth of the fifteen Registry entries is unverified; I scored a8 on the wiki evidence alone and did not assume either rich or stub entries.

Cat hair was collected from animals; the Safety page states the use was confirmed before collection and that animal-welfare advice was sought. Nothing here reaches a whitelist or safety-referral threshold.
pages_read: attributions.txt plus live page check showing the embedded iGEM attributions form
Attempted parts.igem.org entries for BBa_26TUXN4N, BBa_26NOEGF3, BBa_26X192EJ (403, not readable)

calibrated.changed: none. a6 of 3.5 is consistent with Hong Kong JSS: an embedded official form plus named external execution (SEM at Shenzhen University, commercial synthesis and sequencing), but no per-experiment attribution.

one_line.en: A broad four-module project with real controls, honest negative results and a model fitted to its own data, published on a wiki that still carries drafting instructions and a safety page contradicting its own results.
one_line.zh: 四個模組、具備真實對照與誠實陰性結果的廣泛專案，模型以自家數據擬合，但 wiki 仍留有草稿指示，安全頁與結果頁自相矛盾。

strengths: Controlled function data across all four modules, including deactivated-enzyme, empty-vector and no-signal-peptide controls
A real DBTL record where failures drove redesign, from unclear gels to fusion constructs and milder induction
The bile-acid kill switch characterised across four promoter variants and six concentrations, with a stated threshold compared against published environmental levels
A model fitted to the team's own measurements that reports its own failure plainly, plus 14 protocols and a very long notebook
weaknesses: No replicate number or error-bar definition on the Results page although significance markers are used throughout
Keratin degradation is assayed with crude rather than purified enzyme and never quantified as mass lost
The four modules were never operated together, so the system is a design
Constructs were synthesised and assembled commercially and imaging was done by university staff
red_flags: Uncleaned drafting or template instructions left in the published Engineering text
Safety page claims the full enzyme set expresses and degrades keratin, that the circuit functions reliably, and that the enzymes are completely safe to gut mucosa — all beyond the data
Part size and accession inconsistencies between pages
Attributions page is only an embedded form and did not render as readable text

screen.project_title: Uric-acid sensing and degradation in poultry-farm wastewater (HucR sensor + engineered PucLM uricase)
screen.what_they_built: A four-module system: a HucR/HucO uric-acid-responsive mCherry sensor with four promoter architectures, a structure-guided PucLM urate-oxidase variant library, a CRISPR fimH knockout chassis for reduced adhesion, and alginate-bead immobilisation for a fluidised-bed reactor converting uric acid to allantoin.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a (cloning/sensor), BL21(DE3) (expression), K-12 MG1655 (fimH knockout via pEcCas9/pEcgRNA); pUC57 and pET28a backbones. ~27 new BBa_26* parts plus a part-collection page.
screen.best_evidence: /results: HPLC quantification of allantoin production (standard curve R2=0.9899) and uric-acid depletion assays showing E218D and G221A degrading faster than wild-type PucLM with significance marks (P<0.05, P<0.001); purified soluble PucLM and six variants at 78.6 kDa on SDS-PAGE after induction was re-optimised away from inclusion bodies; pHucR-3xHucO dose response over 0-1000 uM uric acid.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: Professor Yao's advice on HucO copy number and insertion position produced the four promoter architectures that were then tested; expert interviews (Dr Li, Dr Shi, Dr Shan) and a water reclamation plant visit shaped the regulatory and deployment framing.
screen.reason: Four coordinated modules all carried to quantitative data — sensor dose response, purified enzyme variants ranked by HPLC product formation, a verified genomic knockout with growth and biofilm controls, and immobilisation tested in a wastewater matrix. Scope, sequencing verification and HP depth put it in the finalist conversation; a full read is needed to check how much of the cloning and HPLC was done by the students versus a service lab.
screen.field_notes: Beijing-HS tackled uric acid, the dominant non-protein nitrogen in poultry wastewater (18-30% of litter nitrogen), with a four-module E. coli system: detection, degradation, biosafety and immobilisation. The sensor used the Deinococcus HucR/HucO MarR regulator driving mCherry across four promoter architectures (pHucR, +1x, 3x and 4x HucO); the 3xHucO design gave the largest endpoint signal and a dose response over 0-1000 uM. For degradation they fused PucL and PucM from B. subtilis, used AlphaFold3 plus pocket analysis to pick six single-site variants (C217S, E218D, G221A, V8L, G11A, L24F), solved an inclusion-body problem by shortening IPTG induction to 10 h at low temperature, purified all seven at 78.6 kDa, and ranked them by uric-acid depletion and by HPLC allantoin production (standard curve R2=0.9899), with E218D best and improved thermostability. Biosafety used pEcCas9/pEcgRNA to delete fimH from MG1655, verified by colony PCR and sequencing, with growth curves showing no proliferation penalty and crystal-violet assays showing a modest biofilm reduction reversed appropriately by 4% D-mannose. Engineered cells were immobilised in sodium alginate beads for a fluidised-bed reactor and tested in a wastewater matrix. Human Practices (9.9k words) includes a public survey, interviews with Drs Li, Shi and Shan, a Gaobeidian water reclamation plant visit and a team exchange; Professor Yao's advice directly produced the HucO copy-number variants that were tested.

screen.project_title: AQUA SHIELD - selective whole-cell biosensors for mercury and lead
screen.what_they_built: Two dual-plasmid E. coli whole-cell biosensors - MerR/PmerT driving GFP for Hg2+ and PbrR/PpbrA driving mCherry for Pb2+ - plus a 3D-printed drone water-sampling rig developed after an unsafe manual sampling attempt.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli TOP10; 20 Registry entries in two collections (MerR reference BBa_26XJNXQ5 and variants E48A/V12E/M143K, PbrR reference BBa_26VNUC25 and a literature variant, fuGFP BBa_26AMB3GV, codon-optimised mCherry BBa_26X8KKP1, B0015-derived terminator, three regulatory composite modules), built on BBa_K346001/K346002 and BBa_I721001/002.
screen.best_evidence: /abstract states both platforms were established in TOP10 and validated by visual observation, fluorescence imaging and microplate-reader measurement, with GFP responding to Hg2+ but not Pb2+ or Cd2+ and mCherry the reverse. The actual figures are inside embedded PDFs on /results, /engineering and /experiments, so no numbers, gels or plots are visible in the page text.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, strongly - a false-positive rapid test on their own river, followed by official testing and a workshop with the kit manufacturer, redirected the project from water treatment to selective detection, and a sampling accident drove the drone build.
screen.reason: The human-practices narrative is the best in this batch - a genuine false positive reframed the whole project - and the drone work is a clean documented failure-to-success engineering cycle. But every wet-lab figure sits inside embedded PDFs rather than on the wiki, the selectivity claim cannot be checked from the page text, and the mutant comparison that is the project's novelty is stated as still running. Not a top-2 read on current evidence.
screen.field_notes: Benenden (Guangzhou campus, Bioremediation village) built AQUA SHIELD, two E. coli TOP10 whole-cell biosensors: MerR-PmerT-GFP for Hg2+ and PbrR-PpbrA-mCherry for Pb2+, each as a dual-plasmid constitutive-regulator plus reporter design, with AI-selected MerR variants (V12E, M143K) benchmarked against the literature E48A mutant. The wet-lab abstract reports both platforms established and cross-selective (GFP to Hg only, mCherry to Pb only) by plate reader, but Results, Engineering and Experiments are PDF embeds, so none of the data is readable on the wiki itself and the mutant screen is described as ongoing until wiki thaw. The strongest documented work is human practices (22k words, closed-loop, SDG targets assessed honestly against what was not demonstrated): a rapid-test kit gave a false positive on the river by their school, the government responded, official testing found nothing, and a workshop with the kit manufacturer explained that the assay responds collectively to Hg, Pb and Cd - this reframed the project around selectivity. A sampling fall into the mud led to a drone sampler: first flight crashed from payload instability, CAD redesign and 3D printing produced an integrated tripod vessel, second flight collected a sample successfully. Contribution registers 20 parts in two collections with careful wording about which claims are validated. Education is 11.7k words; no model page.

screen.project_title: MycoVela: pyomelanin and catalase carrier to protect mycorrhizal fungi in lunar regolith simulant
screen.what_they_built: A proposed calcium-alginate xerogel bead carrying pyomelanin, catalase and trehalose to shield arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi from regolith-generated oxidative stress. Completed work is limited to expressing two bacterial HPPD enzymes (the pyomelanin-precursor step) in E. coli, plus an extensive computational programme.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli KRX (rhamnose-inducible chromosomal T7 polymerase) with two pET-28a(+) HPPD constructs, CNQ36_13270 and SAVERM_5149, inserted between NdeI and XhoI with an N-terminal His tag. No BBa part IDs appear anywhere on the wiki.
screen.best_evidence: SDS-PAGE showing induced target-sized bands in both constructs after correcting induction to 0.2% rhamnose, with ImageJ/BSA densitometry estimating ~8 mg (CNQ36) and ~5 mg (SAVERM) of target-band material in soluble fractions, and Ni-NTA elutions E2/E3 enriched but impure (/results §1). Culture screens report mean ± SD A400 over six replicates: 1.72 ± 0.12 at 30 °C, 1.87 ± 0.13 at 2 mM tyrosine, 1.95 ± 0.19 at 0.05% rhamnose (/results §2). The team states explicitly that A400 is not calibrated pigment mass and that protein identity and catalytic activity remain unconfirmed.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, decisively — Robertas Ursache's review of CIF peptide sulfation and delivery ended their original EndoGate project and moved them to AMF protection; Julie Brisset changed their planned regolith mixtures; Ian Sanders redirected them to moisture and spore germination; Chapman mentors made them replace an oxygen-consumption HPPD assay with HGA detection.
screen.reason: The modelling and Human Practices are the best in this batch — a Bayesian dose-response model validated by deliberately breaking the Hill equation to prove convergence checks were insufficient, 400 simulation-based calibration runs, identifiability analysis that reshaped the measurement panel — and the wiki's honesty about scope is exemplary. But the Project section turns on whether the project worked, and nothing here does yet: no AMF experiment was performed at all, pigment identity and recovered mass were never established, HPPD activity was never assayed, catalase and the carrier exist only as designs, and no parts were contributed to the Registry. By the handbook's rule that a claim without data does not count as working, aspects 2, 7 and 8 are too weak for a finalist slot regardless of the dry-lab quality.
screen.field_notes: BGCFullerton / Team Genesis (Space village, USA) proposed MycoVela, a calcium-alginate xerogel carrying pyomelanin, catalase and trehalose to protect arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi establishing with plants in lunar regolith simulant. Wet-lab work, split between Chapman University and UC Irvine, covered only the pyomelanin precursor step: two HPPD constructs (CNQ36_13270, SAVERM_5149) in E. coli KRX, where an initial IPTG attempt failed because KRX needs rhamnose, after which 0.2% rhamnose gave target-sized bands (stronger in insoluble fractions), ~8 and ~5 mg soluble target-band material by BSA densitometry, and partially enriched Ni-NTA elutions. Three separate A400 screens (n=6) selected 30 °C, 2 mM tyrosine and 0.05% rhamnose, never tested in combination. The dry lab is far more developed: a six-ODE oxidative-stress model with 34 parameters, a sensitivity/identifiability analysis that showed root-contact density was unobservable and cut the measurement panel to germination, hyphal length and peroxide, and a Bayesian dose-response model whose validation included deliberately corrupting the Hill denominator — the broken model passed every convergence check (R-hat 1.0018, zero divergences) but failed parameter recovery, estimating a 20 mg/plant protection EC50 as 86.6. They added parameter recovery and 400 SBC runs as required checks.
