Other outputs: MycoLens microscopy software, a 10-page R. irregularis white-list proposal reviewed by UVA iGEM, a 24-page children's picture book distributed in Vea, Ghana, and 19 public lesson decks. Over forty documented stakeholder conversations, two of which killed earlier project directions. No Registry parts, an Experiments page of three words, and a bare-link Attributions page.

screen.project_title: BioH2 — metabolic engineering of a wild-isolated Clostridium beijerinckii for dark-fermentative hydrogen, with byproduct valorisation
screen.what_they_built: Established an electroporation transformation system for a non-model, environmentally isolated C. beijerinckii strain S63, overexpressed HydA and PFOR candidates in it, attempted a CRISPR thl knockout, and added a spent-broth-to-Bacillus biofertiliser loop after industry feedback.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Clostridium beijerinckii S63 (wild isolate from Yundonghai Wetland Park, provided and genome-sequenced by the supervisor), pNICKclos2.0 backbone; E. coli for cloning; B. subtilis 941 for valorisation. 23 Registry parts, mostly native promoter/CDS/terminator triples for three HydA and two PFOR candidates plus thl-editing components.
screen.best_evidence: /project/results.html: gas chromatography of 72 h fermentations gave H2 volume fraction 40.20 ± 3.45% for parental S63 versus 44.48% (S1-2, HydA-01163), 44.36% (S6-2), 41.14% (S67), 45.00% (S84-2, PFOR-02384) and 46.92% (S18, PFOR-02718), mean ± SD with n = 2. HPLC of the parental strain quantified five organic acids (butyrate 14.797 mM, acetate 9.425 mM, ~90.6% of the total).
screen.hp_integration: Strongly. Industry interviews (CGN engineers, a hydrogen-utilisation manager, a Changzhou field trip) plus their own break-even arithmetic — ¥3,000/t glucose and ¥40/kg H2 would need 6.70 mol H2/mol glucose against a 4.0 theoretical ceiling — convinced them a hydrogen-only system cannot pay, and they added spent-broth valorisation to B. subtilis biofertiliser and repositioned around distributed production.
screen.reason: Genuinely good engineering of a hard, non-model anaerobe — three DBTL cycles ending in a working anaerobic-chamber electroporation protocol is a real achievement, and the economic reasoning that killed their own hydrogen-only premise is unusually mature. But the headline result is a 4–7 percentage-point change in H2 volume fraction at n = 2, with no yield or rate measurement, no expression verification of the overexpressed genes, the thl knockout never assembled, the 23 parts largely uncharacterised native sequences, and several wiki pages still marked under construction. Not top-2 evidence.
screen.field_notes: BGI-College (CHN, Biomanufacturing village) engineered Clostridium beijerinckii S63, a hydrogen-producing strain their supervisor Dr. Yingshan Li isolated from Yundonghai Wetland Park in Foshan and whole-genome sequenced (single 5,870,246 bp chromosome). The team's real engineering achievement is the transformation system: three DBTL cycles, the first two failing (published Clostridium protocols, then systematic sweeps of OD600, voltage 600–1800 V, cell volume and cuvette gap, all yielding no colonies), the third succeeding after Dr. Youduo Wu advised moving the electroporator inside the anaerobic chamber. With it they introduced three HydA and two PFOR overexpression constructs into S63. GC on 72 h sealed-bottle fermentations gave H2 fractions of 44.48%, 44.36%, 41.14% (HydA) and 46.92%, 45.00% (PFOR) against 40.20 ± 3.45% for the parent, n = 2, reported honestly as a modest trend with no yield or rate claim and no verification that the genes were expressed. The CRISPR thl knockout failed: all four Gibson fragments amplified and sequence-verified, but no correct clone was ever recovered, and the team lists assembly inefficiency, junction architecture and plasmid instability as undistinguished hypotheses. Modeling is simple stoichiometry (Y = 4f_acetate + 2f_butyrate, with an idealised 90% acetate case giving 3.60 mol H2/mol glucose) plus a conceptual electron-supply constraint and an interactive visual interface offered as a contribution. HPLC quantified five organic acids in the parental broth. A techno-economic argument — glucose at ¥3,000/t against H2 at ¥40/kg requires 6.70 mol H2/mol glucose, above the 4.0 biochemical ceiling — drove the pivot to co-production, and spent broth supported B. subtilis 941 to roughly 7x10^8–1x10^9 CFU/mL, a number the team flags as unreliable because the countable plates held 7 and 1 colonies. 23 Registry parts, mostly native promoter/CDS/terminator sets; three PFOR parts were withdrawn after the iGEM safety committee flagged candidate PFOR-00042. Attribution is given as a fine-grained per-role contributor table. Proof-of-concept, collaborations and several other pages are placeholder stubs reading 'under construction'.

screen.project_title: PyrLac Glow — dual-biomarker lactate/pyruvate fluorescent screening platform for early cancer detection
screen.what_they_built: Two ratiometric biosensors made by inserting YFP into the E. coli transcription regulators LldR (L-lactate) and PdhR (pyruvate), screened as 5+5 insertion-site variants, plus a portable fluorescence reader prototype. The readout is the F485/F420 ratio, with the lactate/pyruvate pair used to separate tumour metabolism from benign lactate rises.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli Rosetta(DE3) with pRSETA (6xHis), plus 293T transfection for live-cell work; 33 new BBa parts registered (full-length PdhR/LldR/YFP backbones, split/variant fragments, YFP-insertion composites) listed on /parts (694 words).
screen.best_evidence: /results §4.1: purified L4 and P2 give 4-PL dose-response fits (L4 EC50 3.101 mM, Hill 1.413, R2 0.9613; P2 EC50 49.65 uM, Hill 1.192, R2 0.9175) over 0-30 mM lactate and 0-1000 uM pyruvate, with three biological and three technical replicates; §4.3 shows orthogonal specificity against glucose, citrate, malate and PEP, and §4.4 reproduces the dose response in commercial artificial plasma.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — 16 stakeholder interviews across five staged rounds plus 208- and 113-response surveys, with /human-practices and /hardware stating that expert and clinician feedback drove the hardware requirement set and the shift to a grassroots pre-screening positioning; the closed loop is asserted per stage rather than always pinned to a specific construct change.
screen.reason: Real purified-protein data with replicates, fitted standard curves, specificity controls, a plasma matrix test and live-cell work, on top of a 33-part Registry library and three honest DBTL cycles (first-round cloning failure diagnosed and fixed). Deep staged IHP. Main open questions for a full read are attribution (no /attributions page at all; plasmids commercially synthesised, sequencing outsourced) and a hardware prototype that has not yet made a quantitative measurement.
screen.field_notes: Bist-China (Oncology, CHN) built PyrLac Glow, a pair of allosteric YFP-insertion biosensors for L-lactate (LldR) and pyruvate (PdhR) aimed at Warburg-effect-based early cancer pre-screening in primary-care settings. Insertion sites were chosen by an AlphaFold2 + GROMACS RMSF/B-factor screen, giving five variants per sensor (L1-L5, P1-P5), all cloned into pRSETA, expressed in Rosetta(DE3) and Ni-NTA purified with SDS-PAGE shown for every variant. L4 and P2 were selected and characterised by 4-PL dose response (EC50 3.101 mM and 49.65 uM; R2 0.9613 and 0.9175), 1-17 min kinetics, pH 7.0-8.0 and 20-40 C stability, metabolite specificity panels, artificial-plasma dose response and 293T transfection. Thirty-three BBa parts were submitted and organised as basic/split-variant/composite categories. Human practices ran five stages with 16 interviews and two surveys (208 and 113 responses) and fed a portable rotating-disk fluorimeter (Arduino control, Streamlit interface) whose mechanical, optical and electronic workflow is validated but which does not yet quantify metabolites. There is no attributions page and no measurement page, and the plasmids were commercially synthesised, so the student-versus-outside split is not documented.

justification.a1: Two genetically encoded sensors were actually built and characterised: five-site insertion libraries (L1-L5, P1-P5) cloned, expressed, purified, screened, then the winners (L4, P2) taken through dose-response, kinetics, pH/temperature, specificity, artificial plasma and 293T live-cell imaging (Results §2-4; Engineering Cycles 1-2). A portable 16-well rotary fluorometer was also built and bench-tested (Hardware §5). It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS top anchor because the chain stops before the two halves meet: the Hardware page itself states quantitative metabolite detection is 'planned for future iterations', and no real or clinical sample was ever measured.
justification.a2: This is the team's strongest aspect. Fig. 13-17 (Results) show F485/F420 ratios across lactate 0-30 mM and pyruvate 0-1000 microM with error bars, with the 420 nm channel as a flat internal reference, three biological and three technical replicates stated, and 4-PL fits (L4 EC50 3.10 mM; P2 EC50 49.65 microM). SDS-PAGE uses uninduced lanes as negative controls (Fig. 7-10); specificity was tested against pyruvate, PEP-K, malate, glucose and citrate (Fig. 13, 20); 293T imaging has Con vs +Lac/+Pyr panels. Held back from 4.5 by unresolved numbers (P2 R2 is 0.9175 on Results but 0.9975 on Engineering; L4 0.9613 vs 0.9913 in the Cycle 3 table), no statistics or n on the plasma curves ('data points represent technical replicates'), and the central cancer-screening claim resting on the simulated three-sample table in Cycle 3, which the team does label as 'not experimental data'.
justification.a3: The problem framing is quantified (GLOBOCAN 2022 figures, Table 1-2 in Description) and the use case is shaped by real stakeholders: community health staff, oncologists and an HR director set a sub-1000 RMB price ceiling and three deployment scenarios (Human Practices Stages 1, 3, 4). But the impact is not yet demonstrated from the team's own data: the 5 mM / 200 microM thresholds come from literature ranges, and the Description's own limitations table concedes 'Thresholds not clinically calibrated' and 'Artificial plasma is not real blood'. No real blood, patient sample or field-like run exists, which is where TAS's wastewater test earns a 5.
justification.a4: Three DBTL cycles are laid out with explicit engineering questions before testing (Engineering, Cycles 1-3). The genuine data-driven design loop is computational site prediction (AlphaFold2, GROMACS RMSF/B-factor, weighted scoring on the Model page) feeding a five-variant library whose fluorescence screening selected L4 and P2 - a real design-test-select cycle. The cloning iteration (first round failed, YFP insert doubled and ligation extended to 2 h) is honest but is troubleshooting, not redesign, and Cycle 3 explicitly 'does not involve new molecular construction or wet experiments'. The hardware iteration (CMOS to photoresistor, single to dual excitation, module integration) is documented with triggers on the Hardware design tracker.
justification.a5: Sixteen interviews across clinicians, a pathologist, industry scientists, a public health expert, insurance and HR, plus a 208-response public survey, are organised into five stages, each with a 'Why we talked / What we learned / What we changed' structure (Human Practices). The changes are concrete and traceable into the science: the pathologist's warning about benign lactate elevation is what killed the single-lactate design and produced the dual-biomarker scheme; the clinician interview set the 'tolerate false positives, minimise false negatives' rule; community staff feedback killed the home self-test positioning. The team also names its own survey's urban/female sampling bias. This is responsive, two-way HP at the level the handbook rewards.
justification.a6: The attributions page returns 404 (https://2026.igem.wiki/bist-china/attributions), so the handbook's required statement of who did what is simply absent, and the Team page gives only student and advisor carousels (12 students, 7 advisors) plus an AI-usage declaration naming section fact-checkers. The work shown is heavy for a high school team - commercial plasmid synthesis and Sanger sequencing (declared in Results §2.2), Rosetta expression, Ni-NTA purification, GROMACS MD, and CaCl2 transfection of 293T cells - and nothing on the wiki tells me which of these the students ran themselves versus a host lab or the advisors. I am scoring the documentation gap, not alleging outsourcing; a task-level chart like TAS Taipei's would move this score substantially.
justification.a7: This is squarely synthetic biology with standard components: 33 parts are registered (Parts page), split into full-length basics (YFP BBa_26HDAZCW, PdhR BBa_26OKC42U, LldR BBa_26S2KNZ1), ten N/C split fragments per regulator, and ten composite N-fragment-YFP-C-fragment fusion sensors, assembled by a unified scheme with a shared ATSDNVYI linker. The composites are genuine engineered devices expressed in E. coli Rosetta (DE3) and re-used in a CMV eukaryotic context. It is a new-part-heavy library rather than new plus reuse of existing Registry parts, and the modularity is internal to the team's own scheme.
justification.a8: Registry entries carry real content, not just sequences: BBa_26JKE6ZJ (LldR4) has an 18 kB experiment document with design rationale, primer table, both cloning rounds including the failed first round, SDS-PAGE and purification figures, the 4-PL fit, kinetics, specificity, plasma and 293T data, plus a separate design document with the patent-derived site rationale, and chassis fields are filled (E. coli BL21, DH5-alpha). The wiki pages are clear and internally linked. Two deductions: the attributions standard page is missing, and the Registry documentation repeats some mislabelled captions (a lactate figure captioned 'Fig.9 Fluorescence ratio response of P2 sensor against lactate gradient', a pH/temperature figure for L4 captioned as P2).
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem (late diagnosis), the signature (Warburg effect, bidirectional lactate/pyruvate), the solution (two YFP biosensors plus a portable reader) and the decision rule (5 mM / 200 microM, four regions) within the first screens, with an interactive classifier and a 3D reader model. The Description abstract repeats this cleanly. Minor drift: the homepage sells 'PyrLac Glow integrates two fluorescent biosensors with a portable, low-cost reader', while the Hardware page says the reader has not yet measured the biosensors.
justification.w2: Most key claims have a figure with a legend, a control and stated replicates: induced vs uninduced SDS-PAGE, the 420 nm reference channel, six-metabolite interference panels, Con vs treated 293T images, error bars defined as SD of biological replicates. Where evidence is absent the team mostly says so - the Cycle 3 scenario table is flagged 'not experimental data' and the Hardware signal-to-blank ratio is explicitly not called an SNR. Points off for the conflicting R2 values between Results and Engineering and for the plasma curves resting on technical replicates only.
justification.w3: Navigation is short and predictable (Project / Wet Lab / Engagement), every long page carries an on-this-page outline, and the standard URLs that exist are in place. Friction: attributions, measurement, proof-of-concept and implementation all 404, so a judge looking for attribution or measurement content has nowhere to land; protocols in fact live on Experiments but nothing on the 404 tells you that. Several pages are very long (Engineering 7.4 k words, Contribution 11 k), which pushes against 'complete but not sprawling'.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way: Experiments gives full protocols with volumes, temperatures and cycle numbers; the Notebook (7.2 k words) carries day-level records; primer tables are printed in full; the failed first cloning round is reported rather than hidden; the Hardware page offers component selection and open-source design files. What is missing for full reproduction is raw numeric data (only plotted ratios are given) and the attribution/measurement context, so another team would have to re-derive the fits from the figures.
justification.w5: Every content page ends with a numbered reference list and claims in the Description and Engineering backgrounds are cited inline (GLOBOCAN, Vander Heiden 2009, Aguilera 2008 for LldR, Ogasawara 2007 for PdhR), and the Model/Registry design documents credit patent CN113004420A as the source of the insertion hotspot. Two things I would want checked rather than assumed: in the Registry LldR4 document, ref [5] 'Gao Y, et al. Structural insights into the lactate-sensing mechanism of LldR, J Biol Chem 2020;295(12):3892-3904' did not resolve for me, and ref [6] (Baird et al., a DsRed oligomerisation paper) is cited for YFP microenvironment sensitivity. No prior iGEM team is credited for method inheritance even though the Contribution page reviews dozens of them.

J1.one_line: A genuinely strong high-school wet-lab project - two YFP-insertion biosensors built, screened and characterised with controls, replicates and 4-PL fits in buffer, artificial plasma and 293T cells, backed by unusually responsive human practices - held back by a missing attributions page, a reader that has never been run with the sensors, and a cancer-screening claim demonstrated only on simulated samples.
strengths: Real function data with proper controls: induced vs uninduced SDS-PAGE, a flat 420 nm internal reference channel, three biological and three technical replicates, error bars, 4-PL fits with stated EC50 and Hill values (Results Fig. 13-17).
Orthogonal specificity actually tested, not asserted: L4 and P2 each challenged with pyruvate, PEP-K, malate, glucose and citrate across wide gradients (Results Fig. 13, 20; Engineering Fig. 28).
Escalating validation levels - HEPES buffer, commercial artificial plasma, then transient expression in 293T with Con vs +Lac / +Pyr image panels and time-course kinetics (Results 4.4-4.5).

Honest reporting of failure: the first cloning round is shown failing (colony PCR ~750 bp instead of ~1500 bp, vector self-ligation) with the specific fix (double the insert, 2 h ligation) and the successful second round (Engineering Build 1).

Human practices that changed the science - the pathologist interview is what replaced the single-lactate design with the dual-biomarker scheme, and community staff feedback removed the home self-test scenario (Human Practices Stages 1-2).

Substantive Registry documentation: BBa_26JKE6ZJ carries a full experiment write-up with figures, primers, fits and a separate design document citing the patent-derived insertion hotspot, plus declared chassis.
The wiki labels its own gaps - the Cycle 3 three-sample table is marked 'not experimental data' and the Hardware page calls its ratio a signal-to-blank metric rather than an SNR.
weaknesses: The attributions page 404s, and nothing elsewhere says which tasks the students performed versus advisors or a host lab - the single biggest drag on aspect 6.
The portable reader has never been run with the biosensors; Hardware section 5.3 uses diluted YFP and a water blank only, while the homepage presents the integrated platform as the product.

The dual-threshold decision rule (5 mM / 200 microM) is validated only against three invented scenarios; no real blood, patient or even spiked-serum sample was measured, so the screening claim is unproven.
Conflicting goodness-of-fit numbers: P2 R2 is 0.9175 on Results but 0.9975 on Engineering, and L4 is 0.9613 on Results but 0.9913 in the Cycle 3 comparison table.
Several gel panels (e.g. Results Fig. 2-4 / Engineering Fig. 2) show ladders without printed size marks and plate photographs rather than labelled lanes; only one later gel carries bp annotations.
Artificial plasma dose-response is described as technical replicates, with no n, no biological replication and no statistics anywhere on the site.
Cycle 3 adds no new experiment - it re-integrates Cycle 1 and 2 data, so the third DBTL loop is analytical rather than iterative.
Page lengths are heavy (Engineering 7.4 k words, Contribution an 11 k-word general review of iGEM biosensors) relative to the evidence they add.
red_flags: Attributions standard page returns 404; no task-level attribution anywhere on the wiki (handbook p.25-26).
Measurement, proof-of-concept and implementation standard pages also 404.

A high school team transfecting HEK-293T human embryonic kidney cells (Results 4.5; Safety page describes it as a commercial immortalised line in a BSL-1 lab). I do not decide whitelist questions myself - this is one I would send to safety@igem.org for confirmation.

In the Registry LldR4 documentation, reference [5] (Gao Y et al., J Biol Chem 2020;295(12):3892-3904 on LldR lactate sensing) did not resolve when I looked for it, and reference [6] is a DsRed oligomerisation paper cited for YFP microenvironment sensitivity. I am not calling this fabrication; it needs checking with the team before any conclusion.
Internally inconsistent R2 values for the same fits between the Results and Engineering pages.
Several Registry figure captions are mismatched (a lactate curve captioned as the P2 sensor; an L4 pH/temperature panel captioned as P2).
pages_read: https://2026.igem.wiki/bist-china/results (plus figure images r3, r13 from static.igem.wiki)
Registry: BBa_26JKE6ZJ (LldR4) incl. full documentation, BBa_26XHW854 (PdhR2), BBa_26HDAZCW (YFP), BBa_26OKC42U (PdhR)

calibrated.changed: none. a8 4.0 rests on Registry documents I could actually read (an 18 kB experiment document with both cloning rounds, the failed first round included, plus a design document), which outweighs the missing attributions page; a6 2.5 is the no-task-attribution floor, and it matters more here because the workload includes 293T transfection, Ni-NTA purification and GROMACS MD with no statement of who performed them.

justification.a1: Scope is large for a high school team and the steps get progressively harder: a computational insertion-site screen, ten YFP-insertion variants of LldR and PdhR built and purified, full characterisation of the two winners (L4, P2), artificial-plasma and 293T live-cell tests, 33 parts submitted, a 3D-printed rotary 16-well reader, and five stages of IHP (Results §2-4; Engineering Cycles 1-3; Hardware §5). It falls short of GreatBay level only because the chain stops before the two halves meet: the reader was validated with a commercial YFP standard, not with L4 or P2 (Hardware §5.3.1), and no real biological sample was ever measured.
justification.a2: The main molecular function is shown with data, not claimed: ratiometric dose-response for all ten variants (Results Fig. 13-16), 4-PL fits for L4 (EC50 3.101 mM) and P2 (EC50 49.65 microM) (Fig. 17), kinetics to a 12-17 min plateau (Fig. 18-19), pH 7.0-8.0 and 20-40 C stability, a six-metabolite interference panel showing orthogonality (Fig. 20), artificial plasma (Fig. 21-22) and 293T imaging with untreated controls (Fig. 23-24). Controls are present (uninduced lanes in Fig. 7-10, water blank on hardware, buffer-only wells) and three replicates are stated. What is not shown: any real plasma or patient sample, and the cancer-screening claim itself rests on a simulated three-row table in Engineering Test 3, labelled by the team as not experimental data.
justification.a3: The deployment route is concrete and stakeholder-checked rather than generic: community screening, corporate physicals and high-risk follow-up, with household self-testing explicitly abandoned after the Cuiyuan community health centre interview, a price anchor below 1000 RMB (200 RMB for corporate screening), a sub-30-minute turnaround and a named NMPA pathway (HP Stages 1, 3, 4; Hardware §Future 5). It is held to 3.5 because the impact case is argued, not tested: thresholds are admitted to need clinical calibration on large sample sets (Description Table 6), artificial plasma is not blood, and the device has no biology in it yet.
justification.a4: Several cycles genuinely changed the next build. First-round cloning failed with self-ligation and short colony-PCR products, so insert mass was doubled and ligation extended from 1 h to 2 h, and all L1-L5 and P1-P5 then came up (Results §2.2, Fig. 3-4) - redesign, not just repetition. The MD/scoring model picked the sites that were actually built, kinetics set the 15 min read point and pH 7.4/30 C assay conditions that the hardware then adopted, and on the hardware side the curved light channel was removed, the servo-disk connector was re-cut through CAD iterations, and adding the 520/20 nm filter was justified by a measured signal-to-blank improvement from ~4.1x to ~10.6x (Hardware §5.3.3). Cycle 3 is a re-analysis of Cycles 1-2 with no new build, and the model was never refit against the measured data, which keeps this off 5.
justification.a5: This is the strongest aspect. Sixteen interviews and two questionnaires (208 and 113 responses) are organised in five stages, each with a Why we talked / What we learned / What we changed block, and the changes are real design changes: the pathologist's warning about benign lactate elevation is what killed the single-marker design and produced the dual-biomarker architecture; Erika Ferreri's input removed cancer-risk conclusions from the device output in favour of raw concentrations plus QC status; the cancer-survivor and oncologist interviews repositioned the tool as risk pre-screening with a stated false-negative priority. It is reflective and responsive in the handbook's sense, not outreach relabelled. Short of 5 because the questionnaire sample bias (78% female, 92% urban) is acknowledged but never corrected.
justification.a6: There is no attributions page: https://2026.igem.wiki/bist-china/attributions returns 404, and the Team page gives 12 students, 7 advisors and a detailed AI-usage statement but no who-did-what for the laboratory, modelling or hardware work. Some outsourcing is declared in the text (commercial full-length plasmid synthesis, commercial Sanger sequencing - Results §2.2), which is fine, but the 100 ns GROMACS apo/holo simulations, the 293T transfection work and the purification series carry no statement of who executed them. With the handbook's rule that attribution is read from the team page form, I can only score what is there.
justification.a7: The project is squarely synthetic biology - allosteric transcription factors LldR and PdhR repurposed as fluorescent reporters - and 33 parts are listed with BBa IDs in a deliberately modular scheme: full-length backbones, ten split N/C fragments per regulator, and ten composite N-fragment-YFP-C-fragment sensors sharing one ATSDNVYI linker (Parts page). That is a reusable collection by design. I could not reach parts.igem.org to check documentation depth (403 from this network), and the handbook says parts are judged on the Registry, so I cannot credit characterisation I only saw on the wiki; no existing BioBricks are reused in the build either.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely rebuildable: full protocols with volumes, cycles and buffer concentrations (Experiments), a six-week dated notebook, the complete scoring-model specification with weights, constraints and the top-20 residue table (Model §2.3-2.4), and every results figure captioned lane by lane. Against that, Registry page depth is unverified (see a7), the proof-of-concept, measurement and implementation standard pages are 404, and there is an internal inconsistency a reader cannot resolve: Results gives L4 R2 = 0.9613 and P2 R2 = 0.9175, while Engineering Cycle 3 reports 0.9913 and 0.9975 for the same fits.
justification.w1: The home page states the aim in a few lines - a portable dual-biomarker platform reading lactate and pyruvate, with the bidirectional-versus-unidirectional logic that justifies using two markers - and the Description abstract repeats it precisely. After those two pages I can state the aim, the chassis (E. coli for expression, pRSETA vector), the recognition elements and the decision thresholds, which is what this aspect asks for.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim on the Results and Engineering pages is tied to a numbered figure with a caption naming lanes, controls and error bars, and the hardware section reports actual ADC values with SD and n = 3. Two things keep it at 4: the headline screening claim is supported by a simulated scenario table rather than measurement, and the R2 values disagree between Results and Engineering Cycle 3 for the same curves.
justification.w3: Navigation is consistent and the on-this-page index on every long page makes a 7,400-word Engineering page tractable; the interactive four-region threshold tool and the exploded 3D hardware viewer are well placed rather than decorative. Marked down because four standard pages (attributions, proof-of-concept, measurement, implementation) return 404, so a judge following the standard menu hits dead ends, and the Contribution page is a 11,000-word review that buries whatever the actual contribution is.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of this: protocols with concrete parameters, a dated notebook, the full computational pipeline including software used at each stage (ColabFold, SwissDock, GROMACS, FreeSASA, PyMOL), a component list with costs, and an honest limitations table mapping each gap to a next step (Description Table 6; Hardware roadmap). It is long in places - the Contribution review in particular is sprawling rather than complete - which is why it is not higher.
justification.w5: Each page carries a numbered reference list used in-text, including the lactate and pyruvate reference ranges, the patent CN113004420A that the LldR insertion sites were remapped from, and an adapted Warburg figure credited to its source. Spot-checked references (Vander Heiden 2009 Science; Aguilera 2008 J Bacteriol; Ogasawara 2007 J Bacteriol) are real and say what the wiki says they say. Some wiki-generated figures and the AI-assisted schematic in Hardware Fig. 1 are credited only loosely.

J2.one_line: A genuinely well-executed pair of allosteric YFP biosensors with real characterisation data and outstanding human practices, let down by a missing attributions page and by a reader that has never been run with the team's own proteins.
strengths: Ten LldR-YFP and PdhR-YFP insertion variants were actually built, expressed, purified and compared, with uninduced controls on every SDS-PAGE (Results Fig. 7-12) and the two winners (L4, P2) selected on measured ratiometric data rather than assertion.

Characterisation goes well beyond a single curve: 4-PL fits, 1-17 min kinetics, pH and temperature series, a six-metabolite orthogonality panel, artificial-plasma matrix tests and 293T live-cell imaging with untreated controls.
A real cloning failure is reported and fixed by a specific parameter change (insert doubled, ligation 1 h to 2 h), which is a DBTL cycle rather than troubleshooting (Results Fig. 3-4).

Human practices drives design decisions that are visible in the project: the pathologist interview is what replaced the single-lactate design with the dual-biomarker one, and Erika Ferreri's input stripped risk conclusions out of the device output.

Hardware decisions are backed by measurement: the 520/20 nm filter is justified by a signal-to-blank improvement from ~4.1x to ~10.6x with stated SD and n = 3, and the team states plainly that the ~59 ADC water blank is still too high.
weaknesses: No attributions page exists (404), and the Team page gives no who-did-what for the lab, modelling or hardware work, so the division of labour between 12 students, 7 advisors and commercial services cannot be assessed.

The reader was validated with a commercial YFP standard, never with L4 or P2 (Hardware §5.3.1), so the sample-to-result platform the home page presents is two validated halves rather than one working system.

The screening performance claim rests on a three-row table of simulated concentrations (Engineering Test 3), which the team labels as not experimental data; no real plasma or patient sample was measured and the 5 mM / 200 microM thresholds are taken from literature, not fitted.
Internal inconsistency in reported fit quality: L4 R2 = 0.9613 and P2 R2 = 0.9175 on the Results page versus 0.9913 and 0.9975 for the same fits in Engineering Cycle 3.

Parts documentation could not be verified on the Registry from here, and several standard pages (proof-of-concept, measurement, implementation) are 404, so content a judge is directed to look for is not where the handbook expects it.
red_flags: No attributions page (https://2026.igem.wiki/bist-china/attributions returns 404). Not an integrity issue, but it leaves aspect 6 unevidenced and I would raise it with the team.

The project uses HEK-293T human cells for transfection work (Safety page; Results §4.5). High school teams work within the iGEM Whitelist, which excludes activities involving human samples and organisms above BSL-1. A commercially sourced immortalised line may well be permitted, but I cannot determine that from the wiki and would ask safety@igem.org for a determination rather than assume either way. This is a question, not an allegation.

Same 4-PL fits reported with different R2 values on two pages (0.9613/0.9175 in Results vs 0.9913/0.9975 in Engineering Cycle 3). Most likely a transcription error, but it should be reconciled before the data are cited.

parts.igem.org returned 403 from this network, so none of the 33 claimed Registry entries could be inspected. The parts are listed with BBa IDs on the wiki; the panel should re-check Registry depth before finalising aspects 7 and 8.

The Team page declares substantial AI assistance including AI-generated banner images, flowcharts and one hardware schematic (Hardware Fig. 1B, credited as AI-assisted). The declaration is unusually complete and transparent and no evidence figure appears AI-generated; I note it only because the panel should be aware it was disclosed.
pages_read: proof-of-concept / measurement / implementation / software / entrepreneurship / inclusivity / sustainability / design / protocols (all 404)

calibrated.changed: w3 4.0->3.5: four standard pages 404 (attributions, proof-of-concept, measurement, implementation) plus an 11,000-word Contribution review; I applied 3.5 to squirrel-beijing and basis-china for the same thing, so 4.0 here was soft.

justification.a1: PyrLac Glow climbs through several genuinely harder steps in one season: computational insertion-site screening of LldR and PdhR, a ten-variant fusion library, expression and purification of all ten, selection of L4 and P2, characterisation in buffer, artificial plasma and 293T cells, then a 3D-printed rotary 16-well reader and a dual-threshold interpretation tool (Description, Results, Model, Hardware). It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS level mainly because the two halves never meet: the reader was validated with a commercial YFP standard and water, not with L4 or P2 (Hardware 5.3), so the integrated platform remains a promise.
justification.a2: The core claim, that two insertion variants respond specifically and quantitatively to their ligands, is backed by real measurement: 4PL fits for L4 (EC50 3.10 mM) and P2 (EC50 49.65 microM), kinetic plateaus by 12 min, pH 7.0-8.0 and 20-40 C stability, a six-metabolite interference panel showing orthogonal responses, dose-response retained in artificial plasma, and live-cell traces with untransfected background controls, all stated as three biological and three technical replicates (Results 4.1-4.5). Marked down because key numbers disagree between pages: Results gives L4 R2 = 0.9613 and P2 R2 = 0.9175, while Engineering Test 3 and Learn 3 give 0.9913 and 0.9975, and the P2 live-cell dose is 200 microM in the Results text but 1 mM in the Fig. 24 caption.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by people who would use it, not just literature: an oncologist, a pathologist, community health staff who described 3-7 day external-lab report cycles, and a physical-examination administrator (Human Practices Stages 1-4), and the team names three deployment scenarios while dropping household self-testing. But nothing has been tested in a real setting: no real blood, no clinical samples, thresholds admitted to be uncalibrated (Description Table 6), and the team honestly says the device would need NMPA-type validation (Hardware 6).
justification.a4: Three DBTL cycles with at least one real failure-to-redesign: first-round cloning gave vector self-ligation and short colony-PCR products, with colonies only in L1-L3 and P5, which the team diagnosed as insufficient insert and imbalanced stoichiometry, then doubled the insert and extended ligation to 2 h, after which all ten groups produced correct clones (Results 2.2). Hardware shows the same habit at the bench, with three printed servo-connector versions and two Y-tube versions before the disk stayed engaged (Hardware Phase II). Cycle 3 is weaker: it integrates existing curves and specificity data rather than building and testing something new.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the project. Sixteen interviews and two surveys (208 and 113 valid responses) each end in a labelled 'What we changed', and the changes are real and traceable: pathologist and oncologist interviews led the team to abandon lactate alone for the lactate-plus-pyruvate pair that defines the whole project; Erika Ferreri's input turned the device into a professional-use instrument reporting concentrations and QC status rather than a risk verdict; Dr Liu's point about exercise and diet pushed them to measurement rather than diagnosis (Human Practices Stages 1-3, Hardware Phase I). They report their survey's urban, female, young skew, and they decline advice with reasons (short-video outreach, full multi-language support), which is the reflection step most teams skip. Short of 5 because no consent or ethics oversight is mentioned anywhere, including the 30-student pre/post awareness study.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page at all: the standard URL returns 404, and no page says which student ran which experiment, or what the PI, host laboratory or advisors contributed beyond the Safety page's description of PI approval and supervision. Some outside work is disclosed honestly (pRSETA-LldR and pRSETA-PdhR commercially synthesised, Sanger sequencing commercial, Arduino code AI-assisted), and the Team page's AI-usage statement is unusually candid and names the students who fact-checked each section, but 100 ns GROMACS simulations, Ni-NTA purification and 293T transfection are attributed to no one. By my own rule, work I cannot attribute caps this at 3; the missing standard page pulls it to 2.5, and it is a session question rather than an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is squarely synthetic biology built from defined, reusable components: a split-and-insert scheme with a common ATSDNVYI linker applied uniformly to two GntR-family regulators, three full-length basic parts, twenty split-fragment basic parts and ten YFP-inserted composite parts, all carrying BBa IDs (Parts page). Two composite parts, LldR4 and PdhR2, are shown to function. The design reuses well-chosen natural elements and a published patent's insertion hotspots rather than inventing chemistry, which is appropriate, and the reader and Streamlit layer add standard components around them.
justification.a8: On-wiki documentation is good: every figure has a caption naming lanes and controls, the Experiments page gives full protocols with volumes and temperatures, and the Notebook runs week by week. Thirty-three parts carry BBa IDs, so these are registered rather than wiki-only, but I could not open the Registry pages (parts.igem.org returned 403 to me), the Parts page links no per-part data or characterisation, and the STL files and Arduino code are hosted on GitHub, which cannot be judged. A reader cannot yet tell from the Registry which composite carries the dose-response data.
justification.w1: The home page does what the handbook asks: it states the problem, the Warburg rationale and the dual-biomarker solution in a few lines, shows the four-region threshold figure and the reader, then points the visitor to Description, Hardware, Engineering and Human Practices. The Description abstract is a clean, honest summary that names the validation matrices used. A reader knows the goal within about a minute.
justification.w2: Claims are mostly tied to numbered figures with named controls, replicate counts and units, and the team is careful to label what is planned: the hardware page repeatedly states that quantitative lactate and pyruvate measurement is future work and that the optical test used a YFP standard with n = 3 and SD error bars (Hardware 5.3). Against that, the R2 and live-cell dose mismatches noted above, and recurring words like 'successfully' and 'perfectly' around preliminary results, keep this below 4.5.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and the side menu broadly tracks the criteria, with an on-page contents list for every long page. But four standard pages a judge expects are 404: Attributions, Proof of Concept, Implementation and Measurement, and the Contribution page is an 11,000-word general review of iGEM biosensors rather than a contribution future teams can act on, which is exactly the sprawl the handbook warns against.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: week-by-week notebook, full protocols with reagent volumes and cycling conditions, primer sequences, the scoring-model weights and workflow, a costed bill of materials, and explicit limitation-to-next-step tables. Two gaps keep it from 4 or above: the STL and firmware files live on GitHub rather than on iGEM servers, so they are outside what can be judged or relied on, and with no attributions page a future reader cannot tell which steps needed outside expertise.
justification.w5: Citation practice is consistently good for a high school wiki: numbered reference lists on Description, Engineering, Model and Hardware, in-text numbers attached to specific quantitative claims, a figure credited as adapted from Vander Heiden et al., and, to the team's credit, open acknowledgement that the LldR insertion sites derive from patent CN113004420A, with that patent's own fold-activation and Kd figures reported. Two soft spots: a few sources are institutional reference-range pages rather than primary literature, and I could not check that every cited value sits in its source.

J3.one_line: A genuinely strong high school project: two allosteric fluorescent sensors designed by a transparent computational model, built, purified, screened and characterised with controls in buffer, artificial plasma and live cells, wrapped in an unusually thorough stakeholder-to-design loop, but let down by a missing Attributions page, numbers that disagree between pages, and a reader that has never actually read the sensors.
strengths: Human practices is a real loop, not a contact list: 16 interviews and two surveys (208 and 113 responses), each ending in a specific documented change, including the decision to add pyruvate alongside lactate, which is the project's central design idea.

Measured, controlled wet-lab data across three levels of complexity: 4PL dose-response fits with EC50 values, kinetics, pH and temperature series, a six-metabolite specificity panel, artificial plasma, and 293T live-cell traces with untransfected controls and stated replicates.

An honest engineering failure and recovery: first-round ligation failed with vector self-ligation and short colony-PCR products, and the diagnosed fix (double the insert, extend ligation to 2 h) produced correct clones across all ten groups.

A dry-lab model that actually drove the build: the five-feature weighted residue score chose P1-P5 for construction, and the model page states plainly that the weights are heuristic and were not trained on experimental data.

Unusual candour about scope: the Hardware page says outright that the prototype validates workflow rather than measuring metabolites, that the optical test used a YFP substitute, and that the temperature module was omitted.
weaknesses: No Attributions page (404) and no who-did-what anywhere, so I cannot tell which students ran the cloning, purification, MD simulations or cell work, or what the PI and host lab contributed.

Key numbers disagree between pages: L4 R2 is 0.9613 on Results but 0.9913 in Engineering Test 3; P2 is 0.9175 on Results but 0.9975 in Learn 3; the P2 live-cell dose is 200 microM in the Results text and 1 mM in the Fig. 24 caption.
The two halves of the platform never meet: the reader was tested with a commercial YFP standard and water, never with L4 or P2, so the end-to-end claim on the home page is not yet demonstrated.
No consent, anonymity or ethics-oversight statement for the two public surveys or for the 30-student pre/post awareness study.

Sprawl in the wrong place: an 11,000-word general biosensor review on the Contribution page while Proof of Concept, Implementation and Measurement are missing, and the STL files and firmware sit on GitHub, outside what a judge may consider.
red_flags: Attributions standard page returns 404; essential bench and computational work is unattributed. A session question, not an accusation.
Internal inconsistency in reported R2 values and in the live-cell pyruvate dose between Results, Engineering and the figure captions; worth asking which figure is authoritative.
3D-print STL files and Arduino firmware hosted on GitHub rather than on iGEM servers, so they cannot be judged (handbook p.29).

HEK-293T, a human-derived immortalised line, is used for the live-cell work (Safety page). For a high school team this should be checked against the organism whitelist and the safety form; I would raise it as a check with the safety committee rather than as a finding.
Registry pages for the 33 claimed BBa IDs could not be opened from here (403 from parts.igem.org), so the depth of part documentation is unverified; the Parts page itself links no per-part data.

calibrated.changed: none.

one_line.en: Two allosteric biosensors built, screened and characterised with controls in buffer, artificial plasma and live cells, with outstanding human practices, let down by a missing attributions page and a reader never run with the team's own proteins.
one_line.zh: 兩款變構生物感測器建成、篩選並在緩衝液、人工血漿與活細胞中對照表徵，人文實踐出色，但缺歸屬頁，讀取器也從未搭配自家蛋白實測。

strengths: Ten variants built, expressed, purified and compared with uninduced controls on every gel, with winners chosen on measured data
Characterisation well beyond a single curve: dose fits, kinetics, pH and temperature series, a six-metabolite specificity panel and live-cell imaging
A real cloning failure reported and fixed by a specific parameter change
Human Practices that changed the design, with a pathologist interview producing the dual-biomarker scheme
weaknesses: No attributions page and no who-did-what for lab, modelling or hardware work
The reader was validated with a commercial standard and water, never with the team's own sensors
The screening decision rule is validated only against invented scenarios; no real or spiked sample was measured
Conflicting goodness-of-fit values for the same fits on different pages, and no statistics on the artificial-plasma series
red_flags: Attributions standard page returns 404
Use of a human-derived immortalised cell line by a high school team needs a whitelist determination from the safety committee
Internally inconsistent fit statistics and a live-cell dose that differs between text and caption
Several Registry figure captions are mismatched, and firmware and print files sit outside iGEM servers

screen.project_title: Dual-pathway engineered Bacillus subtilis biocontrol of peach gummosis (Botryosphaeria dothidea)
screen.what_they_built: An engineered B. subtilis WB600 carrying a dual-inducible (H2O2 / xylose OR-gate) cassette that secretes a 3xLysM-ChiA chitinase fusion and expresses shRNA/siRNA against the pathogen's LysM effector gene BdLM1, intended as a sprayed or painted orchard biocontrol replacing chemical fungicides.
screen.chassis_and_parts: B. subtilis WB600 chassis, E. coli DH5alpha for cloning, pHT254/pHT43 vectors. 20 parts submitted: 15 BdLM1-targeting siRNA/shRNA basic parts plus the BdLM1 reference gene (BBa_26LZHSC0), and composite parts BBa_26V6ZHNZ (PkatA-PxylA OR-gate promoter), BBa_26DGWI7F (Sp-LysM3-Linker-ChiA), BBa_26JVZCZG and BBa_266RK293 expression cassettes.
screen.best_evidence: /results §IV: plate antagonism assay one day after xylose induction — mean B. dothidea colony radius 2.17 cm with the circular-plasmid engineered strain versus 2.4 cm linearised, 2.57 cm wild-type B. subtilis, 2.73 cm enzyme and 2.8 cm PBS control. No replicate counts, no error bars, no statistics. Cloning is evidenced by seven gel figures (digests and ligation checks) on the same page.
screen.hp_integration: Weak — orchard visits, a professor interview and a public/organisation questionnaire are described in a 603-word page with figure captions but little detail, and a 'before vs after' expert consultation is asserted rather than shown to have changed a design parameter.
screen.reason: A sensible, well-motivated design (targeting the LysM immune-evasion effector from both sides) but the evidence is thin and the headline claim outruns it. The only functional result is a single-timepoint colony-radius table with a 22% reduction versus PBS, no replicates, no error bars and no statistics, and the engineered strain is barely separated from wild-type B. subtilis which the team itself says is intrinsically inhibitory. Their own contribution page states the 20 parts 'passed dry-lab validation', i.e. the RNAi arm was never tested in vivo; no chitinase activity assay, no mCherry expression data and no BdLM1 knockdown measurement are shown despite a chitinase activity kit being listed in the reagents. Pages are short across the board. The member-by-member attribution table is a genuine strength for aspect 6.
screen.field_notes: BJWZ-China (Agriculture, Beijing) targeted peach gummosis caused by Botryosphaeria dothidea, whose secreted LysM protein BdLM1 masks chitin and blocks the tree's PAMP-triggered immunity. Their engineered Bacillus subtilis WB600 carries a PkatA-PxylA dual-input OR-gate promoter (responding to infection-generated H2O2 or to grower-sprayed xylose) driving a secreted Sp-3xLysM-ChiA chitinase fusion with a P2A-mCherry tracker, plus shRNA/siRNA cassettes against the non-LysM region of BdLM1 — 20 Registry parts in total, 15 of them RNAi elements. Cloning into pHT254 is documented by seven agarose gel figures covering plasmid preps, PstI/XbaI and SacI digests and ligation checks. They isolated fungi from 12 field samples across peach orchards, recovering Geotrichum candidum, Alternaria tenuissima, Fusarium solani and B. dothidea, and also used a commercial BSL-1 B. dothidea strain. The one functional test is a PDA plate antagonism assay measuring mean colony radius one day after xylose induction: 2.17 cm (circular plasmid strain), 2.4 cm (linearised), 2.57 cm (wild-type B. subtilis), 2.73 cm (enzyme), 2.8 cm (PBS), reported without replicates or statistics. A tryptophan-auxotrophy growth comparison is offered as the biocontainment argument. No chitinase activity, mCherry fluorescence or BdLM1 silencing data appear; the contribution page describes the parts as dry-lab validated. There is a detailed per-member attribution table, a 1458-word model page, and short human-practices (603 words) and hardware (247 words) pages.

screen.project_title: Methanol biosensor for adulterated alcoholic beverages using engineered PcAOX
screen.what_they_built: A cell-free colorimetric methanol detector for travellers: engineered alcohol oxidase from Phanerochaete chrysosporium (PcAOX) variants selected in silico for methanol-over-ethanol selectivity, plus a hardware pipette cartridge and an ultrafiltration step to strip beverage colour.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli expression of His-tagged PcAOX variants (genes ordered from VectorBuilder); nine BBa parts registered (BBa_264PLYIV, BBa_268V5EML, BBa_26BNVUPA, BBa_26EDTBO0, BBa_26FLA1ZK, BBa_26IK0ZHE, BBa_26TQNPSS, BBa_26WH8SZM, BBa_26YT5ET3).
screen.best_evidence: /results: ultrafiltration (30 kDa MWCO) reduced colorant absorbance by a mean 73.19% across three food dyes (blue 48.65%, yellow 93.12%, red 77.80%) and by 97.09% in a real alcoholic beverage, with calibration curves (beverage curve R2 = 0.97). Also on /results: anti-His western blot showing the expected ~72 kDa monomer band for WT and variants 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: a research trip to Indonesia, Thailand and Laos observing uneven fill levels in supposedly sealed bottles drove the consumer-facing, no-false-negative design brief, and the /ihp page ties stakeholder input to hardware design, enzyme choice, four design principles and the market plan.
screen.reason: The central claim fails: across four kinetic assay formats (5 min, 30 min, extra FAD, 1.5 mL upscale) no enzyme activity was detected for any variant, so the biosensor was never shown to oxidise methanol, and the selectivity gains are docking and MD numbers only. The honest write-up, nine parts, hardware and the ultrafiltration data make this a strong medal team, but aspect 2 is near the floor and that is the aspect finalist selection turns on.
screen.field_notes: BK-Denmark (Denmark, Diagnostics village) built a consumer methanol test for adulterated spirits after two Danish travellers died of methanol poisoning in Indonesia in 2024. They docked 12 PcAOX active-site mutants with AutoDock Vina, carried seven forward, and ran 100 ns GROMACS simulations showing variant 7 with a +59.9 pp occupancy shift toward methanol relative to WT, a figure that depends on recalibrating to a WT baseline the team discusses openly, alongside k_off values they flag as censored. Seven variants plus WT were expressed in E. coli from VectorBuilder constructs and confirmed by anti-His western blot at ~72 kDa, but every kinetic assay (ABTS/HRP at 5 and 30 min, additional FAD, 1.5 mL upscale) showed no activity; the team attributes this to imidazole carryover from elution and a missed buffer exchange. A separate hardware and ultrafiltration study gave their only positive quantitative result: 30 kDa UF reduced dye absorbance by a mean 73.19% and beverage colour by 97.09%, suggesting colour interference is tractable. Nine Registry parts, a 5,090-word entrepreneurship page, a lab-mistakes guidebook written for future teams, and an HP research trip through Southeast Asia. The Attributions page is a sponsor list with no who-did-what breakdown.

screen.project_title: OrbitColi — freeze-dried E. coli Nissle probiotic against spaceflight oxidative stress
screen.what_they_built: Two input modules for a planned AND-gated probiotic: a CadC-TcpP/TcpH bile-acid receptor sensing food intake via GCDCA, and H2O2-responsive PgrxA / PfhuF reporters sensing oxidative stress. Plus a part-characterisation software layer that fits datasheets to feed the team's 2024 circuit calculator.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli Nissle 1917; Golden Gate assembly. Four TcpP loop variants (pBN25_0053 = BBa_25L370I2, pBN26_0003/0004/0005), PgrxA-GFP (BBa_K3953000) and PfhuF-GFP reporters.
screen.best_evidence: /results: fluorescence/OD600 kinetics in Nissle 1917 — pBN25_0053 reached 70,472 at 20 uM and 106,398 at 50 uM GCDCA with basal 2,138, i.e. ~33-fold and ~50-fold activation, versus ~9-fold and ~14-fold for pBN26_0005. The H2O2 arm failed: all PgrxA-GFP and PfhuF-GFP groups including untreated controls fluoresced visibly, with no concentration-dependence (/results, Fig 7).
screen.hp_integration: Not demonstrably — the 9,000-word human-practices page documents extensive consultation, but no specific construct, promoter or assay choice on the results or engineering pages is traced back to it.
screen.reason: One honest DBTL cycle with genuine dose-response data on a bile-acid sensor, but the best-performing variant is the one inherited from BNDS-China 2025, the oxidative-stress arm produced no working sensor, the AND gate and the therapeutic output were never built, and the model was validated on the 2025 dataset rather than this year's. No /attributions, /parts, /safety-and-security or /experiments at the standard slugs, which the handbook asks judges not to hunt for. Solid medal territory, not top-2.
screen.field_notes: BNDS-China (Space village, China) is developing OrbitColi, a freeze-dried E. coli Nissle 1917 probiotic intended to counter radiation- and microgravity-driven oxidative stress on long missions, framed with real dose figures (ISS 100-200 mSv/yr; 300-450 mSv for a three-year Mars round trip). This year's work covered two sensing inputs. Three new CadC-TcpP/TcpH loop variants from Chang et al. 2021 were built by Golden Gate and characterised by plate-reader kinetics in Nissle against GCDCA, TCA and DCA; the 2025 variant pBN25_0053 won on induction ratio (~50-fold at 50 uM, basal 2,138) over the new pBN26_0005 (~14-fold, basal 7,150), and the team states plainly that the variants were assayed on different dates so absolute comparisons are provisional and that DCA discrimination is not established. The PgrxA/PfhuF H2O2 reporters gave visible GFP in every group including untreated controls, so no peroxide response was shown; PgrxA was nonetheless carried forward on literature grounds and written up as a contribution to BBa_K3953000. The modelling page is the most interesting dry-lab piece: it diagnoses the team's own 2024 calculator as using hard-coded rate constants and builds the missing characterisation half, validated against the 2025 split-T7 AND gate. The AND gate and the protective output were not built this year.

screen.project_title: Engineered S. epidermidis for tick-borne disease prevention (Dae2 binders plus topical vaccine)
screen.what_they_built: Two approaches on a skin commensal: secretion of de novo binders against the tick enzyme Dae2 so ingested skin microbes survive and kill the feeding tick, and surface display of OspA/Asp14 antigen fragments as a topical vaccine, screened with bacterial and cell-free two-hybrid assays plus a HiBiT secretion assay.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. epidermidis ATCC 12228, with E. coli DC10B (dcm-) for plasmid prep and E. coli TK310 for two-hybrid; 34 BBa parts documented with full sequences — vectors pLI50/p15A, Ppen, hld RBS, terminators, insulators, signal peptides, HiBiT/His/HA tags, five Dae2 binders in both hosts, anchoring domains.
screen.best_evidence: /results, the team's own summary: the two-hybrid results 'remained inconclusive. Most constructs were assembled, but binding, Dae2 inhibition, and extracellular expression weren't demonstrated.' The bacterial two-hybrid positive control showed limited separation from its uninduced condition (3 technical replicates, plate format), so no binder call could be made.
screen.hp_integration: Substantial HP and safety/security work for a Lyme-endemic New England community, but no documented case of stakeholder input changing the construct design.
screen.reason: Ambitious design, a non-model Gram-positive chassis handled carefully, 15k words of iteration logs and 34 well-documented parts — an excellent record for future teams. But by their own summary nothing worked and the two-hybrid positive control failed, so aspect 2 is near the floor. Cannot be top-2 without a working result.
screen.field_notes: Boston-BOSLab 2026 (Infectious Diseases, USA) engineered the skin commensal Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC 12228 along two tracks: secreting de novo binders against Dae2, the tick antibacterial enzyme, so skin microbes survive ingestion and kill the feeding tick before Borrelia transmission; and displaying nonfunctional OspA/Asp14 antigen fragments as a topical vaccine. Methodology is careful for a community-lab high school team: plasmids passaged through dcm-deficient E. coli DC10B to avoid cytosine methylation before S. epidermidis transformation, a cell-free E. coli lysate two-hybrid as a cheaper screen, and a planned HiBiT extracellular assay for secretion. Four to five documented iterations per subsystem. The outcome is negative and stated plainly on the Results page: assays were attempted, not confirmed; the bacterial two-hybrid positive control barely separated from uninduced, the cell-free format was inconclusive across economy, premium and linear-DNA variants, and S. epidermidis transformation remained a bottleneck. The lasting value is the parts catalogue: 34 BBa entries with sequences, sources and DOIs covering staph vectors, promoters, insulators, signal peptides and tags, plus a strong safety and security page.

screen.project_title: Flowever - biomanufactured melatonin for cut-flower preservation
screen.what_they_built: An E. coli cell factory converting tryptophan to melatonin (nine-gene Version 2.0 with BH4 cofactor synthesis/recycling in a BL21 triple-knockout host), whose fermentation supernatant is formulated with citric acid as a cut-flower vase preservative. The aim is to skip purification so the molecule is affordable as a flower-care ingredient.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and BL21(DE3) dtnaA dtrpR dyddG (purchased knockout strain); 20 documented construct parts across V1.0 and V2.0, incl. multigene modules BBa_26798463 (pET24a-TPH-COMT) and BBa_26D4NGRU (pACYCDuet-7genes), plus a Registry collection 'Melatonin biosynthesis v2.0'.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /engineering Cycle 3: HPLC time course, melatonin 159.02 mg/L mean at 96 h on glycerol vs 104.00 mg/L on glucose (~53% higher), against 1.15-1.47 mg/L for Version 1.0 in Cycle 2; SDS-PAGE soluble bands for all nine enzymes; Cycle 4 carnation trials where the citric-acid formulation beat medium, uninduced-supernatant, added-melatonin and water controls on Days 4-5.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - advice from Dr. Chenxi Qiu and Prof. Ge Qu drove the V1.0-to-V2.0 pathway/cofactor redesign, Prof. Junjie Zhang's input drove the LB-to-M9 washed-cell switch and citric-acid addition, and practitioner/questionnaire feedback added stem-by-stem display scoring and a commercial control to the flower trials.
screen.reason: Real quantitative wet-lab output (159 mg/L by HPLC) tied to four genuine DBTL cycles and an application test with proper controls - above most of the HS field. The caution is aspect 6: plasmids were fully synthesised by a supplier, the triple-knockout strain was purchased, HPLC was run by a third-party lab, and the Attributions page is boilerplate with no who-did-what breakdown. Worth a full read, mainly to settle how much the students executed.
screen.field_notes: BWYA (Beijing, Agriculture village) built 'Flowever', a melatonin-producing E. coli whose unpurified supernatant becomes a cut-flower preservative, explicitly to avoid downstream purification cost. Version 1.0 (XcP4H, PsmH, PsmF, OsCOMT + FolM/PhhB) reached only 1.15-1.47 mg/L over 96 h and pBAD induction gave no detectable expression, so they moved to a Version 2.0 nine-gene design (dSmTPH-N137-C213I, HaTDC, CsNAT, AtOMT-1 plus GTPC/PTPS/SPR/PCD/DHPR for BH4) in BL21(DE3) dtnaA dtrpR dyddG, reaching a mean 159.02 mg/L at 96 h on glycerol versus 104.00 mg/L on glucose. Application work went LB supernatant to washed cells in M9 to citric-acid acidification, with four student groups running matched carnation treatment and control groups and the formulation out-performing medium, uninduced supernatant, added melatonin and water controls on Days 4-5. Twenty parts are documented with a Registry collection; modelling was AlphaFold/ligand work on XcP4H and OsCOMT only, not pathway kinetics. Attribution is the weak point - synthetic plasmids, a purchased knockout strain and third-party HPLC are disclosed in the text but the Attributions page itself carries no contribution breakdown.

screen.project_title: BioShield — biological modules for controlled asbestos-material treatment
screen.what_they_built: Three separately tested modules: an ObcAB-FpOAR oxalic-acid route, a metal-handling pair (PpMT-AtPCS plus a new CsoR/Pcso copper-responsive ZupT circuit) and a candidate MgFP/VsTyr protein 'bio glue' coating, aimed at a future cartridge for asbestos surface treatment.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); 9 parts listed including improved BBa_K4192121 (CAU_China 2022) and BBa_25NKZV98 (SZ_SHD 2025), new basic parts CsoR BBa_26HBA2CF, Pcso BBa_26UTXBCT, ZupT BBa_26S90MRP, VsTyr BBa_26IW2Q32, and composites BBa_261GJVV1 / BBa_2687LU74.
screen.best_evidence: /results: ~10 mM oxalic acid in supernatant after 12 h induction; magnesium-silicate proxy recovered mass 4-31% lower than empty-vector control across four starting masses; copper assay dual module 66.98% below control at 0.1 mM (22.13% at 0.5 mM, 5.40% at 1 mM) with Fe2+ reductions at all three doses. Replicate counts are explicitly undefined in the source.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — 16 numbered stakeholder cycles (occupational physicians, demolition workers, Brazilian asbestos advocates, contractors, a councillor) pushed the team to reframe from asbestos remediation to a narrow auxiliary treatment step and to a magnesium-silicate proxy rather than asbestos itself.
screen.reason: A genuinely good medal team: real comparative data, two improved parts plus a new copper-responsive feedback circuit, disciplined epistemic framing and a deep stakeholder programme. But effect sizes are small and dose-inconsistent, replicate counts undefined, the coating module produced no film, the modules were never integrated, and Attributions just points at the iGEM form.
screen.field_notes: BYHS-CHN 2026 (BioShield, Bioremediation, Shanghai) asks whether synthetic biology could add a controlled auxiliary step to professional asbestos handling, deliberately scoped away from claiming detoxification. Three modules: an improved ObcAB-FpOAR oxalic-acid route (~10 mM OA in supernatant at 12 h; magnesium-silicate proxy recovered mass 4-31% below empty-vector control), a metal module combining an architecture-redesigned PpMT-AtPCS with a new CsoR/Pcso copper-responsive ZupT positive-feedback circuit (dual group 66.98% below control at 0.1 mM Cu, 22.13% at 0.5 mM, 5.40% at 1 mM; Fe2+ lower at all doses), and a VsTyr/MgFP 'bio glue' that changed colour in liquid but failed to form the expected film, leading to an MgFP tag-configuration revision. Nine parts, several improved from CAU_China 2022 and SZ_SHD 2025, with CsoR_Pcso-ZupT-RFP as favourite composite. 16 human-practices cycles spanning Chinese and Canadian/Brazilian asbestos communities visibly reshaped scope. Wiki is well organised with reading-mode controls; attribution detail is deferred to the iGEM form.

screen.project_title: Phage receptor-binding protein plus Ce-UiO-66 nanozyme colorimetric detection of foodborne bacteria
screen.what_they_built: They expressed phage receptor-binding proteins (BSCBD-1, BSCBD-2 for B. subtilis; T7Mtfp, 04922Btfp for E. coli) in E. coli BL21, coupled them to magnetic beads for capture and to a cerium-doped UiO-66 nanozyme for colour development. The result is a 30-minute instrument-free colorimetric assay for whole bacteria.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a cloning host and BL21(DE3) expression host; pET28a backbone with T7 promoter and His tag, SUMO tag used to rescue solubility; 4 new basic parts and 7 new composite parts registered (BBa_268NWXUF, BBa_26XRE72O, BBa_260F9QON, BBa_26LI4L2O plus composites), with a separate Part Collection page.
screen.best_evidence: /results Part 1 and Part 2: linear colorimetric response ((R+G)/B ratio) over 10^0-10^7 CFU/mL with r = 0.9481, 0.9746 and 0.9, giving LODs of 12.7, 10.4 and 19.2 CFU/mL and RSD under 10% across the range (Tables 1 and 2); specificity assays discriminate B. subtilis from E. coli including in 1:1 mixed suspensions, and spiked milk samples gave significantly higher signal than PBS-spiked milk.
screen.hp_integration: Substantial and apparently integrated: a stakeholder map, public survey, restaurant interviews, two technical experts, a commercial expert, a regulatory expert and a site visit feed a named reflective model, and the team states the feedback shaped pricing, product positioning and market-entry sequencing on the Entrepreneurship page, though the clearest changes are commercial rather than molecular.
screen.reason: This is the strongest quantitative characterisation in the batch: validated LODs near 10 CFU/mL with RSD, specificity against a non-target organism and a mixed culture, real-sample milk testing, four clean DBTL cycles and eleven documented new parts. The main doubts a full read must settle are how much of the nanomaterial work (Ce-UiO-66 synthesis, TEM with elemental mapping) the students did themselves, since no attributions page appears in the crawl, and whether the replicate structure behind the error bars is reported.
screen.field_notes: Cataverse-Beijing (Food & Nutrition village, China) built an instrument-free colorimetric assay for foodborne bacteria that avoids the cost and batch variability of AuPt nanoflower systems. Phage receptor-binding proteins act as molecular hooks: BSCBD-1 and BSCBD-2 from Bacillus phages PZA and phi29 for B. subtilis, and T7Mtfp and 04922Btfp tail fibre proteins for E. coli, all cloned into pET28a by homologous recombination, sequence-verified and expressed in BL21(DE3) with Ni-NTA purification and SDS-PAGE. GFP fusions proved specific adsorption by fluorescence against PBS and empty-vector controls. RBPs were then conjugated to carboxylated magnetic beads for enrichment and electrostatically coupled to a cerium-doped UiO-66 MOF nanozyme for colour, with coupling temperature and time optimised by A650 (37 C/60 min for the BSCBDs, 50 C/15 min for T7Mtfp). Sensitivity runs over 10^0-10^7 CFU/mL gave LODs of 12.7, 10.4 and 19.2 CFU/mL with RSD below 10%, and specificity and spiked-milk tests passed. The team reports failures honestly: pET28a-SUMO-04922Btfp never sequenced clean, and the T7Mtfp-GFP and 04922Btfp-GFP fusions went into inclusion bodies. Eleven new Registry parts, a part collection page, extensive IHP with experts and regulators, plus large education and entrepreneurship sections.

screen.project_title: UriCell: modular transport-plus-degradation platform for intestinal uric acid
screen.what_they_built: A four-module system in E. coli Nissle 1917 for gut uric acid management: engineered YgfU transporter variants, localisation-optimised urate oxidase (UOX), catalase CatA for peroxide clearance, and a HucR-HucO uric-acid-responsive promoter with a CAP enhancer driving the degradation enzymes.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a/BL21(DE3) for characterisation, E. coli Nissle 1917 as the therapeutic chassis; pET28a backbones. 38 new BBa_26* parts plus a part collection, and reuse/improvement of earlier parts including BBa_K2752004 (YgfU).
screen.best_evidence: /results Cycle 3: the integrated sensing-plus-degradation circuit reduced extracellular uric acid from 400 uM to about 75 uM in 6 h with hourly sampling, after a dose-dependent mCherry response across 0-400 uM with low basal leakage (Cycle 2). /results Cycle 4: the full circuit kept working in EcN under microanaerobic M9 with 0.2% bile salts at pH 6.5 over 24 h against an empty-vector control, with the growth burden reported rather than hidden.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: 13k-word IHP with a CELL loop, five clinician/industry experts, four gout patients and a site visit, feeding stated changes to product format, pricing and the staged BL21-then-EcN safety strategy, though the link from a specific interview to a specific wet-lab parameter is looser than the engineering pages' internal logic.
screen.reason: The strongest evidence base in this batch: four genuine DBTL cycles, each component characterised alone before integration, a dose-dependent sensor, a quantified degradation endpoint, and survival of the whole circuit in the intended probiotic chassis under gut-like stress, with limitations (growth burden, weak CatA peroxide clearance) stated rather than buried. 38 new Registry parts with a collection. The '60-fold above commercial UOX standard' and '4.5-fold above commercial CatA' claims are the obvious thing for the panel to probe. Deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: Cataverse-GreatBay (CHN, Therapeutics) built UriCell, an engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 for degrading uric acid in the gut as a hyperuricemia therapy. Four sequential DBTL cycles: (1) component characterisation in BL21(DE3) - three UOX configurations compared, with T7-tag-pelB-UOX highest (pelB about 2x cytoplasmic Tag-UOX), a rationally designed YgfU mutant library (T100A, E270A, S426A singles, three doubles, one triple) in which wild type transported only urate while mutants gained xanthine uptake, and purified CatA for H2O2 removal; (2) a HucR-HucO uric-acid-responsive mCherry reporter, where only CAP-enhancer configurations gave a clear dose response across 0-400 uM; (3) mCherry replaced by UOX-CatA, giving UA-dependent induction and a drop from 400 uM to about 75 uM in 6 h; (4) transfer into EcN, still functional under microanaerobic bile-salt M9 at pH 6.5 against empty-vector control, with a measured growth burden and only modest CatA-mediated peroxide clearance flagged as the remaining bottleneck. The model is AlphaFold3 structure prediction plus AutoDock Vina docking of urate vs xanthine, used prospectively to pick the three mutation sites. 38 new BBa parts plus a part collection, improve page, 13k-word IHP, 12.6k-word education. No attributions page.

justification.a1: Four sequential DBTL cycles that genuinely build on each other: three UOX localisation variants benchmarked, a seven-member rational YgfU mutant library, CatA purified, a HucR-HucO/CAP uric-acid sensor characterised with mCherry, the reporter then swapped for UOX-CatA, and finally the whole cassette moved into EcN and run for 24 h in M9 + 0.2% bile salts at pH 6.5 under microanaerobic conditions (Results sections 1-4; Engineering Cycles 1-4). That is the increasing-difficulty ladder the GreatBay_SZ/TAS anchors show. It stops short of a 5 because there is no in vivo or whole-organism step and the headline activity numbers (>60-fold over a commercial UOX standard) are not expressed in defined units.
justification.a2: Function is shown against real controls in most places: Figure 5 (Results) carries pET28a-vector and WT YgfU curves alongside every mutant with error bars and significance marks; Figure 15 compares engineered EcN with an empty-vector EcN across OD600, residual UA fluorescence and A520 over 24 h; the reporter work uses an empty-vector group and a 0-400 uM dose series normalised to OD. Experiments 'Appendix. General Notes' states triplicate samples with error bars (max/min). The deduction is for the headline degradation claim: Figure 13 is a single uncontrolled RFU curve with no abiotic or empty-vector comparison and no uM axis, so '400 uM to ~75 uM in 6 h' rests on an unshown standard-curve conversion, and the Results text 'WT ... did not transport xanthine at all' is not what Figure 5B shows (the WT trace rises above vector).
justification.a3: The need is well framed and stakeholder-tested (Human Practices sections 4-7: four clinicians/industry experts, four patients, a site visit to Guangzhou Shaohe Biotechnology), and the EcN test in bile-salt, microanaerobic M9 is a genuine attempt at an application-like setting rather than LB. Entrepreneurship adds market sizing, a 5P plan and a repriced product. But nothing yet links the measured in vitro degradation to a serum-urate effect: no animal data, no dose estimate, and prevalence/market figures come from literature (one from a Toutiao self-media white paper).
justification.a4: Each cycle states its success criteria before testing (Engineering 1A: 'both expression and activity will be considered during component selection') and test results change the next build: flat response without CAP led to the CAP-enhanced HucO architecture (Improve, Improvement 2); localisation comparison selected T7-tag-pelB-UOX for Cycle 3; mCherry was deliberately used first so that a weak final system could be traced to regulator or enzyme (Learn 2). The notebook's 'cycle summary & handoff' table (Day 3-78) makes the chain explicit. Several Learn sections are written in the future tense ('will determine'), which reads as plan rather than record.
justification.a5: Human Practices runs a declared CELL loop over a public survey, five expert interviews, four patient interviews, a company site visit and five peer-team exchanges, with an ethics framework and a power/interest stakeholder map. Documented changes are real but mostly positioning and commercial: repositioning from 'treating gout' to 'supportive management', pricing 50 to 150 RMB, leading with 'probiotic' over 'transgenic'. The one strong wet-lab link is Dr. Tian's low-oxygen objection, answered by the Cycle 4 anaerobic/bile-salt experiment; more such lab-level consequences would reach a 5.
justification.a6: The /attributions page returns 404 and is not in the navigation; the Awards page points instead to the off-wiki standardized Attributions Form. The Team page gives 20-plus member bios and six advisors (including a PhD-level 'veteran iGEM PI and Advisor'), but nothing says who cloned, who ran the assays, or in whose laboratory the 78-day campaign took place. Outsourcing of Sanger sequencing to a biotech company is declared in Experiments and Engineering, which is good practice, yet without task-level attribution I cannot confirm the core execution was the students'.
justification.a7: The project is built from standard components throughout: pET28a backbones, J23100 and CP6 promoters, three RBSs, a T7 terminator, pelB and T7-tag leaders, mCherry, plus reuse and improvement of prior Registry parts (YgfU BBa_K2752004, HucO BBa_K2913003, CAP BBa_K4514035), assembled into a composite sensing-degradation cassette (BBa_26MLMQ57). The Part Collection lists 47 parts organised as reusable modules. This is clearly a synthetic-biology device project in the TAS Taipei sense.
justification.a8: The wiki-side documentation is good (Part Collection table, Contribution page with origin, length, properties and usage for each basic part, Improve page tying parts to data). Against that: the standard /parts page is 404 and absent from the navigation, so a judge must find part-collection and contribution instead; the Contribution page itself states 'All part numbers below are listed with placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission'; and pre-existing Registry parts (T7 tag BBa_K2933036, pelB BBa_K5119026) are tabulated as 'New part'. parts.igem.org was unreachable from here, so under p.18 I cannot credit Registry-side characterisation I could not see.
justification.w1: The homepage lays out prevalence, the shortcomings of each current therapy, and the three modules (transport, degradation, sensing) with the mutation table, essentially within the first screens, and names the chassis choice. The Description page then expands this cleanly from clinical problem to biological inspiration to five stated innovations. Slight drift comes from 'innovation' framing repeated across several pages.
