justification.w2: Core claims on Results, Engineering and Improve are each tied to a numbered figure: labelled SDS-PAGE with a kDa-marked ladder and named lanes (Figure 2), OD-normalised fluorescence dose series, transport time courses with vector and WT, and the three-panel engineered-vs-empty EcN comparison. Methods are complete in Experiments with reaction tables, primer list and kit catalogue numbers. Marked down because the degradation readouts are reported in RFU or A520 rather than converted concentrations, Figure 13 has no control, and the Measurement page is empty boilerplate despite measurement being central here.
justification.w3: Navigation is consistent, each page has an in-page table of contents, and the project story is easy to follow. But several standard URLs are broken or unlinked: /parts, /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design all return 404, while /measurement, /hardware and /software exist unlinked and still carry the iGEM template text 'This section is ready for verified content during the content-filling phase'. Handbook p.29 asks teams to preserve the standard pages and guide judges from them; here protocols live under 'Experiments' and parts under 'Part collection'.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat much of this: 24 numbered protocols with reaction systems, cycling conditions, a full primer table and kit catalogue numbers (Experiments), a notebook covering Day 1-78 with per-cycle summaries, handoffs and day-by-day PDF logs hosted on static.igem.wiki, and an honest statement of remaining bottlenecks (circuit growth burden in EcN, weak CatA peroxide clearance). What is missing is raw numeric data behind the plots and the UA standard curve.
justification.w5: Each major page carries a numbered reference list with journal citations that resolve (Description 16 refs, Safety 10, HP with PubMed/DOI links), prior iGEM work is credited (the 2024 LZU-China design figure is captioned with its URL, and the YgfU/HucO/CAP parts are credited to earlier teams on the Improve page). Weak points: one prevalence figure rests on a Toutiao self-media 'white paper', some borrowed schematic figures are credited only by bracketed number, and the Part Collection 'New part' labelling misattributes pre-existing Registry parts.

J1.one_line: A genuinely four-cycle wet-lab project with controls, replicates and an engineered-vs-empty-vector test in EcN under gut-like conditions, let down by a missing attributions/parts page, placeholder Registry status and a headline degradation figure with no control.
strengths: Four linked DBTL cycles that escalate in difficulty: UOX localisation variants, a rational YgfU mutant library, CatA, a UA-responsive HucR-HucO/CAP sensor, integration, then transfer into EcN (Results 1-4, Engineering Cycles 1-4)

Real controls in most key figures: pET28a-vector and WT YgfU traces in the transport time courses (Results Figure 5), empty-vector reporter group, and an empty-vector EcN control tracked alongside the engineered strain across OD600, residual UA and A520 for 24 h (Results Figure 15)

Stated statistics and normalisation policy: triplicate samples with error bars, whole-cell activities compared at equal OD600 = 0.5, fluorescence normalised to OD (Experiments, Appendix General Notes)

Data-driven redesign rather than troubleshooting: the flat response of HucO alone led to the CAP-enhanced architecture, and the mCherry reporter was used first specifically so a weak final system could be attributed to regulator or enzyme (Improve Improvement 2; Engineering Learn 2)
Honest reporting of limitations: the circuit imposes a measurable growth burden in EcN and CatA peroxide clearance is described as modest and needing optimisation (Results section 4.2)
Reproducible record: 24 detailed protocols with primer table and kit catalogue numbers, plus a Day 1-78 notebook with cycle handoffs and day-by-day PDF logs
Substantial, two-way Human Practices (five experts, four patients, a company site visit, five peer-team exchanges) with the low-oxygen objection answered by an actual anaerobic bile-salt experiment
weaknesses: No attributions page (/attributions is 404); the Team page gives bios only and the Awards page defers to the off-wiki standardized form, so who did which experiment, and in whose laboratory, is not documented

calibrated.changed: a6 3.0 -> 2.5. I scored HK Joint School, PSI Korea, BIST-China and Hongwen at 2.5 for exactly this situation: no attributions page and no task-level statement anywhere, only member bios plus declared outsourcing of sequencing or synthesis. Cataverse is the same picture (20+ bios, six advisors including a PhD-level PI, nothing saying who cloned or assayed), so 3.0 was softer than the bar I used elsewhere.

justification.a1: Four sequential cycles take the project from three separately benchmarked components (UOX localisation variants, a seven-member YgfU mutant library, CatA) through a dose-responsive UA biosensor to an integrated sensing-degradation cassette, then into the intended probiotic chassis EcN under bile-salt, pH 6.5, microanaerobic conditions for 24 h (Engineering, Results Table 1). That is the GreatBay pattern of increasingly difficult steps told as one story, and it sits on top of a 379-response survey, nine interviews and a costed entrepreneurship plan. It falls short of a 5 only because the final chassis test ends with two unresolved bottlenecks (growth burden, weak CatA clearance) and no in vivo or containment work.
justification.a2: The main function is shown with measured data and controls: WT versus mutant versus empty-vector xanthine uptake time courses (Results Fig. 5; Model Fig. 4), an empty-vector fluorescence baseline and a 0-400 uM dose response (Results Fig. 10), a growth curve run specifically to exclude UA cytotoxicity as a confounder, extracellular UA falling 400 to ~75 uM in 6 h (Results Fig. 13), and engineered versus empty-vector EcN under simulated gut conditions (Fig. 15). Protocols state triplicate samples with error bars (Experiments, Appendix). Held to 4 because the headline '>60-fold over the commercial standard' is reported without units or specific-activity normalisation, and Cycle 4 residual UA is given as a fluorescence signal rather than a concentration.
justification.a3: Impact is argued from a real clinical gap and tested one step beyond the bench: modified M9 with 0.2% bovine bile salts at pH 6.5 under microanaerobic conditions directly answers the low-oxygen objection raised by Dr Jinzhong Tian (Human Practices 4.1), and clinicians, patients and a manufacturer were consulted on format, price and route to market. It stops short of TAS Taipei's standard because nothing is tested in vivo, colonisation and dosing are unresolved, and the containment the team was repeatedly asked about (kill switch, marker removal) is explicitly deferred to a next iteration.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Localisation was treated as an engineering variable and the lead construct chosen on combined expression and activity rather than expression alone (Cycle 1A); mCherry was used deliberately to decouple regulatory from enzymatic characterisation so a later failure could be localised (Learn 2); UA-containing screening plates were invented to triage frameshift clones (Build 2); and the AlphaFold3 plus AutoDock Vina model picked T100/E270/S426 and its prediction was then tested in the wet lab (Model sections 2-3). Each cycle records an explicit handoff (Notebook Table 1). Not a 5 because several Test and Learn sections for Cycles 3-4 are still written in the future tense, and no redesign follows the Cycle 4 findings within the season.
justification.a5: Reflective, responsible and responsive in the p.21-23 sense: a 379-response bilingual survey, five expert interviews, four patient interviews, a company site visit and four team exchanges, each run through a stated CELL loop with a Land step. Traceable changes include repositioning from 'treating gout' to supportive management, lead-with-probiotic communication, a price change from 50 to 150 RMB after patients said 50 was too cheap to trust, and the anaerobic test added after Dr Tian's oxygen concern. Capped at 4 because most consequences for the wet-lab design are promises ('we will design a biosafety plan', kill switch postponed), and the firmest changes are commercial and communicative.
justification.a6: There is no attributions page at all: /attributions returns 404 and is not in the navigation, so the form the handbook says to read (p.25-26) is absent. The Members page gives only personal bios and lists six advisors with no statement of who did what; sequencing is declared as sent to a biotechnology company (Engineering, Build 1C), which is normal and honestly stated. I make no accusation, but with no who-did-what record I cannot verify that students did the core execution of a 47-part, four-cycle programme, and that is exactly what GreatBay 2019's attribution chart provided. This is a question for Q&A.
justification.a7: The work is squarely synthetic biology on standard components: a 47-entry part collection of basic and composite parts with a written reuse rationale (part-collection), an improvement built on three earlier iGEM parts (YgfU BBa_K2752004, HucO BBa_K2913003, CAP BBa_K4514035) rather than from scratch, and modules designed to be lifted out separately. Deductions: everything is on pET28a/T7 backbones rather than an iGEM assembly standard, and the contribution tables label pre-existing Registry parts (T7 tag BBa_K2933036, pelB BBa_K5119026, J23100 BBa_K823004) as 'New part'.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely good: per-part origin, length, properties and usage on the Contribution page, 24 numbered protocols with reaction tables and the full primer list, and a day-indexed notebook. But parts are judged on the Registry (p.18) and I could not reach parts.igem.org (403 from this environment), while the team's own Contribution page says 'All part numbers below are listed with placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission' even as the Improve page says the composite parts are submitted. The standard Parts, Proof of Concept, Implementation and Attributions pages all 404, and Hardware, Measurement and Software are still unedited iGEM template text ending 'This section is ready for verified content during the content-filling phase'.
justification.w1: The home page states the disease, the four treatment gaps and the three modules in one screen, and Description sections 1-4 give the chassis, the staged strategy and five named innovations with a comparison table against the published literature. After the home and description pages I can state the aim, the chassis, the parts and the success criterion. Short of Lambert_GA level because the home page is dense with tables rather than one schematic per idea, and the success criterion is never given as a number up front.
justification.w2: Every substantive claim on Results and Engineering carries a numbered figure (15 figures on Results alone, all present as served images), the Experiments page gives methods, kit catalogue numbers and a statistics note, and negative or partial outcomes are reported rather than hidden (CatA clearance 'relatively modest', engineered EcN growth burden). It is not a 5 because the crawled text never gives units or n for the fold-change comparisons, and the Cycle 4 uric acid result is reported as a fluorescence signal.
justification.w3: The side navigation and per-page table of contents are consistent and the Build the Core to Adapt to EcN flow makes the reading order obvious. Against that, four standard pages judges are told to look for (Parts, Attributions, Proof of Concept, Implementation) return 404, the 'Part' nav item leads only to the part collection, and three pages are still live iGEM boilerplate with the words 'Content filling' on them. The Human Practices and Education pages are also long enough (13,295 and 12,607 words) to sprawl.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: the Notebook indexes all four cycles day by day with explicit handoffs, Experiments lists every protocol and primer sequence, the part collection explains which module to reuse for which purpose, and the remaining bottlenecks are named as next steps. It misses a 5 because the Registry status of the parts is contradicted between pages and there is no attribution or team-process record to tell a future team who did what and how long it took.
justification.w5: Description, Results, Model and Safety all carry numbered reference lists with full journal citations, and the ones I spot-checked are real and say what the wiki claims (Papakostas and Frillingos 2012 JBC 287:15684 on YgfU substrate selectivity; Zhao et al. 2022 Gut Microbes on EcN urate oxidase with an oxygen-recycling system). A borrowed figure on Description credits its source wiki (2024 lzu-china). Not a 5 because in-text citation is uneven, Human Practices switches to loose author-year form with at least one unresolvable entry ('Lin, 2026'), and most of the team's own schematics carry no source note.

J2.one_line: A disciplined four-cycle engineering project with real controls, a docking-guided transporter redesign that was actually tested, and a chassis-level demonstration under gut-like conditions, let down by a missing attributions page and unverifiable Registry entries.
strengths: Four DBTL cycles with genuine handoffs where test data chose the next build: localisation treated as an engineering variable, lead UOX picked on combined expression and activity, mCherry used deliberately to decouple regulation from enzymology (Engineering, Cycles 1A-3).

A rationally curated seven-member YgfU mutant library designed from an AlphaFold3 model and AutoDock Vina docking, whose prediction was then tested: WT transports uric acid but no detectable xanthine, mutants acquire it (Model section 3, Results Fig. 5).

Controls that matter: empty-vector baselines on fluorescence and uptake, a growth curve run specifically to rule out uric acid cytotoxicity as a confounder, and an empty-vector EcN comparator in the simulated-gut run (Results Figs. 10, 12, 15).

A real step toward the intended setting: modified M9 with 0.2% bovine bile salts, pH 6.5, microanaerobic, 24 h, chosen in direct response to an expert's low-oxygen objection (Engineering Cycle 4; Human Practices 4.1).

Honest reporting of what did not work: engineered EcN carries a measurable growth burden and CatA peroxide clearance is only modest, both named as optimisation targets rather than glossed (Results section 4.2, Table 1).

A reproducible record: 24 numbered protocols with reaction tables, kit catalogue numbers, the full primer list and a stated triplicate-with-error-bars convention (Experiments), plus a day-indexed notebook covering Day 1-78.

Human Practices with a documented loop and traceable consequences, including repositioning to supportive management, a price change after patient pushback, and communication led by 'probiotic' rather than 'transgenic' (Human Practices 4.1, 7, conclusion).
weaknesses: No attributions page exists (404, absent from the navigation); the Members page is bios and an advisor list only, so who did what cannot be checked at all.

Registry status is self-contradictory: Contribution says the part numbers are 'placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission' while Improve says the composite parts are submitted; I could not reach parts.igem.org to resolve it.
Pre-existing iGEM parts (T7 tag BBa_K2933036, pelB BBa_K5119026, J23100 BBa_K823004, HucO BBa_K2913003, CAP BBa_K4514035) are listed as 'New part' in the contribution tables.
Hardware, Measurement and Software are unedited iGEM template pages still carrying the words 'This section is ready for verified content during the content-filling phase' and 'Content filling'.
Parts, Proof of Concept and Implementation standard pages return 404, so a judge must hunt across Contribution, Improve and Part collection for the parts story.

Headline enzyme comparisons ('>60-fold' over commercial UOX, '>4.5-fold' over commercial CatA) are given with no units, no specific-activity normalisation and no n, and the Cycle 4 uric acid result is reported as a raw fluorescence signal rather than a concentration.

Several Test and Learn sections in Cycles 3 and 4 are written in the future tense ('We will evaluate'), which blurs what was actually done, and no redesign follows the Cycle 4 findings within the season.
Much of the Human Practices consequence is prospective: the kill switch, biological containment and marker removal that every expert and peer team raised are deferred to a next iteration.
red_flags: No attributions page anywhere on the wiki (https://2026.igem.wiki/cataverse-greatbay/attributions returns 404) for a project spanning 47 parts and four cycles; I make no accusation, but the core-execution question cannot be answered from the wiki and should be asked in Q&A.

Contribution page states part numbers are 'placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission' while the Improve page states the final composite parts 'are submitted to the iGEM registry' - one of these is inaccurate, and I could not verify either (parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403 from this environment), so a7/a8 rest on wiki evidence only.
Previously existing Registry parts are tabulated as the team's 'New part' contributions on the Contribution page.
Three standard pages (Hardware, Measurement, Software) are still unedited iGEM boilerplate left live on the wiki.
pages_read: human-practices (read in part, grepped for design changes)

calibrated.changed: none — a8 3.0 is my lowest documentation score and is justified beyond the unverified Registry: the wiki contradicts itself on whether parts were submitted and three standard pages are live boilerplate. No other team combined those two defects.

justification.a1: UriCell climbs logically through four cycles in one season: three UOX localisation variants, a seven-member YgfU mutant library, CatA, a HucR-HucO/CAP uric-acid sensor characterised with mCherry, integration of sensing with degradation, and transfer into E. coli Nissle 1917 tested in M9 + 0.2% bile salts, pH 6.5, microanaerobic (Results, 'Cycle 4 - Adapt to EcN'). That is more layers than most high school projects carry all the way to data, and each layer has its own measurement rather than a narrative. It falls short of a 5 only because everything stops at in vitro culture and the headline enzyme comparisons are reported without replicate structure.
justification.a2: The core claims are measured, not asserted: WT YgfU transported uric acid but no detectable xanthine while mutants gained it, with empty-vector and WT controls processed in parallel (Model, 'Wet-Lab Validation'); the CAP-containing reporter rose dose-dependently from 0 to 400 uM against a near-flat empty vector (Results 2.1); the integrated circuit cut extracellular UA from 400 uM to about 75 uM in 6 h with hourly sampling (Results 3.2); engineered EcN outperformed an empty-vector EcN under gut-like conditions, and the growth burden is reported honestly. Against that, no page states n, replicates or error bars, and the '>60-fold higher than commercial UOX standards' and '>4.5-fold CatA' claims (Results 1.1, 1.3) rest on an assay description with no definition of the standard.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by people, not only literature: four clinicians (Dr. Tian, Dr. Jian Zhang, Dr. Qingyun Zhang, Dr. Aiqing Li), four gout patients and a 379-response bilingual survey (Human Practices, sections 3-7). Clinicians set concrete adoption conditions - non-inferiority data, no disruption of the native microbiome, a defined adjunct role - and the team narrowed its target to non-acute hyperuricemia rather than refractory gout. The route into a real setting is still only simulated intestinal culture, and the kill switch, marker removal and in vivo work those same clinicians asked for remain future plans.
justification.a4: Four cycles carry Design/Build/Test/Learn headings and the Learn steps genuinely set the next Build: the UOX localisation comparison selects T7-tag-pelB-UOX for integration, the mCherry stage is deliberately run before enzyme integration so a weak final system can be traced to regulator or payload (Engineering, 'Learn 2'), and docking-predicted mutation sites were then tested at the bench (Model, section 3). Two things hold it at 4: several Test and Learn sections are still in future tense ('We will expose the engineered bacteria...', Engineering Test 3, Learn 4) even though data follow, and no cycle reports a failure that forced a redesign - only successive optimisation.
justification.a5: This is a real integrated-HP effort with a stated ethics framework, a power/interest stakeholder map and a CELL loop that ends each engagement with a 'Land' step. At least one Land item reached the bench: Dr. Tian's objection that urate degradation is an oxidation reaction while the gut is low-oxygen is answered by the microanaerobic bile-salt EcN assay in Cycle 4, and his advice kept the xanthine transporter as a side branch rather than the main path (HP section 4; Results 4.2). Other changes are commercial or communicative - price raised from 50 to 150 RMB, repositioning to 'supportive management of hyperuricemia', leading with 'probiotic' rather than 'transgenic'. Many Land entries remain promises, and for the 379-person survey I found no consent or oversight statement in the text, only a figure captioned 'Our Ethics Framework'.
justification.a6: This is the weakest part of the ballot. The Attributions page returns 404, as does the 'Part' link in the navigation bar, and there is no who-did-what chart anywhere. The Team page gives bios in which a few students name a task ('I was mainly responsible for collecting results of agarose gel electrophoresis'; 'Captain of Wet Lab Phase 2'), while six advisors including a veteran iGEM PI are listed with no statement of what they contributed. Sanger sequencing is openly outsourced to a company (Engineering, Build 2), which is good practice, but with Ni-NTA purification, AlphaFold3 modelling, AutoDock Vina docking and 47 constructs on the table a judge cannot currently tell whose hands did the bench and analysis work. I would raise this readily if the session clarifies it; this records a gap, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is built from standard parts throughout and contributes a coherent collection: 47 entries spanning basic coding parts, a seven-member YgfU mutant series, four regulatory architectures and the final integrated cassette BBa_26MLMQ57 (Part collection, Table 1). The improvement to an existing part is genuine and documented - wild-type YgfU (BBa_K2752004) turned into a dual-substrate transporter (BBa_26YDTZEI) and then used as the transport module in every downstream test (Improve, Improvement 1). Modularity is argued concretely: the T7-tag-pelB leader, the UA-gated HucR-HucO/CAP switch and CatA are each offered as reusable blocks.
justification.a8: On the wiki the documentation is genuinely good - Contribution gives origin, length, properties and usage for each new basic part, Part collection tabulates all 47, and Improve explains the improved part with its characterisation. But this aspect asks for Registry-side evidence, and the team's own Contribution page says 'All part numbers below are listed with placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission', which contradicts the Improve page's claim that the final composite part is already submitted. The dedicated Parts page is a 404, and the Contribution tables mark clearly pre-existing parts (BBa_K2933036 T7 tag, BBa_K5119026 pelB, BBa_K2752004 YgfU WT, BBa_K2913003 HucO, BBa_K4514035 CAP, BBa_K823004 J23100) as 'New part'. With the part data effectively living on the wiki, I cap this at 3.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem (humans lack uricase; 13.3% adult prevalence), why current treatments fall short, and the three-module solution with the mutation table, then points on to Description, Results, Parts, IHP and Education. Description builds the case from clinical gap to gut rationale to chassis choice, with a labelled table comparing the project against prior literature. The only drag is that the home page is assembled from many small graphic fragments, so a single schematic of the whole circuit only arrives later, on Engineering and Part collection.
justification.w2: Results is organised by engineering logic with a 'key finding' line per section, controls named (empty vector, WT YgfU, empty-vector EcN), and an honest closing table listing the growth burden and weak CatA peroxide clearance as remaining bottlenecks - that candour counts for a lot. What keeps it below 4 is measurement reporting: no sample sizes, replicates, error bars or statistics appear in the text, some readouts are left implicit ('residual uric acid fluorescence signal', 'A520-associated signal'), and the fold-change comparisons against commercial standards are stated without defining the standard.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and content sits on recognisable pages, but there are real dead ends: Attributions, Parts, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Protocols and Design all return 404, and the 'Part' item in the side menu leads nowhere. Measurement, Hardware and Software are unfilled iGEM scaffolds still carrying the award blurb and the line 'This section is ready for verified measurement content during the content-filling phase' - a judge should not meet template text on a finished wiki. Education (about 12,600 words) and Entrepreneurship (about 7,300) also outweigh Results (about 2,100), the wrong balance for 'complete but not sprawling'.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: 24 numbered protocols with reaction tables and kit catalogue numbers (Experiments), a 78-day notebook split by cycle with explicit handoffs (Notebook, Table 1), a safety page covering training, waste and containment, and a part collection written so modules can be lifted out. Missing are raw data or source files behind the figures, any record of who performed which experiment, and the remaining double-mutant data that Results says are 'documented in the notebook' but which I could not find there.
justification.w5: Reference lists are numbered, real and relevant on Description (16 entries), Results, Model, Safety and Human Practices, and claims are generally tied to the right source - Papakostas and Frillingos 2012 for T100A, Zhao 2022 and He 2023 for prior engineered EcN. The Description figure of EcN living therapeutics carries a credit to another team's wiki (2024.igem.wiki/lzu-china/design), which is the right instinct. Marks come off for provenance inside the parts tables, where pre-existing Registry parts are labelled 'New part', and for the HP page citing 'Lin, 2026' for the 180 million figure with no entry I could follow in the list.

J3.one_line: A genuinely strong four-cycle project - sensor, engineered transporter, degradation cassette and a working transfer into EcN under gut-like conditions - let down by a missing Attributions page, placeholder Registry status and three unfilled template pages.
strengths: Four DBTL cycles that build on each other, from component characterisation in BL21(DE3) to an integrated UA-gated circuit working in E. coli Nissle 1917 under M9 + 0.2% bile salts, pH 6.5, microanaerobic conditions (Results, Cycle 4)

Controls are present where function is claimed: empty vector and wild-type YgfU in the transport assays, empty-vector EcN in the chassis test, and a growth curve that rules out uric acid toxicity as a confounder (Results 3.2)

A real improvement to an existing Registry part - wild-type YgfU (BBa_K2752004) rationally mutated to a dual-substrate uric acid/xanthine transporter (BBa_26YDTZEI) and then used in every downstream experiment (Improve, Improvement 1)
Docking-guided design that was actually tested: an AlphaFold3 structure plus AutoDock Vina picked T100, E270 and S426, and the wet lab then checked the prediction (Model, sections 2-3)
Honest reporting of limitations: the engineered EcN growth burden and the modest CatA peroxide clearance are named as unresolved in the Results summary table

Human Practices with structure and at least one bench consequence: Dr. Tian's low-oxygen objection is answered by the microanaerobic assay, and clinician input narrowed the target population to non-acute hyperuricemia
weaknesses: No Attributions page (404) and no who-did-what chart; advisors are listed with no description of their contribution, so a judge cannot tell which work the students did

Part documentation is effectively wiki-only: Contribution states the part numbers are 'placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission', while Improve says the final composite part is already submitted, and the Parts page is a 404
Measurement, Hardware and Software pages still carry unfilled iGEM template text ('This section is ready for verified ... content during the content-filling phase')
No sample sizes, replicates, error bars or statistics anywhere; large claims such as '>60-fold higher than commercial UOX standards' rest on an undescribed comparison
Several Test and Learn sections are written in future tense ('We will expose the engineered bacteria...'), making the engineering narrative read as a plan even where the data exist

Many Human Practices 'Land' outcomes remain promises (biosafety plan, promoter comparison, in vivo work) rather than changes already made, and the 379-person survey carries no visible consent or ethics-oversight statement
Page balance is off: Education and Entrepreneurship together run roughly 20,000 words against about 2,100 on Results
red_flags: Contribution page labels pre-existing Registry parts (BBa_K2933036 T7 tag, BBa_K5119026 pelB, BBa_K2752004 YgfU WT, BBa_K2913003 HucO, BBa_K4514035 CAP, BBa_K823004 J23100) as 'New part', which misstates provenance - a correction to ask for, not misconduct

Internal contradiction on Registry status: Contribution says 'placeholder identifiers pending final Registry submission' while Improve says the final composite parts 'are submitted to the iGEM registry'; parts.igem.org returned 403 from this environment, so part documentation could not be verified

Attributions page returns 404 while the project uses advanced methods (Ni-NTA purification, AlphaFold3, AutoDock Vina, 47 constructs) - a question for the session about who did the bench and computational work
Unfilled template placeholder text left live on the Measurement, Hardware and Software pages
Human Practices cites 'Lin, 2026' for the 180 million hyperuricemia figure with no matching entry traceable in its reference list
