screen.project_title: ECOECHO: recombinant plant storage proteins from Pichia pastoris as functional ingredients for plant-based meat
screen.what_they_built: Three plant storage proteins - patatin-02 isoform X2 from Andean potato, Edestin1 from hemp and the 11S globulin Me11s from cassava - expressed and secreted from Pichia pastoris GS115, purified, and tested as gelling/water-holding ingredients in actual plant-based patties.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Pichia pastoris GS115 with pPICZalphaA (AOX1 promoter/terminator, alpha-factor secretion signal); E. coli DH5alpha for cloning. 11 parts listed, including new basic parts BBa_26O5NV2L (Pat2), BBa_26DL196B (Ede1), BBa_26NDIHU2 (Me11s) and three composites.
screen.best_evidence: /results: a full functional panel on purified protein - water-holding capacity 97.58% for Pat2 at 4% vs 42.72% for the control, emulsifying activity index 589.57 m2/g and stability index 91.43 min for Pat2 vs 285.57 m2/g and 31.02 min for the reference, thermal aggregation delta-A600 of 0.19 for Me11s vs 0.30 for Pat2, and texture profile analysis of patties giving Pat2 cohesiveness 81.94% and springiness 93.28%.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, at the level of priorities: six expert interviews and a 304-response consumer survey identified texture deviation and water-holding as the decisive repurchase barriers, which is what the functional assay panel was then built to measure.
screen.reason: A clean, coherent medal project that carries three new parts all the way to a measured food product, which is more than most. It falls short of finalist calibre because the three 'DBTL cycles' are three parallel constructions of the same design rather than iteration - nothing is redesigned in response to a result - and the functional data are single measurements with no replicates or error bars (the BCA table is also internally inconsistent with the text, listing concentrations up to 1.166 mg/mL while the text says 0.0011-0.0503 mg/mL). Thermal stability is inferred from a single A600 change. No attributions page, no model, no hardware.
screen.field_notes: Cataverse-Shanghai (Food & Nutrition, China) runs ECOECHO, which expresses plant storage proteins in yeast as functional ingredients that could replace thickener additives in plant-based meat. Pat2 (1119 bp, Solanum stenotomum), Ede1 (1479 bp, Cannabis sativa) and Me11s (1374 bp, Manihot esculenta) were cloned into pPICZalphaA by homologous recombination, sequence-verified, linearised with SacI and transformed into Pichia pastoris GS115, then induced with methanol and purified on His-tag affinity columns with SDS-PAGE bands in the 50-60 kDa region and BCA quantification. A growth comparison across YPD, YPG and BMGY selected 2% YPG with a 3-4 day expression period. The functional panel is the strongest part: water-holding capacity (Pat2 97.58% at 4% against a 42.72% control), emulsifying activity and stability indices (Pat2 589.57 m2/g and 91.43 min versus 285.57 m2/g and 31.02 min for the reference, with all three recombinants above the reference on EAI), thermal aggregation by delta-A600 (Me11s most stable at 0.19), and texture profile analysis of real patties made by adding each purified protein to a soy texturised protein base, where Pat2 gave the highest cohesiveness (81.94%) and springiness (93.28%) and Ede1 the lowest hardness and chewiness, suggested for paste or elderly-friendly formats. Integrated human practices covers six named specialists and a 304-response consumer survey that established texture as the main repurchase barrier. Weaknesses: no replicates or error bars on any functional measurement, an internally inconsistent BCA table, three parallel build cycles rather than true iteration, and empty attributions, model and parts standard pages (parts live on a non-standard /part-collection page).

screen.project_title: BioRestore — biosynthetic pigments anchored by CBM3 fusion enzymes for cultural relic restoration
screen.what_they_built: Four pigment-synthesizing enzymes (CtPOD2, CrtZ, melA, IndC) expressed and purified from E. coli, characterized for pH, temperature and substrate dependence, plus CBM3 fusion versions intended to anchor the pigment onto cellulose surfaces in situ.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning, BL21(DE3) for expression, pET28a backbone. One new basic part (CtPOD2, BBa_26BLEEPT), new data added to four existing basic parts, and eight new composite parts (pET28a-enzyme and pET28a-CBM3-enzyme series).
screen.best_evidence: /results Part 1: SDS-PAGE showing all four purified proteins at expected sizes (CtPOD2 39.5 kDa, IndC 149.6 kDa, melA 72 kDa, CrtZ 24.4 kDa), plus A405 time-courses for the CtPOD2 precarthamin-to-carthamin reaction identifying an optimal enzyme:substrate:buffer ratio and pH 6.5 optimum, with no conversion at pH 7.0; CBM3-CtPOD2 cellulose binding assay reported in Part 2.
screen.hp_integration: Reported at length (8,640 words of HP plus 6,756 of education), with relic-conservation stakeholders framing the in-situ anchoring requirement, but the pack does not show a crisp before-and-after design change traceable to a named conversation.
screen.reason: Clean, complete wet lab with gels, sequencing, purification and enzyme characterization, but only two engineering cycles, no model or hardware, no attributions page, and a literal 'we contributed a total of X new parts' placeholder left on the contribution page. A strong gold-medal profile rather than a finalist one.
screen.field_notes: Cataverse-Union (Fashion & Cosmetics, CHN) built BioRestore, a biosynthetic pigment system for cultural relic restoration. Module 1 expressed four pigment enzymes in pET28a/BL21(DE3) — CtPOD2 (precarthamin to carthamin), CrtZ (beta-carotene to zeaxanthin), melA (tyrosine to melanin) and IndC (glutamine to indigoidine) — with gel-verified inserts, Genewiz sequencing showing no mutations, Ni-NTA purification and SDS-PAGE bands at 39.5, 24.4, 72 and 149.6 kDa. Enzyme characterization covers reaction ratio, pH and temperature per enzyme, read mainly as A405 time courses plus photographed colour change; CtPOD2 peaked at pH 6.5 and was inactive at pH 7.0. Module 2 fused CBM3 to the enzymes so the pigment anchors onto cellulose, with pH, temperature and a cellulose binding assay for CBM3-CtPOD2. Parts: CtPOD2 is new (BBa_26BLEEPT), four existing parts gained new data, and eight pET28a composites were registered; the contribution page still reads 'a total of X new parts', and there is no parts page, no model page, no hardware and no attributions page. Replication is not stated for the enzyme assays. Outreach is heavy: 8,640 words of human practices, 6,756 of education and 7,433 of entrepreneurship, plus a 7,160-word notebook.

screen.project_title: Pestisense — aptamer-based fluorescence detection of rotenone and malathion
screen.what_they_built: A fluorophore-quencher aptamer assay: FAM-labelled DNA aptamers paired with short complementary quencher strands, so that pesticide binding should displace the quencher and restore fluorescence. Two aptamers (AX for rotenone, MalR for malathion) were generated computationally rather than by SELEX.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Cell-free DNA oligonucleotides only, no chassis; 10 Registry entries listed on a 167-word parts page (aptamers plus quencher strands), one BBa ID appearing twice in the table.
screen.best_evidence: /results §05: quencher-functionality tests show fluorescence rising when QDNA is omitted (AT11 +130.6% and +479.1% in two trials; AX10 +28.55%; AX12 +43.63%), supporting quenching; the binding data are weaker, with AX12 giving a 22.3% fluorescence rise from 1 to 20 uM rotenone and the team itself writing that target binding remains unconfirmed.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — nine stakeholder interviews across bioethics, agriculture, neuroscience and health, plus a 500+ response survey, mapped onto a four-value bioethics framework; the influence shows mainly in framing, values and mini-projects rather than in a documented change to the assay design.
screen.reason: The team is commendably honest, but by its own analysis nothing was shown to work: fluorescence trends are non-monotonic, replicates disagree (AX12 +43.6% then -14.8%), AT11 signal sits two orders of magnitude below the others, and no binding was confirmed by any orthogonal method. No limit of detection, no specificity panel, no real sample. A thin wiki overall (results 1,805 words, notebook 63 words, attributions effectively empty). Solidly a medal-level attempt, not a finalist.
screen.field_notes: CCA-SanDiego (Agriculture, USA) built Pestisense, a fluorophore-quencher DNA aptamer assay for the pesticides rotenone and malathion, motivated by pesticide neurotoxicity links to Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease. Three rotenone systems (published AT11 plus computationally generated AX with 10-nt and 12-nt quencher strands) and two malathion systems (published MalA1 plus generated MalR) were tested in two reagent orders: quencher bound first then pesticide added, and pesticide bound to the aptamer first then quencher added. Quenching itself was demonstrated (fluorescence falls as QDNA concentration rises; rises when QDNA is omitted), but pesticide-dependent responses were small and inconsistent, with drops at 20-50 uM, an unexplained 229.7% AT11 spike at 10 uM, AT11 signal two orders of magnitude below the others, and disagreement between replicate trial sets; the team concludes binding is unconfirmed and proposes SPR or MST for future validation. Modelling used Unafold secondary structures, 3dRNA/DNA tertiary models and MAWS/AptaLoop for de novo aptamer generation, validating a prior team's software contribution. Ten parts are listed, including one duplicated BBa ID. Human practices covers nine Zoom stakeholder meetings and a 500+ response survey organised around justice, autonomy, beneficence and non-maleficence. Notebook is 63 words and the attributions page is empty.

screen.project_title: PanCrisp: amplification-free Cas13a detection of salivary miRNAs for early pancreatic cancer screening
screen.what_they_built: A LwaCas13a collateral-cleavage assay with fluorophore-quencher reporter, designed around a five-miRNA salivary panel for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, with one channel (miR-216a-5p) taken through to a working readout, plus a low-cost fluorescence reader.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Cell-free LwaCas13a ribonucleoprotein; IDT ssDNA oligos annealed and T7-transcribed into crRNA and synthetic target RNA; RNaseAlert reporter. ~19 new BBa parts for the crRNA/target library.
screen.best_evidence: /proof-of-concept Results: at 60 min, 0.5 ng, 1 ng and 300 ng targets give 621, 473 and 437 RFU above baseline versus scramble at 58 and no-template at -37, a seven- to tenfold separation without amplification; signal still detectable at 0.05 ng (190 RFU); five wells per condition with standard deviations reported; detection floor placed between 0.01 and 0.05 ng.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in at least one concrete instance: Dr Jaspal's feedback on reliability and reproducibility led them to drop an oral-microbiome channel that would have needed a second Cas13 ortholog, trading breadth for precision on one well-characterised channel. Engagement spans clinicians, PDAC survivors, an FDA representative, CDC Charlotte and PanCAN.
screen.reason: Methodologically the most careful wet lab in the batch for its size: replicates, no-template and scramble controls, kinetic traces, a quantified detection floor and an exceptionally candid account of three mid-range dilutions that inexplicably gave no signal. But scope is narrow: one of five markers, synthetic RNA in buffer only, no saliva matrix, no panel demonstration, and no attributions page at all. Excellent gold/special-award profile rather than top-2.
screen.field_notes: Charlotte-HS (North Carolina, USA, Diagnostics village) built PanCrisp, an amplification-free LwaCas13a assay reading salivary miRNAs for early pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma detection, designed around five markers (miR-21-5p, miR-23a-3p, miR-23b-3p, miR-216a-5p, miR-29c-3p) each in its own reaction because collateral cleavage cannot multiplex in one tube. Only the miR-216a-5p channel was taken to data: kinetic traces rise and plateau by about 40 min; at a 60-minute endpoint the 0.5, 1 and 300 ng conditions reach 621, 473 and 437 RFU above baseline against a scramble control at 58 and no-template at -37, with signal still visible at 0.05 ng and a detection floor between 0.01 and 0.05 ng. Five replicate wells per condition with standard deviations; the team reports that 10, 50 and 100 ng wells were flat, attributes it to a plate-loading error rather than biology, and refuses to present a dose-response curve until it is repeated. They also note the scramble control drifts up after about 150 min, which is why they report a one-hour endpoint. Supporting work: a 6.9k-word model page, software, a low-cost fluorescence reader, 19 Registry parts, and a wide human-practices programme including clinicians, PDAC survivors, an FDA representative, CDC Charlotte and PanCAN, with a documented pivot away from an oral-microbiome channel. No attributions page exists; the results page is empty and the findings live on /proof-of-concept.

screen.project_title: Shewanella oneidensis co-culture biosensor for seafood freshness (TMA to blue amilCP)
screen.what_they_built: They designed a two-strain Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 co-culture in which a cold-induced periplasmic trimethylamine monooxygenase converts spoilage gas TMA to TMAO, and a second strain reports TMAO via the native tor promoter driving the blue chromoprotein amilCP. Work reached verified clones but no colour output.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 as the cold-tolerant chassis, E. coli for intermediate cloning; broad-host-range vectors pDSK519 (PcspA-RBS43-TorA signal peptide-tmm-B0015) and pBBR1MCS-1 (PtorECAD-RBS43-amilCP-B0015); nine parts registered this season plus reused amilCP (BBa_K4594027), RBS43 (BBa_K3814047) and BBa_B0015.
screen.best_evidence: /results final reciprocal PCR of 13 September: PriACP amplified from MR-1B clones 1 and 3 and not from MR-1A clones 2 and 4, with PriTMM giving the reciprocal pattern, supported by reciprocal antibiotic cross-selection on 12 September. The page itself states plainly that TMA-dependent amilCP expression, response time, detection limit, co-culture signal transfer and low-temperature performance were not measured.
screen.hp_integration: Honest but thin and mostly commercial: 83 consumer survey responses (85.5% rank freshness first, 60.2% would buy, over 90% cap the price below 15 RMB) and two in-person seller interviews after a digital seller survey drew no replies; the input informs pricing and positioning rather than altering the genetic design, and the team logs its non-responses.
screen.reason: The wiki is unusually well made and unusually honest, and the three-iteration design story (two plasmids in one cell, then tmm replacing a non-existent Tor gene, then splitting across two co-cultured strains) shows real reasoning, but the project never demonstrated function: no TMA-dependent blue, no detection limit, no cold-chain performance, no sequence confirmation of the constructs, and the Contribution page is empty. Aspect 2 cannot be scored high on construction-stage evidence alone.
screen.field_notes: China SUIS GB (Food & Nutrition village, China) built a seafood-freshness biosensor around Shewanella oneidensis MR-1, chosen because E. coli shuts down at cold-chain temperatures of 0-4 C. The circuit is split across two co-cultured strains to escape plasmid incompatibility: pDSK519 carries PcspA-RBS43-TorA signal peptide-tmm so trimethylamine monooxygenase is exported to the periplasm and oxidises gaseous TMA to TMAO, while pBBR1MCS-1 carries the torECAD promoter driving amilCP so TMAO turns the cells blue; only volatile TMA is sampled because fish muscle is full of endogenous TMAO. Laboratory records are presented date by date with original gel photographs, including a tmm/pDSK519 tube label swap caught and corrected, repeatedly weak 897 bp amilCP digests, measured insert concentrations of 7.3-9.7 ng/uL, and PriTMM primer false positives that forced a reciprocal cross-validation. The final evidence is that reciprocal PCR, which supports pDSK519-tmm in MR-1A clones 2 and 4 and pBBR1MCS-1-amilCP in MR-1B clones 1 and 3; the page states explicitly what was not measured. The Model page is an interactive tube-diameter optimisation balancing colour depth, fill time and cost, with sourced prices and literature constants, and the engineering page quantifies expected cold-temperature penalties (MR-1 doubling time about 67 h at 3 C). Attribution is per-member and detailed; the team says it has no institutional partners or industry mentors.

screen.project_title: Re-CDI Alert: a p-cresol-sensing EcN strain that reports and treats C. difficile recurrence
screen.what_they_built: Engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 carrying the PcrSR-Pcmh two-component p-cresol sensor from Aromatoleum aromaticum EbN1, driving GFP and then a secreted PelB-E3-FLAG anti-TcdB nanobody, as a gut sensor-therapeutic for post-treatment CDI recurrence.
screen.chassis_and_parts: EcN (pMUT1/pMUT2/flhDC-deleted) and BL21 for comparison; dual-plasmid pET28a system. 17 basic + 7 composite parts registered, including BBa_26KCZUBK (PcrS), BBa_260BOJS1 (PcrR), BBa_26ZJ2ARU (UBS-Pcmh-L, 1397 bp), BBa_2664OKFT (E3 nanobody core), plus reused registry parts (J23111, B0032, sfGFP).
screen.best_evidence: /engineering and /measurement: OD600-normalised GFP concentration-response for EΔ-JSRL with a discernible rise at ~500 nM-1 µM p-cresol and a working range of 1 µM-1 mM, triplicate wells, spaced-well plate layout and background subtraction; at 10 µM, o-cresol, m-cresol and phenol stayed near the uninduced control. /contribution Fig. 3: purified E3-containing preparation binds immobilised TcdB with an apparent ELISA EC50 of ~0.27 nM, with the team explicitly noting binding is not neutralisation.
screen.hp_integration: Yes. Clinician interviews moved the target from the general population to patients with a confirmed high recurrence risk, and reframed the China problem from low incidence to under-diagnosis; four documented HP stages also drove the biosafety framing and the switch from a diagnostic-only to a sense-and-treat design.
screen.reason: Six DBTL cycles including three documented construction failures (large deletions, a frameshift missed by colony PCR, failed inverse-PCR repair) that were diagnosed and fixed, then a sensor with a real dose-response, analogue selectivity controls and a quantified nanobody binding assay. Careful hedging language throughout. Main gaps: no attributions page at all and no standalone results page, and the engineered EcN knockout chassis plus nanobody look likely to have outside origin - aspect 6 needs checking in a full read.
screen.field_notes: CHINAGuangdongShimen (Therapeutics, China) builds Re-CDI Alert, an EcN live biotherapeutic that senses p-cresol, a metabolite produced by C. difficile via HpdBCA decarboxylation of p-hydroxyphenylacetate, as an early warning of CDI recurrence. The sensor is the natural PcrSR two-component system from Aromatoleum aromaticum EbN1 with the UBS-Pcmh-L regulatory region (1397 bp) upstream of sfGFP, assembled on modified pET28a as a dual-plasmid system; after three failed assemblies the sequence-verified J23111-pcrSR-2 was obtained and moved into EcN delta-pMUT1 delta-pMUT2 delta-flhDC. Measurement work is unusually deliberate for a high school team: OD600-normalised fluorescence, spaced replicate wells after observing cross-well interference at adjacent concentrations, triplicates, a BL21 vs EcN chassis comparison and a p-cresol growth-tolerance assay. Response onset sits at roughly 500 nM-1 µM with a working range of 1 µM-1 mM, and at 10 µM o-cresol, m-cresol and phenol stayed near the uninduced control. GFP was then replaced with PelB-E3-FLAG plus a His-GSG segment; SDS-PAGE, western blot and ELISA support expression and TcdB binding, with an apparent EC50 near 0.27 nM for the purified preparation. The parts collection has 17 basic and 7 composite entries and deliberately retains two failed early sensing designs as development records. Human practices runs four stages across clinicians, microbiome researchers, regulators and a public survey. There is no attributions page and no separate results page; figures live inside the engineering, measurement and contribution pages.

screen.project_title: VINALYSIS: biosensor for smoke-taint phenols in wine grapes
screen.what_they_built: A field kit to detect guaiacol and syringol in smoke-exposed grapes, using guaiacol-binding aptamer riboswitches driving sfGFP in E. coli and a DesX transcription factor/promoter pair read in a cell-free system, with a 3D-printed heated, stirred fluorescence reader.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli (XL1-Blue) and NEBExpress cell-free system; five new parts including DesX (BBa_26W6S5SR), DesX-responsive promoter (BBa_26DQG804), G-15-2a aptamer (BBa_26DDQ9QR) and two riboswitch composites; J23100, B0034 and RFC1000 standards.
screen.best_evidence: /results: cell-free syringol dilution series shows fluorescence above water controls with A9 (no syringol) dropping, but no concentration-dependent trend; guaiacol riboswitch plate assay in E. coli was a clean negative result — no guaiacol-dependent fluorescence above LoD, with LB autofluorescence ~85% of signal and Welch's t-tests reported. PCR of pT7-plamGFP gave no bands.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — stakeholder conversations with winemakers shaped the kit format and the switch from live E. coli to cell-free (/alternative-platform), but the HP page is thin on how advice changed the biology.
screen.reason: Admirably honest but the core sensing claim is unproven: PCR failed, the syringol plasmid never grew, the cell-free kit was stored 60 C too warm, and the guaiacol riboswitch assay is explicitly a negative result. A 28k-word engineering page and 16 models cannot substitute for a part that works. No parts page at all (word count 0) hurts aspect 8.
screen.field_notes: City-of-London-UK (Agriculture, GBR) targeted smoke taint in wine, where wildfire phenols bind to grape sugars and are released during fermentation. They designed two sensing routes: guaiacol-binding DNA aptamer G-15-2a converted into riboswitches driving sfGFP in E. coli, and the DesX transcription factor with its responsive promoter read in a NEBExpress cell-free system; five new parts are claimed on /contribution but the /parts page is empty. Lab outcomes were largely negative: the pT7-plamGFP PCR produced no bands, syringol-detection plasmid transformants never grew on kanamycin, and the 20-concentration guaiacol riboswitch plate assay found no guaiacol-dependent fluorescence above LoD, with LB autofluorescence accounting for about 85% of the signal. The cell-free syringol series showed fluorescence above water controls without a concentration trend, after the kit was stored a month at -20 C instead of -80 C. The team documents these limitations frankly, runs seven-plus DBTL cycles, builds a 16-model dry lab and a heated, stirred battery-powered fluorescence reader with a defined bill of materials.

screen.project_title: SCOPE — Sustainable Cellulose: Optimizing Products for Everyone
screen.what_they_built: A dual-plasmid attempt to make bacterial cellulose in E. coli C41(DE3): a pgm/galU (UGPase) precursor-supply device characterised under three promoters, plus a proposed BcsABCD operon and in-silico constitutively active BcsAB mutants. Alongside it, a comparative life-cycle analysis of bacterial cellulose versus four mask substrates and HALO, a wheelchair-mounted modular lab organiser.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli TOP10 (cloning) and C41(DE3) (intended expression); pBR322 backbone. New parts galU (BBa_260WJPAC), pgm (BBa_26408P02), pgm+galU+GFP composite (BBa_26N9CJL5), BcsABCD composite (BBa_26XA9UQN); existing BBa_J23100, BBa_J435350, BBa_K4987003/BBa_K1949001 (pCspA/pCold), BBa_E0040/BBa_K1911005, BBa_K1321334.
screen.best_evidence: /results: diagnostic OE-PCR gel where all three promoter–device junctions amplified, band sized against a ladder standard curve at ~3798 bp versus an expected ~3600 bp (5.5% deviation); Anderson and pCspA transformants later fluoresced. Against this, /results also reports the verification digest gave 4.3 kb instead of the expected ~8.0 kb and the GFP assay 'showed no significant increase in GFP over 8 hours'.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in a traceable way: Mohammed Abiola pushed them from biodegradability claims to a full LCA, Dr. Buldum changed backbone (low-copy pBR322) and strain (C41(DE3)), Dr. Ellis drove the UDP-glucose/inducible-promoter strategy, and Chloe Franklin's two sessions produced five named changes to the accessibility audit tool and three to HALO.
screen.reason: Honest, well-structured cloning narrative with real troubleshooting, but the central claim — more UDP-glucose, therefore more cellulose — has no functional data at all. No cellulose was ever made, the UGPase/fluorescence assays are explicitly future work ('We are currently running these experiments'), a verification digest contradicts the construct, and the BcsAB work is molecular dynamics only. Aspects 2 and 8 cannot reach finalist level on assembly gels.
screen.field_notes: Concordia-Shanghai (CHN, Fashion & Cosmetics) attacked bacterial cellulose scale-up after their own LCA found BC has the lowest water demand of five mask substrates (6.3 mL per 1 cm2 x 0.2 mm functional unit) but the highest carbon-related burden, making yield per unit energy the engineering target. The wet lab overexpressed pgm and galU in E. coli C41(DE3) on pBR322 under T7lac, pCspA and Anderson promoters with a GFP tag; 3A assembly failed on an overlooked internal HindIII site and poor gel resolution, so they pivoted to overlap-extension PCR and verified junctions by diagnostic PCR. Fluorescent Anderson and pCspA transformants appeared, but a verification digest gave 4.3 kb rather than ~8.0 kb and the GFP activity assay showed no significant increase over 8 h, so no promoter characterisation or cellulose yield data exists; a second iteration with pCold, eGFP and a higher-copy backbone was ordered but not reported. Dry lab ran 50 ns MD on an AlphaFold BcsAB model and found R583A and E370A/R583A maintained stable UDP-glucose hydrogen bonding while wild-type and E370A did not, proposing a c-di-GMP-independent synthase. The third strand is HALO, a 3D-printed five-subsystem wheelchair-mounted lab organiser developed over two DBTL cycles with wheelchair-using scientists, plus a lab accessibility audit tool revised on specific stakeholder feedback. Human practices is unusually well-logged (stakeholder, insight, project response, limitation, next validation per interview), and the LCA, CAD files and MD-to-proteoliposome pipeline are offered as contributions.

screen.project_title: Engineered Barley Stripe Mosaic Virus-like particles as a targeted doxorubicin carrier for triple-negative breast cancer
screen.what_they_built: BSMV VLP rods expressed in E. coli with engineered inner-channel cysteines for site-selective thiol-Michael conjugation of doxorubicin, a SpyTag/SnoopTag-Catcher surface display of iRGD and Peptide 22 plus endosomal-escape peptides, and a single-plasmid orthogonal pTet/pRha dual expression cassette (second iteration adds a constitutive RhaS activator).
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3)/ClearColi BL21(DE3) with pET and pFREE2 backbones; parts referenced include BBa_2613TQO3 (mTurquoise2), BBa_K2844007 (mNeonGreen), BBa_265ACZ8A, BBa_K4575016, BBa_K4800001, BBa_261NHAMA, BBa_264KTY5D, BBa_26OA6T7W, BBa_26OCSMCO. There is no Parts page on the wiki.
screen.best_evidence: /results Tables 1-2: conjugation labeling efficiency and fold change across four inner-radius cysteine candidates - fluorescein 24.7% to 70.5% (up to 2.9x over the 199C control) and doxorubicin 27.8% to 40.4% (up to 1.4x), with SnoopTag (no cysteine) at N.D. for DOX; TEM (Fig 5, 17) shows rods still assemble after cysteine insertion and look "fuzzy" after Tag/Catcher conjugation, and SDS-PAGE (Fig 16) shows the expected ~75 kDa conjugate band. Cassette characterisation Table 4: with RhaS, mTurquoise2 reaches 3.2x and mNeonGreen 2.7x over the uninduced control with no detectable cross-talk.
screen.hp_integration: Partly: expert input clearly shaped the design (Dr. Quarterman steered the team from pancreatic to TNBC, Ms. Rammohan proposed cysteine conjugation at the C-terminus, Dr. Sullivan introduced Tag/Catcher, Dr. Shah pointed to EGFR), and the Delaware Breast Cancer Coalition's use of Spanish and Haitian Creole translators led to translated wiki sections - but the page is organised around a "BSMV" values acronym rather than an integrated-HP method, and community engagement did not change the biology.
screen.reason: Technically the most sophisticated build in the batch and genuinely data-backed: a modeling funnel (52 candidates to 6 to 2) that fed real cloning, TEM-confirmed assembly, quantified drug conjugation with proper negative and positive controls, and a characterised orthogonal two-promoter cassette offered as a reusable tool. Worth a full read. Two serious drags the panel must weigh: there is no Parts, Attributions or Safety page at all, and the work sits in a University of Delaware lab with SMEs supplying each key design idea, so aspects 5, 6 and 8 are exposed.
screen.field_notes: Delaware high-school team (Oncology) building a rod-shaped plant-virus VLP from Barley Stripe Mosaic Virus into a targeted doxorubicin carrier for triple-negative breast cancer, chosen because Delaware ranks first in US TNBC incidence. Because BSMV has no native cysteines, they brute-forced 52 inner-channel cysteine insertions, used AlphaFold plus PyMOL to measure side-chain distance from the rod axis, shortlisted 6 and tested 4 in vitro; all four still assembled into rods by TEM, and labeling efficiencies reached 70.5% for fluorescein and 40.4% for doxorubicin, with IR candidate 2 carried forward. Surface display uses SpyTag/SnoopTag-Catcher with iRGD and Peptide 22; a single-plasmid orthogonal pTet/pRha cassette on a pFREE2 backbone was characterised by FL/OD kinetics over two iterations, the second adding a constitutive RhaS activator (mTurquoise2 3.2x). They also report a cloning gotcha worth reusing: pTet operator homology drops Gibson efficiency to about 5% correct constructs. Modeling code (mutator.py, structure.py, cysteine_modeling.py, patterned_display.py) is published. No TNBC cell testing yet - efficacy is future work - and the wiki has no Parts, Attributions or Safety page.

screen.project_title: Phosphate-responsive PhoR/PhoB circuit driving YjiC glycosylation of fisetin for UTI inflammation
screen.what_they_built: A planned E. coli genetic switch in which the PhoR/PhoB low-phosphate pathway drives the glycosyltransferase YjiC to glycosylate fisetin, a flavonoid proposed as an anti-inflammatory for recurrent UTIs.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli; a pho-box promoter plasmid with GFP to be swapped for codon-optimised yjiC. Parts listed: BBa_259KUFB0, BBa_25LNMNQ1, BBa_26E07M6T, BBa_26O5WUA2, plus reused BBa_K4942004, BBa_K5432031, BBa_K737023.
screen.best_evidence: /results: a gel showing two bands from a double restriction digest of the GFP-containing plasmid, plus a NanoDrop reading of 4.8 ng/uL for the gel-purified backbone. Everything else is COPASI simulation, e.g. 28.8 uM glycosylated fisetin at 1 uM phosphate versus 0.9 uM at 1000 uM.
screen.hp_integration: Not demonstrated in the screening pack: the human-practices page is long (7,856 words) but the pack shows no instance of stakeholder input changing a design decision.
screen.reason: The wet lab reached only a restriction digest; no construct was assembled, no protein expressed, no glycosylation measured. The five 'DBTL cycles' are parameter sweeps in COPASI with an admitted placeholder glycosylation rate, so they are modelling runs rather than build-test iterations. Nothing here can compete for a finalist slot.
screen.field_notes: DBHS-CA (USA, Therapeutics village) proposed nutrient-controlled glycosylation: the E. coli PhoR/PhoB two-component system driving yjiC to glycosylate fisetin and improve its solubility as an anti-inflammatory for recurrent UTIs. Wet lab stopped at a GFP-removal double digest, evidenced by one gel with two bands and a 4.8 ng/uL NanoDrop reading on the purified backbone; Gibson assembly and all expression and glycosylation assays were never performed, which the team states plainly. The dry lab is the substance: a six-species, seven-reaction COPASI kinetic model giving an active-fraction switch half-point at 4 uM phosphate, roughly 58-fold more YjiC at 1 uM than 1300 uM phosphate, and five parameter runs (baseline, 3x expression, 0.3x expression, tighter promoter, faster fisetin decay) showing that leak control beats expression scaling, with the tighter promoter cutting off-state product 45% without hurting on-state yield. The team flags the glycosylation rate as a placeholder and treats outputs as rankings rather than predictions. The description and human-practices pages are very long; the attributions page is 71 words.

screen.project_title: Fluorosplice — split-Broccoli catalytic hairpin assembly splice-junction sensor
screen.what_they_built: An enzyme-free nucleic-acid biosensor: two kinetically trapped hairpins carrying halves of the Broccoli aptamer that should reconstitute a DFHBI-1T pocket only when a specific exon-exon junction is present, designed with ViennaRNA and tested in HEK293 cells against a luciferase/chimeric-intron reporter.
screen.chassis_and_parts: HEK293 mammalian cells, synthetic PS/2'OMe-modified RNA oligos from GenScript, luciferase splicing reporter plasmid; no BBa parts found anywhere and the Parts page is empty.
screen.best_evidence: /results: at 10x and 20x RNA dosing (420 nM and 840 nM) wells with H1+H2+DFHBI-1T showed bright green fluorescence while dye-only wells showed minimal signal — qualitative microscopy only. The luciferase ASO assay showed no consistent concentration-dependent effect and large replicate SDs; junction discrimination was never demonstrated.
screen.hp_integration: Human practices and entrepreneurship pages are substantial, but nothing shown changes the sensor architecture; the design changes come from lab failures, not stakeholders.
screen.reason: Honest four-round troubleshooting narrative, but the central claim — isoform-specific detection — is never shown. Evidence is qualitative fluorescence consistent with aptamer folding without any junction specificity, the ASO/luciferase data are internally inconsistent, and no parts were registered or documented.
screen.field_notes: DelNorte-SD 2026 (Fluorosplice, Diagnostics, San Diego) built a split-Broccoli catalytic hairpin assembly sensor meant to light up on a specific exon-exon junction, using ViennaRNA to tune toehold length, lock-stem stability and off-state leak, and adapting the published CHARGE CHA framework. Four wet-lab rounds in HEK293 cells are documented with unusual candour: round 1 killed all cells through simultaneous reverse transfection of plasmid and RNA; fixes were staggered 24 h transfections, hemocytometer-standardised seeding at 100,000 cells/well, a shortened 4 h readout window and 10x/20x RNA dosing (420 and 840 nM), which finally produced bright green fluorescence absent from dye-only controls. A column-5 media washout killed the signal, explained correctly by reversible DFHBI-1T binding. The luciferase/ASO splicing-modulation arm failed: luminescence was flat across ASO conditions with a vertical plate gradient attributed to uneven plasmid uptake and to ASOs arriving 24 h after the reporter. No registry parts, empty Parts page, no model page content. Future work proposes a two-colour ratiometric spliced/unspliced sensor.

screen.project_title: ECLIPSE — LATTE and HybriDock-Pep peptide-design software driving a LOCKR-based malaria diagnostic
screen.what_they_built: Two CPU-friendly protein-design tools (HybriDock-Pep for peptide docking/scoring, LATTE for grafting binders into the LOCKR latch and optimising charge), used to design PfLDH binders grafted into LucCage, plus a coffee-ring droplet model and a custom temperature/humidity chamber.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3), pET28a(+) and pACYCDuet-1. Nineteen Registry parts including PfLB-1 (BBa_262FI0XF), PfLB-1.5 charge-optimised (BBa_265TUSL2), PfLDH baseline lucCage (BBa_26UA0L8M), PfLDH charge-optimised lucCage (BBa_26TCYKK2) and His-Tev-lucKey (BBa_26HBQM4N).
screen.best_evidence: /results: the strongest experimental data are external — GenScript tested three constructs at 16 h/15 C and 4 h/37 C with SDS-PAGE plus anti-His western blot and BSA quantity references, and Dr. McShan's lab ran HisTrap FF chromatograms (elution peak ~75.6 mAU rising to ~125.5 mAU against a saturated ~2,800 mAU flowthrough). The team's own gels never showed a band at the expected molecular weight: pre- and post-induction lanes were indistinguishable.
screen.hp_integration: Partly. Dr. Fox (UCB) corrected their SDS-PAGE loading method, the LOCKR authors Langan and Boyken advised on testing the software tools, and Dr. Kraft reshaped the outreach framing; the feedback improved methods and communication rather than redirecting the design.
screen.reason: The software and hardware work is real and the failure reporting is admirably candid, but nothing was shown to function: no in-house expression confirmed, no binding, no switch activation, no luminescence, no diagnostic readout. The expression and purification evidence that does exist came from GenScript and an external university lab, which also pulls aspect 6 down. Nineteen Registry parts are deposited on the strength of designs rather than data. Aspect 2 is close to the floor, so this cannot be a top-2 project however good the tooling is.
screen.field_notes: Denmark-GA (USA, Software & AI village) built ECLIPSE around two tools: HybriDock-Pep, a peptide docking and scoring pipeline (pose generation, relaxation, clash removal, geometry-based ML scorer) meant to beat AF2-Multimer and HADDOCK 2.4 on protein-peptide interactions, and LATTE, a CPU-only tool that grafts a binder into the LOCKR latch register, scans for acidic residues that interfere with lucKey binding, optimises charge, and sweeps lucKey concentration and temperature for target fold-change. They applied them to PfLDH, designing PfLB-1 and the charge-optimised PfLB-1.5, grafted into LucCage, with a coffee-ring droplet assay as the intended readout and a self-built temperature/humidity chamber (targeting 22-34 C and 25-90% RH, modelled on regions with HRP2 deletions) to test it under field-relevant conditions. The modeling page is the largest on the wiki (~14,000 words), combining Hu-Larson evaporation, Deegan edge-weighted evaporation and lubrication theory to predict how a drying droplet concentrates PfLDH at its edge. Wet lab did not work: transformations initially gave almost no colonies until mentors suggested concentrating cells; pre- and post-induction SDS-PAGE lanes were identical so expression was never confirmed in-house; the team lists its own causes candidly (no positive or negative controls, plasmids never sequence-verified before use, 100 mL culture cap, Coomassie insensitivity, inconsistent lane loading, a non-aliquoted IPTG stock degraded by repeated freeze-thaw, and forgetting to take pre-induction samples so untransformed BL21 lysate was substituted). The only expression and purification evidence comes from outside: GenScript evaluated three constructs under two induction conditions with SDS-PAGE and anti-His western blot, and Dr. Andrew McShan's lab at Georgia Tech ran Ni-NTA FPLC purifications. Nineteen parts are registered, but none is shown to bind PfLDH or to open the LOCKR switch, and no luminescence or diagnostic result appears anywhere. Strong education (~9,000 words) and entrepreneurship (~7,000 words) pages; team and notebook pages are nearly empty.

screen.project_title: A chitosan–genipin immobilized dual-enzyme system to reduce acrylamide in fried food
screen.what_they_built: An LEA-peptide-stabilised, immobilised dual-enzyme preparation (L-asparaginase plus glucose oxidase) applied to potato slices before frying to remove both acrylamide precursors, asparagine and reducing sugars.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning and BL21(DE3) for expression, pET-28a backbone; carrier is genipin-crosslinked chitosan. Thirteen new parts listed for the LEA module alone (LEA1–LEA5 basic parts BBa_26RNKSSG, BBa_262X550Y, BBa_26L8XFKN, BBa_26LOJ66X, BBa_26M5PDSB, a GS linker, and pET28a-GFP-LEA composites), plus ASN-LEA4 and GOX-LEA4 fusions.
screen.best_evidence: /results, potato food model: standardised 1 g slices treated with immobilised ASN, immobilised GOX or both, fried at 130 C for 200 s, acrylamide by ELISA — A450 approximately 0.58 untreated, 0.53 ASN, 0.49 GOX, 0.38 dual, reported as a statistically significant synergy. Supporting: GFP-LEA4 retained ~90% fluorescence after 30 min at 60 C versus ~70% for free GFP; immobilisation efficiency ASN >97%, GOX >85%; after ten reuse cycles GOX kept 72.2% and ASN 46% of initial activity (86.7% and 71% after five).
screen.hp_integration: Yes — thirteen rounds including a public survey, Banan Wanda food-street merchants, a mooncake factory visit and two peer-review milestones; reusability and recovery were prioritised because food scientists and industry engineers repeatedly named single-use enzyme cost as the adoption barrier, and the team re-validated its revisions with the same experts.
screen.reason: The only team in this batch whose chain runs all the way from a screened protein module to a measured effect in a real food: LEA4 selected on GFP data, carried into two fusion enzymes that keep activity and gain thermostability, immobilised with quantified loading, recovery and ten-cycle reuse, then shown to reduce acrylamide in fried potato with a dual-enzyme synergy. That is aspects 2 and 4 satisfied with numbers. A full read should test replication, the ELISA quantification (A450 only, no ppb calibration shown), and how much of the bench work was student-executed.
screen.field_notes: DEPU (CHN, Food & Nutrition) targeted acrylamide, an IARC Group 2A contaminant formed above 120 C from asparagine and reducing sugars, with a chitosan–genipin immobilised dual-enzyme preparation of L-asparaginase and glucose oxidase applied before frying so cooking method and flavour are unchanged. Four DBTL cycles each generated data for the next: five LEA-derived peptides from Polypedilum vanderplanki motifs were screened as GFP fusions across 30-80 C, with LEA4 the winner (about 90% versus 70% fluorescence retention after 30 min at 60 C, protection lost at 80 C and above); LEA4 fusions to ASN and GOX retained or slightly increased catalytic activity and held significantly higher residual activity than controls at every point in a 50-80 C by 10-40 min matrix; immobilisation gave ASN >97% and GOX >85% loading with GOX >88% and ASN >77.7% activity recovery, and ten reuse cycles left 72.2% and 46%; the final test fried standardised 1 g potato slices at 130 C for 200 s and measured acrylamide by ELISA, giving A450 of about 0.58 untreated versus 0.38 for the dual-enzyme treatment, with each single enzyme intermediate. Cloning is documented with mutant primer design, colony PCR, sequencing and transfer to BL21. Thirteen rounds of integrated human practices (public survey, restaurant and factory site visits, food scientists, regulatory and investment experts, two peer-review rounds with UESTC, SCU, UCS-B and Cataverse-GreatBay, then re-validation with the original experts) are tied to specific design changes, and the team ran a 2025 project on waste hotpot oil. Weak spots: the Model page is an empty template, hardware and measurement pages are stubs, there is no Parts page (only a part-collection page), and acrylamide is reported as raw ELISA absorbance rather than concentration.

screen.project_title: Reefense: ROS-responsive Bacillus subtilis probiotic secreting an anti-Vibrio endolysin to protect coral
screen.what_they_built: B. subtilis carrying a plasmid that puts the phage-derived endolysin Lysqdvp001 (with sfGFP and an amyE signal peptide) behind an oxidative-stress-responsive, perR-regulated promoter, so the antimicrobial switches on only when heat-stressed coral releases hydrogen peroxide. Plus two dry-lab tools (Reef Codon, Plasmid Builder) and two conceptual devices.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Bacillus subtilis; 12 parts listed including BBa_26FLJO7K (Lysqdvp001 endolysin), BBa_26D8J7ZR (composite ROS-inducible Lysqdvp001 plasmid), BBa_2682OLUC (Ori1030), BBa_K2934002 (PkatA), BBa_K2273023 (amyE signal peptide), BBa_25SIIXDB (sfGFP).
screen.best_evidence: /results zone-of-inhibition assay: transformed B. subtilis activated with 0.1 uM H2O2 produced inhibition zones against a V. coralliilyticus lawn of 0.80 and 0.90 cm (trial 1) and 0.92 and 0.66 cm (trial 2), against a citric-acid positive control at 1.37 and 1.46 cm, while untransformed and activated-untransformed B. subtilis gave no observable zone. The fluorescence arm is effectively null and the team says so: ImageJ green-channel intensity changed only +3.72% at 1 uM and -6.75% at 100 uM versus the untreated control, with the page noting that "presence of fluorescence alone does not establish the magnitude of induction".
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and it changed the construct: Sophia Riazi-Sekowski at Scripps pushed the team off a 37 C temperature-responsive promoter toward a reactive-oxygen-species sensor more relevant to coral stress - the central design decision of the project; the Coral Restoration Foundation repositioned the product as a complementary tool rather than a universal fix; Victoria Lydick prompted coral-mucus intermediate testing; Aqua SD inspired the syringe microdosing delivery concept. 12 conversations with 11 stakeholders across 7 fields, with interview notes published as a PDF.
screen.reason: Borderline, but worth a full read on the strength of the human-practices work, which is the best in this batch and demonstrably rewrote the construct, combined with a genuine controlled result: an engineered strain inhibiting its target pathogen where the untransformed and uninduced controls do not. The caveat for the panel is that the quantitative core is thin - two trials of a zone assay, no replicate statistics, a fluorescence readout that is essentially null, and no direct evidence tying the inhibition to endolysin expression (the team concedes this in Future Directions). The Proof of Concept page's claim that induction "confirmed successful endolysin expression" outruns that evidence, and there is no Attributions page.
screen.field_notes: San Diego high-school team (Conservation) engineering Bacillus subtilis as a coral probiotic that releases the phage endolysin Lysqdvp001 against Vibrio coralliilyticus only when reactive oxygen species signal that the coral is heat-stressed, so the coral holobiont is left alone the rest of the time. Iteration 1 used a cI857/pR temperature-inducible plasmid and failed - no fluorescence, no inhibition - which the team attributes to inability to hold temperature steady; iteration 2 moved to a perR-regulated H2O2-responsive promoter. Zone-of-inhibition assays repeated twice gave 0.66-0.92 cm zones for induced transformed cells with clean negative controls, while ImageJ fluorescence quantification showed changes of only a few percent across 0.1-100 uM H2O2 and is reported as inconclusive. Twelve parts listed, including the composite ROS-inducible plasmid. Dry lab contributes Reef Codon (condition-aware codon optimisation) and a Plasmid Builder that chains retrieval, optimisation and assembly; hardware is two conceptual devices (PG-Sense reader, Reef Doser). Human practices runs on a five-phase "Seek, Evaluate, Adapt" framework with 12 documented conversations and published interview notes, and the promoter switch came directly from a Scripps researcher. Wet-lab mentorship from the Rohwer Lab at SDSU; no Attributions page, and attribution detail is buried in the HP page.

screen.project_title: TheraNova: engineered E. coli sensing gut inflammation, delivering anti-TNF shRNA via OMVs and butyrate
screen.what_they_built: Six plasmid constructs in E. coli: a pNorVbeta nitric-oxide-responsive promoter driving an shTNF hairpin with MS2/MC2 loops, plus four MCP-ClyA-FLAG-nanobody/fluorophore OMV display fusions (one candidate, three controls), and a separate pNorVbeta-TES4 butyrate arm. Intended as an orally delivered IBD therapy.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5alpha (cloning) / Turbo; pET-28a(+) backbone for constructs 1-5, pCI-Neo for construct 6. Registry parts used/made: pNorVbeta BBa_K4387000, ClyA BBa_K257007, MCP BBa_K25I7WLOC, 3xMS2 BBa_K2619006, sfGFP BBa_K2553008, FLAG BBa_25DVCA3A, shTNF BBa_26Y6OS7J, four ClyA fusions (BBa_26FOKP56, BBa_26IMXODB, BBa_26C22OBZ, BBa_2695G0NJ), CDH17 nanobody BBa_26RZQBQA. No /parts page in the crawl.
screen.best_evidence: /results: all six constructs assembled and confirmed by whole-plasmid nanopore sequencing (clone #5-2 rejected for an MC2-loop deletion the digest missed); NgoMIV digest screens with predicted band sizes (3047/932/574/160 bp). Functionally, only 'FLAG by dot blot: increased signal' in two quantified rounds, with the team themselves writing that unequal protein loading and background staining 'prevent a conclusion about reliable circuit activation'. Microscopy was negative, GFP dot blot inconclusive.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in part: clinician and patient interviews (gastroenterologist Dr Sehmbhi, pharma contact Rajesh Mehta, a surgeon arguing for E. coli Nissle 1917) pushed the team toward oral administration, a defined treatment endpoint and layered biocontainment, though the containment work remains proposed rather than built.
screen.reason: Exemplary honesty and clean build/verification work, with a genuinely well-designed control grid (three fluorophore-swap controls) and three documented failures traced by controls. But the central question - does the NO switch turn the circuit on - is unresolved by wiki freeze: one ambiguous dot-blot signal, negative microscopy, and every therapeutic assay (butyrate, vesicle isolation, Caco-2, TNF knockdown) listed as future work. Finalists need a part that demonstrably worked; this does not clear that bar despite strong writing.
screen.field_notes: Epiphany-NYC (Therapeutics, USA) built TheraNova, an E. coli system for leaky gut/IBD combining an shRNA against TNF carried in outer membrane vesicles with a butyrate-producing arm. Six constructs were assembled by NEBuilder Gibson into pET-28a(+) and all verified by Plasmidsaurus whole-plasmid nanopore sequencing; construct 6 (pNorVbeta-TES4) was abandoned after six weeks of false-positive ampicillin colonies and bought as a synthesised plasmid instead. Four ClyA fusion variants were built deliberately as one candidate plus three fluorophore-swap controls so a failure could be localised to the inside or outside end of the display protein. Functional induction with a nitric oxide donor (2000 and 4000 uM, plus a strict anaerobic run) gave increased anti-FLAG dot-blot signal but negative fluorescence microscopy and an uninterpretable negative control in the final run; the team attribute this to insufficient native NorR and had an unfinished NorR-on-plasmid redesign at freeze. Human practices rests on clinician and patient interviews that shaped administration route, treatment endpoint and biocontainment priorities; entrepreneurship and education pages are large. No attributions, parts or proof-of-concept page was present in the crawl.

screen.project_title: EcoPatch: sustainable alginate hydrogel wound patch with ROS-reducing biomass extract and movement sensing
screen.what_they_built: An alginate-polyacrylamide double-network hydrogel patch for chronic wounds that carries a ROS-reducing extract from the invasive weed water hyacinth and an embedded silver-nanowire strain sensor whose resistance change is read in real time through a voltage divider and an nRF52840 microcontroller.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and Top10, pAIP4 backbone (pAIP4_5Y33 from Addgene #234204) expressing alginate lyases FlAlyA/5Y33, Alyw203 and AlgL7 as His-SUMO fusions, plus an empty-vector control. Only one BBa ID (BBa_26UHIL8J) appears in the whole crawl and the parts-collection page is 119 words.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering: DNS reducing-sugar assay showing 5Y33 and Alyw203 reactions above empty-vector control (p<0.001, ANOVA with Dunnett), and the LPS-induced ROS assay in RAW 264.7 macrophages where water hyacinth extract significantly reduced ROS (p<0.001 versus LPS) while AOS did not, leading to selection of 100 ug/mL extract. SDS-PAGE across three temperatures and two IPTG concentrations shows 5Y33 and Alyw203 soluble at 18-26 C and AlgL7 failing.
screen.hp_integration: Plausibly yes — a very large human-practices section (7.8k words) plus entrepreneurship, inclusivity and sustainability pages, but from the screening pack the link from stakeholder input to a specific design change is not demonstrated the way the lab-driven choices are.
screen.reason: Competent, honest and statistically careful work, and the negative AOS result is reported rather than buried, but it is largely materials science and electronics with a thin synthetic-biology core (aspect 7). The only engineered-biology element is heterologous expression of three literature alginate lyases, and the enzyme product (AOS) failed the ROS assay, so the active ingredient in the final patch is a plant extract requiring no synthetic biology at all. The model page is explicitly illustrative with assumed parameters and no wet-lab calibration, no complete-patch testing (ROS retention, sensing reliability, wound effect) was done — the team says so itself — and Registry documentation is essentially absent (one part ID, a 119-word parts page, no attributions page). Good medal-level team, not finalist calibre.
screen.field_notes: ESSENTIAL KOREA (Biomanufacturing, Seoul) built EcoPatch, an alginate-polyacrylamide double-network hydrogel wound patch combining a ROS-reducing ingredient with real-time deformation sensing, framed around valorising aquatic biomass. They cloned and expressed three alginate lyases in E. coli BL21(DE3) as His-SUMO fusions — FlAlyA/5Y33 from Addgene #234204, Alyw203 and AlgL7 — screening three temperatures and two IPTG levels by SDS-PAGE; 5Y33 and Alyw203 were soluble at 18-26 C while AlgL7 expressed poorly, and they propose a temperature-dependent proteolytic cleavage model to explain Alyw203 running at 55-57 kDa instead of 70 kDa at low temperature. A DNS assay confirmed both enzymes degraded alginate (p<0.001 versus empty vector). In an LPS-induced ROS assay in RAW 264.7 macrophages the enzymatically produced alginate oligosaccharides gave no significant reduction while hydroethanolic water hyacinth extract did, so 100 ug/mL extract was chosen for the patch — a negative result the team reports openly as a lesson that substrate conversion does not imply bioactivity. The hydrogel was engineered over two DBTL cycles from Ca2+-crosslinked alginate alone to a Ca2+-alginate/PAAm double network with stress-strain testing. Sensing uses a silver-nanowire layer as a variable resistor in a 1 kOhm voltage divider read by an nRF52840 ADC at 3000 mV, with a documented Python real-time resistance plotter. The dry-lab page presents Fickian release and ROS reaction-diffusion equations with explicitly illustrative, uncalibrated parameters. Extensive human practices, entrepreneurship, inclusivity and sustainability pages; almost no Registry presence (one BBa ID, 119-word parts page) and no attributions page.

screen.project_title: ProteaSign: electrochemical protease-activity sensor for chronic wounds
screen.what_they_built: A disposable gold-electrode cartridge that measures MMP-9 and neutrophil serine protease activity in wound exudate using methylene-blue-labelled cleavable peptide probes read by square-wave voltammetry, supported by sfGFP-based protein biosensors (pES-01 His/FLAG depletion, pDUAL split-GFP turn-on) to validate per-enzyme substrate specificity.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli with pSB1C3 BioBrick backbone for pES-01 (chosen on mentor advice for Registry submission) and a chloramphenicol-resistant pDUAL plasmid; the device side uses MicruX gold electrodes with a C6-ferrocene/MCH self-assembled monolayer and custom MB-peptide SGKIPRTLTA. No BBa part IDs appear anywhere in the crawl and there is no parts page.
screen.best_evidence: Modelling only in reachable form: /swv forward model predicts that after 30 min MMP-9 cuts ~14% of probes in a healing wound (6 nM) versus ~52% in a chronic wound (30 nM) from a coverage of 3e-12 mol/cm2, 3.1e10 probes, 7.4 nm spacing, with the cut fraction read as 1 - dI(T)/dI(0). The notebook records real lab days with 20, 50 and 200 nM MMP-9 at Greenwich and a first ferrocene peak, but no measured voltammogram, no results page and the SWV 'Results' and 'Validation' sections render empty in the static crawl.
screen.hp_integration: Cannot be assessed: the human practices page is listed in the navigation but returned no content in the crawl, so there is no visible evidence that stakeholder input changed the design.
screen.reason: The dry lab is the best thing here - a substrate predictor, a surface-enzyme kinetics model and a six-step SWV forward model with runnable code and clinically anchored concentrations - and the writing and referencing are excellent. But the wiki fails the judging basics: no results page, no parts page, no BBa IDs, no safety page, and the Test/Learn panels of all three engineering cycles plus the SWV Results and Validation sections are behind JavaScript, so no experimental outcome is readable. Human practices renders empty. Judges are not required to hunt, and on what is visible nothing has been shown to work. Also note the wet lab ran in two university labs (KCL and Greenwich), which the panel should weigh against aspect 6.
screen.field_notes: Eton-College-UK (Diagnostics, GBR) built ProteaSign, an electrochemical cartridge intended to separate MMP-9 activity from neutrophil serine protease activity in chronic wound exudate, motivated by an NHS cost of GBP 8.3 billion a year. The sensor is a 1.7 mm2 gold working electrode carrying MB-labelled cleavable peptide probes with a C6-ferrocene internal reference for calibration-free ratiometric readout, read by square-wave voltammetry. Three DBTL cycles are described: pES-01 (sfGFP with FLAG and His tags flanking a TEV site, in pSB1C3, cleavage read by Ni-NTA depletion) and pDUAL (split sfGFP1-10 / sfGFP11-in-eglin-C turn-on sensor) at King's College London, and the electrode device at the University of Greenwich. The dry lab is the strength: a substrate predictor, a surface-enzyme kinetics page and a 19.5k-word SWV forward model deriving probe coverage, spacing, single-probe signal and cut fraction, predicting ~14% probe cleavage at 6 nM versus ~52% at 30 nM MMP-9 over 30 min. The notebook shows eleven lab days at Greenwich in Aug-Sep 2026 with MMP-9 at 20, 50 and 200 nM, but no measured data reaches the wiki in static form: there is no results page, no parts page and no BBa IDs, no safety page, the human practices page is empty in the crawl, and the Test/Learn tabs and SWV Results/Validation sections do not render. Attributions are detailed and per-person.

screen.project_title: ProLac — making a food-grade probiotic prefer lactose (Phase I)
screen.what_they_built: An in-silico design (COBRApy single-gene-deletion scan of iLca334_548) nominating a glucose-PTS knockout (peg2612/manM) in Lacticaseibacillus paracasei CICC 6109, plus bench characterization of the purchased wild-type strain (16S ID, growth/CFU, Nanopore plasmid sequencing) and a prototype bench fluorescence reader. No engineered strain was built; construction is explicitly deferred to next year.
screen.chassis_and_parts: L. paracasei CICC 6109 (food-grade, purchased). No parts built or registered — /parts states plainly that construction and registration are scheduled for next year and that nothing carries a BBa number. Only three legacy BBa IDs appear anywhere on the wiki.
screen.best_evidence: /results: 99.45% mean 16S rRNA identity (1017 bp, 100% coverage) confirming strain identity, and 1.0x10^8 peak CFU/mL at 7 h (OD600 0.431) — explicitly single-replicate, with the page itself flagging an unresolved x100 dilution-column ambiguity. FBA numbers (0.5281/h dual-sugar vs 0.0176/h glucose-only for the knockout) are simulation, not experiment.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, demonstrably: an own survey (n=193, /survey) plus stakeholder loops on /human-practices are each written as who-was-engaged / what-changed, and the team says the survey reframed the project toward strain identity and consumer awareness.
screen.reason: Unusually honest and well-built wiki, but there is no engineered construct, no registered part and no experimental test of the central design — the knockout exists only in FBA. Aspects 2, 4 and 7 cannot rise far above the midpoint, so it cannot reach top-2 on the Project section however good the craft is.
screen.field_notes: FHS-China (Foundational Advance, CHN) ran Phase I of ProLac: making a food-grade probiotic prefer lactose. Dry lab used the published genome-scale model iLca334_548 (548 genes) with a COBRApy single-deletion scan and FVA to confirm the literature glucose-PTS gene peg2612 is non-essential and that its removal shifts dual-sugar uptake toward lactose. Wet lab characterized the purchased L. paracasei CICC 6109 chassis only: 16S identity at 99.45% mean over 1017 bp, growth and viability to 1.0x10^8 CFU/mL at 7 h (single replicate, with an acknowledged dilution-column ambiguity), and Oxford Nanopore sequencing of two native plasmids (5295 bp / 4858 bp). Hardware is a Dacai 3.5-inch smart-display plus single-green-channel fluorescence module bench reader over UART, documented frankly with several specifications still 'to be confirmed on the unit' and photobleaching unmeasured. Human practices rest on an own survey of 193 valid respondents (204 collected, Jul-Aug 2026) with stakeholder loops recorded as decision changes; the wiki is bilingual EN/ZH with a judging navigation map, and the parts page states explicitly that nothing is registered this year.

screen.project_title: PathoLogic — Fur/RhlR dual-input AND-gate EcN probiotic that degrades P. aeruginosa biofilm in cystic fibrosis airways
screen.what_they_built: An E. coli Nissle 1917 circuit that fires only when iron is low (CF airway) AND C4-HSL from P. aeruginosa is present, then expresses PL5-family alginate lyase with a Lysis E release element. Three modules characterised separately and then assembled.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli Nissle 1917 (therapeutic chassis), BL21(DE3) for enzyme production; pTrc99k and pET28a. New composite parts BBa_26OMNZN5, BBa_26A3KNIX, BBa_263VVT1T, BBa_26V52UVI, BBa_26VZS20D plus an improvement of BBa_K2315014 using SsrA tags and Prhl(LR) (BBa_K1529310).
screen.best_evidence: /results Figures 7-9: AND-logic verified in EcN — only low-iron plus C4-HSL gave time-dependent GFP elevation while all five other input combinations stayed at baseline, with growth curves ruling out density artefacts; gradient dosing gave a C4-HSL LOD of 53.1 nM (R2=0.894) with cross-reactivity testing against other AHLs; in artificial lung fluid, SDS-PAGE showed time-dependent extracellular alginate lyase and DNS assays showed rising activity after Lysis E autolysis.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, specifically: Dr Guangquan Chen's point about patient-to-patient variation in airway iron made them characterise dose response rather than one fixed low-iron condition, and Dr An's and Dr Xin Wang's biosafety input made low uninduced leakage a selection criterion and prompted the full C4-HSL gradient and the planned kill switch.
screen.reason: A genuine two-input logic gate built from screened, individually characterised parts, demonstrated in the therapeutic chassis with all six input combinations as controls, plus a measured analytical LOD, a documented Registry part improvement, and effector release shown in a CF-mimicking fluid. This is the strongest synthetic-biology design-and-standards case in the batch and clearly deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: GCGS (Foshan, China) built PathoLogic, an E. coli Nissle 1917 probiotic carrying a Fur-RhlR AND gate for Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilm in cystic fibrosis. They screened two iron-responsive promoters and chose chimeric PfhuA1 over native PfepA for low leakage and dose-dependent derepression under 2,2'-bipyridine, with growth curves confirming the signal was not a density artefact. For the pathogen input they improved Registry part BBa_K2315014 by fusing four SsrA degradation tag variants to RhlR; tags killed induction on weak wild-type Prhl, so they swapped in TokyoTech's stronger Prhl(LR) (BBa_K1529310), and RhlR-SsrA-ASV-Prhl(LR) gave the best background-to-induction tradeoff. The effector, a PL5-family alginate lyase, was Ni-NTA purified and characterised by DNS assay (optimum 37 C, active at pH 7, no saturation over 60 min). Assembled in EcN, GFP rose only under low-iron plus C4-HSL across six input conditions; gradient dosing gave an LOD of 53.1 nM (R2=0.894) with weak C12-HSL cross-reactivity, and in artificial lung fluid Lysis E-driven autolysis released alginate lyase with rising DNS activity. The team states its limitation plainly: no live P. aeruginosa biofilm was tested, only purified sodium alginate. IHP with clinicians, biosafety and industry experts measurably changed the test design (dose response instead of a single low-iron point; leakage as a selection criterion) and set the planned temperature kill switch; the wiki has no model page.

justification.a1: Four linked pieces of work build in difficulty: two iron promoters compared, ten RhlR sensor variants screened, an alginate lyase expressed, purified and biochemically profiled, then the assembled Fur-RhlR AND gate moved into the EcN chassis and characterised for dose response, limit of detection and cross-reactivity (Engineering cycles 1-4; Results sections 1-4). The effector circuit was then run in artificial lung fluid with supernatant SDS-PAGE and DNS activity (Results Figure 9). What keeps it off a 5 is that the therapeutic claim itself, biofilm degradation, was never tested on P. aeruginosa biofilm, as the team says plainly.
justification.a2: The AND gate is shown against the right controls: blank, iron-rich, low-iron only, C4-HSL only and iron-rich + C4-HSL all stay near basal while only the combined condition rises, with growth curves alongside and fluorescence normalised to OD600 (Results Figure 7; Engineering Test 4). Promoter screening used three biological replicates over a 20 h time course (Engineering Test 1), and the tag screens report significance calls including ns and p<0.05 (Figures 14F, 15F); the enzyme assay has a negative control at p<0.001 (Figure 24A). Short of 5 because the key efficacy step is missing, replicate numbers are stated for cycle 1 only, and the Results Discussion admits the artificial-lung-fluid effector test 'has not been fully completed' while the section above states the release was confirmed.
justification.a3: The indication is well chosen and grounded: CF prevalence and P. aeruginosa colonisation are cited (Description sections 2-3), and clinicians, a regulator and two companies commented on route, dosing and reimbursement (IHP interviews 3-7). The team's own number that bears on use is an LOD of 53.1 nM for C4-HSL set against reported sputum ranges (Results Figure 8C), a genuine data-to-use link. But the inhaled live biotherapeutic is explicitly 'an expert guided conceptual design' with no formulation, device or biofilm data, so the impact case stops short of the real-setting test TAS Taipei ran.
justification.a4: Cycle 2a is a real design-test-redesign: SsrA tags cut leakage but killed induction on wild-type Prhl, the team diagnosed insufficient transcriptional strength and in cycle 2b swapped in Prhl(LR) (BBa_K1529310), which restored dose-dependent induction across all four tags (Engineering Learn 2a, Test 2b). Criteria for success (low uninduced leakage plus large dynamic range) are stated before testing in each Design section, and a second data-driven change came from IHP, moving from a single fixed C4-HSL dose to gradient characterisation (Results section 4). Not a 5 only because the later cycles are assembly and characterisation rather than a further failure-driven redesign.
justification.a5: Seven expert engagements (clinical, biosafety, industry, regulatory), two company visits, a 398-response bilingual survey and two cross-team exchanges are each written up with a gather-consult-gain-synthesise structure (IHP page). Several exchanges changed the project: dropping the VOC diagnostic module after Dr Chen called it feasible but not novel, adding gradient dose-response testing, choosing a temperature-sensitive kill switch over a pH switch with reasons given, and repositioning the product as an antibiotic adjunct. It falls short of 5 because many 'Synthesize & Sustain' items are future intentions rather than work done this season, and there is no direct patient voice.
justification.a6: Member profiles on the Team page describe individual roles (cloning, data recording, illustration, notebook keeping), and the Safety page shows students were trained and worked under lab instructor supervision, which reads as student-executed work. However there is no attributions page on the wiki (/attributions returns 404) and no task-level chart saying who ran which assay; the Awards page points judges to the submitted Attributions Form instead. Without that breakdown I cannot tell how much of the cloning, purification and plate-reader work was the students' versus a host lab's.
justification.a7: This is squarely synthetic biology with standard components: a collection of 29 parts including reused Registry parts (BBa_K2315014 from Shanghai_tech_2017, BBa_K1529310 from Tokyo_Tech, BBa_E0040) plus new basic and composite parts for the tags, promoters, lyase and the two dual-response plasmids (part-collection page). The engineering is genuine device design, cascading an iron-derepressed promoter onto a quorum-sensing activator and tuning it with degradation tags. Just short of 5 because the Registry entries themselves could not be opened from here to confirm sequence-level documentation.
justification.a8: Wiki documentation is detailed: a parts table with numbers, types and descriptions, and a Contribution page giving design principle, usage, properties and characterisation for each of the five new composite parts. Two things hold it down: the standard URLs /parts and /attributions both return 404 with the content living at /part-collection, exactly the relocation the handbook warns about on p.29, and parts.igem.org returned 403 to me so the Registry entries that are the real basis for part scoring are unverified.
justification.w1: The home page gives the disease, the two input signals, the effector and the self-lysis safeguard under a plain Sense / Respond / Restore frame, with a one-line statement of what was shown for each response module. A reader knows within a screen what the team built and why CF plus P. aeruginosa biofilm is the target. Minor drift only: the homepage summary states modules 'can be expressed successfully' without pointing straight at the controlling figure.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim on Results and Engineering is tied to a numbered figure with panels named in the caption, and the text states the comparison being made: negative controls, iron-rich versus chelator groups, untagged versus tagged constructs, OD-normalised fluorescence, significance calls. Methods are complete enough to match the data to a protocol on the Experiments page. It is not a 5 because n is given only once, the artificial-lung-fluid claim conflicts with the Discussion, and a few captions are mislabelled (a PfepA caption on a PfhuA1 panel in Contribution).
justification.w3: Every page carries a contents list, the section order mirrors the ballot (Description, Experiments, Results, Engineering, Parts, IHP, Safety), and the persistent menu makes the project readable end to end. Against that, /parts and /attributions are 404 so a judge following standard URLs lands on an error page, the menu carries both 'Part' and 'Parts' entries without explaining the difference, and the notebook is a stack of embedded PDFs rather than readable page content.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: full reagent and instrument tables, step-by-step cloning, expression, purification, DNS and dose-response protocols, a part-by-part collection, and cycle-by-cycle laboratory records. Failures are kept in rather than hidden, notably the collapse of induction with SsrA tags on wild-type Prhl. Reproduction would still be hampered by raw data not being posted, the notebook being PDF-only, and n not being stated for most assays.
justification.w5: Each major page ends with a numbered reference list and the text carries inline bracketed citations, including for images taken from literature (Description Figures 2, 3, 4). Prior iGEM work is credited by team and year, Shanghai_tech_2017 for BBa_K2315014 and Tokyo_Tech 2016 for the Prhl(LR) rationale, which is the behaviour the handbook rewards. The references I spot-checked resolve; a 5 would need every figure to name its source as consistently as the Description page does.

J1.one_line: A genuinely strong high-school wet-lab project: a two-input AND gate built module by module with proper controls and statistics, held back by the untested biofilm claim, a missing attributions page and two broken standard URLs.
