calibrated.changed: none. a6 3.5 sits above the bios-only teams because the member profiles describe individual experimental roles (cloning, data recording, notebook keeping) and below the 4.0 teams because no task-level chart exists and /attributions is a 404.

justification.a1: Four linked DBTL cycles take the project from two candidate Fur promoters, through a four-variant SsrA screen and a promoter swap, to an assembled AND gate in the EcN chassis, then to LOD/cross-reactivity characterisation and a 48 h test in artificial lung fluid with Lysis-E-driven enzyme release (Engineering, Cycles 1-4; Results Figs 2-9). That is a chain of increasingly difficult steps of the kind the handbook rewards (GreatBay_SZ, p.33-34), delivered with real data at each stage. It falls short of 5 only because the therapeutic claim never reaches a biofilm: no P. aeruginosa material was tested, and the inhaled product remains a conceptual design (Results, 'Our Product').
justification.a2: The AND logic is demonstrated against all five non-permissive control combinations (blank, iron-rich, low-iron only, C4-HSL only, iron-rich + C4-HSL) with normalised RFU/OD600 time courses and an endpoint blue-light photograph (Results Fig 7; Engineering Fig 29). Enzyme activity is quantified by DNS against a negative control with ***p<0.001, with temperature and pH profiles (Engineering Fig 24), and supernatant SDS-PAGE plus rising DNS activity show conditional release in artificial lung fluid (Fig 31/Fig 9). Two things hold it below 4.5: the central therapeutic function (alginate/biofilm degradation by the engineered cells) is only ever shown on purified sodium alginate, and the Results Discussion states 'Therapeutic output test ... has not been fully completed. We lack direct evidence for circuit-triggered protein release in CF-mimicking medium' while Figure 9 on the same page claims exactly that evidence.
justification.a3: The deployment route is concrete and expert-shaped: spray-dried trehalose-mannitol DPI or mesh-nebulised suspension, with jet and ultrasonic nebulisers ruled out on shear and heat grounds (Results, 'Our Product', from Dr Xin Wang), and a regulatory pathway narrowed to therapeutic biological product registration after Dr Huihui Bao ruled out the food route (IHP, Interview 7). Positioning as an antibiotic adjunct rather than first line is a credible constraint. But nothing was tested in a realistic setting - no device, no particle sizing, no biofilm, no microbiome data - so this stays a well-argued plan rather than TAS Taipei's tested wastewater-style rig.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Cycle 2a is a real failure with a mechanistic reading: SsrA tags cut leakage but abolished C4-HSL induction on wild-type Prhl, and the team concluded degradation rate exceeded synthesis rate; Cycle 2b then redesigns by swapping in Prhl(LR) (BBa_K1529310) and recovers dose-stratified induction across all four tags, selecting ASV (Engineering, Learn 2a / Test 2b, Figs 15 and 20). Selection criteria were stated in advance (low leakage plus dynamic range) and the final circuit was quantified as a sensor: LOD 53.1 nM, log-dose fit R2=0.894, C12-HSL cross-reactivity (Fig 30). Not a 5 because the one modelling claim - 'circuit level simulation further predicted' that weak Prhl would break the AND gate (Design 2b) - has no model page behind it (the /model URL is 404), so that prediction is unverifiable.
justification.a5: A 398-response bilingual survey plus seven expert interviews spanning clinical, biosafety, industrial and regulatory perspectives, two corporate visits and three cross-team events, all run through the team's own gather-consult-gain-synthesise cycle (IHP page). Two changes are traceable into the wet lab: after Dr An and Dr Wang, the team replaced single-dose AND-gate verification with a full C4-HSL gradient and LOD measurement (Results, section 4), and public concern about off-target activation made uninduced leakage a formal selection criterion. Short of 5 because a large share of the 'Synthesize & Sustain' outcomes are future intentions ('we will add experiments...') rather than work actually done, and the patient voice is survey-level rather than sustained engagement.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page at all: /attributions, /attribution and /team/attributions all return 404, and no equivalent who-did-what table appears anywhere on the wiki. The handbook reads attribution from that form (p.25-26), so the completeness check simply cannot be made. What exists is self-written member blurbs on the Team page naming general roles (wet lab, illustration, data curation, PPT) plus an advisor list, and the safety training record suggests students did the bench work, but at no point is it stated which steps were done by students versus advisors or an outside lab. I raise this as a missing-document question rather than any accusation.
justification.a7: The project is squarely synthetic biology built on registry standards: a 29-entry part collection organised by module, with new basic parts (PfhuA1 BBa_K3378002 usage, fepA promoter BBa_26WUJGHQ, four SsrA tags, Lysis E BBa_26Z4O394, alginate lyase BBa_26XNB6Y2) and new composites including the dual-response constructs BBa_26V52UVI and BBa_26VZS20D (part-collection page). Prior iGEM work is reused and explicitly improved: Shanghai_tech_2017's BBa_K2315014 plus Tokyo_Tech's BBa_K1529310, with the improved sensor submitted as BBa_26QSD9SO (Improve page). Not 5 because parts.igem.org would not serve me any part page (403 from the CDN), so I could not confirm on the Registry itself that these entries exist with the described content.
justification.a8: On-wiki documentation is genuinely good: the Contribution page gives design principle, usage, properties, engineering and characterisation per new part; the Experiments page lists reagents with catalogue numbers, instruments with models, and step-by-step protocols including the LOD and artificial-lung-fluid assays. Against that, my rule is that parts are judged on the Registry (p.18) and I could not reach a single part page to check annotation, topology or data there. Two standard pages a judge is told to look at - Attributions and Model - are 404, and the notebook exists only as five embedded PDFs with 346 words of surrounding text.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the chassis and the logic in one pass - CF, 78% chronic P. aeruginosa, alginate biofilm, engineered EcN as a SENSE / RESPOND / RESTORE living sensor - and the Description and Results overviews name the three modules plus the assembled AND gate in the first screen. After the home and description pages I could state the aim, chassis, inputs, effector and success criterion without hunting. Short of 5 because the headline numbers (20,000 CF patients in China, 78%) arrive without in-text citations on the home page.
justification.w2: Claims are overwhelmingly measured rather than asserted: gels and sequencing for every build, three biological replicates and OD600 growth controls alongside every fluorescence figure, significance marks (ns, *, ***), and a dose-response fit with a stated R2 and LOD (Results Figs 2-9; Engineering Figs 5-31). Limitations are stated plainly, including that no live P. aeruginosa was ever used. It is held at 4 by the self-contradiction on the Results page about whether circuit-triggered release in CF-mimicking medium was demonstrated, and by the unsupported 'circuit level simulation' claim with no model behind it.
justification.w3: Navigation is workable - a grouped menu (Project / Outreach) and a per-page contents list on every long page - and the pages read in a sensible order from Description to Engineering to Results. But a judge following the standard-page URLs hits 404 at /attributions, /model, /parts, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /measurement and /inclusivity, with the parts table living instead at /part-collection, and the menu carries both 'Part' and 'Parts' entries. Dead standard pages and a split parts/part naming are exactly what the aspect penalises.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of this: the Experiments page gives named kits, catalogue numbers, instrument models and assay conditions; the part collection tables every construct with its registry number; the Engineering page records what failed and why, which is the most reusable thing here (SsrA tags only work above a transcription-strength floor). The notebook is the weak point - five embedded PDFs with almost no text around them, so the day-to-day record depends entirely on those attachments rendering.
justification.w5: Engineering and Results each carry a numbered reference list that is used in text at the right places (Fur mechanism, lasR-null CF isolates, SsrA variants, C4-HSL in sputum), and prior iGEM work is credited by team and part number (Shanghai_tech_2017, Tokyo_Tech 2016). In-text citation thins out badly on the home page, the IHP narrative and the survey analysis, where figures and statistics mostly stand uncited. I could not resolve reference 1 (Pathogens 2026, 15, 557) offline; I note it as something to check rather than as a finding.

J2.one_line: A disciplined four-cycle engineering project with a genuine failure-driven redesign and a characterised AND gate in EcN, let down by a missing Attributions page, several dead standard pages, and a therapeutic claim that never meets a biofilm.
strengths: Cycle 2a/2b is a textbook DBTL turn: SsrA tags killed induction on wild-type Prhl, the team diagnosed degradation outrunning synthesis, swapped in Prhl(LR) (BBa_K1529310), and recovered dose-stratified response (Engineering, Learn 2a and Test 2b, Figs 15 and 20).
AND-gate logic tested against all five non-permissive input combinations with growth controls and normalised RFU/OD600, plus an end-point photograph (Results Fig 7 / Engineering Fig 29).
The final circuit is characterised as an instrument, not just demonstrated: LOD 53.1 nM for C4-HSL, log-dose fit R2=0.894, and a C12-HSL cross-reactivity test (Engineering Fig 30).

Effector module taken from clone to purified protein to quantified activity: soluble expression, Ni-NTA purification, DNS assay with negative control at ***p<0.001, and temperature and pH optima matched against CF airway conditions (Engineering Fig 24).
A 29-part collection built on reused registry and prior iGEM parts, with the improved C4-HSL sensor submitted back as BBa_26QSD9SO (part-collection and Improve pages).
Human practices with traceable consequences - the gradient-dose LOD work was added after Dr An and Dr Wang, and the regulatory route was reset to drug registration after Dr Bao (IHP, Interview 7).
Limitations are stated by the team themselves, including that safety rules barred any live P. aeruginosa work, which is the honesty the handbook rewards.
weaknesses: No Attributions page exists (404 at /attributions and every variant I tried), so who did which experiment, and what advisors contributed, cannot be established.
The therapeutic function is only ever shown on purified sodium alginate; no biofilm, no P. aeruginosa, so biofilm degradation stays a claim.

The Results Discussion says there is no direct evidence for circuit-triggered protein release in CF-mimicking medium, while Figure 9 on the same page presents that evidence - one of the two statements is wrong.
A 'circuit level simulation' is cited as justification for the Cycle 2b redesign, but /model is 404 and no modelling appears anywhere on the wiki.
Seven standard page URLs return 404 (attributions, model, parts, proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, inclusivity), and the parts table sits at the non-standard /part-collection.
Registry depth is unverified: parts.igem.org returned 403 for every part I tried, so the documentation credit rests on the wiki's own tables.
The notebook is 346 words plus five embedded PDFs, thin as a standalone record.

Internal contradiction on the Results page about whether circuit-triggered enzyme release in artificial lung fluid was demonstrated (Discussion bullet 2 versus Figure 9).
'Circuit level simulation further predicted...' (Engineering, Design 2b) with no model page or data anywhere on the wiki - treat that prediction as unverified.
Reference 1 (Capraz Yavuz, Pathogens 2026, 15, 557, DOI 10.3390/pathogens15050557) could not be resolved from here; worth a routine check rather than a finding.
Registry part pages were unreachable (403) during review, so a7/a8 could not be confirmed against the Registry as the handbook requires.

justification.a1: The project climbs through five linked DBTL cycles on the Engineering page: two iron promoters screened, four SsrA tags screened twice (with and without P rhl(LR)), alginate lyase expressed/purified/characterised, then both sensors assembled into an AND gate in EcN and tested in artificial lung fluid with a dose-response, LOD and cross-reactivity panel (Results §4). That is genuine scale and scope for a high school season. It stops short of the GreatBay/TAS top anchor because there is no model, no hardware, and the therapeutic claim is never tested against the real pathogen.
justification.a2: The core circuit demonstrably works with controls: P fhuA1 shows low basal and dose-dependent mCherry while P fepA does not, with OD600 curves ruling out density artefacts (Engineering Test 1, 3 biological replicates); the AND gate gives signal only in low-iron + C4-HSL and stays near-basal in all five other conditions, with endpoint quantification and a blue-light photograph (Results Fig. 7). Enzyme activity is quantified by DNS against a negative control (p<0.001) with temperature, pH and time profiles (Results Fig. 5). Honest limits are stated: no live P. aeruginosa biofilm was ever tested, so the therapeutic end of the claim is in vitro only.
justification.a3: The need is real and confirmed by a clinician with CF experience (Dr Guangquan Chen) and by a regulatory expert who defined the only compliant approval route (Dr Huihui Bao), and the team repositioned the product as an antibiotic adjunct rather than a standalone therapy (Human Practices, Results Discussion). Testing in artificial lung fluid is a reasonable step toward the real setting. Deployment, however, is still a concept: the inhaled DPI formulation on the Results 'Our Product' section is explicitly expert-guided design with no spray-drying or viability data.
justification.a4: Cycle 2a is a real failure that drove a redesign: SsrA tags cut background but abolished C4-HSL induction on wild-type P rhl, and the Learn step diagnoses degradation outrunning transcription, leading directly to the P rhl(LR) swap in Cycle 2b that restored induction across all four tags (Engineering, Learn 2a/2b). Success criteria (low uninduced leakage plus large dynamic range) are stated before testing, and component choices in Cycle 4 follow from the earlier data. No model fitted to their own data: the 'circuit level simulation' mentioned in Design 2b has no page or figure behind it (the /model page is 404).
justification.a5: This is unusually well traced for a high school team: a 398-response bilingual survey plus seven named experts, two company visits and three cross-team events, each written up in a Gather-Construct-Gain-Synthesize loop (Human Practices). At least two changes show up in the wet-lab data rather than only in prose: Dr Chen's point about patient-to-patient variability produced the iron dose-response instead of one fixed concentration, and Dr An's and Dr Wang's comments produced the C4-HSL gradient, LOD and cross-reactivity work in Results Fig. 8; Dr Chen also persuaded them to drop the VOC diagnostic module. Held below 5 because several consequences (temperature kill switch, encapsulation, microbiome testing) remain plans, and the survey, which reached patients and caregivers, carries no statement of consent or ethics oversight.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page on this wiki at all: /attributions returns 404 and the navigation has no link to one; the Awards page simply tells judges to 'follow our submitted attributions form'. The Team page gives only self-written bios in general terms ('basic molecular experiments', 'contribute to research activities'), with no who-did-what table and no figure captions naming who ran an experiment. The work shown (Ni-NTA purification, SDS-PAGE, EcN transformation, plate-reader time courses) is demanding, and the wiki never says where it was done or who supervised, so I cannot tell from the wiki what the students did themselves. This is a documentation gap and a question for the session, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The design is built from standard parts and reuses registry work properly: BBa_K2315014 from Shanghai_tech_2017 as the baseline and BBa_K1529310 (P rhl(LR)) from Tokyo_Tech as the fix, with the improvement BBa_26QSD9SO and five new composite parts listed on the Contribution page. The Part-collection page separates basic parts (promoters, mCherry, pTrc99k vector) from composites, and the final device is a modular two-input AND gate with tuned RBS strengths for lyase and Lysis E. Clearly a synthetic biology project in the standard-parts idiom.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is strong: each part on the Contribution page carries design principle, usage and biology, properties and characterisation tied to a named figure, and the Experiments page lists reagents, catalogue numbers and instruments. I could not confirm the Registry entries myself (parts.igem.org returned 403 to me), and the Awards page claim that measurement results were 'posted on the registry' is therefore unverified. Discoverability also costs the team: /parts is a 404 and the list lives at /part-collection, and the notebook is an embedded PDF rather than readable page text.
justification.w1: The home page is short (about 550 words) and does the job: SENSE / RESPOND / RESTORE, what CF is, why P. aeruginosa biofilm defeats antibiotics, and the two-signal EcN solution, with a schematic of the AND gate and links onward. The Description page then develops background, limitations of current treatment and the design rationale in order. A reader knows the goal within a screen.
justification.w2: Most claims are tied to a numbered figure with panels, controls, growth normalisation and statistics (Engineering Figs. 6-7, 14-15, 19-20, 24, 29-31), and planned work is generally labelled as future. One contradiction undercuts this: the Results Discussion states that the alginate lyase-Lysis E test in artificial lung fluid 'has not been fully completed' and that 'we lack direct evidence for circuit-triggered protein release in CF-mimicking medium', while the section above it and Engineering Test 4 present Figure 9/31 as confirming exactly that release. A reader cannot tell which statement to believe.
justification.w3: Navigation is consistent across pages and the Awards page gives a useful evidence index mapping criteria to pages. But several standard pages judges are told to expect are absent: /attributions, /parts, /model, /proof-of-concept and /measurement all 404, with the parts list moved to /part-collection and proof-of-concept folded into Results. That is content judges have to hunt for, and the attributions material is not on the wiki at all.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: the Experiments page has protocols with reagent brands and catalogue numbers and instrument models, the Engineering page records what failed and why, and the part pages explain the SsrA-versus-promoter trade-off explicitly for reuse. Against that, the notebook is a 346-word shell around embedded PDFs rather than a readable record, no raw data tables or numeric values are provided alongside the plots, and the missing attributions page means the division of labour is lost.
justification.w5: References are numbered, per-page and specific, and prior iGEM work is credited by name and part number (Shanghai_tech_2017 for BBa_K2315014, Tokyo_Tech 2016 for P rhl(LR)). Background figures in the Description carry bracketed source citations, and the LOD discussion cites clinical sputum C4-HSL measurements (Erickson 2002) for the physiological range it claims to cover. Minor lapses only: a few figure credits are implicit in the surrounding citation, and the survey's COVID-awareness inference leans on a single Lancet correspondence.

J3.one_line: A disciplined, honest AND-gate therapeutic with five real DBTL cycles and controlled data in the EcN chassis, badly let down by having no attributions anywhere on the wiki.
strengths: Five DBTL cycles with a genuine failure and redesign: SsrA tags killed induction on wild-type P rhl, and the diagnosis (degradation outrunning weak transcription) led directly to the P rhl(LR) swap that rescued it (Engineering, Learn 2a/2b)

AND-gate logic shown with all six input combinations, growth-normalised fluorescence, endpoint quantification and a visual check, in the therapeutic EcN chassis rather than only in DH5a (Results Fig. 7)
Analytical characterisation beyond a yes/no result: C4-HSL dose-response with LOD 53.1 nM (R2 = 0.894) and a cross-reactivity panel against C12-HSL (Results Fig. 8)

Stakeholder input that is visible in the data, not just the prose: the iron dose-response and the C4-HSL gradient work were both added after specific expert comments (Human Practices; Results sections 1 and 4)
Limitations stated plainly and repeatedly, including that no live P. aeruginosa biofilm was ever tested because the organism is off-whitelist (Results Discussion; Engineering Learn 3)
Prior iGEM work credited precisely by team and part number, with the improvement built on it rather than around it (Improve page)
weaknesses: No attributions content on the wiki: /attributions is a 404, nothing in the navigation, and the Awards page defers to the submitted form, so a judge cannot see who did which experiment or what outside help was used
Team page bios describe roles only in general terms ('basic molecular experiments', 'research activities'), and no figure caption names an experimenter
The Results Discussion says the artificial-lung-fluid effector test is not complete and lacks direct evidence of protein release, while the same page presents Figure 9 as confirming that release
Registry documentation is claimed but not demonstrable from the wiki alone; the part data a reader can actually inspect sits on the Contribution and Part-collection pages
Several standard pages are missing (/parts, /model, /proof-of-concept, /measurement), so parts live at /part-collection and proof-of-concept is folded into Results
The notebook page is a shell around embedded PDFs, and no numeric or raw data accompany the plots
The 398-person public survey, which reached patients and caregivers, carries no statement of consent, anonymity or ethics oversight
The inhaled DPI product section reads as design but is explicitly conceptual, with no formulation or viability data behind it
red_flags: No Attributions page exists on the wiki (https://2026.igem.wiki/gcgs/attributions returns 404 and no nav link); with purification, plate-reader and EcN work shown, who performed the bench work is unclear. A question for the session, not an accusation.

Internal contradiction on the Results page: the Discussion says 'Therapeutic output test for the plasmid (alginate lyase-Lysis E) inside artificial lung fluid medium has not been fully completed. We lack direct evidence for circuit-triggered protein release in CF-mimicking medium', while the section above presents Figure 9 (SDS-PAGE plus DNS) as verifying exactly that.

Registry part pages for the claimed new parts could not be retrieved during this review (parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403), so the Awards-page claim that measurement data were posted to the Registry is unverified rather than disproved.
The 398-response public survey, which included CF patients and caregivers and may have included minors, is reported with no mention of informed consent or ethics oversight.

calibrated.changed: none, after reconsidering a8. I nearly cut it to 3.5 for the 404 on /parts, but the per-part documentation on Contribution (design principle, usage, biology, properties, each tied to a named characterisation figure) is as specific as Hongwen's and Korea HS's at 4.0, so the consistent fix was to raise SHSID rather than lower this.

one_line.en: A disciplined AND-gate therapeutic with a genuine failure-driven redesign and characterised logic in the therapeutic chassis, badly let down by having no attributions anywhere.
one_line.zh: 嚴謹的 AND 閘治療設計，有真實因失敗而改版的過程，並在治療底盤中完成邏輯表徵，但完全沒有任何貢獻歸屬。

strengths: A textbook redesign cycle: degradation tags abolished induction, the cause was diagnosed and a stronger promoter restored dose-stratified response
AND-gate logic demonstrated across all input combinations with growth controls and normalised fluorescence
Analytical characterisation beyond a yes/no result, with a detection limit, a dose fit and a cross-reactivity panel
Effector module taken from clone to purified protein to quantified activity against a negative control, with optima matched to the application
weaknesses: The therapeutic claim rests on purified substrate only; no biofilm and no target organism were ever tested
No attributions page and no task-level statement of who performed which experiment
Replicate number stated for one cycle only, with significance reported elsewhere without n
Notebook is embedded PDFs with almost no on-page text; several standard pages are 404
red_flags: No Attributions page exists on the wiki
Internal contradiction on the same Results page about whether circuit-triggered release in artificial lung fluid was demonstrated
A circuit-level simulation is cited as justification for a redesign while no model page or modelling data exists anywhere
Public survey including patients and caregivers reported with no consent or ethics statement

screen.project_title: ReLEAF - forecast-driven, light-controlled production of plant protectants
screen.what_they_built: An end-to-end agricultural system: field sensors and a weather-fitted stress model decide when a crop needs help, green light switches CcaSR-controlled Bacillus subtilis WB800 to secrete ACC deaminase, a hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor with an in-line home-built photometer and digital twin releases the protein while retaining cells, and the protectant is tested on Arabidopsis and in a hydroponics box.
screen.chassis_and_parts: B. subtilis WB800 (and 168) with Golden Gate pSTK Level 1/2 assembly; ~36 new Registry parts covering CcaSR green-light module, Pveg/PcpcG2-veg promoters, Csn and SamyQ secretion peptides, and wild-type plus codon-optimised AcdS, LEA14 and BoPep4 variants, built on standards such as BBa_B0015 and BBa_J23100.
screen.best_evidence: /results: anti-His ELISA quantified secreted protectants (ACCD ~16 ug/mL, about three times LEA14 and BoPep4; codon variants compared at 8 and 12 h), DNPH showed ACCD activity requires PLP (48 vs 32 nmol a-KB/mL/h) and that activity peaks at 18 h while protein peaks at 12 h in the bioreactor; active ACCD was present in the cell-free shell side for 72 h with no colonies on that side; the in-line photometer fits the commercial BioDrop with R2 0.992-0.9997 and ran 434 h unattended; a growth rate registered 13 days in advance (0.2986 h-1, 90% CI 0.2705-0.3300) was met by run 6 (0.286 +/- 0.010 h-1).
screen.hp_integration: Yes - farm-level interviews and geospatial analysis of Taiwanese counties (farm size, farmer age 63.8, rice yield trends) set the stress index, the dose model and the hand-applied delivery route the team actually tested.
screen.reason: The widest verified scope in the batch: quantified secretion and enzyme activity, a plant assay where treatment timing changes the outcome, a built and calibrated bioreactor plus photometer with hundreds of hours of logged runs, a pre-registered prediction that was scored, and a stress model validated out-of-sample against county yields. The system is not yet closed end to end (no forecast has driven a light, field sensors are bench-only, the green strip is not in the reactor) and the wiki is very large, but this is clearly a full-read candidate.
screen.field_notes: GEMS-Taiwan (Biomanufacturing village, Taiwan) built ReLEAF, a forecast-to-field plant-protection system. Wet lab: B. subtilis WB800 carrying Golden Gate-assembled constitutive (Pveg) and green-light (CcaSR/PcpcG2-veg) modules secreting ACC deaminase, LEA14 and BoPep4 via Csn or SamyQ signal peptides, with codon-optimised variants; verified by colony PCR and Sanger, quantified by anti-His ELISA (ACCD ~16 ug/mL, ~3x the others) and DNPH activity assay (PLP-dependent; activity lags protein by about six hours in the reactor). Electroporation voltage was optimised empirically per construct (2.1-2.5 kV). Plant work on Arabidopsis under salt and heat ladders found that timing decides the effect - pre- and post-treatment rescue, co-treatment does not. Hardware: a 40x24x62 cm hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor that kept active ACCD in the cell-free shell for 72 h with no colonies crossing, an in-line home-built OD600 photometer agreeing with a BioDrop (slope 0.942, R2 0.9997; R2 0.992 against silica standards) over a 434 h run, and a 24-tube LED light-plate rig. Dry lab: a digital twin with autoencoder fault detection (26.7 h lead before a channel failure, 6.1% false alarms), a Kalman growth forecast 41% better than persistence at 2 h, a pre-registered growth-rate prediction confirmed 13 days later, a stress index fitted to 25 years of county rice yields (365 vs 419 kg/ha error against a trend line), and protein design by docking and MD. Human practices (24.7k words), education (12.2k) and entrepreneurship (17k) are large. Honest about gaps: the forecast has never driven a light, leaf-minus-air sensor offsets (-0.2 to +1.8 C) are instrument artefacts not canopy signal, and delivery was by hand.

justification.a1: The chain is long and each link carries its own data: Golden Gate assembly of five modules, secretion of three protectants from B. subtilis WB800, a light plate characterisation, Arabidopsis rescue across agar, hydroponics and soil, and a hollow-fiber perfusion reactor that delivered active ACC deaminase to a cell-free shell for 72 h (Results, Membrane bioreactor). Four instruments were built and characterised, including an inline OD600 photometer that ran 434 h unattended (Results, Culture monitoring). That is scale and scope well past tick-box, comparable to the TAS Taipei two-route-plus-model pattern; it falls short of a 5 only because the headline integration, green light driving the reactor, was never run, as the team states on Engineering.
justification.a2: The production arm is genuinely demonstrated: anti-His Western in lysate, lumen and shell at ~41 kDa (Fig 57), ELISA above 2 ug/mL through 72 h with DNPH specific activity rising to 6-8 U/mg from 18 h (Fig 67), and plant rescue with mock/TB and WB800-only controls, n = 9-40, mean +- SEM and p values (Figs 43, 45, 49-52). The optogenetic switch, which is the project's central claim, is not: ELISA was flat at 12-13 ug/mL under green and red alike (Fig 24), DNPH favoured green at 13 h but inverted at 16 h and favoured red at 8 h elsewhere, and the team itself notes their red LEDs emit 640 nm rather than the ~672 nm CcaSR needs. Containment rests on two unreplicated platings with no log reduction and, for one, undocumented incubation (Results). Honest reporting throughout, but the switch is not yet shown to work.
justification.a3: The use case is unusually well grounded: Taiwan climate-volatility and farm-size mapping on Description and Geospatial Analysis, five farmer engagements and a 50-person public forum on Integrated Human Practices, and a costed deployment model (37.6 kU per application, 81 L of vessel, US$3800) on Math Model. It stops short of a 5 because nothing has been tested in a field, the protectant was applied by hand rather than through the hydroponic or irrigation route the design assumes, and the team's own two pages disagree on payback by more than an order of magnitude (68 years on Math Model against 4.9 from Geospatial Analysis), which they flag but do not resolve.
justification.a4: Engineering documents twelve DBTL cycles across three cloning pipelines and names what each cycle could not distinguish, including the move off MoClo 2.0 into SubtiToolKit after a screen full of background. The hardware iterations are data-driven rather than troubleshooting: photometer tubing extended to 30 cm after pump vibration destabilised cycle 2, permeate flow cut 24 to 12 mL/min plus an acceptance filter after run 5's bubble failure, and automated KOH dosing withdrawn after it corroded the feeding valve, with antibiotic resupply identified as the cause of the spurious second exponential (Results, Membrane bioreactor). The pre-registered growth-rate prediction, written 1 October and scored against run 6 thirteen days later, with secondary endpoints declared unscorable in advance, is a stated measure of success ahead of testing and is better than most collegiate practice.
justification.a5: The Project Evolution Map on Integrated Human Practices ties named experts to specific design changes with dates: Prof. Chen Wen-Liang's biosafety concern (10 April) moved the project from released PGPR to a contained bioreactor, expert critique moved stress sensing out of the cell into electronic sensors, and osmotic stress was dropped on resource grounds. Thirty-one stakeholders across farmers, researchers, a plant-protectant company and a hydroponic farm, plus a public forum of over 50, with return visits carrying updated prototypes. This is reflective and responsive rather than outreach; it misses a 5 because the later-stage feedback on cartridge maintenance and regulation is recorded as future work rather than as changes already made.
justification.a6: The team page carries a task-level ownership matrix (owner versus member across Cloning, Bioreactor, Plant, Protectant, Model and others) and the 684-entry notebook records operator and recorder per entry, which is the GreatBay-style evidence I look for. Against that, the dedicated Attribution page is completely blank, both in the crawl and when fetched live, so there is no statement anywhere of what the six instructors, four returning student advisors, the NTU postdoc who met the plant sub-team weekly, or the DNA suppliers did versus the students. With that much standing support undeclared, I cannot place this above shared-credit territory even though the figure captions and notebook read like student work.
justification.a7: Thirty-five Registry entries built as a Level 0/1/2 Golden Gate hierarchy on the SubtiToolKit, with fourteen prior Registry parts explicitly credited in a 'Parts we built on' table (Parts). The design is properly modular: an acceptor cassette with an sfGFP/mScarlet-I dropout holds the cargo position open, and promoters, signal peptides and cargos are exchangeable, with codon-recoded variants of all three protectants deposited. This is unambiguously a synthetic biology project on standard components, in the sense the handbook applies to TAS Taipei.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is excellent and the Parts page states each entry's documentation level honestly. The Registry itself is thin where it matters: by the team's own ledger only three of thirty-five entries carry Characterization, eight cargo parts carry Design only and four regulatory parts carry none, so most experimental evidence lives on the wiki rather than on the part page, which is where p.18 says I must look. I could not open parts.igem.org to verify (403 from the Registry's CDN), so I score the team's own statement. Four standard URLs (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design) return 404; the content exists under Results, Experiments and Engineering and the navigation reaches it, but the standard pages were not preserved.
justification.w1: Description opens with a one-paragraph abstract, a five-stage system summary and a technical map that names every component as wet lab, dry lab or hardware with its current state. The homepage carries the problem (climate volatility over Taiwan's small farms), the five design demands and a six-step walkthrough of how the system runs. It is clear and unusually candid about state, but it is a long scrolling narrative rather than Lambert's one-screen summary, so the outcome takes more than one screen to reach.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is attached to a numbered figure with a legend that gives n, the control arm and the statistics: the plant work states mean +- SEM with p values and names TB mock and plasmid-free WB800 controls, and the reactor section separates ELISA concentration from DNPH activity on the same samples. The Results page labels endpoints Measured or Partial, and Math Model carries a provenance ledger marking which inputs are the team's own, which are literature, and which (the canopy correction) are modelled and not measured. Short of 5 because several load-bearing reactor assays are n = 1, some ELISA wells are extrapolated beyond the standard curve with signal in the no-plasmid control, and two blot comparisons are described as not quantified.
justification.w3: Navigation is organised by Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Engagement and Team with a per-page contents rail, and the Hardware page has an explicit 'For judges' entry point, so the ballot content is findable. Two frictions: four standard URLs 404 rather than redirect, and the wiki runs to roughly 180,000 words across thirty-odd pages, which strains the 'complete but not sprawling' test even though the extra pages are substantive rather than padding.
justification.w4: This is the strongest aspect. Twenty-four of twenty-five protocol sheets are downloadable PDFs with reagent volumes, the 684-entry electronic notebook is exported month by month with failed runs and repeated gels deliberately retained, and the plant sub-team's nineteen weekly mentor reports and daily plan log are posted as well. Failures are written up rather than buried: the AmilCP reporter that never coloured, the KOH valve corrosion, the lost 10 h of data when a host computer updated. A future team could rebuild this project from the ground up.
justification.w5: Each page closes with a numbered reference list carrying DOIs, prior Registry parts are credited individually in their own table, and Math Model attributes every input to a public record, a publication or a specific bench run with its date and n. The tooling (SnapGene, IDT, Twist, GenScript) and an AI assistant are named in the homepage acknowledgements, which is more transparency than most teams offer. Gaps are small: a few photographic figures carry no source line, and I did not find collaborations with other iGEM teams credited beyond the part lineage.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete and honest high-school project: real secretion, plant-rescue and perfusion-reactor data with controls, four built instruments and twelve documented DBTL cycles, held back by an optogenetic switch that is not yet convincingly demonstrated and a blank Attribution page.
strengths: Secreted ACC deaminase demonstrated across three orthogonal assays (anti-His Western, competitive ELISA, DNPH activity) with a plasmid-free WB800 control, and shown active in the cell-free shell permeate at 6-8 U/mg from 18 h through 72 h (Results, Figs 57, 66, 67).

Plant rescue tested in three systems (agar, hydroponics, soil) under salt and heat with mock and WB800-only controls, n = 9-40, mean +- SEM and stated p values, and the negative finding that co-treatment does not rescue while pre- and post-treatment do (Results, Figs 42-52).

A pre-registered prediction: a growth rate fitted to light-plate data was registered on 1 October with a 90% interval and pass criterion, then scored against reactor run 6 thirteen days later (0.286 +- 0.010 vs 0.2986 h-1 registered), with secondary endpoints declared unscorable in advance (Results, Stress detection).

Hardware iterations driven by test results rather than by re-running protocols: photometer tubing extended after pump vibration, permeate flow halved plus an acceptance filter after run 5's bubble failure, automated KOH dosing withdrawn after valve corrosion, antibiotic resupply shown to remove the spurious second exponential (Results, Membrane bioreactor).

Human Practices with dated, named design changes: Prof. Chen Wen-Liang's biosafety concern moved the project from released PGPR to a contained hollow-fiber bioreactor, and expert critique moved stress sensing out of the cell into electronic sensors (Integrated Human Practices, Project Evolution Map).

A reproducibility package rare at any level: 24 downloadable protocol PDFs, a 684-entry notebook exported with failures and repeats retained, hardware files, and a provenance ledger on Math Model marking every input as measured, literature, public record or modelled.
Failures are reported, not hidden: the AmilCP reporter that never coloured, the MoClo 2.0 screen that produced no usable clone, the leaked run, and the 10 h of data lost to a host-computer update.
weaknesses: The optogenetic switch, the project's central claim, is not convincingly demonstrated. ELISA was flat at 12-13 ug/mL under green and red alike at 13 h and 16 h (Fig 24), DNPH favoured green at 13 h but inverted by 16 h (Fig 25), and in the pre-cultured set red exceeded green at 8 h. The team identifies a likely cause (red LEDs at 640 nm rather than the ~672 nm CcaSR needs) but did not test or fix it.

Containment rests on two unreplicated platings with no quantitative log reduction, and the team records that incubation conditions for the June sample were never documented (Results, Membrane bioreactor).
Several load-bearing numbers are n = 1, including the secreted-activity figure feeding the whole dose model (7.25 mU/mL, DNPH, 7 October, n = 1, flagged by the team as below quantitation).

Competitive ELISA gave detectable signal in the plasmid-free WB800 control and several calculated concentrations fell outside the standard-curve range, which the team acknowledges but which weakens every absolute concentration on the page.

The Attribution page is entirely blank, live as well as in the crawl, so the role of six instructors, four returning student advisors and a weekly NTU postdoc mentor is nowhere delineated against the students' own work.

The integrated claim is not closed end to end: every reactor run used constitutive constructs in B. subtilis 168 or WB800, no forecast has driven a light, and no light-driven culture has reached the reactor, as the team states on Engineering and Results.
Two of the team's own pages disagree on deployment payback by more than an order of magnitude (68 years on Math Model, 4.9 from Geospatial Analysis) with no resolution offered.
Four standard URLs (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design) return 404; the content exists elsewhere and the navigation reaches it, but p.29 asks for standard pages to be preserved.
red_flags: Attribution page is completely blank (verified live at https://2026.igem.wiki/gems-taiwan/attributions, ~4.7 KB with no body content) despite substantial instructor, student-advisor and academic-mentor involvement visible elsewhere on the wiki. This lowers a6; it is a documentation gap, not an integrity matter.
Standard pages proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols and design return 404 (p.29 asks that standard URLs be preserved).

Containment evidence is n = 1 twice over, with no detection limit and no log-reduction figure, for the claim that underpins the project's biosafety case. The team says so itself, which is to their credit, but the claim should not be read as established.

Registry part pages could not be opened for verification during this review (parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403 from its CDN for every part tried). Aspect 8 is therefore scored from the team's own documentation-status table on the Parts page, which reports only 3 of 35 entries at Characterization level.

No academic-integrity concern found. Citations sampled on Results, Parts and Math Model resolve to real literature with correct DOIs; figures are described with stated n and controls rather than presented as cleaned; modelled quantities are explicitly labelled as modelled; and AI tooling is named in the homepage acknowledgements. Nothing here warrants a report to the RCC.

calibrated.changed: a6 3.5 -> 4.0. I gave Mingdao 4.0 for a task-level role list on the team page plus declared outsourcing, while penalising GEMS to 3.5 despite stronger evidence of the same kind: a task-level ownership matrix across six workstreams and a 684-entry notebook recording operator and recorder per entry. The blank Attributions page is a real gap and keeps it off 4.5, but on the evidence actually present this is at least Mingdao's level.

justification.a1: The scale achieved is at my top anchor for a high school team: a four-module CcaSR optogenetic circuit assembled into one Level 2 plasmid in B. subtilis WB800, three secreted protectant cargos, a self-built hollow-fibre perfusion bioreactor with inline photometer, pressure, pH and servo valve control, a 24-well light plate, plant assays on agar, hydroponics and soil, and a digital twin with fault detection and a pre-registered prediction (Results; Engineering; Software). Like GreatBay_SZ it is told as one chain of increasingly hard steps rather than a pile of modules. I hold it off 5 because the chain is not closed: by the team's own statement on Results, 'no forecast has yet driven a light, and no light driven by a forecast has reached a culture', and the hardware runs to September were on strain 168 or constitutive cargo rather than the light switch.
justification.a2: Most central claims are measured, with controls. ACCD, LEA14 and BoPep4 are detected by anti-His ELISA against a six-point curve (R2 0.9967, Table 2) and ACCD activity by DNPH with a PLP-minus arm and a plasmid-free WB800 control (Figs 12, 34). The reactor result is the strongest single piece: anti-His blot of lysate, lumen and shell at ~41 kDa (Fig 57), shell permeate above 2 ug/mL through 72 h with specific activity rising to 6-8 U/mg (Fig 67), and no shell-side colonies (Fig 58). Plant rescue is quantified with fresh weight and chlorophyll, n = 9-40, with significance marks (Figs 43, 45, 49) and includes negative findings (BoPep4 co-treatment harms plants). What is not shown is the headline function: ELISA is flat across green and red at both 3-8 h and 13-16 h (Figs 22, 24), DNPH disagrees between runs and inverts at 16 h, the WB800 control itself gives ELISA signal, and several ACCD values are extrapolated past the standard curve (Measurement). The team says all of this plainly, which I credit, but the light switch is not yet demonstrated as a switch.
justification.a3: The deployment case is argued carefully and with real constraints rather than slogans: 99.2% of Taiwanese farms under 2 ha and a mean manager age of 63.8 (Description), a 40 x 24 x 62 cm on-farm unit, a cartridge swapped like an ink cartridge, and a Laws and Regulations page on the Taiwanese route. The Math Model is honest where it hurts, showing that the 5.4-day production time for one hectare does not fit inside a three-day forecast, and that payback is 68 years on their own loss figure against 4.9 from Geospatial Analysis. Against my TAS Taipei anchor, though, nothing has been tested in a realistic setting: both field sensors have only been run on the bench and never in a field (Description), the hydroponic box was dosed by hand, and the reactor has never been plumbed to a crop.
justification.a4: This is the best engineering record I have read from a high school team and it is what pulls the project up. Twelve cloning DBTL cycles across three pipelines, where failures change the next build: MoClo abandoned for the SubtiToolKit after cycle 1 assembly efficiency, primers rediversified in cycle 4 because shared repeats confounded the BoPep4 screens, electroporation swept per construct and per strain (1.1 to 2.5 kV, Figs 7-11). The hardware cycles are the same discipline with instruments: photometer tubing extended to 30 cm after pump vibration displaced the optical axis (Fig 61), permeate flow cut from 24 to 12 mL/min plus an acceptance gate, which turned the unreadable run 5 into run 6's clean 0.14 to 2.71 curve, automated KOH dosing implemented then withdrawn on finding valve corrosion, and the second exponential phase tested as plasmid loss by resupplying erythromycin in cycle 4 and watching it disappear (Fig 63). A growth rate fitted on the light plate was registered on 1 October with an interval and then scored against run 6 thirteen days later (0.286 +/- 0.010 inside 0.2705-0.3300). That is prediction, not decoration.
justification.a5: 31 stakeholders over seven months, organised as a project evolution map with explicit 'What we changed' rows (Integrated Human Practices, around ten of them). The changes are real and traceable: Dr Jennifer Brophy's challenge to the kill-switch plan moved containment to a physical membrane, Prof. Chen Wen-Liang's biosafety objection moved the sensing out of the cell and into electronics, Prof. Chang's input on transmembrane pressure, caking and foaming reshaped the reactor, Yes Health iFarm changed the hydroponic setup, and Director Wu's point about rice overabundance moved the target crop to cherry tomato and strawberry. This is reflective and responsive in the handbook's sense rather than outreach relabelled as HP. It falls short of 5 only in that the page is long and partly repeats itself, and a few consultations end in intentions rather than a change.
justification.a6: The Attribution page is empty. I fetched it both as static HTML and with a headless render and it contains navigation and a footer, nothing else, so the form the handbook tells me to read is not there. The Members page partly rescues this with a genuine task-ownership matrix (19 tasks with owner and member counts, 23 on Lab, 9 on Protectant) and per-student accounts of what they did, which reads as student-led execution with six instructors and four returning student advisors in support. But the roles of those six instructors and of the outside suppliers thanked on the home page (IDT, Twist Bioscience, GenScript, and 'Claude') are nowhere stated, so I cannot tell what was synthesised or executed outside the team. I make no accusation; I record it as the first question I would ask, and score the missing form.
justification.a7: The collection is designed for reuse, which is what I look for beyond part count: 35 Registry entries built on the SubtiToolKit Golden Gate standard, five interchangeable modules, standard parts reused (B0015, Pveg, PliaG, J23100) and one green-light cassette deliberately left as a fluorescent dropout so a future cargo can be dropped into the same architecture (Parts). The Level 2 device BBa_260MVA1K joins the PCB, sensing, transduction and Csn-AcdS cassettes in one vector and was verified at its internal junctions. Codon-optimised variants (AcdS 2.1, BoPep4 2.1/2.2) were built as a comparison set rather than a single construct. I could not open parts.igem.org this session (CloudFront 403, then a CAPTCHA I will not attempt), so the deposits themselves are unverified by me.
justification.a8: The wiki-side documentation is exceptional: a Measurement page that gives the physical principle, calibration and controls for each assay, 25 protocol sheets with downloadable PDFs down to reagent volumes (Experiments), an Engineering page with data behind every cycle, and a provenance ledger in the Math Model naming which of fifteen inputs are measured, public, published or uncited. On the Registry side, which is what this aspect turns on, the team's own table shows only two entries marked Characterization, most marked Experiment, and at least one (BBa_263IW021) with no documentation; and I could not reach the Registry to check depth myself. The three sheets that produced no result on the wiki are declared, which I credit.
justification.w1: A reader can state the aim, chassis, parts and success criterion after the home and description pages: predict field stress, switch on CcaSR in B. subtilis WB800 with 520 nm green light, secrete ACC deaminase, keep the cells behind a 0.2 um hollow-fibre membrane and spray the permeate. The Description's component map is the best piece of communication here, giving each of the twelve subsystems one paragraph plus a frank state-of-play line ('Both have been characterized on the bench so far; neither has run in a field'). Not a 5 only because the five-demand framing on the home page takes a while to reach the mechanism.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently tied to numbered figures with methods, replicate counts and statistics, and the negative results are kept in: the AmilCP reporter that never coloured, with the A588 numbers and a folding explanation (Fig 17), the contaminated agar plate excluded as ND (Fig 42), the leak at 37 h that made OD600 rise spuriously (Fig 65), and the 13 h green DNPH peak that did not repeat at 16 h. Limits are stated where they bite, for example that the calibration used non-living particles so OD cannot be read as cell count, and that containment rests on two unreplicated platings with no log reduction. I withhold the 5 because the central light-control claim rests on assays the team themselves show to be inconsistent.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly (Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Engagement, Team) with on-page contents and a 'For judges' entry on Hardware. Against that, four standard pages a judge goes to first return 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design) and Attribution renders empty, so the content is there but not where the rubric sends me. The site is also genuinely sprawling: 33,000 words on Engineering and 28,000 on Measurement, against the handbook's 'complete but not sprawling'.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this. The Contribution page hands over printable hardware files and standardised dimensions for the reactor, photometer, light plate and hydroponics box, a 15-page plant protocol, a 96-well DNPH activity assay, the digital twin software and an LLM-assisted GIS workflow, each with notes on what worked and what did not. The 25 protocol PDFs, the dry lab notebook and the per-cycle engineering record are all on iGEM servers, and the site repository is on iGEM GitLab. The empty Attribution page and the missing protocols route are what keep it off 5.
justification.w5: Technical pages cite properly and the references resolve to real work: Castillo-Hair 2019 and Haller 2025 for CcaSR in B. subtilis, Caro-Astorga 2025 for the SubtiToolKit, Beal 2020 for OD-to-cell-count, van de Hulst for the silica extinction model, plus vendor specifications for the hollow-fibre module and pump. The signal-peptide correction factor is openly sourced to Brockmeier 2006 and Ying 2013 with the caveat that the two peptides have never been compared in one experiment, which is the right way to cite a borrowed constant. Marked down because Description and the whole Human Practices page carry no citations at all.

J2.one_line: An unusually complete engineered system for a high school team, with real DBTL cycles and honest data, let down by an empty Attribution page and a light switch that is built but not yet shown to switch.
strengths: Genuine DBTL across twelve cloning cycles and the hardware: the MoClo-to-SubtiToolKit switch, primer rediversification after the BoPep4 screens, the 30 cm tubing fix for pump vibration, the 24 to 12 mL/min flow change plus acceptance gate that turned unreadable run 5 into run 6's clean 0.14 to 2.71 curve, and KOH dosing withdrawn after it corroded the feed valve

A pre-registered prediction: a growth rate fitted on the light plate, registered with a 90% interval on 1 October, then scored against run 6 thirteen days later at 0.286 +/- 0.010 h-1, inside the interval

The bioreactor result is measured end to end for its own claim: anti-His blot across lysate, lumen and shell (Fig 57), shell permeate above 2 ug/mL for 72 h with specific activity 6-8 U/mg (Fig 67), and no shell-side colonies (Fig 58)

Plant rescue quantified with fresh weight and chlorophyll across agar, hydroponic and soil systems, n = 9-40, with WB800 and medium controls, and with the inconvenient findings kept in (BoPep4 co-treatment inhibits growth)

Human Practices that changed the design and says so: the kill switch dropped for physical containment after Dr Brophy, sensing moved out of the cell after Prof. Chen, target crop changed to cherry tomato and strawberry after Director Wu
A parts collection built for reuse on a published Golden Gate standard, including a cargo slot left open as a fluorescent dropout

Self-criticism that would do credit to an industrial report: the Math Model's provenance ledger for fifteen inputs, the admission that the 5.4-day production time does not fit a three-day forecast, and the 68-year versus 4.9-year payback disagreement left on the page
weaknesses: The Attribution page has no content at all, so the form the handbook tells judges to read is absent and the roles of six instructors and of outside suppliers are undeclared
Four standard pages return 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design), so a judge following the standard route misses content that exists elsewhere

The optogenetic switch is not demonstrated as a switch: ELISA is flat across green and red at every time point, DNPH results invert between 13 and 16 h, and red light at 640 nm does not turn the circuit off
No stage of the system has been joined to the next end to end; by the team's own statement no forecast has driven a light and no light driven by a forecast has reached a culture
Both field sensors have only run on the bench, and their leaf-minus-air offset drifts by site (-0.2 to +1.8 C), so no stress threshold can be set from them yet
Containment rests on two unreplicated platings with no detection limit, no log reduction, and undocumented incubation for the June sample
ELISA quantification is shaky where it matters: the plasmid-free WB800 control gives signal and several ACCD values are extrapolated beyond the standard curve
The wiki is very long (33,000 words on Engineering, 28,000 on Measurement) against the handbook's 'complete but not sprawling'
red_flags: Attribution page is empty (verified by both static fetch and headless render of https://2026.igem.wiki/gems-taiwan/attributions); I would ask in Q&A who did the gene synthesis and what the six instructors and four student advisors executed. Not an accusation, a missing disclosure.

'Claude' is listed among the acknowledgements on the home page with no statement anywhere of what AI was used for; the Software page separately describes a farmer-facing LLM feature. With the Attribution page empty, there is no AI-use declaration to read. I raise this as a question only; I saw no concrete indicator of AI-generated evidence figures or fabricated citations, and the references I checked are real papers.

Parts could not be verified this session: parts.igem.org returned CloudFront 403 to curl and a CAPTCHA under headless Chrome, which I did not attempt to solve. a7 and a8 therefore rest on the team's own parts table, which itself marks only two entries as characterised and at least one as undocumented. Another judge with Registry access should confirm the 35 deposits.

Quantification caveats the team discloses but that still cap confidence in the yield numbers: WB800 negative control produces ELISA signal, and several reported ACCD concentrations lie outside the standard curve.
pages_read: attributions (empty; checked live via curl and headless Chrome)
x__plant, x__hardware_bioreactor, x__drylab_notebook, x__geospatial_analysis, x__md_simulations, x__protein_design (skim)
attempted parts.igem.org for BBa_260MVA1K, BBa_26PGPSGK, BBa_261XH2RS - blocked by 403 then CAPTCHA, not verified

calibrated.changed: a6 2.5->3.0: I gave squirrel-beijing and plklfc 3.0 for a missing form plus genuine per-task credits elsewhere, and this team's 19-task ownership matrix with per-student accounts is at least as good, so 2.5 was harsher than my own bar. a8 4.0->3.5: by the team's own parts table only two entries are characterised and one is undocumented, with the Registry unreachable — the same situation where I gave hk-joint-school and labi-taiwan 3.5 despite excellent wiki documentation.

justification.a1: The scope is near the top of what I have seen from a high school team: an optogenetic CcaSR circuit in B. subtilis WB800, three protectant cargos, a self-built hollow-fiber perfusion bioreactor with an inline photometer, a 24-well light plate, a digital twin, a stress index fitted to 25 years of county rice yields, and plant assays in agar, hydroponics and soil (Description; Results; Engineering). Unlike most ambitious projects, almost every layer carries data, and the team states plainly on Engineering that 'none of these numbers is the light switch doing anything'. It falls just short of the GreatBay climb because the chain is never joined end to end: no forecast has driven a light, and no light-driven culture has fed the reactor.
justification.a2: Measured and controlled: ELISA and DNPH on supernatants against a plasmid-free WB800 control (Results, Figures 12-14, Table 2), anti-His Western blots of lysate, lumen and shell showing ~41 kDa ACCD crossing the membrane (Figure 57), active enzyme above 2 ug/mL in the cell-free shell for 72 h with specific activity 5-8.4 U/mg (Figure 67), no colonies on the shell side (Figure 58), and Arabidopsis rescue with mock and WB800 controls, n = 9-40 and p values (Figures 43, 45, 49-52). The central claim, light control, is the weak one: ELISA shows no light dependence (Figures 22, 24), DNPH green-versus-red inverts between 13 h and 16 h (Figure 25), and the red LED is at 640 nm when CcaSR needs ~672 nm, all of which the team reports honestly. Containment rests on two unreplicated platings with no log reduction.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by the people who would use the system, not just literature: Ms. Chen in Tamsui, the Taipei Expo and Water Garden farmers' markets, the World Vegetable Center and CH Biotech (Integrated Human Practices), and the deployment case is worked out in cost and geography across 346 townships (Math Model M5; Geospatial Analysis). I credit the honesty that ReLEAF conflicts with Taiwan's organic production rules, which excludes many of the very farmers interviewed, and that the two payback estimates disagree (68 years against 4.9). It is not yet a 5 because nothing has run in a field: the sensors have only been on the bench, and the permeate was carried to plants by hand.
justification.a4: This is the strongest engineering record on the ballot. Failure drives redesign repeatedly: MoClo 2.0 background leads to the SubtiToolKit with an intermediate cloning step (Engineering, cloning cycle 1-2); pump vibration on short tubing is fixed by a 30 cm extension in cycle 3; a pH feedback loop is built, then withdrawn when 1 M KOH corrodes the feeding valve, with the team noting that peroxide and KOH cannot be told apart in their data; antibiotic resupply removes the spurious second exponential and explains it as plasmid loss (Results, Figure 63); run 5's bubbles lead to a lower permeate flow and an acceptance filter in run 6. The pre-registered growth-rate prediction from the light plate, written down on 1 October and scored on run 6 thirteen days later, with the secondary endpoints left unscored for the stated reason, is a level of discipline I rarely see at any level.
justification.a5: The 4A loop is real and traceable. Dr. Brophy's input replaced a kill switch with physical containment; Prof. Chen Wen-Liang turned soil release into a contained bioreactor; Prof. Cheng Mei-Chun moved the plant model from hydroponics to an agar-to-soil transition and removed osmotic stress; Mr. Chen Ke-Wei's typhoon and animal question moved the unit indoors; Prof. Huang Chieh-Chen's advice shifted dosing to the seedling stage and to periodic operation (Integrated Human Practices, project evolution map and 'the gap we noticed' table). Critical voices were kept, not smoothed over: the natural farmers who argued that protecting a crop from every stress weakens it, and the organic-certification conflict. What is missing is any statement of consent or ethics oversight for the farmer interviews and the student surveys, which keeps this below a 5.
justification.a6: The Members page is unusually explicit, with a task matrix of nineteen tasks naming each student as task owner or task member, defined training thresholds for a wet lab or dry lab 'major', and separate listings for student advisors and six instructors. Outside help is named in context too: Prof. Huang supplied the WB800 strain and Prof. Cheng the Arabidopsis seeds (Integrated Human Practices). But the Attribution page itself is empty, both in the crawl and when I rendered it live, so the one place the handbook sends a judge says nothing, and figure captions never say who ran which experiment. With sophisticated work on the page (Western blots, competitive ELISA, an instrumented perfusion loop) and six instructors listed, I cannot tell from the wiki where the students' hands stopped, so this is a session question rather than a criticism.
justification.a7: The design is standard parts throughout: 35 Registry entries in five interchangeable modules built with SubtiToolKit Golden Gate across Levels 0, 1 and 2, assembled from fourteen prior entries that are individually credited with what each contributes (Parts). The Level 2 device joins PCB production, CcaS-m3 sensing, CcaR transduction and a PcpcG2-veg protectant cassette in one pSTK vector, and the open mScarlet-I dropout cassette is a genuinely reusable entry point for a cargo the team has not built. Hardware and the digital twin add standard components in the handbook's wider sense. Short of 5 only because the headline device is verified by junction checks and a double digest rather than end-to-end sequencing, as the team states.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is excellent: every figure has a quantitative caption, protocols and build manuals are on the wiki as PDFs, and the Parts page maps each of the 35 entries to a Registry ID with its documentation level declared. That declaration is also what holds the score down: only a handful are marked 'Characterization', most say 'Experiment' or 'Design', and four regulatory entries plus one green-light cassette carry none. I could not open parts.igem.org from here to verify depth (403), so I score the self-reported picture, which is honest but uneven, with the richest data (time courses, blots, controls) living on the wiki rather than in the Registry entries.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the five demands, the whole device and the six-step mechanism in a few readable screens, with maps and a labelled 3D model, and ends by routing the reader to Description, Results, Hardware, Measurement and Human Practices. Description then gives a technical map in which each component says what it is and, pointedly, what has not yet been done ('Both have been characterized on the bench so far; neither has run in a field'). I would only ask that the home page's 'Green light switches production on' be softened to match the equivocal induction data on Results.
justification.w2: Claims are tied to figures with units, replicate counts and statistics, and model output is labelled as such: the stress-detection table marks each endpoint 'Measured' or 'Partial', and the Math Model's provenance ledger tags every input as ours, public record, literature or 'modeled, not measured', with five assumptions and what would overturn each. Negative results are kept, including the colourless AmilCP supernatant and the leaf-minus-air offset that makes a canopy threshold impossible for now. It is not a 5 because several load-bearing numbers are n = 1 (secreted activity, the 72 h ELISA points, the containment platings) and the light-induction conclusion is stated more firmly in the abstracts than Figures 22-25 support.
justification.w3: Navigation is coherent and the Description page acts as a map, but a great deal of the evidence sits off the standard pages (plant, hardware-bioreactor, hardware-photometer, development, geospatial-analysis, md-simulations), and proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols and design all return 404 while Attribution and Inclusivity render as headings with no content. At roughly 190,000 words the wiki is closer to sprawling than to 'complete but not sprawling', and some pages (Engineering at 33,000 words, Measurement at 28,000) ask a lot of a judge. Everything is reachable, which is why this is still above the middle.
justification.w4: This is the part a future team will thank them for: assembly guides and user manuals for the bioreactor, both photometers and the light plate, a dated hardware notebook from March to October with entries such as 'Zeroed against the wrong thing', a 15-page plant protocol, a scaled-down DNPH assay sheet, print files, the part collection and MIT-licensed digital twin source on iGEM GitLab (Contribution; Hardware). Failures and their causes are written down in enough detail to be avoided. The empty Attribution page and the missing Protocols standard page are the only real gaps in the record.
justification.w5: Each page carries its own reference list with DOIs, the Parts page credits all fourteen borrowed Registry entries by BBa number and says what each does in the constructs, and the LLM-assisted GIS workflow is disclosed with its prompt and the prompt-engineering literature behind it. A few entries are thin (the Ying 2013 SamyQ citation has no journal or volume, and the vendor specifications are listed without links), and I could not check that every DOI resolves to the claim made. Figure provenance for the maps and photographs is not stated, though they appear to be the team's own.

J3.one_line: An unusually honest and deeply engineered high school project: real secretion, containment and plant-rescue data plus a pre-registered prediction, let down by an equivocal light switch, an empty Attribution page and considerable sprawl.
strengths: Twelve-plus documented DBTL cycles in which specific failures changed the next build (MoClo to SubtiToolKit, photometer tubing extension, KOH corrosion ending automated pH dosing, antibiotic resupply removing the spurious second exponential) - Engineering and Results

A pre-registered growth-rate prediction written down on 1 October from light-plate data and scored against bioreactor run 6 thirteen days later, with secondary endpoints left unscored for a stated reason (Results, stress detection)

Membrane function demonstrated rather than asserted: anti-His Western blots of lysate, lumen and shell, active ACCD above 2 ug/mL in the cell-free shell through 72 h at 5-8.4 U/mg, and no colonies on the shell side (Results, Figures 57, 58, 67)

Human practices with traceable consequences and retained criticism: kill switch replaced by physical containment, soil release replaced by a contained reactor, hydroponics replaced by agar-to-soil, the unit moved indoors after a typhoon question, and the organic-certification conflict acknowledged as excluding many interviewed farmers

An exceptional handover record for future teams: assembly guides, user manuals, a dated hardware notebook naming its own mistakes, a 15-page plant protocol, a scaled-down DNPH sheet and MIT-licensed digital twin source on iGEM GitLab (Contribution, Hardware)

A model that states the provenance of all fifteen inputs, lists five assumptions with what would overturn each, and reports that its own payback figure (68 years) disagrees with the Geospatial page (4.9)
weaknesses: The optogenetic switch, the project's central mechanism, is not convincingly demonstrated: ELISA shows no light dependence at any time point, DNPH green-versus-red inverts between 13 h and 16 h, and the red LED emits at 640 nm when CcaSR needs about 672 nm (Results, Figures 22-25)

The chain is never joined end to end - no forecast has driven a light and no light-driven culture has fed the reactor, and the field sensors have only been run on a bench with a site-dependent offset of -0.2 to +1.8 C (Results, field sensors)

The Attribution page is empty both in the crawl and when rendered live, so despite a good task matrix on Members there is no single statement of what students did versus the six instructors and the host labs that supplied strains and seeds
Several load-bearing numbers rest on n = 1 (secreted activity 7.25 mU/mL, the 72 h ELISA points, both containment platings, with incubation conditions for the June plate undocumented)
Sprawl: roughly 190,000 words with much of the evidence on non-standard pages, while proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols and design return 404 and Inclusivity renders as a heading only
Richest characterisation data live on the wiki rather than in Registry entries; by the team's own table most of the 35 parts are marked only 'Experiment' or 'Design'
red_flags: Attribution page published but empty (verified live with headless Chrome, 2026.igem.wiki/gems-taiwan/attributions) - raises an attribution question for the session rather than an accusation

Pre- and post-lesson surveys of elementary and junior high students, and farmer interviews with named individuals and photographs, with no mention anywhere of consent, anonymisation or ethics oversight

Home page and several abstracts state 'Green light switches ACCD on' more firmly than Figures 22-25 support; the Engineering page's own caveat ('none of these numbers is the light switch doing anything') is the more accurate statement
Registry entries could not be verified from this environment (parts.igem.org returned 403), so part-level documentation depth is scored from the team's own self-reported table

Disclosed AI use (an LLM prompt for GIS data preparation, an optional API-key chat in the app, Claude listed among acknowledgements) appears limited and legitimate; I found no sign of fabricated data or AI-authored reasoning presented as the team's voice

calibrated.changed: a2 3.5 to 4.0. Side by side I was harsher here than anywhere else for the same evidence class. GEMS reports ELISA and DNPH against a plasmid-free control, anti-His blots of three compartments, specific activity in U/mg, shell-side sterility and Arabidopsis rescue with n = 9-40 and p values; I gave 4.0 to Cataverse, whose own pages state no sample sizes, replicates or error bars anywhere, and to SHSID, whose colour scoring has no stated replicates. Penalising the failed light switch twice, once in a2 and once in the one-line summary, put a well-controlled multi-module dataset below weaker ones. The equivocal induction remains the reason this is not 4.5.

one_line.en: The most complete engineered system in the field — real secretion, plant-rescue and reactor data, four instruments, twelve DBTL cycles and a pre-registered prediction — undercut by a light switch that is not shown to switch and a blank Attribution page.
one_line.zh: 全場最完整的工程系統——真實的分泌、植物救援與反應器數據，四台儀器，十二個 DBTL 循環，還有預先登記的預測——但光控開關未能證實會切換，Attribution 頁完全空白。

strengths: Secreted ACC deaminase shown by three orthogonal assays with a plasmid-free control, and active in the cell-free shell permeate at 6-8 U/mg from 18 h to 72 h
Plant rescue in agar, hydroponics and soil under salt and heat, n = 9-40, with mock and WB800-only controls and an inconvenient negative finding retained
A pre-registered growth-rate prediction with a stated interval and pass criterion, scored against a later reactor run, with secondary endpoints declared unscorable in advance
Hardware and cloning iterations driven by test results, plus a provenance ledger, 24 protocol PDFs and a 684-entry notebook with failures retained
weaknesses: The optogenetic switch, the central mechanism, is not demonstrated: ELISA flat under green and red, DNPH inverting between 13 h and 16 h, red exceeding green at 8 h in one set
The Attribution page is empty on the live site, leaving six instructors, four student advisors and a postdoc mentor undeclared
Several load-bearing numbers are n = 1, including the secreted-activity figure behind the dose model and both containment platings, with no log reduction
The system is never joined end to end — no forecast HAS driven a light, no light-driven culture HAS reached the reactor, and both field sensors have only run on a bench
red_flags: Results banner states that green light switches ACCD on while the figures beneath it do not support that, and the team's own Engineering caveat is the more accurate statement
