Four standard URLs (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design) return 404
Two of the team's own pages disagree on deployment payback by more than an order of magnitude with no resolution

screen.project_title: SENTINEL-LOOP — dual lead/cadmium whole-cell biosensing, surface-display removal and SWASV verification
screen.what_they_built: A designed three-layer prototype: PbrR and CadR whole-cell biosensors for lead and cadmium, Lpp-OmpA surface display of PbBD and EC20 peptides for removal, and square-wave anodic stripping voltammetry on a bismuth-film screen-printed electrode as an orthogonal check. Six modules were planned; the integrated loop was never attempted.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli with pSB3K3 and pBR322 constructs, all from ordered synthetic DNA (no source organisms cultured). Parts page lists designs but the crawl found no BBa IDs anywhere on the wiki.
screen.best_evidence: There is no experimental performance evidence. /results states plainly: "this page reports no experimental performance numbers" and every assay table (EC50, Hill coefficient, LoD, specificity matrix) is empty with em-dashes. The strongest real findings are software-side, on /engineering: a self-written test recovered a known growth rate of 0.50 as 0.38, exposing a 30-47% underestimate of metabolic burden, and a second test showed the pipeline was fabricating blank replicates and emitting synthetic LoDs indistinguishable from measured ones. Wet-lab findings are limited to a rejected clone (A07, D508Y in lacZ, caught by full-insert sequencing) and the phosphate-precipitation argument that moved the lead assay out of M9.
screen.hp_integration: Barely — the human practices page is 374 words and nothing on the wiki shows stakeholder input altering a design decision.
screen.reason: Exemplary scientific honesty and genuinely useful software-engineering discipline (provenance labels, refusal to emit an LoD without real blanks, Sobol analysis over 2,304 runs, 96 tests), and the M9-phosphate warning is a real gift to future teams. But the handbook requires evidence that the project worked, and there is none: no induction curve, no removal number, not a single voltammetry sweep. Aspects 2 and 5 collapse and no amount of candour can lift this into the top two.
screen.field_notes: GeorgetownPrep (Bioremediation, USA) designed SENTINEL-LOOP, a detect-remove-verify prototype for lead and cadmium in water: PbrR and CadR whole-cell biosensors, Lpp-OmpA surface display of PbBD and EC20 for capture, and square-wave anodic stripping voltammetry on bismuth-film screen-printed electrodes as an orthogonal read-out. No wet-lab performance data exists; the results page explicitly withholds every number rather than substituting simulation, and tables for EC50, LoD, dynamic range and cross-metal specificity are left empty by design. Of six modules, only the modelling module closed full DBTL cycles: self-written tests caught a growth-rate fitter understating metabolic burden by 30-47% and a pipeline silently fabricating blank replicates to manufacture a limit of detection, both fixed, with SYNTHETIC/PREDICTED/FITTED provenance labels, a 2,304-run Sobol sensitivity decomposition and 96 tests including an Ishigami analytic check. Two transferable wet-lab warnings are recorded: any Pb(II) induction assay in standard phosphate minimal medium measures Pb3(PO4)2 precipitation rather than sensing and still yields a plausible dose-response curve, and junction-only sequencing passed a clone carrying a D508Y substitution inside lacZ. The team also reports mis-scaled antibiotic plates (~2x kanamycin, ~3.3x carbenicillin) that cost them colony-size burden evidence. Human practices is 374 words; the crawl found no registered BBa parts.

screen.project_title: HoldeX — paper-based cell-free toehold detection of antibiotic resistance genes in water
screen.what_they_built: A cell-free, paper-based screening platform for the resistance genes mcr-1, blaNDM-1 and blaKPC-2: NUPACK-designed toehold switches driving GFP first, then the colorimetric enzymes GusA, XylE and LacZ, read in the ARGUS 3D-printed device with image-analysis software and a surveillance database.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning, BL21(DE3) for reporter enzyme expression, and an E. coli cell-free extract (pJL1 backbone, T7) for the actual assay; pET-21a for reporter production. A Registry collection of nine parts: three switch–GFP constructs, three switch–enzyme constructs and three trigger RNAs.
screen.best_evidence: /results, second-round screening: MCR1_4, NDM1_4 and KPC2_4 each gave higher endpoint GFP fluorescence with their cognate trigger RNA than without over 1.5 h, after a first round where all nine designs failed to separate +/- trigger. On paper, all three switch–enzyme constructs developed visible colour, and CIELAB/CIEDE2000 analysis put 3 uM trigger samples closer to the 5 uM positive control than to the no-trigger control (relative colour-difference change 46.80% MCR1, 41.06% KPC2, 40.20% NDM1).
screen.hp_integration: Yes — a public survey drove the stakeholder map and the education plan, and engagement across five stages reframed the product as a government-facing preliminary screening and data system for livestock AMR operated by trained frontline staff, with positive or uncertain results explicitly routed to standard confirmatory laboratory methods rather than standing alone.
screen.reason: Complete design-build-test chain with its own failure round: switches screened, redesigned on NUPACK evidence, re-tested, reporters independently expressed (SDS-PAGE, substrate titration) and then integrated on paper with instrumented colour analysis, plus hardware, software and a nine-part Registry collection. The scale and closure of the loop is finalist-shaped for a high school team; the open questions (no LOD, no environmental sample, no RPA-to-colour end-to-end run, single-replicate colour data, background colour in the negative) are exactly what a full read should probe.
screen.field_notes: GHCIS (CHN, Conservation) built a portable screening platform for antibiotic resistance genes in environmental water, combining recombinase polymerase amplification, toehold switches and paper-based cell-free expression with an enzymatic colour readout, targeting mcr-1, blaNDM-1 and blaKPC-2 under a One Health framing. Four linked DBTL cycles are documented: nine first-round switches in pJL1-sfGFP gave no separation between plus and minus trigger (NDM1_3 rose in both), a NUPACK 4.1.0.1 redesign against AMRFinder family panels produced MCR1_4, NDM1_4 and KPC2_4 with cognate activation proxies of 0.873-0.940 and cross-gene proxies below 3e-4, and these showed higher endpoint fluorescence with cognate trigger over 1.5 h. LacZ, XylE and GusA were cloned into pET-21a, expressed in BL21(DE3) with SDS-PAGE bands at 116, 34.5 and 68.2 kDa including soluble fractions, and titrated against CPRG, catechol and X-Glc; the three were then fused behind the selected switches and dried onto Whatman paper, where all three gave visible colour at 3 and 5 uM trigger with measurable background at 0 uM. Colour was quantified by RGB to CIELAB conversion and CIEDE2000 in their own ARGUS software, and the ARGUS hardware (temperature control for RPA, illumination, sample drawer, strip card) is shared as STEP and STL files alongside a role-based surveillance database. The team states plainly that no limit of detection, no specificity or predictive-value figures and no environmental-sample performance have been established, and that the complete DNA-to-colour workflow has not been run. Registry collection of nine parts; education and entrepreneurship pages are very large.

screen.project_title: ZipTide: computationally screened octapeptides against zonulin-driven gut barrier damage
screen.what_they_built: A descriptor-based screen of the 8-residue peptide space ranked against larazotide, yielding three candidate peptides (ZT-1 to ZT-3) tested for reversal of gliadin-induced zonulin release in Caco-2 cells.
screen.chassis_and_parts: No living chassis in the tested work; synthetic octapeptides ordered from a supplier and assayed on Caco-2 cells. Parts: BBa_2672PHOM, BBa_2693TUBQ, BBa_26T1WXK7, BBa_26ZR81G2.
screen.best_evidence: /results: one ELISA run (19 October 2026) in which gliadin raised supernatant zonulin about 4.8-fold (1.27 to 6.04 ng/mL), larazotide reversed 30.5%, ZT-1 reversed 13.5% against a pre-registered 15.3% threshold, and ZT-3 reversed -10.7%; standard curve R2 = 0.9991. One sample per group, read three times.
screen.hp_integration: Extensive engagement (30,438-word human-practices page plus a 19,217-word culture-bridge page); a clinical research associate and an accredited laboratory consulted in October named the missing vehicle and viability controls and set a seven-measurement floor for statistics, which shaped the future-work plan rather than the run that was performed.
screen.reason: The team's own pre-registered criterion returned a negative: both tested candidates missed the threshold, there is one biological sample per group, no vehicle, cell-free or viability control, no statistical test, and the delivered peptide concentrations were never confirmed because the vials arrived short (ZT-2 arrived empty and was never tested). The intellectual honesty is exemplary and the screen is elegant, but aspect 2 cannot carry a finalist case, and the wiki runs to well over 100,000 words across HP, sustainability, education and culture pages against the handbook's 'complete but not sprawling' standard.
screen.field_notes: Gikal (Turkiye, Therapeutics village) designed ZipTide, octapeptides intended to repair zonulin-driven tight-junction opening in the small intestine, targeting the PAR2/EGFR pathway that releases ZO-1 from occludin and claudin-1. The screen collapses 25.6 billion ordered 8-mers onto 2,220,075 order-independent compositions using MW, pI, GRAVY and net charge, ranks by Euclidean distance to larazotide (AT-1001) on five normalised descriptors in Python and Biopython, then applies toxicity, allergenicity and haemolysis predictors; running larazotide through the pipeline as a control exposed AllerTOP v2 as a likely high-false-positive filter on short peptides, which the team then demoted to a conservative pre-screen. The single wet-lab run was an ELISA on gliadin-challenged Caco-2 cells: gliadin raised zonulin 4.8-fold, larazotide reversed 30.5%, ZT-1 13.5% (below the pre-set 15.3% bar) and ZT-3 -10.7%; ZT-2 was never tested because its vial arrived empty, and the other vials were short so delivered doses are unconfirmed. The team reports the negative against its own pre-registered criterion, lists the missing controls (cell-free, vehicle, viability), notes one sample per group with triplicate reads so no error bar or statistical test is possible, and records that one of four validity conditions failed. Three DBTL passes are described with two declared closed. The wiki carries a bilingual voice-assistant reader and very large HP, sustainability, education and culture-bridge pages.

screen.project_title: Expelliodor — protein-based axillary odour management
screen.what_they_built: Three protein strategies against the body-odour precursor Cys-Gly-3M3SH: AI de novo precursor binders, de novo binders that lock the S. hominis peptide transporter PepTSh, and an engineered CGTase that glycosylates the precursor, plus two-strain E. coli co-cultures making terpenoid ester fragrances, all tested on a PepTSh-expressing E. coli surrogate with an Ellman thiol readout.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3)/DH5α surrogate expressing PepTSh; ~30 new BBa parts (BBa_26... series) covering binders, CGTase variants, MVA/borneol and geranyl-butyrate modules; reuse of GreatBay-China 2018 pMVA.
screen.best_evidence: /model and /engineering: of 9 designed precursor binders 4 significantly lowered 3M3SH vs negative control; 4 of 5 transporter binders reduced it (max 21%); CGTase groups gave >50% lower mean thiol than the 0.676 ± 0.108 mM GSH-equivalent control; /engineering/terpenoid-ester GC-MS plus standard curve gave 1.2269 µg/mL bornyl acetate and 2.0116 µg/mL geranyl butyrate.
screen.hp_integration: Five-stage, multi-cycle iHP (surveys, patients, industry, community) chose the woody/floral scent targets and the non-antiperspirant, autonomy-respecting product framing, and fed the packaging and accessibility design.
screen.reason: Quantitative, controlled wet-lab evidence that de novo designed and engineered parts actually reduced the target metabolite, two DBTL cycles per module, GC-MS-quantified secondary products, ~30 documented parts and deep iHP. Clear Gate A pass; the soft spot for the panel is the near-empty Attributions page (aspect 6).
screen.field_notes: GreatBay-SCIE 2026 (Expelliodor, Fashion & Cosmetics, CHN) attacks axillary odour at the precursor level rather than by killing skin flora or blocking sweat. They built a PepTSh-expressing E. coli surrogate so all assays could run in a high-school-legal chassis, then tested three routes: RFdiffusion3/Proteina de novo precursor binders (4 of 9 significantly reduced 3M3SH), de novo transporter binders restricting the IF-to-OF transition (4 of 5 active, max 21% reduction), and CGTase glycosylation (treatment groups >50% below the 0.676 ± 0.108 mM GSH-equivalent control in Ellman's assay, wild type best; T370R expressed poorly and was dropped). A parallel two-strain E. coli co-culture produced bornyl acetate (1.2269 µg/mL) and geranyl butyrate (2.0116 µg/mL), both confirmed by GC-MS fragment matching and quantified against standard curves. About 30 new BBa parts, a Characterize-DBTL framework with two cycles per module, docking/MD plus thermostability redesign, a five-stage iHP programme and very large education/inclusivity work (tactile graphics, sign language). Attributions page is essentially a contact block, which is the main unverified area.

justification.a1: Three mechanistically distinct interventions on one pathway (de novo precursor binder, de novo conformation-selective transporter binder, engineered CGTase) were each built and tested in a surrogate the team made themselves (Engineering/Surrogate Construction), plus two fragrance esters produced and confirmed by GC-MS (Engineering/Terpenoid Ester), a design software (Software, FoundryUI) and a formulation/packaging study (Hardware). That is real scale and scope in increasing difficulty, close to the GreatBay_SZ/TAS anchor; it falls just short of a 5 because the final integrated product was never assembled or tested as one thing, and the optimisation round for the binders was designed but never run.
justification.a2: Function is shown against proper controls with stated units and statistics: PepTSh-expressing E. coli gave a precursor-dependent rise in thiol vs empty-vector control (Engineering/Surrogate Construction, Fig. 3b, ±SD n=3); four of nine precursor binders gave significant reductions (0.202-0.210 vs 0.228 mM GSH-eq, Welch t-test, Fig. 5b); four of five transporter binders were significant, TB2 at 26.7% (Fig. 13b, ANOVA + Dunnett); CGTase treatments cut thiol >50% vs PBS (Fig. 9b, p<0.001). It is not a 5 because Ellman's is an indirect, non-specific thiol readout (the team says so on Measurement), the replicates are technical only and Measurement itself notes batch-to-batch variation, the binder effects are ~8-11%, and no direct evidence of binding (no ITC/SPR) or of a glycosylated product (no LC-MS) is shown.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and expert-informed: formulation and skincare experts, an immunologist, a patent expert, Amcor and the deodorant brand KleanK shaped the roll-on format, buffer, pH 6.0 and packaging material, with a pilot-scale cost of about ¥1.18 per 50 mL bottle (Hardware) and an in-silico HLA-II/allergen screen of all 14 candidates (Safety). What is missing for a 5 is any test in a real-world-like setting: no skin or sweat-derived precursor, no S. hominis, no stability or delivery data in the actual container, so impact is argued from surrogate assays and literature rather than measured in use.
justification.a4: The C-DBTL cycles are genuine iterations driven by data or feedback, not just troubleshooting: the SynBio expert's advice led to redesigning the transporter-binder plasmids with a DsbA periplasmic signal so the binder could reach PepTSh (HP Stage 3, Cycle 3; Engineering/Transporter Binder); KleanK's storage/transport concern triggered a whole second CGTase cycle for thermostability with SPURS-guided multi-point mutants and a heat-precipitation test (Engineering/CGTase Cycle 2). Failures are reported honestly (BC9 would not transform, the intended T370K came back as T370L, WR6/KR6 undelivered). It stops short of 5 because the heat assay is only qualitative visible precipitation with no post-heat activity data, and Precursor Binder Cycle 2 has a Design and Build but no Test.
justification.a5: 46 stakeholder interactions across five stages with an explicit iterative ODOR cycle and a stakeholder classification (Human Practices overview), and the feedback visibly changed the project: fragrance choice from survey preferences, thermostability added after KleanK, periplasmic expression after Prof. Meng, accessible packaging after inclusive-design work, and the slogan rewritten to "Expel the Odor, on Your Terms" after sociologists and a psychiatrist pushed back on the stigma framing. This is two-way dialogue shaping both design and messaging, at the GreatBay_SZ level; it is not quite a 5 only because some later-stage activity (seminar, handbook) is outreach whose effect on the technical project is less direct.
justification.a6: The Attributions page is empty - it renders a heading and nothing else (verified live at /attributions as well as in the crawl), so the handbook's task-level attribution simply is not there. The Members page lists only advisors (all students or former team members) with no task breakdown. DNA synthesis is declared as outsourced to CoWin Biotech and Guangzhou RiboBio, which is normal and fine, but nothing states who ran the GC-MS, the plate-reader assays or the MD simulations, and the project leans on substantial compute. Figure captions and the notebook-style detail suggest students did the bench work, but with no attributions page I cannot verify it, so I cannot score above the middle here.
justification.a7: This is squarely synthetic biology with standard components: 30 BBa parts registered (Parts), including de novo coding parts, four CGTase variants, and composites for the butyryl-CoA, borneol and esterification modules, assembled by Golden Gate into pSEVA331, pET-28a(+) and the pW1 (ptac-RiboJ-BsaI) vector, with a RiboJ insulator used for expression consistency. Prior iGEM material is reused and credited (GreatBay-China 2018 pMVA, the GreatBay-SCIE 2025 geraniol strain), exactly the new-plus-reuse pattern the TAS anchor describes. Modularity is real (two-strain co-culture, dual-plasmid surrogate).
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is thorough and the Parts page lists all 30 BBa numbers with types and rationale. But the handbook judges parts on the Registry entry alone, and I could not reach parts.igem.org at all (403 / CAPTCHA challenge, which I will not attempt to solve), so the Registry side is unverified from here. What I can see is a warning sign: the wiki part descriptions are identical boilerplate repeated verbatim across all nine precursor binders and all five transporter binders, with no per-part sequence features, host, or characterisation data, and the experimental evidence lives only on the Engineering/Measurement pages. The empty Notebook page and the 404 on /results, /experiments and /proof-of-concept also push this down.
justification.w1: The project is explained very well once you reach Description - abstract, pathway figure, limitations of current products, three routes with a schematic each. The landing page, though, is only a teaser ("Have you experienced that embarrassing moment...") with no statement of problem, approach or result, so a judge arriving at the homepage learns nothing about what was built or found within one screen. Clear, but with real drift at the entry point.
justification.w2: Most key claims carry a figure with a named control, a legend defining n and the error bars, and the statistical test used - for example the Ellman's panels on Measurement (Fig. 2a-d) and the SDS-PAGE/assay pairs throughout Engineering, with the surrogate's empty-vector control and the CGTase PBS control both stated. Short of 5 because replicates are technical only (Measurement's own Future Improvements section says biological replicates are needed), no raw data or gel ladder sizes are given in the text, and the central readout is acknowledged not to detect 3M3SH specifically.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and purposeful: Wet Lab / Dry Lab / Human Practice groupings, per-section document sidebars (Engineering splits into Surrogate Construction, Precursor Binder, CGTase, Transporter Binder, Terpenoid Ester, Conclusion), an on-this-page rail, and a search box. Standard URLs are preserved and the non-standard pages (/members, /engineering/cgtase) are reachable from the nav. Minor friction: team content sits at /members while /team 404s, and /results, /experiments and /proof-of-concept are absent, so a judge looking for "Results" must infer it lives under Engineering and Measurement.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this: the Protocols page is dense with step-by-step tables, Measurement gives the full Ellman's protocol with the GSH standard curve and dilution table, every construct and vector is named, and the failures are written down (failed transformation, the T370L mix-up, undelivered plasmids). Two gaps keep it below 4: the Notebook page is completely empty, so there is no dated record of what was done when, and no raw data files or attributions are provided.
justification.w5: Referencing is a strength. Numbered inline citations with DOIs run through Description (19 refs), Engineering, Model, Measurement, Safety and Hardware, figures cite their sources, and prior iGEM work is explicitly credited (GreatBay-SCIE 2025 for the geraniol strain and the enzyme idea, GreatBay-China 2018 for pMVA). I could not resolve one very recent reference (Yang et al., Nat Commun 2026) from this environment, which is a limitation of my check rather than an observed defect.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete high-school project: three distinct AI-designed interventions on one odour pathway, all built and tested against controls in a surrogate the team made themselves, held back by an empty Attributions page, an empty Notebook, and an indirect readout run only in technical replicates.
strengths: The team built their own test platform before testing anything: PepTSh expressed in E. coli, verified by colony PCR and sequencing, then validated functionally by a precursor dose-response in thiol output against an empty-vector control (Engineering/Surrogate Construction, Fig. 3b). That is the right order of work and it is what makes the three downstream assays interpretable.

Controls, statistics and units are stated nearly everywhere: PBS or empty-vector controls, ±SD with n given, Welch t-tests for the precursor binders and one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's for the transporter binders and CGTase (Measurement Fig. 2; Engineering Figs. 5b, 9b, 13b).

Honest reporting of failure: BC9 would not transform, T370R gave too little protein to test, the intended T370K turned out to be T370L and the team says the rational-design conclusion is therefore inconclusive, and wild-type CGTase outperformed the engineered variants (Engineering/CGTase Cycle 1, Learn).

Human Practices genuinely changed the science and the framing - DsbA periplasmic fusion after the SynBio expert, a whole thermostability cycle after KleanK's storage concern, fragrance choice from the team's own survey, and the slogan rewritten to "on Your Terms" after social-science input (HP Stage 3 and Stage 5).

The fragrance module is independently verified rather than asserted: GC-MS spectra matched to library references plus GC quantification against standard curves (1.23 µg/mL bornyl acetate, 2.01 µg/mL geranyl butyrate), with the low yield acknowledged as needing optimisation.
Safety work goes beyond a checklist: NetMHCIIpan-4.3 HLA-II presentation and AllergenOnline screens of all 14 protein candidates, tabulated per candidate, with BC11 flagged for follow-up (Safety).
weaknesses: The Attributions page is empty - heading only, confirmed on the live wiki - so there is no task-level record of who did what, and no statement of who ran the GC-MS, the plate-reader assays or the MD simulations. The handbook puts this on the team page and it is the single biggest avoidable loss on this ballot.
The Notebook page is also empty, so there is no dated experimental record to accompany the otherwise good Protocols page.

The central readout, Ellman's assay, measures total free thiol rather than 3M3SH, and the team runs technical replicates only; Measurement's own Future Improvements section notes batch-to-batch variation and the need for biological replicates. The precursor-binder effects (~8-11% reduction) are small relative to that caveat.

No direct evidence of the proposed mechanisms: no binding measurement (ITC, SPR, thermal shift) for any binder, and no mass-spec confirmation that CGTase actually glycosylated the precursor - the inference rests entirely on reduced downstream thiol.
CGTase thermostability is assessed only by visible precipitate after heating, with no post-heat activity assay, so the SPURS redesign is supported qualitatively at best.

Part descriptions are identical boilerplate repeated across all nine precursor binders and all five transporter binders, with no per-part characterisation; combined with the Registry being unreachable from here, documentation of the parts themselves is the weakest part of an otherwise strong wiki.
The homepage carries no project summary, and /results, /experiments and /proof-of-concept return 404, so the evidence must be found under Engineering and Measurement.
red_flags: Attributions page renders empty (verified live at https://2026.igem.wiki/greatbay-scie/attributions) - task ownership cannot be verified; lowers a6 under p.25-26. Not an integrity concern, a documentation gap.
Notebook page renders empty - no dated lab record.

Registry entries could not be inspected: parts.igem.org returned 403 / an AWS CAPTCHA challenge, which I did not attempt to solve. a8 is therefore scored on the wiki's part tables alone, and the Registry side is explicitly unverified rather than judged absent.

Precursor Binder Cycle 2 (LASErMPNN affinity designs) has Design and Build but no Test - plasmids had not arrived. Correctly labelled as future work by the team; no credit given as a result, no concern raised.
Thermostability claim rests on qualitative visible precipitation only; the team labels it as initial support and calls for quantitative assays. Scored as qualitative.

One reference (Yang et al., Nat Commun 2026;17:4851) could not be resolved from this environment. This is a limitation of my offline check, not an allegation - no integrity concern is raised and nothing here warrants an RCC contact.

calibrated.changed: a5 4.5 -> 5.0 and a6 3.0 -> 2.5. a5: my own justification says the HP reaches the GreatBay_SZ anchor - 46 interactions, design changes (periplasmic expression, thermostability cycle), and messaging changed after sociologist and psychiatrist pushback. I awarded 5.0 to HK Joint School and PLKLFC for less breadth with the same depth of consequence, so withholding it for some later-stage outreach was a harsher bar than I used elsewhere. a6: empty Attributions page, a Members page listing only advisors, no task-level statement anywhere, and an empty Notebook page - this is the 2.5 picture, not the 3.0 one.

justification.a1: Three mechanistically distinct interventions on one pathway (de novo precursor binders, de novo conformation-selective transporter binders, engineered CGTase), all built on a purpose-made PepTSh-expressing E. coli surrogate, plus two fragrance esters produced in two-strain co-cultures and quantified by GC/GC-MS (engineering/terpenoid-ester), 30 Registry parts, and a de novo design GUI (software). That is the GreatBay-2019-style chain of increasingly hard steps. It falls short of a 5 only because the measured effects are small (TB2 26.70%; binders ~8%), the three routes were never combined or tested together, and nothing was tested in S. hominis or in a formulation.
justification.a2: Measured, not claimed: the surrogate shows a precursor-concentration-dependent thiol rise versus an empty-vector control (engineering/surrogate-construction Fig. 3b, n=3, ±SD); four of nine precursor binders give significant reductions by Welch's t-test (Fig. 5b); four of five transporter binders are significant by one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's (Fig. 13b, TB2 0.2614±0.0127 vs 0.3566±0.0131 mM); CGTase groups are >50% below control (Fig. 9b); esters are confirmed by matching mass spectra and quantified against standard curves (1.2269 and 2.0116 ug/mL). Held below 4.5 because Ellman's assay measures total free thiol, not 3M3SH specifically (the team says so on measurement), replicates are technical and the team admits batch-to-batch variation, no PepTSh band appeared on SDS-PAGE, and the claimed binding/glycosylation mechanisms were never directly confirmed.
justification.a3: The deployment route is worked out seriously for a high school team: five delivery formats compared against protein-stability and accessibility constraints with named industry input (KleanK, Amcor, formulation and packaging experts), a PP roll-on with high-barrier and low-adsorption coatings, braille and grip features, and a pilot-scale cost of about 1.18 RMB per 50 mL bottle (hardware). But nothing has been tested in a realistic setting: no protein stability in the actual container, no skin or fabric test, no S. hominis, and the hardware page itself says validation is ongoing. That is stakeholder-checked planning, which is a 3.5, not TAS Taipei's tested wastewater rig.
justification.a4: Real cycles, and test data changed the next build: the KleanK warehouse-temperature comment drove a SPURS-guided thermostability redesign that was built and tested (WR2/WR4/WR8 showed little heat-induced precipitate where WT, T370L and T370R/F183W precipitated, engineering/cgtase Fig. 11); cycle-1 binder hits drove LASErMPNN affinity redesign with per-mutation delta-NLL and RMSD (Table 1). Failures are reported openly: BC9 transformation failed, faint purification bands excluded candidates, and the intended T370K was found to be T370L, which the team says leaves the rational-design conclusion inconclusive. Below 4.5 because no quantified success criterion was stated up front, the precursor-binder cycle 2 was never built, and the thermostability test is qualitative precipitation with no post-heat activity measurement.
justification.a5: 46 stakeholder interactions over five stages and 23 ODOR cycles, with design changes traceable to specific people: the immunologist's advice produced the in-silico HLA-II and AllergenOnline screen of all 14 candidates (safety-and-security Table 1, BC11 flagged at 36.29% identity); formulation and packaging experts moved the format from stick and freeze-dried to a coated roll-on; sociologist, psychiatrist and anthropologist work changed the slogan to 'Expel the Odor, on Your Terms' and produced a stigma seminar and bilingual handbook. This is reflective, responsible and responsive in the handbook's sense rather than outreach relabelled as HP.
justification.a6: The Attributions page is empty: rendering https://2026.igem.wiki/greatbay-scie/attributions live returns only the heading, with no who-did-what table and no statement of outside help, so the required record is absent. Credit does exist elsewhere - Registry entries name individual designers with CRediT roles (BBa_26DV4FUW lists five students across conceptualisation, investigation, validation and writing) and the members page lists the team - but the wiki also shows nine returning alumni advisors, commercial DNA synthesis by CoWin Biotech and Guangzhou RiboBio, and regulatory parts 'provided by Link Spider', none of which is reconciled anywhere. I am not alleging anything; I simply cannot verify the division of labour from the page the handbook points to, and that caps this aspect.
justification.a7: Thirty new parts are registered and listed with descriptions on the parts page, including composites (BBa_26G9CJVF, BBa_269IWP38, BBa_26HC9XRI, BBa_266MBZD7), and the Registry entry I checked offers RFC 10 and RFC 1000 export with host, topology and length. The work is genuinely modular: standard vectors (pSEVA331 with AraC-PBAD and a RiboJ insulator, pET-28a(+), pW1 with Ptac-RiboJ), reuse of GreatBay-China 2018's pMVA and GreatBay-SCIE 2025's geraniol strain, a DsbA signal peptide for periplasmic targeting, and FoundryUI as reusable design software.
justification.a8: Registry pages carry Design plus Construction and Protein Expression, Soluble Expression and Functional Value Characterisation entries, which is well past a stub, and the wiki supports them with a protocols page of 59 tables and a measurement page giving the GSH standard curve and the full Ellman's procedure so another team could repeat it. Short of 4.5 because the Notebook page is completely empty and the Attributions page is empty, so the project's timeline and division of work are undocumented.
justification.w1: The description page states the aim, the chassis, the three routes and the fragrance module clearly, with Figs. 2-7 giving one schematic per idea, and the parts page abstract restates it in one paragraph. The home page, however, is essentially a teaser (131 words of 'that embarrassing moment') with no concept summary, so a visitor must click through to learn what the project is.
justification.w2: Claims are tied to numbered figures with error bars, n, named statistical tests and significance levels across the five engineering subpages, and the measurement page collects the four assay panels in one place with the standard curve. Marked down from 5 because the evidence is technical replicates only (acknowledged under 'Future Improvements'), the key readout is an indirect thiol proxy, and raw notebook records are absent.
justification.w3: Navigation is good: grouped top menus, per-section document sidebars, on-page contents and a search box, with Engineering, Model, HP and Software each split into readable subpages. Against that, several standard URLs 404 (results, proof-of-concept, implementation, team), notebook and attributions render empty, and education and inclusivity run to roughly 16,000 words each, which is sprawl rather than completeness.
justification.w4: A future team could pick this up: protocols, a reusable Ellman's measurement method explicitly offered to other teams, a contribution page covering measurement, parts, model, software and wiki accessibility, 30 documented Registry parts, and FoundryUI with installation and example workflows. The empty notebook is the main gap, since the chronological record of what was tried and when is missing.
justification.w5: Every substantive page carries numbered references with DOIs, and claims such as the ABCC11 genotype link, the PepTSh transport mechanism and the CGTase thermostability figure are each cited to a specific source. In-text citation is consistent rather than decorative; I did not verify every DOI, and a handful of figures are team-made schematics without separate credit lines.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineered three-route project with measured, controlled, statistically tested results and outstanding Registry documentation, let down by an empty attributions page and small, indirect effect sizes.
strengths: Purpose-built PepTSh-expressing E. coli surrogate validated with a dose-response curve against an empty-vector control (engineering/surrogate-construction Fig. 3b) before being used to test all three routes
Functional data with controls, n=3 and named statistical tests for all three protein routes, including TB2 at a 26.70% thiol reduction (engineering/transporter-binder Fig. 13b)
Stakeholder feedback that visibly changed the build: KleanK's storage-temperature concern produced the SPURS thermostability redesign tested by heat precipitation (engineering/cgtase Fig. 11)
Thirty Registry parts with design, construction, soluble expression and functional characterisation entries, per-person CRediT roles and RFC 10/RFC 1000 export
Honest reporting of failures: failed BC9 transformation, faint purification bands, and the T370K variant that turned out to be T370L, which the team says leaves its design conclusion inconclusive
An in-silico HLA-II and allergen screen of all 14 candidates prompted by an immunologist, with BC11 flagged rather than buried (safety-and-security Table 1)
weaknesses: The Attributions page renders empty on the live wiki, so the required who-did-what record is missing despite nine returning advisors and commercial synthesis of every construct
The Notebook page is empty, leaving no chronological experimental record
Ellman's assay measures total free thiol, not 3M3SH, so every functional claim rests on an indirect proxy
Only technical replicates; the team itself notes batch-to-batch variation and the need for biological replicates
No PepTSh band at the expected 55.4 kDa on SDS-PAGE, so surrogate expression is inferred from activity alone

The three routes were never combined, never tested in S. hominis, and never tested in the proposed formulation or on skin; the hardware work is design and costing, with no bench measurement of a built prototype
red_flags: Attributions page present in navigation but empty of content (verified by rendering the live page), so student versus advisor and outsourced execution cannot be assessed - a question for Q&A, not an accusation
Regulatory parts 'provided by Link Spider' and all constructs synthesised by CoWin Biotech or Guangzhou RiboBio; declared in the text but not reconciled on any attribution page
Notebook page empty, so the wet-lab timeline cannot be checked against the volume of work claimed

calibrated.changed: none — a6 2.5 for an empty page partly offset by per-part CRediT roles on the Registry is correctly above the bios-only teams (2.0) and below the per-task-record teams (3.0). a8 4.0 stands because I actually read Registry entries here with Design plus three characterisation sections.

justification.a1: The scope climbs logically: a PepTSh-expressing E. coli surrogate is built and validated first (engineering/surrogate-construction), then three mechanistically distinct interventions are designed and tested on it, then two are optimised in a second cycle, and in parallel two fragrance esters are produced and confirmed by GC-MS (engineering/terpenoid-ester), with a design GUI (software) and packaging work (hardware) on top. This is GreatBay-2019-like breadth within one season. It falls just short of a 5 because the measured effects are small and semi-quantitative (an ~8% thiol drop for the best precursor binder, 26.7% for TB2) and the second-cycle precursor binders were never tested.
justification.a2: The core claims are measured, not asserted: the surrogate shows a precursor-concentration-dependent thiol rise against an empty-vector control (Fig. 3b, engineering/surrogate-construction, n=3 with SD); 4 of 9 precursor binders, 4 of 5 transporter binders and all tested CGTases give statistically significant reductions against their own controls with named tests (Welch's t-test; one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's) in Figs. 5b, 13b and 9b; bornyl acetate (1.2269 ug/mL) and geranyl butyrate (2.0116 ug/mL) are quantified against standard curves with matching mass spectra. Against this, no PepTSh band appeared on SDS-PAGE, Ellman's assay measures total thiol rather than 3M3SH specifically, and the Measurement page states only technical replicates were run, so each effect size is not yet secure.
justification.a3: The need is evidenced rather than assumed: a 486-respondent local survey plus interviews with a dermatologist, axillary surgeon, former surgical patient, gym and hotel owners (human-practices stages 1-2), and the Description page documents concrete harms of existing options. A Chinese deodorant brand, KleanK, approached the team unprompted and offered later consumer testing (human-practices stage 3 cycle 2), and the Hardware page carries formulation, packaging-material and cost estimates. It is not a 5 because nothing has yet been tested on skin, in S. hominis, or in any setting closer to the axilla than an E. coli suspension.
justification.a4: Several loops are genuine rather than decorative. The transporter-binder assay failed on E. coli outer-membrane permeability, an expert suggested DsbA-directed periplasmic export, and the plasmids were rebuilt accordingly and then worked (engineering/transporter-binder; human-practices stage 3 cycle 3). A warehouse-temperature concern from KleanK triggered a whole second CGTase cycle on thermostability, with WR2/WR4/WR8 showing reduced heat precipitation. Honesty is a strength: the intended T370K came back as T370L, wild-type CGTase outperformed its own variants, and the team says plainly that the rational-design strategy is therefore inconclusive. The Model page plots its own computational metrics against its own A412 results and reports where MD metrics disagreed.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the project and reaches the GreatBay-SCIE 2025 standard in the handbook. Changes are traceable to named people: modelling expert Mr. Li redirected the first target from the membrane transporter to the small-molecule precursor; Professor Meng produced both the periplasmic-expression fix and the terpenoid-ester route; KleanK produced the freeze-dried format and the thermostability work; an immunologist produced the NetMHCIIpan/AllergenOnline screen reported on the Safety page. The team also re-examined its own framing, changing the slogan to 'Expel the Odor, on Your Terms' after sociologists and a psychiatrist raised stigma, and the Safety page documents interview consent, wiki-publication permission, survey confidentiality and face-blurring for under-18s.
justification.a6: This is the one serious gap. The Attributions page is blank: rendering https://2026.igem.wiki/greatbay-scie/attributions in headless Chrome returns navigation and footer only. The Notebook page is likewise empty. The Members page lists 29 student names only behind a whack-a-mole reveal game, with no roles, while nine advisors have full biographies, and the Safety page says 'our PIs and advisors provided continuous supervision'. Outside help is named honestly where it occurs (Link Spider, CoWin Biotech, Guangzhou RiboBio, GreatBay-China 2018's pMVA, GreatBay-SCIE 2025's geraniol strain), so I see no sign of misrepresentation, but a judge cannot tell which students did the cloning, the assays or the modelling, so this stays at or below 3 until the session clarifies it.
justification.a7: The work is squarely synthetic biology built on standard components: Golden Gate assembly into pSEVA331 and pET-28a(+), a shared pW1 (Ptac-RiboJ) backbone standardising the 5' UTR, AraC-PBAD with a RiboJ insulator for expression consistency, and reuse of two previous iGEM constructs. Thirty parts are listed on the Parts page, including five composites, and the novel contributions (nine de novo precursor binders, five transporter binders, four CGTase variants) were built and functionally tested, not merely designed. The FoundryUI node-based design tool is a further standard component contributed to the community.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is good: every part is tabled with number, type and a mechanistic description (parts), protocols are given in 59 tables, the Measurement page gives the full Ellman's protocol with a GSH standard curve, and the Safety page tabulates per-candidate allergenicity and HLA-II screening. Two things hold this down. I could not reach parts.igem.org from this environment (403), so I cannot confirm that sequence features, characterisation and experiments were deposited on the Registry rather than only on the wiki. And the per-part descriptions are identical boilerplate within each group - all nine precursor binders carry word-for-word the same text - while the blank Notebook page means no raw bench record supports them.
justification.w1: The Description page is excellent: abstract, inspiration, the full odour pathway, a fair review of why existing products fail, and a clear statement of the three routes with schematics. But the home page itself carries only an atmospheric teaser ('Have you experienced that embarrassing moment...') and about 130 words, with no statement of problem, approach and goal and no entry schematic, so a judge has to click into Description before the project is clear. That is the main distance from the Lambert_GA and Patras standard.
justification.w2: Results are tied to figures throughout, with controls named in the captions, error bars defined as SD with n=3, and the statistical test stated (Welch's t-test, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett's). Crucially, modelled and measured work are kept apart: the Model page labels the precursor-binder affinity results as not yet available, the Engineering page says the cycle-2 plasmids did not arrive in time, and the Measurement page flags the absence of biological replicates. The deductions are the indirect readout (total thiol as a proxy for 3M3SH) and the small, technical-replicate-only datasets behind the significance marks.
justification.w3: Navigation is competent - nested Engineering, Model, HP and Software sections, per-page contents, a search box - but content is not where the handbook says judges should find it. results, proof-of-concept, implementation and team all 404, with the material relocated; Notebook and Attributions are published but empty; and 29 member names are reachable only by playing a whack-a-mole game, which is a real accessibility problem on a wiki that otherwise argues for inclusive design. Education (about 16,200 words) and Inclusivity (about 16,700 words) dwarf the evidence pages, so the wiki is complete but it sprawls.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of the wet lab: the Protocols page gives 59 tabulated procedures from competent-cell preparation to the thermostability assay, Measurement gives the assay end to end with its standard curve, Parts lists every construct, Software documents installation and node development, and Safety records the lab zoning. What is missing is the day-to-day record and the data behind the figures - the Notebook page is empty, no raw absorbance or GC files are provided, and with Attributions blank there is no record of who ran what.
justification.w5: Citation practice is consistently good: numbered reference lists with DOIs on Description, Engineering, Model, Measurement and Safety; prior iGEM work credited by name (GreatBay-China 2018's pMVA, GreatBay-SCIE 2025's geraniol strain and the enzyme idea); design tools, databases and the Yang et al. monoterpene-ester paper cited where used; and Peter Carr quoted with attribution on the HP page. The reservations are minor: figures and schematics carry no explicit credit line, and I could not verify from plain text that every linked DOI resolves.

J3.one_line: An unusually complete high school project: three AI-designed interventions all tested against controls on the team's own E. coli surrogate, outstanding integrated human practices that visibly redirected the science, but a blank Attributions page and empty Notebook leave who-did-what undocumented.
strengths: Built its own validated test platform first: PepTSh expressed in E. coli gives a precursor-dependent thiol signal against an empty-vector control (engineering/surrogate-construction, Fig. 3b), so every later claim is measured on a system the team characterised itself.
Three mechanistically distinct routes all reach statistically tested wet-lab data with controls (Figs. 5b, 9b, 13b), rather than stopping at cloning or at modelled predictions.

Human practices genuinely changed the design: the first binder target was switched on expert advice, the transporter-binder assay was rebuilt with a DsbA periplasmic signal, thermostability engineering was added after an industry meeting, and the fragrance route came from the same conversation (human-practices stage 3).

Honest reporting of what went wrong: T370K was obtained as T370L, wild-type CGTase beat its own variants, no PepTSh band appeared on SDS-PAGE, plasmids arrived too late to test, and the Measurement page admits only technical replicates were run.

The Model page tests its own computational metrics against its own experimental results and reports the disagreements, including where MD metrics failed for the Proteina-Complexa route - rare self-criticism at this level.
Participant ethics are documented: interview consent, permission to publish on the wiki, survey confidentiality and face-blurring for under-18s (safety-and-security).
weaknesses: The Attributions page is empty (verified by rendering the live page), and the Notebook page is empty too, so there is no record of which student did which experiment or analysis, against nine named advisors and stated PI supervision.

Effect sizes are small and indirect: the best precursor binder reduces thiol by roughly 8% and TB2 by 26.7%, measured by an assay that detects total free thiol rather than 3M3SH specifically, with n=3 technical replicates only.
Second-cycle precursor binders (BC7/BR8/BR10 mutants) were designed and ordered but never tested, so the LASErMPNN affinity work is a plan, not a result.
Several standard page URLs return 404 (results, proof-of-concept, implementation, team) with content relocated, which makes a judge hunt for material.
Very long on Education (about 16,200 words) and Inclusivity (about 16,700 words) relative to the evidence-bearing pages; the home page carries only a teaser with no problem-approach-goal statement.
red_flags: Attributions standard page is published but contains no content at all (live page rendered 2026-10-23); Notebook page likewise empty. An attribution-documentation gap to raise as a question at the session, not an accusation.
Member names are hidden behind an interactive whack-a-mole game with no roles listed, while advisors get full biographies - an accessibility and attribution problem rather than an integrity one.

Registry part pages could not be verified from this environment (parts.igem.org returned 403), so whether the 30 claimed BBa entries carry sequence features and characterisation data is unconfirmed; wiki part descriptions are identical boilerplate within each group.
Measurement page states results rest on technical replicates only, with biological replicates listed as future work - the significance asterisks should be read with that in mind.

calibrated.changed: none. The a5 of 5 survives the consent cross-check that cost HK Joint School half a point: the Safety page documents interview consent, wiki-publication permission, survey confidentiality and face-blurring for under-18s, so this and LaBi are the only two 5s left on a5, which matches my rarity self-check.

one_line.en: Three AI-designed interventions on one pathway, all built and tested against controls on a surrogate the team made itself, held back by an empty Attributions page, an empty Notebook and small indirect effects.
one_line.zh: 針對同一途徑的三種 AI 設計介入，全部建成並在自建替代系統上對照測試，但歸屬頁與實驗紀錄頁皆空白，效應量小且屬間接測量。

strengths: The team built and validated its own test platform first with a dose-response against an empty-vector control, which makes the three downstream assays interpretable
Controls, statistics and units stated nearly everywhere, with named tests for each route
Honest reporting of failure, including a variant that turned out to be a different substitution and a wild-type enzyme outperforming the engineered ones
Safety work beyond a checklist, with computational immunogenicity and allergen screens of all candidates and one flagged for follow-up
weaknesses: The Attributions page renders empty, so there is no record of who ran the instruments or the simulations
The Notebook page is also empty, leaving no dated experimental record
The central readout measures total free thiol rather than the target molecule, with technical replicates only and small effect sizes
No direct evidence of the proposed mechanisms — no binding measurement and no mass-spec confirmation of the enzymatic step
red_flags: Attributions page published but empty, verified live
Notebook page empty
Regulatory parts supplied by an outside company and all constructs commercially synthesised, declared in text but not reconciled on any attribution page
Part descriptions are identical boilerplate repeated across each group

screen.project_title: ReefBond: a mussel-adhesion plus mineralisation fusion protein for coral fragment attachment
screen.what_they_built: Eight SUMO-Mfp3-acidic peptide fusion proteins expressed in E. coli, screened down to SUMO-Mfp3-v12-Asp8, tested for glass retention after agitation and for cell-free mineral deposition, plus two iterations of an underwater material-testing rig with wave settings and environmental logging.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5-alpha and BL21(DE3) on pET21a(+) with SUMO tag, (GGGS)3 linker and His6. 28 part entries (12 basic, 16 composite) including BBa_26KZTJZC, the T7-SUMO-Mfp3-v12-Asp8 cassette named as best new composite part.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering and /parts: Ni-NTA purification gels showing the low-molecular-weight target enriched in 100% Buffer B for both Mfp3 variants; Coomassie-stained glass and tin foil retaining more protein after tyrosinase treatment following 10 min agitation at 25 C and 60 rpm; and a cell-free deposition assay where the protein-treated group gave a visible pale deposit with SEM showing micrometre-scale plate-like aggregates. All qualitative or image-based, with no quantified adhesion force, deposit mass or mineral identification.
screen.hp_integration: Present but not decisive from the screening pack: stakeholder work informed the evaluation framing and the need for an underwater test rig, but no construct change is traced to a stakeholder.
screen.reason: Well-organised six-cycle engineering story, a genuine 8-member fusion library, 28 documented parts and an iterated hardware platform, and the team is careful not to overclaim. But the biology stops at qualitative staining and SEM images: no adhesion strength, no mineral phase identification, no coral or even aquarium result, and the team itself says the rig's accuracy and repeatability are unvalidated. Good medal team, not finalist evidence.
screen.field_notes: GYHS (Conservation, China) built ReefBond, a bifunctional protein for attaching transplanted coral fragments that fuses a mussel foot protein-3 adhesion module to an acidic mineralisation peptide. Six DBTL cycles ran two parallel strands. On the biology side, Mfp3-v12 and Mfp3-v15 were expressed in E. coli BL21(DE3) from pET21a(+), fractionated (most protein in the pellet) and purified by Ni-NTA with the target enriched in 100% Buffer B; tyrosinase treatment visibly improved retention on glass and tin foil after 10 min agitation at 60 rpm, with NBT staining for DOPA-related reactivity. Eight fusions pairing the two Mfp3 variants with Asp8, a CARP3-derived peptide, (DE)6 and (DDE)4 were screened on expression and recovery, selecting SUMO-Mfp3-v12-Asp8 (BBa_26KZTJZC, 531 bp, 176 aa), which retained glass staining after washing and, in a cell-free assay, produced a pale deposit whose SEM showed micrometre plate-like and elongated structures. No adhesion force, deposit mass or mineral phase was measured and no coral was tested. On the hardware side, V1 established underwater bonding and handheld pull testing with commercial 502 adhesive, and V2 added removable mounts, rail-guided motorised loading, five wave-pump settings, six-channel environmental monitoring, scheduled photography, time-lapse and CSV export through a ReefBond monitor application; the team states calibration and repeatability remain unvalidated. 28 part entries (12 basic including four reused Registry elements, 16 composite) are documented. The wiki has no results, experiments, notebook, model, measurement or attributions page, with the data presented inside Engineering and Parts.

screen.project_title: V.A.U.L.T.: engineered major vault protein nanoparticles for mRNA stabilisation and targeted delivery
screen.what_they_built: A proposed modular vault carrier - MVP scaffold with an N-terminal adenoviral pVI endosomal-escape peptide and a C-terminal Z domain for antibody targeting, plus a PABPC1-INT adaptor to hold poly(A) mRNA - intended to let mRNA be stored at -18 C. Lab work reached Golden Gate assembly and transformation; nothing was sequenced.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli, pOdd2 backbone with T7/lacO promoter, BBa_B0034_m1 RBS and BBa_B0015 terminator. No new Registry identifiers: the Part Collection page states that verified identifiers, final construct records and characterisation data are not yet present and declines to call it a validated collection.
screen.best_evidence: /results: colony counts from nine transformations on 29 September, reported with full controls. Six of seven Golden Gate reactions gave white colonies; the His-PABPC1-UbC11-INT reaction gave 1 white against roughly 1200-1500 red. The Golden Gate negative control, which should have been empty, grew about 115 red colonies, which the team reports as uncut backbone and an open question. Sequencing had not returned, so no construct is confirmed.
screen.hp_integration: Yes at the concept level - Dr. Eva Bertosin's account of DNA origami's limits moved them off origami onto MVP, the Leiden and TU Delft teams pushed them from a single insulin application to a general mRNA platform, and Prof. Masanori Osawa supplied the PABPC1-UbC11-INT vs INT-UbK0-PABPC1 cleavage designs that solved their release problem.
screen.reason: Five days of lab access at TU Delft produced colony counts and no confirmed construct; the assembly negative control failed. Nothing about storage, loading, release, targeting or translation was tested, and the team says so throughout. The intellectual honesty, the annotated references page and the engineering page's insistence that uptake, escape and translation be judged separately are genuinely above average for a first-year school team, but there is no experimental result for aspects 2, 4 or 8 to rest on. A visible 'TODO(team)' placeholder remains on the Description page and the Attributions page is 5 words.
screen.field_notes: Gymnasium Leiden (Therapeutics, NLD), the first Dutch high school iGEM team, proposed V.A.U.L.T.: major vault protein nanoparticles carrying mRNA, with an adenoviral pVI peptide for endosomal escape, a Z domain for antibody-mediated targeting, and a PABPC1-INT adaptor binding the poly(A) tail to vPARP's INT site, aiming at -18 C storage instead of -80 C. The team states clearly that the -18 C figure is a hypothesis, not a measured shelf life. With five days of borrowed bench time at TU Delft they ran seven Golden Gate reactions plus two controls into pOdd2 (T7/lacO, BBa_B0034_m1, BBa_B0015) and reported every colony count: six of seven reactions gave white colonies, the His-PABPC1-UbC11-INT reaction gave one white against 1200-1500 red, the water control was clean and the backbone positive control behaved, but the Golden Gate negative control grew roughly 115 red colonies, which they read as uncut backbone carried through. Sequencing had not returned, so no construct is confirmed and no part has a Registry identifier. Cycles 2 and 3 of the engineering page are marked 'not written up yet'. The design page is unusually disciplined about what the literature does and does not support, including the caution that DEC-205 targeting in the steady state produced tolerance rather than immunity, and the references page annotates each of 36 sources with its limits. The journey, collaboration and sponsors pages document how a school team built funding and lab access from nothing, which is the project's real contribution.

screen.project_title: DCO (Dental Calculus Obstructor) — a four-enzyme anti-biofilm toothpaste with recombinant glucanases and a hydroxyapatite-binding AMP
screen.what_they_built: Recombinant production of two complementary glucanases (PmGH87 α-1,3, CoGH66 α-1,6) plus a hydroxyapatite-binding antimicrobial peptide, combined with commercial papain and DNase I into a cocktail tested on an artificial dental calculus model and formulated into a staged-release toothpaste.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5α / Rosetta(DE3), pET-32a with TrxA–6xHis–enterokinase. Six Registry parts: PmGH87 (BBa_2638U4UV), CoGH66 (BBa_265V2WY8), CoGH66 Q172P (BBa_260WPOJS), CoGH66 Y166Q (BBa_2654ZBYJ), G12R 18aa AMP (BBa_26082O0Q), SHABP 21aa AMP (BBa_26ZTHMQV).
screen.best_evidence: /wet-lab/results: both glucanases expressed solubly, purified to tag-free protein (59.46 and 99.16 kDa) and shown substrate-specific by DNS assay against PBS, heat-inactivated and wrong-substrate controls, mean ± SD from three independent replicates, on α-1,3-glucan the team extracted themselves from shiitake. /engineering Test 3: on the BF+MU artificial calculus model, crystal violet biomass after the complete four-enzyme cocktail was significantly lower than the no-enzyme control (p < 0.05), while the gravimetric assay showed nothing (p > 0.05) and is reported as a failure.
screen.hp_integration: Repeatedly. Clinical experts redirected the target from already-mineralised calculus to early biofilm; expert advice on protease/DNase expression difficulty and commercial availability narrowed the synbio effort to glucanases only; oral-microbiology input added the hydroxyapatite-binding AMP arm because enzymatic removal alone does not stop recolonisation; an iGEM committee ruling on the white list forced the α-1,3-glucan substrate to come from shiitake instead of Aspergillus niger.
screen.reason: Closest thing in this batch to the GreatBay_SZ pattern: six Registry parts, functioning enzymes shown active with proper negative and heat-inactivated controls and triplicates, a model-to-mutant-to-wet-lab loop where the experiment overturned the computational ranking (Q172P beat the predicted top candidate Y166Q), a purpose-built artificial calculus assay, and failures (18aa peptide not expressed, gravimetric assay null) reported rather than hidden. Deep expert-driven HP that visibly changed scope. Deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: HangzhouFourteenAP (CHN, Biomanufacturing village) built DCO, an enzyme toothpaste aimed at dental plaque maturation rather than mineralised calculus. Four cycles. Cycle 1 narrowed the synthetic-biology effort to two glycoside hydrolases — PmGH87 (mutanase, α-1,3) and CoGH66 (dextranase, α-1,6) — after expert consultation showed proteases are toxic to express in E. coli and DNase I is cheap commercially; papain and bovine DNase I were bought in. Both glucanases were cloned into pET-32a by Gibson assembly, sequence-verified, expressed solubly in Rosetta(DE3) (76.54 and 116.24 kDa tagged), purified on Ni beads with on-bead enterokinase cleavage to 59.46 and 99.16 kDa, and assayed by DNS against substrate they prepared themselves (α-1,3-glucan extracted from shiitake after iGEM told them Aspergillus niger is off the white list): PmGH87 active only on α-1,3, CoGH66 strong on α-1,6 and weak on the shiitake extract, each with PBS and heat-inactivated controls and n = 3. Cycle 2 added a hydroxyapatite-binding AMP arm; of two candidates the 21aa SHABP expressed (~19.55 kDa) and gave a clear inhibition zone, while the 18aa G12R gave no induced band and no zone — reported as a failure. The modeling page runs a real structure-guided pipeline (PDB 8IUB, PyMOL contact residues, MAFFT/ESPript conservation, FoldX ΔΔG_fold and ΔΔG_bind) that ranked Y166Q first and Q172P second; both mutants were built, sequence-verified and DNS-assayed, and the experiment inverted the ranking (net OD540: Q172P 1.881, WT 0.996, Y166Q 0.629), which the team reports and reinterprets. Cycle 3 adapted a published B. subtilis BF+MU artificial calculus model and tested the full cocktail against four single-omission formulations: gravimetry showed nothing (p > 0.05, attributed to balance sensitivity and uneven mineralisation), crystal violet showed the complete cocktail significantly below the no-enzyme control (p < 0.05) with omission groups not separated. Cycle 4 is formulation only (sodium alginate/methylcellulose segregation, three-stage release), with no human testing and no efficacy claim. Twelve named external advisors; extensive entrepreneurship, education, measurement and sustainability pages; AI use disclosed in detail with per-section human reviewers named.

justification.a1: The chain of results builds in difficulty in the way the GreatBay/TAS anchors do: two glucanases cloned, expressed, purified and shown substrate-specific; an AMP screen in which one of two candidates failed; an artificial dental calculus model built and then used for a six-arm single-component-dropout study; and finally two CoGH66 point mutants built and assayed (Engineering cycles 1-4; Measurement). It stops short of a 5 because every efficacy number is in vitro on a Bacillus subtilis surrogate biofilm and the delivery prototype never got past benchtop carrier preparation (Engineering, Test 4).
justification.a2: Function is shown against proper controls with replicates and plotted readouts: the DNS assays carry PBS, heat-inactivated-enzyme and wrong-substrate controls with mean +/- SD of three replicates and a glucose standard curve (y=3.702x+0.3017, R2=0.9606) (wet-lab/results Fig. 3; Engineering Fig. 5), and the AMP agar-diffusion assay shows a zone only for 21aa, with the 18aa failure reported honestly. The Measurement page tabulates every raw replicate for gravimetry, crystal violet (complete cocktail 0.532 +/- 0.049 vs PBS 1.240 +/- 0.107, 57.1% reduction) and acridine orange, runs ANOVA before planned t-tests, and states that n=3 uncorrected comparisons are exploratory. Held back from 5 by crude-lysate assays with volumetric rather than specific activity, the surrogate organism, and a non-significant gravimetric endpoint.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and has been shaped by clinicians, an investor and an oral-care quality director, and the regulatory route is concrete (toothpaste filed under GB22115, chewing gum kept claim-free under GB2760, iHP 7.1-7.3), backed by two user surveys (N=350, N=137). But the impact is still inferred: nothing was tested in a real-world-like setting, the efficacy figures come from a B. subtilis model, and the 95.5% biofilm-degradation number is from the literature, not the team's data (project/description).
justification.a4: Four cycles each turn a test result into a design change rather than mere troubleshooting: failed 18aa expression selected 21aa for the formulation (Test 2); a failed gravimetric endpoint drove the switch to crystal violet and acridine orange (Test 3); and the FoldX prediction that Y166Q was the top candidate was overturned by the DNS assay (net OD540 Q172P 1.881, WT 0.996, Y166Q 0.629), after which the team explicitly revised its ranking and kept Y166Q as a mechanistic probe (Modeling, sections 6-8 and Discussion). Thresholds were stated before testing (FoldX priority cutoff dG_fold < 0 and dG_bind < -1 kcal/mol). The PCR re-optimisation in Build 1 is ordinary troubleshooting, and Cycle 4 has no Test.
justification.a5: Twelve named experts across periodontics, enzymology, structural biology, food regulation, investment and marketing, each tied to a specific decision: dropping recombinant protease/DNase in favour of two recombinant glucanases (iHP 3.2), targeting the pre-mineralisation biofilm rather than hardened calculus after Dr Wang Yongwu's 'egg hitting a stone' comment (2.2), abandoning the chimeric enzyme for single-point mutation on Prof Wang Zhiguo's advice (5.1), and compartmentalised sequential release to stop papain digesting the other components (6.1-6.2). Survey work (N=350 and N=137) is reported with numbers and fed the dosage-form and claims decisions. Just short of 5 because the exchange is mostly experts advising the team rather than a sustained two-way relationship, and several resulting formats (film, mouthwash) were never tested.
justification.a6: The dated notebook (wet-lab/notes, July-August 2026) and the detailed protocol page read like student bench work, and the AI-usage box names section authors, but there is no attributions page at all: https://2026.igem.wiki/hangzhoufourteenap/attributions returns the site's 404. The team page lists roles (Wet Lab Lead, Dry Lab Lead) but never says who ran which experiment, what the mentors and the five listed instructors contributed, or where the lab was; gene synthesis and Sanger sequencing are plainly outsourced but not declared as such. Under p.25-26 that incomplete attribution is what caps this score, not any evidence of outsourced execution.
justification.a7: Six parts are registered (BBa_2638U4UV, BBa_265V2WY8, BBa_260WPOJS, BBa_2654ZBYJ, BBa_26082O0Q, BBa_26ZTHMQV) and the design is a genuine expression device: codon-optimised ORFs in pET-32a under T7/lac with RBS, TrxA and 6xHis tags, enterokinase site and T7 terminator, assembled by Gibson and verified by colony PCR and sequencing (wet-lab/parts). Two of the six are team-made site-directed mutants, so there is new content alongside reuse of a standard backbone. Like TAS Taipei, novelty is modest but the project is clearly built on synthetic biology and standard components.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation itself is strong - figure legends name every lane and control, primers are tabulated, raw replicate values are given - but the handbook judges parts on the Registry, and I could not render any content from the six Registry pages (they load as an empty SPA shell), so I cannot confirm they carry the annotation, rationale and characterisation data the wiki describes. Worse for navigation, the standard URLs /parts, /results, /description, /experiments, /protocols, /notebook and /attributions all return the team's 404 page; the content sits at /wet-lab/parts, /wet-lab/results and /project/description instead (p.29).
justification.w1: The project goal - enzymatically dismantling the organic matrix of dental calculus plus an enamel-anchoring antimicrobial peptide - comes across clearly, and the home page is honest in its framing ('Professional scaling remains essential', 'proposed mechanism'). It is not within one screen, though: the landing sequence opens with a large GBD caseload map and licensing panel and uses letter-spaced animated headings, so the reader reaches 'our biological approach' only at section 04.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is backed by a figure with named controls, and the Measurement page goes further than most teams by printing the per-replicate numbers behind all three endpoints (Tables 2-4) alongside ANOVA F-statistics and a statement that the pairwise tests are uncorrected. Negative results are shown rather than hidden: the failed 18aa expression, the null gravimetric result, and the mutant whose measured activity contradicted the prediction. Short of 5 only because some activity data come from crude lysates and the key efficacy model uses a surrogate organism.
justification.w3: The side nav is grouped sensibly (Project / Wet Lab / Engagement) and each page has a working On This Page index, but the standard iGEM page URLs are broken: /results, /parts, /description, /attributions, /notebook, /protocols and /experiments all render the site's 404 screen, with the real content relocated under /wet-lab/ and /project/. A judge who types a standard URL, as p.29 expects to be able to do, finds nothing. There is also no attributions page to find anywhere.
justification.w4: A future team could largely rebuild this: 21 protocols with volumes, temperatures and cycling conditions (wet-lab/experiments), a dated day-by-day notebook, the full primer table including the mutagenesis primers, raw replicate data, and an explicit limitations list (surrogate organism, single application, no mineral-phase measurement). The Contribution page adds a reusable guide to multi-enzyme encapsulation with the team's own alginate/gelatin/methylcellulose recipes. Missing: raw gel images cannot be checked from text, and no attributions or protocol for the artificial calculus mineral solution composition at the standard URL.
justification.w5: Referencing is unusually careful for a high school wiki: numbered inline citations throughout Description, Engineering, Modeling and Measurement with full journal references, the GBD and WHO map data given with query parameters, licences (IHME non-commercial, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) and a note that WHO did not endorse the adaptation, and a candid AI-usage disclosure naming which figures were AI-generated. Small gaps: no prior iGEM team work is credited anywhere, and the Contribution review cites secondary sources for several performance figures.

J1.one_line: A genuinely well-controlled high school wet-lab project: two glucanases expressed, purified and shown substrate-specific, a six-arm dropout test on a self-built artificial calculus model with raw replicate data, and a modelling prediction honestly overturned by experiment - undercut by a missing attributions page and broken standard URLs.
strengths: Substrate-specificity shown with real controls: PmGH87 active on shiitake alpha-1,3-glucan but not alpha-1,6, with PBS and heat-inactivated controls and n=3 (wet-lab/results Fig. 3D-G)
Measurement page prints every replicate value for three endpoints, runs ANOVA before planned t-tests, and labels n=3 pairwise results as exploratory (Tables 2-4)

A closed engineering loop where the computational prediction was wrong and the team said so: FoldX ranked Y166Q first, DNS measured Q172P highest (net OD540 1.881 vs WT 0.996, Y166Q 0.629), and the ranking was revised (Modeling, Discussion)
Failures reported rather than buried: 18aa peptide not expressed and no inhibition zone; gravimetric endpoint non-significant

Human practices changed the science repeatedly - abandoning recombinant protease/DNase, retargeting from mineralised calculus to the pre-mineralisation biofilm, dropping the chimeric enzyme, and keeping preventive claims off the chewing gum for GB2760 compliance
Safety handled as a design constraint, with White List substitutions (B. subtilis for S. mutans, shiitake for A. niger) declared and their interpretive cost acknowledged
weaknesses: No attributions page anywhere; /attributions 404s and the team page gives only role labels, so no experiment has a named owner and the mentors' and host lab's contribution is undefined
Standard URLs /results, /parts, /description, /experiments, /protocols and /notebook all return the site's 404; content was relocated to /wet-lab/ and /project/ paths (p.29)
The six Registry entries could not be read - the Registry pages render as an empty shell - so part documentation can only be credited from the wiki, which p.18 does not allow
Efficacy rests on a B. subtilis surrogate biofilm, a single enzyme application and no mineral-phase measurement, so 'dental calculus degradation' is a proof of concept only
Enzyme activity reported as volumetric U/mL from crude lysates with no specific activity or purified-enzyme kinetics, which the team acknowledges

The AMP evidence is a single zone-of-inhibition plate against Lactobacillus with no hydroxyapatite-binding measurement, so the central anchoring claim is modelled (AlphaFold ipTM) rather than measured
red_flags: Standard page URLs (results, parts, description, experiments, protocols, notebook, attributions) return 404 on the team namespace - a p.29 problem, not an integrity one
No attributions page at all (p.25-26)
Registry part pages would not render for me, so part documentation is unverified
AlphaFold ipTM scores and FoldX energies are used as screening evidence; the team labels them as predictions, which is the correct handling, but the hydroxyapatite-binding claim rests on them

Team discloses AI-generated imagery for the product-matrix and SDG figures; these are illustrative schematics, not evidentiary data figures, and I saw no sign of AI-made or cleaned gels or plots - noted for transparency, not as a concern to report
pages_read: registry.igem.org part pages BBa_2638U4UV, BBa_265V2WY8, BBa_26ZTHMQV (would not render)

calibrated.changed: none. a2 4.5 is consistent with the other control-rich ballots (Labi, HongKong-JSS): named negative controls, n=3 with SD, ANOVA before planned t-tests, raw replicate tables, and an honestly reported null endpoint.

justification.a1: DCO runs a long chain of increasingly difficult steps, each with data: four pET-32a constructs built and sequence-verified (Results Fig.1), two glucanases expressed, purified and shown substrate-specific (Fig.2-3), an AMP screened and one of two expressed with a visible inhibition zone, a structure-guided mutant pair built and assayed (Modeling Fig.6-8), and a B. subtilis artificial-calculus model with three endpoints and a five-arm omission series (Measurement Tables 2-4), plus benchtop preparation of the three-carrier toothpaste. That is close to GreatBay-level scope for a high school team; it falls short of 5 only because the final efficacy sits in a surrogate model and the delivery system was never release-tested.
justification.a2: The main function is measured, not claimed: DNS assays with PBS, heat-inactivated and wrong-substrate controls show PmGH87 is strictly alpha-1,3 specific and CoGH66 alpha-1,6 preferring (Engineering Fig.5C-F), and the crystal violet assay gives 57.1% biomass reduction versus PBS with ANOVA F(5,12)=29.8, p<0.001 and raw triplicate values (Measurement Table 3). Honest negatives are reported: the gravimetric endpoint was null, the 18aa peptide never expressed, papain omission only reached p=0.08. Held back from higher by the B. subtilis surrogate, crude-lysate rather than purified enzyme in several activity assays, and no mineral-phase (calcium release) measurement.
justification.a3: The need is quantified and local (96.7% calculus detection in adults 35-44, dentist ratio 1:7,768, Description), and productisation is unusually concrete for a HS team: a quality director steered the team to carry the anti-calculus claim on toothpaste under GB22115 and to drop preventive claims from the chewing gum under GB2760 (iHP 7.1), backed by a 137-user format survey. What is missing is any test in a realistic setting - no saliva, no enamel chips, no release kinetics from the carriers - so deployment remains argued rather than demonstrated.
justification.a4: Several cycles are real, not decorative. Expert feasibility review cut three recombinant enzyme classes to one and bought in papain/DNase I (Engineering Design 1); a chimeric-enzyme route was dropped on structural advice (iHP 5.1); the failed 18aa expression selected 21aa; a null gravimetric endpoint drove the switch to crystal violet and acridine orange (Test 3). Best of all, the FoldX prediction was falsified by their own data - Q172P net OD540 1.881 vs WT 0.996 vs Y166Q 0.629 - and the team revised the ranking and said why (Modeling section 8, Discussion).
