Short of 5 because Cycle 4 has no Test and some Cycle 1 work is ordinary PCR troubleshooting.
justification.a5: Twelve named experts with affiliations, and the design visibly moves after each: Dr Wang Yongwu's point that dissolving mineralised calculus is futile reset the target to the pre-mineralisation biofilm (iHP 2.2), Dr Wang Haoran's advice set the recombinant/commercial split, Prof Yu Haining specified the compartmentalised sequential release that became the three-carrier formulation (iHP 6.1-6.2), and Mr Yu Feng's regulatory input changed the claim structure. Two user surveys (N=350, N=137) are reported with figures. Not a 5 only because the inputs are paraphrased rather than evidenced with interview records, and the reflective ethics of enzymatic oral-microbiome disruption is touched lightly.
justification.a6: This is the weak aspect. The standard /attributions page returns the site's 404 (verified live, not just in the crawl), so there is no attribution form to read. The Team/members page lists eleven students by nickname with three lead roles and five mentors, with no statement of who did what or what outside help was used. The only per-person breakdown is inside the AI-usage modal. The Registry entries are all 'Designed by Devon Larkin', a name that appears nowhere on the team pages - I make no accusation, but I would ask the team in Q&A who that is and who performed the cloning, sequencing and instrument work.
justification.a7: Six new basic parts are registered and biosafety-cleared, each with role, topology, host organisms and RFC10/RFC1000 export: PmGH87 BBa_2638U4UV, CoGH66 BBa_265V2WY8, the two mutants BBa_260WPOJS and BBa_2654ZBYJ, and the two AMPs BBa_26082O0Q and BBa_26ZTHMQV. The shared pET-32a cassette (T7/lacO, RBS, TrxA, 6xHis, enterokinase site, T7 terminator) is genuinely modular and was reused unchanged across glucanases, peptides and mutants. Not a 5 because the parts are single-host CDSs rather than a collection designed for other teams to reuse, and two of the six have no function data behind them.
justification.a8: Registry pages carry functional descriptions, GenBank/literature sources, host strains and separate Design, Experiment, Characterisation and Application documentation entries (checked on BBa_2638U4UV, BBa_26ZTHMQV, BBa_260WPOJS). The wiki backs this with full protocols, a dated notebook, figure captions that name every lane and control, and raw per-replicate tables. Deductions: BBa_260WPOJS still says experimental characterisation is pending even though the DNS data exist on the Modeling page, and the AMP part BBa_26082O0Q documents a construct that never expressed.
justification.w1: The Description page states the problem, the three-module solution and the chassis clearly, and the home page ends with an honest 'from concept to evidence' box that marks clinical removal as unvalidated. But the aim is reached only after a long animated scroll through a world map and letter-spaced hero text; a judge cannot state the success criterion from the first screen the way Lambert_GA allows.
justification.w2: Among the strongest evidence presentations I have read at this level: per-replicate tables for every endpoint (Measurement Tables 2-4), standard curves with R2, named controls in each figure panel, ANOVA before planned t-tests with an explicit note that the pairwise tests are uncorrected and exploratory at n=3, and a Limitations section that names the surrogate organism, the single application and the missing mineral assay.
justification.w3: Navigation is the real defect. Following the iGEM standard page names, /results, /parts, /attributions, /description, /experiments, /notebook, /protocols, /team and /proof-of-concept all render the site's own 404 screen; the content actually lives at /wet-lab/results, /wet-lab/parts, /project/description and /team/members, reachable only from the custom top menu. A judge arriving by the standard URLs sees an empty project. Within the custom menu the per-page sidebars work well, which keeps this above a 2.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: dated July-August notebook, a 22-item protocol page from PCR mixes to artificial calculus formation and BCA, the full FoldX/MAFFT/PyMOL pipeline described step by step, and a Contribution page that distils multi-enzyme storage and protease cross-degradation into a reusable guide. It is long, and the Contribution page drifts into a general literature review, which costs it the top mark.
justification.w5: Every substantive page carries a numbered reference list that is actually used in text, the key methods cite their sources (Cha et al. 2025 for the calculus model, Zhang et al. 1999 for the glucan extraction, Cortez et al. 2023 for the glucanase pair), and the home-page map states IHME/WHO data provenance, licences and boundary sources. Spot-checked references resolve to real, on-topic papers. Short of 5 because several schematic figures carry no explicit credit line despite the AI-usage box saying some imagery was machine-generated.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineered high-school project - two glucanases expressed, purified and characterised with proper controls, a computational prediction overturned by the team's own assay, and a five-arm omission test on a mineralised biofilm - undermined mainly by a missing attributions page and standard wiki URLs that 404.
strengths: Measured, controlled data at every stage: substrate-swap and heat-inactivated controls in the DNS assays (Engineering Fig.5), triplicate raw values and ANOVA for crystal violet and acridine orange (Measurement Tables 3-4)

A model that was corrected by experiment: FoldX ranked Y166Q first, the DNS assay put Q172P first (net OD540 1.881 vs 0.996 WT vs 0.629 Y166Q), and the team rebuilt its ranking and explained the discrepancy (Modeling sections 5-8)
Failures reported rather than hidden: null gravimetric endpoint, non-expressing 18aa peptide, papain omission at p=0.08, and a Limitations list naming the B. subtilis surrogate

Human practices that visibly change the design - target window moved to the pre-mineralisation biofilm, chimeric enzyme dropped, three-carrier sequential release specified, and the regulatory claim moved onto toothpaste only (iHP 2.2, 5.1, 6.2, 7.1)
Six new parts registered with sequences, hosts, sources and Design/Experiment/Characterisation documentation, all built on one reusable pET-32a cassette
weaknesses: No attribution content at all: /attributions is a 404 and the Team page gives only names and three role labels, so who did the cloning, sequencing and instrument work cannot be judged
The standard iGEM page URLs (results, parts, description, notebook, protocols, team, proof-of-concept) all 404; content is reachable only through the team's custom menu
Efficacy rests on a B. subtilis surrogate whose EPS is not the alpha-glucan the glucanases were chosen for, so the headline synergy claim is not tested on the intended substrate
Activity comparisons were run on crude lysates normalised by BCA rather than purified enzyme, so no specific activities or kinetics support the mutant claim

Cycle 4 (formulation) has no test - no release kinetics, no stability or activity-retention data - yet the Contribution page asserts that an all-in-one mix caused rapid activity loss without showing the measurement
No mineral-phase measurement (calcium release or spectroscopy), so 'calculus degradation' is inferred from organic-matrix stains only
red_flags: Standard attributions page returns 404 on the live wiki (verified by direct fetch); no attribution form anywhere - aspect 6 cannot be verified and should be a Q&A question, not an accusation
All six Registry parts are listed as 'Designed by Devon Larkin', a name that appears nowhere among the eleven students or five mentors on the Team page - worth asking the team to explain

The team discloses using Doubao 2.1 to generate imagery (product family, SDG figure, usage matrix). These are illustrative, not evidence figures, and the disclosure is commendable, but a judge should confirm no data figure was machine-generated
Contribution page states 'a simple all-in-one mix led to rapid activity loss' as an experimental finding with no data, figure or assay behind it
pages_read: results / parts / description / notebook / protocols / proof-of-concept standard URLs (404 or duplicate)

calibrated.changed: none — w3 2.5 is the lowest navigation score I gave and it is justified: every standard URL 404s, which is worse than the six-or-seven-page cases I put at 3.0-3.5. a8 4.0 stands because I verified three Registry entries directly.

justification.a1: In one season the team cloned and sequence-verified six pET-32a constructs, expressed and purified two glucanases, expressed one of two AMPs, designed and built two CoGH66 point mutants from a structural pipeline, built an artificial-calculus model and ran a six-arm omission study on it, then prepared three encapsulation carriers (wet-lab/results; Engineering Cycles 1-4; Modeling). The story climbs from enzyme selection to function to synergy to formulation, with failures left in view (18aa not expressed; gravimetric endpoint null; FoldX top candidate beaten by the back-up). It falls short of a 5 only because the headline target, mineralised calculus from S. mutans, was never actually tested: the surrogate biofilm and the absence of any mineral-phase measurement leave the central claim one step away.
justification.a2: Function is measured, not asserted: DNS assays with PBS, heat-inactivated and swapped-substrate controls show PmGH87 acting only on alpha-1,3-glucan and CoGH66 mainly on alpha-1,6 (Engineering Fig. 5C-F), the 21aa peptide gives an inhibition zone while the negative control and 18aa do not (Fig. 9C), and the Measurement page gives per-replicate tables, ANOVA and the complete cocktail at 57.1% lower CV OD580 than PBS (Table 3). Against that, the glucanase and mutant activities come from crude lysates with no purified-enzyme kinetics, n=3 throughout, and the biofilm is B. subtilis rather than S. mutans, which the team itself flags. Solid, controlled, honestly bounded function data, but the project's own target biology is not yet demonstrated.
justification.a3: The need is real and confirmed by people who see it: Dr Lei and Dr Wang Yongwu on patient compliance and on why dissolving mineralised calculus is futile, Mr Fan on unmet market demand, and 350 and 137 respondent surveys on the knowing-doing gap (iHP 1.2-1.3, 7.2). The route to deployment is unusually concrete for a high school team, with Mr Yu Feng steering the filing to GB22115 for toothpaste and GB2760 forbidding preventive claims on chewing gum (iHP 7.1). It stays at 3.5 because nothing was tested in anything like the mouth: no real enamel, saliva, cytotoxicity or irritation data, as the Safety page section 10 states plainly.
justification.a4: Four cycles each contain a Learn step that visibly changed the next Build. The three-enzyme plan became two recombinant glucanases plus commercial papain and DNase I after expert input on protease toxicity and DNase yield (Cycle 1 Design); A. niger was replaced by shiitake glucan and S. mutans by B. subtilis after White List constraints (Cycle 1 Test, Cycle 3 Design); the gravimetric endpoint failed and was replaced by crystal violet and acridine orange (Cycle 3 Test); papain's cross-degradation of the other components drove the three-carrier sequential-release design (Cycle 4). Best of all, the model was corrected by data: FoldX ranked Y166Q first, but DNS on protein-normalised lysates gave Q172P net OD540 1.881 versus WT 0.996 and Y166Q 0.629, and the team rewrote its ranking and discussed why predicted binding need not raise turnover (Modeling, Discussion).
justification.a5: The iHP page names twelve stakeholders with a stated reason for each, and the design changes are traceable: Dr Wang Yongwu's 'egg hitting a stone' remark moved the target from mineralised calculus to the pre-mineralisation biofilm (2.2), Dr Wang Haoran's advice split recombinant from commercial enzymes (3.2), Professor Wang Zhiguo's folding objection killed the chimeric-enzyme route in favour of point mutation (5.1), Dr Shi Jing's input added the HAp-binding AMP module (4.1), and Mr Yu Feng's regulatory reading made toothpaste the claim-bearing format (7.1). Negative impacts are considered too, including microbiome disruption and the explicit refusal to position the product as a replacement for scaling. Short of 5 only because the two surveys are reported as percentages with no instrument, sampling or consent and ethics statement, and the consulted voices are largely supportive rather than critical.
justification.a6: This is the weak point. The standard Attributions page returns a 404, the Team page lists eleven students with role labels (Team Leader, Wet Lab Lead, Dry Lab Lead) and five mentors with no tasks attached, and the dated Notebook entries carry protocols but no names. The only named division of labour anywhere is in the AI Usage box, which assigns wiki sections to students (Darn and Jack for wet lab, Tony for the model, Luke for the survey). Nothing on the wiki says who ran the Ni purification, the enterokinase cleavage, the fluorescence microscopy or the FoldX runs, or what the five instructors and the host lab contributed. I am not alleging anything: I simply cannot tell, so this stays at 2.5 until the session clarifies it.
justification.a7: The project is built on standard components: codon-optimised ORFs in pET-32a under T7 with lac operator, RBS, TrxA, 6xHis and an enterokinase site, assembled by Gibson and exportable as RFC 10 and RFC 1000 from the Registry entries. Six parts are registered, and two of them, CoGH66 Q172P (BBa_260WPOJS) and Y166Q (BBa_2654ZBYJ), are genuinely new engineered variants, with Q172P showing higher apparent activity than wild type. Marked down from 5 because the registered parts are basic CDSs rather than the composite cassettes the team actually built, and the expression scaffold itself is off-the-shelf.
justification.a8: All six parts are live on the Registry with sequence, length, GC, role and topology ontology terms, host strains, source (GenBank accession or the originating paper for the peptides), a functional description, and attached Design, Experiment, Characterisation and, for two parts, Application documents (checked on bba-2638u4uv, bba-265v2wy8, bba-260wpojs, bba-2654zbyj, bba-26082o0q, bba-26ZTHMQV). The wiki backs this with full figure captions, a protocols page of 22 methods, a dated notebook and per-replicate raw tables (Measurement Tables 2-4). Not a 5 because there is no collection-level documentation and the Registry entries lean on the wiki for the omission-study data.
justification.w1: The home page opens with the DCO name, a one-line statement of the approach, and a guided scroll through global burden, how calculus forms, the enzyme targets and surface protection, with a 'Skip to the project story' link for judges in a hurry. The Description page then states the problem, the three-module solution and its evidential basis in a few screens (Figure 3 schematic). Minor cost: the decorative letter-spaced headings make the opening screens slow to read.
justification.w2: Claims are tied to figures and, unusually, to raw numbers: Measurement Tables 2-4 give every replicate for the gravimetric, crystal violet and acridine orange endpoints, with ANOVA F values and an explicit note that the pairwise t-tests are uncorrected and exploratory at n=3. Modelled results are labelled as such throughout (the FoldX candidates are called computational predictions; Cycle 4's chewing gum and film formats are flagged as proposed and not validated). Two small blemishes: the Engineering Test 3 narration describes the CV significances slightly differently from the Measurement page, and the AlphaFold peptide-calcium ipTM screen is used for ranking at pTM around 0.4, which the team acknowledges but still relies on.
justification.w3: The side menu maps cleanly onto the criteria and On This Page anchors help inside the long Engineering and iHP pages. But the content sits on non-standard paths (project/description, wet-lab/results, wet-lab/parts), and the standard URLs a judge would try, including /description, /results, /parts, /proof-of-concept, /team and /attributions, land on the site's 404 page. Against the handbook's instruction that teams must guide judges from the standard pages, that costs real marks, and no Attributions page exists at any address I could find.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: 22 protocols on the Experiments page, a dated July-August notebook, primer sequences (Results Table 1), the full FoldX and alignment workflow with PDB 8IUB, raw replicate tables, a frank Safety page listing what was never tested, and a Contribution page on enzyme storage and release written for others to reuse. What is missing is the human record: no who-did-what, no statement of which equipment or help came from outside, and the mutant work stops before purified kinetics.
justification.w5: Every page carries a numbered reference list with journals, volumes and DOIs or PubMed links, in-text markers are used consistently, the artificial-calculus figure is credited as adapted from Cha et al., and the B. subtilis mineralisation claim is sourced to a named thesis. The home page map goes further than most, giving IHME GBD and WHO citations, the exact query, boundary sources and the licence terms for each layer. AI assistance is disclosed with models, uses and the named students who fact-checked each section. The only lapses are a white-paper citation that resolves to a news article and several literature-derived schematics whose redrawing is not stated.

J3.one_line: A disciplined, evidence-led dental-calculus project: six registered parts, controlled enzyme assays, a model corrected by its own wet-lab data and genuinely design-changing stakeholder work, let down by an absent Attributions page and standard page URLs that 404.
strengths: Measured function with real controls: substrate-swap, PBS and heat-inactivated controls for both glucanases, an AMP inhibition zone against a negative control, and a six-arm omission study with every replicate value printed (Measurement Tables 2-4)

A model that was wrong and said so: FoldX ranked Y166Q top, the DNS assay on protein-normalised lysates put Q172P first (net OD540 1.881 vs WT 0.996 vs Y166Q 0.629), and the team revised its ranking and explained the discrepancy (Modeling, Discussion)

Stakeholder input with visible consequences, each traceable to a named expert: target shifted to the pre-mineralisation biofilm, recombinant work narrowed to the glucanases, chimeric enzyme abandoned, AMP module added, toothpaste made the claim-bearing format under GB22115 (iHP 2.2, 3.2, 4.1, 5.1, 7.1)

Honesty about limits throughout: failed 18aa expression, null gravimetric result, B. subtilis as a surrogate, no mineral-phase measurement, and a Safety section 10 that simply lists what has not been tested
All six parts documented on the Registry itself with sequence, host, role, source and attached Design, Experiment and Characterisation records, not just on the wiki
weaknesses: No Attributions page (the standard URL 404s) and no named division of bench work: the notebook carries protocols without names, and five instructors are listed with no tasks, so I cannot tell what the students did themselves

The central biology is demonstrated on a surrogate: B. subtilis biofilm rather than S. mutans, and crystal violet measures organic biomass, so 'calculus degradation' is never shown as mineral loss (no calcium release or spectroscopic analysis)
Glucanase and mutant activities rest on crude lysates at n=3 with no purified-enzyme kinetics or specific activities, which the team identifies as the next step but has not taken
Content sits on non-standard paths while /description, /results, /parts, /team and /proof-of-concept return the site's 404 page, making judges hunt against the handbook's guidance
Two user surveys (N=350, N=137) are reported only as headline percentages, with no instrument, sampling description or statement of consent and ethics oversight
red_flags: Standard wiki URLs (description, results, parts, attributions, team, proof-of-concept, experiments, notebook, protocols) resolve to a 404 page; the content lives at project/description, wet-lab/results and similar paths reachable only from the site's own navigation
No Attributions page anywhere on the wiki; the only division of labour is a writing-section list inside the AI Usage disclosure box
All six Registry entries are credited to a designer name (Devon Larkin) that does not appear on the Team Members page; worth a clarifying question at the session, not an accusation
Surveys of 350 and 137 respondents reported without consent, sampling or ethics-oversight information
Minor internal inconsistency: Engineering Test 3 describes the crystal violet significances more cautiously than Reflection 3 on the same page, while the Measurement page gives the full statistics

calibrated.changed: none. a6 of 2.5 is consistent with the other teams whose only division of labour is a role label or a writing-section list. a8 of 4.5 is earned on verified Registry entries, which is the distinction I apply throughout.

one_line.en: A well-controlled enzyme project where the computational prediction was overturned by the team's own assay and said so, undermined by a missing attributions page and standard URLs that 404.
one_line.zh: 對照嚴謹的酵素專案，計算預測被自家實驗推翻並據實說明，但缺少歸屬頁且標準網址 404。

strengths: Substrate specificity shown with substrate-swap, buffer and heat-inactivated controls at n = 3
A measurement page printing every replicate value, running ANOVA before planned tests and labelling small-n results as exploratory
A closed loop where the predicted top mutant lost to the measured top mutant and the ranking was revised with an explanation
Human Practices that repeatedly changed the science, including retargeting the intervention window and dropping a chimeric enzyme
weaknesses: No attributions page and no named owner for any experiment, with five instructors listed without tasks
Efficacy rests on a surrogate organism whose matrix is not the polymer the enzymes target, and no mineral-phase measurement was made
Activity reported from crude lysates with no specific activity or purified-enzyme kinetics
The formulation cycle HAS no test data, yet a formulation finding is asserted on the Contribution page
red_flags: All six Registry parts are credited to a designer name that appears nowhere among the listed students or mentors
Standard URLs for results, parts, description, team, experiments, protocols and notebook all return 404
Two surveys reported as headline percentages with no consent, sampling or ethics information
AI-generated imagery disclosed for illustrative figures

screen.project_title: AstroFlora: plant probiotics regulating ABA and IAA under simulated microgravity
screen.what_they_built: Two independent E. coli systems — a PYR1-GST-HAB1 ABA response module and a pBAD-IAMT1 IAA degradation module — intended as plant probiotics for space agriculture, tested alongside Floraspin, a home-built clinostat-style microgravity simulator used for Arabidopsis germination.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and TOP10; pET28a and pBAD vectors; three parts (BBa_26GF679M PYR1 basic, BBa_26SCPZZD and BBa_2686PQE4 composites).
screen.best_evidence: /engineering: SDS-PAGE plus an ALP (pNPP, 405 nm) assay with calibration curve for HAB1 activity across IPTG and ABA gradients; Salkowski OD530 assay showing IAA consumption rising with arabinose (0 to 1%) in three experimental groups. Both are relative-only — the team states background colour prevents absolute IAA quantification.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — interviews with aerospace centre staff, botany professors and an engineering professor; the suggestion to switch to a plant-endophyte chassis is recorded as future work rather than implemented.
screen.reason: Honest five-cycle engineering story with real troubleshooting, but no results page at all, only three parts, and the two central claims stay semi-quantitative: HAB1 activity is confounded by leaky expression and the IAA assay is explicitly relative because of LB background. No model page and no education page. Not top-2 calibre.
screen.field_notes: HAS (Space village, CHN) built AstroFlora, bacterial plant probiotics meant to correct hormone imbalances that stunt plants in microgravity. Two separate E. coli systems were made: pET28a-PYR1-GST-HAB1, where ABA binding to PYR1 should modulate the PP2C phosphatase HAB1, and pBAD-IAMT1 to methylate and remove excess auxin. Cloning is well documented with gels and a two-step PCR workaround for HAB1 homology arms. Testing reached only semi-quantitative evidence: SDS-PAGE plus a pNPP alkaline-phosphatase assay with a calibration curve showed HAB1 expressed leakily and largely independently of IPTG and ABA, and a Salkowski OD530 assay showed IAA declining as arabinose rose from 0 to 1%, which the team says can only be read as a relative change because LB background colour cannot be subtracted. Five DBTL cycles include a failed TOP10 expression at 37 C fixed by 18 C overnight induction. Supporting work is Floraspin, a low-cost open-source microgravity simulator with speed, temperature, humidity and germination tests and a cost breakdown, plus a 13.5k-word protocols/notebook and a 10k-word entrepreneurship page; the results page is empty and no model or education page exists.

screen.project_title: Dual-strain EcN probiotic for hyperlysinemia
screen.what_they_built: Two engineered E. coli Nissle strains that split the human saccharopine lysine-degradation pathway between them (LKR+SDH upstream, ALDH+AASDHPPT downstream) and are physically coupled by SpyTag/SpyCatcher surface display, with an ldcC knockout chassis and an oxygen/arabinose-responsive kill switch, intended as a gut-resident therapy for an ultra-rare metabolic disease.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli Nissle 1917 dldcC; eCPX outer-membrane display of SpyTag and SpyCatcher; Bxb1-PcyoA-lysisE kill switch with RBS strength tuning (BBa_B0029/B0031/B0033/B0035); ~22 new BBa parts plus standard RBS/promoter parts, collected on a part-collection page.
screen.best_evidence: /results: HPLC-MS with an L-lysine standard curve shows endogenous lysine consumption eliminated in EcN dldcC and relieved growth inhibition at 5 mg/mL lysine (p < 0.05); co-culture time courses show lysine consumption over 24 h with a 2:1 upstream:downstream ratio optimal and only a modest, non-significant gain from Spy cross-linking; fluorescence microscopy with ImageJ quantifies chimeric cluster number and size versus a no-Spy negative control; kill-switch lysis confirmed by CFU drop after arabinose induction, cross-checked by supernatant GFP release.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - Dr. Mingjun Sun suggested the SpyTag/SpyCatcher coupling that became the binding module, and Prof. Liujie Huo's advice added the artificial colonic fluid stability tests; HP runs six staged rounds with a documented second pass through technical, clinical and commercial stages.
screen.reason: A genuinely engineered multi-module system with measured outputs at every layer - genome knockout verified by HPLC-MS, quantified cell-cell coupling, lysine clearance time courses, and a kill switch characterised three independent ways with the limits of each stated. A NetLogo model chose the SpyCatcher RBS before the bench work, and the Discussion names exactly what is missing. The reservation is aspect 6: the Attributions page is effectively empty, so the division of labour cannot be checked. Full read warranted.
screen.field_notes: HFI (Guangzhou, Therapeutics) targeted hyperlysinemia, an AASS-deficiency disorder affecting about 1 in 411,000 newborns with no therapy beyond lifelong protein restriction, using two cooperating E. coli Nissle strains. They first knocked out ldcC to remove endogenous lysine decarboxylation, verifying by growth curves under a lysine gradient and by HPLC-MS of supernatant lysine. The human saccharopine pathway was split across strains - LKR+SDH in strain A, ALDH+AASDHPPT in strain B - and the two were covalently coupled via eCPX-displayed SpyTag and SpyCatcher; fluorescence microscopy with ImageJ quantified chimeric cluster number, size and distribution against a no-Spy control, with many free single cells remaining exactly as their NetLogo agent-based model had predicted. That model, run before the bench work, also selected BBa_B0035 as the SpyCatcher RBS by trading cluster size against burden. Lysine clearance over 24 h was best at a 2:1 strain ratio, but Spy cross-linking gave only a modest, non-significant improvement over free mixing, and they state plainly that saccharopine and AASA intermediates were never quantified, so complete flux through the cascade is unproven. Strains survived 48 h in artificial colonic fluid with stable EGFP accumulation. The Bxb1-PcyoA-lysisE kill switch suffered recombinase leakage, fixed by low-strength RBS screening, and was characterised by OD600, CFU and a new supernatant GFP-release assay with the limitations of each method spelled out. HP ran six stages twice over, including patient-side and regulatory interviews. The Attributions page carries no content.

screen.project_title: REIGN — PlyPl23-royalisin fusion against American foulbrood
screen.what_they_built: An in-silico designed recombinant fusion of the bacteriophage endolysin PlyPl23 and the bee defensin royalisin joined by a (GGGGS)3 linker, codon-optimised for E. coli BL21 and ordered as a gBlock with tac promoter, RBS, His tag and rrnB terminator, intended for delivery in bee feed against Paenibacillus larvae.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21 (planned only); 8 BBa parts designed and tabled (PlyPl23 BBa_26L5QMWB, royalisin BBa_26BDJ0I8, fusion BBa_26HILAZD, (GGGGS)3 linker, 6xHis, tac, RBS, rrnB) — designs with no build or test data.
screen.best_evidence: /model and /engineering: AlphaFold 3 solution dynamics, GROMACS stability in a modelled midgut, protease cleavage-site prediction and diffusion/advection transport modelling. The team states that 'the downstream experimental stages needed to establish successful plasmid assembly, protein expression, purification, and antibacterial activity were not completed'; Iteration 7 (surrogate assay on P. alvei) is written entirely in the future tense.
screen.hp_integration: Yes and materially — stakeholder findings killed the original pollination-substitute project in Phase 0 and redirected the team to protecting bees from AFB; beekeeper and company interviews shaped the feed-delivery format and the education workshops.
screen.reason: Honest, well-written, with a real HP-driven pivot and a competent multi-layer computational workflow, but there is no wet-lab result of any kind — no cloning, expression, purification or activity data — and the parts exist only as designs. Modelled predictions are not experimental results.
screen.field_notes: HG-Tokyo 2026 (REIGN, Conservation, Japan) targets American foulbrood in honey bees with a designed fusion protein, PlyPl23-(GGGGS)3-royalisin, combining a phage endolysin active against Paenibacillus larvae with a bee defensin, codon-optimised for E. coli BL21 and ordered as a gBlock carrying tac promoter, RBS, 6xHis and rrnB terminator. The project is entirely computational: seven engineering iterations covering linker design, AlphaFold 3 solution dynamics, GROMACS midgut stability, gut transport and advection modelling, protease cleavage-site plus structural accessibility prediction, and molecular docking to the cell envelope. The team states explicitly that plasmid assembly, expression, purification and antibacterial testing were not completed, and the surrogate agar-diffusion assay on Paenibacillus alvei is written as planned work. Human practices is the strongest section: Phase 0 abandoned an earlier bee-pollination-substitute idea after strawberry farmers and public surveys showed no demand, and beekeeper and bee-health-company interviews set the AFB focus and the bee-feed delivery route. Eight parts are tabled as designs; the Attributions page is a single link to the iGEM form.

screen.project_title: AiyUReady — an indirect methanol biosensor for Aiyu fruit ripeness
screen.what_they_built: A two-plasmid colour biosensor: methanol dehydrogenase converts ripening-associated methanol to formaldehyde, and a formaldehyde-responsive promoter then drives the AmilCP chromoprotein for a visible readout of Aiyu harvest readiness.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning and MG1655 for the dual-plasmid system; pSB1C3 upstream and pJUMP23-1A downstream. Mostly existing Registry parts — BBa_K1585200 (MDH), BBa_K2728001 (pFrmR), BBa_K592009 (amilCP), J23100/J23105/J23106, B0032/B0034, B0015 — plus two new composites BBa_26WY86QQ and BBa_26OVY7TQ.
screen.best_evidence: /results, final table: OD590/OD700 across 0, 1, 5, 10 and 50 mM methanol for both the High-Sensitivity and Max-Signal upstream strains, measured hourly for three hours, with ratios clustered around 1.09-1.26 and no concentration trend; no visible colour difference between pellets. Negative but real data. The dual-plasmid MG1655 run produced almost no biomass (one tube with a pellet too small to read), and the downstream plate showed blue colonies without formaldehyde, which the team reads as pFrmR leakiness.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — two meetings with Aiyu farmer Mr. Lin Chien-wen established the ripeness problem and the 80% accuracy baseline that motivated the whole project, and dry-lab modelling killed the Low-Toxicity upstream variant for failing a 1 uM detection floor; but no stakeholder input visibly changed the circuit after the concept stage.
screen.reason: The system was never shown to work and, by the team's own account, was never fully verified: faint or absent digest bands, an acknowledged wrong verification primer pair, a downstream construct whose only confirmation is a gel with no image recorded, a dual-plasmid host that would not grow, and a dual-bacterial workaround with a flat dose response and no colour. Honest and well-written, but aspect 2 is close to the floor and aspect 8 cannot be rescued by documentation of unverified constructs.
screen.field_notes: HIA-Taiwan (TWN, Agriculture) addressed harvest timing in Aiyu (Ficus pumila var. awkeotsang), a Taiwanese crop with roughly NT$1 billion annual output whose value collapses if picked outside the window, where experienced farmers self-report about 80% accuracy. Because no well-characterised methanol-responsive promoter exists, they designed an indirect two-stage sensor: NAD-dependent MDH from Bacillus methanolicus (BBa_K1585200) oxidises the methanol released by endogenous pectin methylesterase during ripening, and the resulting formaldehyde activates pFrmR (BBa_K2728001) driving amilCP (BBa_K592009). Three upstream variants (J23105/B0032 basic, J23106/B0034 high-sensitivity, J23100/B0034 max-signal) were built on pSB1C3 with a shared pJUMP23-1A downstream; a fourth low-toxicity variant was dropped after modelling predicted it would miss the 1 uM detection floor. Construction struggled throughout: smeared or faint PCR and digest bands, an incorrect verification primer combination, one transformation with no colonies, and a downstream verification gel described as normal but not photographed. Co-transformation into MG1655 produced almost no growth, attributed tentatively to dual-plasmid burden, so the team split the modules into two DH5a populations mixed 3:7 and dosed 0-100 mM methanol, quantifying amilCP as OD590/OD700 to avoid pigment interference with OD600; the ratios showed no dose dependence over three hours and pellets showed no colour, while uninduced downstream colonies were already blue, indicating pFrmR leakiness. The contribution page proposes a single-plasmid redesign plus a constitutive FrmR cassette to restore repression. A large model page and a separate proof-of-concept page exist; the wiki is clearly written and candid, but the notebook is a stub and no functional claim is supported.

screen.project_title: Green Mining: designed metal-binding proteins in alginate beads for Ni/Co/Li recovery from battery leachate
screen.what_they_built: Six de novo metal-binding proteins (Ni, Co, Li; RFdiffusion3 + ProteinMPNN) encoded as 6 CDS parts and 12 plasmids in E. coli, immobilised in alginate beads, packed into a 3D-printed six-stage detachable cartridge run on a peristaltic pump. They also converted a filament 3D printer into a room-temperature syringe bioprinter and wrote BioPrintCAD toolpath software.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli Rosetta (pTYB21 T7-ompA series) and TOP10 (pUC19 lac-LacZalpha series); 18 Registry entries (6 coding parts BBa_26GVBXIZ, BBa_26NMV3V3, BBa_267C35CF, BBa_26NR6YC9, BBa_265LOJU4, BBa_2673WRUO plus 12 complete plasmids). Alginate (HV/LV), PETG printed cartridges.
screen.best_evidence: /results/metal-binding-assay: nickel eluate from high-viscosity pGM-T7-NiCP2 beads 7.64 +/- 1.30 mg/L vs 0.11 mg/L for plasmid-free TOP10 beads, with all individual absorbances and three independent preparations tabulated; cobalt means 4.91-8.72 mg/L/g with HV > LV in all four paired comparisons (Welch p = 0.008, flagged as exploratory). /engineering and /results/3d-modeling-and-printing: one mixed 100 mL feed (10.0 mg each metal) through the printed six-stage stack, pair elutions giving 91 +/- 8 (Ni), 117 +/- 11 (Co), 84 +/- 14 (Li) mg/L, i.e. 18.2/23.4/16.8% of feed.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and traceably: a battery-recycler (Chase Solar) pushed them to a mixed aqueous feed at a practical flow rate, which produced the modular six-stage stack; DreamTec's enclosed professional printer led to the acrylic cabinet; Dr Keith Kwong's advice on sucrose and bench-side syringe filling changed the bioink formulation to 2% alginate + 10% sucrose; Prof. Sze (CUHK) pushed matrix-matched calibration and blanks, which the team records as still pending.
screen.reason: Best-calibrated evidence in the batch: triplicate bead assays with a plasmid-free control, raw per-replicate tables, a working printed device run end to end, 18 Registry entries and unusually honest statements of what has NOT been shown (no selectivity, lithium extrapolated beyond calibration, CP2 eluate plates clear). Engineering page is a genuine limitation/response/evidence/next-test ledger. Attribution is itemised per school and per student. Deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: HK League (Hong Kong, Bioremediation) targets the aqueous stream left after battery hydrometallurgy or bioleaching rather than the battery itself. Six de novo proteins (GM-NiCP1/2, GM-CoCP1/2, GM-LiCP1/2, 163-302 aa) were designed by hand-building a donor-atom site then generating backbone with RFdiffusion3 and sequence with ProteinMPNN; each was cloned into a T7-ompA pTYB21 vector and a lac-LacZalpha pUC19 vector, giving 18 Registry entries, with 27 Sanger reads covering every coding region and an anti-OmpA blot on the six induced T7 lysates. Cells were immobilised in high- and low-viscosity alginate beads and assayed in triplicate: high-viscosity GM-NiCP2 gave 7.64 +/- 1.30 mg/L nickel against 0.11 mg/L for plasmid-free TOP10 beads, cobalt 4.91-8.72 mg/L/g, and lithium only as conductivity-derived equivalents above the calibrated range. A printed six-stage detachable cartridge, packed with beads and driven by a peristaltic pump, completed one load-wash-imidazole-elution of a 10.0 mg mixed Ni/Co/Li feed, recovering a calculated 18.2/23.4/16.8%; the team states this is a handling record, not a selectivity measurement. Hardware work includes a desktop printer converted to a bench syringe pump with blunt 27 G needle and filtered acrylic enclosure, bioink trials ending at 2% alginate + 10% sucrose under 0.22% CaCl2, printed lattices containing engineered E. coli, downloadable STLs, and a browser-based BioPrintCAD toolpath tool. Human practices with a battery recycler, two bioprinting companies, a protein-design consultancy and a CUHK chemist each map to a named design change; attributions break the work down by the six participating schools and by individual student.

justification.a1: The chain is genuinely long for a high school team and each link has a page behind it: six de novo metal-binding proteins, twelve plasmids, Sanger-verified, transformed in two hosts, cells immobilised in two alginate grades, beads assayed per metal, then packed into a self-printed six-stage cartridge that completed a mixed load/wash/imidazole elution (home, engineering, results/3d-modeling-and-printing). A converted syringe bioprinter and two open-source teaching apps sit alongside it. It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS top anchor because the hardest claim in the chain, metal-selective capture by the designed proteins, is explicitly left unmeasured ('Selective recovery, continuous-flow performance and reuse remain to be measured', engineering).
justification.a2: There is real measured data: the bead assay (results/metal-binding-assay) has three independent preparations per condition, OLS calibrations with R2 reported, individual absorbances tabulated, and a plasmid-free TOP10 reference; high-viscosity pGM-T7-NiCP2 gave 7.64 +/- 1.30 mg/L against 0.11 mg/L for plasmid-free beads, and the cartridge run carried a distilled-water control (0.4/0.2/2.3 mg/L against 91/117/84 mg/L). What is missing is protein-level evidence: the only blot is an anti-OmpA immunoblot, which reports OmpA signal and not the designed cargo, and the team says so on the results page even though the home page card reads 'a band at the size of its metal-binding protein'. The plasmid-free control is a single value in one alginate grade only, there is no cell-free alginate blank, lithium is non-specific conductivity extrapolated two to three times beyond the top standard, and the cartridge run is one run whose eluates were each read only for the assigned metal, so selectivity is untested.
justification.a3: The problem framing is well sourced (IEA figures on the description page) and the target stream, post-leaching aqueous liquor, was chosen after talking to Chase Solar and Dr Bing Wong (human-practices). But everything was run on laboratory-prepared single- and mixed-salt solutions rather than leachate or any real-world-like matrix, and the only impact-shaped number, 18.2/23.4/16.8% of metal fed, is a recovery fraction from one run with no mass balance or cross-metal composition. This sits above a generic problem statement but below TAS Taipei's wastewater-style test.
justification.a4: The engineering page is the strongest part of the submission: a table of observed limitation, design response, evidence in hand and the test still to be made, with three cycles that are redesign rather than troubleshooting. The hot-end nozzle was replaced by a bench syringe because a hot end cannot handle room-temperature hydrogel; the one-body column was redrawn as detachable cartridges so pairs could be eluted separately, then printed and run; and after strands floated or stuck to the plate bottom in the calcium bath the ink was reformulated to 2% alginate with 10% sucrose in 0.22% CaCl2 (results/bioprinting-and-bioink). Design targets were stated before testing (pLDDT > 80, RMSD < 2 A, donor distance windows on the model page), and the team records where those targets were not met.
justification.a5: Six substantive consultations are documented with named people and, for most, a specific consequence: Chase Solar and Dr Bing Wong pushed the application to a dissolved stream, Dr Keith Kwong's advice produced the sucrose ink and the bench-syringe arrangement, DreamTec's enclosed machine led to the acrylic cabinet, and Prof. Sze Tung Po's matrix-effects point is carried into the stated plan for matrix blanks and detection limits (human-practices). Two questions brought back from Grand APIC are tied to named next experiments, and three prior iGEM teams are credited as inputs. It is mostly technical-advisory dialogue; there is little engagement with community, regulatory or end-user perspectives on deploying engineered bacteria, which is what separates this from the top anchor.
justification.a6: The attributions page lists what each of the six schools did (CIS: bioprinting, plasmid design, western blot, cell counts; HGC: metal-binding assay; WFN: transformation and protein expression) and then names individual students against specific tasks. Supervisors, two advising doctors and a sponsor are separately declared as giving experimental-design advice and training rather than doing the work, and the AI tools used for design, figures, code and video are listed openly. The bench work reads as the students' own; the deduction is for the external AI/bioinformatics training and consultancy behind the protein-design pipeline, whose boundary with student work is not sharply drawn.
justification.a7: This is squarely a synthetic biology project: six de novo coding sequences, each placed in two defined cassettes, T7-lacO-RBS-ompA on pTYB21 and lac-LacZalpha on pUC19, with the same cargo swapped between translation contexts so the architecture is genuinely modular (parts, dna-design). Eighteen entries are registered as six linear CDS parts plus twelve complete plasmids, which is a sensible split for reuse. The backbones are commercial vectors rather than Registry parts, and no existing Registry parts are reused, so the standard-components side is thinner than the design side.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is excellent and anchored on standard pages: a parts index with length, GC, type, a map and FASTA per entry, plasmid maps with Sanger read arcs and read-to-map identities of 98.3-100%, and coding regions stated by coordinate (parts, dna-model). Eighteen Registry entries are claimed under HK League (2026). I could not load parts.igem.org during judging (403), so I could not confirm what characterisation each entry carries; the wiki itself only promises 'sequence notes and authors' there, which suggests the assay data live on the wiki rather than in the Registry entries, and p.18 asks me to judge parts on the Registry.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem (metals left in an aqueous stream after battery recycling), the approach (designed binding site, cells in alginate, printed cartridge) and the outcome in milestone cards that carry actual numbers, including the 18.2/23.4/16.8% shares, within roughly one screen of scrolling. The five-step 'Design, build, transform, immobilise, then test' strip maps one-to-one onto the pages that record each step. A little of the opening is scroll-driven atmosphere before the science starts.
justification.w2: Most key claims carry a figure, a table of individual values and a stated control: the bead assay gives per-preparation absorbances and concentrations, the eluate-plate result gives all fourteen plates with a positive control and an uninoculated plate, and the cartridge result gives a distilled-water run beside the mixed feed. Scope statements are unusually honest, flagging the 138% ratio, the plates with fewer than 30 colonies, the 550/33 pair, and the lithium values as extrapolated equivalents. Against that, the one expression figure does not measure the designed proteins, the plasmid-free control is n = 1 in one alginate grade, and the home page summarises the blot more strongly than the results page does.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped as Project / Science / Engineering / Impact / Team / Resources, and the Experiments and Results sections are mirrored one page per experiment, which makes method and data easy to pair. Related-pages footers link sideways between the assay, bead and cartridge pages. Friction: measurement, proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols and sustainability all return 404 on their standard URLs, so a judge following the standard page list finds empty slots even though the content exists under Experiments and Engineering.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: per-experiment methods with concentrations and timings, raw individual readings rather than only means, calibration equations, STL downloads for both cartridge geometries, the two test G-code files and a photographic-estimate CSV, plus a contribution page that states for each asset what still has to be verified before reuse. Failures are kept on the page (floating and adhered strands, the low-pLDDT 163-residue refold). The notebook page is the weak point: it is a protein-design PDF only, with no wet-lab daily record.
justification.w5: The description and model pages carry numbered references to named journal articles (Harper 2019, Larouche 2020, Sethurajan 2021, Lee and Mooney 2012) and to IEA reports, with the method tools cited to RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN and AlphaFold. Prior iGEM work is credited by team and year (BIT-China 2024, Waterloo 2020, Fudan 2024) on the human practices page, and AI tools used for figures, text and code are disclosed on the attributions page. Inline linking is good in the introductory pages but thinner on the engineering and hardware pages, where several design choices and illustrative figures carry no source.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete and unusually honest high school project that carries a de novo protein design all the way to a self-printed cartridge run, held back by the fact that no evidence shows the designed proteins themselves are expressed or doing the binding.
strengths: Full documented chain from designed binding site to an operated device: six de novo sequences, twelve Sanger-verified plasmids (27 reads, 98.3-100% identity), colonies from all twelve, beads from both alginate grades, and a printed six-stage cartridge that completed one load, wash and imidazole elution.

The bead assay is properly designed for a high school lab: eight conditions per metal, three independent preparations each, OLS calibrations with R2 stated, individual absorbances and concentrations tabulated, and a plasmid-free TOP10 reference included.

Controls appear where they matter most: fourteen eluate plates with a positive control (pGM-Plac-LiCP2 in TOP10) and an uninoculated plate, and a distilled-water run through the cartridge beside the mixed feed.

The engineering page is a real DBTL record, with a limitation / response / evidence / next-test table and three redesigns driven by observed failures (hot end to bench syringe, one-body column to detachable cartridges, ink reformulated after strands floated or stuck).

Scope and limits are stated by the team themselves: separate pair elution is called a handling step and not selectivity, the resistance ratio is called a plated phenotype and not plasmid retention, and lithium values are labelled extrapolated equivalents.
Attribution is specific to schools and to individual students, with advisors, sponsor and AI tools declared separately from student work.
Human practices produced named, traceable design changes: the sucrose ink, the bench-syringe arrangement, the printer enclosure and the planned matrix blanks each trace to a named consultation.
weaknesses: No protein-level evidence for the six designed proteins. The only blot is anti-OmpA, which reports OmpA signal, not the designed cargo; the team concedes this on the results page while the home page card says the band is 'at the size of its metal-binding protein'.

The plasmid-free TOP10 control is a single value, given only for the low-viscosity CP2 condition, while the largest effect in the dataset is high- versus low-viscosity alginate. With no cell-free crosslinked-alginate blank, the metal signal cannot be attributed to the designed protein rather than to the gel or the cells.

Lithium is read as bulk conductivity, which is not lithium-specific, and every engineered sample sits two to three times above the highest standard (1.104 mS/cm), so the lithium 'equivalents' are extrapolations rather than measurements.

The cartridge run is a single run, and each pair eluate was read only for its assigned metal, so there is no cross-metal composition, no mass balance (18.2 + 23.4 + 16.8% leaves most of the feed unaccounted for) and no selectivity demonstrated. A cobalt eluate at 1.17 times the feed concentration is reported without explanation of the mechanism.

The six-hour ampicillin time course rests on plates with fewer than 30 colonies in 35 of 36 induced pTYB21 counts, with one flagged 550/33 pair and a 138% ratio; the team discloses this, but the time course carries little weight.
Notebook coverage is thin: the page links one protein-design PDF and there is no wet-lab daily record, and the protocols standard URL is empty.
Five standard page URLs (measurement, proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, sustainability) return 404, so a judge working from the standard page list hits dead ends.
Some assets a future team would need (BioPrintCAD and the two teaching apps) live in external repositories, which under p.29 cannot be judged.
red_flags: Home page evidence card overstates the immunoblot: 'Every induced T7 lysate showed a band at the size of its metal-binding protein', where the results page describes the same figure as anti-OmpA signal. Not an integrity concern (the results page is accurate), but the summary claim outruns the figure.

parts.igem.org returned 403 to me throughout, so I could not verify the eighteen claimed Registry entries or what characterisation data they hold; this is scored as a limit of my access, not against the team.
Cobalt pair eluate (117 mg/L) exceeds the 100 mg/L feed with no stated explanation, and the SD on a single cartridge run is not defined as replicate reads or replicate runs.

No safety concerns: whitelist E. coli only, BSC handling, autoclave at 121 C for 25 min, EPD-licensed collection of metal waste, and a surface-screening protocol with controls before display. Nothing for the RCC.

calibrated.changed: none. a6 4.5 is the top of my range here and is earned by school-level plus named-student task attribution with supervisors and AI tools declared separately; a2 3.5 is correct because the only expression evidence is an anti-OmpA blot that does not measure the designed cargo, so the central binding claim is unsupported at protein level.

justification.a1: The scope is large for a high school team and it is one connected chain, not a pile of modules: six de novo metal-binding proteins, each cargo in two expression architectures (18 Registry entries), twelve transformations, alginate immobilisation, a converted syringe bioprinter, a printed six-stage cartridge that was actually operated, and three open-source tools (Parts, Engineering, Metal Recovery System). It falls short of the GreatBay anchor because the last and most important link - that the designed protein, rather than the alginate or the cells, does the binding - is not closed, and the cartridge run is a single operation (Engineering, "Where the workflow stands").
justification.a2: Construction is solidly verified: twelve ampicillin-resistant transformations with plate photographs, 27 Sanger reads at 98.3-100% identity covering every coding region (DNA Model), and a six-hour CFU time course with duplicate plates. Function is partly measured: the metal binding assay has three independent preparations per condition, calibration lines with R2 of 0.98-0.9999, and a plasmid-free TOP10 reference (nickel 0.11 mg/L vs 7.64 +/- 1.30 for HV pGM-T7-NiCP2), and the printed stack returned 91/117/84 mg/L against a distilled-water control (Results, 3D Modeling and 3D Printing). But the plasmid-free control exists only for the low-viscosity CP2 condition while the leads are high-viscosity, so the strongest effect is confounded with alginate grade; lithium is extrapolated conductivity well above the top standard (1.104 mS/cm vs samples 1.56-3.11); and the anti-OmpA blot measures OmpA signal, not the designed proteins. The team states each of these limits itself, which is to its credit, but they cap the claim at "measured eluate signals", not "the designed proteins work".
justification.a3: The target feed was narrowed by stakeholders to a dissolved aqueous stream after leaching, which is a sensible and defended boundary (Human Practices, Mr Chau and Dr Bing Wong; Metal Recovery System, "Boundary of the recovery system as operated"). Everything to date is a prepared 100 mg/L laboratory solution; no real or surrogate leachate, no pH or competing-ion work, no reuse cycles, and no cross-metal composition in the eluates, so selectivity - the thing that would make this useful - is still unmeasured. The route is plausible and argued, with the next tests named, which is level-3 work rather than TAS Taipei's tested wastewater-style setup.
justification.a4: This is the team's strongest aspect. The engineering page gives a limitation-response-evidence-next test table and the cycles are real: a one-body column became six clamped detachable cartridges so pairs could be eluted separately; a hot-end nozzle was replaced by a bench syringe and 27 G needle after it proved wrong for room-temperature hydrogel; strands that floated or stuck in the CaCl2 bath led to a 2% alginate + 10% sucrose ink printed under 0.22% CaCl2. The protein workflow has the same shape - unassembled fragments and a 35-residue linker contig produced an extended ribbon and a pLDDT 42.9 refold, which created explicit site-assembly, compactness and confidence gates (Protein Design, checkpoints 01-04). What keeps it off 5 is that almost none of the redesigns were validated against a quantified success criterion: the sucrose change has no matched comparison, printed line width versus commanded path is unmeasured, and the cartridge has no leakage or pressure data.
justification.a5: Seven named consultations, each with a recorded change: Chau and Dr Wong fixed the feed on a dissolved stream, DreamTec's cabinet led to the enclosure, Dr Kwong's advice produced the sucrose ink and bench-syringe arrangement, and Prof. Sze's analytical-quality questions produced a plan for matrix blanks and detection limits (Human Practices, Project Decisions). The Grand APIC exchange brought back two concrete questions on channelling and cell containment that are visibly carried into the containment plans. It is reflective and responsive on the technical side; it is thinner on the responsible side - no engagement with recycling workers, regulators or the communities near recycling operations, and site visits (T-PARK, CLP) are closer to education than to practices that shaped the project.
justification.a6: The attributions page gives each of the six schools a task list, names individual students with their specific roles, and separates school supervision from technical advice (Dr Kwong, Dr Nelson Lai, Solar Trinity Science as sponsor-consultant). The AI tool declaration is unusually complete and honest - RFdiffusion3/ProteinMPNN/AlphaFold for design, Cursor/Grok/Codex for wiki and code, NanoBanana and Google Flow for illustrations - with the team taking responsibility for scientific interpretation. It is short of 5 because there is no who-did-what matrix at the level of individual experiments, DNA synthesis and the Sanger service are not stated as outsourced or in-house, and the weight of CodeLifeAI's training and workflow in the protein design is hard to size from the page.
justification.a7: Eighteen entries are published under HK League (2026): six cargo CDS parts and twelve complete plasmids, with the cargo deliberately entered separately from the vector so another team can drop it into its own cassette (Parts, "A coding entry is the cargo plus its first stop"). The two architectures - T7/ompA on pTYB21 and lac/LacZa on pUC19 - are a genuine modularity decision rather than decoration, and the design is synthetic biology at its core rather than hardware with biology attached. I could not reach parts.igem.org from my environment (403), so the Registry entries' own content is unverified by me; no RFC10/RFC1000 assembly compatibility is claimed anywhere.
justification.a8: On the wiki the documentation is excellent and traceable: plasmid maps with annotated features, Sanger arcs with per-read identity and coverage figures, full FASTA downloads for every cargo and plasmid, assay calibration equations and R2 values, individual per-preparation readings rather than only means, and STL files for the cartridges. The handbook judges parts on the Registry, not the wiki, and I was unable to open any of the 18 Registry pages to check annotation, host, rationale and characterisation, so I score what I can verify and mark the Registry depth as unconfirmed. The missing protocols page is a real gap - methods are scattered across the six experiment pages instead.
justification.w1: After the home page and Description I can state the aim, the feed, the chassis, the parts and the five-step chain without hunting: designed binding proteins for Ni, Co and Li, expressed in E. coli, immobilised in calcium alginate, packed into a printed six-stage cartridge, tested on a mixed aqueous solution. The "Our approach" and "Evidence" cards on the home page each name a result and link to the page that holds it, close to the Lambert_GA pattern. It loses half a point because the headline cards state outcomes more confidently than the results pages do - "beads bound the target metals" and "a band at the size of its metal-binding protein" are both softened once you open the page.
justification.w2: Most main claims are backed by data I can inspect: plate photographs, CFU curves with range bars, a resistance-ratio table, the eluate-plate table with positive and uninoculated controls, nickel and cobalt tables giving every individual absorbance and concentration, and the cartridge table with a water control. Unusually for a high school wiki, the limits are written next to the numbers - that 35 of 36 ampicillin counts were under 30 colonies, that lithium equivalents are extrapolated, that separate elution is a handling step and not a selectivity measurement. Short of 5 because the key comparison lacks a matched control (no plasmid-free high-viscosity beads), the cartridge rests on one run, and the blot cannot support protein-level expression of the six designs.
justification.w3: The menu groups pages into Project, Science, Engineering, Impact, Team and Resources, each experiment has a matching results page, and "Related pages" footers make the path through the project easy to follow. Against that, six standard pages return 404 - proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, protocols, inclusivity and sustainability - and a judge going straight to Proof of Concept or Implementation, as many will, finds nothing; the material exists but only under team-chosen names such as Metal Recovery System. The scroll-driven home page is heavy, though a reduce-motion control and text descriptions of the 3D views are provided.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: full sequences and FASTA files, plasmid maps, printable STLs, calibration equations, bead casting ratios and elution volumes, and a Contribution page that pairs each reusable item with a "before reusing" caveat (verify sealing and bead retention; conductivity is not a lithium-specific assay). That honest framing is more useful than a longer wiki would be. The notebook, however, is one linked file and 370 words, and there is no protocols page, so day-to-day sequence and troubleshooting history has to be inferred from the experiment pages.
justification.w5: Method references are real and checkable - RFdiffusion3, ProteinMPNN (Dauparas 2022, Science 378:49-56), AlphaFold (Jumper 2021, Nature 596:583-589), Yu 2014 on ECF Ni/Co transporter specificity - and the IEA figures on the Description page are attributed to specific IEA assessments rather than floated as facts. Prior iGEM work is cited and used rather than name-dropped: BIT-China 2024 for competing-ion comparison, Fudan 2024 for uptake versus sorption, Waterloo 2020 for packed columns, with explicit statements about what is not transferable. Hardware and the results pages carry few citations, and AI-generated illustrations are declared only collectively on the attributions page rather than in the captions where they appear.

J2.one_line: A wide, well-integrated and unusually honest project - de novo designed proteins through Registry parts, beads, a converted bioprinter and a cartridge that was actually run - held back from the top by the one thing it never shows: that the designed protein, rather than the alginate, binds the metal.
strengths: A genuinely connected chain, each link evidenced on its own page: six designed cargos, 18 Registry entries, twelve verified transformations with 27 Sanger reads, alginate beads, and a printed six-stage cartridge that completed a load, wash and imidazole elution (Engineering; Metal Recovery System).

Real DBTL with redesign driven by observation, not troubleshooting: one-body column to six detachable clamped cartridges; hot-end nozzle to bench syringe and 27 G needle; floating and adhering strands in the CaCl2 bath to a 2% alginate + 10% sucrose ink under 0.22% CaCl2 (Engineering cycle table).

Measurement discipline rare at high school level: three independent preparations per bead condition, every individual absorbance published, OLS calibration lines with R2 given, a distilled-water control run through the cartridge, and eluate plating with positive and uninoculated controls (Metal Binding Assay; Alginate Bead Formation).

Design iterations are documented as failures with their fixes - unassembled fragments, a 35-residue linker contig that returned an extended ribbon, and an early refold at pLDDT 42.9 that created explicit confidence and compactness gates (Protein Design, checkpoints 01-04).

Modularity designed for reuse: the cargo CDS is deposited separately from the twelve complete plasmids so another team can use its own cassette, and each cargo exists in both T7/ompA and lac/LacZa contexts (Parts).

Human Practices with traceable consequences - the feed was narrowed to a dissolved stream, the enclosure was added after DreamTec, the sucrose ink came from Dr Kwong, and Prof. Sze's analytical-quality questions produced a named plan for matrix blanks and detection limits (Human Practices, Project Decisions).

Safety is treated as work rather than a form: BSC handling, 121 C / 25 min autoclaving of beads and bioink, EPD-licensed collection of metal waste, and a six-position surface swab screen with positive and negative controls before Jamboree transport, with its own limits stated (Safety and Security).

The wiki repeatedly states what its data cannot support - that separate elution is handling and not selectivity, that resistance ratio is not plasmid retention, that conductivity is not lithium-specific. That discipline makes the whole record more trustworthy.
weaknesses: The plasmid-free TOP10 control exists only for low-viscosity CP2 beads, while every lead result is high-viscosity (e.g. 7.64 +/- 1.30 mg/L nickel for HV pGM-T7-NiCP2). With no matched high-viscosity plasmid-free control, the headline binding and the HV > LV effect cannot be separated from the alginate itself.
No protein-level evidence of binding anywhere: no purified protein, no isolated binding measurement, no metal-free or scrambled-sequence construct. Everything rests on whole cells in gel.

The anti-OmpA immunoblot detects OmpA, which every E. coli has; the band in all six lanes does not establish expression of the six designed proteins, and the home page's "a band at the size of its metal-binding protein" is stronger than the blot supports. The figure is also noted as contrast-enhanced for display.

Lithium is conductivity extrapolated far above the top standard (1.104 mS/cm versus samples of 1.56-3.11), yet the home page still leads with "199.5 mg L-1 lithium equivalent". The team flags the extrapolation on the results page; the headline does not.

The cartridge result is one run. Cobalt eluted at 117 mg/L against a 100 mg/L feed with no mass balance, no breakthrough or wash fractions measured, and no cross-metal composition, so the 18.2 / 23.4 / 16.8% figures describe where metal was collected, not recovery or selectivity.

Hardware is demonstrated but not measured: no printed line width against the commanded path, no repeatability, no cartridge leakage or pressure data. The handbook's test for hardware - measurements - is not met for the printer.

Six standard pages return 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, protocols, inclusivity, sustainability). The content largely exists under team-chosen names, but judges are not required to hunt for it.
The notebook is a single linked file of around 370 words and there is no protocols page, so the day-by-day record a future team would want is missing even though the experiment pages are good.
The three software tools and the printed-part sources live in external repositories, which cannot be judged; what is on the wiki is description and screenshots.

I could not open any of the 18 claimed Registry pages (parts.igem.org returned 403 from my environment), so the Registry documentation depth that aspect 8 is supposed to rest on is unverified by me and should be checked by a judge with access.
red_flags: Home-page summary cards state outcomes more strongly than the underlying results pages ("Beads bound the target metals", "a band at the size of its metal-binding protein"). Not an integrity issue - the caveats are present one click away - but the first impression overstates the evidence.
The anti-OmpA blot is described as "contrast enhanced for display". Declared, and routine practice, but it is an evidence figure and I would ask to see the unenhanced membrane in Q&A.

Extensive AI tool use is declared (RFdiffusion3/ProteinMPNN/AlphaFold for design; Cursor, Grok and Codex for wiki and code; NanoBanana and Google Flow for illustrations). The declaration is exemplary and the evidence figures appear to be the team's own plots and photographs; the AI-made illustrations are credited collectively on the attributions page rather than in individual captions, which would be better practice.
Whether DNA synthesis and Sanger sequencing were in-house or outsourced is not stated. Not an accusation - most high school teams buy both - but aspect 6 would be firmer if the page said so.
pages_read: attempted: parts.igem.org pages for BBa_26GVBXIZ, BBa_26UG9UME, BBa_265LOJU4 - all returned HTTP 403 from this environment, not verified

calibrated.changed: w3 4.0->3.5: six standard pages 404 including proof-of-concept and implementation, which is the level I scored 3.5 elsewhere. a6 4.0 stands — per-school and per-student task lists plus a full AI declaration is genuinely in the top band.

justification.a1: The chain runs the whole way: six de novo metal-binding proteins (RFdiffusion3/ProteinMPNN, Protein Model page), twelve plasmids, transformation in two hosts, calcium-alginate immobilisation, a converted syringe bioprinter, and a printed six-stage cartridge that completed one mixed Ni/Co/Li load, wash and imidazole elution (Engineering; Results/3D Modeling and 3D Printing). That is a lot of scope for a six-school high school consortium, with hardware, software and education layered on. It falls short of a 5 because the step that would make the story elegant - evidence that the designed binding sites, rather than biomass or gel, do the capturing - is the one step not closed.
justification.a2: There is real measured data: eight bead conditions per metal, three independent preparations each, with calibration fits and a plasmid-free TOP10 reference (nickel 0.11 vs 7.64 +/- 1.30 mg/L for HV pGM-T7-NiCP2; cobalt 0.21 vs 8.72 +/- 2.45 mg/L/g), and a cartridge run with a distilled-water control (Results/Metal Binding Assay; Results/3D Modeling and 3D Printing). But the only no-protein control is a single low-viscosity preparation while every lead is high-viscosity, the T7-vs-lac comparison confounds host, promoter, vector and leader (stated by the team), lithium is a non-specific conductivity reading extrapolated 2-3x beyond its 10 mmol/L calibration, and expression rests on an anti-OmpA blot, an antibody against a native E. coli protein, not against the cargo. Function is therefore preliminary with weak controls.
justification.a3: The target is well chosen and grounded: Mr Charles Chau (Chase Solar) and Dr Bing Wong both pushed the team onto a dissolved aqueous stream rather than whole batteries, and the Description page sets this against hydrometallurgy and bioleaching with IEA figures (Human Practices; Description). The cartridge is a credible format for that stream and the team names its limits - laboratory-prepared solutions, not leachate, no pH window or prefiltration yet, no cross-metal composition (Human Practices, Project decisions). A 4 would need a test in something closer to the real matrix.
justification.a4: The Engineering page opens with a limitation / response / evidence / next-test table and then carries three genuine loops: a single-body column that could not be eluted stage by stage became six clamped detachable cartridges that were printed and run; a hot-end nozzle unsuited to room-temperature hydrogel became a bench syringe and 27 G needle; and strands that floated or stuck in the calcium bath led to 2% alginate with 10% sucrose under 0.22% CaCl2. Each Learn step visibly changed the next Build, and the pending tests (line width vs commanded path, leakage and pressure, fraction composition) are named. No comparable loop exists on the biology - no protein was redesigned in response to data - which keeps it below 5.
justification.a5: Several design changes are traceable to named people: the cabinet-style enclosure after seeing enclosed professional equipment at DreamTec, the bench-syringe arrangement and sucrose ink after Dr Keith Kwong (CodeLifeAI), per-metal modular cartridges and a dissolved feed after Mr Chau and Dr Bing Wong, and an analytical-quality agenda (matrix blanks, cell-free alginate blank, detection limits) from Prof. Sze Tung Po at CUHK. The team also brought two questions back from Grand APIC about flow paths and cell retention in gel and tied them to the eluate plates (Human Practices). It is a 4 rather than a 5 because several consequences are still plans, and the CLP centre, T-PARK, radio and ecology items are outreach rather than an exchange with the project.
justification.a6: The Attributions page gives a per-school breakdown of tasks (CIS: bioprinting, plasmid design, western blot, cell counts; WFN: transformation, expression, protein design, 3D printing; HTS: metal-binding assay and blot) plus named individual roles, supervisors by school, and named external advisers including a sponsor. AI tool use is disclosed unusually fully - RFdiffusion/ProteinMPNN/AlphaFold for design, Cursor, Grok and Codex for wiki and software, NanoBanana and Google Flow for figures - with the team taking responsibility for interpretation. It is short of 5 because the individual list covers only a handful of the students shown on the Team page, and advisers are credited with "assay optimisation and protocol troubleshooting", so who held the pipette for the blot and the cartridge run is still a session question rather than an accusation.
justification.a7: Six de novo coding sequences and twelve complete plasmids are listed with lengths, GC content and FASTA links, in two deliberately different cassettes - T7-ompA on pTYB21 and lac-LacZalpha on pUC19 - so the same cargo can be used in either translation context (Parts; DNA Design). The open-source BioPrintCAD toolpath app and the printed cartridge geometry act as further standard components (Contribution). The design is clearly built on synthetic biology, but because passenger-specific expression and binding are unconfirmed, the new parts are contributed as designs with suggestive rather than established function.
justification.a8: The Parts page lists eighteen Registry entries with part numbers, type, length, maps and FASTA, and the DNA Model page reports 27 Sanger reads covering every coding region. On the wiki the documentation is excellent: individual absorbances per preparation, bead masses, calibration equations and R2 values are all tabulated (Results/Metal Binding Assay; Experiments/Metal Binding Assay). I could not reach parts.igem.org during judging (403), so I could not confirm how much of the characterisation lives on the Registry rather than only on the wiki; by the parts rule that caps this at 3.5 until the session clarifies.
justification.w1: The home page gives the problem, the approach and the five-step chain in a few lines, with a schematic and milestone cards that link straight to the result page behind each claim. The Description page then builds the context with IEA figures and cathode compositions without losing the thread back to "separation after dissolution". A reader knows within a screen what was designed, what was built and what was measured.
justification.w2: Claims are tied to tables with units, n and SD, individual preparation readings are shown alongside the means, and the team repeatedly separates what was measured from what is planned ("Separation performance remains to be validated"; "Values are extrapolated estimates"). The cartridge run carries a distilled-water control and shows the arithmetic from concentration to percentage of feed. Marks are held back for the control-design gaps (one plasmid-free condition, wrong alginate grade), the conductivity extrapolation, and a stated 10 mL eluent on the experiment page against 20 mL in the cartridge run.
justification.w3: Navigation maps onto the judging criteria - Project, Science (with Experiments and Results paired page by page), Engineering, Impact, Team, Resources - and every result page carries "Related pages" back to its method and parts. Nothing important is buried off the standard pages; the extra pages are reached in one click from Results or Experiments. It is long, but each page earns its place rather than repeating the others.
justification.w4: Experiment pages give concentrations, volumes, wash times, calibration equations and instrument models, the Downloads page carries the STL files for both cartridge housings, and the Contribution page is written as a set of starting points with explicit "before you reuse this" caveats - an unusually generous record. Against that, the Notebook page is one linked file of protein-design notes only, with no wet-lab day book, and BioPrintCAD, Westbend and GeneCraft live in off-wiki repositories that cannot be judged. A future team could repeat the beads and the cartridge, but would have to reconstruct the wet-lab chronology.
justification.w5: The Description and Protein Model pages carry numbered references that resolve to real sources (Harper 2019, Larouche 2020, Sethurajan 2021, Lee and Mooney 2012, IEA 2024/2025; RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, AlphaFold) and the claims match what those sources say. Prior iGEM work is acknowledged by team and year - BIT-China 2024, Waterloo 2020, Fudan 2024 - and AI figure tools are disclosed on the Attributions page. Lapses: the illustrative figures are not credited one by one at the point of use, and the Hardware and Human Practices pages carry little citation of their own.

J3.one_line: An ambitious six-school chain from de novo metal-binding proteins to a printed six-stage cartridge, documented with unusual honesty about its limits - but the central question, whether the designed proteins rather than the biomass do the binding, is not yet answered by the controls.
