strengths: Complete, operated chain: six designed proteins, twelve plasmids, alginate beads and a printed six-stage cartridge that took one mixed Ni/Co/Li feed through load, wash and imidazole elution (Engineering; Results/3D Modeling and 3D Printing).
Quantitative bead assay with three independent preparations per condition, published calibration fits, individual readings and a plasmid-free TOP10 reference (Results/Metal Binding Assay).

Three documented engineering loops in which an observed failure changed the next build: one-body column to detachable stack, hot end to bench syringe, floating strand to 2% alginate with 10% sucrose (Engineering).

Stakeholder advice with visible consequences - DreamTec's enclosed printer led to the cabinet enclosure, Dr Kwong's advice to the sucrose ink and bench syringe, Chau and Wong to the dissolved-stream focus (Human Practices).

Exceptionally disciplined writing: resistance ratio is called a plated phenotype not plasmid retention, pair elution is called a handling step not selectivity, lithium equivalents are labelled extrapolated, and the low-colony-count caveat is volunteered by the team itself.

Safety work that is actually evidenced: autoclave conditions, EPD-licensed metal waste collection, and six swab positions with positive and negative controls before the Jamboree display (Safety and Security).
Thorough AI-tool disclosure and a per-school task chart on the Attributions page.
weaknesses: The only no-protein control is a single low-viscosity plasmid-free TOP10 preparation, while every lead condition is high-viscosity alginate; since grade alone changes the readings in all eight paired comparisons, the control cannot carry the claim that the designed protein is responsible.

Expression evidence is an anti-OmpA immunoblot on the induced T7 lysates. That antibody targets a native E. coli outer-membrane protein, so a band near 16-25 kDa does not establish that the cargo was made; no anti-tag blot, purification or mass check is shown.

Lithium is read only as bulk conductivity, with every engineered sample above the top standard and "equivalents" extrapolated 2-3x beyond the calibrated range; the team says so, but the lithium claims rest on it.
The cartridge result is a single run with no cross-metal analysis of each pair eluate, so the 18.2 / 23.4 / 16.8% shares describe collection, not separation - as the team acknowledges.
The eluent volume is 10 mL on the Metal Binding Assay experiment page and 20 mL in the cartridge calculation; a reader has to work out that these are different experiments.
The Notebook page is a single protein-design file with no wet-lab day book, and the three software tools live in off-wiki repositories that cannot be judged.
The individual-contributions list names only a fraction of the students shown on the Team page, so for several key tasks (the blot, the cartridge run) it is not clear which student did the work.
red_flags: Many illustrative figures were produced with AI image and animation tools (NanoBanana, Google Flow). This is disclosed on the Attributions page and the figures are conceptual, not evidentiary; the data figures are plots of tabulated readings. No integrity concern, but worth confirming at the session that no evidentiary image was AI-processed beyond the stated contrast enhancement of the blot.
The anti-OmpA blot caption says it is contrast enhanced for display; the raw membrane should be available on request.
parts.igem.org returned 403 during judging, so the depth of the eighteen Registry entries could not be verified from outside the wiki.
BioPrintCAD, Westbend and GeneCraft source are hosted off the iGEM wiki and are therefore outside what I can score.
pages_read: crawl metadata for hardware, software, education, entrepreneurship, dna-design, dna-model, downloads and the remaining experiment/results pages

calibrated.changed: none. a2 of 3 is the right place relative to the section: a single low-viscosity no-protein control against high-viscosity leads, a confounded promoter comparison and an anti-OmpA blot standing in for cargo expression mean the designed binding sites are not shown to be what binds.

one_line.en: A wide six-school chain from de novo designed proteins to an operated cartridge, written with unusual honesty about its limits, but never showing that the designed protein rather than the gel does the binding.
one_line.zh: 六校合作、從全新設計蛋白到實際運行匣體的完整鏈條，對自身限制書寫異常誠實，但始終未證明結合來自設計蛋白而非膠體。

strengths: A genuinely connected chain, each link evidenced: designed cargos, verified plasmids, beads and a printed cartridge that completed load, wash and elution
Three independent preparations per bead condition with every individual reading published and calibration fits stated
Three documented engineering loops where an observed failure changed the next build
Repeated discipline about what the data cannot support — elution called handling not selectivity, resistance called a plated phenotype, lithium called extrapolated
weaknesses: The only plasmid-free control exists for one bead grade while every lead result uses the other, so binding cannot be separated from the alginate
The immunoblot targets a native outer-membrane protein, so it cannot establish expression of the designed cargo
Lithium is read as bulk conductivity well above the top standard
The cartridge result is a single run with no mass balance, no cross-metal composition and no selectivity demonstrated

Software tools and printed-part sources live in external repositories that cannot be judged

screen.project_title: FlaminGone — a curli-amyloid bio-coating fire retardant with substrate-binding and hydrophobic domains
screen.what_they_built: A modular CsgA amyloid scaffold fused to BslA (hydrophobicity), polyethylene-binding peptide (adhesion) and AI-designed retardant peptides, applied as a two-layer coating with ammonium polyphosphate and expandable graphite to polyethylene scaffolding netting, plus PyroForge, an ESM-2-based ML tool that designed the better retardant peptide.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli K-12 and BL21(DE3), pET vectors with T7/LacO. Sixteen Registry parts including CsgA-BslA (BBa_26QZ8KBC), the dual-operon curli secretion machine (BBa_26914CJG, built on UNILausanne's BBa_K4685031), CsgA-PEbp (BBa_26EKX9DH), CsgA-BslA-PEbp (BBa_268M7GQI) and CsgA-Alp(1)-PEbp (BBa_26LGXFBV).
screen.best_evidence: /results: UL 94-style vertical burn on wood — uncoated and CsgA-only reached the 3 cm mark at 12.38 s and 13.27 s and burned out, while CsgA-BslA delayed it to 42.90 s and reached 8.5 cm at 68.00 s; binder-free APP/EG self-extinguished in 6.00 s on first flame but failed at 99.49 s on second exposure. NFPA 701 burnt distance on PE netting put software-designed Alp(2) at 8.5 cm against rationally designed Alp(1) at 10.5 cm. Arabidopsis germination on post-combustion ash extract ran 75–85% from 5% to 100% strength against a 75% DI-water control.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and it changed the target. The team started optimising raw fire retardancy; management at a major real-estate developer told them the decisive problem with halogenated retardants is toxic combustion gases (HCl, HBr, dioxins), so the project pivoted to a low-smoke, non-toxic, biodegradable coating — which is why the Arabidopsis ecotoxicity and ash-extract work exists at all.
screen.reason: Standards-anchored quantitative evidence that the engineered protein does the job (UL 94 timings, NFPA 701 burnt distances, weathering cycles to ASTM D6944, phytotoxicity dose series), sixteen parts in a genuinely modular plug-and-play architecture, five DBTL cycles with host/media/induction optimisation data, and a software tool whose designed peptide measurably beat the hand-designed one. The scope-to-evidence ratio is the best in this batch alongside HangzhouFourteenAP. Full read warranted.
screen.field_notes: HK-Joint-School (HKG, Biomanufacturing village) built FlaminGone, a sprayable bio-coating fire retardant for polyethylene construction scaffolding netting. The scaffold is E. coli curli subunit CsgA, self-assembling into amyloid nanofibrils, fused in various combinations to BslA (B. subtilis hydrophobin, weatherproofing), PEbp (polyethylene-binding peptide, adhesion) and Alp(1)/Alp(2) retardant peptides; sixteen IPTG-inducible parts are registered. Cycle 1 compared a seven-gene dual-operon secretion machine against a single T7-CsgA-BslA construct and found the simple construct in K-12 with YESCA broth and 0.5 mM IPTG gave double the yield, attributed to metabolic burden. A key engineering decision was abandoning the single-chain trifunctional fusion for a two-layer application — CsgA-PEbp bio-primer anchoring to the plastic, CsgA-BslA + APP/EG top-coat cross-linking through CsgA-CsgA fibril entanglement — because additives mixed into long fusions flake during thermal expansion. Fire data is anchored to recognised standards: UL 94-derived vertical burn on wood strips (uncoated 12.38 s to the 3 cm mark, CsgA-only 13.27 s, CsgA-BslA 42.90 s and 68.00 s to 8.5 cm; binder-free APP/EG self-extinguished at 6.00 s then failed catastrophically at 99.49 s on second flame, demonstrating why the protein binder is needed), and NFPA 701 average burnt distance on PE netting, the standard the Hong Kong Buildings Department uses for scaffolding screens. Weathering included rain washing, humidity, UV, thermal shock to ASTM D6944 (-5 to 50 C) and NaOH washing. Their ML software PyroForge uses ESM-2 sequence features to predict Tm, folding free energy and mutational stability; its redesigned peptide Alp(2) (GYRYRYRYRYRW) gave 8.5 cm burnt distance versus 10.5 cm for Alp(1), which had been designed by prompting an LLM — an unusually clean head-to-head between LLM-suggested and software-guided design. Ecotoxicity was tested with Arabidopsis thaliana germination on a 0–100% gradient of post-combustion ash extract and 12 h simulated rain runoff (75–85% germination against a 75% control). Ten named stakeholders drove a documented pivot from raw flame performance to low-smoke non-toxicity. Large model, measurement, software and education pages; the attribution page is only 87 words, and replicate counts for the burn tests are not stated in the results text.

justification.a1: The scope is unusually wide for a high school team and the results build on one another: expression optimisation across strain, medium and inducer (Results §3), UL94 wood screening (Measurement §7), NFPA 701 testing on real industrial PE scaffolding netting (Measurement §9), weathering/UV/thermal-shock durability, then Arabidopsis phytotoxicity on ash and runoff (Results §4). On top of that sit GROMACS MD simulations that diagnosed a wet-lab failure (Model, third round) and a machine-learning tool whose designed peptide was then burnt on netting (Software §8). This is close to the GreatBay_SZ pattern of increasing difficulty. It falls short of 5 because most of the measured flame suppression comes from the APP/EG additives rather than from the engineered protein itself, and the cone calorimeter run that would have quantified heat release was never completed (Measurement §8.3).
justification.a2: Function is shown against genuinely good negative controls: uncoated wood, CsgA-only protein, and binder-free water+APP/EG, with numbers in every comparison (Results §2 and §3; Measurement Tables 1-3). The PE netting assay reports three trials per formulation with individual values (4.5/5.0/4.8 cm for the two-layer system vs 13.1 cm for CsgA alone), and the IPTG table gives raw triplicates showing a clean bell-shaped dose response. Three things hold this at 4: the claim that BslA passes through CsgG and is secreted (Description; Engineering Cycle 3) is not supported by the method used, since the extraction protocol mechanically lyses whole cells and so cannot separate secreted from intracellular protein; the 2.10 vs 0.90 microgram/microlitre yields rest on eyeballed band intensity rather than densitometry, and the gel I examined (result-figure5) is faint enough that I cannot see the stated difference; and no group anywhere carries error bars or a statistical test, with some burn groups at n=2.
justification.a3: The impact case was built from stakeholder contact rather than assumed. The SHKP interview demolished the team's original premise (nets cost about HKD40 a roll, the market is shrinking to metal scaffolding, and the developer would not spray anything onto their own nets for liability reasons), and the team recorded that honestly and pivoted the selling point to non-toxicity and low smoke (Human Practices, Phase 1 Market Research). Testing then happened on actual scaffolding netting under NFPA 701, the standard the Hong Kong Buildings Department accepts, plus simulated rain and runoff phytotoxicity, which is a real-world-like setting. It stops short of 5 because the cost analysis Prof. Yuen specifically asked for was never produced, and the low-smoke, low-toxicity claim that became the whole selling point has no measurement behind it: both the cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR work is listed as unfinished.
justification.a4: Cycle 5 on the Engineering page is a complete DBTL loop of the kind I look for: MD simulation predicted weak inter-layer CsgA-CsgA junctions, the first wet-lab flame test showed Layer 2 peeling off Layer 1, a literature search identified alkaline electrostatic repulsion between CsgA fibres, the NaOH pre-treatment was removed from the protocol, and retesting at neutral pH gave the project's best char length of 4.8 cm. Cycle 4 likewise turned an observed failure (graphite expansion prying the coating off) into the two-layer redesign. The software has its own documented iterations, including a data-leakage fix that honestly dropped the reported correlation from 0.85 to 0.46 and a sign-inversion bug that had been ranking the most destabilising mutations first (Software §6). Measures of success were set in advance as published standard thresholds. Not a 5 because Cycles 1 and 2 read more as screening and optimisation than as redesign driven by a failed prediction.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the project and reaches the GreatBay_SZ bar of human practices informing the design itself. Ten named engagements are documented, and I can trace a specific design change to most of them: SHKP moved the project from fire retardancy to non-toxicity; Prof. Guan Yeoh contributed both the APP/EG intumescent chemistry and the split into a two-layer system, which became the final architecture; Prof. Yuen supplied the testing standards and the weathering-chamber idea that was then built from a storage bin and UV tubes; Prof. Joshua Ho's suggestion of a head-to-head comparison produced the S669 benchmark in Software §4.4. The exchange runs both ways and includes feedback the team did not want to hear, which they report rather than bury.
justification.a6: The attributions page (2026.igem.wiki/hk-joint-school/attribution) is completely empty, which I confirmed on the live site, and that is precisely where the handbook now puts this information. The team-members page assigns roles only at the level of six schools (Measurement, Wet-lab, Software, Model, Education, Wiki), never to a person or a task. What credit I can give comes from scattered honesty elsewhere: the model acknowledgements state plainly that advisor Mr Leung Chung Ki built the polyethylene layer, extended the Amber14SB force field and ran the umbrella sampling that produced the binding free energies; plasmids are declared as ordered from Twist Bioscience; the cone calorimeter is declared as run at PolyU. But PyroForge is a production-grade Dockerised ML service with Zenodo DOIs, Celery queues and a 226-respondent user test, and nothing on the wiki tells me which students built any of it. I cannot assemble the picture that TAS Taipei gave through its figure captions and attributions page.
justification.a7: Sixteen parts are contributed to the Registry: six IPTG-inducible T7/LacO/RBS composite constructs built on the CsgA curli scaffold with swappable terminal domains, plus a ten-member PE-binding peptide basic-part library (Parts page; Contribution §2). Prior iGEM work is reused and credited, with the dual-operon secretion construct BBa_26914CJG built on UNILausanne 2023's BBa_K4685031 as a reference framework. A new part (the PyroForge-optimised Alp(2) fusion) sits alongside reuse of existing ones, which is the TAS Taipei pattern. Half a point off because the ten PEbp entries are sequence-only predictions with no experimental characterisation, and because the measured fire performance leans heavily on inorganic APP/EG rather than on the engineered biology.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely good: part-by-part genetic architecture tables, protocols with supplier catalogue numbers, raw trial values rather than only means, MD run parameters detailed enough to reproduce, and code, training data and model weights archived under Zenodo DOIs (Software §7). The Registry itself is where I must judge parts, and parts.igem.org returned 403 to me throughout, so I could not confirm what sits on those sixteen entries; the team's own Parts page carries no per-part characterisation, controls or sequence features, which usually mirrors a thin Registry page, and I have scored on that assumption while flagging it. Against this, the attributions page is blank, safety lives at /safety rather than the standard slug, and two different PEbp sequences (BBa_26FNXNXW and BBa_26OKJ6Y6) are both given a binding score of -25.4, which looks like a copy-paste error.
justification.w1: The Description page opens with an abstract that states the problem, the construct, the software and the outcome in one paragraph, and the problem-to-solution chain is easy to follow from there. The home page, though, is 94 words: a logo carousel, the line "iGEM 2026 team" and a list of links, with no statement of what FlaminGone is or what it achieved. A judge or a visitor landing on the front door learns nothing within one screen and has to click through to Description, which is exactly the test the Lambert_GA example sets.
justification.w2: Most key claims are backed by a figure or a data table with real controls, and I value that the team published raw per-trial numbers (NFPA 701 char lengths, IPTG dry masses in triplicate) rather than only summary bars. The gels are labelled by lane, include negative-control and BSA-standard lanes, and are visibly unretouched. What keeps this off 4.5 is the measurement detail: the DNA and protein ladders carry no per-band size marks, protein quantification is described as "visual band intensity", no plot anywhere carries error bars or a stated n in its legend, the phytotoxicity assay appears to be a single dish of 20 seeds per concentration, and the Results page reframes the NaOH experiment as a deliberate durability test that "perfectly validates" the MD prediction when the Engineering page makes clear it was an unexpected failure diagnosed afterwards.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly (Team, Project, Lab, Engagement) and every long page carries a numbered table of contents, which makes a 9,000-word Measurement page navigable. Friction costs it half a point in each direction: the attributions and team pages sit at non-standard slugs (/attribution, /team-members) with the attributions page empty, safety sits at /safety rather than /safety-and-security, and Measurement spends four full sections on coating methods the team decided not to use before reaching the one they adopted, which is sprawl rather than completeness.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this. Protocols carry supplier catalogue numbers, buffer compositions and centrifugation settings; the MD sections give force field, thermostat, barostat, cutoffs and run lengths; code is on iGEM GitLab under Apache 2.0 with data and weights on Zenodo under DOIs. Failures are recorded rather than hidden, including the Layer 2 flaking, Alp(2) losing to BslA, the Apple MPS embedding collapse and the unfinished cone calorimeter. Two gaps stop it reaching 5: the notebook is a 355-word phase timeline with no dated entries behind it, and with no attributions a future reader cannot tell which parts of the work were student-executed.
justification.w5: Each page ends with a numbered reference list in a consistent style with DOIs or resolvable links, prior iGEM work is credited by part number (UNILausanne 2023's BBa_K4685031), expert input is quoted with name and title, and the computational tools and training datasets are cited to their primary papers (AlphaFold 3, GROMACS, LINCS, ESM-2, Meltome Atlas, Tsuboyama 2023, Bondi 1964). Deductions are small: a Scribd upload is used as the flammability reference for polyethylene, the Liu 2014 reference is duplicated as entries 3 and 5 on the Model page, and the Our World in Data wildfire figures on the Description page are credited in the caption but never tied to a numbered reference.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete high school project: real controls and raw numbers across two fire standards, a genuine MD-to-wet-lab-to-protocol-change DBTL loop, and outstanding human practices, undercut by a completely blank attributions page that leaves me unable to tell who did the work.
strengths: Proper negative controls throughout the fire testing (uncoated substrate, CsgA-only protein, binder-free water+APP/EG), so the contribution of each component is separable rather than asserted - Results sections 2 and 3

Raw per-trial data published rather than only means: three individual NFPA 701 char lengths per formulation and triplicate dry masses across five IPTG concentrations showing a clean bell-shaped response (result-table-4)

Engineering Cycle 5 is a complete DBTL loop where a prediction, a failure and a literature finding changed the protocol: MD predicted weak inter-layer CsgA junctions, the coating flaked, alkaline repulsion was identified, the NaOH pre-treatment was dropped, and char length fell to 4.8 cm

Human practices that visibly steered the science: SHKP redirected the project from fire retardancy to non-toxicity, Prof. Guan Yeoh contributed both the intumescent additives and the two-layer architecture that became the final design, and Prof. Joshua Ho's suggestion produced the S669 external benchmark

Failures and negative results are reported rather than hidden - the two-layer system initially losing to the single chain, Alp(2) being beaten by BslA, the data-leakage fix that lowered the reported model correlation from 0.85 to 0.46, and the cone calorimeter that did not finish before the freeze

Reproducibility is taken seriously: protocols with supplier catalogue numbers, full MD run parameters, code on iGEM GitLab under Apache 2.0, and datasets and model weights archived on Zenodo with DOIs
weaknesses: The attributions page is live but completely empty, and the team-members page divides work only among six schools, never among people or tasks - so for an exceptionally sophisticated software and modelling effort I cannot establish how much the students did themselves

The claim that BslA passes through the CsgG channel and is secreted is not supported by the method used: the extraction protocol mechanically lyses whole cells, so Congo Red staining and SDS-PAGE of the resulting pellet cannot distinguish secreted from intracellular protein

Protein yields of 2.10 vs 0.90 micrograms per microlitre rest on visually estimated band intensity rather than densitometry, and on the published gel those bands are faint enough that the stated difference is not apparent

No error bars, standard deviations on the wiki plots, or statistical tests anywhere in the lab results, with some burn-test groups at n=2 and the phytotoxicity assay apparently one dish of 20 seeds per concentration

Low smoke and low toxicity became the project's selling point after the SHKP interview, but neither was measured: the cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR work is listed as incomplete, and the cost analysis Prof. Yuen requested never appeared

The Results page presents the NaOH experiment as a deliberate durability test that 'perfectly validates' the MD prediction, while the Engineering page makes clear it was an unexpected failure explained after the fact - the same data told two different ways

Non-standard page locations (/attribution, /team-members, /safety) plus a 94-word home page that states nothing about the project, and a Measurement page that spends four sections on coating methods the team rejected
red_flags: No academic integrity concern found; I am not referring anything to the RCC. The gels are visibly unretouched with scratches and staining artefacts left in, which is the opposite of cleaned evidentiary figures, and the AI-generated peptide Alp(1) is openly labelled as Gemini-generated and then tested rather than presented as a measured result.

Routine safety question for safety@igem.org, not a judgement of mine: the Safety page states the strains are RG1 (DH5alpha, K-12 W3110, BL21(DE3)) but that the laboratories are classified BSL-2 and 'all procedures were carried out under Biosafety Level 2 containment'. For a High School team the whitelist excludes BSL-2 and higher work, so I would ask the safety committee to confirm this is RG1 work performed in a BSL-2-rated room rather than BSL-2 work.

Parts must be judged on the Registry, and parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403 to every request I made, so I could not inspect any of the sixteen claimed entries. My a8 score rests on the wiki's own part documentation with that caveat, and should be revisited if the Registry pages are reachable.

Two different PE-binding peptide sequences (BBa_26FNXNXW, GFRHRIFWQHWW, and BBa_26OKJ6Y6, DWMWRREFFMHR) are both listed with an identical reported binding score of -25.4 on the Parts and Contribution pages, which looks like a transcription error in the library table.

Modelled results are kept distinct from measured ones throughout, which I checked specifically: the MD free energies are labelled as simulation, the PyroForge outputs as predictions, and the peptide comparison is settled by a physical burn test. No modelled figure is presented as experimental data.
Presentation not assessed, per the brief - the videos are not visible to this panel. Aspect 9 left blank as it belongs to the Judging Session.
pages_read: attribution (at /attribution, confirmed empty on the live site)
figures inspected directly: result-figure3 (diagnostic digest gel), result-figure5 (SDS-PAGE), result-table-4 (IPTG triplicates)
parts.igem.org Registry pages for BBa_26QZ8KBC, BBa_26EKX9DH, BBa_26CC4C9Q - all returned HTTP 403, not assessable

calibrated.changed: none. a6 2.5 is the floor I apply to a blank attributions page with only school-level role assignment, and here an advisor is separately recorded as having built the polyethylene layer and run the umbrella sampling, so the deduction is evidenced rather than inferred.

justification.a1: FlaminGone chains a long sequence of increasingly hard steps and finishes most of them: six IPTG-inducible constructs expressed in E. coli K-12, expression optimised across strain/medium/inducer, UL94 screening on wood, then modified NFPA 701 on real industrial PE scaffolding netting down to 4.8 cm char, DIY UV/moisture/thermal weathering, Arabidopsis ecotoxicity, GROMACS MD with umbrella-sampling free energies, and a deployed, externally benchmarked ML tool (PyroForge, Software p.4.4). That breadth with this much measured data is close to GreatBay-level scope for a high school team. It falls short of a 5 because the two instrument-grade tests that would settle the fire claims (cone calorimeter, TGA-FTIR, Measurement 8.3 and 11.2) returned no results, and char density was never measured as Prof. Yeoh advised.
justification.a2: The main function is shown with real controls and replicates: Results Fig.2-3 digests, Congo Red pellets (Fig.4), SDS-PAGE F+/F- against a BSA standard (Fig.5), and NFPA 701 on PE netting with n=3 per formulation against CsgA-only (13.1 cm), binder-free APP/EG (11.4 cm) and the two-layer system (4.8 cm, trials 4.5/5.0/4.8). UL94 vertical shows 1.00 s self-extinguishment after both flame applications versus total burnout for uncoated and CsgA-only controls. Against that, yield is quantified by visual band intensity rather than a protein assay (~2.10 vs ~0.90 ug/uL), the Cycle 2 adhesion claim ("resisted mechanical detachment") has no figure or number behind it, the germination control is reported as 75% in one paragraph and 85% in the next (Results 4c/4d), and the ecotoxicity assay appears to be one 20-seed plate per concentration with no replicate dishes.
justification.a3: The route to use is concrete and stakeholder-tested rather than asserted. SHKP told them scaffolding nets cost ~HKD40/roll, that fire performance is not the industry's priority, and that contractors would not spray a coating themselves for liability reasons; the team moved the selling point to non-toxicity and the application point to net manufacturers (HP, SHKP section). They test against NFPA 701, the standard the HK Buildings Department actually accepts for scaffolding screens (PNRC85), and report the 15.2 cm pass threshold. It is not a 5 because no cost analysis was produced despite two experts naming cost as the deciding constraint, and nothing was tested on an actual site.
justification.a4: Five cycles each have test data that change the next build. Cycle 1 drops the seven-gene operon construct on yield data; Cycle 4 blends APP/EG and observes flaking; Cycle 5 splits into the two-layer system, the first flame test unexpectedly loses to the single chain, the team traces the flaking to residual NaOH from their own net pre-treatment via curli pH literature, removes the wash, retests at pH 7 and reaches 4.8 cm. The MD work earns its place here: the inter-layer CsgA-CsgA simulation predicted weak cross-beta junctions before the wet lab saw delamination, and the modelling team fed the revised protocol back (Model, fourth round). Success is quantified throughout in char length and self-extinguishment time. Short of 5 only because the char-quality criterion Prof. Yeoh set (>1 mm, high density, SEM) was never measured, so the mechanism behind the best result is argued rather than verified.
justification.a5: Ten documented engagements plus a 174-respondent survey, each written up with a reflection and a traceable consequence: Prof. Yuen set the testing standards and durability approach; SHKP redirected the value proposition and the point of application; Prof. Ruan set the toxicology endpoints; Prof. Chan raised heat denaturation, which created PyroForge; Prof. Yeoh produced the APP/EG additives and the two-layer architecture that became the final design; Mr Lee produced the three-chamber substitute for an industrial weathering chamber, with his limitations quoted; Mr Wong produced sonication for Z-DNA and the Arabidopsis assay; Prof. Ho produced the S669 head-to-head benchmark. This is responsive HP in the p.21-22 sense, not outreach relabelled. It stops short of 5 because several commitments made to experts (cytotoxicity on lung and skin cell lines, 120-day degradation half-life) remain plans.
justification.a6: This is the weak point. The standard /attributions URL 404s and the team's own "Attribution" page in the navigation renders with no content at all (I checked the live page: 87 words, all navigation and footer), so there is no who-did-what form of the kind p.25-26 asks for and p.26 of the handbook treats as the record. The Team Members page assigns work only at school level (Measurement, Software/Wet-lab, Model, Education, Wiki). Meanwhile outside contributions are visible in passing: the Model acknowledgements state "our advisor has assisted us in performing umbrella sampling", the binding free energies that support the Model conclusions, and PolyU is to run the cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR. None of that is an integrity concern and all of it is openly stated, but with no attribution form I cannot tell how much of the lab, modelling and software execution was student work, and that is exactly what this aspect asks.
justification.a7: Synthetic biology is the core of the project, not decoration: curli display with fused functional domains, six composite constructs with the architecture spelled out (T7-LacO-RBS-CsgA-linker-domain) and a ten-member PEbp basic-part library, built in part on a prior iGEM part, BBa_K4685031 from UNILausanne 2023, which is credited. The modular swap-the-binding-domain framing is a genuine reuse design, and PyroForge adds a software contribution with an iGEM Registry homology search built in. Short of 5 because nine of the ten PEbp parts are deposited sequences "expected to bind" with only a computed binding score and no experiment, and no RFC10/RFC1000 assembly compatibility is stated anywhere.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is genuinely rebuildable: Experiments gives staged protocols with supplier catalogue numbers, Measurement explains every protocol modification and why school conditions forced it, and Software lists weights and datasets on Zenodo with DOIs. The Parts page, however, gives each part only a description, architecture string and functional role, with no characterisation data attached to the part entries, and nine PEbp parts carry nothing but a binding score. I could not reach parts.igem.org in this session (403 from the CDN on four part numbers), so Registry depth is unverified rather than judged poor; under the p.18 Registry-only rule I cannot credit the wiki data toward the part pages. The empty attribution page also counts against project-component documentation.
justification.w1: The Description page is well built: a tight abstract, the three components with structures and reasons, the staged construct designs, and the two-layer mechanism. The home page does not do its job, though: 94 words, a photo carousel, the words "iGEM 2026 team." and a link list, with no sentence anywhere stating what FlaminGone is. A judge or visitor landing on the front page learns nothing about the project until they click through, which is the opposite of the Lambert_GA pattern.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently carried by data. Gels for every construct, SDS-PAGE with a BSA reference, UL94 vertical and horizontal tables with per-trial values, NFPA 701 with three trials per formulation and the standard's own pass threshold quoted, weathering results with percentage drops, MD distance traces with a stated 0.35 nm contact criterion, and model benchmark figures. Most impressive for evidence discipline is what they do not hide: the Software page states plainly that PyroForge-optimised Alp2 (8.5 cm) still lost to CsgA-BslA-PEbp (7.1 cm), and Engineering Cycle 5 reports the two-layer system losing its first flame test. The missing cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR data, and the internally inconsistent germination control, keep it off 5.
justification.w3: The side navigation is grouped sensibly (Team / Project / Lab / Engagement) and every page carries its own table of contents, so within the site the flow is good. The problem is at the standard URLs: /attributions, /safety-and-security, /team, /proof-of-concept, /implementation and /protocols all 404, with the content living at /attribution, /safety and /team-members instead, and the Attribution page is blank when you do reach it. Since judges are told they need not hunt (p.29), content that only exists at non-standard paths is a real cost here, and no proof-of-concept or implementation page exists at all.
justification.w4: A future team could reproduce most of this. The Experiments page is a complete protocol set from competent cell preparation through ecotoxicity, the Measurement page explains how to build UV, moisture and thermal chambers out of a storage bin, foil and a freezer when no industrial chamber exists, and records why 3D printing, Mayer rod and brushing were each rejected before soaking was chosen, which is exactly the kind of negative knowledge that usually goes unrecorded. Code is on iGEM GitLab and data and weights on Zenodo with DOIs. Against that the Notebook is a 355-word timeline of headings with no daily entries, so the day-to-day record is effectively absent.
justification.w5: Every substantive page carries a numbered IEEE-style reference list with DOIs that resolve, in-text citation is used throughout the Description, Results, Model and HP pages, and prior iGEM work is credited by part number (BBa_K4685031, UNILausanne 2023). Figure data sources are named for the wildfire charts (Global Wildfire Information System, Our World in Data, EM-DAT). I found no sign of fabricated references in the entries I checked. Weaknesses are minor rather than structural: a WHO fact sheet cited through a "Share.google" URL, a Scribd upload used as a technical source on PE flammability, one duplicated reference in the Measurement list, and most photographs and schematics carry no credit line.

J2.one_line: An unusually complete high-school project: five real DBTL cycles ending in a model-diagnosed redesign, standards-based fire testing with controls on the actual target substrate, strong responsive HP and a benchmarked software tool, badly let down by a completely empty attributions page.
strengths: Genuine model-to-bench feedback loop: MD predicted weak CsgA-CsgA inter-layer junctions, the wet lab saw the top coat flake off, literature identified alkaline repulsion, the NaOH pre-treatment was removed and the retest gave the project-best 4.8 cm char length (Engineering, 5th Cycle)

Fire testing done properly for a school lab: UL94 vertical and horizontal plus modified NFPA 701 with uncoated, CsgA-only and binder-free additive controls, n=3 trials, per-trial values reported, and results placed against the standard's own 15.2 cm pass threshold (Measurement 7.4, 9.5)

Human Practices that visibly changed the project: SHKP moved the value proposition from fire performance to non-toxicity and the application point to manufacturers; Prof. Yeoh produced both the APP/EG additives and the two-layer architecture that became the final design; Mr Lee produced the three-chamber weathering substitute, with its limitations printed

Honest negative reporting: the Software page states that PyroForge-optimised Alp2 (8.5 cm) still lost to CsgA-BslA-PEbp (7.1 cm), and Engineering records the two-layer system losing its first flame test rather than only the version that worked

PyroForge is a real tool, not a demo: ESM-2 features with three trained heads, parent-disjoint splits enforced by unit test, a documented data-leakage bug found and fixed, external S669 benchmarking added on Prof. Ho's advice, 226-user acceptance testing, code on iGEM GitLab and weights on Zenodo with DOIs
weaknesses: The attributions form is missing entirely: /attributions 404s and the linked Attribution page renders with no content, so there is no record of who did what, against a project whose modelling and software are advanced enough that this matters most

Several standard pages 404 (proof-of-concept, implementation, team, safety-and-security, protocols); content exists at non-standard paths or not at all, which costs the reader under the rule that judges need not hunt

The two tests that would settle the fire-performance claims, cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR, produced no results before the freeze, and char thickness and density were never measured despite being the criterion the fire-safety expert set

Protein yield rests on visual SDS-PAGE band intensity against a BSA standard (~2.10 vs ~0.90 ug/uL) rather than a quantitative protein assay, and the Cycle 2 PE adhesion claim has no measurement behind it at all
Nine of the ten PEbp Registry parts are deposited sequences with a computed binding score and no experimental characterisation; only KWFFEKWWMMRR was actually built and tested
The home page contains no statement of what the project is, and the Notebook is a 355-word timeline of headings with no entries
red_flags: Attributions page is empty (verified on the live site), so the student-versus-outside-help split cannot be assessed; I raise this as a question for Q&A, not as an allegation

Model acknowledgements state that an advisor assisted in performing the umbrella sampling that produced the binding free energies used in the Model conclusions; declared, but it is outside execution on a headline computational result
Cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR were outsourced to The Hong Kong Polytechnic University and the page says results 'will be discussed in the judging session' - these cannot be scored as evidence
Internal inconsistency in the ecotoxicity baseline: the DI water control germination rate is given as 75% in Results 4(c) and 85% in Results 4(d)
Registry part pages could not be reached in this session (parts.igem.org returned CloudFront 403 for all four parts I tried), so Registry documentation depth is unverified rather than judged
pages_read: attempted Registry: BBa_26QZ8KBC, BBa_26EKX9DH, BBa_26CC4C9Q, BBa_26LG0ASA (403)

calibrated.changed: none — empty page with only school-level task assignment is the 2.0 band I used for labi-taiwan, cataverse and squirrel-guangzhou.

justification.a1: FlaminGone climbs through genuinely harder steps inside one season: curli fusion design, expression optimisation across strains/media/inducer, a wet-lab-tested AI-designed peptide, intumescent formulation, a two-layer coating, weathering and ecotoxicity screening, plus an MD pipeline and a benchmarked ML tool (Engineering, Results, Model, Software pages). It is not a single demonstration but a platform carried to measured performance on real industrial PE scaffolding netting (Results §3). It falls short of a 5 only because several branches are unfinished or overstated (cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR never run; 9 of 10 'characterized' PEbp parts never built).
justification.a2: Core function is measured, not asserted: restriction-digest gels for every construct (Results Figs 2-3), Congo Red red pellets, SDS-PAGE F+/F- showing the 37 kDa monomer only after formic acid (evidence of real amyloid), and flame tests with proper comparators - uncoated wood, CsgA alone, water+APP/EG binder-free, protein alone, protein+additive (Results §2, Measurement Tables 1-3). NFPA 701 on PE netting gives 4.8 +/- 0.2 cm for the two-layer system vs 13.1 cm raw CsgA control, with n=3. It is 4 rather than 5 because protein yield is quantified by visual band intensity against a BSA standard rather than a real assay, most tables are images without error bars, and the Human Practices page states cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR 'confirmed' non-toxicity while Measurement §11-12 says those results were never collected.
justification.a3: The need is real and locally grounded (Wang Fuk Court fire; HK Buildings Dept PNRC85 standards), and the team tested on the actual substrate - industrial PE scaffolding netting - under an adapted NFPA 701 protocol that HK regulators recognise. Crucially, SHKP told them the scaffolding-net market is shrinking, costs HKD~40/roll and that they would refuse to spray a third-party coating for liability reasons, and the team published that negative finding and repositioned toward net manufacturers and non-toxicity (HP, SHKP section). It stops short of 5 because the cost analysis Prof. Yuen asked for was never produced and the team kept scaffolding nets as the lead application against its main stakeholder's advice.
justification.a4: Five DBTL cycles each contain a failure that changed the next build (Engineering page): the seven-gene operon's metabolic burden halved yield so they reverted to the single T7-CsgA-BslA construct; single-layer APP/EG flaked during intumescence so they split the system; and the two-layer coat peeled on NaOH-washed netting until MD simulations plus a curli-pH paper pinpointed alkaline electrostatic repulsion, after which removing the NaOH wash restored a seamless matrix at 4.8 cm. The modelling and software are used for design, not decoration - PyroForge-optimised Alp(2) beat the LLM-drafted Alp(1) in a burn test (8.5 vs 10.5 cm). Short of 5 because success criteria are mostly set after the fact and the MD 'prediction' of inter-layer failure is reported alongside, not clearly before, the wet-lab result.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the wiki: ten named stakeholders with a traceable consequence each. SHKP's feedback pivoted the whole selling point from fire retardancy to non-toxicity and low smoke; Prof. Yeoh's advice produced APP/EG and the two-layer architecture that is now the final design; Prof. Chan's heat-denaturation worry produced the PyroForge thermostability platform; Mr. Lee's three-chamber substitute made durability testing possible in a school lab, with limitations stated; Mr. Wong's advice put sonication into the purification protocol and chose Arabidopsis for the phytotoxicity assay. A 174-respondent survey is reported with its own design consequence, and critical voices are kept rather than smoothed over. The one gap is that consent or ethics oversight for the street interviews is never mentioned.
justification.a6: The Attribution page is empty - banner image and title only (https://2026.igem.wiki/hk-joint-school/attribution/, verified live). The Team Members page assigns work only at school level (Measurement, Wet-lab, Model, Wiki), never to students, and no figure caption says who ran an experiment. Against that, the Model page acknowledgements disclose that advisor Mr Leung Chung Ki built the polyethylene layer, extended the Amber14SB force field and ran the umbrella sampling that produced the PEbp binding free energies, and Measurement §12 says PolyU will perform the cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR; those disclosures are honest but describe substantial adult-executed work with no student-side counterweight. Until the session clarifies who did the bench and modelling work, this cannot go above 3.
justification.a7: The project is built squarely from standard parts: six IPTG-inducible T7-LacO-RBS composites and a ten-member PEbp basic-part library (Parts, Contribution), with the dual-operon construct explicitly built on UNILausanne 2023's BBa_K4685031 and credited. Several composites were built, expressed and shown to work (CsgA-BslA, CsgA-PEbp, CsgA-Alp(2)-PEbp), and PyroForge counts as a standard software component. Held just below 5 because the modular 'plug-and-play' claim to cellulose and mineral substrates is design talk only, and nine of the ten peptide parts exist as sequences with literature binding scores, never built.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely good: every part is listed with registry ID, genetic architecture, functional role and description, and is cross-linked to the cycle and the burn data that used it (Parts, Contribution, Engineering). I could not reach parts.igem.org (403 from this environment) to confirm sequence features, topology and characterisation on the Registry itself, so the Registry side is unverified rather than credited. The ten PEbp entries are called a 'characterized library' when their only data are binding scores taken from Bergman et al. 2026, and no raw data files or downloadable tables are offered anywhere.
justification.w1: The home page carries a carousel, a logo and the single line 'iGEM 2026 team.' - no problem, no approach, no goal, no schematic (home.txt, 94 words). A judge has to open Description before learning what FlaminGone is. Once there, the abstract is excellent: one paragraph that names the problem, the CsgA-BslA-PEbp architecture, the two-layer system, PyroForge and the fire result.
justification.w2: Most claims are tied to something a reader can check: gels, Congo Red pellets, SDS-PAGE lanes with densitometry, burn tables with controls and n=3, and weathering comparisons with percentage drops (Results, Measurement). Model and software outputs are kept separate from wet-lab results and limitations are stated frankly (Model, 'Limitations and uncertainties'). Points come off for data tables delivered as images without error bars, yield quantified by eye, 'zero ecotoxicity' resting on 20-seed germination counts, and the Human Practices page asserting that cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR confirmed non-toxicity when Measurement says those tests were never completed.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and conventional: Project / Lab / Engagement groups, standard page names, a per-page contents list at the top of every long page, and consistent internal cross-links ('for complete protocol details, please visit our Experiments page'). It loses half a point for the dead Attributions page, for Safety and Team sitting at non-standard URLs (/safety, /team-members) while the standard slugs 404, and for very long pages (Human Practices ~11,900 words, Measurement ~9,100) that drift toward sprawl.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: Experiments gives full protocols with supplier catalogue numbers, Measurement documents the UL94, NFPA 701, weathering-chamber and ecotoxicity setups including the school-lab substitutions and their limits, and Model records force-field customisation and box geometry. Against that, the Notebook is only a 355-word list of phase titles with no dated entries, no raw data are posted, code and weights live on GitLab/Zenodo rather than the wiki, and the empty Attributions page removes the who-did-what record future readers would need.
justification.w5: Every substantive page carries a numbered IEEE-style reference list, figures from Our World in Data are credited, and prior iGEM work (UNILausanne 2023 BBa_K4685031) is acknowledged in the part description. Lapses keep this from 4: in Measurement the 'Waterlox. Uneven, Rough, and Blotchy First Coats' entry links to a ScienceDirect article and the Ossila bar-coating entry links to the Krasucki PDF; in Model, reference 5 duplicates reference 3 and the GROMACS entry is garbled and repeated; WHO is cited via a 'Share.google' link and PE flammability via Scribd.

J3.one_line: A rare high school project where the biology, the modelling and the stakeholder work genuinely feed each other - five real DBTL cycles ending in a measured 4.8 cm char length on industrial PE netting - but the Attributions page is completely empty, which is the one thing I cannot score around.
strengths: Human Practices is integrated, not decorative: SHKP's market pushback moved the whole value proposition to non-toxicity, and Prof. Yeoh's advice produced the two-layer CsgA-PEbp / CsgA-BslA+APP/EG architecture that is the final design (Human Practices page).

Flame testing is done with the controls that matter - uncoated wood, CsgA alone, binder-free water+APP/EG, protein alone, protein+additives - so the 4.8 cm vs 13.1 cm result on PE netting means something (Results sections 2-3, Measurement Tables 1-3).

A real failure diagnosed and fixed: the top-coat peeled off the primer, MD simulations and a curli-pH paper pointed at alkaline repulsion from the NaOH pre-wash, removing it restored a seamless matrix (Engineering 5th cycle, Model literature-insight section).

PyroForge is unusually rigorous for a high school team - leakage removed by parent-grouped cross-validation (r fell from 0.85 to 0.46 and they say so), external S669/Ssym benchmarking, antisymmetry enforced - and its designed peptide Alp(2) actually outperformed Alp(1) in a burn test (Software section 4, Results section 3c).

Protocols are reproducible, with supplier catalogue numbers, and the school-lab substitutes for an industrial weathering chamber are published together with their stated limitations (Experiments, Measurement section 10).
weaknesses: The Attributions page renders only a banner - no student roles, no named external contributors, nothing (verified live). Team Members assigns work by school, never by person, and no figure caption says who ran an experiment.

Modelling work credited to an adult advisor (building the PE layer, extending the Amber14SB force field, running umbrella sampling) is disclosed in the Model acknowledgements but never bounded against what the students themselves did.

The Human Practices page says cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR tests were conducted and confirmed the product's non-toxicity; Measurement sections 11-12 say those results were never collected and PolyU will run them later. The claim should be removed, not left for the session.
The ten-member PEbp library is called 'characterized' but nine entries carry only literature binding scores and were never built or tested; only KWFFEKWWMMRR reached the bench.
The home page tells a visitor nothing about the project - problem, approach and goal all live one click away in Description.
Quantitative data arrive as images of tables with no error bars, protein yield is estimated from visual band intensity, and the ecotoxicity conclusion rests on 20-seed germination counts.
red_flags: Internal contradiction on completed work: Human Practices (Prof. Guan and Mr. Lee sections) states cone calorimeter and TGA-FTIR tests were performed and confirmed non-toxicity, while Measurement sections 11-12 state those results could not be collected before the wiki freeze and will be run by The Hong Kong Polytechnic University. Ask at the session; as written it is an unsupported claim, not evidence of misconduct.

Attributions page is empty (https://2026.igem.wiki/hk-joint-school/attribution/ renders title and banner only), while the Model page discloses advisor-built force-field work and PolyU-run instrumentation. This is an attribution question for the session, not an accusation.
Over-labelled parts: Contribution calls the 10-peptide PEbp library 'characterized' when nine members have only in-silico binding scores drawn from Bergman et al. 2026.

Minor citation failures: a Waterlox coating-troubleshooting reference linking to a ScienceDirect URL and an Ossila reference linking to the Krasucki PDF (Measurement); duplicated and garbled GROMACS and Liu 2014 entries (Model); WHO cited through a 'Share.google' link (Description).
pages_read: Registry part pages attempted: BBa_26QZ8KBC, BBa_26EKX9DH, BBa_26LG0ASA, BBa_26CC4C9Q - all returned HTTP 403 from parts.igem.org, so Registry content is unverified

calibrated.changed: a5 5 to 4.5 and a6 2.5 to 3.0. On a5 I contradicted myself inside my own justification: I wrote that consent and ethics oversight for the street interviews are never mentioned, which is exactly the gap for which I held GEMS, Hangzhou, Squirrel Guangzhou, Keystone, GCGS and others to 4.5, and then awarded 5 anyway. The stakeholder work is still among the two or three strongest here. On a6, an empty page alone should not put this below teams with equally thin student-level attribution: the Model page names the advisor who built the polyethylene layer and ran the umbrella sampling, and Measurement names PolyU for the pending instrumentation, which is more disclosed outside help than SHSID or Cataverse offer at 2.5, and matches the 3.0 band I used for Mingdao, Keystone and Squirrel Guangzhou.

one_line.en: A rare project where biology, modelling and stakeholder work genuinely feed each other, ending in a measured fire-test result on the real substrate, with a completely empty attributions page.
one_line.zh: 生物、模擬與利害關係人工作真正互相餵養的少見專案，最終在真實基材上取得實測防火結果，但歸屬頁完全空白。

strengths: Negative controls throughout the fire testing so each component's contribution is separable rather than asserted
Raw per-trial data published rather than only means, across two fire standards
A complete loop where a simulation prediction, a physical failure and a literature finding changed the protocol and improved the result
A benchmarked software tool with a data-leakage bug found, fixed and reported, plus code and weights archived with identifiers
weaknesses: The attributions page is empty and team members are divided only among schools, never among people or tasks
The secretion claim is not supported by the method used, since the extraction lyses whole cells
Protein yields rest on visual band intensity rather than densitometry, with no error bars or statistics anywhere in the lab results
The low-smoke, low-toxicity selling point was never measured, and the home page states nothing about the project
red_flags: Attributions page renders empty while advisor-performed simulation work is disclosed elsewhere
Human Practices states that instrument tests were performed and confirmed non-toxicity while the Measurement page states those results were never collected
Nine of ten library parts are labelled characterised but carry only computed scores
A safety question for the committee about work described as carried out under BSL-2 containment by a high school team

screen.project_title: Engineered lanmodulin variants for selective terbium recovery from fluorescent-lamp phosphor waste
screen.what_they_built: Rationally designed and MD-ranked lanmodulin (LanM) point mutants intended to bind terbium more tightly than wild type, plus CBDcex-fused versions for anchoring onto cellulose so the protein behaves as a reusable column rather than a consumable reagent.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli NiCo21(DE3)/BL21, His-tagged constructs purified by nickel IMAC. 14 parts registered: LanM WT and five mutants (D43N, T90Y_E95D, T90W, T114W, T41W), the same six as (GGGGS)3-CBDcex-6xHis fusions, the linker, and CBDcex adapted from Imperial 2014 BBa_K1321003.
screen.best_evidence: /results: Arsenazo III competition titration of T90Y_E95D, 2 uM protein with 10 uM AZ3 titrated 0-16.67 uM TbCl3 in triplicate, full 21-point absorbance table at 660 nm reported with the no-protein control. Protein samples rose from ~0.099 to ~0.570 versus ~0.095 to ~0.303 for the control, but the team concludes the data cannot be interpreted — visible precipitation above a 4:1 Tb:protein ratio causes light scattering, there is no distinguishable binding transition, and no affinity or stoichiometry can be extracted. /engineering reports the supporting negative: SDS-PAGE showed only 5 of 11 constructs expressed (WT, T90W, T41W, D43N, T90Y_E95D).
screen.hp_integration: Yes in the sense that it should have changed the project but did not in time — a CUHK chemistry lecturer told the team Arsenazo III would chelate the metal itself and suggested back-titration with ICP-MS instead, and separately that fluorescent lamps are being replaced by terbium-free LEDs and that engineered protein may cost more than the extraction it replaces. These critiques are reported candidly but the assay and the premise were not revised.
screen.reason: A well-chosen, genuinely hard problem with 14 registered parts and honest reporting, but nothing was shown to work: six of eleven constructs did not express, the only binding assay was destroyed by precipitation and is explicitly uninterpretable, the CBDcex-cellulose immobilisation that the whole product concept rests on was never tested, and the expert's objection that the target feedstock is disappearing was never answered. Results is 716 words and there is effectively no model page.
screen.field_notes: HK-PLKNPLC (Po Leung Kuk Ngan Po Ling College, Bioremediation, HKG) engineered lanmodulin variants to recover terbium from spent fluorescent-lamp phosphor, chosen because LanM binds lanthanides at picomolar affinity and discriminates against calcium by 1e8 while industrial separation needs hundreds of counter-current solvent-extraction stages. Eleven constructs (WT, own designs D43N/T90Y/E95D/T90Y_E95D, six published tryptophan variants) were ranked by MD-derived Coulombic and Lennard-Jones interaction energies after the team rejected MM/GBSA and MM/PBSA for lacking polarisable Tb3+ parameters — a thoughtful negative methods result in itself, and the two energy components disagreed on ranking. Only 5 of 11 expressed on nickel IMAC; the team attributes this to inclusion bodies and proposes Lemo21(DE3). The Arsenazo III competition assay in 1x PBS failed outright because TbCl3 precipitates with phosphate, and the repeated assay still showed precipitation above 4:1 Tb:protein, so no affinity or stoichiometry could be determined; the full triplicate 21-point table is published anyway. 14 parts registered including six CBDcex-(GGGGS)3 fusions for cellulose immobilisation that were never tested. Human practices is notable for publishing damaging expert criticism verbatim: a CUHK chemist challenged both the assay chemistry (suggesting back-titration plus ICP-MS) and the premise, since LEDs are displacing terbium-containing lamps. A WEEE Park deputy general manager interview grounds the e-waste context.

screen.project_title: prbA esterase pre-treatment to remove parabens from food waste
screen.what_they_built: E. coli BL21(DE3) expressing prbA, a paraben-hydrolysing esterase, as a pre-treatment step so preservatives in food waste stop inhibiting the microbes used in anaerobic digestion at facilities like Hong Kong's O-PARK.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); prbA cloned in an IDT vector, in pelB-prbA(xsc)-pET22b+ and in a 6xHis double-tagged version; 14 new parts characterised (12 basic, 2 composite), including the putative native prbA promoter and RBS validated by GFP expression (BBa_26MSEOFB).
screen.best_evidence: /results: MIC of methyl-paraben rises from 400-500 mg/L for wild-type BL21(DE3) to 1000-1500 mg/L for the cycle-1 prbA strain (CFU plate method with positive, negative, uninduced and no-cell controls); pNPA esterase assay with two-way ANOVA (enzyme condition F = 52.5, p = 3e-17), a Brown-Forsythe variance check and Welch-Satterthwaite contrasts with Holm correction showing recombinant prbA significantly faster than commercial liver esterase at 0.10, 0.20 and 0.25 mM.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in structure - the 'iCycle' six-step framework with public, implementation, safety and iGEMer stakeholder classes - but the pack does not show a specific stakeholder conversation that changed a construct or assay.
screen.reason: A genuinely solid gold-medal project: a real phenotype shift (MIC roughly tripled), properly analysed enzyme kinetics against a commercial comparator, 14 characterised parts including a native promoter/RBS, and honest reporting of a cycle that went backwards. But the central claim stays partly unresolved - cycle 2 gave a lower MIC than cycle 1, cycle 3 was never MIC-tested, and HPLC is qualitative peak identification rather than a degradation rate. Not top-2 calibre without that closure.
screen.field_notes: HKSSC (Hong Kong, Food & Nutrition) tackled an overlooked bottleneck in food-waste recycling: parabens preserved in the waste inhibit the microbes that digest it. They expressed prbA esterase in E. coli BL21(DE3) across three cycles (IDT construct; pelB-prbA(xsc)-pET22b+ for periplasmic targeting and IMAC; then a 6xHis double-tagged version with pelB removed). Using CFU plate counts rather than OD600, and first building an OD-to-CFU standard curve, they put wild-type MIC for methyl-paraben at 400-500 mg/L and the cycle-1 engineered strain at 1000-1500 mg/L. Cycle 2 unexpectedly gave a lower MIC (500-600 mg/L) with faint SDS-PAGE bands, which they attribute to pelB-induced stress and protein loss during intracellular purification - the reflection is candid and drove cycle 3, which was never MIC-tested for want of time. Downstream characterisation is the strongest part: a pNPA esterase assay analysed by two-way ANOVA (p < 1e-16 for enzyme condition and substrate), a Brown-Forsythe test that found unequal variances, and Welch-Satterthwaite contrasts with Holm correction showing prbA beats commercial liver esterase at low substrate. HPLC confirmed the methyl-paraben peak at 9 min and product peaks but gives no degradation rate. Fourteen new parts were characterised including prbA's putative native promoter and RBS, demonstrated by GFP-expressing colonies patterned into the team name. The Attributions page is only ~111 words.

screen.project_title: AmpliRen: toehold-switch and HCR household test kit for urinary miRNAs in chronic kidney disease
screen.what_they_built: A home test-kit concept for chronic kidney disease that detects urinary miR-21-5p and miR-192-5p, first with cell-free toehold switches driving EGFP and then, after that failed to give usable signal, with enzyme-free hybridisation chain reaction producing G-quadruplexes read by ThT fluorescence or hemin/TMB colour.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli with pET-14b-EGFP for cloning and a cell-free expression system for the switch assays; HCR components are synthetic DNA hairpins (H1/H2 and G4H1/G4H2) adapted from Miao et al. 2016 and Peng et al. 2022. Fourteen BBa IDs appear in the crawl but the /parts page is short (749 words) and characterisation lives on /results.
screen.best_evidence: /results: five-replicate cell-free EGFP assay — positive control 28.1-fold over no-plasmid control, but miR-21-5p-7 only 1.18-fold, miR-21-5p-9 0.92-fold, miR-192-5p-6 1.03-fold, miR-192-5p-7 1.51-fold, none reaching significance. Best positive data are the HCR ThT assay: miR-21 significant at 100 nM versus control (n=3, one-way ANOVA with Dunnett, p<0.001) and hemin/TMB colour rising from 0.1477 to 0.1894 A.U. between 0 and 100 nM.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — nephrology and user feedback supported the at-home, urine-based format, and practicality concerns (EGFP invisible by eye, ThT needing a UV reader) drove successive readout changes, but the documented redesigns are mostly technical rather than stakeholder-driven.
screen.reason: Honest, well-structured and very readable, with four explicit DBTL cycles and candid reporting of failure — creditable, but it is exactly what keeps it out of the top two. The core detector does not work: toehold switches gave no significant target-dependent signal across five replicates, miR-192 HCR behaves non-monotonically (colour peaks at 100 pM then falls), free G4H1 hairpins self-fold and produce signal without target, and the gels are smears the team itself calls inconclusive. Only the miR-21 HCR arm shows a defensible dose response, and only at nanomolar concentrations far above urinary miRNA levels, so the project's own premise of detecting trace biomarkers is not demonstrated. No model, hardware or attributions page. Strong education and HP sections lift the wiki score but aspects 2 and 8 are weak.
screen.field_notes: HongKong-HS (Diagnostics, Hong Kong; a five-school consortium) developed AmpliRen, a proposed household urine test for chronic kidney disease targeting miR-21-5p (fibrosis severity) and miR-192-5p (early warning). Cycle 1 used miRADAR from Wageningen 2024 to design 16 toehold candidates and NUPACK to shortlist four. Cycle 2 cloned them into pET-14b-EGFP with XbaI/NdeI, confirmed inserts by Sanger sequencing, and tested cell-free expression five times: the plasmid-only positive control gave 28-fold induction, proving the assay worked, but no toehold candidate reached significance (best was miR-192-5p-7 at 1.51-fold, miR-21-5p-9 actually decreased). An mCherry colorimetric redesign was begun but not finished. Cycles 3-4 pivoted to enzyme-free hybridisation chain reaction with G-quadruplex-bearing hairpins: agarose smearing was inconclusive, PAGE showed faint high-molecular-weight bands at 10 nM, ThT fluorescence gave a significant miR-21 response at 100 nM (ANOVA with Dunnett, p<0.001) but a paradoxical dip for miR-192 at 1 nM, and a hemin/TMB DNAzyme colour readout rose with miR-21 from 1-100 nM while miR-192 peaked at 100 pM then declined. The team attributes background to free hairpins self-forming G-quadruplexes and proposes redesigning hairpin minimum free energies. The wiki is well designed with an interactive engineering timeline, large education and human-practices sections, and a site map, but has no model, hardware or attributions page, and all assay work remains at concentrations far above clinical urinary miRNA levels.

screen.project_title: MerMAID: MerR-based mercury assay for in-field detection in agricultural water
screen.what_they_built: A MerR/pMer mercury-responsive E. coli biosensor with the mRFP1e reporter giving two readouts from one protein - visible pellet colour and red fluorescence - plus a 3D-printed phone-camera fluorescence box, an integrated fluorometer and a sample extraction unit.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5alpha throughout; pKMV, pKAN-IDT and pUC57-KAN backbones, all kanamycin and high-copy. Design 429 selected from more than ten variants. New parts BBa_260COQ5F, BBa_26BL7PZU, BBa_26K7J4Y3, BBa_26W1VZU8 plus heavy reuse of Anderson promoters, B0030-series RBSs and B0015 terminators; a dedicated /parts page exists.
screen.best_evidence: /results: Design 429 characterised in five matched independent runs from 0.005 to 5 uM Hg (~1-1000 ppb). All 51 assessed treatments exceeded their matched controls in both pellet readouts; the two readouts ranked concentrations identically (Spearman rho = 1.00); at ~1 ppb both rose above matched controls in 5/5 runs (paired t-test p = 0.0080 colour, p = 0.0346 fluorescence); at 5 uM pellet fluorescence gave 7.95x fold response versus 3.26x colour and 1.61x culture fluorescence. Selectivity: mercury beat Pb, Zn and Cd in all eight matched comparisons, largest off-target response 6.5% (fluorescence). Soil extracts reached 10.44x; alginate-encapsulated cells still turned red.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - a dedicated 12.6k-word human practices page titled 'Who we listened to and what changed', and the engineering cycles are framed around questions raised externally; the move to a phone-camera readout without a plate reader is explicitly an accessibility decision for in-field agricultural users.
screen.reason: The strongest team in this batch by a clear margin and a credible top-2 candidate. The characterisation is genuinely rigorous for any iGEM team: five independent matched runs, paired statistics at the lowest dose, a selectivity panel, reference-stability and OD-normalisation checks, documented data exclusions, and a stated refusal to call 1 ppb a validated limit of detection. Nine wet-lab DBTL cycles include a frankly reported failed aptamer route and an ECF20 amplifier that lost discrimination. Hardware (fluorescence box, integrated fluorometer, extraction unit) and a model page back it up. The one real caveat for the panel is aspect 6: all constructs were ordered as sequence-verified synthesised plasmids, the team did no cloning, and the supervisor prepared the mercury solutions - the student work is in design, characterisation, imaging, analysis and hardware.
screen.field_notes: HongKong-JSS (Agriculture, HKG) built MerMAID, a MerR-based mercury biosensor for agricultural water with a dual colour/fluorescence readout from a single mRFP1e reporter. Nine wet-lab DBTL cycles are documented, including an abandoned RNA-switch route (a DNA mercury-binding motif wrongly assumed to work as a riboswitch), an ECF20 amplifier that produced high uninduced expression, and screening of more than ten designs to select Design 429. Characterisation used five independent matched runs at 0.005-5 uM HgCl2: every assessed treatment exceeded its matched control in both pellet readouts, the two readouts ranked doses identically (rho = 1.00), ~1 ppb was detected above control in 5/5 runs with paired p = 0.0080 (colour) and 0.0346 (fluorescence), and 5 uM gave 7.95x pellet fluorescence versus 3.26x colour. Selectivity against Pb, Zn and Cd held in all eight matched comparisons; soil extracts gave up to 10.44x and alginate beads retained visible colour. Measurement infrastructure is their own: a 3D-printed BP570/BP610 fluorescence box, locked-setting phone camera, ImageJ pipeline with reference normalisation, OD600 = 0.8 standardisation, and a later integrated fluorometer. Limitations are stated explicitly (thresholds derived on the same five runs, visual readout needs a centrifuge, soil mercury never measured directly). Constructs were ordered as synthesised sequence-verified plasmids from IDT, GenScript and BGI - the team did no cloning - and the supervisor prepared all mercury solutions.

justification.a1: Thirteen prototypes (2 aptamer, 11 protein), nine wet-lab DBTL cycles, a selected Design 429 characterised over 0.005-5 µM in five matched independent runs, a log-linear calibration model with held-out validation runs, two hardware platforms (Extraction V1-V3, Detection V1-V4 with a C12880 spectrometer), plus soil-extract and alginate-bead trials (Engineering, Results, Model, Hardware). That is several linked results increasing in difficulty, close to the GreatBay_SZ/TAS anchors. It falls just short of a 5 because the construct building was entirely outsourced and the field-facing steps (beads, soil, equipment-free colour) stayed qualitative or unresolved.
justification.a2: Results Tables 9-13 give a graded dose response across five independent runs with mean ± SD, all 51 within-run treatments above their matched four-hour controls, paired t-tests at ~1 ppb (p = 0.0080 colour, p = 0.0346 pellet fluorescence), CVs by concentration, and a leave-run-in/out robustness check; selectivity against Pb, Zn and Cd at 1 µM is matched by run and timepoint (Table 16-17). The team's own Detection Unit V3.0 independently reproduced the dose dependence (2,567 to 24,367 ADC counts, R² = 0.9898, Hardware), which is a second instrument agreeing with the phone-camera data. Held below 5 because the main runs carry only uninduced same-strain controls (vector-only and wild-type comparisons were qualitative and in separate preliminary experiments, Results 2.4), all primary readouts are ImageJ intensity ratios rather than calibrated fluorometry, and the team rightly concedes 1 ppb is the lowest tested concentration, not a validated LOD.
justification.a3: The use case is well grounded in Hong Kong's 2% local vegetable production and the rice methylmercury literature (Description), and it was taken to users: on-site trials at Blue Girl Organic Farm and Yeung Marine Products Limited, plus 195 public participants with 84.1% finding the readout understandable (Engineering, Detection Unit Cycle 4). What is missing is impact evidence from real contaminated material: soil work used lab-spiked soil with nominal, unmeasured concentrations (Results 8.1), no field sample was ever quantified, and the USD 350 bill of materials still sits far above the USD 40 users asked for. Credible and stakeholder-supported, but not yet demonstrated in a real-world setting as TAS's wastewater rig was.
justification.a4: This is the strongest part of the project. Nine wet-lab cycles each state the question, the build, the test and what changed, including real failures: the aptamer route abandoned after recognising a DNA motif had been treated as an RNA switch, ECF20 amplification dropped because every colony was red before induction, and a culture-management overhaul after subcultures a and c showed strong uninduced colour. Cycle 9 converted wet-lab limitations into a written hardware requirement list, and the hardware cycles answer them with measured outcomes (580 nm long-pass replaced by 560/610 narrow bandpass, 11,469 to 15,844 ADC counts). Short of 5 only because quantitative success criteria were usually set after rather than before testing, and some cycles (culture handling) are troubleshooting rather than redesign.
justification.a5: Four documented stages with government departments (EPD, AFCD, WSD, DSD), seven academics, WEEE·PARK, farms, an aquaculture firm and wet-market vendors, plus surveys of 333 and 195 people, each engagement closed with an explicit "what this changed" (Human Practices). Traceable design changes include dropping drinking water as the primary target, adding soil and pH conditioning, the modular extraction architecture after Prof. Odukoya, the dual colour/fluorescence mRFP1e readout, and the interface rule separating device-ready status from sample safety. The page is also unusually honest that interest in a device is not evidence of its effectiveness. Just short of 5 because the biology itself was shaped less by stakeholders than the hardware was.
justification.a6: Students clearly ran the assays, imaging, ImageJ analysis, statistics, modelling and both hardware builds, and the team page assigns every named student a work area. Three things are outsourced and openly declared: no cloning at all (every construct ordered as a sequence-verified synthesised plasmid from IDT, GenScript or BGI, Experiments Protocol 2), all mercury solutions prepared by the supervisor (Engineering, Safety), and competent cells supplied by the Amgen Biotech Experience programme. The attributions page carries only the official iGEM form iframe, so task-level attribution of the kind TAS Taipei showed could not be read from the page itself; the role labels on the team page are broad categories rather than tasks.
justification.a7: The final device BBa_26BL7PZU is a genuine engineered genetic device: a divergent MerR/pMer architecture with p429 driving merR and pMer driving mRFP1e, built from Registry parts (B0034, B0032, B0031, B0015, K3380107, K3702162, K2796033) with three new basic parts, and the variant series deliberately walks promoter and RBS strength (Parts, Engineering Cycles 2 and 7). Orthogonal sigma-factor control (ECF20/pECF20, BBa_K4491110) and RiboJ insulation show real standard-part thinking even where the module failed. Only short of 5 because the comparison between P429 and J23106 designs changed several features at once, so part-level attribution of the improvement is incomplete.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is excellent: a Parts page that separates submitted, unsubmitted and control designs, gives sequences for parts with no Registry entry, and states plainly that only experimentally characterised parts were submitted. The handbook judges parts on the Registry entry alone, and the team itself says only "a brief summary of the characterization data" is recorded on the Registry page, which suggests the entry is thinner than the wiki; I could not open parts.igem.org during judging (403) to verify annotation, controls and characterisation on BBa_26BL7PZU, BBa_26W1VZU8 and BBa_260COQ5F. The lab notebook is an embedded PDF on static.igem.wiki rather than page content, which is acceptable but less inspectable.
justification.w1: The home page states the project in one line (a living sensor that glows red with mercury, a portable reader, an extraction platform) and gives a Results-at-a-glance block with the caveat that the complete system's detection limit is not established. The index page numbers and one-line-describes every page. Marked down slightly because the mercury-background scrollytelling runs long before the reader reaches what the team actually did.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is tied to a numbered table or graph with n, SD, matched controls and stated units, and the caveats are specific (reference division is not background subtraction; thresholds were derived and tested on the same five runs). The Model page keeps validation runs out of the fit and reports RMSE of 0.0483 µM (colour) and 0.0319 µM (fluorescence) including the failures. It is not a 5 because the soil and bead work is unreplicated and qualitative, the master data tables behind the figures are referenced but not published as raw files, and all optical evidence is image-derived.
justification.w3: Navigation is consistent (Project / Engagement / People menus, an indexed landing page, per-page chapter contents) and standard URLs are intact for every page that exists.
