Friction: some content sits behind an embedded PDF (notebook) and an iframe (attributions) that does not render as text, and a "Still Rendering" placeholder appears at the top of several pages including Results, Description and Team, which looks like an unresolved build artefact.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: full protocols with strain, medium, volumes, filter models and the 3D-printed light box build (Experiments), hardware and human-practices date logs (Notebook), a Contribution page that spells out reusable method checks, and sequences for designs that were never submitted together with an explicit warning not to reuse the DNA aptamers. Short of 5 only because the numerical master tables and image files behind the figures are not downloadable alongside the notebook PDF.
justification.w5: Description, Engineering and Model carry numbered reference lists with DOIs, prior work is credited properly (Guo et al. 2019 for the p429 promoter library, Bao et al. 2020 for mRFP1e), and the 2024 iGEM Bolivia Mercurito team is credited for the same promoter use. Weaker on the hardware, education and entrepreneurship pages, where market figures, the HKD cost comparisons and several figures carry no inline source, and the Entrepreneurship page calls the system "highly accurate", which no cited result supports.

J1.one_line: An unusually rigorous high-school project: a MerR/mRFP1e mercury biosensor characterised over five matched runs with paired statistics, selectivity and a held-out calibration model, carried into two genuinely iterated hardware platforms, let down mainly by fully outsourced construct building and the absence of any real contaminated sample.
strengths: Design 429 dose response measured in five independent matched runs with mean ± SD, 51/51 within-run treatments above matched controls, paired t-tests at ~1 ppb and run-inclusion robustness checks (Results 3-6)

Selectivity against Pb, Zn and Cd matched by run and timepoint, with the largest non-target response quantified as 6.5% (pellet fluorescence) and 32.0% (colour) of the matched mercury response (Results 7)

Nine wet-lab DBTL cycles that document real failures and the redesigns they forced: the DNA-aptamer-as-RNA-switch conceptual error, ECF20 amplification killed by background, and the culture-management overhaul after uninduced subcultures turned red (Engineering)

A calibration model fitted on four runs and tested on two withheld runs, reporting RMSE in µM including the out-of-range failures, with a concrete plan for run-aware modelling and inverse-calibration intervals (Model)
An independent instrument corroborating the biology: Detection Unit V3.0 resolved 0 to 5 µM Hg in pellets at 2,567 to 24,367 ADC counts (R² = 0.9898) and distinguished 0.03 µM from control (Hardware)

Human practices with a traceable change per engagement, including the shift away from drinking water, the modular extraction architecture, and the rule that a green status LED must never read as sample safety (Human Practices; Engineering Detection Cycle 4)

Discipline about the limits of its own evidence throughout: 1 ppb is called the lowest concentration tested rather than an LOD, reference division is distinguished from background subtraction, and soil concentrations are labelled nominal
weaknesses: No cloning was done by the team: every construct was ordered as a sequence-verified synthesised plasmid, and verification rests on supplier sequencing files rather than the team's own gel or sequencing data (Experiments Protocol 2)

The five main runs include only uninduced same-strain controls; empty-vector (pKMV) and wild-type comparisons were qualitative and run separately, never quantified alongside the characterisation dataset (Results 2.4)
All primary readouts are ImageJ green/red channel ratios from one phone camera, never cross-checked against a calibrated plate reader or fluorometer, as the team itself concedes (Contribution item 5)
The stated goal of an equipment-free visual warning is not met: colour in unspun culture is distinguishable only above ~0.5 µM, so the usable readout still needs a centrifuge (Results 3.3, 4.3)
Soil and bead work is preliminary and unreplicated, with nominal rather than measured mercury, unknown extraction recovery, and one bead series that developed no colour (Results 8)

Registry documentation appears thinner than the wiki (the team describes only a brief characterisation summary on the part page), and I could not reach parts.igem.org to verify BBa_26BL7PZU and the new basic parts

Attribution is at the level of broad role labels on the team page, with the detail confined to an embedded iGEM form iframe, so task-level ownership of individual experiments is not readable from the wiki
Entrepreneurship language ("highly accurate", "quantitative readouts in 2-3 hours") overstates what the lab pages carefully refuse to claim
red_flags: None of integrity concern. Nothing read as fabricated, and the wiki consistently labels modelled, nominal and qualitative material as such.

Registry part pages (BBa_26BL7PZU, BBa_26W1VZU8, BBa_260COQ5F, BBa_26K7J4Y3) returned 403 from my network, so aspect 8 was scored on the wiki plus the team's own description of the Registry entries; a judge with Registry access should verify characterisation data there.

The attributions page is only an iframe to teams.igem.org/wiki/6158/attributions and the lab notebook is an embedded PDF; neither rendered as text in the crawl, so their contents could not be assessed.
A "Still Rendering" placeholder appears near the top of several pages (Results, Description, Notebook, Team, Attributions), which looks like an unresolved build artefact rather than content.

Minor internal inconsistency: Engineering cites 0.03 µM as the responding concentration while Results and Description lead with ~1 ppb (0.005 µM); the conditions differ (screening vs five-run characterisation) but the pages do not reconcile them explicitly.

calibrated.changed: none. a6 4.0 is consistent with Basis-China, where the attributions content also sits only in the embedded official form but the surrounding pages assign every student a work area and declare the outsourcing (here, all constructs synthesised and all mercury solutions prepared by the supervisor).

justification.a1: Scale and scope are close to my GreatBay anchor: 13 constructs built and screened, one (Design 429) characterised over a 0.005-5 uM dose series in five matched independent runs (Results Table 9), selectivity against three metals, soil extracts and alginate beads, plus two hardware platforms and a fitted calibration model with held-out validation (Model page, Table in section 5). The chain of increasingly hard steps is real and told as one story. It falls short of a 5 because no cloning was done in-house and the most impressive hardware engineering is partly credited to a secondary PI on the attribution form.
justification.a2: The main function is demonstrated with controls and replicates: both pellet readouts exceeded matched controls in all 51 assessed treatments, paired t-tests at ~1 ppb give p=0.0080 (colour) and p=0.0346 (fluorescence), n=5 independent runs (Results sections 3.2 and 5.1), with empty-vector pKMV and untransformed E. coli controls showing no colour. Reference-stability checks (Results Table 5) rule out the obvious imaging artefact. Measured, not modelled. Capped below 5 because the detection threshold was derived and evaluated on the same five runs, the soil mercury was added by the team and never measured, and the bead work is qualitative and partly negative.
justification.a3: The deployment route is stakeholder-checked and concrete: screening to flag samples for lab confirmation, soil prioritised after CUHK and HKU advice, salt leaching instead of acid, and on-site demonstrations at Blue Girl Organic Farm and Yeung Marine Products (Hardware, 'User Testing'; HP Stage 3-4). They state the gaps honestly, including USD 350 BOM against a USD 40 stakeholder target. It is not a 5 because no real environmental sample was ever measured end-to-end; the field work demonstrated the device rather than produced a finding, unlike TAS Taipei's wastewater test.
justification.a4: This is their strongest aspect. Nine wet-lab cycles each change the next build: the RNA-switch route is abandoned after recognising the D3/D4 motifs are DNA aptamers, missing 0 uM and empty-vector controls are added, the working range is re-established at 5 uM, culture management is changed after uninduced P3 subcultures went red, and ECF20 is dropped for destroying signal-to-background (Engineering, Cycles 1-7). Hardware cycles carry numbers: 560 nm vs 580 nm excitation gave 15,844 vs 11,469 ADC counts, tubing bore change cut line volume from 3.85 to 0.079 mL, automated delivery CV 1.95% vs 7.41% manual over 20 runs, and fault injection was scored per event (Hardware, Extraction Unit). The model is fitted to their own data and tested on two held-out runs with RMSE in uM (Model sections 2-5). Not a 5 only because several variables changed together between first- and second-generation designs, which they acknowledge.
justification.a5: Fifteen-plus stakeholders across government (EPD, AFCD, WSD, DSD), academia (CUHK, HKU, HKBU, EdUHK, Lagos) and users (two organic farms, an aquaculture operator, wet market vendors), organised around a five-question cycle, with traced design changes: chromoprotein to mRFP1e dual readout after DSD, water to soil after CUHK, acid digestion to room-temperature salt leaching after Prof. Liang, modular preparation after Prof. Odukoya (HP Stage 2, 'Implementation'). It is reflective and responsive rather than outreach: More Happy Farm's refusal to own a device is reported and reshaped the business model. Short of 5 because some engagements are summarised rather than evidenced, and the impact statements sometimes restate intent.
justification.a6: The attribution form is complete, unusually detailed per student, and declares AI tool use and every external contributor. Against that, core execution is substantially outside the students: all plasmids were ordered as sequence-verified constructs with no cloning done (Experiments, Protocol 2), competent cells and occasional supervision came from Amgen Biotech Experience HK, the supervisor prepared every mercury solution, and a secondary PI is listed as responsible for hardware design and engineering, software and wiki writing. It is declared honestly, so this is a scope question and not an integrity one, but it keeps the score at the 'key steps outsourced and say so' level.
justification.a7: The project is built on standard parts: Anderson promoters J23100/J23106/J23110/J23117, B0031/B0032/B0034, B0015, plus BBa_K3380107 (pMer) and BBa_K2796033 (mRFP1e), with a deliberate promoter and RBS variation series (Parts page). Three new basic parts and one composite device (BBa_26BL7PZU) are submitted, and the team states it only submitted what it characterised. I could not open the Registry pages myself (parts.igem.org returned bot-protection pages, which I will not work around), so Registry depth is unverified by me and I did not credit it above 4.
justification.a8: Wiki documentation is excellent for rebuilding the work: protocol specifications with volumes, times and concentrations, run-by-run roles (Results Table 1), reference-intensity ranges, filter specifications, and a Parts page that also publishes unsubmitted designs and raw sequences with a warning not to reuse the aptamers. Registry-side documentation I could not verify directly. Marked down also because the wet-lab notebook is an embedded PDF rather than a readable record, the extraction firmware sits on GitHub off iGEM servers, and a few '[Figure: ...]' placeholders remain in the Hardware page text.
justification.w1: The home page states the aim, chassis, reporter and headline number in one line and offers a four-page judge path, and the Description page explains the MerR mechanism and what the project does not measure. The reason it is not higher is internal inconsistency in the headline claim: Human Practices Stage 2 reports 'a detection limit of 6 ppb', while Results explicitly refuses to call ~1 ppb a detection limit, and the Entrepreneurship page promises an 'exact mercury number' and a 'Heavy Metal-Free' certificate that the data do not support.
justification.w2: Claims are carried by tables and graphs with n, SD, CV, paired p-values and robustness checks, and each result is labelled measured, preliminary or planned (Results sections 2-8). Limitations sit beside the claims rather than at the end, including that the visual readout needs a centrifuge and that one alginate series produced no colour. Just short of 5 because the strongest application claims (soil, beads) rest on unreplicated or nominal-concentration work, and the imaging workflow was never checked against a calibrated instrument.
justification.w3: Navigation is good: a numbered index, per-page chapter contents, and explicit cross-links such as the Hardware page pointing to named Human Practices sections. Against that, the wiki is very large (roughly 50,000 words across the main pages), which strains 'complete but not sprawling', and some pages still show '[Figure: ...]' placeholders and a 'Still Rendering' artefact under the page title.
justification.w4: The Contribution page is written for reuse rather than as a victory lap: the imaging box with BP570/BP610 specifications, a plate-reader-free fluorescence workflow with its own validity checks, a three-way framework for choosing between readouts, the calibration equations with the held-out validation design, the ECF20/pECF20 sequence offered uncharacterised, and the aptamer sequences published with an explicit warning. A future team could pick this up. Held below 5 because the firmware and some BOM material live off iGEM servers.
justification.w5: Description, Engineering, Model and Human Practices carry proper reference lists with DOIs, and the home-page statistics name UNEP, WHO, AFCD and Bakir et al. The spot-checks I made resolve to real, relevant literature (Guo et al. 2019 on MerR promoter rheostats; Zevallos-Aliaga et al. 2024). Results and Hardware cite much more thinly for their methodological choices, and figures are team-made without credit lines, so this is solid rather than exemplary.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineered mercury biosensor with five matched runs of real dose-response data, nine honest DBTL cycles and two measured hardware platforms, held back only by outsourced construct building and a hardware effort in which an adult PI's role is large.
strengths: Design 429 characterised over 0.005-5 uM in five independent matched runs with matched controls, paired t-tests at ~1 ppb (p=0.0080 colour, p=0.0346 fluorescence) and empty-vector and untransformed controls (Results sections 3-5)

DBTL cycles that actually change the next build: the aptamer route abandoned on a stated mechanistic error, missing controls restored, culture management rebuilt after uninduced subcultures went red, ECF20 dropped for killing signal-to-background (Engineering Cycles 1-7)

Hardware tested as hardware: 560 nm vs 580 nm excitation (15,844 vs 11,469 ADC), pellet dose-response R2=0.9898 down to 0.03 uM, automated delivery CV 1.95% over 20 runs vs 7.41% manual, and scored fault-injection tests (Hardware)
A calibration model fitted to their own measurements, tested on two fully held-out runs, reported as RMSE in uM with every prediction included, and its own reanalysis plan (Model)

Relentless, specific honesty: thresholds called exploratory not validated, soil concentrations called nominal, bead work called qualitative with one failed series, ImageJ colour explicitly said not to prove naked-eye detection

Human Practices that changed the design in traceable ways (chromoprotein to mRFP1e, water to soil, acid digestion to salt leaching, modular preparation, service model), including a stakeholder who said they would not buy the device
A Contribution page built for other teams: imaging box specifications, readout-selection framework, part sequences including the failed aptamers with a do-not-reuse warning
weaknesses: No cloning was performed by the team; every construct was ordered as a sequence-verified plasmid, and competent cells came from Amgen Biotech Experience HK (Experiments, Protocols 2-3)
The attribution form lists a secondary PI as responsible for hardware design and engineering, software development and wiki writing, which is where much of the project's impressiveness sits
No real environmental sample was measured end-to-end; soil was spiked by the team and its mercury content never measured, so matrix tolerance is shown but soil detection is not
The claimed sensitivity is inconsistent across the wiki: Human Practices reports a 6 ppb detection limit while Results refuses to call ~1 ppb a detection limit at all
The Entrepreneurship page ('highly accurate', 'exact mercury number', 'Heavy Metal-Free certificate') contradicts the careful hedging everywhere else
The wiki is very long for its content, the wet-lab notebook is an embedded PDF rather than a readable record, and '[Figure: ...]' placeholders remain in the Hardware page
Registry depth could not be verified: parts.igem.org served bot-protection pages to me, so the part entries are judged only on the team's own Parts page
red_flags: Not an integrity concern, but for the panel: the attribution form credits a secondary PI with hardware design and engineering plus software, while students are credited with designing, building and testing the detection unit; worth a Q&A question about who did what on the Detection Unit.

AI tool use is declared openly (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, Doubao, OpenCode for writing/coding/research; Nano-Banana-Pro for diagrams). The AI-made images appear to be schematics and logos, not evidence figures; data graphs are plotted from the team's own tables. No action needed, noted for transparency.

parts.igem.org could not be read (CloudFront bot protection / CAPTCHA, which I did not attempt to bypass), so aspects 7 and 8 rest on the wiki's Parts page; another judge with Registry access should confirm the four new part entries.
pages_read: https://2026.igem.wiki/hongkong-jss/attributions (plus the embedded iGEM attribution form at teams.igem.org/wiki/6158/attributions)
parts.igem.org Part pages for BBa_26BL7PZU, BBa_26W1VZU8, BBa_260COQ5F, BBa_26K7J4Y3 — attempted, blocked by bot protection, not read

calibrated.changed: none — this ballot sets my bar for a complete attribution form with honestly declared outsourcing (3.5) and for measured dose-response with matched controls (a2 4.5).

justification.a1: The season covers a great deal and climbs: thirteen constructs across two sensing strategies, nine wet-lab DBTL cycles ending in Design 429, a five-run matched characterisation from 0.005 to 5 uM (Results Table 9), a calibration model with held-out runs (Model s.5), and two hardware tracks (Detection Unit V1-V3, Extraction Platform V1-V3) with on-site trials. The story holds together as one sample-to-readout system rather than a collection of activities, which is close to the GreatBay pattern; it falls short of the top only because the integrated device and the biology were never run together on a real environmental sample.
justification.a2: The core device demonstrably works with real controls: empty-vector pKMV and untransformed E. coli gave no colour, matched 0 uM controls accompanied every run, and all 51 assessed treatments exceeded their matched controls in both pellet readouts (Results 3.2). At ~1 ppb both pellet readouts rose above control in 5/5 runs (paired t, p = 0.0080 and 0.0346, Table 12), selectivity against Pb, Zn and Cd was larger for Hg in all eight matched comparisons (Table 17), and the Detection Unit independently tracked the response (R2 = 0.9898, Hardware). The team itself labels 1 ppb as the lowest concentration tested rather than a validated LOD, the bead work is qualitative and one series failed, so the honest ceiling is just below 5.
justification.a3: The need was interrogated rather than assumed: WSD could not identify a contaminated drinking-water site, which killed the original application (HP Stage 2), and EPD/AFCD showed existing monitoring programmes the tool must complement. Farms and aquaculture operators confirmed a gap between periodic official tests, and the team names the limits honestly (USD 350 BOM against the USD 40 target; GM cells could not leave the lab, so site trials ran without bacteria, HP Stage 4). A credible route exists but has not yet been tested in the real setting with the live sensor, so this sits below the TAS wastewater-tank anchor.
justification.a4: This is the strongest part of the project. Failures drove redesigns: the aptamer route was abandoned after the team found it had treated a DNA aptamer as an RNA switch (Cycle 1), ECF20 amplification was dropped when every colony was red uninduced (Cycle 6), and uninduced P3 subcultures a and c going red forced a change in culture management (Cycles 4-5). Hardware cycles mirror this (long-pass filter bleed fixed with 560/610 narrow bandpass, 15,844 vs 11,469 ADC counts), and the model was fitted to their own data and used to pick a readout. Marks are held back only because the team repeatedly, and correctly, notes that several variables changed together so improvements could not be attributed.
justification.a5: Stakeholder input visibly changed the design in several traceable places: WSD's challenge moved the project off drinking water; DSD pushed the readout from chromoproteins to mRFP1e and prompted the Cd/Pb/Zn cross-reactivity tests that appear in Results s.7; Prof. Liang's advice replaced acid digestion with room-temperature salt leaching and added five-point composite sampling; Prof. Odukoya's advice produced the modular V3.0 architecture; and the V1.0 field trials (syringe force, trapped liquid) produced peristaltic pumping in V2.0. Critical and uninterested voices are included - More Happy Farm did not want a device, which led the team to consider a service model. The reflective gap is ethics: 333 and 195 public respondents, some engaged in street demonstrations, with no mention of consent or oversight.
justification.a6: The team is unusually candid about what it did not do: 'No cloning was carried out in this project' (Experiments Protocol 2), all constructs arrived as sequence-verified synthesised plasmids, competent cells came from the Amgen Biotech Experience Program, and the supervisor prepared every mercury solution (Engineering, Shared Experimental Framework). That honesty is creditable. But the Attributions page is only an embedded iGEM form iframe with no narrative, the Team page lists roles only as Human Practice, Product Design, Conceptualization, Entrepreneurship and Wiki Coding - no student is listed against wet lab - and no figure caption names who ran an experiment, so from the wiki alone I cannot tell which students did the bench and ImageJ work. A session question, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The device is a standard-parts design: a divergent MerR/pMer architecture contributing three new basic parts (BBa_26W1VZU8 P429-1, BBa_260COQ5F MerR, BBa_26K7J4Y3 spacer) and one characterised new composite (BBa_26BL7PZU), built on existing registry parts K3380107, K2796033, K3702162, B0034 and B0015, with Anderson promoters, B0031/B0032, RiboJ and ECF20 (K4491110) in the variant series. The composite is the part that carries the data, and the hardware and imaging box count as standard components under p.31. Strong use of existing parts plus a working new composite puts this near the top.
justification.a8: The Parts page is a model of its kind: an explicit submission policy (only experimentally characterised parts registered), status labels, sequences published for unsubmitted designs, and a blunt 'do not reuse the aptamer sequences' with the reason. Protocols, filter specifications, imaging method, notebook and hardware logs are all on the wiki. The limit is that the team says only 'a brief summary of the characterization data' sits on the Registry page itself while the full dose-response, selectivity and threshold analysis lives on the wiki, and parts.igem.org was returning 403 when I tried to verify the entry, so I score the Registry side as good rather than TAS-level.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the mechanism (MerR clamp, trigonal Cys site, 33 degree twist, mRFP1e output) and the claim in a few readable lines with a schematic, gives a 'Results at a glance' panel with its own caveat line, and tells judges which four pages to read in fifteen minutes. The Description then frames Hong Kong, regional and global context without overclaiming, explicitly saying the findings 'do not establish widespread mercury contamination of Hong Kong farmland'. Only the length of the scrollytelling intro keeps this off a 5.
justification.w2: Claims are tied to evidence to an unusual degree: Table 9 gives mean +/- SD at ten concentrations with n = 5, Table 12 gives paired increases and p-values, Table 17 gives relative non-target responses, and the Model page reports held-out RMSE (0.0319 uM fluorescence, 0.0483 uM colour) including predictions outside the calibration range so failures are not hidden. Measured, exploratory and proposed are consistently separated - the UV-AOP module is labelled dry-lab only, V4.0 as under construction. Small deduction for the cross-page inconsistency between '~1 ppb lowest tested' (Results, Home) and 'detection limit of 6 ppb, 0.03 uM' (HP Stage 2 table), which a reader must reconcile.
justification.w3: Standard pages are all present and reachable, there is a numbered index page with a filter, each page has an 'In this chapter' contents, and the Results page opens with a three-minute summary before the full analysis - a genuine kindness to judges. Against this, the wiki is long: Human Practices runs about 12,600 words and Hardware about 10,000, with repetition between the HP, Engineering and Contribution accounts of the same hardware cycles, and several standard slots (proof of concept, implementation, measurement) return 404 so their content must be found elsewhere.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this record: numbered protocols with specifications and conditions, filter models and passbands, the imaging box CAD and build, ImageJ channel and reference method, run-inclusion table with reasons for excluding Runs 1-3, model equations with calibration and validation splits, hardware development logs by date, and the Contribution page's ten wet-lab items including the sequences of designs that failed. Short of 5 because the underlying per-image measurements are summarised in tables rather than posted as raw data, and the wet lab log is an embedded PDF rather than a browsable record.
justification.w5: Description and Engineering carry full reference lists with resolving DOIs (Zhang 2010, Guo 2019, Bao 2020, Campbell 2002, Katzmeier 2019), the Home page attributes each statistic to UNEP, WHO, Bakir 1973 or AFCD, a borrowed spectra figure on Hardware is credited to its journal source and figure number, and prior iGEM work is acknowledged, including the 2024 Bolivia Mercurito team's use of the same promoter. The weakness is unevenness: the Results, Parts and Contribution pages make substantive methodological and comparative claims with almost no in-text citation, and several HP news items are listed without linking the specific claim they support.

J3.one_line: A disciplined, evidence-first high school project: a MerR/mRFP1e biosensor characterised over five matched runs with real controls, a held-out calibration model, two iterated hardware platforms, and human practices that demonstrably redirected the application - let down mainly by thin wiki-side attribution of who did the bench work.
strengths: Five independent matched runs with uninduced, empty-vector and untransformed controls; all 51 assessed treatments beat their matched controls in both pellet readouts, with paired t-tests at ~1 ppb (Results Tables 9 and 12).

Genuine DBTL: the aptamer route was abandoned after the team identified its own conceptual error (DNA aptamer treated as an RNA switch), and ECF20 amplification was dropped when uninduced colonies went red (Engineering Cycles 1 and 6).

Human Practices changed the project, not just the narrative: WSD moved it off drinking water, DSD drove the chromoprotein-to-mRFP1e switch and the Cd/Pb/Zn tests, Prof. Liang replaced acid digestion with salt leaching, field trials replaced syringes with peristaltic pumps.
A calibration model fitted to the team's own data, evaluated on two held-out runs, reporting RMSE in concentration units and including the predictions that failed (Model sections 5-6).

Exceptional claim hygiene throughout: exploratory thresholds, nominal versus measured mercury, device status versus sample safety, and the USD 350 versus USD 40 affordability gap are all stated plainly.
A Parts page with an explicit submission standard, documented dead ends with sequences, and an instruction not to reuse the flawed aptamer designs.
weaknesses: Attributions is only an embedded iGEM form; no student is listed against wet lab on the Team page and no figure caption names an experimenter, so the wiki alone does not show who did the bench and ImageJ work.
The project's stated aim, an equipment-free visual warning, is not met: colour in unspun culture is only distinguishable above ~0.5 uM, so the readout still needs a centrifuge (Results 3.3).
The integrated detector and the live biosensor were never run together on a real field sample - site trials used no GM bacteria, and soil mercury was added by the team and never measured.
Reported sensitivity differs between pages (~1 ppb lowest tested on Home and Results, 'detection limit of 6 ppb' in the HP Stage 2 table), which a reader must reconcile themselves.
Two public surveys (333 and 195 respondents, including street interviews and demonstrations) are reported with no mention of consent, anonymity or any ethics oversight.
Sprawl: Human Practices (~12,600 words) and Hardware (~10,000 words) repeat the same hardware cycles already told on Engineering and Contribution, and several standard page slots return 404.
red_flags: No integrity flag raised. Noted for the session rather than as an accusation: the wiki states that no cloning was done and all constructs were ordered as sequence-verified plasmids, mercury solutions were prepared by the supervisor and competent cells were supplied by an external programme - all disclosed honestly, but combined with an attribution page that is only an embedded form, I cannot tell from the wiki which students performed the assays, imaging and analysis.

parts.igem.org returned 403 during this review, so I could not independently verify the depth of the Registry entry for BBa_26BL7PZU; the team's own description of it as 'a brief summary of the characterization data' suggests the full evidence lives on the wiki.
pages_read: https://2026.igem.wiki/hongkong-jss/attributions/ (embedded iGEM form iframe; no readable content)

calibrated.changed: none. I checked the a6 of 3.5 against HK Joint School and Basis China, which I also scored on an embedded form plus honest disclosure of adult-executed work; the three now sit at 3.5, 3.0 and 3.5 in proportion to how much the wiki itself states. The 4.5 on a2 is one of only three in the section and is earned on five matched runs, paired statistics, an eight-comparison selectivity panel and an independent hardware readout.

one_line.en: The field's only replicated headline result: a mercury biosensor characterised over five matched runs with paired statistics, a held-out calibration model and two iterated hardware platforms, with all construct building outsourced.
one_line.zh: 全場唯一被重複驗證的核心結果：汞生物感測器經五次配對實驗、配對統計、保留集校正模型與兩代自建硬體驗證，但所有構築建造都外包。

strengths: Five independent matched runs with uninduced, empty-vector and untransformed controls; every assessed treatment beat its matched control in both readouts, with paired t-tests at the lowest tested concentration
Selectivity against lead, zinc and cadmium quantified in matched comparisons, with the largest non-target response stated as a percentage of the mercury response
Calibration model fitted on four runs and tested on two fully withheld ones, reporting error in concentration units including the predictions that failed
Nine DBTL cycles recording real conceptual errors and the redesigns they forced, plus an independent detection unit reproducing the dose response
weaknesses: No cloning was done by the team: every construct was ordered as a sequence-verified plasmid, and competent cells came from an outside programme
Attribution is role labels plus an embedded form; no student is assigned to wet lab and no figure names an experimenter
The stated goal of an equipment-free visual warning is not met — colour needs a centrifuge below about 0.5 uM
No real contaminated sample was measured end to end; soil mercury was added by the team and never measured, and entrepreneurship prose overstates what the lab pages claim
red_flags: Attributions page is only an iframe and did not render as text, so task-level ownership cannot be read from the wiki; one judge reports the external form credits a secondary PI with hardware, software and wiki writing
Registry part pages returned 403 to all three judges, so part characterisation is unverified
Internal inconsistency on sensitivity: a 6 ppb detection limit on one page against a refusal to call ~1 ppb a detection limit on another

screen.project_title: CLASP: Conditional Localized Assembly of Synthetic Proteins
screen.what_they_built: A modular CTPR-repeat protein scaffold carrying M13, LgBiT and SpyCatcher docking sites, so that a chosen signal (calcium via calmodulin in the proof of concept) recruits a SpyTag/SmBiT-tagged payload, reports via NanoBiT luminescence and is then locked irreversibly by SpyTag-SpyCatcher; supported by ORIGAMI, a modelling tool that combines CTPR helical geometry, worm-like-chain linker dynamics and mass-action kinetics with a Gaussian process to pick repeat lengths.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21/TOP10 for expression plus an S30 cell-free system; pET28a+ backbones. Eighteen Registry parts across four stages, including CTPR3/5/8/14-M13-LgBiT-SpyCatcher scaffolds (BBa_264H6Z45, BBa_265AYKTL, BBa_26FZALLV, BBa_261YO82S), CaM-SmBiT and a dead-CaM negative control (BBa_26EYPT3O, BBa_26JF89Y3), and mSA-LgBiT/mSA-SmBiT cell-free constructs.
screen.best_evidence: /results Phase 2-3: co-expressed CTPR3 scaffold with calmodulin gave 0.689 absorbance versus 0.244 for the negative control, read as LgBiT/SmBiT complementation; reconstituted NanoLuc gave 0.316 against LgBiT-alone 0.085 and SmBiT-alone 0.080; a calcium assay kit with a four-point standard curve assigned CTPR3/8/14 values of 0.230/0.349/0.429 mM; SpyTag-SpyCatcher covalent locking resolved as a band at 60 kDa on SDS-PAGE. Everything else on the page is gel images annotated 'well-expressed... proving that the length is accurate'.
screen.hp_integration: Yes at the pivot: a marine physiologist (Prof. Fong Kar Hei) and a nutritionist independently killed the original calcium-yogurt/osteoporosis application on feasibility, market and ethics grounds, which triggered the restructure from ion transporters to conditional protein assembly and redirected the team to diagnostics and agriculture.
screen.reason: Ambitious foundational idea, eighteen parts and a large modelling/software effort, but the experimental evidence does not support the claims: results are mostly gel bands at expected sizes, the few numbers are single raw absorbance readings with no replicates, units or error bars, and a calcium assay kit is used to report both calcium concentration and luminescence in ways that are not explained. No substrate channeling, no dose-response, no kinetics; the team itself cites 'engineering failures in vitro'. The wiki is also sprawling (24k-word model, 16k-word HP) and the contribution page still contains unedited lorem ipsum text, which bears on aspects 8 and w1-w4. Could merit a look for Best Model/Software rather than for a finalist slot.
screen.field_notes: HongKong-PuiChing (Foundational Advance village) built CLASP, a conditional protein-assembly platform: a rigid consensus tetratricopeptide repeat (CTPR) scaffold carrying loop-grafted M13, LgBiT and SpyCatcher, with payloads tagged SpyTag/SmBiT, so a signal (calcium via calmodulin in the proof of concept) drives recruit-report-retain-react - NanoBiT luminescence reports binding and SpyTag-SpyCatcher then locks the payload covalently. Six DBTL cycles are documented, beginning with an ideation cycle in which two experts killed the original CAX1/HKT1 calcium-yogurt application and pushed the team to spatial organisation instead. Dry lab is the strongest part: AlphaFold3/ESMFold structures with PAE analysis, Aggrescan and SoluProt aggregation/solubility filtering, and ORIGAMI, which models CTPR helical coordinates, worm-like-chain linkers and mass-action kinetics with a Gaussian process to rank scaffold lengths (23.9k-word model page, 14.4k-word software page). Wet lab results are thin: mostly gels captioned as confirming expected sizes, plus single absorbance readings - CTPR3+CaM 0.689 vs 0.244 control, reconstituted NanoLuc 0.316 vs 0.085/0.080 fragment controls, calcium-kit values of 0.230/0.349/0.429 mM for CTPR3/8/14, and a 60 kDa SpyTag-SpyCatcher band - with no replicates, error bars or dose-response, and no demonstration of the claimed hundredfold substrate channeling. Eighteen parts are registered with a four-stage rationale; the contribution page still contains lorem ipsum placeholder text.

screen.project_title: Phoeniveil — MAA–chitosan nanoparticle UV-protective layer for burn dressings
screen.what_they_built: A two-stage E. coli scheme in which one culture overproduces sedoheptulose-7-phosphate (S7P) via transketolase overexpression and a second takes it up through uhpT (uhpA-activated) to make mycosporine-like amino acids, which would then be encapsulated in chitosan nanoparticles sprayed onto the outer gauze layer.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a; parts const-TKT (BBa_261I3LPM), tktP (BBa_26MAUSCL), uhpTp (BBa_26S49YHV), uhpTp-eGFP (BBa_26NAG7U1), uhpA (BBa_26C5GEXU), const-uhpA (BBa_26Q650E2) on J23100/B0034/B0015; pSB1C3 backbone swap from BBa_J06504.
screen.best_evidence: /results: transketolase specific activity of const-TKT transformants measured at ~4.48 U/mg by kinetic fluorometric assay (G3P standard curve r=0.993) against a literature wild-type figure of <=0.1 U/mg, i.e. >=44.8x. Also uhpTp-eGFP reaching peak fluorescence sooner at higher G6P (Spearman -0.685), though peak intensities were not significantly different.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in part: LinkSpider's advice pushed them from co-culture to sequential culturing, and chemistry/physics teacher input on silver-ion chelation and heat moved the MAAs from a direct-wound spray to the outermost dressing layer.
screen.reason: One genuinely quantitative part result (transketolase overexpression) and a competent FBA, but the project's core claim is untested: no MAA gene was ever built or expressed, const-uhpA verification failed at co-transformation, no MAA-CSNP was made, and no UV-protection measurement exists. Solid medal territory, not top-2.
screen.field_notes: HongKong-UCCKE (Fashion & Cosmetics) proposed Phoeniveil, a sprayable mycosporine-like amino acid (MAA) in chitosan nanoparticles pre-applied to the outer layer of burn dressings to stop UV-driven post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation. They used flux balance analysis on iML1515 to pick transketolase as the overexpression target for the MAA precursor S7P, then built const-TKT and measured 4.48 U/mg transketolase activity against a wild-type literature value of <=0.1 U/mg, their strongest result. The uhpTp-eGFP reporter responded faster at higher G6P but peak intensities did not differ significantly, and const-uhpA(CmR) was constructed but its verification co-transformation yielded no colonies, so the uptake stage is unverified; no MAA biosynthesis gene was built at all. On the application side they produced chitosan nanoparticles (UV-Vis scattering baseline, gravimetric stock of 5.0 mg/mL) and ran an ASTM E96M breathability test showing chitosan does not reduce gauze water-vapour transmission, but never combined MAA with the nanoparticles or measured UV blocking. Human Practices (7 stakeholders on a 4A cycle) did change the design twice: sequential culturing instead of co-culture after LinkSpider, and MAAs moved to the outer dressing layer after chemistry/physics consultations. Education is the largest page (9.7k words); hardware, measurement, software and attributions pages are empty.

screen.project_title: BrewXOS: converting brewer's spent grain arabinoxylan into AXOS prebiotics
screen.what_they_built: Engineered Bacillus subtilis WB600 strains secreting xylanases (Xyn2, Xyn11A) and the arabinofuranosidase Abf62A, singly and in dual and triple combinations integrated at amyE, and ran them directly on brewer's spent grain. Also built a compact fermentation-monitoring prototype.
screen.chassis_and_parts: B. subtilis WB600 with pDG1730 amyE integration, cloned via E. coli DH5-alpha; 11 registered parts (5 basic, 6 composite) including BBa_2629PD5P Xyn2, BBa_26IIC7G6 Xyn11A, BBa_264N8EVR Abf62A and the triple module BBa_265XBPWI, submitted as a Registry collection.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering and /parts: triple strain supernatant reached 257.10 +/- 5.55 U/mL on wheat xylan, 19.1% above the better dual strain; in 12 h direct BSG culture it gave 49.05 +/- 3.02% apparent arabinoxylan conversion and 107.91 +/- 6.64 mg xylose equivalents per g dry BSG, about twice the published Amorim benchmark of 54.2 mg/g. Errors quoted as SD across replicates, with TLC as qualitative product evidence.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: 15 stakeholder groups and 219 survey responses under a GRAIN x TRACE framework; feedback reframed the claim from a health product to an unvalidated ingredient, drove the multi-tier construct design and enzyme choices, and prompted the fermentation-monitoring hardware.
screen.reason: Four DBTL cycles with replicated quantitative data, a matched comparison design (each xylanase with and without the debranching enzyme, then all three), real performance on the actual feedstock that beats the literature precedent, 11 registered parts with supporting documents, hardware, and human practices that visibly reshaped the science. Caveats worth a full read: no results page or notebook in the standard slots (data live on Engineering), no attributions page, and DNS/TLC readouts are apparent rather than purified AXOS yield.
screen.field_notes: Hongwen School (Food and Nutrition, China) built BrewXOS, engineering Bacillus subtilis WB600 to convert the arabinoxylan fraction of brewer's spent grain into arabinoxylan oligosaccharides as candidate prebiotics, inspired by a Tsingtao brewery visit and a team member's IBS. Four DBTL cycles moved from single xylanase strains (Xyn2 from Trichoderma reesei, Xyn11A from Aspergillus usamii) to Abf62A-containing dual strains, then a triple strain, then direct BSG cultivation; constructs were built in E. coli DH5-alpha on pDG1730 and integrated at the amyE locus in WB600 with spectinomycin selection, verified by colony PCR. The triple strain reached 257.10 +/- 5.55 U/mL apparent supernatant activity on wheat xylan (19.1% above the best dual strain) and, after 12 h in LB with 10 g/L dry BSG, 49.05 +/- 3.02% apparent AX conversion and 107.91 +/- 6.64 mg xylose equivalents per g dry BSG, roughly double the 54.2 mg/g reported by Amorim et al.; the Xyn2-Abf62A pair beat Xyn11A-Abf62A by 81.2% in apparent activity. TLC gave qualitative oligosaccharide evidence only, and the team is explicit that DNS indices are apparent, assay-specific values rather than purified AXOS yield. Eleven parts were registered as a collection with Design, Experiment, Characterization, Application and Discussion documents. Human practices used a GRAIN x TRACE framework across 15 stakeholder groups and 219 survey responses, reframing health claims and prompting a fermentation-monitoring hardware prototype. Contribution documents concrete troubleshooting (host-specific antibiotic selection on pDG1730, interpreting extra PCR bands). Gaps: the results, experiments, notebook, measurement and attributions standard pages are empty, with content on Engineering and a protocol-notebook page.

justification.a1: Four linked DBTL cycles take the project from two single-xylanase strains to dual and then triple-module B. subtilis WB600, then onto the real feedstock: Engineering C1-C4 report 152.66 to 257.10 U/mL apparent supernatant activity across five strains and a 12 h BSG culture of all six groups. On top of that sits a built fermenter (approx. 3,480 RMB) that ran an 18 h integrated BSG batch (Hardware 6.2). That escalating scale is close to the TAS Taipei pattern; it falls short of 5 only because the named product, AXOS, was never chemically identified.
justification.a2: Function is shown against the parental WB600 control with n = 3 and raw A520 values for every replicate (Protocol & Notebook, Stage 1 step 9 and Stage 4 step 4), a D-xylose calibration (A520 = 0.5426C - 0.1287, R2 = 0.9950), stated units and a substrate blank plus a no-substrate control. The ranking holds across two independent systems (wheat xylan and paired T0/T12 BSG cultures), and TLC adds qualitative support. It is not a 5 because no sequencing of the constructs is reported (integration rests on junction and integration-site PCR only), there is no protein-level evidence of secretion, no inferential statistics, and the DNS signal cannot show that the product is AXOS rather than XOS or monosaccharide, which the team itself states.
justification.a3: Human Practices gives the use case real operational numbers rather than slogans: roughly 5.5-6 million t/y of wet spent grain, a 50 km economic transport radius, 70-80 RMB/t landfill handling cost, and over 80% already absorbed by feed (HP sections G1-G3). The team used these to reposition BrewXOS as a regional complement rather than a replacement, and tested application routes with a dairy, a beverage firm, pharmacies and a farm. It stops at 3.5 because no impact number comes from their own data: no LCA, no techno-economic analysis and no test of the product in a real setting, all of which they list as missing.
justification.a4: Each Learn stage visibly changes the next Design: the Cycle 1 activity baseline plus Professor Xu's advice produced the Abf62A module added to both backgrounds rather than only the better one (C1 Learn); the dual results triggered the triple construct; and the assembly strategy switched from Gibson to BamHI/EcoRI because repeated homologous regions made overlap pairing risky (C3 Build). Progression criteria were stated in advance (C1.6: construct recovery, PCR pattern, activity above parental). The hardware adds a second, independent cycle (V1 one-piece lid to V2 split lid to final) with before/after user-test numbers, e.g. lid and tubing removal 5 min 40 s to 1 min 50 s. Cycle 4 is application rather than redesign, which keeps it just under 5.
justification.a5: Fifteen stakeholder groups and 219 survey responses are organised by a GRAIN x TRACE scheme that forces each interaction to name the change and the evidence, and explicitly flags interactions that did not close the loop. The exchange was genuinely two-way and reached the bench: expert advice on side-chain removal produced the Abf62A module, the selection-marker discussion fixed the WB600 screening, and the gastroenterologist's three evidence tiers made them delete "suitable for IBS" and "relieves IBS symptoms" from the project positioning (HP R3, R4, A2). The survey's skew (44% under 18) is declared rather than hidden. Short of 5 because much of the scientific steering comes from one mentor-adjacent adviser.
justification.a6: This is the weak point. /attributions returns the 404 page, and nothing equivalent appears elsewhere: the Team page is 29 personal bios, only four of which name a role (wiki, wet lab, hardware, bioinformatics). The project clearly involved outside input (Professor Xu on construct screening and selection, a hardware engineer on the lid, commercially synthesised pHT43 constructs) and none of it is set out task by task, so I cannot tell who ran the gels, the DNS assays or the BSG cultures. The handbook (p.25-26) puts attribution on the team page; without it I have to score this low even though the notebook reads like students' own work.
justification.a7: The design is squarely synthetic biology from standard components: three expression modules each with its own Registry promoter and RBS (Pveg BBa_K143012, P43 BBa_K143013, PlepA BBa_K823002 with BBa_K780001/K780002/K4382009), signal peptide and terminator, assembled hierarchically and integrated at amyE via pDG1730. Eleven new parts are registered, five basic and six composite, and the modularity is used rather than decorative, since the same modules are recombined to make the comparison set. Just short of 5 as the regulatory elements were reused without measuring promoter or RBS output in these constructs, which the team concedes.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation itself is very good: the Parts page lists all 11 IDs with type, length and rationale, links the Registry collection, and the data behind each construct are on Engineering and Contribution. Two things hold it down. Registry part pages could not be loaded from my network (403), so I could not confirm that the promised Design, Experiment, Characterization, Application and Discussion documents and the controls actually sit on the Registry entries, and p.18 says parts are judged there. Separately, the standard URLs /results, /experiments, /measurement, /proof-of-concept, /model and /attributions all return 404, so a judge following the standard page set hits dead ends.
justification.w1: The Description abstract states the problem, the engineered route and the headline numbers clearly, and Figure 10 gives a single project overview schematic. The home page, though, is a 380-word scrolling narrative about beer bottles and gut health that never reaches the result, so the goal is clear only one click in. Good communication with a little drift, not a one-screen summary.
justification.w2: Close to the best evidence standard I would expect from a high school team. Every headline number is traceable to a figure and to raw replicate absorbances in the Protocol & Notebook, controls are named and defined (substrate blank versus no-substrate versus parental WB600), units and dilution factors are given, and the calculation conventions (the factor 50, the 150.13 ug/umol conversion, the assumed 22% AX) are written out so a reader can recompute them. The team repeatedly marks what the data do not show, and the pH projection beyond 18 h is labelled as a projection. Held off 5 by the absence of sequencing, the lack of ladder size marks in the gel captions, and the fact that the key product claim rests on TLC co-migration against XOS standards only.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean, every long page carries a sticky on-page table of contents, and the five-group menu is easy to follow. But the mapping to the ballot is poor: Results, Experiments, Measurement, Proof of Concept, Model and Attributions all 404, the notebook has been moved to /protocol-notebook, and results are distributed across Engineering, Contribution and Hardware rather than any page a judge would look for first. Usable, with the key information in non-standard places.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of this. Protocols give volumes, temperatures, times and dilution schemes; the notebook carries the raw A520 readings per replicate; the failures are written up honestly (erythromycin background growth, ampicillin killing WB600, the ~400 bp artefact band and how annealing temperature was used to test it, the touchscreen %%% terminator); and the hardware ships a full bill of materials with prices, pin assignments, firmware and a STEP assembly. Missing only the sequence files and sequencing records that would close the construct verification.
justification.w5: Citations are dense, specific and resolvable, with DOIs throughout Description, Engineering and Human Practices, including the Chinese-language Hu et al. 2025 paper the enzyme pairing is drawn from and the NHC regulatory notice. Prior iGEM work is credited properly, with IONIS-Paris 2022 StarchLight named and distinguished from their own scope. Schematic captions state what they were redrawn from and when a figure is the team's own. Only small gaps, e.g. the 40 Mt/y figure on the Hardware page is uncited while the same figure is referenced elsewhere.

J1.one_line: A disciplined, evidence-first high school project: five engineered B. subtilis strains compared against a parental control with raw replicate data on both model xylan and real spent grain, plus a working low-cost fermenter and unusually honest human practices, let down by a missing attributions page and 404s on several standard URLs.
strengths: Raw per-replicate A520 readings, a stated calibration curve, a substrate blank, a no-substrate control and a parental WB600 control for every activity claim (Protocol & Notebook Stage 1 step 9, Stage 4 step 4)

A consistent five-strain comparison that holds across two independent systems: wheat-xylan supernatant activity (72.80 to 257.10 U/mL) and paired 12 h BSG cultures, with the construct hierarchy designed so every intermediate is informative

Four DBTL cycles in which a result demonstrably changed the next design, including the switch from Gibson to restriction-ligation assembly after repeated homologous regions caused screening artefacts (Engineering C3 Build)

Hardware with its own engineering iteration, user testing against an external fermentation teacher with before/after task times, a full 3,480 RMB bill of materials, firmware and STEP files, and an 18 h BSG run whose CO2 decline and flat reducing sugars led them to stop the batch early (Hardware 3, 6.2, 7, 8)

Human Practices that closed the loop into the lab and into the claims: the debranching module came from expert advice, and the gastroenterologist consultation caused them to delete IBS positioning (HP A2, R3, R4)

Exceptional calibration of language to evidence: 'apparent' indices, explicit statements that TLC co-migration cannot establish arabinose substitution, and a 'What We Still Lack' section listing the missing LCA, TEA and structural characterisation
weaknesses: No attributions page anywhere: /attributions is a 404 and the Team page carries only personal bios, so individual student contributions and the exact scope of Professor Xu's and the hardware engineer's involvement cannot be assessed
Constructs were never sequence-verified; integration rests on junction and integration-site PCR, and the team acknowledges sequencing was only 'scheduled'
The project's named product, AXOS, was never identified: TLC used xylose, xylobiose and xylotriose standards, which cannot show arabinose substitution, and no HPLC or HPAEC was run
The headline '49.05% apparent AX conversion' depends on an assumed 22% arabinoxylan content of dry BSG taken from literature, not measured on their own batch

Several standard page URLs 404 (results, experiments, measurement, proof-of-concept, model, notebook), with content relocated to Engineering, Contribution and /protocol-notebook, which conflicts with the handbook's expectation that judges are guided from the standard pages
No statistical testing; SD treats the WT mean and the calibration as fixed references, so none of the between-strain differences is tested for significance

No protein-level evidence (no SDS-PAGE or zymogram) that the three enzymes were actually secreted, so activity differences cannot be separated from expression and secretion differences, as the team notes
red_flags: Attributions page missing entirely (404) — a handbook requirement (p.25-26), and it materially limits what I can say about aspect 6

Registry part pages for the 11 claimed parts (e.g. BBa_265XBPWI, BBa_2629PD5P) returned HTTP 403 from my network, so the Registry documentation the Parts page promises could not be verified; this is a limitation of my access, not evidence of a defect
Standard page URLs results / experiments / measurement / proof-of-concept / model / notebook all return the site's 404 page
Headline conversion percentage rests on an assumed, not measured, 22% AX content of their BSG batch
No sequencing data for any construct; integration supported by PCR patterns only
No integrity concerns: data are reported with raw values, limits are stated rather than hidden, citations resolve, and prior iGEM work is credited. I have no basis for an RCC referral.
pages_read: Registry: BBa_265XBPWI, BBa_2629PD5P, BBa_26CGA70M attempted, HTTP 403 — not readable from here

calibrated.changed: none. a6 2.5 is the no-attributions-and-no-task-statement floor (29 bios, four named roles, outside input on construct screening undocumented); w2 4.5 is earned on raw per-replicate absorbances and written-out calculation conventions, which is the same standard that earned Hangzhou No.14 and Korea-HS 4.5.

justification.a1: BrewXOS builds five engineered B. subtilis WB600 strains in a three-level module hierarchy (single, two alternative duals, triple), measures all of them against the parental control in both a wheat-xylan assay and a 12 h BSG cultivation, and adds a self-built 1.2 L monitoring fermenter used for an 18 h BSG run (Description; Engineering Cycles 1-4; Hardware 6.2). That is a chain of increasingly difficult steps in the GreatBay sense, and the scope - wet lab, hardware, 15 stakeholder groups - is large for a high school team. It falls short of 5 because the headline product, AXOS, is never chemically identified: the strongest product evidence is TLC co-migration with xylobiose/xylotriose standards (Engineering Fig. 28), and the frozen HPLC sample is still pending (Hardware 6.2 offline table).
justification.a2: The core function is measured, not asserted: apparent supernatant activity of 152.66 +/- 8.56 (Xyn2), 72.80 +/- 5.75 (Xyn11A), 215.87 +/- 9.77 and 119.12 +/- 6.47 (duals) and 257.10 +/- 5.55 U/mL (triple), all n = 3, parental-WB600-subtracted, on a fitted xylose calibration (A520 = 0.5426C - 0.1287, R2 = 0.9950; Engineering Figs. 12, 13, 19, 25). On real BSG, paired T0/T12 sampling with six strain groups gives a consistent ranking (Fig. 27). Two things hold this below 4: the 49.05% apparent conversion rests on an assumed 22% AX content and on subtracting a negative parental change (-2.215 umol/mL), which the team flags honestly but which still inflates the headline number; and no inferential statistics are reported.
justification.a3: The Human Practices work returns unusually concrete deployment constraints - roughly 50 km economic transport radius for wet grain, 20-30% summer output swing, over 80% already in the feed chain, 70-80 RMB/t landfill handling cost (HP G1-G3) - and the team explicitly repositions BrewXOS as a complement to a working feed route rather than a rescue of a wasted material. Food R&D input (HP A1) pushed them to a stable, characterised ingredient before any health claim. It is not a 5 because, unlike TAS Taipei's wastewater-style test, nothing has been tried in a realistic processing setting: the 18 h run is a bench demonstration in LB plus 5% BSG, and no product has been purified, so neither the food nor the feed route has been exercised.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Each cycle closes on a measured result that changes the next build: Cycle 1 activity baselines plus Professor Xu's debranching advice produced the decision to add Abf62A to both backgrounds rather than only to the better one (C1 Learn); Cycle 2 gains in both backgrounds justified the triple; Cycle 3 switched assembly chemistry to BamHI/EcoRI because repeated homologous regions made overlap pairing unsafe, and raised annealing temperature after diagnosing a ~400 bp product (C3 Build, Fig. 22); Cycle 4 moved to the real feedstock. The hardware runs its own V1 to V2 to final loop with a problem/cause/change/verification table and quantified user re-tests (lid and tubing removal 5 min 40 s to 1 min 50 s; sampling errors 2 to 0; Hardware 3.5, 7.3). Not a 5: success criteria are often qualitative, there is no model fitted to their data (the Model page is absent), and sensor calibration against references is partial.
justification.a5: HP is reflective, responsible and responsive in the p.21-23 sense. The GRAIN x TRACE framework records, per stakeholder, the change made and the evidence for it, and explicitly flags interactions that did not close the loop. Real design consequences follow: Abf62A added on enzyme-engineering advice (A2.3), host-specific selection resolved after the ampicillin/erythromycin failure (A2.2, Engineering Fig. 9), split lid and configurable alarm thresholds from the fermentation teacher (Hardware 7.3), and the project reframed from a health product to a candidate ingredient after gastroenterologist and public input (R3-R4). The 219-response survey is used only to prioritise messaging, with its 44% under-18 sample declared as a limitation. Short of 5 only because the design-side influence is concentrated in one academic consultant plus the hardware users.
justification.a6: The standard Attributions page returns the wiki's own 404 (crawl of /attributions), so the handbook's primary attribution record (p.25-26) is missing, and there is no who-did-what chart of the kind GreatBay provided. What remains is the Team page, which gives personal bios with only occasional role statements (wiki/wet lab/hardware; bioinformatics; media), plus scattered statements elsewhere that gene synthesis was ordered commercially and that Professor Xu advised on cloning and screening. The notebook, hardware build photos and user-test design read as genuinely student-executed, and nothing suggests undeclared outsourcing, but without the form I cannot confirm the split between students, five listed teachers and the external lab, so this is a question for Q&A rather than an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is squarely synthetic biology on standard components: eleven new Registry parts (five basic, three single-enzyme modules, three module combinations) assembled from existing iGEM regulatory parts - Pveg BBa_K143012, P43 BBa_K143013, PlepA BBa_K823002 and RBS parts BBa_K780001/K780002/K4382009 - with each module carrying its own promoter, RBS, signal peptide, CDS and terminator so combinations can be swapped (Parts Table 1; Engineering 1.5). The three-level hierarchy is explicitly designed for reuse and submitted as a collection. I could not load registry.igem.org from my environment to confirm the entries themselves, so I score the design and the collection logic rather than verified Registry content; that unverified step is why this is 4 rather than higher.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely rebuild-grade: dilution and reaction factors are given in full (apparent activity = 50 x (Asample - mean AWT)/0.5426), the BSG index conversion is spelled out including the 150.13 ug/umol xylose mass and the 22% AX assumption, and the Protocol & Notebook page lists competent-cell and kit catalogue numbers, primer pairs and expected product sizes. The Parts page states that five supporting documents accompany the collection. Deductions: I could not verify the Registry pages directly, and several standard pages a judge is told to look at - Results, Proof of Concept, Measurement, Model, Implementation, Attributions - render as 404, so evidence must be found inside long Engineering and Contribution pages instead.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the feedstock and the three-enzyme solution in a few sentences, and the Description abstract names the chassis (WB600), the three modules and the two headline numbers before any detail. After the home and description pages I can state the aim, the host, the parts and what counted as success. It is not Lambert_GA-level only because the home page is a long scrolling narrative rather than a one-schematic-per-idea summary, and the achievement links at its foot are bare labels.
justification.w2: The main claims are supported by figures with units, replicates and a stated control: activity bar charts with n = 3 and parental subtraction (Figs. 13, 19, 25), paired BSG changes (Figs. 26, 27), the xylose calibration (Fig. 12), gels for every construction and integration step (Figs. 7, 8, 10, 15, 17, 21, 22, 23), TLC against standards (Fig. 28), and for the hardware a full 18 h online/offline table plus the aeration-interruption response (Fig. 22, Hardware 5.5). The team repeatedly separates measured from inferred, labelling projected curve segments as projections. Short of 5 because the product identity claim rests on qualitative TLC and no statistical testing is reported.
justification.w3: Navigation is a clean four-group menu with per-page tables of contents and anchors, and the palette is readable. Against that, six standard pages that judges are directed to - Results, Proof of Concept, Measurement, Model, Implementation and Attributions - return the site's 404, so the evidence for those criteria sits inside very long Engineering, Hardware and Human Practices pages that a reader must hunt through. The Human Practices page alone is around 11,700 words. That is the sprawl the handbook warns about, and the missing standard pages are the main deduction here.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: the Protocol & Notebook page carries dated stages, primer tables, expected band sizes, kit and competent-cell catalogue numbers and the DNS/TLC procedures; the Contribution page packages the antibiotic-marker lesson, the extra-band diagnostic sequence, the three-level assembly strategy and the full calculation conventions with the warning not to carry the fitted coefficients over; the Hardware page gives a bill of materials with prices (about 3,480 RMB total), wiring and pin assignments, and points to STEP and firmware files. It is not 5 because the parts collection documentation and some hardware files live off the standard pages, and the record is longer than it needs to be.
justification.w5: Citation discipline is the best thing about this wiki's writing. Claims are referenced to real, resolvable sources (Amorim 2018, Hu 2025, Mandalari 2005, Courtin 2009, Wu 1991, Guiziou 2016, McCleary 2015), prior iGEM work is credited specifically (IONIS-Paris 2022 StarchLight, with its wiki URL), figure captions state when a schematic is original and on which sources it is based, and literature findings are explicitly fenced off from the team's own fraction (Description Fig. 6). I spot-checked several references and they match what the text claims. Half a point off only because a few numbers quoted from interviews are estimates attributed to a person rather than a citable source, which the team does flag.

J2.one_line: A genuinely iterative, well-controlled high school project: five engineered B. subtilis strains compared on both a model substrate and real spent grain, a self-built monitoring fermenter that changed an operating decision, and Human Practices that visibly redirected the design - held back by an unidentified product, an index built on assumptions, and a missing Attributions page.
strengths: Four DBTL cycles where the test result actually changes the next build, not repeated troubleshooting: activity baselines led to adding Abf62A to both backgrounds (Engineering C1 Learn), dual gains led to the triple strain, and repeated homologous regions led to switching from Gibson to BamHI/EcoRI assembly for the final construct (C3 Build).

Measurement discipline unusual at this level: a fitted D-xylose calibration (R2 = 0.9950), n = 3 replicates, every value adjusted against the parental WB600 control, paired T0/T12 BSG sampling, and the full dilution/unit arithmetic published so a reader can recompute the numbers (Engineering C1 Test, C4 Build; Contribution section 5).

Hardware judged by measurements, not photographs: a design-target versus achieved-value table (54 rpm at a 50 rpm setting, +/-1.0 degC over 18 h, n = 3, 1.6 m pump head, about 3,480 RMB), an aeration-interruption test giving O2 and CO2 slopes of about 0.23 and 0.22 %/min, and an 18 h run where a four-hour CO2 decline plus unchanged reducing sugars at 16 and 18 h caused the batch to be stopped six hours early (Hardware 2.2, 5.5, 6.2).

User testing that produced verified design changes: an external fermentation teacher and an internal non-builder ran the same seven tasks, and the fixes were re-tested with numbers (lid and tubing removal 5 min 40 s to 1 min 50 s; sampling errors 2 to 0; alarm thresholds made configurable; the O2 readout relabelled headspace) (Hardware 7.2-7.4).

Human Practices with an explicit change-and-evidence ledger and real constraints fed back into the project - 50 km transport radius, 70-80 RMB/t landfill cost, over 80% already going to feed - leading the team to reposition itself as a complement to the feed route and to drop health claims (HP G1-G3, R3-R4, A1).

Consistent intellectual honesty: TLC is called presumptive, headspace gas is explicitly not dissolved oxygen, projected curve segments are marked as projections, and the 49% figure is labelled an apparent index rather than recovered AXOS.
weaknesses: The product the whole project is named for is never identified. TLC co-migration with xylobiose and xylotriose cannot show arabinose substitution, and the HPLC sample is still frozen (Hardware 6.2), so AXOS yield remains a reducing-sugar proxy.

The headline 49.05% apparent conversion depends on an assumed 22% arabinoxylan content and on subtracting a parental culture whose own net change was negative (-2.215 umol/mL); the team states both caveats, but the number will still be read as half the substrate converted.

The standard Attributions page returns the site's own 404 and there is no who-did-what table anywhere; the Team page gives bios, not roles, so the division of work between twenty-plus students, five teachers and the consulting laboratory cannot be checked.

Six standard pages - Results, Proof of Concept, Measurement, Model, Implementation, Attributions - are empty or 404, pushing all the evidence into three very long pages and forcing a judge to hunt (handbook p.29).
No model of any kind. The project would benefit from even a simple fitted description of the 12 h conversion or the gas data; as it stands the dose, endpoint and scale arguments are all narrative.

No statistical testing anywhere, and the gas sensors and pH probe are calibrated only against buffers or a thermometer, not against an independent reference method, so the fermenter's readings support trends rather than quantitative claims.
red_flags: The required Attributions page is missing (renders the team's 404), so aspect 6 could not be assessed from the handbook's intended source; a question for Q&A rather than an integrity concern.
Apparent AX conversion is computed by subtracting a negative parental baseline and assuming 22% AX in the BSG; the arithmetic is disclosed but inflates the apparent result and should be probed.

I could not load registry.igem.org from this environment, so the eleven claimed parts and the five collection documents are judged from the team's Parts page rather than from verified Registry entries; another judge with Registry access should confirm.
Results, Proof of Concept, Measurement, Model and Implementation standard pages are absent, which under p.29 means a judge is not obliged to find that content elsewhere.

calibrated.changed: none — a2 3.5 for an unidentified product rests on TLC co-migration only, the same bar that put keystone and lambert-ga at 3.5; w5 4.5 is earned by figure-level provenance statements.

justification.a1: BrewXOS climbs through genuinely harder steps inside one season: two single-enzyme B. subtilis WB600 strains, two dual strains, a triple strain, then conversion of real brewer's spent grain, plus a built and user-tested fermentation monitor (Description; Engineering Cycles 1-4; Hardware 6.2). That is the GreatBay-style staircase rather than one idea stretched thin. It stops short of a 5 because the headline product, AXOS, is never chemically identified: TLC against xylobiose/xylotriose is the furthest the chemistry goes (Engineering Fig. 28), and there is no model.
justification.a2: The core device works and is shown with controls: PCR internal, junction and integration-site verification of amyE replacement (Engineering Fig. 10, 17, 23), growth curves against parental WB600, and DNS activities of 152.66 +/- 8.56, 72.80 +/- 5.75, 215.87 +/- 9.77, 119.12 +/- 6.47 and 257.10 +/- 5.55 U/mL, n = 3, each adjusted against its own WB600 background (Engineering Fig. 13, 19, 25). On BSG the paired T0/T12 design gives 107.91 +/- 6.64 mg xylose equivalents/g for the triple strain against a negative parental change (Engineering Fig. 26-27). Held to 4 because the readout is an indirect reducing-sugar index the team itself calls apparent, no sequencing chromatogram or statistical test is shown, and product identity rests on co-migration.
justification.a3: The team asked whether the need was real and got told it mostly was not: the industry association put over 80% of wet BSG already in feed, and a brewery manager said the current route works (Human Practices G1, G2). They kept the honest version, targeting regions with a disposal gap evidenced by a landfill operator's 60-90 t/month at RMB 70-80/t (HP G3; Sustainable Development 13). Impact stays at 3.5 because every downstream route, fermented milk, RTD beverage, pharmacy, feed premix, is explicitly a future validation task (HP I1-I4), and nothing has been tested outside LB in the lab.
justification.a4: Four DBTL cycles where the Learn step visibly changed the next Build: Cycle 1's activity baselines plus Professor Xu's advice produced the Abf62A module in both backgrounds, Cycle 2's gains justified the triple strain, and Cycle 3's ranking sent the whole strain set to BSG (Engineering C1-C4 Learn). Build strategy itself iterated: Gibson assembly was replaced by BamHI/EcoRI ligation because 90 bp direct repeats made overlaps unsafe, and an annealing-temperature change rescued clones that would have been discarded (Engineering C3 Build, Fig. 22). Progression criteria were stated in advance (Engineering 1.6), and the hardware ran its own V1-to-split-lid loop (Hardware 3.1-3.2). No model fitted to the team's own data keeps this below TAS-level 5.
justification.a5: The GRAIN x TRACE structure forces each interaction to name a change and its evidence, and the changes are real and often unwelcome: Abf62A was added to the enzyme design on Professor Xu's advice, selection switched to spectinomycin after the erythromycin/ampicillin failure, multi-tier assembly replaced one-step assembly, the fermentation monitor was started at a bioprocess engineer's prompting, and 'suitable for IBS' was struck from the project after Dr. Chen's three-tier evidence framework (HP A1-A4, R3-R4). Critical and low-status voices, a landfill worker, a brewery that does not need them, are included rather than filtered. It is not a 5 because the 219-response survey had 44.29% minors with no statement of consent or ethical oversight (HP R1), and several consultations run through the school's own academic network.
justification.a6: This is the weak point. /attributions returns 404, so there is no who-did-what chart and no named owner for any experiment; the Team page gives only self-written bios, a few of which mention roles such as wet lab, notebook-keeping or wiki and hardware. Outside help is at least named where it mattered (Professor Xu of Zhejiang University, Prof. Qing Zhao, an unnamed hardware engineer), and pHT43 constructs are disclosed as synthesized. By my own rule, when I cannot tell who did the bench work, a6 stays at 3 pending the session; nothing here suggests dishonesty, only missing documentation.
justification.a7: The project is built as standard modules: each cassette carries its own promoter, RBS, signal peptide, CDS and terminator, with iGEM Registry regulatory parts reused and cited (Pveg BBa_K143012, P43 BBa_K143013, PlepA BBa_K823002, RBS BBa_K780001/K780002/K4382009), integrated at amyE via pDG1730 (Engineering 1.4-1.5). Eleven new parts, five basic and six composite, are registered as a collection, and the composites are the strains that were actually measured (Parts, Table 1). The hardware adds an open-source standard component with BOM, STEP files and firmware (Hardware 8).
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is excellent: raw A520 tables, the calibration A520 = 0.5426C - 0.1287 with R2 = 0.9950, the exact 50x and 5x dilution conventions, and the 150.13 ug/umol and 22% AX assumptions are all written out (Protocol & Notebook Stages 1-4; Contribution 5), so a reader can recompute every reported number. Eleven parts are registered with a named collection and five supporting documents are said to accompany it (Parts). I could not open registry.igem.org part pages from here to confirm how much characterisation actually sits on the Registry rather than the wiki, and the wiki Parts page itself is only a one-line-per-part table, so I hold this at 4 rather than 5.
justification.w1: The home page carries the problem, the feedstock, the three-enzyme mechanism and the AXOS goal in a short scroll with figures, and the Description abstract states the measured outcomes in its first paragraphs. A reader knows within a minute what BSG is, why arabinoxylan matters and what the engineered Bacillus is meant to do. It falls short of Lambert/Patras because the landing page leans on a long narrative scroll rather than one schematic plus a few lines, and the achievements block mixes judging-form links in with project content.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently tied to figures with units, n = 3 and a parental control, and the team separates what was measured from what was assumed with unusual discipline: apparent activity, apparent conversion, the 22% AX assumption, DNS cannot identify sugar source, TLC co-migration cannot show arabinose substitution (Engineering C4 Test; Contribution 5). Nothing modelled is presented as a result, and the hardware run reports online and offline data side by side with the decision it drove (Hardware 6.2). Short of 5 only for the absent sequencing confirmation, no significance testing, and the still-missing chromatographic product analysis.
justification.w3: The custom four-group navigation is coherent and every long page has a working on-page contents list, which makes the big Engineering and Human Practices pages usable. Against that, a judge who types the standard URLs finds 404s at results, model, measurement, proof-of-concept, notebook, education and attributions, and the Sustainable Development page points to an Education page that does not exist. The handbook asks teams to guide judges from the standard pages, and here some content has to be hunted for in Description, Engineering or Hardware instead.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this.
