Protocol & Notebook gives staged protocols with raw absorbance readings and the exact calculation factors, Contribution packages the selection-marker and extra-PCR-band troubleshooting as reusable decision sequences, and Hardware publishes BOM, wiring and pin assignments, firmware instructions and mechanical files. The honest statements of what each method cannot show are themselves reusable. Only the missing attributions record, and the absence of sequencing records on the wiki, keep this off 5.
justification.w5: References are full, DOI-bearing and placed where the claims are made (Description; Engineering refs 1-16; Contribution refs 1-4), prior iGEM work is credited specifically rather than in passing (IONIS-Paris 2022 StarchLight), Registry part IDs are cited with links, and schematics are labelled as original work based on named sources. I spot-checked several citations against the claims they support and found them appropriate. Minor lapses: a few Engineering captions read as drafting instructions to an illustrator (Figures 0 and 6 begin 'Show the...'), and the Hardware figure set is less consistently credited than the Description figures.

J3.one_line: A disciplined, evidence-honest BSG-to-AXOS project: five engineered B. subtilis strains across four real DBTL cycles with controlled assays, a built and user-tested fermentation monitor, and human practices that demonstrably changed the enzyme design, let down only by a missing attributions record and unidentified product chemistry.
strengths: Four genuine DBTL cycles in which each Learn step changed the next Design: Xyn2/Xyn11A baselines led to adding Abf62A in both backgrounds, then the triple strain, then real BSG (Engineering C1-C4 Learn)

Controlled, replicated measurement throughout: n = 3, parental WB600 subtraction, paired T0/T12 sampling, a published xylose calibration and the raw A520 readings behind every figure (Protocol & Notebook; Contribution 5)

Human practices with traceable consequences, including an enzyme module added on expert advice, a selection-marker fix that unblocked the build, and the deletion of all IBS and therapeutic claims after a gastroenterologist interview (HP A2, R3-R4)
Unusually honest framing: 'apparent' indices are defined, the brewery's existing feed route is accepted rather than dismissed, and TLC is explicitly said not to prove arabinose substitution

A hardware prototype that is actually built, run for 18 h, and usability-tested by an external expert and an uninvolved team member, with an operational decision (early stop at 18 h) driven by its CO2 and sugar data (Hardware 6.2, 7)
Reusable outputs for other teams: troubleshooting decision sequences, a three-level part collection, BOM, STEP files and firmware (Contribution 1-5; Hardware 8)
weaknesses: No attributions page on the wiki (/attributions is a 404) and no who-did-what chart, so which students ran which experiment cannot be established from the wiki
The product is never chemically identified: no HPLC or structural analysis, so 'AXOS yield' remains a DNS reducing-sugar index and the arabinose substitution that defines AXOS is unverified

Several standard page URLs (results, model, measurement, proof-of-concept, notebook, education, attributions) return 404, and the Sustainable Development page links to an Education page that does not exist
No model of any kind, and no statistical testing of the strain comparisons despite n = 3 throughout
Sequencing is repeatedly named as the independent check but no sequencing result is shown; genotype confidence rests on PCR patterns alone
The 219-response survey was 44.29% minors with no statement of consent, anonymity or ethical oversight
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404; outside help is named in prose (Professor Xu, Zhejiang University; Prof. Qing Zhao, CAS Chenshan) but the division of labour between students, teachers and any host lab is undocumented. A question for the session, not an accusation.

Two Engineering figure captions (Figure 0 and Figure 6) begin 'Show the...', reading as unedited instructions to an illustrator rather than descriptions of the figure. A production lapse, but worth noting on a wiki that is otherwise carefully written.

Registry depth could not be verified from here: registry.igem.org part pages are a JavaScript app and parts.igem.org returned 403, so the claim that five supporting documents accompany the collection rests on the wiki's own statement.
Survey of 219 respondents, 44.29% under 18, with no mention of consent or ethics oversight; the team does state the sampling limitation and uses the data only for message prioritisation.

The Description's 'to our knowledge, the first project' claim is appropriately hedged ('Among the iGEM project records we reviewed') and prior work (IONIS-Paris 2022) is credited; I found no integrity issue here.
pages_read: Registry: BBa_265XBPWI and BBa_2629PD5P attempted, not retrievable (403 / JS-only app)

calibrated.changed: none. a3 of 3.5 is lower than Mingdao's 4.0 on similar waste-chain fieldwork, but that reflects what the team found rather than how it worked: over 80% of wet BSG is already used, so the need itself is narrower, and the team says so.

one_line.en: A disciplined five-strain comparison with raw replicate data on both a model substrate and real spent grain, plus a built and user-tested fermenter, let down by an unidentified product and a missing attributions page.
one_line.zh: 五株菌的嚴謹比較，模型基質與真實酒糟都附原始重複數據，並有自建且經使用者測試的發酵槽，但產物未經鑑定、歸屬頁缺失。

strengths: Raw per-replicate readings, a stated calibration curve, substrate blank, no-substrate control and parental control for every activity claim
A consistent strain comparison holding across two independent systems, with every intermediate construct informative
Hardware with its own iteration, external user testing with before/after task times, a full bill of materials and an operating decision driven by its own data
Exceptional calibration of language to evidence, including an explicit list of what the team still lacks
weaknesses: The named product was never identified — the chromatography standards used cannot show the substitution that defines it
The headline conversion figure depends on an assumed substrate composition from literature and on subtracting a negative parental baseline
Constructs were never sequence-verified; integration rests on PCR patterns only
No statistical testing and no protein-level evidence of secretion
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404 and the Team page gives bios, not roles
Six standard pages are empty or 404, pushing all evidence into three very long pages
Two figure captions read as unedited instructions to an illustrator
Survey with a large minority of minors reported with no consent or ethics statement

screen.project_title: Jungle PFAS biosensor: RNA-seq promoter discovery plus an MBP-FRET cell-free sensor
screen.what_they_built: Two parallel branches toward a PFAS/PFOA water biosensor: an RNA-seq screen in E. coli BL21 to find PFOA-responsive promoters, and an in-silico redesign of maltose-binding protein into a FRET sensor for PFOA.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); maltose-binding protein scaffold with FRET fluorophores. No BBa part IDs found anywhere on the wiki and no Parts page (parts=0 words); nothing submitted to the Registry that the pack shows.
screen.best_evidence: /results: a 21-sample RNA-seq experiment (control plus six PFOA time/concentration groups, biological triplicates), 19.6-24.8M clean reads per library, Q30 96.8-97.1%, ~99.6% mapping, DESeq2 with BH correction, yielding a six-gene shortlist (bsmA, gadE, yihL, emrR, marR, cadA) with log2FC and p-adj < 0.0005. Supporting OD600 growth curve, NanoDrop purity table for all 21 samples and Qubit quantification on /results.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, traceably: Dr Dibra's advice added the 10/30/90-minute sampling windows and a three-gene signature plan, and Dr Palmer's advice restricted analysis to upregulated genes and switched the team to FDR-corrected p-values (/timeline, /human-practices).
screen.reason: The transcriptomics is well executed for a high school team and the HP is real, but no biosensor was ever built or tested: the FRET branch stops at a single unreplicated 50 ns MD run predicting a FRET efficiency change of at most ~0.09, there are no Registry parts at all, and the Attributions page is a 116-word stub ending in 'Placeholder content for demonstration'. Aspects 2, 7 and 8 are too weak for a top-2 slot.
screen.field_notes: HS-Kentucky (USA, Bioremediation village) addressed PFAS/PFOA contamination in Kentucky waterways with a two-branch biosensor plan. Branch A ran a 21-sample RNA-seq experiment on E. coli BL21 exposed to 0.01 and 10 uM PFOA for 10, 30 and 90 minutes in triplicate, with library QC, DESeq2 analysis by Novogene and a student-run shortlisting pipeline producing six candidate PFOA-responsive promoters (bsmA, gadE, yihL, emrR, marR, cadA); the students note many hits are acid-stress genes, a specificity caveat they plan to test by pH analysis. Branch B used P2Rank, docking and GROMACS to design maltose-binding-protein mutants for PFOA, predicting only a ~0.09 FRET efficiency change from single 50 ns simulations without replicates, and recommending a maltose positive control before any wet-lab build. No cloning, no reporter construct, no Registry parts and no Parts page; sequencing and primary bioinformatics were outsourced to Novogene while culture, treatment and RNA extraction were student work. Human practices is well integrated, with named experts (Dibra, Palmer, Reade, Donovan, farmer Adam Nordell) each changing a specific design decision. The Attributions page is a 116-word stub containing placeholder text.

screen.project_title: BrewZyme: quorum-quenching enzymes immobilized on spent coffee grounds for sewer biofilm control
screen.what_they_built: AHL lactonases (AiiA, AidC, plus AhlX and the metagenomic QQ-2) expressed in E. coli, adsorbed onto alkali-pretreated spent coffee grounds, encapsulated in calcium alginate and packed into a replaceable tea-bag pouch for grease-trap placement; characterized with a purpose-built dual sfGFP/lacZ AHL reporter.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); 6 registered parts - four enzyme CDSs (BBa_26PSKGOJ AiiA, BBa_26NJBJKX AidC, BBa_26FYMBQO AhlX, BBa_26H6PD1O QQ-2) and two composite reporters (BBa_263SXB1Q LuxR-sfGFP, BBa_26T4H42F LuxR-lacZ). Constructs synthesized by Tsingke; transformation, expression and all assays done by the team.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering cycle 3 (the /results page is empty and this data is reachable only through Engineering): coffee grounds loaded with AiiA crude extract knocked the sfGFP reporter signal down dose-dependently - mean fluorescence 598.4 (50 ug/mL) to 351.6 (100) to 152.2 (200) to 35.4 (400) against an AHL-only control of 682.7 and a no-AHL blank of 28.3, n = 4 replicates, with AidC behaving similarly. Storage at 4 C for 24 h and 48 h largely abolished the effect (AiiA 400 ug/mL rose from 35.4 to 646 to 768), which the team reports rather than hides. Reporter calibration on the same page: fluorescence 28.8 to 895.8 on 1 mM AHL and a plateau above 0.01 uM.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, decisively: peer feedback at the South China regional meeting plus field research killed the original "coffee grounds to tagatose" project and produced the quorum-quenching pivot; Professors Yang Liang, Deng Xu and Yang Zhen set the experimental route (confirm AHL is present in real sewers, check competitive binding, choose the right immobilization chemistry); an interview with Bao'an Drainage Co. fixed the product form, deployment point and compliance boundary.
screen.reason: Four completed DBTL cycles with replicated quantitative data, a reporter system the team built and calibrated themselves, a demonstrated immobilized-enzyme function, and a documented stability failure reported honestly - done in a school BSL-1 lab at the open bench. Deserves a full read. The wiki is the weak point: the Results page is literally empty and the Attributions page is four words, so judges must be told the data lives under Engineering and Measurement.
screen.field_notes: Shenzhen high-school team (Biomanufacturing) immobilizing AHL lactonases on spent coffee grounds to block quorum sensing and prevent biofilm in cafe and restaurant drains - waste from one end of the shop treating the problem at the other. Four DBTL cycles: build and calibrate a dual sfGFP/lacZ AHL reporter and show SCG adsorbs beta-Gal; add expression strains and optimize adsorption; immobilize AiiA and AidC and prove dose-dependent AHL degradation (n = 4, with 24 h and 48 h loss of activity at 4 C reported); then generalize to a platform. Six Registry parts, including two composite reporters that are reusable by any quorum-quenching team. Hardware is a calcium-alginate bead pouch, chosen after rejecting a filter cartridge and a hydrogel. Human practices (CAFE/SIP framework) caused a whole-project pivot away from tagatose production and set the experimental route; a drainage utility interview fixed the deployment boundary and compliance picture. Two structural wiki defects: /results is empty and /attributions is four words, so the quantitative evidence is only reachable from Engineering.

screen.project_title: SiShield: engineering rice silicon transporters OsLsi1/OsLsi2 into Nicotiana benthamiana for salt tolerance
screen.what_they_built: They transferred the rice silicic acid influx and efflux transporters OsLsi1 and OsLsi2 into Nicotiana benthamiana under constitutive, root-specific and salt-inducible promoters, including single-vector dual-gene modules, and generated stable transgenic lines. They then measured silicon accumulation, growth and stress physiology under salt stress with and without silicon supplementation.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Nicotiana benthamiana as validation chassis (tomato stable transformation stated as not started), E. coli DH5a and Agrobacterium GV3101; Super1300-C-GFP and Super1300-N-GFP localisation vectors and pBI121 expression backbone with the 35S promoter swapped for pNtREL1 (root-preferential) or pRD29A (stress-inducible); eighteen BBa parts including the dual-transporter cassettes.
screen.best_evidence: /results sections 3-4: promoter behaviour validated in T1 lines by qRT-PCR against NbUBC with three biological and three technical replicates (pNtREL1 root-preferential, pRD29A salt-induced), silicon quantified by molybdenum blue against a standard curve (y = 0.0824x - 0.0786), and after 20 days of 50 mM NaCl the transgenic lines, six replicates each, showed greater leaf area, higher silicon, higher SOD/POD/CAT, lower MDA and electrolyte leakage and higher chlorophyll than WT and empty-vector controls, with the pRD29A dual-gene line best; the C-terminal versus N-terminal GFP comparison (Figures 5 and 6) is a clean documented failure and fix.
screen.hp_integration: An 11,000-word human practices page sits alongside education, entrepreneurship, sustainability and hardware pages; the pack does not show the specific design change traced to a named stakeholder, so the strength of integration needs checking in a full read, but the stated scope restriction (contained N. benthamiana only, no field use of transgenic tobacco) reads as a responsibility-driven decision.
screen.reason: The most complete engineering story in the batch: five iterative cycles that each changed the next design, an empty-vector control alongside wild type, stable transgenic lines rather than transient expression only, promoter specificity verified in both space and stress condition, quantified silicon against a calibration curve, six biological replicates on the physiology, and an explicit synergy metric for the dual-gene module. It also states its own limits plainly (tomato transformation not started, no field data). The open questions for a full read are how much of the confocal, qRT-PCR and physiology work was done by the students (attributions is only 165 words) and whether the synergy claim survives scrutiny.
screen.field_notes: HSET-China (Agriculture village, China) built SiShield, a platform for moving the rice silicon uptake system into a silicon-poor plant to improve salt tolerance, framed by FAO's figure of 1.381 billion hectares of salt-affected soil. Five DBTL cycles drive the project: C-terminal GFP fusions of OsLsi1 and OsLsi2 mislocalised to cytoplasm and nucleus, N-terminal fusions then co-localised cleanly with the CD3-1007 plasma membrane marker, two promoters (root-preferential pNtREL1 and salt-inducible pRD29A) replaced 35S in pBI121, dual-gene cassettes put both transporters on one vector, and a final cycle tested salt stress with and without exogenous silicon. Stable transgenic lines were generated by leaf-disc transformation, T0 and T1 integration confirmed by PCR with WT negative controls, and promoter behaviour verified by qRT-PCR against NbUBC with three biological and three technical replicates. Silicon content was measured by molybdenum blue colorimetry against a standard curve; after 20 days of 50 mM NaCl the transgenic lines, six replicates each, kept larger leaf area, more silicon, higher SOD/POD/CAT, lower MDA and electrolyte leakage and more chlorophyll than wild type and an empty-vector control, with the pRD29A dual-gene line strongest. The team defined explicit metrics (root enrichment ratio, salt-induced fold change, silicon accumulation fold, an interaction score for synergy, and a biomass improvement index) and reports positive synergy. Eighteen Registry parts, a 3,614-word hardware page, a proof-of-concept page, and repeated statements that tomato stable transformation has not started and that field and pesticide-reduction claims remain unvalidated.

screen.project_title: ORA-GUARD: engineered oral probiotic for halitosis (VSC degradation)
screen.what_they_built: Sox multi-enzyme complex and methanethiol oxidase (MTO) expressed in E. coli and intended for CRISPR-Cas9 genomic integration into Streptococcus salivarius K12, plus a four-layer biosafety stack (GRAS chassis, D-Ala auxotrophy, PcspA/RNA-thermometer CcdB kill switch, marker removal). Enzymes are meant to scavenge H2S, CH3SH and dimethyl sulfide from saliva.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21 + pET-28a(+) for expression; S. salivarius K12 with pSET4s-based CRISPR plasmid as the final chassis. No BBa part IDs appear anywhere on the wiki and there is no Parts page.
screen.best_evidence: /results Figs 6-10: SDS-PAGE of purified SoxXA, SoxYZ, SoxB, SoxCD and MTO at expected masses with untransformed-lysate and wash-buffer controls; /engineering Fig 5 shows plasmid loss after 5 days of passage without selection, which drove the switch to genomic integration. /results Figs 15-17 claim ORA-GUARD degrades VSCs comparably to purified enzyme with Blank, wild-type K12 and PureEnzyme arms (n=3, 0-24 h), but no numbers are quoted in the text.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in several places: 745 survey responses pushed biosafety from a single safeguard to four layers, dentist interviews changed the dosage form from capsule to mouthwash/lozenge, and ethics/biosafety advisers plus the plasmid-loss data together drove the move from plasmid to chromosomal integration.
screen.reason: Much of the Results page is written in planning or expectation tense rather than as completed work ('we plan to first clone', 'the survival rate is expected to decrease sharply', 'this part of the experiment remains to be further optimized'), and the auxotroph still grew without D-Ala. No Registry parts, no Parts page, no attributions page and no notebook, which caps aspects 7 and 8 hard. The engineering page also names Paracoccus pantotrophus K12 as the chassis where everything else says S. salivarius K12, an unresolved contradiction. Solid medal-level work, not top-2.
screen.field_notes: ICJFLS (Jinan Foreign Language School, CHN, Therapeutics) built ORA-GUARD, an engineered oral probiotic that degrades the volatile sulfur compounds behind halitosis. Sox (SoxXA/SoxYZ/SoxB/SoxCD from Paracoccus pantotrophus) and MTO (Hyphomicrobium sp.) were codon-optimised, cloned separately into pET-28a(+) with a pelB secretion signal, expressed in BL21 and His-purified, with SDS-PAGE at expected masses for all five constructs. A single-plasmid CRISPR-Cas9 system on temperature-sensitive pSET4s was used to integrate the cassettes into S. salivarius K12, verified by colony PCR, followed by temperature-based plasmid curing. VSC degradation was assayed in DROOL artificial saliva with Fusobacterium nucleatum as the producer, OralChroma/GC-MS readout, n=3, four arms including purified enzyme; the figures are present but no degradation percentages are stated. Biosafety is a declared four-layer system, but the auxotroph still grew without D-alanine and the kill-switch CFU result is written as expected rather than measured. Two contributions are offered for reuse: an S. salivarius K12 culture and electroporation protocol with troubleshooting (the team argues no prior iGEM team genetically manipulated K12) and a parametric ODE enzyme-kinetics simulator. No BBa parts, no Parts or Attributions page.

screen.project_title: AURA: an inline miR-223 biosensor for bovine mastitis
screen.what_they_built: A DNA 'catapult' hairpin probe re-targeted from miR-21 to miR-223 (a mastitis inflammation marker in milk), read out by 6-FAM/BHQ-1 fluorescence, plus a proposed FET sensing chamber, CAD hardware and the UdderNet software platform. The molecular sensing module was built and tested; the integrated inline device was not.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Cell-free synthetic oligonucleotides (no living chassis). Seven Registry parts: four catapult probe variants (BBa_26PD7O10 baseline, BBa_26IRC2X4 1bp invasion replacement, BBa_268GQMMU stem -2bp, BBa_26U24IU9 3'-end -2bp lead) and three reset strands (BBa_26LF0186, BBa_263Q2IYI, BBa_26LMF1QY).
screen.best_evidence: /results Experiment 1: five probe designs compared head-to-head at 120 min, 3 technical replicates each; SNR 6.41 (original miR-21), 6.73 (baseline miR-223), 11.81 (stem -2bp), 15.59 (1bp replacement), 17.96 (3'-end -2bp), with water blank 208 RFU and SDs reported. /results Experiment 2: synthetic miR-223 RNA at 39 C rose 4,138 to 20,595 RFU (+397.7%) vs no-target control -336 RFU; RNase H reset dropped RNA signal 26,466 to 7,279 RFU (-72.5%) vs -18.1% for the untreated DNA reference.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: Swiss smallholder farmers said a mastitis-only test was not worth the cost, which moved the target to large dairies and to an inline design integrated into the milking line; a vet at Cattle Health Switzerland pushed them to complement existing conductivity sensors and shaped UdderNet's use of existing temperature/pH feeds; EPFL FET researcher Nakatsuka changed the probe tether and stem length and flagged free-ion interference in raw milk.
screen.reason: Five genuine DBTL cycles with replicated quantitative data at every step, a measurable engineering improvement (SNR 6.73 to 17.96) carried through to RNA at body temperature, an honest failed cycle (bead-based strand displacement, with the loss-vs-reset confound named), and HP that visibly redirected the product. Weak points a full read must test: no FET readout, nothing measured in milk, parts page empty, attributions page essentially blank (8 words), and placeholder figures on the homepage ('up to US $0 billion', '< 0%').
screen.field_notes: Institut-Le-Rosey-CH (Switzerland, Agriculture village) built AURA, a proposed inline milk biosensor for subclinical bovine mastitis that detects miR-223, a host inflammation microRNA. They adapted the published Park et al. miR-21 'catapult' DNA actuator to miR-223 and ran five DBTL cycles: NUPACK-style free-energy screening of nine variants, fluorescence comparison of four built probes (SNR 6.73 baseline to 17.96 for the 3'-end -2bp lead, BBa_26U24IU9), validation with real synthetic miR-223 RNA at 39 C (+16,457 RFU over 30 min vs a flat no-target control), an RNase H reset that cut RNA signal 72.5% and allowed re-detection, and a toehold strand-displacement reset that failed inconclusively because streptavidin beads were lost during washing. Seven parts are registered with sequences and matched characterization. Hardware is CAD only (sliding-sleeve sampling valve, FET sensing chamber, ~100 mm fitting) and the FET readout was never built, so fluorescence stands in for the real transducer and nothing was tested in milk. Human Practices with Swiss farmers, a Cattle Health Switzerland vet and EPFL bio-FET researcher Nako Nakatsuka moved the target from small to large farms, made the device inline, and changed the probe tether and stem length.

screen.project_title: Slimbio: natural sulfotransferase (SULT) inhibitors from Chinese herbs as an anti-obesity functional food
screen.what_they_built: Heterologous expression of three human cytosolic sulfotransferases (SULT2A1, SULT2B1, SULT1E1) in E. coli for in vitro inhibitor screening, plus a pETDuet UGT88D4 + UGD dual-enzyme system for biosynthesis of flavonoid glycosides.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with pET29a and pETDuet-1; 5 new basic parts (SULT2A1 BBa_26MCZCKK, SULT2B1 BBa_26N8AR13, SULT1E1 BBa_262P51YG, UGT88D4 BBa_26OD8QOI, UGD BBa_266LC6KG) and 4 composite parts including BBa_264KX9Q7 (UGT88D4-UGD).
screen.best_evidence: /results and /model: 4-methylumbelliferone fluorescence assay with 12-point dose-response curves (0.1-200 µM) against all three isoforms, giving IC50 ~8 µM for mefenamic acid against SULT2B1, ~25-35 µM for the other best pairs and 35-55 µM for SULT2A1, with Lineweaver-Burk double-reciprocal plots indicating a competitive pattern for SULT2B1; docking scores (-7.6 to -7.1 kcal/mol for the best ligand) are compared against the wet-lab ranking.
screen.hp_integration: Partly. Three named academics (Profs Huo, Wu and Duan) are recorded as revising the SULT2B1 target hypothesis, reordering biosynthesis and yield priorities, and replacing a single endpoint with layered safety/function/mechanism validation; Dr Bao moved the output from a research prototype toward a health-food regulatory pathway.
screen.reason: Competent medal-level work but not finalist calibre. The synthetic biology is thin - mostly heterologous expression of human enzymes as assay reagents, with one genuine two-enzyme biosynthesis construct - and the headline claim (herbal anti-obesity food) is several steps beyond an in vitro IC50 with no cell or animal data. IC50s were interpolated by defining 0% and 100% inhibition from the end points of a single curve rather than fitting, and the model and results pages disagree on which compound inhibits which isoform. The description page is riddled with spelling errors and one candidate is described both as 'glucuronic acid' and 'oroxylin A glucuronide', while mefenamic acid (an NSAID) is presented inside a natural-herb framing. No attributions page.
screen.field_notes: JZIB-QDHS (Food & Nutrition, China) proposes Slimbio, an anti-obesity functional food built on inhibiting cytosolic sulfotransferases linked to lipid and steroid metabolism. Three human isoforms, SULT2A1 (852 bp), SULT2B1 (1092 bp) and SULT1E1 (879 bp), were amplified, cloned into pET29a by homologous recombination, sequence-verified, expressed in BL21(DE3) with IPTG optimisation and low-temperature (16 C) induction for solubility, and checked by SDS-PAGE. Activity was measured with a 4-methylumbelliferone fluorescence assay using PAPS as the sulfo donor, where loss of fluorescence tracks sulfation. Three candidates from docking - mefenamic acid, a glucuronide labelled QCZS, and amentoflavone - were tested over 12 concentrations from 0.1 to 200 µM; the strongest result was roughly 8 µM against SULT2B1, with SULT2A1 least sensitive at 35-55 µM, and Lineweaver-Burk plots read as competitive inhibition. AutoDock Vina scores (best around -7.6 kcal/mol) are cross-checked against the assay ranking, including one ligand with positive, clashing scores against SULT1E1. A separate pETDuet UGT88D4 + UGD dual-expression construct was built for flavonoid glycoside biosynthesis with HPLC analysis. Nine parts were contributed. Integrated human practices is structured in four stages with three named expert iteration cycles plus a regulatory consultation. There is no attributions page, no hardware or software, the description page has many spelling errors, and the model and results pages give inconsistent IC50 assignments.

screen.project_title: BIO-NOVA / MANUCODE: dual-enzyme biosynthesis of UDCA from poultry gallbladder CDCA
screen.what_they_built: A 7alpha-HSDH / 7beta-HSDH cascade in E. coli BL21(DE3) converting waste-derived chenodeoxycholic acid to ursodeoxycholic acid, improved by semi-rational cofactor-switching mutagenesis of 7beta-HSDH and by rigid/flexible linker fusion of the two enzymes.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5alpha for cloning, BL21(DE3) for expression; pRSF-Duet vector. Wild-type co-expression plasmid, four point mutants (E18A, R40A, R41A, S68A) and two fusion constructs with (EAAAK)2 and (GGGGS)2 linkers. 19 new BBa parts registered, with a /part-collection page.
screen.best_evidence: /results section 6: HPLC whole-cell catalysis with standard curves for CDCA, 7-KLCA and UDCA showing R41A and S68A mutants giving higher UDCA titres than the mutant baseline, and the flexible (GGGGS)2 fusion strain giving markedly lower 7-KLCA intermediate accumulation and higher UDCA than the free dual-enzyme control. Section 5 WST-8 cofactor assays (NADH curve y=0.2435x+0.0358, R2=0.9926) show the R41A mutant with the best NAD+ utilisation and near-zero NADPH consumption, i.e. the designed cofactor switch worked.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: stakeholder mapping plus patient consultations (a long-term UDCA user on affordability) and eight expert interviews (hepatology, VC, poultry supply chain, biocatalysis, compliance) are tied to a 'Summary of Project Iterations' listing changes undertaken, including pressure to justify the waste-sourcing route against existing enzymatic processes.
screen.reason: This is a complete design-build-test-learn arc that ends in product: the cofactor mismatch was diagnosed, four rational mutants were made and assayed, the winning strategy (flexible-linker fusion) was then shown by HPLC to cut intermediate accumulation and raise UDCA titre. Controls (empty vector, enzyme-free blanks, wild-type) are stated throughout and sequence verification is complete. Worth a full read; the panel should check how much of the HPLC, affinity chromatography and protein purification the students did themselves, since there is no attributions page in the crawl and reported numeric titres live mostly in figures rather than text.
screen.field_notes: KCIS (Bioremediation, China) built BIO-NOVA/MANUCODE, a two-enzyme E. coli platform converting chenodeoxycholic acid from discarded poultry gallbladders into ursodeoxycholic acid, the first-line drug for primary biliary cholangitis, as an alternative to bear bile and chemical synthesis. In pRSF-Duet/BL21(DE3) they built a wild-type 7alpha-HSDH/7beta-HSDH co-expression plasmid, four 7beta-HSDH point mutants chosen by homology modelling of the cofactor pocket (E18A, R40A, R41A, S68A), and two fusion enzymes with (EAAAK)2 and (GGGGS)2 linkers; all were confirmed by full-length Sanger sequencing and purified by Ni and Strep-Tactin affinity chromatography with SDS-PAGE at 28.7, 30.5 and 60 kDa. WST-8 cofactor assays with standard curves showed the designed NADPH-to-NADH preference switch, R41A best; HPLC of whole-cell catalysis quantified CDCA consumption, 7-KLCA accumulation and UDCA formation, with the flexible-linker fusion reducing intermediate buildup and raising UDCA titre. Integrated human practices covers patients, a hepatologist, investors, poultry supply chain and compliance experts, with an explicit project-iteration table. Nineteen new Registry parts and a part collection page; no attributions page was crawled.

screen.project_title: Herculyeast — secreted yeast proteinase and lipase for household food-waste pretreatment
screen.what_they_built: Engineered S. cerevisiae carrying MFalpha1 prepro-leader fusions to PEP4 (Proteinase A) and TGL1 (sterol esterase) under pGAL1,10 or ADH1 promoters, intended to secrete hydrolases that pre-digest household food waste. Proposed products are a household two-chamber reactor and an enzyme drain unblocker.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. cerevisiae BY4741 (and E. coli for cloning); 2-micron shuttle plasmid donated by Academia Sinica. 8 BBa 2026 part IDs, including pGAL1,10-prepro and pGAL1,10-prepro-PEP4 composite parts. Builds on UM_Macau 2021 and the team's own 2023 secretion chassis.
screen.best_evidence: /results: RT-qPCR galactose time-course for pGAL1,10-prepro-PEP4 in BY4741 — ~3-fold at 30 min, 7-fold at 60 min, 10-fold at 90 min, dropping to 5-fold at 120 min, with no prepro-PEP4 mRNA in the pGAL1,10-prepro control at any time point. Six gel figures (Figs 1-6) document PCR and colony-PCR confirmation of prepro, PEP4 and ADH1-TGL1 cloning steps against sized ladders.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in a limited, mostly commercial direction — the microeconomics expert's feedback visibly rewrote the Business Model Canvas, pod pricing (NTD 1000 to 900) and reactor siting, and expert advice redirected functional testing from Western blot to RT-qPCR, but no stakeholder input changed the core biology.
screen.reason: Clean cloning and one good induction time-course, but the project never shows the enzyme working: the casein degradation assay is explicitly incomplete ("We are currently performing..."), four of six planned constructs were never built, and no secreted-activity or food-waste data exists. Transcription is not function, so aspect 2 stays low. A strong, honest gold-medal wiki, not a top-2 project.
screen.field_notes: KCIS-Xiugang-Taipei (Taiwan, Food & Nutrition) built Herculyeast: S. cerevisiae secreting Proteinase A (PEP4) and sterol esterase (TGL1) via an MFalpha1 prepro leader to pretreat household food waste ahead of Taiwan's 2027 swill-feeding ban. Cloning is documented gel-by-gel (prepro 267 bp, PEP4 1215 bp, TGL1 1647 bp) with colony PCR and positive controls; pGAL1,10-prepro and pGAL1,10-prepro-PEP4 were registered as composite parts. The one functional dataset is an RT-qPCR galactose induction time-course reaching ~10-fold at 90 min with a flat prepro-only control; the casein spectrophotometric activity assay and all ADH1-prepro constructs were not completed and the team says so plainly. A 13.5k-word model page builds three models including a user-facing degradation-rate calculator, revised after a professor rejected the Frossling correlation for a slurry reactor in favour of a Sherwood correlation for agitated multi-particle systems. Human practices is heavily entrepreneurial (business model, pod subscription pricing, B2C/B2B/B2G framing) with 4.4k words on entrepreneurship and 5.7k on education; attributions are itemised per member and PI. Failure discussion is a real strength: the engineering page records model errors and the ADH1 cloning failure as learning.

screen.project_title: FELIX: a lipase disinfection spray plus an EcN-delivered RNAi platform against feline coronavirus
screen.what_they_built: A two-barrier system for feline infectious peritonitis: recombinant GDSL lipases (CbAE-1, CbAE-2) as the active ingredient of an environmental spray that strips the viral lipid envelope, and engineered E. coli Nissle 1917 carrying anti-N shRNA, a V4-ELP-EEP13 self-assembling nanoparticle monomer, a quorum-sensing-coupled oscillatory lysis circuit for release, and a cold-inducible Doc/Phd kill switch.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5-alpha, BL21(DE3) and EcN 1917; pET28a(+). 16 new parts including four lipases (Est29, Lip29, CbAE-1 BBa_26QZKDR1, CbAE-2), V4-ELP-EEP13, two shRNAs, and the composite J23119-RBS2-RNAT_U6-1-phd (BBa_26CAPW3Q); builds on BBa_K2969047 (UCAS-China 2019), BBa_K3143002 and BBa_K4761040.
screen.best_evidence: /results section 2.4 and /contribution: the improved cold-inducible toxin-antitoxin switch gives an escape frequency of 3.19x10^-3 +/- 0.199 across three replicate plate counts, about an order of magnitude below the 2.318x10^-2 +/- 0.122 reported for the original UCAS-China 2019 device, with 25 C vs 37 C growth curves alongside. The lipase evidence is comparative halo size on egg-yolk LB agar (CbAE-1/2 beating Est29/Lip29), and the oscillatory lysis circuit did not oscillate - the OD600 curves show only suppressed growth, which the team reports and explains.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - a 439-response owner survey, a China Agricultural University vet (Dr. Zhang) and a cat-cafe/cattery operator moved the project off post-onset treatment and diagnosis entirely, onto pre-mutation prevention plus litter-box-scenario environmental decontamination; Dr. Zhang also supplied the reference that identified CbAE-1/2, and a spray droplet size above 50 um was adopted on inhalation-safety advice.
screen.reason: Ambitious five-module design but the evidence does not reach finalist level. The only properly quantified result is the kill-switch escape frequency, and that is a single assay set; the lipase claim rests on halo size on egg yolk agar with no FCoV or even liposome assay; the oscillatory lysis circuit failed to oscillate; and the entire delivery module - nanoparticle assembly, siRNA protection, knockdown - is supported only by citations to Eweje et al., which the team states openly. The improved-part comparison against UCAS-China 2019 is the strongest piece of work here and a good medal case. Attribution is a blocker: the /attributions page is an unloaded embedded form (76 words).
screen.field_notes: KCSCD (Therapeutics, CHN) built FELIX against feline infectious peritonitis, splitting the problem into environmental decontamination and in-vivo prevention after a vet and a cattery operator argued them out of diagnosis and treatment. Four GDSL lipases were cloned into pET28a(+)/BL21 and compared by halo size on egg-yolk LB agar; CbAE-1 and CbAE-2 from Chromobacterium sp. Beijing outperformed Est29 and Lip29 and were carried forward as spray actives, though no assay against FCoV, a pseudovirus or even a liposome was run. The in-vivo arm engineers EcN to express an anti-N shRNA plus the V4-ELP-EEP13 nanoparticle monomer; because neither is secretable, release depends on a LuxRm/LuxI quorum-sensing circuit with aiiA negative feedback driving lysis protein E. That circuit did not oscillate: OD600 showed only reduced growth, which the team attributes to debris masking the dynamics and to leaky lysis expression, and they propose degradation tags and viable counts next. The delivery claims (near-100% siRNA encapsulation, ~75% GFP and ~95% GAPDH knockdown) are all quoted from Eweje et al. 2026, explicitly labelled as literature feasibility rather than their own data. The best work is the biosafety module: they improved UCAS-China 2019's cold-inducible Doc switch (BBa_K2969047) by adding the Phd antitoxin, HiZJU-China 2023's RNA thermometer U6-1 upstream of phd, and an arabinose redundancy, measuring an escape frequency of 3.19x10^-3 +/- 0.199 against the original's 2.318x10^-2. A delay-differential-equation model of the oscillator (Novak-Tyson framework, Hopf bifurcation, Hill n=2 to 4, 20 min delay) was built alongside and used to interpret the failure. The attributions page is a broken embedded form, and figure numbering on the Results page skips from 7 to 9.

screen.project_title: Synbeans — engineered S. cerevisiae for coffee-processing wastewater (pectin and lactate degradation)
screen.what_they_built: Two immobilised yeast strains: one secreting polygalacturonase PgaA to break down pectin, one expressing JEN1/CYB2/DLD1 to consume L- and D-lactate, both carrying a MazEF temperature kill switch, encapsulated in sodium alginate beads and tested in simulated coffee wastewater.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. cerevisiae W303 with pRS426 (URA3, TEF1 promoter, alpha-factor secretion signal); E. coli DH5a for cloning. ~14 new BBa_26* parts plus a part-collection page (pgaA, pelB, PME, JEN1, CYB2, DLD1, MazEF).
screen.best_evidence: /results: three candidate pectinases compared head to head — clear-zone diameters 1.257 cm (PgaA), 0.917 (PelB), 0 (PME) with CK at 0, and DNS-quantified conversion of 10 mg/mL pectin at 25% (PgaA) versus 2% (PelB) and 0% (PME), with PBS and empty-yeast controls negligible; pH/temperature optima mapped (50 C, pH 5). Lactate: HPLC total lactate (standard curve R2=0.9851) showing 167.7 consumed by the engineered strain at 72 h versus 116.6 by empty-vector yeast, plus separate L- and D-lactate assays showing D-lactate consumed only by the engineered strain.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, with an explicit decision table: Prof. Feng Xie's point on contact time replaced the fast-flowing exit with a storage/treatment tank and added residence time and oxygen transfer as operating parameters; plant manager Yunhai Jiang's input repositioned Synbeans as a possible pre- or secondary treatment compatible with downstream systems.
screen.reason: Enzyme candidates chosen by measured comparison rather than assertion, two functions demonstrated with proper empty-vector controls and HPLC, a working kill switch, immobilisation, and application-level COD/pH readouts in simulated wastewater — all tied to field-based human practices with a documented decision trail. Deserves a full read as a top-2 candidate.
screen.field_notes: Keystone (Synbeans, China) engineered S. cerevisiae W303 to treat coffee-processing wastewater, which is acidic and loaded with pectin and lactate. They cloned three pectin-active enzymes (pgaA, pelB, PME) into pRS426 under TEF1, verified by sequencing and colony PCR, showed no growth burden, and compared them directly: clear-zone diameters of 1.257, 0.917 and 0 cm and DNS-based conversion of 25%, 2% and 0% on 10 mg/mL pectin, with PBS and empty-yeast controls flat, so PgaA was carried forward (optimum 50 C, pH 5). A second strain expressing JEN1, CYB2 and DLD1 consumed both lactate enantiomers; separate L-/D-lactate assays showed empty-vector yeast touches only L-lactate while the engineered strain also removes D-lactate, and HPLC (R2=0.9851) gave 167.7 consumed versus 116.6 for the negative control at 72 h. Both strains carry a MazEF kill switch shown to block colony formation at 10, 20 and 40 C while leaving 30 C growth unaffected, and both were immobilised in sodium alginate microspheres with COD and pH measured in simulated wastewater. Human Practices is unusually substantive for a high school team (17k words): a Yunnan coffee plant visit, street interviews, a power-interest matrix and a table mapping each stakeholder insight to a design decision and the validation still outstanding — Feng Xie's contact-time point added a treatment tank and residence/oxygen parameters, and a processing-plant manager repositioned the system as a pre- or secondary treatment. Education, entrepreneurship and SDG pages are large; no hardware or measurement page.

justification.a1: Synbeans builds several linked results of rising difficulty: three pectinases cloned and compared in S. cerevisiae W303, the winner (pgaA, 25% conversion vs pelB 2%, PME 0%, Results Table 3) re-engineered with an alpha-factor secretion signal, a three-gene lactate module (JEN1-CYB2-DLD1), a mazEF temperature kill switch, alginate-chitosan immobilisation, then simulated and real coffee wastewater trials. That is close to GreatBay-style escalation in scope. It falls short of a 5 because the end of the chain is the weakest link: on the real sample pH moved only 3.23 to 3.67 and the COD table (Results, Part 5) reports values of 6 and 2-4 mg/L, which cannot be coffee wastewater the team itself describes as 2,000-7,400 mg/L.
justification.a2: Enzyme-level function is genuinely demonstrated with controls: clear-zone assay with CK and empty-yeast NC at zero and measured diameters in triplicate (Results Table 2), DNS galacturonic acid quantitation against a standard curve, and temperature/pH optima where PBS blank and empty-yeast controls stay at baseline (Figure 10). Immobilised pgaA degraded pectin in simulated wastewater to ~1.5 mg/mL galacturonic acid over 96 h with blank and NC flat and significance marked (Figures 18-19). The lactate claim is weaker: the empty-vector strain itself consumed 116.6 of the units the engineered strain consumed 167.7 (Results, HPLC section), so the engineered gain over the chassis is modest and reported without units or n, and the kill switch only shows construct-specific killing at 20 degrees since the team states 10 and 40 degrees kill wild-type yeast too (Figure 28).
justification.a3: The impact case is better grounded than most: a team member visited a Yunnan wet-processing factory (Description, Figure 1), the team obtained real coffee wastewater and ran COD and pH on it (Results, Part 5), and processors, a village secretary and a policy researcher shaped where the system could be deployed (Human Practices). But the measured effect on the real sample is small and the headline COD figures are internally inconsistent in units, so the link from the team's own data to the stated goal of COD below 150 mg/L and pH 6.0-8.0 (Description, Goals) is not yet made.
justification.a4: There is one clean, data-driven redesign: the first clear-zone assay with whole cells produced no halo (Engineering, Learn 1.1, Figure 14 labelled Failed), the team reasoned with Prof. Xie Feng that pectin cannot cross the yeast wall, added the alpha-factor signal in Cycle 1.2, and the secreted enzyme then produced a 2.36 cm clear zone and degraded pectin in simulated wastewater. A second, smaller iteration changed the assay itself from spotting cells to spotting purified protein. The cycles are clearly laid out as Design/Build/Test/Learn with part IDs, but quantifiable success criteria are mostly stated after the fact, and the dry lab contributes AlphaFold structure prediction only rather than a process model that feeds back into design.
justification.a5: Human Practices is the strongest section. The ECPR framework (Engage, Capture, Project iteration, Re-verify) is applied to roughly a dozen stakeholders, and the overview table explicitly separates decisions already adopted from what still needs validating. Concrete changes are traceable: Feng Xie's residence-time point replaced a fast-flow exit with a storage/treatment tank; Yuhan Bao's containment argument removed open-environment application from the near-term plan; Jiazhi Hou's input deleted the assumed certification price premium; Yunhai Jiang's plant-scale contrast repositioned Synbeans as a pre-treatment or secondary step. This is two-way dialogue shaping the design, close to the GreatBay standard.
justification.a6: The notebook timeline names a lead student for nearly every activity and records that safety training and technique teaching came from Mr. Baldeep and Ms. Duan, which reads as student-run bench work. Members also describe their own tasks (one member names gene-cassette construction and protein purification). Against that, the standard /attributions page returns 404 and the team page carries personal bios rather than task attribution, so wet-lab entries collapse to 'All Wet Lab Students' and it is not stated who ran the HPLC, the Sanger sequencing or the gene synthesis. The Awards page says an Attributions Form exists, but a form submitted elsewhere is not something I can read.
justification.a7: This is squarely synthetic biology with standard components: a pRS426 shuttle backbone with TEF1p/CYC1t and a second ADH1p/ADH1t cassette, an alpha-factor secretion signal, codon-optimised heterologous enzyme genes, a P2A-linked polycistronic lactate cassette, and reuse of an existing Registry part, MazEF BBa_K4990016, taken with credit from CPU-China 2023. Twelve new parts are declared with IDs, types and functions in the Part Collection table. Like TAS Taipei, most parts are not novel, but the devices are real engineered genetic constructs assembled from standard elements.
justification.a8: The wiki documents constructs thoroughly: plasmid maps, sequencing verification, a part table with IDs, types and functions, and full protocols on Experiments. The Registry side I could not confirm, and several documentation faults are visible from the wiki alone: the standard /parts, /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation and /measurement URLs all 404, and the part counts contradict each other (Part Collection says 13 new parts, 6 basic and 7 composite; Contribution says 13 new parts, 9 basic and 4 composite, with a table listing 12). The alpha-factor is described as fused at the C-terminus in Description and Engineering Learn 1.1 but at the N-terminus in Learn 1.2, which matters for a secretion signal.
justification.w1: The homepage carries the reader from coffee cherry anatomy to wastewater COD/BOD/pH figures to the three-module design (pectin, lactate, mazEF biosafety) and the Build/Express/Test outline, all with the one-line summary 'Engineering living systems for more sustainable coffee wastewater treatment.' Problem, approach and system are clear quickly. The scroll-driven animation means the outcome itself is a little further down than one screen, which is the only real drift.
justification.w2: Most key claims are tied to a named figure with controls identified in the caption: CK and NC lanes on the SDS-PAGE (Figure 6), blank and empty-yeast controls on the enzyme assays, blank plus empty-vector negative control on the lactate and pectin time courses, standard curves with stated R2, and significance levels defined. Triplicates are stated for the protein concentration, clear-zone and wastewater sampling. It stops short of 5 because n and error bars are not stated everywhere, the real-sample COD figures are semi-quantitative with implausible units, and one consumption value is given to ten decimal places with no units.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly (Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Engagement) with a search box, and the Awards page maps the work onto medal criteria, which helps a judge. The friction is real though: six standard page URLs return 404, so a judge going straight to /parts, /attributions or /proof-of-concept finds nothing and has to work out that the content lives under Part Collection, Contribution and Results. The heavy homepage animation also slows a reader who wants the result.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way with this: the Experiments page gives full protocols from media recipes through transformation, SDS-PAGE, DNS and HPLC conditions, the Notebook adds six sets of scanned experimental records as PDFs, the Part Collection lists every construct, and the failed first clear-zone assay is shown and explained rather than hidden. Raw numeric data behind the figures are not posted as tables or files, which is what keeps it below a 5.
justification.w5: Referencing is dense and mostly resolvable, with DOIs on the primary literature throughout Description, Contribution and Model, the assay kits linked to their supplier pages, prior iGEM work credited (CPU-China 2023 for the temperature-regulated mazEF system, plus Registry links), and the AI-generated Figure 3 in Description openly labelled as such. Deductions are small: some background claims lean on blog and vendor pages, and the COD range cited as 2,000-7,400 mg/L in Description becomes 8,000-15,000 mg/L in Model against the same Figueroa Campos reference.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete high-school wet-lab project: three pectinases screened with controls, a data-driven secretion redesign, a lactate module and a kill switch, let down at the end by weak and unit-confused real-wastewater data and several missing standard pages.
strengths: Enzyme screening done properly: clear-zone diameters in triplicate with CK and empty-yeast controls at zero, DNS quantitation against a standard curve, and a stated conversion comparison (pgaA 25%, pelB 2%, PME 0%) that includes the enzyme that did not work (Results Tables 2-3).

A genuine DBTL loop driven by a failure: the first whole-cell clear-zone assay produced no halo (Engineering Figure 14, labelled Failed), the team diagnosed that pectin cannot cross the yeast wall, added the alpha-factor signal, and the secreted enzyme then cleared pectin and degraded it in simulated wastewater.

Integrated Human Practices with traceable consequences: the ECPR table separates adopted decisions from open questions, and names specific changes (storage tank for residence time, open-environment use dropped, certification premium removed, repositioning as pre-treatment).

Controls appear in the application experiments too: both a blank and an immobilised empty-vector yeast negative control run alongside the engineered strain in the pectin, L-/D-lactate and HPLC time courses, which is what exposed the chassis's own lactate consumption.
Reproducibility is well served: full protocols on Experiments, six sets of scanned experimental records on Notebook, plasmid maps, and a part table giving ID, type and function for every construct.
weaknesses: The real-sample COD result, which carries the application claim, reports 6 mg/L untreated and 2-4 mg/L treated, three orders of magnitude below the 2,000-7,400 mg/L the team cites for coffee wastewater; no n, no method detail beyond a colour change, and no dilution factor is given (Results, Part 5).

The engineered lactate gain over the chassis is modest and under-analysed: the empty-vector strain consumed 116.6 to the engineered strain's 167.7 at 72 h, reported without units and to ten decimal places, and the HPLC standard curve runs to 1000 mg/mL, which is not a credible lactic acid series.

Kill-switch evidence rests on a single temperature: the team itself notes 10 and 40 degrees are unsuitable for yeast growth, so only the 20-degree point distinguishes mazEF strains from wild type, and there is no reporter data showing the NoChill06 RNA thermometer actually gates MazE translation in yeast.

The stated project goals (COD to below 150 mg/L, pH restored to 6.0-8.0) are not met or honestly reconciled: pH on the real sample moved only 3.23 to 3.67, and the wiki does not step back to say how far short that is.

Documentation inconsistencies: /parts, /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /measurement and /protocols all 404; the new-part count is given two different ways on two pages; and the alpha-factor is placed at the C-terminus on one page and the N-terminus on another.
red_flags: COD values on the real coffee wastewater (6 mg/L untreated, 2-4 mg/L treated) are inconsistent by roughly 1000-fold with the team's own cited influent range; I would treat the COD removal claim as unsupported until the raw method and dilution are shown.
No attributions page on the wiki (/attributions returns 404) and the team page gives bios, not task-level attribution; who ran the HPLC, Sanger sequencing and gene synthesis is not stated.

Description Figure 3 is an AI-generated illustration. The team labels it openly as 'Picture generated by Doubao AI', so this is honest disclosure of an illustrative image, not evidentiary figure manipulation, and I raise no integrity concern.

Registry entries for the 12 new parts could not be inspected from here (parts.igem.org returned 403 and registry.igem.org renders client-side), so aspect 8 is scored on the wiki's part table alone; the Registry depth should be checked directly before the panel settles a8.
Several standard page URLs are missing, which under p.29 puts content where a judge would have to hunt for it, even though the material does exist elsewhere inside the team namespace.
pages_read: crawl_meta.json (404 status of parts, attributions, proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement, protocols, design, software, hardware, inclusivity)

calibrated.changed: none. a2 3.5 matches SHSID and Mingdao: the enzyme-level work has proper blank and empty-vector controls, but the end-of-chain claim (COD removal on the real sample) is unsupported, and the lactate gain over the chassis is small and reported without units or n.

justification.a1: Real scope for a high school team: three pectinases screened and compared quantitatively, the winner re-built with an alpha-factor secretion signal, a separate three-gene lactate module (JEN1/CYB2/DLD1), a mazEF temperature kill switch, alginate-chitosan immobilisation, and a test on real coffee wastewater (Results Parts 1-5). It is a chain of increasingly difficult steps in the GreatBay sense, but the final stage is weak: real-sample pH moved only 3.23 to 3.67 at 72 h (Results Table 4) and the COD numbers are reported in units that cannot be reconciled with their own 2000-7400 mg/L background. Strong medal-level scope, short of finalist scale because the integrated system is demonstrated but not shown to work.
justification.a2: The core functions are measured, not just claimed: clear-zone diameters with a CK of 0 (Results Table 2, pgaA 1.257 cm vs pelB 0.917, PME 0), DNS-quantified conversion of 25% for pgaA vs 2% for pelB against PBS and empty-yeast controls (Table 3, Figure 10), SDS-PAGE bands at the predicted masses with an empty-vector lane (Figure 6), and lactate removal by the immobilised engineered strain significantly below both blank and empty-vector controls for L- and D-lactate (Figure 23) plus an HPLC time course (Figures 24-25). Two weaknesses hold this below 4: the kill-switch test is confounded, since no colonies grew at 10 or 40 C for wild type either, so only the 20 C point is informative (Figure 28, and the team says so); and the real-sample COD result (CK 6 mg/L, treated 2-4 mg/L, Results Figure 30) is a single colorimetric reading with no replicates and units three orders of magnitude off the stated influent load.
justification.a3: The route to use is concrete and stakeholder-checked rather than generic: after Yunhai Jiang (processing-plant management) and Feng Xie, Synbeans was repositioned as a pre-treatment or secondary step inside a managed system with residence time and oxygen transfer as operating parameters, and Yuhan Bao's biosafety input removed open-environment use (Human Practices, Key Stakeholder Decisions table). The team also tested a real factory sample rather than only simulated wastewater. But the one real-sample run shows only a 0.4 pH unit change and an uninterpretable COD reduction, and the Sustainability page derives a 33-67% removal from that same questionable pair of numbers, so the impact case is argued well but not yet demonstrated.
justification.a4: There is one genuine cycle in the handbook's sense: the first clear-zone assay with whole cells failed (Engineering, Figure 14, labelled Failed), the team diagnosed that pectin cannot reach intracellular enzyme, and Cycle 1.2 rebuilt the construct with an alpha-factor signal peptide, after which secreted pgaA gave a 2.36 cm zone (Engineering Test 1.2). The pgaA temperature/pH optimisation (50 C, pH 5, Results Figure 10) is also real characterisation. Against that, the Learn sections for Cycle 1.2 and Cycle 2 mostly restate success, no quantified success criterion is ever stated for COD, pH or removal rate, the alginate formulation was not optimised against measured data, and the AlphaFold work predicted structures without being tested against any measurement. One complete cycle plus competent characterisation: a 3.5, not a 4.5.
justification.a5: The strongest part of the project. The ECPR framework (Engage, Capture, Project iteration, Re-verify) makes each engagement traceable, and the Key Stakeholder Decisions table names four stakeholders, the decision adopted and, unusually, what still needs validating: residence time and oxygen transfer added after Feng Xie, repositioning as pre-treatment after Yunhai Jiang, the assumed certification price premium deleted after Jiazhi Hou, and open-environment deployment dropped with containment and leak monitoring added after Yuhan Bao. That is reflective, responsible and responsive in the p.21-22 sense, and the design changes are traceable rather than asserted. It falls short of 5 because the field visit and street interviews shaped framing more than engineering, and the re-verification steps are listed as future work.
justification.a6: The standard Attributions page returns 404 (https://2026.igem.wiki/keystone/attributions), so the form the handbook tells me to read (p.25-26) is not on the wiki and I cannot check that every field is complete. What I can see is good: the Notebook table assigns dated tasks to named students and advisors (Business Plan to Kevin Yu, storybook to Aruna Wo, SDGs to named members, wet lab blocks to All Wet Lab Students), and the Team page describes the PI and a PhD instructor in supervisory and troubleshooting roles only. No outsourcing is declared or evident, so this is a documentation gap rather than an integrity concern, but with the required page missing I cannot verify the split and score it at 2.5.
justification.a7: Thirteen new parts were registered, six basic and seven composite, and the Registry entries are live and real: BBa_26MHROWU and BBa_26AURGFO both show annotated plasmid maps (2u ori, TEF1p, CYC1t, URA3, ADH1p, mazF), host organisms, biosafety screening cleared, and RFC10/RFC1000 export. The team reused standard parts rather than reinventing them, taking MazEF (BBa_K4990016) and the ADH1 promoter/terminator (BBa_K4081990, BBa_K4081823) and crediting the 2023 CPU-China temperature circuit. The Part Collection page explains how the four units compose into one system, which is the reusable-collection case the handbook rewards.
justification.a8: The two flagship composite parts are documented on the Registry with structured entries (design, plasmid construction, characterisation, temperature switch, simulated-wastewater and real-sample sections on BBa_26MHROWU; L-/D-lactate and HPLC characterisation on BBa_26AURGFO), and basic parts such as BBa_26NEE31B carry origin, sequence, GC content and functional description. The wiki side is thorough enough to rebuild from: Experiments lists protocols from media prep to BCA and microsphere formation. It is short of 4 because the standard Parts page is 404 and the collection sits under Wet Lab, the basic-part Registry entries carry design notes only without characterisation data, and the Part Collection table misdescribes BBa_26RVHJ1L (pRS426 vector) with the JEN1 transporter description.
justification.w1: The home page is the best-communicated part of this wiki: the cherry anatomy walkthrough, the washed-process chain, the COD figure against the 150 mg/L standard, and then three jobs (degrade pectin, metabolise lactate, contain with mazEF) with the gene names attached. After the home and Description pages I can state the aim, the chassis (S. cerevisiae W303), the parts and the intended deployment without guessing. It is one sentence and one schematic per idea in the Lambert_GA manner; what keeps it from 5 is that no measurable success criterion is ever stated alongside the goal of returning pH to 6.0-8.0.
justification.w2: Most main claims carry a figure, a table or numbers: gels for every construct, sequencing confirmation, growth curves against empty vector, BSA and galacturonic acid standard curves, clear-zone diameters in triplicate, conversion percentages, significance marks on the lactate assays, and HPLC chromatograms with an R-squared of 0.9851. The gaps are at the end of the chain, which is where it matters most: the real-sample COD is one number per condition in units inconsistent with the team's own background figures, the pH table gives no replicate spread despite the n=3 header, and the kill-switch conclusion rests on a comparison where the controls also failed to grow.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and the long pages have working in-page section menus, but six standard pages return 404, including Parts, Attributions, Proof of Concept and Implementation, and the parts content sits at /part-collection under a Wet Lab menu. The handbook says judges are not required to hunt (p.29), and here I had to. The Engagement pages are also very long (Human Practices 17,355 words, Education 11,220) relative to Results at 3,847, which is the sprawl the digital handbook warns about.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of this: the Experiments page gives protocols from media and transformation through SDS-PAGE, BCA, DNS and microsphere formation, the Contribution page documents each new part with origin and length, the HPLC method is given in full (mobile phase, flow rate, column), and everything sits on iGEM servers with the GitLab repo linked. The Notebook itself is thin at about 1,000 words, mostly a Gantt-style schedule rather than dated observations, and the failed first clear-zone attempt is told only in the Engineering narrative, so the record of what went wrong is less complete than the record of what worked.
justification.w5: References are present and specific on the science pages, with in-text citation of the primary sources behind each gene (Zhou 2015 for pgaA, Guo 1995 for pelB, Soares-Silva 2007 for JEN1, Lodi 1993, Wakamatsu 2013), and the spot checks I made resolve to real papers that say what the wiki says. Prior iGEM work is credited: the temperature circuit is attributed to 2023 CPU-China and the MazEF part to BBa_K4990016. Two deductions: an AI-generated illustration is used in the Background (Figure 3, disclosed as Doubao AI, which is honest but is presented alongside real field photos), and many photographs and schematics across Education and Human Practices carry no credit line.

J2.one_line: A well-executed two-module yeast wastewater project with real comparative enzyme data, one genuine failure-driven redesign and unusually traceable Human Practices, let down by a thin real-sample demonstration, confounded kill-switch controls and six missing standard pages including Attributions.
strengths: Quantitative head-to-head enzyme screen with proper controls: clear-zone diameters in triplicate (CK 0, pgaA 1.257 cm, pelB 0.917 cm, PME 0) and DNS conversion rates of 25% vs 2% vs 0% (Results Tables 2-3, Figure 10), with PBS blank and empty-yeast negative controls on every condition.

One real DBTL cycle in the handbook's sense: the whole-cell clear-zone assay failed (Engineering Figure 14, labelled Failed), the team diagnosed that pectin cannot cross the yeast wall, added an alpha-factor signal peptide in Cycle 1.2, and then measured a 2.36 cm secreted-enzyme zone.

Human Practices with a documented decision trail: the ECPR method plus a Key Stakeholder Decisions table naming Feng Xie, Yunhai Jiang, Jiazhi Hou and Yuhan Bao, each with the design change adopted (residence time and oxygen transfer, repositioning as pre-treatment, removal of the certification price premium, no open-environment use) and the validation still outstanding.

Thirteen new Registry parts with live, annotated entries: BBa_26MHROWU and BBa_26AURGFO carry plasmid maps, host organisms, biosafety screening and structured characterisation sections, and the team reused standard parts (MazEF BBa_K4990016, ADH1p/t from BBa_K4081990/K4081823) crediting 2023 CPU-China.

Lactate module tested with both an enzymatic L-/D- assay against blank and empty-vector controls with significance marks (Figure 23) and an independent HPLC time course with a standard curve (R-squared 0.9851, Figures 24-25) - two methods agreeing on the same claim.
weaknesses: The real-sample demonstration, which is the whole point of the project, is the weakest evidence on the wiki: pH moved from 3.23 to 3.67 in 72 h (Table 4) and the COD readings are single values of 6 mg/L untreated and 2-4 mg/L treated, which cannot be squared with the team's own stated influent of 2000-7400 mg/L - no dilution factor, method or replicates are given.

The mazEF kill-switch test is confounded. No colonies grew at 10 C or 40 C for the wild type either, so those points say nothing about the switch; only the 20 C comparison is informative, and the team's own text concedes 10 and 40 C are simply unsuitable for yeast growth (Results Figure 28).

No quantified success criterion is ever stated. The stated goal is to return pH to 6.0-8.0 and remove COD and BOD, but no target removal rate, treatment time or microsphere loading is set in advance, so nothing in the Results can be scored pass or fail. BOD was never measured at all (Sustainability: 'completed in future work').

Six standard pages return 404 - Parts, Attributions, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Hardware, Software, Inclusivity - so the attributions form the handbook requires me to read is absent, and the parts content has to be found at /part-collection under a Wet Lab menu.

The modelling is decoration rather than engineering: AlphaFold pLDDT scores for six proteins are reported as evidence of reliability, but no prediction is tested against a measurement and no model is fitted to the team's own data, unlike the TAS Taipei dose calculator the handbook holds up.

Internal inconsistencies suggest uneven proofreading of the technical record: the alpha factor is placed at the C-terminus in the Description and Engineering overview but the N-terminus in Learn 1.2, and the Part Collection table gives BBa_26RVHJ1L (the pRS426 vector) the JEN1 transporter's description.
red_flags: Required standard page https://2026.igem.wiki/keystone/attributions returns 404, so the attributions form cannot be checked against handbook p.25-26; the Awards page states a standardized Attributions Form exists but does not link it on the wiki. Not an integrity concern - no outsourcing is declared or evident, and the Notebook assigns dated tasks to named students - but it caps what I can verify for aspect 6.

COD results are reported in units that contradict the team's own background (treated 2-4 mg/L and untreated 6 mg/L against a stated influent of 2000-7400 mg/L), and the Sustainability page then computes a headline 33.3-66.7% removal from exactly those two numbers. I read this as an unreported dilution or a test-kit scale rather than fabrication, but the integrated-system performance claim rests on it and I mark it unverified.

Figure 3 on the Description page is an AI-generated image (disclosed in the caption as 'Picture generated by Doubao AI') showing a coffee farmer and a factory of wastewater, placed among genuine field photographs from the Yunnan visit. The disclosure is honest and it is an illustration, not an evidence figure, so this is not an RCC matter - but I would prefer it not sit alongside real field documentation.

The kill-switch claim ('activated as expected below 25 C and above 37 C') goes beyond what the data support, since the wild-type control also failed to grow at 10 and 40 C. The team partly acknowledges this in the same paragraph; I note it as an over-claim, not misconduct.

calibrated.changed: a6 2.5->3.0: the notebook assigns dated tasks to named students and advisors and the team page describes the PI and instructor as supervisory only — the same evidence that earned squirrel-beijing 3.0. The missing form alone should not drop this below that bar.

justification.a1: Synbeans carries one coherent idea a long way in a season: three pectinases screened in S. cerevisiae W303, the winner (pgaA) re-engineered for secretion with an alpha-factor, a separate JEN1/CYB2/DLD1 lactate strain, a mazEF temperature kill switch, alginate-chitosan immobilisation, then tests in simulated and in real coffee wastewater (Results, Engineering). That is more layers than most HS projects manage, and the Home page tells the cherry-to-wastewater story well. It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS top band because the final system-level result on real wastewater is marginal (pH 3.23 to 3.67, Results Table 4) and the model adds structure prediction rather than system design.
justification.a2: The core biology is shown working with controls, not asserted: clear-zone diameters in triplicate with CK at zero (pgaA 1.257 cm, pelB 0.917, PME 0), DNS conversion rates of 25%, 2% and 0% against PBS and empty-yeast controls, SDS-PAGE bands at the predicted masses with an empty-vector lane, growth curves overlapping pRS426, galacturonic acid rising to about 1.5 mg/mL over 96 h in simulated wastewater with blank and negative controls and significance marks (Results Figures 8-19). D-lactate falls only in the engineered strain while the empty-vector strain also removes L-lactate, which the team states honestly (Results Figure 23). Marks off because the real-sample COD numbers (2-4 mg/L treated vs 6 mg/L untreated, Results Figure 30) are an order of magnitude away from the 2,000-7,400 mg/L the project is built on and are left unexplained, the HPLC consumption figure is reported as 167.7498817 with no units, and the kill-switch experiment is only informative at 20 C since the team concedes 10 and 40 C kill wild-type yeast too.
justification.a3: The need is real and locally grounded: a team member visited a Baoshan wet-processing plant and the problem was then checked with a village secretary, a fresh-cherry plant manager, an estate owner, a certification agronomist and a Luckin sustainability staffer (IHP). Those conversations produced a concrete, limited deployment picture: an equalisation or treatment tank inside an existing facility rather than a flow-through outlet, and recoverable microspheres (IHP, Entrepreneurship). It is a 4 rather than a 5 because the demonstrated effect on real wastewater is still small and the team says so; impact on a working line remains to be shown.
justification.a4: Three labelled DBTL cycles each contain a genuine Learn that changed the next Build: screening three pectinases and dropping PME and pelB on measured conversion data; discovering that intracellular pectinase cannot reach its substrate and adding the alpha-factor signal peptide after Prof. Xie Feng's advice (Engineering, Learn 1.1); then adding mazEF and building the lactate cassette (Cycle 2). Process-level redesign also came from HP, with the rapid single-pass outlet replaced by a residence tank. The ceiling is the modelling: the Model page is AlphaFold3 structure prediction, and its own Limitations admit the predictions were never quantitatively integrated with the clear-zone or degradation data, so there is nothing like TAS's fitted kinetic calculator.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the wiki. The ECPR frame (Engage, Capture, Project Iteration, Re-verify) is applied consistently, and the Overview table names four stakeholders, the decision adopted and what still needs validation. The changes are traceable and sometimes unwelcome to the team: Feng Xie's residence-time challenge killed the flow-through design; Yuhan Bao's point that a factory boundary does not contain cells removed open-environment deployment and demoted the kill switch to one layer of a containment stack; Jiazhi Hou's input deleted an assumed certification price premium. A 573-response public survey is reported with its limits stated rather than over-read. Half a point off because no consent or ethics oversight is described for the survey and street interviews, which the handbook asks for.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page on the wiki (2026.igem.wiki/keystone/attributions returns 404), although the Awards page says a standardised Attributions Form records responsibilities. What exists is partial: the Notebook timeline assigns a lead student or students to each activity, including HP meetings and wiki work, and names Mr. Baldeep and Ms. Duan for safety training, while Members bios state roles (wet lab, outreach, design). But the wet-lab blocks are credited only to 'All Wet Lab Students', no figure caption says who ran which assay, and sequencing, HPLC and gene synthesis services are not attributed anywhere. I would ask about this at the session rather than assume outside execution.
justification.a7: The design is standard-parts synthetic biology in a yeast idiom: pRS426 shuttle vectors with the TEF1 promoter and CYC1 terminator, His tags, an alpha-factor secretion signal, ADH1p/ADH1t, and composite expression cassettes (Part Collection, Contribution). The team reuses an existing Registry part, MazEF BBa_K4990016, and credits the CPU-China 2023 temperature-control design explicitly. At least two composite parts are shown to function (BBa_26MHROWU pectin degradation, BBa_26AURGFO lactate removal), which is well above a paper design; it is not a 5 because assembly is homologous recombination rather than an iGEM assembly standard and the switch part is adopted rather than improved.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely good: the Part Collection lists 16-17 part IDs with type and function, and the Contribution page gives each basic part a length, organism of origin, properties and usage with literature (for example pgaA Km 3.20 mg/mL, Vmax 40.97 umol/min/mL). But the parts data I can verify live only on the wiki, since the Registry pages render client-side and I could not confirm their content, and the handbook is clear that wiki-only part documentation does not meet the parts requirement. There are also internal inconsistencies that a judge notices: Contribution says 9 basic and 4 composite parts while Part Collection says 6 and 7, and the pRS426 vector entry carries the JEN1 description by mistake.
justification.w1: The Home page sets the problem in a few steps (cherry anatomy, washed process, COD 2,000-7,400 mg/L against a 150 mg/L standard) and then states the approach in one screen: contain, degrade, recover, with the three modules named. A reader knows within a minute what the team is trying to do and why. It loses a point because the scrollytelling is heavy and the single sentence of project goal arrives after a lot of animation.
justification.w2: Most claims on Results and Engineering carry a figure, a control lane or group, and often triplicate values (clear-zone table, protein concentration table, conversion table, significance marks on the degradation figures). Model outputs are kept on the Model page and labelled as predictions, and the team states plainly where the effect was partial. Held at 4 by the loose quantitative hygiene: missing or implausible units in the HPLC section (a standard curve to 1000 mg/mL), the unexplained COD scale, and n not always stated.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and the menu groups Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab and Engagement sensibly, with an Awards page mapping deliverables to medal criteria. Against that, several standard pages a judge expects are simply absent (attributions, parts, proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement all 404), and their content is either renamed (Part Collection) or scattered, which makes the judge hunt. Some pages are also very long for what they carry (Human Practices at about 17,000 words, Education at 11,000).
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: the Experiments page gives media recipes, PCR, recombination, transformation, purification, SDS-PAGE, BCA, microsphere preparation and the HPLC conditions; the Notebook gives a dated timeline with leads; the Contribution page gives part sequences lengths and origins. What is missing is raw data (no deposited readings behind the curves) and a notebook that records what went wrong week to week, which is what would lift this to a 5.
