justification.w5: Each major page ends with a full reference list in a consistent style, in-text citations are attached to the biology claims, the reused temperature circuit is credited to CPU-China 2023 with the part ID, and the one AI-generated illustration is labelled 'Picture generated by Doubao AI', which is the right disclosure. Minor lapses keep it from 5: the COD of coffee wastewater is given as 2,000-7,400 mg/L on Description and 8,000-15,000 mg/L on Model with different sources and no reconciliation, and several survey percentages are reported without a link to the underlying instrument.

J3.one_line: A disciplined coffee-wastewater project with two functional yeast modules shown against controls and an unusually honest, decision-changing Human Practices chain, let down by a missing Attributions page, shaky real-sample measurements, and a model that never meets the wet-lab data.
strengths: Measured function with controls at every stage: clear-zone diameters in triplicate with a zero control, 25% vs 2% vs 0% conversion for pgaA/pelB/PME, SDS-PAGE against an empty-vector lane, and time-resolved galacturonic acid and D/L-lactate data with blank and negative controls (Results Figures 8-25)

A real Learn step that changed the build: intracellular pectinase could not reach its substrate, so an alpha-factor signal peptide was added and extracellular degradation was then demonstrated (Engineering Cycle 1.1 to 1.2)

Human Practices with a traceable chain and a published table of decisions adopted versus what still needs validating; critical input (Feng Xie on residence time and kill-switch escape, Yuhan Bao on containment and on novelty not justifying a project) visibly removed design options rather than confirming them (IHP)

Honest reporting of weak results: the empty-vector strain's own L-lactate consumption, the small pH shift on real wastewater (3.23 to 3.67), and the admission that 10 and 40 C kill wild-type yeast too, so only 20 C tests the switch
Full protocols on the Experiments page and a dated Notebook timeline with named student leads for each activity
weaknesses: No Attributions page on the wiki (404) and no per-experiment credit, so who ran the bench work, and whether sequencing/HPLC were outside services, cannot be established from the standard pages

Real-sample COD is reported as 2-4 mg/L treated against 6 mg/L untreated, which is three orders of magnitude from the 2,000-7,400 mg/L the whole project is premised on, with no explanation of the kit scale or units

The Model page is AlphaFold3 structure prediction only; its own Limitations section concedes the predictions were never integrated with clear-zone, concentration or degradation data, so no model guided or explained the system quantitatively

Part documentation that I can verify lives on the wiki rather than the Registry, and the two part listings disagree (9 basic + 4 composite on Contribution vs 6 basic + 7 composite on Part Collection); the pRS426 entry carries the JEN1 description by mistake

Several standard pages are missing (attributions, parts, proof-of-concept, implementation, measurement all 404) while Human Practices and Education run to 17,000 and 11,000 words, so the wiki is sprawling in places and empty where judges look
No mention of consent or ethics oversight for the 573-respondent public survey and the street interviews
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404 (https://2026.igem.wiki/keystone/attributions) although the Awards page states that an Attributions Form records student responsibilities; a session question about who performed the cloning, purification and HPLC, not an accusation

Quantitative hygiene: HPLC consumption reported as '167.7498817' with no units, and a lactic acid standard curve spanning 0-1000 mg/mL, which is implausible for the stated wastewater; likely mg/L mislabelling rather than fabrication, but it should be checked
Internal inconsistency in a headline figure: coffee wastewater COD is 2,000-7,400 mg/L on Description and 8,000-15,000 mg/L on Model, each with a different citation and no reconciliation

One illustrative figure is AI-generated (Description Figure 3) but is clearly disclosed as such; no evidentiary figure appears generated. No safety or whitelist concerns: chassis are E. coli DH5-alpha and S. cerevisiae W303, both declared BSL-1/RG-1 on the Safety page
pages_read: Registry lookups attempted for BBa_26MHROWU, BBa_26NEE31B, BBa_26AURGFO (pages render client-side; content not verifiable)

calibrated.changed: none.

one_line.en: A two-module yeast wastewater project with real comparative enzyme data and one genuine failure-driven redesign, let down by real-sample measurements that contradict the project's own premise.
one_line.zh: 雙模組酵母廢水專案，具真實的酵素比較數據與一次因失敗而改版的過程，但真實樣品的測值與專案自身前提互相矛盾。

strengths: Quantitative head-to-head enzyme screen with blank and empty-yeast controls, reporting the enzyme that did not work
A genuine loop: a failed whole-cell assay was diagnosed as a transport problem, a signal peptide was added, and secreted activity was then measured
Human Practices with a published table separating adopted decisions from open questions, and named changes that removed design options
Controls in the application experiments too, including an empty-vector strain that exposed the chassis's own consumption
weaknesses: Real-sample oxygen-demand values are three orders of magnitude from the influent range the project is premised on, with no method detail or dilution factor
The engineered gain over the chassis is modest and reported without units at implausible precision
Kill-switch evidence is confounded because the wild type also failed to grow at the extreme temperatures
Stated project goals are not met or reconciled, and six standard pages return 404
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404 although an attributions form is said to exist
Headline removal percentages computed from the contradictory oxygen-demand values
Kill-switch claim goes beyond what the confounded data support
A disclosed AI-generated illustration sits among genuine field photographs

screen.project_title: The Cluck is Ticking — E. coli cadaverine biosensor for chicken spoilage
screen.what_they_built: An E. coli biosensor using the native CadC regulator to convert cadaverine (a meat-spoilage amine) into amilCP blue chromoprotein output, plus a smartphone image-processing model that turns the colour into a predicted expiration date and a packaging-insert hardware concept.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli NEB T7 Express / BL21(DE3); Twist pET-28a(+) and pET_blank_Kan backbones. Eleven new Registry parts (basic: cadC BBa_26704YS0, amilCP BBa_26RENFJ6, CI-LVA BBa_26MEDO4C, mRFP, SLP2018-2-1208 promoter, cadBA promoter with H-NS sites; composites BBa_26WZK7AR, BBa_261PZTXS, BBa_26RF609J, BBa_26ASQUIZ, BBa_26T6WP1H), derived from BBa_K592009 and BBa_C0051.
screen.best_evidence: /results, pET_cadC_cadBAp_amilCP cadaverine assay: PBS-washed pellets read on a plate reader at 6 h and 24 h, 400-700 nm spectra, showing a clear 588 nm amilCP peak at 0 mM cadaverine, flat at 40 mM at both times and flat at 4 mM only at 6 h — cadaverine inhibits CadC, but only well above the ~2 mM released by spoiled meat. Also /results IPTG two-fold dilution series giving a visible dark-purple to yellow gradient.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in places — a BU iGEM alumna's advice changed them to cadaverine/putrescine dihydrochloride and set the fume-hood aliquoting protocol for their community lab, and food-pantry and grocery stakeholders drove the in-package absorbent-pad hardware format rather than a test strip.
screen.reason: Five honest DBTL cycles with sequencing-diagnosed frameshifts, leaky-terminator fixes and a working final construct, a quantitative plate-reader cadaverine response, a validated MD screen and a validated smartphone absorbance model. The biosensor does not yet respond at the biologically relevant ~2 mM and the inverted (cadaverine-up = blue-up) pathway was never built, so aspect 2 is capped, but the engineering depth is finalist-adjacent and deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: US high school team (Khan Lab School, Mountain View) working at the BioCurious community lab on meat-spoilage sensing in the Food & Nutrition village. They placed amilCP under the cadBA promoter with CadC, intending a CI-repressor inversion so colour rises with cadaverine. Two ordered constructs were frameshifted by unintended start codons at the insertion site; they diagnosed this by Plasmidsaurus sequencing, fixed one by site-directed mutagenesis, and redesigned the third construct with a weak SLP2018-2-1208 promoter, H-NS silencer regions and a T7hyb1 terminator. The cadaverine assay showed inhibition of CadC at 40 mM but not at 4 mM after 24 h, and they calculated ~63 CadC copies per cell (vs 1-3 native) to explain apparent pH independence. Dry lab contributed a molecular-dynamics pipeline benchmarked against literature mutants (resolves 12.5x but not 7x binding changes) and an open-source smartphone absorbance model validated against a plate reader (9.6% vs 22.6% deviation from Beer-Lambert ideal) and against synthetic noisy plate images (EC50 recovered to 2.5% error). Eleven Registry parts, a packaging hardware design with Janus membrane and TSCA Tier 1 framing, and stakeholder-by-stakeholder HP entries in Expertise/Advice/Implementation format. Note: some sequence review and protocol reformatting is credited to Claude, and lab supervision came from community-lab mentors.

screen.project_title: MelanoShield: bacterial melanin as a bio-based wood flame-retardant coating
screen.what_they_built: An E. coli strain carrying a copper-inducible Priestia megaterium tyrosinase that produces melanin, and a two-layer melanin/chitosan coating applied to oak and tested for flame resistance.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning and BL21 (non-DE3) for protein work; a 5,709 bp pET-22b(+) pCopA-RBS30-tyrosinase-LE-6xHis construct built from Addgene #239454 with two synonymous substitutions removing internal BseRI and XhoI sites. Parts: BBa_262OK4RW, BBa_263QUR21, BBa_26DHR36G, BBa_26MD3039, BBa_26XNC06W, plus BBa_K274001.
screen.best_evidence: /results: the W9 melanin-extract coating gave a mean mass loss of 3.06 +/- 0.73% on flame-exposed oak versus 9.36 +/- 1.82% untreated and 3.67 +/- 0.73% for the commercial product FP (three specimens per condition, Welch tests with Holm correction), and flame-exposed W9 specimens carried a 154-210 um char layer against 101-111 um on bare oak. Anti-His western blot (Figure 10) shows copper-dependent signal at ~33 kDa with clean empty-vector and no-copper controls.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: firefighters, a fire-research institute and architects are each credited on /human-practices and /attributions with changing a specific decision, and the attributions page is written as a per-person account of what each contributor altered.
screen.reason: A complete chain from Sanger-verified construct to expressed protein to a measured materials property, run with replicates, Welch/Holm statistics and confidence intervals, and documented with unusual discipline: the team states on its own results page that the untreated-wood comparison did not survive Holm adjustment and lists four things that remain unproven. That combination of real data and verifiable honesty is finalist territory for a high school team. The panel should weigh how much of the coating effect comes from melanin rather than from the rest of the crude lysate, since enzyme activity was never assayed.
screen.field_notes: Korea-HS (Korea, Biomanufacturing village) built MelanoShield, a wood fire-protective coating from bacterially produced eumelanin, motivated by the 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires and by the supply limits of plant-extracted bio-retardants. They removed internal BseRI and XhoI sites from a Priestia megaterium tyrosinase by synonymous substitution, cloned the 891 bp insert into a pET-22b(+) pCopA-RBS30 copper-responsive backbone (5,709 bp final), and verified the insert and both junctions by Sanger sequencing while stating that the whole plasmid was not sequenced. Copper-dependent expression of the 33 kDa His-tagged protein was shown by SDS-PAGE across two copper ranges and confirmed by anti-His western blot with empty-vector and no-copper controls. Recovered supernatant pigment precipitated at pH 2, redissolved in 1 M NaOH and matched a melanin standard's log-linear absorbance slope to about 0.5%, at 0.419 mg dried material per mL. The headline materials result is a two-layer coating from crude tyrosinase-strain extract giving 3.06 +/- 0.73% mass loss on flame-exposed oak against 9.36 +/- 1.82% untreated and 3.67 +/- 0.73% for a commercial product, with char layers of 154-210 um versus 101-111 um, analysed by Welch t-tests and Welch ANOVA with Holm correction and Kruskal-Wallis checks in NumPy, SciPy and statsmodels. The team flags four unresolved questions (pigment composition, catalytic activity, the melanin-specific contribution to coating performance, and whether the char is thermally protective), reports a failed Bradford calibration honestly (two of three curves unusable, R2 0.069 and 0.027), records that no member had handled a micropipette before the project, and maintains a 7,132-word measurement page, a 3,786-word per-person attributions page and a dedicated AI-use page.

justification.a1: MelanoShield runs a genuinely linked chain of increasing difficulty: a synthetic tyrosinase redesigned to remove internal BseRI/XhoI sites, cloned into a pCopA/CueR copper-responsive vector, expression shown by anti-His blot, pigment produced and benchmarked against an authentic Sepia melanin standard, then twelve coating formulations sprayed on oak, flame-tested against untreated wood and a marketed product, and finally FE-SEM char cross-sections (Description s5; Results s1-6). That is close to the TAS Taipei pattern of two working routes plus a prototype and a benchmark. It falls short of a 5 because the enzyme was never assayed for activity and the coating used crude lysate, so the biology-to-material link is inferred rather than closed.
justification.a2: The molecular half works with proper controls: anti-His Western with empty-vector and no-copper lanes showing no band at 33 kDa (Results Fig 10); pigment index higher than empty vector at every L-tyrosine level, n=3 independent cultures, Holm-adjusted p 0.0011-0.0118 (Table 6); recovered pigment 4.19 +/- 0.34 mg vs 0.03 +/- 0.01 mg empty vector, with log-linear slope matching the standard to 0.5% (Tables 7-8). The application half is weaker and the team says so: W9 at 3.06 +/- 0.73% vs 9.36 +/- 1.82% untreated did not survive Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.194, Table 12), the char difference is p = 0.038 Welch but p = 0.10 by permutation, and the decisive empty-vector-extract control is missing. Honest qualitative and descriptive reporting throughout, but the headline coating claim is not established.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and stakeholder-shaped: KICT explained that application and effective thickness define the test standard, Neotec set quasi-non-combustible as the bar, and the team benchmarked against a Korea Fire Institute-approved product rather than only bare wood (Human Practices 2.1-2.2; Results s5). Own-data numbers support it - 419 mg/L pigment recovery and mass loss within the commercial product's range. It is not a 4.5 or 5 because nothing was tested in a real-world-like setting, no cost model was built despite cost being named as the main barrier by two stakeholders, and durability, inhalation and thermal protection are all acknowledged as untested.
justification.a4: Six DBTL modules are documented with explicit Design/Build/Test/Learn text, and at least two iterations are real redesigns rather than troubleshooting: the flat single-layer screen (eight of eleven coated specimens worse than untreated, one specimen each) led to a two-layer application with n=3 and the addition of a commercial benchmark (Engineering 05, Cycles 1-2); and the Bradford module recorded three standard curves, found two with no concentration response (R2 0.069, 0.027) and reported the extrapolated range rather than hiding it. W9 was chosen on reproducibility rather than the lowest mean, with the single-point sensitivity shown in Table 13. The 400-650 nm fit window was fixed before analysis, which is a stated measure of success; the Future plans table pre-commits to effect size and controls for the next round.
justification.a5: Thirteen-plus stakeholders across firefighters, KICT, NIFC, architects, four building-materials firms, and four academics, each written up with what changed (Human Practices s2). Four concrete experimental changes are traceable: adding the anti-His Western so expression did not rest on a stained band, comparing the pigment to an authentic standard before calling it melanin, dropping the drying step and using wet unpurified material on Prof. Gosset's advice, and planning a spread-on comparison and inhalation measurement after Prof. Park Soyoung's humidifier-disinfectant analogy. The occupational-medicine interview is a genuine two-way exchange that produced a safety caveat against the team's own interest, which is the responsive strand the handbook asks for.
justification.a6: The Attributions page gives a task-level account for every one of the sixteen students, two PIs, two instructors, four student advisors and external contributors, naming who ran transformations, extractions, coating application and fire measurements (Attributions, Team Member Contributions). Outsourcing is declared and bounded: gene synthesis by an IGSC member, Sanger sequencing, and a supervising professor who lectured, supervised all wet-lab sessions and handled strain disposal. AI use is disclosed in unusual detail, including that the decorative illustrations were AI-drawn and that no data figure was AI-made. Not a 5 only because instructor involvement in experimental design is described as review at each major decision point and the FE-SEM operator is not named.
justification.a7: The project is a proper genetic device: pCopA-RBS30-tyrosinase-LE-6xHis on a modified pET-22b(+) backbone, driven through the host's chromosomal CueR with no plasmid-borne regulator, reusing two Addgene sources and adding a re-engineered coding sequence (Description s4). Five nested parts are claimed - promoter, core CDS, tagged CDS, cassette and full 5,709 bp plasmid - deliberately layered so another team can take one level (Contribution Table 1). I could not load the Registry pages (parts.igem.org returned 403 at the time of judging), so the part entries themselves are unverified by me and I score the design, not the entries.
justification.a8: Wiki documentation is outstanding: every quantitative claim has a table, n, SD, test and a stated limitation, and the Contribution page lists what each Registry entry contains. But the standard /parts page is a 404, as are /model, /proof-of-concept, /protocols and /implementation, so a judge following the standard URLs for parts finds nothing and has to discover the content on Contribution (handbook p.29 asks teams to guide judges from the standard pages). Since p.18 says parts are judged on the Registry alone and I could not reach those entries, I can credit only what the wiki shows, which is why this sits at 3.5 rather than higher.
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem, the mechanism in four steps, the three objectives and the headline numbers (3.06% vs 9.36% and 3.67%, 154-210 um char, 0.419 mg/mL) inside one screen-and-a-bit, with a sourced stat strip. Unusually, it also carries a 'What we have not shown' block listing the four open questions, so the reader is calibrated before leaving the front page. A small drift is that the fire-performance framing is louder than the caveat that none of the coating comparisons survived multiple-comparison correction.
justification.w2: Results and Measurement are the strongest pages: same-day controls for every assay, the melanin standard carried through the entire precipitation-wash-dry-scan procedure rather than measured alongside, per-specimen raw masses in Tables 10-11, Welch plus Kruskal-Wallis plus Holm with both raw and corrected p-values, Hedges' g, and confidence intervals quoted in preference to p-values at n=3. Limits are stated where they bite: eleven of eighteen Bradford values extrapolated beyond calibration, whole-culture A400/OD600 without blank subtraction labelled an index not a concentration, and the missing empty-vector-extract coating control named explicitly. Short of 5 only because that missing control leaves the central application claim unsupported and no raw data files are posted.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and grouped (Project / Wet Lab / HP / Sustainability / Team), figures are numbered continuously within sections, and cross-links between Description, Engineering, Results and Measurement are accurate. The friction is that several standard URLs 404 - /parts, /model, /protocols, /proof-of-concept, /implementation - with their content folded into Contribution and Measurement instead, which costs a judge time. Page lengths are large (Engineering ~12,800 words, Results ~9,100) and there is real repetition of the same tables across Engineering and Results, pushing toward 'sprawling'.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild this: the 891 bp modified sequence is printed in the Engineering appendix with both substituted bases marked, the verified primer pair is given with Tm, GC and a warning about its 3' poly-A run, Measurement s4 gives step-by-step protocols, and the Contribution troubleshooting table records what failed and what was changed. Failures are kept in view rather than deleted, including the flat single-layer screen and the two dead Bradford curves. Not a 5 because raw instrument files are not deposited and the notebook is comparatively brief (~4,000 words) against the volume of work described.
justification.w5: References are numbered, consistent across pages, and nearly all carry DOIs or resolvable URLs, with Addgene plasmids cited by number and RRID and the bioRxiv preprint flagged as not peer reviewed. Figure captions distinguish measured data from literature-derived schematics (Figures 2 and 6 on Description are explicitly labelled as not measured in this project), and the AI Use page accounts for image provenance. Prior iGEM work is credited on Human Practices (Nanjing, PuiChing, Mingdao, Cambridge, BBa_K274001), though that crediting is lighter than the GreatBay standard and does not appear beside the design decisions it informed.

J1.one_line: A disciplined, control-rich high-school project that genuinely engineered a copper-inducible melanin strain and prototyped a wood coating, let down only by an unassayed enzyme, a missing empty-vector extract control, and Registry/standard-page gaps.
strengths: Anti-His Western with two negative controls plus pigment recovery of 4.19 +/- 0.34 mg vs 0.03 +/- 0.01 mg for empty vector, and a spectral slope matching an authentic Sepia melanin standard to 0.5% with the standard carried through the whole procedure (Results s1, s3).

Statistical honesty rare at any level: raw and Holm-corrected p-values side by side, confidence intervals preferred over p at n=3, a permutation check on the char result, and eleven of eighteen Bradford values flagged as extrapolated (Results s2, s5, s6).

A real data-driven redesign - one sprayed layer gave no protection across all eleven coatings, so the team doubled the application, raised n from 1 to 3 and added a commercial benchmark (Engineering module 05).

Human Practices that changed the bench: the melanin-standard comparison, the added Western blot, dropping the drying step on Prof. Gosset's advice, and a planned inhalation study after an occupational-medicine interview (Human Practices s2).

Task-level attribution for all sixteen students and every instructor, advisor and external contributor, plus a detailed AI-use declaration stating that no data figure was AI-generated (Attributions; AI Use & Credits).
weaknesses: Tyrosinase activity was never assayed; the Western shows presence, not catalysis, so the central enzymatic claim rests on an indirect pigment index (Results s7).

Coatings used crude soluble lysate of unmeasured melanin content, and the empty-vector extract control that would attribute the effect to melanin was not run - the team names this gap itself (Results s7).
No coating comparison survived Holm correction; the best W9-vs-untreated result is adjusted p = 0.194 at n=3, and the char comparison is p = 0.038 Welch but p = 0.10 by permutation.

The standard /parts page is a 404 (as are /model, /protocols, /proof-of-concept, /implementation), so part documentation must be hunted for on Contribution; I could not reach the Registry entries themselves to judge them under p.18.

Engineering (~12,800 words) and Results (~9,100 words) duplicate several tables verbatim, which strains the 'complete but not sprawling' test; flame exposure used a hand-set burner distance with no jig and no standardized heat flux.
red_flags: Registry part pages for the five claimed parts (BBa_262OK4RW, BBa_263QUR21, BBa_26XNC06W, BBa_26DHR36G, BBa_26MD3039) returned HTTP 403 when I tried to load them, so their content is unverified by me; this is a limitation of my access, not an allegation about the team.

Decorative illustrations and the mascot were AI-drawn and the wiki HTML was AI-assisted; the team discloses this explicitly and states no data figure or citation came from an AI tool. I see no integrity concern to raise, but a judge with access should spot-check that the data figures match the laboratory records.
No model/hardware/software content exists; the project is purely wet lab plus HP, which is legitimate but means aspects normally supported by a model carry no evidence here.

calibrated.changed: w3 4.0 -> 3.5. Five standard URLs are 404 (/parts, /model, /protocols, /proof-of-concept, /implementation) and there is real duplication of the same tables across Engineering and Results. I scored Squirrel Beijing and Labi 3.5 for five missing standard pages with comparable sprawl, so 4.0 here was softer than the bar I used on them. a6 4.5 stays: this is the most complete attribution on the ballot, naming who ran transformations, extractions, coating application and fire measurements.

justification.a1: MelanoShield runs a genuinely long chain of increasingly difficult steps for a high school team: synonymous removal of internal BseRI/XhoI sites before gene synthesis, cloning into a copper-responsive vector, anti-His confirmation of a 33 kDa product, a Bradford copper-response series, a substrate-response pigment index, gravimetric recovery of 4.19 mg from 10 mL supernatant benchmarked against a Sepia melanin standard, then eleven coating formulations, two flame-test rounds against untreated oak and a commercial product, and post-fire FE-SEM cross-sections (Results sections 1-6). The biology and the material halves are actually joined: every coated specimen used pigment from their own strain. It falls short of a 5 only because the headline application result (W9 vs untreated oak) does not survive their own Holm correction and the pigment's contribution is not isolated.
justification.a2: The production claim is properly supported: anti-His signal near 33 kDa appearing from 100 uM copper with no band in either the empty-vector or no-copper control (Results Fig. 10); pigment index higher in the tyrosinase strain at all four L-tyrosine levels with three independent cultures each (Table 5); and a purified preparation that precipitates at pH 2, redissolves in 1 M NaOH and matches the commercial standard to 0.5% in log-linear slope while the empty-vector prep gives 0.03 mg and sits at the blank (Table 7). The coating claim is weaker and the team says so: 3.06 +/- 0.73% vs 9.36 +/- 1.82% untreated, Holm-adjusted p = 0.194, n = 3, with no empty-vector-extract control and no enzyme activity assay. Measured production, descriptive application.
justification.a3: The deployment route is specific and stakeholder-shaped rather than generic: KICT told them a fire rating is meaningless without a defined application and rated coating thickness, Dr. Yoseb Song put purification and extraction at 60-70% of cost which pushed them to a minimally processed extract, and Prof. Nam Jeong-min identified small residential timber buildings exempt from retardant requirements as the end use (Human Practices sections 3-4). They also record the limits honestly: the coating is dark and colours the wood, and performance only matched, not beat, a commercial product in their own non-standard rig. What is missing for a 5 is any test in a realistic setting or against a Korean standard test method.
justification.a4: This is the strongest part of the project from an engineering standpoint. Six modules are written as explicit DBTL cycles, and the team distinguishes a redesign from a repeated comparison (Engineering overview). Test data genuinely drove redesigns: the one-layer screen failed to show protection (eight of eleven coated specimens lost more mass than bare oak, Table 10), so round two moved to two layers with n = 3 independent batches; W9 was chosen over the lower-mean W10 because W10's rank depends on a single 0.27% observation (Table 13); the 400-650 nm fit window was fixed before analysis; two of three Bradford curves were recorded as failures rather than averaged away. They name the confound they created (layer count not tested side by side) and specify the verification experiment, including the empty-vector-extract control they never ran. No model is attempted, which keeps this below GreatBay/TAS level.
justification.a5: Twelve-plus stakeholders over four months across firefighters, KICT, an architecture professor, an OECD researcher, KAIST and UNAM metabolic engineers, and four materials companies at COEX, with a dated interview table. Several design changes trace directly to specific people: Prof. Gosset's warning that dried melanin behaves like charcoal removed the drying step so the coating is applied wet and unpurified; Neotec and Gosset prompted the standard-versus-pigment identity comparison; Prof. Park Soyoung (occupational medicine) raised inhalation exposure from spray application, which now sits in Future plans as a spread-on comparison. They also mark their own failure to close loops with the people who advised them. Outreach (crossword, surveys) is kept separate from design-shaping HP, which is the right distinction.
justification.a6: The Attributions page gives a first-person account per member, names the two PIs and Prof. Woo Rin Lee as laboratory supervisor, credits Liz for lab arrangements, declares the FE-SEM as performed at a Material Characterization Center (Notebook 10/11), and the AI Use page states that illustrations were AI-drawn while all data figures are unmodified team records. Against that, all five Registry entries list Prof. Woo Rin Lee as the sole designer with Conceptualisation, Data Curation, Formal Analysis, Investigation and Supervision, and no student is credited on any part; the Results page also records that none of the students had handled a pipette before. I do not read this as an integrity problem, but it is the question I would put to the team: who made the construct design decisions? That uncertainty is what keeps this at 3.5.
justification.a7: Five parts are on the Registry as a deliberately layered, reusable collection: pCopA promoter (BBa_262OK4RW, 31 bp), the RE-site-cleaned tyrosinase CDS (BBa_263QUR21, 891 bp), the His-tagged version (BBa_26XNC06W), the cassette (BBa_26DHR36G, 949 bp) and the full 5,709 bp construct (BBa_26MD3039), each with RFC 10 and RFC 1000 export and the composite showing its component annotations. The genuinely reusable new contribution is small but real: two synonymous substitutions that make a published tyrosinase cloneable with standard enzymes, plus verified amplification primers (Contribution sections 2-3). Nothing is novel at the pathway level, and host-dependence on chromosomal CueR is correctly flagged on the part page.
justification.a8: Registry entries carry role with SO terms, topology, composition, host organisms, GC content, source Addgene plasmid, functional descriptions that include the copper confound, and Design (and for pCopA, Experiment) documentation tabs; biosafety screening is cleared. The wiki side is better still: the Measurement page gives measurand, unit, instrument and replication for every quantity, full protocols, CVs, and a section on what was not recorded. The deductions are that the parts were created only days before the deadline with most characterisation data living on the wiki rather than in the Registry entries, and the team's own /parts page returns 404, so a judge following the standard-page route finds no parts index.
justification.w1: The home page states the chassis, the switch, the pathway and the three objectives in four short steps, and the Description page makes the gap, the construct and the success criterion explicit within two screens. Unusually, the home page carries a 'What we have not shown' block listing the four open questions, so a reader leaves with an accurate picture rather than a sales pitch. I could state the aim, the host, the parts and the measure of success after the home and Description pages alone.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is traceable to a table of per-specimen numbers: Table 2 (eighteen Bradford values with calibration-range flags), Table 5 (pigment index by strain and substrate), Table 7 (dry pellet mass, A400, slope, R2 for all six preparations), Table 11 (all 39 mass-loss measurements), Table 15 (char thickness with matched exposed bare-oak control). Statistics are appropriate and conservative, with Welch tests, Holm correction, Kruskal-Wallis checks, effect sizes and permutation tests reported alongside each other, and no measurement excluded. It stops short of 5 because the central application result rests on n = 3 and the pigment used in the coating was never the material that was characterised.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and the page order follows the project, but several standard pages are missing: /parts, /model, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols, /hardware and /education all return 404. Parts live on Contribution, protocols on Measurement and proof-of-concept inside Results, which works if you read the home page's 'Where to start' panel but costs a judge time who goes to the standard URLs. Content itself is long but well sectioned, with figures and tables numbered consistently and limits stated inline.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild this. The Contribution page hands over the five nested parts, the two substitutions that make the enzyme cloneable, the verified primer pair with Tm and a warning about its 3' poly-A run, and three transferable measurement practices. Measurement gives full protocols plus an explicit list of parameters that were not recorded, and Engineering's Future plans specifies the verification experiment including the missing empty-vector extract control and batch-tracking scheme. It is long, but it is organised rather than sprawling.
justification.w5: In-text numbered references appear on every page that makes an external claim, the reference lists are consistent between Description, Results and Engineering, and the sources I recognise (Sendovski 2011 on bacterial tyrosinase, Changela 2003 on CueR, the polydopamine-epoxy work) are real and are used for what they actually say. Prior iGEM work is cited specifically, including Cambridge's BBa_K274001 melA part and Nanjing's coating-versus-additive conclusion. Image provenance is handled by a dedicated AI Use and Credits page that states which illustrations were AI-drawn and asserts no data figure was AI-made or cleaned.

J2.one_line: A rare high school project that carries one idea all the way from a cloneable tyrosinase to a bacterially made wood coating measured against a commercial product, documented with unusual statistical honesty; the open questions are enzyme activity, pigment identity and a coating effect that does not survive its own correction.
strengths: Integrated chain from sequence design to material test: every coated oak disc used pigment made by their own strain, grown under conditions chosen in an earlier module (Results sections 1-6, Engineering modules 01-06).

Real DBTL, not a diagram: a failed single-layer screen (eight of eleven coated specimens worse than bare oak, Table 10) drove the two-layer redesign, and W9 was chosen for batch-to-batch consistency over W10's lower mean that hinged on one observation (Table 13).

Controls that most teams skip: empty-vector strain carried through pigment recovery (0.03 mg vs 4.19 mg), a melanin standard put through every purification step, and exposed bare-oak char controls that reduce the claimable char contribution from 183.7 um to 77 um.

Measurement discipline: per-measurand units, instruments and replication tabulated, a pre-specified 400-650 nm fit window, two failed Bradford curves reported rather than averaged, and eleven of eighteen protein values flagged as outside the calibration range.

Human practices that changed the build: the drying step was dropped on Prof. Gosset's advice, the coating uses a wet unpurified extract because purification is 60-70% of cost (Dr. Song), and an inhalation question from an occupational medicine researcher is carried into Future plans.

Five nested Registry parts with SO terms, host organisms, RFC 10/1000 export and a stated reuse rationale, plus verified primers and the two synonymous substitutions that make the published tyrosinase cloneable.
weaknesses: The central application claim is descriptive only: W9 vs untreated oak gives Holm-adjusted p = 0.194 at n = 3, and the commercial product also fails to separate from untreated wood in their rig, which says as much about the apparatus as about the coating.
No enzyme activity assay. A dopachrome assay at 475 nm is cheap and would have converted 'the tagged protein is present' into 'the enzyme works'.

The coating used crude sonicated lysate, not the purified pigment that was characterised, and the empty-vector extract control that would attribute the effect to melanin was never run, so the project's own headline cannot yet be credited to melanin.

Flame exposure was not standardised: burner-to-specimen distance set by hand, flame applied locally while mass loss is measured over the whole disc, no coating mass per unit area, no moisture conditioning. Char thickness is a geometric proxy with no temperature or heat-release measurement behind it.

All five Registry parts are credited solely to the supervising professor, with Conceptualisation and Investigation roles and no student named, which sits oddly against an otherwise detailed student attribution page.
Standard pages /parts, /model, /proof-of-concept, /implementation and /protocols return 404; the content exists but a judge has to be steered to it from the home page.
red_flags: Not an integrity concern, but a question for the panel: every Registry entry (BBa_262OK4RW, BBa_263QUR21, BBa_26XNC06W, BBa_26DHR36G, BBa_26MD3039) lists instructor Prof. Woo Rin Lee as the sole designer with Conceptualisation, Data Curation, Formal Analysis, Investigation and Supervision roles, and no student is credited on any part. I would ask the team who made the construct design decisions rather than infer anything.

Several standard pages (parts, model, proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols) are 404; content is reachable from Contribution, Measurement and Results, so I judged it, but teams should not rely on judges rerouting.

Safety note only, no action needed: the project involves open-flame testing of coated wood. The Safety page records that the iGEM Safety and Security Committee already asked them to reassess the fire hazard and that they responded with a documented risk assessment, a designated location, adult supervision and a stop criterion. Organisms are DH5-alpha and BL21, Risk Group 1, and no live engineered cells were in any fire test.
pages_read: Registry: BBa_262OK4RW, BBa_263QUR21, BBa_26DHR36G, BBa_26MD3039 (rendered part pages)

calibrated.changed: none — a6 3.5 (full readable form, but instructor sole designer on all five Registry entries) sits correctly between hongkong-jss/sms (4.0, complete and student-attributed) and the per-task-notebook teams (3.0); w3 3.5 matches my bar of 'five or more missing standard pages, otherwise good navigation'.

justification.a1: MelanoShield climbs from a restriction-site-cleaned synthetic tyrosinase, through copper-inducible expression and pigment recovery benchmarked against a Sepia melanin standard, to twelve sprayed coating formulations tested on oak against a marketed Korean fire protector, then FE-SEM of the char (Description; Results sections 1-6). That is two connected halves — a production route and a materials application — carried to data inside one season, which is more scope than most HS teams manage. It falls short of a 5 because the enzyme itself was never assayed, the coating used crude lysate rather than the pigment they characterised, and the headline coating comparison does not survive their own multiplicity correction (Results section 5).
justification.a2: The core biology is demonstrated with same-day controls: an anti-His blot puts a 33 kDa signal in copper-treated lanes and nothing in the empty-vector or no-copper lanes (Results Figure 10); the pigment index beats the empty vector at every L-tyrosine level, n=3 independent cultures, Holm p = 0.0011-0.0118 (Results Table 6); and recovered material gives 4.19 ± 0.34 mg per 10 mL against 0.03 ± 0.01 mg for the empty vector, with a log-linear spectral slope within 0.5% of the Sepia standard (Results Tables 7-8). The application half is weaker and the team says so: W9 at 3.06 ± 0.73% mass loss versus 9.36 ± 1.82% untreated reaches only Holm p = 0.194 (Results Table 12), the char difference of 77 µm sits at Welch p = 0.038 but permutation p = 0.10, and the empty-vector-extract control that would attribute any of it to melanin was never run.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by users rather than asserted: firefighters on what a retardant actually does, KICT on the three test endpoints and cost as the commercialisation barrier, Prof. Nam Jeong-min on VOC-heavy flame-retardant paints and on small residential buildings being exempt from treatment requirements (Human Practices sections 2.1-2.2). From that they chose the under-regulated small-building market as the realistic entry point and named factory application as a route around spray exposure (Human Practices section 4). It stops short of 5 because nothing was tested in or near a real setting and the product matched, rather than beat, a commercial spray on a hand-set bench burner.
justification.a4: Six modules each run as Design-Build-Test-Learn with the decision carried forward stated (Engineering Table 1). One Learn step genuinely changed the next Build: the single-layer screen gave a flat negative, with eight of eleven coated specimens losing more mass than untreated wood, so they doubled the application and raised replication to three independently prepared batches rather than changing the chemistry (Engineering Module 05). Two failed Bradford standard curves (R² 0.069 and 0.027) were reported rather than averaged away, and W9 was chosen on reproducibility with a leave-one-out sensitivity table (Engineering Table 16). No model was fitted to their own data and used for design, and they admit layer count cannot be isolated because the rounds differed in time and replication, which keeps this below the TAS calculator standard.
justification.a5: This is the strongest section and the chain is traceable in both directions. Prof. Gosset's advice that dried melanin will not redissolve removed the drying step, so the coating uses wet unpurified material; Prof. Lim's advice produced the anti-His blot and five copper levels; Song's and KICT's cost figures (60-70% of cost in purification) are why the first coating was made from crude extract; KICT's point that thickness is itself a test parameter fed the two-layer round (Human Practices section 3.1). A critical voice was sought out rather than avoided: Prof. Park Soyoung's humidifier-disinfectant argument that aerosolisation is the hazard, and that 'eco-friendly' framing lowers scrutiny, is carried into Engineering Future plans as an unanswered question. Two gaps hold it off 5: the spread-on comparison is planned, not run, and the surveys of 52 members of the public and the session with children at a care centre carry no mention of consent or ethical oversight, while the Safety page states 'We collected no data about people'.
justification.a6: Every member has their own Specific Tasks entry naming concrete work — Nicholas Ha on melanin extraction and instrument readings, Iyla on extraction, recovery and fire-test measurements, Yunho Lee designing and analysing the surveys — and instructor and PI roles are bounded, with Prof. Woo Rin Lee named as laboratory supervisor and strain-disposal holder (Attributions). AI use is disclosed in unusual detail, including that the mascot and decorative figures were drawn with Claude while no evidentiary figure was AI-made or cleaned (AI Use & Credits). Two things would need a session question rather than an accusation: who physically performed the Sanger reads and the SU5000 FE-SEM imaging is never said, and the Attributions summary of Prof. Gosset ('advised us to dry the melanin') contradicts the Human Practices account that he told them not to.
justification.a7: Five nested parts are submitted — pCopA promoter BBa_262OK4RW, the cleaned 891 bp tyrosinase BBa_263QUR21, the tagged 918 bp version BBa_26XNC06W, the cassette BBa_26DHR36G and the 5,709 bp construct BBa_26MD3039 (Contribution Table 1) — and the layering is deliberate so a team can take the promoter without the enzyme. The genuine design contribution is small but real and reusable: two synonymous substitutions (T153G, A495T) that remove internal BseRI and XhoI sites so the gene can be restriction-cloned at all, with the protein unchanged at all 297 positions (Contribution Table 2), plus a verified primer pair with its own weakness flagged. The system otherwise reuses an existing Addgene pCopA-RBS30 arrangement with the reporter swapped, so the synthetic-biology design work is competent rather than inventive.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is genuinely good: per-specimen mass records, a preparation-by-preparation purification log including solvent blanks (Measurement Table 4), full formulation compositions, protocols written to be repeated, and the modified coding sequence in an Engineering appendix. Contribution section 6 states what each Registry entry carries, down to Sanger coverage of the insert and both junctions on BBa_263QUR21. Two things cap this at 4: the wiki has no standard Parts page (it 404s, so the part table must be found on Contribution or at the end of Engineering), and I could not open the Registry entries to confirm the documentation described there, while the Bradford raw readings and the Sanger reads are said to be 'held in our laboratory records' rather than shown.
justification.w1: The home page gives the problem, the four-step mechanism (copper in, tyrosinase, eumelanin, char barrier) and the three objectives within a screen, then the headline numbers with the page each rests on. Unusually, it also carries a 'What we have not shown' block naming the four open questions before the reader reaches any results page, and an 'Explore the wiki' panel that says what each page contains. A reader knows what MelanoShield is and what it has not proved in about two minutes.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is tied to a figure or table with n, SD, confidence interval and a same-day control, and the separation between measured, modelled and planned is policed hard: Description Figure 2's chemistry comparison is labelled as the team's own qualitative reading, Figure 6's pathway is labelled as unmeasured, and the Future plans table states that no result is reported for any entry. Non-significance is reported rather than buried — 'none of these comparisons reached significance' after Holm (Results section 5) — and the crude extract is repeatedly distinguished from the characterised pigment. It is short of 5 only because the Bradford raw readings and Sanger traces are kept off-wiki and the Bradford estimates themselves rest on one usable curve with eleven of eighteen values extrapolated.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and the side menu maps onto the judging criteria, but several standard pages are missing: Parts, Model, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Education and Inclusivity all 404, with the part table folded into Contribution and Engineering and the implementation discussion into Human Practices section 4. Judges should not have to hunt for the parts list. There is also real sprawl and duplication — Engineering runs about 12,800 words and repeats the Bradford tables, pigment tables and coating tables almost verbatim from Results — which sits against the 'complete but not sprawling' standard.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: dated session-by-session methods (Experiments Table 1), protocols written for repetition (Measurement section 4), every formulation's composition, verified primers with their 3' weakness flagged, a troubleshooting table of what failed and what was changed (Contribution Table 5), a prioritised list of the next five measurements, and a safety page detailing the flame-test risk assessment and stop criterion. The reusable measurement practices — carrying the standard through the whole procedure, measuring the bare substrate under identical exposure, recording more than one standard curve — are written up as transferable advice. Only the absence of posted raw data files keeps it from 5.
justification.w5: Citations are consistent and specific across pages, with DOIs, Addgene RRIDs for both source plasmids, Sigma catalogue number for the standard, and an explicit statement separating the team's own measurements from the literature supporting background claims. Prior iGEM work is not just listed but argued with: Mingdao 2015's model-house test shaped their testing, PuiChing Macau 2020's adhesion fusion was considered and rejected because eumelanin offers no handle, and Cambridge 2009's BBa_K274001 is contrasted with their single-input copper design (Human Practices section 5.2). Image credit is given (NASA chart in Description Figure 1) and AI-drawn decorative artwork is credited and distinguished from evidentiary figures. I could not resolve the external links from this environment, so the score reflects form and specificity rather than verified link resolution.

J3.one_line: A disciplined high-school project that really did make melanin in E. coli and really did put it on wood: controlled, replicated upstream biology, an honestly under-powered coating result, and human practices that changed the bench work in traceable ways.
strengths: Core production chain is demonstrated with same-day controls at every step: anti-His blot with empty-vector and no-copper lanes, pigment index beating the empty vector at all four substrate levels (n=3 cultures), and 4.19 mg recovered pigment against 0.03 mg for the empty vector with a spectral slope within 0.5% of a Sepia standard

Unusual intellectual honesty — the single-layer screen is reported as a flat failure, two Bradford curves are reported as unusable, eleven of eighteen protein values are flagged as extrapolated, the Holm-corrected coating comparison is reported as non-significant, and the missing empty-vector-extract control is named by the team itself

Human practices with traceable consequences: Gosset's advice removed the drying step, Lim's advice produced the Western blot and the five-level copper experiment, KICT's thickness point drove the two-layer round, and Park Soyoung's aerosol argument is carried forward as an open safety question rather than dismissed

Attribution and AI disclosure are among the clearest I have seen at this level — per-member Specific Tasks, bounded instructor role, named external contributors with what each changed, and an explicit statement that no evidentiary figure was AI-made or cleaned

A small but genuinely reusable parts contribution: two synonymous substitutions that make the P. megaterium tyrosinase restriction-cloneable, submitted as a nested five-part collection with a verified primer pair and a troubleshooting record
weaknesses: The headline application result does not survive the team's own statistics: W9 against untreated oak is Holm p = 0.194 and the char difference gives permutation p = 0.10, so the coating remains a promising descriptive result at n=3 rather than a demonstrated effect

Enzyme activity was never assayed and the pigment was never chemically identified, so the catalytic claim rests on the pigment response, and the coating used crude lysate whose melanin content is unknown — the melanin-specific contribution is unresolved

Several standard wiki pages 404 (Parts, Model, Proof of Concept, Implementation), so the five Registry parts must be found on Contribution or at the foot of Engineering; the Registry entries themselves could not be opened from here to confirm the documentation described
Engineering and Results duplicate the same tables and prose at length (Engineering is about 12,800 words), which works against the complete-but-not-sprawling standard

Public surveys of 52 people and an activity session with children at a care centre carry no mention of consent, anonymity or adult oversight, and the Safety page states that no data about people was collected, which contradicts the survey work
red_flags: Internal inconsistency in attribution of advice: Human Practices says Prof. Gosset told them dried melanin behaves like charcoal so they cut the drying step, while the Attributions entry says he 'advised us to dry the melanin before formulation'. Likely a drafting error, but it is the one place where a documented design change and its stated source disagree — worth asking at the session.

Safety page asserts 'We collected no data about people, so no human subjects research was involved' while Human Practices reports in-person and online surveys of 52 and 49 respondents and a session with children; no consent or ethics statement appears anywhere on the wiki.

Registry part pages (BBa_262OK4RW, BBa_263QUR21, BBa_26XNC06W, BBa_26DHR36G, BBa_26MD3039) returned HTTP 403 from this environment, so the documentation the Contribution page says lives there is asserted but unverified by me.

Some supporting evidence is explicitly off-wiki — the individual Bradford standard readings and the Sanger reads are said to be held in laboratory records and available on request — so the sequence-verification claim that underpins the construct cannot be checked from the wiki alone.
pages_read: Registry part pages attempted (HTTP 403, not readable)

calibrated.changed: none. a2 of 4 holds: the upstream biology is controlled and replicated, but the coating comparison does not survive the team's own multiplicity correction and the empty-vector-extract control was never run, so this cannot sit with the three 4.5s.

one_line.en: A narrow but unusually clean chain from a cloneable tyrosinase to a bacterially made wood coating, with the best statistical honesty on the ballot and a headline coating result that does not survive its own correction.
one_line.zh: 從可選殖酪胺酸酶到細菌製木材塗層，鏈條雖窄但異常乾淨，統計誠實度全場最佳，但頭條塗層結果通不過自己的校正。

strengths: Anti-His Western with two negative controls plus 4.19 mg recovered pigment against 0.03 mg for empty vector, and a spectral slope matching an authentic melanin standard carried through the whole procedure
Raw and corrected p-values reported side by side, confidence intervals preferred at n = 3, a permutation check run against the team's own favourable result, and failed calibration curves published
A real data-driven redesign: a failed single-layer screen drove the two-layer round with higher replication and a commercial benchmark
Task-level attribution for every student, instructor and external contributor, with an explicit statement that no data figure was AI-generated
weaknesses: No coating comparison survives Holm correction; the best result is adjusted p = 0.194 at n = 3 and the commercial benchmark also fails to separate from bare wood
Tyrosinase activity was never assayed, so the enzymatic claim rests on an indirect pigment index
Coatings used crude lysate of unmeasured melanin content and the empty-vector extract control was never run
Narrowest scope of the leaders — no model, hardware or software — and Engineering and Results duplicate tables at length
red_flags: Two judges report that all five Registry entries name the supervising professor as sole designer with no student credited, which sits oddly against an otherwise detailed student attribution page
Standard pages parts, model, proof-of-concept, implementation and protocols return 404
Safety page states no data about people was collected while Human Practices reports surveys and a session with children, with no consent statement anywhere

screen.project_title: BlueCatcher — an ML-guided electrochemical miRNA biosensor for major depressive disorder
screen.what_they_built: A four-stage biosensor: three-way-junction DNA probes that recognize miR-124-3p and release a trigger, a toehold switch that converts the trigger into sfGFP/reporter expression, nuclease-mediated cleavage of an MB-labelled reporter, and an Au@SPCE square-wave-voltammetry readout — with a machine-learning design loop and a bioinformatics pipeline choosing the target.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and EPI300, plus cell-free reactions. ~40 new 2026 BBa parts in two documented collections (TWJ probe set and toehold switch sensor/trigger library, pL001-pL034 plasmid series).
screen.best_evidence: /results: background-corrected trigger-dependent toehold activation of approximately 60-fold (pL001 vs pL003, trigger-only pL004 subtracted; IPTG induction p<0.0001), supported by restriction-digest gels at expected 6,181/5,404 bp, Sanger chromatograms, and a 117-colony vs 3-colony ligase/no-ligase control.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and unusually rigorously: the IHP page writes down assumptions first and records four reversals, e.g. a psychiatrist and a clinical psychologist moved the output from a red/green binary verdict to a raw continuous value read only by a clinician, and an ML expert's challenge rebuilt the training pipeline around the team's own toehold screening data.
screen.reason: Module-by-module experimental validation with proper controls, a real design-predict-test ML loop feeding back into wet lab, hardware and electrochemistry, and the most disciplined human practices in the batch. The strongest candidate here; needs a full read, with attribution and the prior-team inheritance checked carefully.
screen.field_notes: Labi-Taiwan (Diagnostics, TWN; formerly Taipei-KCISLK-V3) built BlueCatcher, an electrochemical miRNA biosensor for major depressive disorder. A bioinformatics pipeline (differential expression, miRNA-mRNA networks, GSEA, WGCNA, HMDD and literature screening) narrowed 2,656 mature miRNAs to 16 candidates, an 8-miRNA shortlist and finally miR-124-3p as the first engineering target. Wet lab adapted a published CT2 toehold pair into a T7/sfGFP architecture, built sensor-only (pL003) and trigger-only (pL004) controls by BamHI/HindIII digestion and self-ligation of pL001 with gel and Sanger verification, and measured roughly 60-fold background-corrected trigger-dependent activation in BL21(DE3) (p<0.0001). They then screened ML-redesigned toehold switches, validated TWJ probes by native PAGE and FRET, screened nucleases and selected AciI, and built an Au@SPCE platform detecting an MB-labelled reporter by SWV; around 40 new parts are documented across two collections. The TWJ ML model was trained on the predecessor team's screening data, which judges should check against attribution expectations — the attributions page is only 69 words and the team page 181. Entrepreneurship is substantial (about 10,900 words) and the IHP page documents four assumption reversals against named clinicians, bioinformaticians and biosensing researchers plus a 432-respondent Taiwan depression awareness survey. End-to-end integration of recognition through electrochemical readout is stated as remaining future work.

justification.a1: The scope is unusually large for a high school team and the pieces build on one another: a reprocessed miRNA-seq discovery pipeline (Model, 2,656 mature miRNAs to 16 to 5 targets), 34 plasmids built and sequenced, two ML models whose predictions were then tested at the bench, nuclease selection, and an Au@SPCE readout with a stated LOD (Results, Figures 2-28). It stops one step short of the GreatBay/TAS arc because the full chain miRNA to TWJ to toehold to AciI to reporter to SWV was never closed; the team says so plainly in Future Perspectives. The TWJ-to-toehold coupling at 1 nM miR-124-3p (Figure 29) is the nearest thing to an integrated proof and is explicitly called initial.
justification.a2: Nearly every functional claim carries the controls I look for: sensor-only and trigger-only plasmids built specifically as controls, a no-ligase transformation control (117 vs 3 colonies, Figure 3), blank and four non-target miRNAs for TWJ specificity (Figure 18), and a 0 nM electrode control (Figure 27). Replicates are stated (n = 3 throughout), error bars defined as SD, ANOVA used, units given, and the SWV work reports R2 = 0.9457, LOD 7.53 nM and a between-batch CV of 10.66% (Figures 27-28). Two things hold it below 5: all targets were tested as synthetic DNA analogues in buffer rather than RNA miRNA in a biological matrix, and the complete sensing path was never demonstrated end to end.
justification.a3: The use case is specific and has been narrowed by the people who would use it: an auxiliary molecular readout for clinicians at first presentation, during treatment and in remission, with workplace and EAP deployment ruled out after an HR/EAP interview (Human Practices, Phase 4). The Entrepreneurship page gives a six-year roadmap, a B2B model and a competitive comparison, and the Education survey (n = 432) supplies the team's own evidence that perceived stigma, not literacy, is the public-facing problem. What is missing is any measurement in a real-world-like setting: no plasma, serum or spiked-matrix test, so the clinical impact rests on roadmap and literature rather than the team's own data.
justification.a4: The Engineering page runs eleven labelled DBTL cycles and several are genuine redesigns driven by a result, not troubleshooting. The first nine toehold candidates gave no significant in vivo ON/OFF response (Figure 9), which triggered an ML-guided second design round (pL026-pL028) that did (Figure 11B). The electrochemical work is the clearest cycle: the first SWV series showed no consistent concentration dependence (Figure 26), and the team then changed fabrication, acquisition parameters and baseline processing and re-ran the series to obtain a log-linear calibration (Figure 27). Success criteria are usually stated before the test, and the team also reports learning that cell-free and in vivo rank orders disagree.
justification.a5: This is the strongest human practices work I have read from a high school team this round. Fourteen external engagements are organised with AREA, each phase closes with an explicit Before to After, and the changes are substantive rather than cosmetic: the user moved from patient to clinician after the Star Clubhouse visit, the red/green indicator was abandoned for a raw continuous value after clinical psychologist input, the ML pipeline was repointed from predicting disease to predicting probe and switch designs after a bioinformatics interview, and workplace use was excluded. The three epistemological boundaries (correlation is not causation, biomarker is not disease, biologisation is not reductionism) are applied as design constraints, not decoration.
justification.a6: The per-person attribution is specific and task-level, and students clearly ran a great deal of the bench and dry-lab work. But the lab PI's own entry states that she designed the overall experimental workflow, developed and refined the protocols, and conducted most of the preliminary experiments before student implementation; two laboratory teaching assistants gave hands-on support during sessions, a second instructor also ran part of the preliminary work, and Twist synthesised the 13 parental plasmids. That is more adult design and pre-work than the GreatBay or TAS pattern, so a6 sits at the upper end of shared work. I credit the team for declaring it openly, including a frank note about a former member and academic integrity.
justification.a7: The project is built from recognisable synthetic biology parts: T7-driven toehold switch sensors with sfGFP reporters adapted from Fang et al. 2025 but rebuilt with a new promoter and reporter, trigger RNAs, a 21-nt linker and T7 terminator reused from earlier Registry entries (BBa_K5038001, BBa_K5106019), plus a DNA three-way junction recognition layer and a cell-free expression chassis. Parental plasmids were deliberately designed with BamHI/HindIII sites so sensor-only and trigger-only controls could be cut from them, and XhoI/NotI sites so sfGFP can later be swapped for AciI, which is real modularity. The electrochemical layer is hardware, but the biology is not nominal.
justification.a8: Forty-three Registry entries are listed on the Parts page and the ones I opened resolve with sequence, circular/linear topology, Engineered Region role, designed-for host (E. coli BL21, DH5alpha) and a rationale; BBa_26AL8EMO also carries Registry documentation items of type experiment and characterisation, including the cell-free evaluation text and a plate image. Against that, the characterisedIn field is empty on the parts I checked and most entries appear to lean on the wiki for their data, which p.18 does not let me credit. The Parts table also contains one malformed identifier, Bba-2697uew4 for pL027, which does not resolve as written.
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem (no objective, repeatable molecular reference for MDD), the approach (miRNA biomarker discovery, functional nucleic acid probes, portable electrochemical reader) and the positioning as an auxiliary rather than diagnostic tool within roughly one screen. The Description page then gives an Overview, Strategy and a four-item Achievement list that match what the Results page actually shows. A little of the landing-page copy is marketing cadence (fast, accurate, portable, cost-friendly) ahead of the evidence, which is the only drift.
justification.w2: Figures carry full legends with excitation and emission wavelengths, gel percentages and run conditions, statistical tests and n, and the gels name their lanes and mark expected fragment sizes (Figures 2, 14, 21, 24). Supplementary files on the wiki provide plasmid maps for pL001-pL034, transformation plate records and three parts of Sanger verification. Failures and limits are shown rather than hidden, including the non-significant initial screen and the unusable first SWV series. The one gap is that the integration claim rests on a single modest experiment at 1 nM.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly (Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Entrepreneurship, Human Practices) and the per-page section menus make long pages tractable. But five standard URLs return nothing: proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, inclusivity and sustainability. Protocols are in fact on the Experiments page and the proof-of-concept content is inside Results, yet a judge following the standard page list hits dead ends, which p.29 warns against. The pages are also heavy (Engineering alone is about 18,400 words) with much of the substance folded behind plus-toggles, so the wiki edges toward sprawling.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way with this. The 66-page laboratory notebook PDF is hosted on the team's own static namespace, the Experiments page gives step-by-step protocols with volumes and buffers, the Measurement page explains why each technique was chosen, supplementary files hold plasmid maps and sequencing traces, and the software is in the iGEM GitLab repository with local-install instructions and a documented NUPACK licensing workaround. Failures and dead ends are recorded, which is what makes a record genuinely reusable. Raw numeric data behind the plots are not posted, which is the main thing stopping a 5.
justification.w5: References are numbered per page with resolvable DOIs (Fang 2025, Angenent-Mari 2020, Sadat Mousavi 2020, Anshori 2022, Pheeney and Barton 2012), the GEO accessions for the discovery cohort are named, and the survey instruments are credited to their published scales. Nine prior iGEM teams are credited on the Description page with an explicit statement of what each contributed, and the TWJ model is openly said to be trained on the 2025 Taipei-KCISLK-V3 dataset. AI tool use is declared on the attribution form, including FigureLabs for figure layout with the note that figures were redrawn. Inline citation on a few of the longer narrative passages is lighter than elsewhere.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete high school project: a real target-discovery pipeline, ML models validated at the bench, control-rich assays with replicates and statistics, and the best human practices work in the field, held back from the very top by a chain that was never closed end to end and by a PI who designed the protocols and ran the preliminary experiments.
strengths: Control discipline is excellent throughout: purpose-built sensor-only and trigger-only plasmids, a no-ligase transformation control (117 vs 3 colonies, Results Fig 3), blank plus four non-target miRNAs for specificity (Fig 18), and a 0 nM electrode control, with n = 3 and ANOVA stated on essentially every quantitative figure.

Genuine data-driven redesign rather than troubleshooting: nine initial toehold candidates gave no significant in vivo response (Fig 9), prompting an ML-guided second round that did (Fig 11B); the first SWV series showed no concentration dependence (Fig 26), prompting a fabrication and acquisition overhaul that produced a log-linear calibration with LOD 7.53 nM and between-batch CV 10.66% (Figs 27-28).

Failures and limits are reported rather than smoothed over, including the in vivo versus cell-free rank-order disagreement and the honest statement that the complete miRNA-to-SWV path is not yet connected (Results, Future Perspectives).

Human Practices is substantive and traceable: fourteen engagements under AREA with a Before-to-After per phase, including abandoning the red/green readout, moving the user from patient to clinician, repointing the ML model from predicting disease to predicting probe designs, and excluding workplace/EAP deployment.

Dry lab is real work, not decoration: FASTQ reprocessing on Galaxy with miRDeep2, differential expression, GSEA and WGCNA narrowing 2,656 mature miRNAs to 5 targets, and ML models with an 80/20 split plus a 35-design external validation set and five-fold cross-validation.

Reproducibility material is strong for a high school team: a 66-page notebook PDF on the team's own static namespace, protocols with volumes on the Experiments page, plasmid maps, transformation plate records and Sanger verification as supplementary files, and the software in the iGEM GitLab repository.
weaknesses: The complete sensing chain was never demonstrated. sfGFP remains the toehold output; AciI-mediated reporter cleavage was shown only on purified components by PAGE and was never coupled to the Au@SPCE readout, so no miRNA-to-current measurement exists.

All miRNA targets were tested as synthetic DNA analogues in clean buffer. No RNA target, no plasma, serum or spiked-matrix experiment, which is exactly the matrix-effect risk the team's own interviewee (Ja-An Annie Ho) raised.

The attributions form states that the lab PI designed the experimental workflow, wrote and refined the protocols and conducted most of the preliminary experiments before student implementation, with two laboratory teaching assistants giving hands-on support. Declared honestly, but it lowers aspect 6.

Five standard page URLs are dead: proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, inclusivity and sustainability. The content exists elsewhere (Results, Experiments) but judges following the standard list hit nothing.

Registry entries carry sequence, topology, host and rationale, but the characterisedIn field is empty on the parts I opened and most experimental evidence sits on the wiki rather than on the Registry entry, which p.18 does not allow me to credit to the part.
One Parts table identifier is malformed, Bba-2697uew4 for pL027, and does not resolve as written.
The TWJ-to-toehold integration rests on a single low-signal experiment at 1 nM miR-124-3p (Fig 29) with no replication across targets; the team itself calls the fluorescence relatively low.

The portable reader and BlueCatcher app are presented as CAD renderings and interface mock-ups on the Hardware page; all electrochemistry reported was done on a benchtop analyser, and no built reader was tested.
The wiki is heavy (Engineering about 18,400 words, Entrepreneurship about 10,900) with much substance folded behind plus-toggles, which sits uneasily with 'complete but not sprawling'.
red_flags: Five standard pages (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, inclusivity, sustainability) return no content, so a judge following the standard URL list finds dead pages; content is reachable only from non-standard pages.

Attributions disclose that the PI designed the experimental workflow and protocols and ran most preliminary experiments before students implemented them; this lowers aspect 6 but is not an integrity matter and was declared clearly.
Malformed Registry identifier 'Bba-2697uew4' in the composite parts table (Parts page, Table 5) does not resolve.

Hardware reader and companion app are design concepts only; the Hardware page describes automated operation in the present tense ('fully automated once the sample is loaded') although no built device was tested. I treated this as design, not result.

No integrity concerns found. AI tool use (ChatGPT, Claude, FigureLabs) is declared on the attribution form with scope, and figures are stated to have been redrawn in PowerPoint/BioRender. Nothing here warrants an RCC referral.

Safety is within the High School Whitelist: RG1 E. coli BL21(DE3) and EPI300 only, synthetic DNA analogues, public GEO datasets, BSL-1 facility at NTU. The n = 432 public survey used an informed-consent statement and anonymous collection.
pages_read: notebook (66-page PDF on team static namespace)
Registry API entries BBa_26AL8EMO, BBa_26XZJS0J, BBa_26VNLRU2, BBa_26PULKVH and documentation for BBa_26AL8EMO

calibrated.changed: none. a6 3.5 still sits correctly between the teams with full task-level attribution (4.0-4.5) and those with none (2.5-3.0): the attribution is specific, but the declared PI pre-work (workflow design, protocol development, most preliminary experiments) is more adult design than SMS-Shenzhen's declared sponsor-lab arrangement, which I scored 4.0.

justification.a1: The scope is far beyond a typical high school project and is told as one chain: a GEO miRNA-seq discovery cohort narrowed to miR-124-3p, 34 plasmids built and sequence-verified, 25 TWJ probe combinations screened per target by FRET, a three-nuclease screen, and an Au@SPCE electrochemical readout with an LOD of 7.53 nM and a 10.66% between-batch CV (Results, Figures 15-18, 20-22, 27-28). It falls short of a 5 only because the chain is never closed: sfGFP was never replaced by AciI, the electrode was only ever driven by synthetic MB-reporter rather than by the biology, and the portable reader on the Hardware page is a CAD exploded view with no bench measurement at all.
justification.a2: The main modules are shown working with real controls and replicates: sensor-only and trigger-only plasmids as background controls with a ~60-fold background-corrected activation (Results Figure 5), in-gel fluorescence confirming the band is sfGFP (Figure 6), TWJ specificity against four non-target miRNAs (Figure 18), a 0-200 nM concentration series (Figure 17), and TWJ-to-toehold coupling still detectable at 1 nM miR-124-3p (Figure 29). Failures are reported rather than hidden - nine first-round candidates gave no significant ON/OFF (Figure 9) and the first SWV series was non-monotonic (Figure 26). The deductions are for an unintegrated device chain and no test in any biological matrix; everything is clean buffer.
justification.a3: The route to use is unusually well argued for a high school team: the Human Practices page records the output being redefined from a red/green light to a raw value returned only to the clinician, workplace and EAP settings being excluded after a conversation with an HR/EAP consultant, and the claim wording unified as auxiliary screening after regulatory advice. The team also states plainly that the panel was discovered in a female-only cohort and should not be assumed to transfer to males (Engineering, Dry Lab Target Selection Cycle 2). What keeps this below 4 by my scale is that nothing was tested in a realistic setting - no plasma, serum or spiked matrix, unlike the wastewater-style test TAS Taipei ran.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect and the one I looked at hardest. Several cycles are real, not troubleshooting: the H2O2 pretreatment was dropped after CV showed no advantage over H2SO4 alone (Engineering, Signal Generation Cycle 1); the non-monotonic SWV response in Cycle 3 drove standardisation of acquisition parameters and baseline fitting, producing y = 2.313 log(X) - 2.028, R2 = 0.9457 in Cycle 4; Trigger A failed to form the B-Initiator complex on native PAGE, so Trigger C was carried forward (Cycle 4, Figure 11). The models are fitted to the team's own 2,500-design TWJ dataset and then tested prospectively on miR-124-3p and miR-3137, neither in the training set, with native PAGE matching the Signal/No Signal calls (Results Figure 14). The team also states honestly that it could not isolate how much of the improvement came from model ranking.
justification.a5: Fourteen external engagements across four AREA phases, each closing with a named Before and After that points at a specific conversation: the user moved from patient to clinician after Star Clubhouse and two psychologists, the ML pipeline was rebuilt to predict probes rather than disease after a bioinformatics scholar challenged it, the binary indicator was abandoned after field questions showed people read a light as a graded verdict, and sampling time and medication controls were written into the protocol after a neurobiologist raised circadian effects. The survey (n = 432, with reported internal consistency of 0.66/0.84/0.72) was used to retire the team's own destigmatisation claim rather than to decorate the page. Just short of 5 because much of the strongest material sits on sub-pages (Stakeholders, Responsibilities) rather than being fully evidenced on the standard page.
