justification.a6: The Attributions page renders with navigation and footer only - no who-did-what form, no fields, nothing (corpus attributions.txt, 69 words, and the live page fetches empty). That is the one place the handbook tells me to look. Against that, the wet lab was run in the Biochemistry Center at National Taiwan University (Safety page, Figure 1), plasmids were synthesised and NGS-verified by Twist Bioscience (Parts page), and three AI assistants supported literature screening (Engineering, Dry Lab Cycle 4) - all declared, which is to the team's credit, but with no attribution form I cannot tell which students executed the cloning, electrochemistry or sequencing analysis. I am not alleging anything; I simply cannot verify it, and the missing form is itself the deficiency.
justification.a7: The project is genuinely built on standard synthetic biology parts: a toehold switch collection of 13 sensors, 7 triggers, shared T7 promoter/sfGFP/linker/terminator components and 13 composite sensor-trigger plasmids, with 43 BBa IDs listed on the Parts page. The parental plasmid is deliberately modular - BamHI and HindIII sites to generate sensor-only and trigger-only controls, XhoI and NotI around the reporter so sfGFP can be swapped for AciI later - which is exactly the reuse-oriented design the Parts criteria ask for, and the TWJ/THS predictor software extends it to new targets. Not a 5 because the architecture is adapted from Fang et al. (2025) and I could not open the Registry pages to confirm the entries are more than listings.
justification.a8: On the wiki the documentation is excellent: every claim carries a numbered figure with a full caption, supplementary plasmid maps for pL001-pL034, bacterial culture and transformation plate records, three parts of Sanger sequencing verification, and reusable protocols on the Contribution and Experiments pages. The Registry side I could not verify - parts.igem.org returned 403 to me - and the handbook rule is that parts are judged on the Registry, not the wiki, so I cannot award the documentation credit the wiki alone would suggest. The Parts table also contains a malformed ID (Bba-2697uew4 for pL027), the Notebook page is nothing but an embedded file, and engineering cycle text cross-references Figure 19A-F inside a block whose figure is numbered 13.
justification.w1: The home page states the aim in one line - more objective, more accessible depression monitoring - and names the three pillars (miRNA biomarker discovery, functional nucleic acid probes, portable electrochemical reader) with one sentence each. After the Description page I can state the chassis, the target, the sensing chain and what success would look like. It loses a point because the home page leans on large statistics and rhetorical questions before the mechanism appears, and the actual molecular architecture is only reachable one page deeper.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim on the Results page is anchored to a figure with replicates, error bars and a named statistical test: n = 3 throughout, p-values reported, one-way ANOVA for the concentration and specificity series, a negative control at 0 nM, and a between-batch reproducibility experiment. The team consistently distinguishes what was measured from what is predicted or planned - the Future Perspectives section states explicitly that sfGFP has not yet been replaced by AciI and that end-to-end signal transmission is not established. Just short of 5 because the hardware reader and the app interface are presented as figures with no measurement behind them.
justification.w3: Navigation by Project / Wet Lab / Dry Lab / Human Practices / Entrepreneurship is coherent and each page has a working in-page contents list. But six standard pages - proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design, inclusivity and sustainability - return nothing, which forces a judge to hunt for proof of concept inside Results and for design inside Parts and Engineering. The pages that do exist are very long (Engineering ~18,400 words, Model ~14,500, Entrepreneurship ~10,900); this is sprawling rather than complete but not sprawling.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: full protocols on the Experiments page, plasmid maps and sequencing records as supplementary files, the TWJ/THS predictor with local installation instructions, and a Contribution page that spells out what is reusable. Two things stop a team reproducing the work - the Laboratory Notebook page is 79 words wrapping an embedded file rather than a dated record, and with no attributions a reader cannot tell which steps needed a university lab. The useful material is also scattered across very long pages.
justification.w5: Every page closes with a numbered reference list, in-text citation is used where it matters (Fang et al. for the sensor-trigger architecture, Sadat Mousavi et al. for the nuclease strategy, Anshori et al. for gold electrodeposition, Angenent-Mari et al. for the toehold training set), and the Description page credits nine prior iGEM teams with specific statements of what was taken from each. The DOIs I spot-checked are well formed and match the claims they support. Below 5 because figures and schematics carry no credit line, and the Education-page survey instrument is referenced but its source is not.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineering-led high school project with real DBTL cycles, controlled data and outstanding Human Practices, held back by an empty Attributions page, six missing standard pages, and a sensing chain whose modules work separately but were never joined end to end.
strengths: Real engineering cycles where data changed the design: H2O2 pretreatment dropped after CV showed no benefit, non-monotonic SWV fixed by standardising acquisition and baseline fitting (R2 = 0.9457, LOD 7.53 nM), Trigger A abandoned after native PAGE showed no B-Initiator complex

Controls and replicates throughout: sensor-only and trigger-only plasmids, in-gel fluorescence confirming the band is sfGFP, specificity against four non-target miRNAs, 0-200 nM concentration series, n = 3 with stated statistics
Models fitted to the team's own 2,500-design TWJ dataset and tested prospectively on two miRNAs absent from training, with native PAGE confirming the Signal / No Signal calls

Human Practices with fourteen engagements and a traceable Before to After for each: user redefined from patient to clinician, binary indicator abandoned, workplace and EAP settings excluded, sampling-time controls written into the protocol

Honest negative reporting - nine first-round toehold candidates gave no significant ON/OFF, the ML-best candidate in cells was not the best in cell-free, and the female-only discovery cohort is named as a limit on the panel
A modular parts collection built for reuse: restriction sites deliberately placed to generate controls and to swap sfGFP for the eventual nuclease output
weaknesses: The Attributions page is empty - navigation and footer only - so there is no who-did-what record, despite work in a university lab, commercial plasmid synthesis and declared AI assistance in literature screening
Six standard pages (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design, inclusivity, sustainability) return nothing, pushing a judge to hunt for proof of concept inside Results
The sensing chain is never closed: sfGFP was not replaced by AciI, and the electrode was only ever challenged with synthetic MB-reporter, never with the output of the biology
The portable reader and the BlueCatcher app are design renderings with no bench measurement, calibration or sensor characterisation - the Hardware page carries no units or data at all
Nothing was tested in any biological matrix; all performance figures come from clean buffer, and the team's own stakeholder warned about matrix effects
Sprawl: Engineering ~18,400 words, Model ~14,500, Entrepreneurship ~10,900, with substantial duplication of the same figures and text between Results and Engineering
The Laboratory Notebook page is a 79-word wrapper around an embedded file rather than a dated record
red_flags: Attributions page renders empty on both the crawl and a live fetch - no attribution form, which the handbook treats as the primary source for aspect 6; I raise this as a question for the team, not an allegation

Parts page states three AI assistants supported literature searching, screening and structured extraction for the miRNA evidence review, with team verification of original sources claimed; the team also writes that its literature screening ledger is still being reconciled, so the 8-of-16 literature support figure should be treated as unverified

Registry part pages could not be reached from here (parts.igem.org returned 403), so the depth of the 43 claimed BBa entries is unverified; aspects 7 and 8 are scored on that uncertainty, not on the wiki tables
Malformed part ID in the Parts composite table: 'Bba-2697uew4' for pL027, where every other entry follows BBa_26xxxxxx

Figure cross-reference errors in the Engineering page (Signal Generation Cycle 1 text cites Figure 19A-F while the panel is numbered Figure 13; Cycle 2 text cites Figure 25C and F, a Results-page number)

Several supplementary files (plasmid maps, plate records, sequencing verification, protocols, notebook) are embedded viewers; I could read their captions and context but not their contents, so the verification they claim is taken as stated rather than checked

calibrated.changed: none — empty form with declared university-lab and commercial synthesis is the 2.0 band; w3 3.0 for six missing standard pages plus heavy sprawl matches cataverse and keystone.

justification.a1: BlueCatcher climbs through four linked layers in one season: a transcriptomic target-selection pipeline that ends at miR-124-3p (Model), a TWJ recognition module characterised by PAGE and FRET, a toehold-switch module screened in E. coli and cell-free, a nuclease/reporter arm, and an Au@SPCE electrochemical readout with a calibration curve (Results). On top sits a trained, experimentally tested ML design tool (Software) and a four-phase HP programme. It falls short of a 5 only because the modules were never joined end to end: the Results page itself states the next step is replacing sfGFP with AciI and testing whether cleavage gives an SWV response.
justification.a2: The core pieces demonstrably work with proper controls: the reference switch gave ~60-fold trigger-dependent activation against sensor-only and trigger-only plasmids with n=3 and p<0.0001, confirmed at protein level by in-gel fluorescence against CBB staining (Results Figs 5-6); the selected TWJ pairs show concentration dependence 0-200 nM and discriminate four non-target miRNAs (Figs 17-18); SWV gives R²=0.9457, LOD 7.53 nM and a 10.66% between-batch CV (Figs 27-28). What is not shown is the device: no AciI-driven cleavage on the electrode, no end-to-end miRNA-to-current signal, and no human sample of any kind, which the team states plainly rather than glossing over.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by people who would use it, not just literature: a psychiatrist of fifteen years, two clinical psychologists, a regulatory specialist and an MDD patient all appear with specific positions on the Integrated HP page, and the deployment route (healthcare institutions and health-examination centres as a B2B channel, workplace and EAP settings excluded) is concrete and bounded. It stops short of 5 because nothing was tested in or near a real clinical setting; clinical-sample validation sits in the roadmap, and the pre-market timeline was honestly stretched from three years to six.
justification.a4: Several real DBTL loops turn on failures: the nine first-generation switches gave no significant ON/OFF difference in vivo, and that failure drove the ML redesign (pL026-028, all p<0.0001) on the Engineering page; Trigger A failed to form the B-Initiator complex in native PAGE, so Trigger C was carried forward; the H2O2 pretreatment was dropped after CV showed it added nothing; unstable first SWV measurements drove parameter and baseline-processing optimisation. The ML model was trained on the team's own TWJ screening data, used prospectively, and its cell-free failure to reproduce in-vivo ranking is reported rather than hidden. Quantitative success criteria are mostly implicit rather than pre-stated, which keeps it just below 5.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the project. The AREA structure records assumptions before each phase and each of the four phases names a reversal traceable to a named person: a psychiatrist and a clinical psychologist moved the target from MDD-as-entity to symptom domains; a bioinformatician rebuilt the ML pipeline so the model predicts probes, not disease; two psychologists and an STS scholar killed the red/green indicator in favour of a raw value with three written exclusions; an EAP consultant removed workplace deployment. Critical voices are kept intact, including a patient whose biomedicalisation argument the team says it cannot refute, and the n=432 survey reports informed consent, translated scales, alpha values and its own limitations.
justification.a6: Attribution is unusually honest and granular: the iGEM form gives per-student task lists, discloses ChatGPT/Claude/FigureLabs use, names IDT and Twist offers, and even records two members withdrawn, one over integrity concerns. Against that, the primary PI's own entry says she designed the experimental workflow and protocols and conducted most of the preliminary experiments before student implementation; the 13 plasmids were synthesised and cloned by Twist; and the 2,500-combination TWJ training set came from last year's Taipei-KCISLK-V3 team. All disclosed, but it leaves adults and predecessors holding a large share of the design and build, so 3.5 with a session question rather than any accusation.
justification.a7: The design is built from programmable nucleic-acid components with a clear standard-parts logic: 43 BBa IDs on the Parts page covering 13 sensors, 7 triggers, shared T7/sfGFP/linker/terminator elements, and 13 sensor-trigger composites, with the parental plasmid deliberately carrying BamHI/HindIII sites to generate controls and XhoI/NotI to swap the reporter later. Several composites are shown to work (pL001, pL013, pL026-028), and the BlueCatcher software counts as a reusable standard component. Two previously registered parts are reused and credited.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is excellent: figure captions carry n, statistics and instrument settings, and plasmid maps, transformation plate records and Sanger traces are posted as supplementary PDFs on static.igem.wiki, with protocols on the Contribution page. I could not open the Registry entries to check their depth (parts.igem.org served a bot-verification page, which I did not attempt to bypass), and one listed ID on the Parts page is malformed ("Bba-2697uew4" for pL027), which suggests the Registry links were not all checked. Without verified Registry-side characterisation I hold this at 4.
justification.w1: The Description page states the gap, the four-direction strategy and the achievements compactly, and Figure 3 gives an integrated-approach schematic. The home page funnels a reader through problem, question and the three technical pillars with links onward to Results, Model, HP and Entrepreneurship. The scrolling home narrative takes a little longer than Lambert-style directness to say exactly what is detected and how.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently tied to figures with controls, replicates and statistics, and the separation of evidence types is explicit: the Model page has a dedicated limitations block stating no human specimens were tested and that pathway convergence is within-cohort integration, not replication, and the Results page labels the TWJ-toehold coupling as an initial proof of concept with low absolute fluorescence. The hardware reader and companion app are design concepts with no measured data, which the Hardware page's "we aim to develop" wording signals but does not flag as strongly as elsewhere.
justification.w3: Standard pages are all present and the Wet Lab / Dry Lab / HP grouping maps onto the judging criteria, with per-page tables of contents and collapsible sections. Two substantive HP pages (Stakeholders, Responsibilities) sit off the standard set, though the HP page links them clearly. The main deduction is bulk: Engineering runs to ~18,400 words and Model ~14,500, with material repeated almost verbatim between Engineering and Results, which is closer to sprawling than to "complete but not sprawling".
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: three reusable protocols, a notebook PDF, plasmid maps for pL001-pL034, transformation records, full Sanger verification, a software user manual, local installation instructions and an iGEM GitLab repository. The raw 2,500-design TWJ dataset is withheld as ongoing research, and the online predictor is a demonstration only because NUPACK cannot be redistributed, so full reproduction of the ML step needs a local install.
justification.w5: Citations are dense, specific and resolve to real literature (Green 2014, Angenent-Mari 2020, Sadat Mousavi 2020, Fang 2025, Anshori 2022), the survey instruments are properly attributed to DepSter and the Depression Stigma Scale, and nine prior iGEM teams including the team's own 2025 predecessor are credited on the Description page with what was taken from each. AI assistance in literature screening is disclosed with a stated team verification step, and the screening count is marked provisional. Figure-tool credit (BioRender, FigureLabs) appears in the attribution form rather than in captions.

J3.one_line: A technically deep, honestly reported modular miRNA biosensor with outstanding integrated human practices; the modules work separately with real controls, but the device was never joined end to end and the PI carried much of the experimental design.
strengths: Human Practices is the best kind: four phases, fourteen named engagements, and a reversal in each one that is traceable to a specific conversation (binary red/green indicator abandoned, workplace/EAP deployment excluded, ML repositioned to predict probes rather than disease)

Real experimental evidence with controls throughout: sensor-only and trigger-only plasmids for every switch claim, in-gel fluorescence plus Coomassie at protein level, four non-target miRNAs for specificity, and an SWV calibration with LOD 7.53 nM and 10.66% between-batch CV

Failures are reported and acted on: nine first-generation switches gave no significant ON/OFF response in vivo, Trigger A failed to form the B-Initiator complex, and the ML-favoured candidates lost to non-ML pL013 in the cell-free system, all stated plainly

The machine-learning tool was trained on the team's own screening data, validated on 35 held-out designs, used prospectively to design pL026-028, and then tested in the lab, with the software released on iGEM GitLab

Unusually disciplined epistemic framing: explicit limitation blocks on the Model page, three written boundaries, three exclusions, and an admission that the patient's biomedicalisation critique cannot be refuted
weaknesses: No end-to-end demonstration: sfGFP is still the toehold output, AciI-mediated cleavage was never coupled to the electrode, and no human serum or plasma was tested, so the headline claim of MDD miRNA detection remains unproven as a system

The primary PI's own attribution entry says she designed the experimental workflow and protocols and ran most preliminary experiments before student implementation, and the TWJ training set came from last year's team, which bounds how much of the design was the students' own

Hardware is a design, not a result: the portable reader and the BlueCatcher app carry no measured data, and the app's Low/Moderate/High banding sits awkwardly against the HP decision that the output must be a raw value rather than a graded verdict
Sprawl and duplication: Engineering (~18,400 words) and Results (~8,900) repeat large passages almost verbatim, making the evidence harder to audit than it needs to be
Registry-side documentation could not be verified from the wiki alone, and one composite part ID on the Parts page is malformed ("Bba-2697uew4"), suggesting the links were not all checked
red_flags: Could not verify Registry part pages: parts.igem.org returned a bot-verification challenge, which I did not attempt to bypass. Registry depth is therefore unconfirmed and a8 is capped accordingly; ask the team to show a part page in session.

Hardware page describes a three-level Low/Moderate/High app output, which conflicts with the Integrated HP page's decision that the device gives a raw value and no graded verdict. Likely an un-updated page rather than misconduct, but worth asking.

The HP, Stakeholders and Responsibilities prose is markedly more fluent and more conceptually assured than most student-written sections elsewhere on the wiki. AI use for organisation and polish is disclosed in the attribution form, which the handbook permits; I record this as an attribution question for the session, not a penalty.

A former member was removed partly over academic-integrity concerns (disclosed in the attribution form). The disclosure itself is creditable; no evidence of any integrity problem in the submitted work was found.

calibrated.changed: none. The a5 of 5 survives the cross-check: unlike the other two teams I gave 5 on this aspect, the n=432 survey reports informed consent, translated instruments and alpha values, so it does not have the reflective gap I docked eleven other teams for.

screen.project_title: SWARM: de novo minibinders against Deformed Wing Virus VP3 plus multiplexed RNAi against Varroa
screen.what_they_built: A two-arm honeybee-health platform: computationally designed de novo minibinders targeting the DWV VP3 capsid protein, and dsRNA targeting three Varroa salivary genes, supported by the PRINCE binding-site prioritisation tool and the Vapor-X low-cost drying hardware.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli expression for minibinder and VP3; Sf9 insect cells with a psiCHECK-2 dual-luciferase reporter for the RNAi arm; T7 RiboMAX dsRNA synthesis. ~37 new BBa parts registered.
screen.best_evidence: /results: anti-His/anti-FLAG dot blots with ImageJ integrated-density quantification show the FLAG minibinder co-eluting with His-VP3 (Wash 3: 8,427 vs 7,501) while the minibinder alone peaks at only 2,783; Adaptyv BLI gives a lead candidate at 603.6 nM combined affinity (95% CI 497.1-733.3 nM) across two replicates; GFP-nanobody positive control shows ~91% of recovered fluorescence shifting into low-imidazole washes.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, explicitly: researcher advice moved them from nanobodies to minibinders and narrowed designs to specific VP3 regions; beekeepers shaped delivery via existing hive-feeding practice. Four-phase stakeholder programme with an H.I.V.E. reflection framework and a documented 'Project Pivots' section.
screen.reason: Clear top-of-field candidate: a failed first campaign of 15 designs followed by a second of 20 that produced one measured binder at ~604 nM is genuine iterative engineering with a quantitative endpoint, backed by an in-house co-purification assay with a proper positive control, 37 registered parts, hardware, software and one of the deepest HP programmes in the batch. Needs a full read to weigh how much of the key affinity measurement was done by Adaptyv rather than the students, and to judge the unfinished RNAi arm.
screen.field_notes: Lambert-GA (Suwanee, Georgia, USA, Conservation village) ran SWARM, attacking honeybee decline on two fronts: de novo minibinders against the Deformed Wing Virus VP3 capsid protein and multiplexed RNAi against three Varroa destructor salivary genes. A first campaign of 15 minibinder designs produced no confirmed binder; a revised binding-site strategy and 20 new designs yielded one confirmed VP3 binder measured at 603.6 nM (95% CI 497.1-733.3) by Adaptyv BLI. In-house evidence is a Ni-NTA co-purification read by anti-His and anti-FLAG dot blots with ImageJ quantification, run against an established anti-GFP nanobody positive control. The RNAi arm reached dsRNA synthesis and assembly of an Sf9 dual-luciferase reporter, but 12 transfection-optimisation conditions failed on cell availability and high background, and the team says so plainly; no silencing was demonstrated. Deliverables include PRINCE (binding-site prioritisation), Vapor-X (low-cost lab drying hardware, iterated for sealing and heating), a seven-part modelling tutorial series, and ~37 new Registry parts. Human practices is very large (22k words, four phases, H.I.V.E. framework) and documents real pivots, including nanobody-to-minibinder. Attributions exist only as a short sponsor list plus a link to the official form; external support includes the Styczynski Lab at Georgia Tech and Adaptyv.

justification.a1: SWARM runs two parallel molecular routes (de novo minibinders against the DWV VP3 P-domain, and six siRNAs against three Varroa salivary-gland genes) plus PRINCE software, hardware and a delivery concept (Description, Minibinder Design, RNAi Experimentation). The scope and the in-house GFP/nanobody pull-down pipeline are well above the typical HS field. It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS anchor because no linked chain of successes exists: the RNAi arm stopped at an uninterpretable reporter, and the in-house VP3 binding result is explicitly called preliminary.
justification.a2: The GFP-nanobody positive control is genuinely well done: three conditions, dot blot plus an independent fluorescence readout, ImageJ quantification, ~76% of GFP-only fluorescence in flowthrough vs ~91% of combined-sample fluorescence in imidazole washes (Minibinder Experimentation, Figs. 5-7). For the actual project claim, the VP3-minibinder co-elution is single-run, the fraction schedule differs from the control, and the Parts page itself states signal before the minibinder-addition point limits interpretation. The only hard affinity number (603.6 nM, 95% CI 497-733 nM) came from Adaptyv's BLI, not the team's bench. The RNAi arm produced no knockdown data: background luminescence swamped the reporter (Results, Figs. 7-9).
justification.a3: The problem framing is quantified and sourced (55.6% US colony loss 2024-25, ~88,000 Georgia colonies lost, resistance and brood limits of existing miticides in Table 1 of Description). The delivery concept is built around formats beekeepers already use, syrup pouch and in-hive feeder, and was shaped by beekeeper input. But no efficacy was demonstrated in bees or in a hive-like setting, and the team says so plainly, so impact remains credible rather than tested.
justification.a4: Design choices are traceable to evidence and advice: antibodies rejected on digestion grounds, nanobodies dropped after Manglik's point about library sizes, minibinders chosen and then hotspot-focused on Adaptyv's advice after a first round of 15 candidates produced no confirmed binding (Description; Minibinder Design). That failed round feeding a redesign is a real DBTL turn. On the RNAi side the iteration is still troubleshooting plus a planned promoter swap (HSV-TK to AC5.1) that has not been tested, and success criteria are not stated in advance.
justification.a5: HP is extensive (22k words) and demonstrably two-way: Lamp and Kadowaki narrowed the target to VP3's exposed P-domain, Manglik redirected the binder class, Cotet and Howe changed the design strategy, Pettis addressed the ecological question of eliminating an obligate invasive parasite, and beekeepers shaped the delivery format. Each is tied to a named decision in the Description. It is a notch below the anchor because the lab execution itself, as opposed to the design choices, is less visibly reshaped by stakeholders.
justification.a6: Students clearly ran the in-house work: miniprep, cell-free expression, Ni-NTA, dot blots, ImageJ, Sf9 culture, transfections. But the decisive binding measurement, the BLI affinity, was done by Adaptyv, candidate screening was external, and the team works with the Styczynski Lab at Georgia Tech. The attributions page is essentially empty, carrying only a link to the official form, so there is no task-level breakdown of who did what, which is the TAS/GreatBay standard.
justification.a7: This is squarely synthetic biology with standard components: codon-optimised VP3 in pET-28a(+) with directional BamHI/HindIII cloning in frame with the N-terminal 6xHis, a FLAG-tagged minibinder in pET-11a via NdeI/BamHI, a four-fragment HiFi reassembly of psiCHECK-2 with an HSV-TK promoter and a synthetic multi-target insert, plus reuse of an existing backbone (BBa_K2141000). 38 parts are registered. Design rationale is strong; the gap to 5 is that few of these constructs are backed by function data.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is clear and the Parts page maps 38 Registry IDs to roles, with honest statements that the AC5.1 reporter is uncharacterised and that the siRNAs remain candidates. Several entries are primers and inserts rather than characterised devices, and the experimental evidence sits on the wiki rather than in the Registry records, which is the p.18 limit. One control plasmid is flagged as having no confirmed Registry ID.
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem, the two routes and the outcome quickly, with a sourced statistics band (DWV in 44+ countries, 75% of crop types, 55.6% US losses) and a six-card map of the project from problem to outreach. The Bentley narrative and the scroll-driven RNAi mechanism explain the biology without jargon. A reader knows within a screen what was attempted and roughly how far it got.
justification.w2: Most claims carry a figure: dot blots with ImageJ integrated-density numbers, fluorescence on a log RFU scale, triplicate wells for the luciferase conditions, fragment concentrations in a table. Crucially the team states its own limits, that a gel does not establish annealing or silencing, that colony growth does not confirm assembly, that no digest or sequencing verified the pooled reporter. That honesty is worth credit under p.20, but it also means replicates, n and error bars are thin and the central VP3 result is unreplicated.
justification.w3: Navigation follows the project structure, each sub-page carries an on-page section list, and overview/design/experimentation are consistently split for both arms. Standard URLs are largely intact. Friction: measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, design and safety-and-security return 404 at their standard addresses while a safety page lives at /safety, so a judge looking for protocols or safety at the expected URL finds nothing.
justification.w4: Design reasoning is reproducible in detail, full codon-optimised sequences, restriction strategy, media and passage conditions for Sf9, reagent kits and catalogue-level references. Failures are recorded rather than hidden, which is exactly what future teams need. But the lab notebook page holds only 141 words, no protocols page resolves, and raw data are not posted, so someone could rebuild the constructs but not repeat the assays step by step.
justification.w5: Referencing is a clear strength: numbered inline citations throughout, DOIs that resolve, per-section reference blocks on the experimentation pages, kit manuals and protocol sources cited for every method, PDB 3G9A credited for the structural analysis, and Addgene #111090 named for the control plasmid. Stakeholder statements are attributed to named individuals with affiliations. Minor gap: a few figures derived from cited structures are not individually re-cited at the caption.

J1.one_line: An ambitious, beautifully documented two-arm project with an exemplary positive control and unusually honest reporting, but the headline binding number came from an external contractor and the team's own function data stops at preliminary.
strengths: The GFP-nanobody positive control is the best piece of bench work on the wiki: three conditions, two orthogonal readouts (dot blot plus fluorescence), ImageJ quantification, and a coherent interpretation (~76% of GFP-only fluorescence in flowthrough vs ~91% of combined-sample fluorescence in imidazole-containing washes).

Unusually honest negative reporting. The team states that colony growth does not confirm assembly, that no diagnostic digest or sequencing was done, that the RNAi gel does not establish annealing or silencing, and that background luminescence made the Sf9 reporter uninterpretable. Under handbook p.20 this honest qualitative reporting counts for more than dressed-up numbers.

Human Practices genuinely drove design: the target narrowed to VP3's exposed P-domain after Lamp and Kadowaki, the binder class switched from nanobodies to minibinders after Manglik, hotspot-focused redesign after Adaptyv, and the ecological question of eliminating Varroa put to an entomologist.

Strong, traceable molecular design: codon optimisation against a published usage table with internal restriction sites screened, in-frame tag placement reasoned explicitly, and a four-fragment HiFi reporter rebuild with the full primer set registered.
Referencing and sourcing are near-exemplary, with resolvable DOIs, per-section reference lists, kit manuals cited for each method, and Addgene/PDB accessions named.
weaknesses: The only quantitative binding measurement (apparent KD 603.6 nM, 95% CI 497.1-733.3 nM) was produced by Adaptyv Bio's BLI screening, not by the students. The in-house pull-down is a single run whose interpretation the team's own Parts page undercuts.

The attributions page contains no content beyond a link to the official form. With an external screening partner, a university host lab and ten sponsors, there is no way to see task-level ownership, which is the standard the handbook's HS case studies set.
The RNAi arm produced no knockdown data at all. Six siRNAs remain candidates; the reporter could not be distinguished from background and the pooled plasmid prep was never sequence-verified.

The VP3 pull-down used a different wash/fraction schedule from the GFP control (an extra imidazole-free wash), so the validated control does not directly validate the experimental run; the team notes this but does not repeat the control under matched conditions.
No replicates, n or error bars for the dot-blot quantification; single integrated-density values are compared across conditions.

Five standard pages return 404 at their expected URLs (measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, design, safety-and-security), with safety relocated to /safety. The notebook page is 141 words, so protocols are not recoverable from the standard pages.
red_flags: Headline binding affinity (604 nM) generated by an external commercial partner (Adaptyv Bio) rather than the team; the wiki does present this transparently, but it lowers aspect 6 rather than counting as the team's own demonstrated function.
Attributions page effectively empty (87 words, just a link to the official form) despite substantial external involvement.
Five standard page slugs 404 (measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, design, safety-and-security); under p.29 content a judge must hunt for cannot be credited.
Key constructs advanced without verification: assembled reporter never gel-checked, digested or sequenced, and four colonies pooled before miniprep.

No integrity concern identified. Citations sampled resolve, figures are not presented as cleaner than the text admits, and modelled/predicted structures are explicitly labelled as not establishing binding. No RCC referral warranted on what I read.

calibrated.changed: none. a6 3.0 rather than 2.5 because the in-house pipeline (cell-free expression, Ni-NTA, dot blots, ImageJ, Sf9 culture) is clearly student-run and the external contributions are named in the text, even though the attributions page is empty; the decisive affinity measurement being contracted out is what keeps it from going higher.

justification.a1: The scope is at the top of the high-school field: a de novo minibinder against DWV VP3 taken from 35 submitted designs to one BLI-confirmed binder at KD 603.6 nM (Model-Design, Table 3), a benchmarking study over 5,721 labelled designs, an open-source site-ranking tool (PRINCE, validated on 93 held-out clusters), a $80 vacuum dryer validated by two outside labs (Hardware), and four models including a six-year colony simulation. Like GreatBay_SZ, it is a chain of increasingly hard steps told as one story. It falls short of a clean 5 only because the second wetlab arm (RNAi) produced no interpretable silencing data and nothing was tested in a bee or a hive.
justification.a2: Measured: BLI binding of l79_s469532_mpnn9 to the VP3 construct across two replicates, 603.6 nM, 95% CI 497.1-733.3 nM (Model-Design Table 3); GFP/anti-GFP nanobody positive control with dot-blot quantification and a fluorescence readout where ~91% of recovered fluorescence shifted into the imidazole washes only with nanobody present (Minibinder Experimentation, Figs 6-7); Vapor-X recoveries at UAB (38/43 compounds within 5%). Not established: the in-house VP3 pull-down is preliminary and the team's own Parts page says signal before the minibinder-addition point limits its interpretation; GFP minibinder candidates did not bind; the Sf9 luciferase work was swamped by background and gave no knockdown data (Results). Neutralisation of DWV, the actual project function, is untested.
justification.a3: The deployment route is concrete and stakeholder-checked: a dsRNA syrup pouch modelled on the registered Norroa format and a dried minibinder packet mixed into sucrose for a standard hive-top feeder, with Professor Bartlett endorsing sucrose delivery and a noted drawback for migratory operations (Implementation). EPA FIFRA/FFDCA registration and honey-residue requirements are named, and dsRNA manufacturing cost is framed honestly as an industry target rather than a price. It is not a 5 because, unlike TAS Taipei's wastewater rig, nothing was tried in a realistic setting: the page states plainly that neither component has been tested in colonies.
justification.a4: The minibinder arm is a complete cycle that changed the design: round 1, 15 candidates, zero binders; the team then benchmarked metrics against 5,721 experimental outcomes, found ipSAE ranking weak within a single target, built PRINCE, moved to the QP/A-ridge epitope and added SolubleMPNN; round 2, 20 candidates, one confirmed binder (Engineering 1.1-1.2; Model-Design). Hardware shows the same discipline with measurements driving each redesign: hot glue leaked, epoxy resin sealed, conical tubes dried only to the 0.1 mL mark, the steel bowl plus thermal putty dried saline completely (Engineering 1.1-4.3). The team also states what it cannot attribute, for example that the round-2 success cannot be assigned to PRINCE alone. The RNAi cycles are closer to troubleshooting (gel resolution, cell recovery) and end without data.
justification.a5: Twenty-eight documented interactions over four phases, each run through a Hear-Inquire-Validate-Evolve record that the team requires to end in a concrete change or a stated reason for none (Integrated Human Practices). Five dated pivots are traced to named people: Manglik moved them off nanobodies, Cotet moved them from the whole P-domain to specific hotspots, Golan to Sf9 cells, Styczynski to a simpler, literature-parameterised PK model, Houck to adding SDG 11. Safety questions were taken to the field too (Pettis on removing an invasive obligate parasite, Bartlett on bee immunity). This is reflective, responsible and responsive in the p.21-23 sense rather than outreach relabelled as HP.
justification.a6: Roles are listed per student on the Team page (wetlab, hardware, modeling, HP leads) and outside help is declared without hedging: Adaptyv ran the BLI screening, GenScript synthesised the constructs, Promega troubleshot the transcription, Nebius gave compute, UAB and Georgia Tech ran the external hardware tests. Against that, the Attributions page on the wiki is a single link to the official form with no who-did-what table, and the headline evidence for aspect 2 (the BLI binding call) was generated by a company rather than the students, who could only reach a preliminary pull-down themselves. Declared outsourcing, so no integrity concern, but it does cap this aspect.
justification.a7: The Parts page registers 38 BBa entries across two collections: the FLAG-tagged VP3 minibinder insert and its pET-11a expression plasmid, the His-tagged VP3 target in pET-28a(+), six siRNA candidates, the HSV-TK and AC5.1 psiCHECK-2 reporters with their primers, three GFP minibinder candidates, and reuse of the existing backbone BBa_K2141000. PRINCE is released as a web app plus CLI with datasets, which counts as software under p.18. It is not a 5: compatibility with RFC10/RFC1000 is never discussed, a large share of the entries are primers or candidates with no characterisation, and the table itself marks the AC5.1 reporter and siRNAs as pending.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is strong enough to rebuild from: codon-optimised sequences with GC content and restriction sites (Minibinder Design Tables 2-4), fraction schedules, reagent volumes, an itemised $80.07 bill of materials, a construction manual and a downloadable CSV of all 35 submitted designs with per-design scores and assay outcomes. The Parts page states for each collection what evidence exists and what does not. I could not open parts.igem.org from this environment (403), so the depth of the Registry records themselves is unverified; the team's own text says several entries have characterisation pending, which is where a8 is likely to sit.
justification.w1: A reader can state the aim after the home page: minibinders against DWV VP3 plus multiplexed RNAi against three Varroa salivary genes, delivered through existing hive feeding. The home page carries the quantitative framing (55.6% US colony losses, 75% of crop types pollinator-dependent) and a six-card project map, and the Description restates target, chassis, parts and the comparison table that justifies minibinders over antibodies and nanobodies. Close to the Lambert/Patras standard; a half point off because the home page headline 'Neutralizing DWV' asserts more than any result supports, even though the inner pages disclaim it.
justification.w2: Most central claims carry data: ImageJ integrated densities for every dot-blot fraction, GFP fluorescence percentages, BLI replicates with a confidence interval, Bradford calibration curves, UAB chromatograms and per-compound recoveries, Renilla and firefly calibration equations. The team labels weak results as weak, including an explicit note that the BSA concentration column is internally inconsistent and unverified. Two things hold it below 4.5: a block of RNAi figures on the Engineering page rendered as 'Figure unavailable' in my read, so those claims could not be checked against an image, and the whole RNAi arm rests on inconclusive luminescence.
justification.w3: Navigation is purposeful: a Judging page that maps medal and special-award criteria to the evidence, per-page section rails, previous/next chaining across the whole wiki, and a home-page map grouping wetlab, drylab, modeling and HP. Interactive elements (epitope map, structure viewer, sortable design table, drying calculator) are used where they help rather than as decoration. The 22,000-word HP page and the spread of wetlab content across overview/design/experimentation sub-pages make some evidence a few clicks deep.
justification.w4: A future team gets the Vapor-X construction manual with a priced parts list, the PRINCE repository with datasets and a reproduction guide, plasmid maps and full codon-optimised sequences, protocol tables with volumes, the raw UAB and Georgia Tech data files, and a seven-part modeling video series. The failures are recorded as carefully as the successes, which is what makes a record useful. The Lab Notebook page is near-empty (about 140 words), so the day-to-day record that would let someone retrace the timeline is missing, and some assets sit on GitLab rather than the wiki.
justification.w5: Referencing is consistent and specific: numbered in-text citations on every page, reference lists split by section on the experimentation pages, and figure-level attribution on the home page including a note that the minibinder image is a predicted pose, not a solved complex. The DWV-B '44+ countries' figure is accompanied by a paragraph explaining exactly how the number was derived from two papers and what it does not mean, which is better practice than most. Spot-checked references (Skubnik 2017 PNAS, MacMillan 2024 mSphere, Cao 2022 Nature, Becchimanzi 2025) match the claims made of them.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineered project: a failed first design campaign turned into a data-driven redesign that produced an externally measured DWV VP3 binder, backed by a cheap, externally validated dryer and unusually honest reporting, with the RNAi half still unfinished.
strengths: Complete, data-driven DBTL on the minibinder: 0/15 binders, then a benchmark over 5,721 experimental designs showing confidence metrics fail within a single target, then a new epitope (QP/A-ridge) and SolubleMPNN, then 1/20 confirmed at KD 603.6 nM with two replicates and a 95% CI (Engineering 1.1-1.2; Model-Design Tables 2-4).

Hardware judged the way hardware should be: Vapor-X iterated against measurements, costed at $80.07 line by line, with external validation at UAB (38/43 compounds recovered within 5% of undried controls) and Georgia Tech (~98% of fresh-control GFP expression from dried plasmid plus lysate), plus a classroom trial and a build manual.

Honest reporting that a judge can rely on: the 29 kPa reading is flagged as below the BME280's 30-110 kPa range and therefore not a validated measurement; the BSA concentration table is marked internally inconsistent; the Parts page states that the in-house pull-down does not establish binding by the registered candidate; all 35 submitted designs, including 18 negatives and 16 unusable assays, are published with scores.

Human practices with traceable consequences: 28 stakeholders in four phases, an explicit rule that a H.I.V.E. record must end in a change or a documented reason for none, and five dated pivots tied to named advisors (nanobodies to minibinders, P-domain to hotspots, model simplification, Sf9 platform, SDG 11).

Reusable output beyond the team's own project: PRINCE released as web app, CLI and datasets with a held-out benchmark (45.8% top-three majority hit vs 23.8% random), 38 Registry entries, a GFP minibinder design offered as a cheap substitute for commercial anti-GFP nanobodies, and the Vapor-X build files.
weaknesses: The RNAi half produced no functional result: RNA synthesis was shown on a gel, the psiCHECK-2 reporter assembly was never verified by digest or sequencing, and the Sf9 transfection optimisation was defeated by background luminescence and cell shortage, so none of the six siRNAs has any knockdown evidence (Results; RNAi Experimentation).

The binding evidence that anchors the project was generated outside the team. The in-house His/FLAG pull-down is qualitative, uses an unmatched fraction schedule relative to its GFP control (an extra imidazole-free wash, noted by the team), and the team itself says signal before the minibinder-addition point limits its interpretation; the quantitative BLI number came from Adaptyv.

Nothing was tested on the actual target system. Binding is to an isolated recombinant VP3 construct, not the assembled virus, and neither component has been given to bees or a colony; the home page's 'Neutralizing DWV' badge outruns that evidence even though inner pages disclaim it.

The wiki Attributions page is a bare link to the official form, with no who-did-what table; roles must be inferred from the Team page. For a project where a vendor, two university labs and a synthesis company each did a load-bearing step, an on-wiki contribution chart of the GreatBay kind is the missing piece.

Registry depth is asserted rather than shown. Many of the 38 entries are primers or candidates the team itself marks as characterisation pending, RFC10/RFC1000 compatibility is never addressed, and a block of RNAi figures on the Engineering page did not render for me ('Figure unavailable'), leaving those claims unverified.
red_flags: Could not open parts.igem.org from this environment (HTTP 403 for BBa_26PZBBQI, BBa_26BKSY8J, BBa_26H9ID1L), so Registry-page depth behind aspects 7 and 8 is unverified by me and should be checked by another panel member.

Several RNAi figures on the Engineering page rendered as 'Figure unavailable. Please try again later.' (Figs RNAi 1A-6D). Likely a loading issue rather than missing content, since the Results page shows the same figures, but the engineering claims resting on them could not be checked against an image.

Home page headline 'Neutralizing DWV' is not supported by any result on the wiki; neutralisation is explicitly disclaimed on Results and Model-Design. Overstatement in the shop window, not fabrication.

Vapor-X ships a published default Wi-Fi password ('vaporx2026') giving anyone in range control of a heater; the team notes this limitation itself, but it is a safety point worth raising in Q&A rather than a handbook safety violation.
No integrity concerns found. Spot-checked citations resolve and say what is claimed; outside contributions (Adaptyv, GenScript, Promega, Nebius, UAB, Georgia Tech) are declared openly.
pages_read: human-practices (overview, H.I.V.E., stakeholder list, project pivots)

calibrated.changed: a8 4.0->3.5: Registry unverified and the team's own Parts page marks several entries pending characterisation with many entries being primers — the identical pattern I scored 3.5 for hk-league, psi-korea and mammothedu. Wiki-side documentation strength alone did not earn others a 4.0.

justification.a1: SWARM carries two molecular arms (de novo VP3 minibinders and multiplexed siRNA against three Varroa salivary genes) plus PRINCE software, the Vapor-X dryer and four models, and the climb from a failed first design round to one confirmed binder is a real escalation (/engineering, /software, /description). It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS top band because only one of the two biology arms produced a positive result, the RNAi screen never got past transfection optimisation (/results), and the headline binding measurement was generated by a commercial service rather than in the team's own hands.
justification.a2: The one solid functional claim is the Adaptyv BLI lead candidate at 603.6 nM across two replicates with a 95% CI of 497.1-733.3 nM (/results, /software), and the team is careful to say this is binding to a VP3 construct, not antiviral protection in bees. Their own pull-down evidence is weak and they say so: Results calls it 'preliminary evidence', while /parts states that signal appearing before the annotated minibinder-addition point means the result 'does not establish binding by the registered candidate'. RNAi is honestly reported as inconclusive (high background luminescence, insufficient Sf9 density, no diagnostic digest or sequencing of the assembled reporter), so the second arm has no function data at all.
justification.a3: The need is confirmed by many named beekeepers and researchers rather than by literature alone, including Claressa Lucas's 'Every colony has them' and Peter Helfrich on treatment timing (/human-practices), and /implementation ties delivery to equipment beekeepers already own: a Norroa-style syrup pouch and a hive-top feeder. The team states plainly that neither component has been tested in honeybee colonies and that EPA registration would be required, which is honest but keeps this below the TAS anchor, where the system was adapted to and tested in something close to the real setting.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Failures drive redesigns throughout: fifteen first-round designs with zero binders led to PRINCE-based hotspot reselection plus SolubleMPNN, producing one binder in round two (/engineering, Iterations 1.1-1.2); premature elution in the positive control led to recalculated imidazole wash buffers (1.3-1.4); invisible RNA bands led to a Promega-advised purification change and a 3% gel (RNAi 1.1-1.2); hardware went jar sealant to epoxy, conical tubes to a steel bowl with thermal putty (3.1-3.3). The team even notes where a change is confounded ('we could not determine which modification contributed most'), and models carry two to three iterations each. The main gap is that several Learn steps end in planned rather than completed verification (the ELISA is still planned).
justification.a5: The H.I.V.E. loop is structured so that each interaction must end in a concrete change or a documented reason none was needed, and the Project Pivots timeline gives five dated changes each tied to a named person: Manglik on library sizes moved them from nanobodies to minibinders, Cotet and Howe moved designs from the whole P-domain to specific hotspots, Golan to Sf9 cells, Styczynski to literature-supported model parameters (/human-practices). They also asked the uncomfortable ecological question, consulting entomologist Jeff Pettis on whether eliminating an invasive obligate parasite is acceptable (/description, /safety). Short of 5 because much of Phase 1 reshaped outreach framing rather than the design, stakeholder 'Validate' blocks are paraphrased rather than attributed quotes, and no consent or ethics oversight is mentioned for the interviews and classroom work.
justification.a6: Attribution is the weakest part of an otherwise careful wiki: /attributions contains only a link to the official form, with no who-did-what chart, no per-experiment names and no figure captions naming the student who ran the work. Outside help is disclosed honestly at the project level (Adaptyv ran the binding screen and helped interpret it, GenScript synthesised the constructs, UAB and Georgia Tech ran the hardware validation, Nebius gave GPU credits, per /team and /engineering), but the single result the project rests on was produced by a vendor, and the wiki does not let a judge see which students did the cloning, purification, dot blots, modelling or code. Per my own rule this stays at 3 until the session clarifies; it is a question, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is built from standard components: 38 Registry IDs on /parts covering six siRNA candidates, a four-fragment HSV-TK psiCHECK-2 reporter and an AC5.1 composite variant, pET-28a(+)/pET-11a expression constructs with His and FLAG tags, and the existing BBa_K2141000 backbone reused. PRINCE and Vapor-X count as standard software and hardware components, and the GFP minibinder is offered as a general-purpose reagent for other teams (/contribution). It is not a 5 because the one new part with demonstrated function was validated externally and the composite reporter is explicitly uncharacterised.
justification.a8: The parts roster is unusually disciplined: every entry states its intended role separately from the evidence collected, AC5.1 entries are labelled 'Experimental characterization pending', and the RNAi characterization paragraph says outright that the six siRNAs remain candidates (/parts). Against that, most registered parts carry negative or inconclusive data, one GFP control plasmid has no confirmed Registry ID, and I could not open parts.igem.org during judging (403), so I could not verify that sequence features, topology and experiments really sit on the Registry rather than only on the wiki, which under the Parts guidance caps this short of 4.
justification.w1: The home page tells the problem, the two mechanisms and the goal through a scrolling narrative with real numbers (55.6% annual US colony loss, 44+ countries with DWV-B) and a six-card map into the project, and /description restates it in a few readable paragraphs with a table of existing Varroa treatments and their limits. A judge knows what SWARM is within a minute. Half a point off only because the animated home page carries some decorative weight before the science starts.
justification.w2: Claims are generally tied to a figure, a table or an integrated-density number: dot blot quantification (8,427 anti-His and 7,501 anti-FLAG in Wash 3), GFP fluorescence distribution (~76% in flowthrough alone, ~91% in low-imidazole washes combined), the UAB recovery workbook recomputed to a 99.29% mean, and the Bradford table flagged as internally inconsistent and 'unverified' (/results, /minibinder-experimentation, /hardware). Modelled and planned outcomes are consistently labelled as such. It is not a 5 because the decisive binding number is a vendor's, several engineering figures did not render for me on /engineering, and n is often unstated.
justification.w3: Navigation is good: a judging page maps criteria to evidence, the side menu follows the project, and nested pages (minibinder-design, rnai-experimentation, model-design) are reachable from the standard pages. Points come off for standard paths that 404 (measurement, safety-and-security, proof-of-concept, protocols, design) with Safety living at /safety instead, for /inclusivity duplicating the Education content, and for the lab notebook existing only as embedded PDFs, all of which make a judge hunt against the p.29 rule.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: reagent and buffer tables for every purification and transfection iteration, a Vapor-X construction guide with priced parts and failed prototypes, open PRINCE code with a reproduction guide, a modelling video series, and two notebook PDFs (/engineering, /hardware, /contribution, /notebook). What is missing for reproducibility is the human record: no attributions detail, no raw-data files for the dot blots or luciferase runs on the wiki, and notebook content locked in PDF embeds.
justification.w5: Citation practice is among the best I have seen from a high school team: numbered references with DOIs on every content page, image and artwork credits on the home page, Addgene plasmid numbers given, and a reference note that explains exactly how the '44+ countries' figure was derived from two papers and which locations were excluded to avoid double counting. The references I spot-checked by title and DOI are real and support the claims made. Half a point off because some stakeholder statements in the H.I.V.E. 'Validate' blocks are paraphrase presented in quotation-like form, so a reader cannot tell what was said verbatim.

J3.one_line: An ambitious, unusually self-critical two-arm bee project whose engineering iteration and stakeholder-driven pivots are finalist-grade, but whose one confirmed result was produced by a commercial vendor and whose wiki says nothing about which student did what.
strengths: Genuine failure-driven DBTL across four workstreams: zero binders in 15 designs led to PRINCE hotspot reselection plus SolubleMPNN and one confirmed binder in 20 (/engineering)
Five dated project pivots each traceable to a named stakeholder, including the nanobody-to-minibinder switch after Dr. Manglik's advice on library sizes (/human-practices Project Pivots)

Exceptional intellectual honesty: the wiki repeatedly states what its own data cannot establish, including that the in-house pull-down does not establish binding by the registered candidate (/parts) and that the Bradford concentration columns are unverified (/hardware)
PRINCE is a real, benchmarked, open-source contribution (45.8% top-three majority-hit on 93 homolog-free clusters vs 23.8% random) that other teams can reuse (/software)
Citation and data-provenance practice is excellent, including a note explaining how the 44+ countries figure was assembled and what it cannot show (/home references)
Vapor-X is cheap ($80.07 components), documented well enough to rebuild, and independently tested at UAB (38/43 compounds within 5%) and Georgia Tech (~98% GFP fluorescence retained)
weaknesses: The Attributions page is a bare link to the official form: no who-did-what chart, no named roles per experiment, no student names in figure captions
The project's headline evidence, the 603.6 nM BLI measurement, was generated by Adaptyv Bio rather than by the students, and construct synthesis went to GenScript

The RNAi arm produced no function data: reporter assembly was never verified by digest or sequencing, and luciferase optimisation failed on background and cell density (/results, /rnai-experimentation)

Results and Parts describe the same pull-down differently ('preliminary evidence of successful VP3-minibinder binding' vs 'these results do not establish binding by the registered candidate'), which a reader has to reconcile themselves
Several standard page paths 404 (measurement, safety-and-security, proof-of-concept, protocols, design) and the lab notebook exists only as embedded PDFs
No mention of consent or ethics oversight for the stakeholder interviews, classroom work or the neurodivergent-student programme
red_flags: Attributions page contains no content beyond a link to the iGEM form, while the project involves vendor-run assays and university-run validation: raise as a session question about who did each step, not as an accusation
parts.igem.org returned 403 during judging, so I could not confirm that the 38 claimed Registry entries carry sequence features and experimental data; wiki-only part documentation would cap a8 at 3

Some passages read as reviewer-style annotations inserted into the team's own prose (for example 'The synthesized target fragment was the fourth assembly component; its concentration is not reported here'), a voice question worth asking in session rather than penalising
Multiple figures on /engineering rendered as 'Figure unavailable' in the crawl, so parts of the RNAi engineering evidence could not be inspected

calibrated.changed: none. a2 of 3.5 is consistent with the bar I used elsewhere: one confirmed functional result, produced by a vendor, with the team's own pull-down explicitly not establishing binding and the second arm carrying no function data at all.

one_line.en: An ambitious two-arm project with an exemplary positive control, honest negative reporting and a cheap externally validated dryer, where the one confirmed binding number came from a commercial vendor.
one_line.zh: 企圖心強的雙線專案，陽性對照堪稱典範、陰性結果誠實呈報、乾燥器低成本且經外部驗證，但唯一確認的結合數據來自商業廠商。

strengths: The positive control is the best bench work on the wiki: three conditions, two orthogonal readouts, quantification and a coherent interpretation
Unusually honest negative reporting, including that colony growth does not confirm assembly and that a reporter was uninterpretable
Human Practices genuinely drove design across five dated pivots traceable to named advisors
Hardware costed line by line, externally validated at two universities, with a build manual and a classroom trial
weaknesses: The only quantitative binding measurement was produced by a commercial screening partner, not the students
The RNA-interference arm produced no knockdown data at all, and the reporter was never sequence-verified
The attributions page is a bare link to the official form despite a vendor, two university labs and ten sponsors
No replicates or error bars for the quantified dot blot, and the experimental pull-down used a different schedule from its validated control
red_flags: Headline affinity generated by an external commercial partner rather than the team
Five standard page slugs return 404 and the notebook page is very short
Home page headline claims neutralisation, which inner pages explicitly disclaim
Shipped hardware carries a published default wireless password giving anyone in range control of a heater

screen.project_title: Oat Shield: biodegradable oat-husk cellulose wound dressing carrying the antimicrobial peptide subtilin
screen.what_they_built: Cellulose extracted from Alberta oat-husk waste and formed into bandage material over three prototype iterations (organosolv and a modified Tencel/NMMO route), plus His-tagged SpaS (subtilin) and GFP-SpaS fusion expressed in E. coli for purification and loading into the dressing.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with IDT-supplied pET plasmids (B. subtilis ATCC 6633 and a pHT01/Pgrac design were planned but not executed); parts BBa_265NN80I (SpaS) and BBa_26Y339S2 (GFP-SpaS with internal TEV site), referencing BBa_B0030 and the 2014 LMU-Munich BBa_K1351012. No Parts page.
screen.best_evidence: /results disk-diffusion assay: purified SpaS and SpaS-GFP produced concentration-dependent zones of clearance against Gram-positive M. luteus, with water and storage buffer giving none and ampicillin and subtilin-producing B. subtilis giving the expected inhibition. But the supporting figures are unfinished placeholders - "Figure 5 Upload the annotated purification gel" and "Figure 6 Upload the final plate and label each disk" - and no zone diameters are reported. The same page records that SDS-PAGE "did not support a sufficiently certain conclusion" and the anti-His Western detected nothing.
screen.hp_integration: Modestly: MindFuel Tech Futures Challenge judging selected Oat Shield over two rival pitches and flagged that the plan leaned too hard on the genetic circuit; Genome Alberta's Julie Greer recommended organosolv and preserving long cellulose fibres, which ended the blender-based extraction; a BioTreks review and a nurse interview refined protocols and wound-care framing. Biosafety concerns about live bacteria in a dressing drove the pivot to purified peptide.
screen.reason: The central claims are not evidenced: protein could not be detected by gel or Western, the one positive assay is reported without numbers and its figures are literally unuploaded placeholders, and the model is purely theoretical with parameters not measured. The wiki is unfinished down to the page title ("TeamName") and has no Parts, Attributions, Safety or Education pages. Nowhere near top-2.
screen.field_notes: Alberta high-school team (Therapeutics) turning oat-husk agricultural waste into a biodegradable antimicrobial wound dressing carrying subtilin, a lantibiotic active against Gram-positive wound pathogens. Three bandage prototype iterations - hydrogen peroxide/NaOH treatment, then longer lignin degradation with carrageenan as gellant, then abandoning the blender to preserve long fibres, moving to organosolv and a modified Tencel/NMMO route. The genetic arm pivoted from live engineered B. subtilis with a CtsR heat-inducible circuit to simply expressing and purifying the peptide, on biosafety grounds; an IDT pET plasmid was ordered rather than built, and in E. coli neither SDS-PAGE nor anti-His Western detected SpaS, though the SpaS-GFP cells looked visibly green. A disk-diffusion assay on M. luteus showed concentration-dependent clearance for both purified proteins, but no diameters are given and the plate and gel figures are unuploaded placeholders. The model is a one-dimensional Fick's law diffusion calculation in R compared against MIC, with the diffusion coefficient assumed, not measured. Two Registry parts submitted; no Parts, Attributions, Safety or Education pages, and the wiki still carries the template title "TeamName".

screen.project_title: HiSSC — high-throughput barcoded screening of combinatorial siRNA cocktails for hyperlipidemia
screen.what_they_built: A pooled single-cell screening platform: 40 siRNA duplexes against 10 lipid-metabolism genes loaded onto fluorescently barcoded photoporation beads, delivered to HepG2 cells, with an imaging pipeline that segments cells, decodes 6-bit barcodes and links siRNA identity to per-cell lipid dye intensity.
screen.chassis_and_parts: HepG2 human hepatoma cells; Dynabeads M-270 Amine with gold nanorods and PDDA coating, 980 nm photoporation. No BioBrick or Registry parts of any kind, and no parts page.
screen.best_evidence: /results: 602 fields, 138,410 of 152,755 beads decoded (90.6%), 93,900 bead-bearing cells, 87,277 transfected cells and 7,196 unique combinations; split-half reproducibility of the 40 effect sizes r = 0.95 (P<0.001), single-agent effect vs dose-amplification r = 0.69, within-pathway pairs beating cross-pathway pairs (Mann-Whitney P = 0.021), and 84 of the reliable top 100 combinations being two-siRNA pairs built on MLXIPL and DGAT2.
screen.hp_integration: Barely — one expert (Dr Clay Semenkovich) warned that cultured hepatocytes adapt to media and are a poor proxy for whole-body physiology, which the team says reframed the screen as candidate prioritisation rather than proof; no stakeholder input visibly changed the design itself.
screen.reason: The dataset is genuinely large and internally reproducible, but the readout is a lipid membrane dye only — no mRNA or protein knockdown was measured, so "silencing" is inferred from a proxy. There is no synthetic biology in the standard-parts sense: zero Registry parts, no constructs, nothing other teams can reuse except code. Attributions record one week of wet lab against eleven weeks of dry lab on a platform adapted from a published Nature Communications method, leaving it unclear who operated the photoporation and imaging, and Human Practices is one page of 616 words. Against the Project aspects as a whole this does not read as top-2.
screen.field_notes: US high school team (Ladue Horton Watkins, Missouri, Therapeutics village) screening combinatorial siRNA cocktails for hyperlipidemia. The library is 40 duplexes, four per gene across MLXIPL, SREBF2, ACACA, FASN, SCD, DGAT2, PNPLA3, HMGCR, LDLR and SOAT2, designed from NCBI transcripts, filtered in-house and cross-checked with siDirect2 and BLASTn-short. Delivery is gold-nanorod photoporation from barcoded Dynabeads, the method adapted from Guo et al. 2024. The imaging pipeline went through three documented iterations — dual-channel segmentation, per-channel 95th-percentile background thresholds for barcode bits, and bead-to-cell assignment with cell-level aggregation — which is the clearest engineering content on the wiki. Headline findings: MLXIPL, DGAT2 and ACACA emerge as hubs, top pairs beat the best single siRNA, and the hits map onto the GLP-1 downstream axis. Important caveats a full read would need to resolve: the only phenotype is BODIPY/membrane lipid dye intensity (no qPCR or protein), gene comparisons are only valid within a dye class because more Qdots read brighter, there are no Registry parts, and the attributions page shows one week of bench work with no named external lab despite the specialised instrumentation.

screen.project_title: SHIELD — acid-responsive antimicrobial peptide hydrogel coating for orthodontic appliances
screen.what_they_built: A calcium-alginate hydrogel coating for braces combining three modules: alkaline phosphatase (PhoK, CBM106-anchored) that mineralises calcium glycerophosphate into nano-hydroxyapatite, an LL-37 antimicrobial peptide released by an MtuI intein that self-cleaves below pH 6.5, and a dual mineral/hydrogel barrier for sustained release.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3)/DH5alpha, pET28a and pET30a; 21 BBa 2026 part IDs. Fusion architecture L6KD-PT-PEP-MtuI-(AMP or HiBiT), CBM106-linker-ALP fusions, Golden Gate assembly.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering: pNPP alkaline-phosphatase assay against a standard curve (y=2.5980x-0.01995, R2=0.9992, n=3) gives PhoK 21.785 U/mL versus G15-21 8.765, PhoA 6.69 and near-zero for Bs-PhoA and R-PhoD; pH 5.5-8.0 mineralisation series shows PhoK precipitating nHA within ~12 h versus 36 h for others and retaining activity at pH 6.0-7.0. AMP screen gives measured inhibition-zone diameters (KSL-W ~10 mm, 8DSS ~9 mm, LL-37 ~8 mm), blood-agar hemolysis eliminating KSL-W, OD600 growth curves, and an LL-37 MIC bounded only as >13.7 ug/mL. HiBiT/LgBiT luminescence demonstrates acid-triggered release from the hydrogel at pH 6.5 versus 8.0.
screen.hp_integration: Yes and traceably — Dr Chen and Dr Li's point that the oral cavity is not neutral forced the mineralisation assays to be rerun across pH 5.5-8.0 rather than only pH 8.0, and Dr Zhang's insistence that safety precedes efficacy added the hemolysis screen, which eliminated the best-killing peptide (KSL-W) in favour of LL-37.
screen.reason: Borderline but worth a full read. Three complete DBTL cycles each closed by real measurements, two genuine screens (5 ALPs, 6 AMPs) with numbers, and a clever HiBiT surrogate reporter that actually demonstrates the acid-triggered release the product depends on. Against it: there is no results page, no model page and no education page, the wiki hides all data inside a 7k-word engineering page, the MIC was never pinned down, plasmids were synthesised by a commercial vendor, and nothing has been tested on a real appliance or an oral biofilm.
screen.field_notes: LINKS-Union (Therapeutics, CHN) built SHIELD, an acid-responsive antimicrobial-peptide hydrogel coating for orthodontic braces, motivated by white-spot lesions and gingivitis in orthodontic patients. Three modules: mineralisation (alkaline phosphatase hydrolyses calcium glycerophosphate to deposit nano-hydroxyapatite in situ), antibacterial (LL-37 liberated when the MtuI intein self-cleaves below pH 6.5), and sustained release (dual barrier of mineral layer plus 3% sodium alginate). Five candidate ALPs fused to a CBM106 alginate-binding/solubility module were screened by pNPP assay: PhoK won at 21.785 U/mL, 2.5x the runner-up, and mineralised fastest across pH 6.0-8.0. Six AMPs were screened by inhibition zone, LGG probiotic sparing, blood-agar hemolysis and OD600 growth curves; KSL-W was dropped for beta-hemolysis despite the largest zone and LL-37 selected, with MIC only bounded at >13.7 ug/mL. Release kinetics were measured by swapping the AMP for an 11-aa HiBiT tag in the same L6KD-PT-PEP-MtuI scaffold and reading NanoLuc luminescence from hydrogel supernatant at pH 6.5 versus 8.0. 21 parts registered. Structural weakness: results.txt is empty and there is no model, education or software page; everything lives in engineering (7.1k words) and entrepreneurship (9.3k words). Plasmid synthesis was outsourced to Guangzhou Ruibo. Figures are hand-drawn with AI polish, declared on the page.

screen.project_title: BioCall: yeast-produced semiochemicals to recruit ladybirds to urban trees
screen.what_they_built: Engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae modules to make the aphid-predator volatiles methyl salicylate, beta-caryophyllene and (E)-beta-farnesene (plus limonene and linalool candidates), with a nine-promoter panel to tune EbF output, aimed at reducing aphid honeydew on Shanghai street trees.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. cerevisiae BY4741 with YeastFab HCKan/POT Golden Gate assembly; very large parts library (35+ new BBa IDs) of enzyme CDSs, nine promoters and terminators, plus reused BBa_K3993005, BBa_K4161502.
screen.best_evidence: /results: UPLC-MS/MS with external standard calibration identified MeSA at 2.79 min in engineered broth and absent in negative control, CsSAMT1 > AtSAMT1 consistent with docking (-6.4 vs -5.9 kcal/mol); GC-MS SIM quantified EbF across a nine-promoter panel; SDS-PAGE bands at 43.4/41.0 kDa. Multi-module assembly could not be confidently verified.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — 10k-word IHP with SWOT and stakeholder mapping, Century Park pest managers, street cleaners and farm visits; containment and the indoor-production framing came out of those conversations.
screen.reason: Three volatiles made and quantified by UPLC-MS/MS and GC-MS, a genuine nine-promoter characterization panel, a big documented parts library and strong IHP. Held back because the central biological claim — that the blend actually recruits ladybirds — was never tested, and the multi-module strain failed. Borderline but worth a full read for the measurement and parts work.
screen.field_notes: MammothEdu-East (Agriculture, CHN) traced sticky honeydew on Shanghai streets to aphids and proposed BioCall, a yeast platform producing semiochemicals that recruit ladybirds. In S. cerevisiae BY4741 they built YeastFab Golden Gate modules for methyl salicylate (AtSAMT1 vs CsSAMT1), beta-caryophyllene (OjTPS1 vs NtTPS7) and (E)-beta-farnesene (MpEbFS), choosing candidates by AlphaFold plus AutoDock Vina docking and then testing them: UPLC-MS/MS in MRM mode with external standard calibration confirmed MeSA at 2.79 min with CsSAMT1 outproducing AtSAMT1, matching the docking ranking, and GC-MS SIM quantified EbF across a nine-promoter panel (CCW12, CDS1, GAL1, GAL7, HHF1, PGK1, TDH2, TEF1, TEF2). Salicylic acid supplementation up to 1 mM did not inhibit growth, fixing 0.5 mM for production. Attempts to combine two or three transcription units into one strain could not be verified, and no ladybird behavioural assay was done, which the team states plainly on its own game page. Strengths are a 35-part library, a measurement page describing the analytical methods, a 10k-word IHP with SWOT and stakeholder analysis, an explicit AI-use disclosure and detailed wiki credits.

screen.project_title: BioSonde: PET-derived PHA foam housing for radiosondes
screen.what_they_built: A two-part biological route in salt-tolerant Halomonas sp. LA5 - engineered PETase variants to hydrolyse PET/BHET, and an RBS-optimised phaCAB pathway to make PHB - aimed at replacing the expanded polystyrene shell of weather-balloon radiosondes, which are released ~600,000-950,000 times a year and almost never recovered.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Halomonas sp. LA5 (production), E. coli S17-1 (conjugative donor), BL21 and TOP10; pSEVA321 and p321-ds05 backbones. Six PETase designs across dsPETase05 and IsPETase families, a nine-member RBS reporter library, and RBS7 (BBa_K2800034, 20 nt GAGCGAGAAGGAGGTAAAGT) carried into R7-phaCAB. Around 50 new BBa parts registered plus reuse of BBa_K2800031-34, B0030, B0034.
screen.best_evidence: /results: OD600-normalised GFP across eight RBS variants in LA5 on a BMG Omega reader - RBS7 at 50,077 RFU/OD600 (484x wild type) versus RBS3 at 16,559 (160x) and RBS8 at 1,839 (17.8x), with a full table. LC-MS screening of three PETase constructs in two hosts, three feeds and two timepoints (216 responses, mean +/- SD, n = 2) with Level 1b annotation of the TPA feature at m/z 167.0344. Six-flask 72 h LA5-phaCAB fermentation gave net recovered masses of 0.02-0.08 g, largest under BHET + TPA.
screen.hp_integration: Yes and unusually well written: the project moved from a plastic bottle to 'designed-to-be-lost' products after reporting on balloon debris washing up in Victoria and a Chinese Academy of Sciences report on radiosonde recovery, and the six human-practices chapters track how the application, the product form and the environmental claim each changed.
screen.reason: Impressive scope, honest reporting and the best measurement discipline in the batch after HongKong-JSS, with a genuinely useful quantitative RBS characterisation. But the project's own claim is not demonstrated: PETase activity rests on tentative relative LC-MS peak areas with n = 2 and a Level 3 annotation for the key BHET-derived feature, the phaCAB construct was built but never functionally compared, and the 0.02-0.08 g of recovered flask material was never chemically confirmed as PHB - the team say so themselves. Strong medal and special-prize profile rather than a top-2 finalist; read fully only if panel capacity allows.
