screen.field_notes: MammothEdu-United (Biomanufacturing, China) built BioSonde, a route from waste PET to PHA foam for radiosonde housings, framed around 'designed-to-be-lost' products that are released ~600,000-950,000 times a year and rarely recovered. The chassis is salt-tolerant Halomonas sp. LA5 with E. coli S17-1 conjugative delivery; six PETase designs (dsPETase05 and IsPETase families) were PCR-screened and three carried into a focused culture comparison, and a nine-variant RBS GFP library was screened in LA5 on a plate reader, where RBS7 gave 50,077 RFU/OD600, 484x wild type, and was taken into an R7-phaCAB pSEVA321 construct. LC-MS with SVR-corrected relative peak areas tracked a tentative BHET feature (Level 3), an annotated TPA feature at m/z 167.0344 and a 3-hydroxybutyrate feature across seven feed conditions and two hosts; a six-flask 72 h LA5-phaCAB fermentation in high-salt M9 recovered 0.02-0.08 g of endpoint material, largest under BHET + TPA, but the material was not chemically characterised and no PHB was confirmed. The team state plainly that absolute substrate conversion and polymer production require separate calibrated assays and that the integrated route is the next step. Human practices (21k words, six chapters), education (13k), attributions (6.7k), measurement, proof-of-concept, hardware and model pages are all substantial, and roughly fifty new Registry parts are listed.

justification.a1: The scope is wide for a high school team: a PETase variant panel on two scaffolds, a conjugative delivery pipeline into Halomonas sp. LA5, an eleven-member RBS library, a 48-run MD study, an LCA workbook and a 3D shell model (Description sections 6-8; Engineering cycles 1-8). But the results do not yet build on each other in increasing difficulty the way GreatBay's silk work did: only the RBS-GFP screen produced a measured functional outcome, and the headline PET-to-PHA conversion is not yet demonstrated (Results section 5; Proof of Concept section 8). Impressive framing and breadth, moderate completed achievement.
justification.a2: One module is shown to work with a control: the RBS-GFP panel in LA5 gave RBS7 at 50,077 RFU/OD600 against wild-type LA5 at 103.36, with medium blanks subtracted and OD600 normalisation (Results Table 2, Figure 11). Everything downstream of that is unproven: the PETase comparison rests on relative LC-MS peak areas with n = 2 A/B samples, no abiotic control, no enzyme-input normalisation and a Level 3 annotation for the BHET feature (Results section 2); the six-flask phaCAB run reports 0.02-0.08 g of recovered material weighed to 0.01 g precision with no polymer identification (Results Table 3). The team states all of this plainly rather than claiming success, which I credit under p.20, but the central claim is not yet supported by data.
justification.a3: The problem is unusually well bounded: roughly 700,000-950,000 releases a year, 131 Chinese stations, GB/T 44451-2024 mass and envelope limits, and priced quotes of about 5,000 yuan for the imported biodegradable Vaisala unit against 2,000 yuan for the domestic instrument (Description sections 1 and 9). The adoption route names the real customer (licensed instrument manufacturers), four gates to 2030 and a draft technical specification for degradable covers. What is missing is the team's own measured evidence linking material to use: no shell was moulded, and the carbon and cost figures are model outputs, as they label them.
justification.a4: Eight DBTL cycles are documented with design questions, builds, measured tests and decisions (Engineering page). The strongest is genuine: the measured RBS panel changed the next build, carrying the 20 nt RBS7 element onto phaCAB in pSEVA321 (Cycle 6 into Cycle 7), and the MD factorial screen selected V3 before functional testing against a stated two-SD criterion. Other cycles are closer to troubleshooting (the 13 July transformation failure fixed by SOC recovery on 16 July) or produced a measurement-plan change rather than a redesign (the plastic-contact weighing anomaly, where the LB control lost more mass than any culture).
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the project and is at grand-prize level for a high school team. Thirty-one engagements are documented through a consistent Set-Sound-Shift-Steer structure, each with a traceable change: SUSTech-BIO 2025 produced the M1/M2/M3 module architecture, Junbin Li and Lehan Li set the rules for the enzyme panel (each variant against its own parent, library kept to two digits), Zhou Weili's ethics review drove the three-barrier containment design, and BUCT introduced the LCA. The team also audited its own survey, noting that its introduction told respondents the shell 'degrades completely in seawater in 6-12 months', which conflicts with the published rates they later used. That is reflective, responsive practice, not outreach.
justification.a6: Attribution is task-level for every student and instructor, in the style the handbook praises in TAS Taipei: named owners for PETase experiments, fermentation, LC-MS data curation, modelling and notebook keeping. Outside contributions are declared rather than hidden: instructor Xiaojuan Wang supplied the S17-1 donor, the LA5 strain and plasmid vectors and ran the training; a two-month placement at a BGI base hosted much of the bench work; the LC-MS was run by an external provider whose method the team then critiques; the wiki itself was built by advisor Weisi Wang with Codex assistance, with an AI-assisted visual register published. Students evidently did the hands-on work, but the host lab and advisor support are substantial enough to keep this short of 5.
justification.a7: The design is squarely synthetic biology on standard components: a pSEVA321 backbone, conjugative delivery through S17-1, an RBS library screened with a GFP reporter, and the phaCAB operon, with reuse of existing Registry parts (BBa_K089001, BBa_K089003, BBa_K2800031-34) alongside new PETase CDS designs (Parts page; Design page). The module architecture is explicitly modular, with the reserved glcDEFG assimilation cluster held as a separate option. This is a genuine engineered genetic device built from registry-compatible parts.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is excellent and the Parts page lists 53 entries by class, Registry ID, new/existing status and function, with the Contribution page honestly recording that two cassette designs contain an internal stop codon and that the V3 plasmid design carries TGA at insert codon 19. I could not open parts.igem.org during judging (403 from the CDN), so I cannot verify the depth of the Registry entries themselves, and p.18 says parts are judged there; given how little functional data exists, I expect sequences and rationale rather than characterisation with controls. The count is also inflated by primer and plasmid-record entries.
justification.w1: The homepage carries the problem clearly within one screen: what a radiosonde is, that almost none come back, and that the shell is the component to replace. The 'designed to be lost' framing is a genuinely good piece of science communication. What is harder to find on first arrival is what the team actually achieved at the bench this season, which sits several pages in.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently tied to figures with legends that state n, units, dilution corrections and blank subtraction, and the Measurement page is unusually rigorous for a high school team: it separates dilution correction from calibration, flags a conflicting 11 August notebook multiplier, and states that peak areas are not concentrations without compound-specific calibration. The gap is that controls exist for growth (empty vector, wild type, medium blanks) but not for the central hydrolysis and polymer claims, and the GFP panel has technical wells only, no biological repeats. The team says so itself, which keeps this at 4 rather than dropping it.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly into Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Engagement and Team, with an on-page contents list for every long page and a working image viewer. Friction comes from relocated standard pages: /protocols, /implementation, /software and /inclusivity return 404, with the protocols content living at /protocol and the implementation content folded into Description section 9. The longest pages (Human Practices at about 21,000 words) test the 'complete but not sprawling' standard.
justification.w4: A later team could pick this up. Both lab notebooks are posted (Beijing electronic, Shenzhen scanned plus digitised), the protocol page numbers procedures P01-P20 and maps them to experiments, and the Contribution page publishes a failure log classified as resolved, partly resolved or open, including the unresolved case of colonies that grew on chloramphenicol plates but stayed clear in chloramphenicol liquid. The LCA workbook, the foam mass-and-lifetime calculation and the media salt table are all reusable. Notebooks as PDFs are slightly less navigable than on-page entries.
justification.w5: Referencing is the best I have seen on this ballot. Pages carry APA reference lists with DOIs, interviews are cited as dated personal communications with consent recorded, map data and fonts carry their licences, prior iGEM teams (HZAU-China, MammothEdu-South and -East) are credited for specific advice, and there is a published register of AI-assisted visuals naming tools per image. I have not resolved every citation individually, which is the only reason this is not a 5.

J1.one_line: An exceptionally well-framed and honestly documented project whose human practices and record-keeping are grand-prize calibre, but whose central PET-to-PHA claim rests on screening data without controls, sequence confirmation or polymer identification.
strengths: Human practices is genuinely integrated: 31 engagements in a consistent Set-Sound-Shift-Steer format, each with a traceable change to the design (module architecture, enzyme-panel rules, containment design, LCA), plus a self-audit of the team's own leading survey wording.

The problem is bounded and quantified rather than a 'save the world' pitch: GB/T 44451-2024 mass and envelope limits, 131 Chinese stations, and priced quotes from two named meteorologists for the imported and domestic instruments.

One real measured functional result with a control: the RBS-GFP panel in LA5, with wild-type reference, medium blanks and OD600 normalisation, which then changed the next build by carrying RBS7 onto phaCAB.

Unusual metrological honesty for a high school team. The Measurement page separates correction from calibration, flags a conflicting notebook dilution factor, and refuses to call relative peak areas concentrations.
A reusable record: two notebooks, numbered protocols P01-P20, an LCA workbook, and a published failure log marking which problems were resolved, partly resolved or still open.
Referencing and provenance, including dated personal communications, licences for map and font data, credit to specific prior iGEM teams, and a register of AI-assisted visuals.
weaknesses: The PETase branch has no activity assay. Ranking rests on n = 2 relative LC-MS peak areas with no abiotic control and no normalisation to enzyme input, and the key BHET feature carries only a Level 3 annotation.

No clone used in a functional assay has been sequence-confirmed, and the team records that the V3 plasmid design carries a TGA at insert codon 19 and that two cassette designs contain internal stop codons. That undercuts the gold-medal part claim.

No PHA was identified. The six-flask run reports 0.02-0.08 g of recovered material weighed at 0.01 g precision, with no polymer identity, no drying or purification procedure and no biomass normalisation.
The GFP panel used three technical wells, not independent cultures, so biological variability is uncharacterised; the fluorescence and OD600 runs were separate and paired afterwards.
No shell was built. Mass, foaming behaviour and marine lifetime are estimates from a 3D model and published rates, and the foaming literature is for a copolymer the current pathway does not make.
Four standard page URLs (protocols, implementation, software, inclusivity) are 404 while the content sits elsewhere, and the longest pages strain the 'complete but not sprawling' test.
red_flags: I could not reach parts.igem.org during judging (403 from the CDN), so the 53 claimed Registry entries could not be verified. Under p.18 parts are judged on the Registry alone, so a8 reflects what the wiki documents, with that caveat.

AI-assisted illustrations are used (education comic, team flag) and are declared with tools named on the credits page. They are decorative, not evidentiary, and I treat the disclosure as good practice, not an integrity concern. No figure on the project pages is presented as AI-cleaned or AI-made data.

Modelled results are present in quantity (MD, LCA, cost, shell mass and lifetime) but each is labelled as modelled by the team, including the explicit note that LCA panels are 'model results, not measurements from a plant'. I scored only the measured evidence.
Organisms used (E. coli TOP10, BL21, S17-1; Halomonas sp. LA5) are whitelist-compatible. No safety referral needed.
pages_read: attempted Registry pages BBa_26HJP00J, BBa_26AXZRCI, BBa_266GW6XH, BBa_262M5JXC (403, not readable)

calibrated.changed: none. a2 3.0 is the right place for a project whose only controlled functional result is an RBS-GFP screen, with the central PET-to-PHA claim resting on n=2 relative peak areas with no abiotic control and 0.02-0.08 g of unidentified recovered material; the team says so itself, which is why this is 3.0 rather than lower under p.20. a5 5.0 is secure - 31 engagements with traceable design consequences and a self-audit of their own survey wording.

justification.a1: The scope is large and unusually coherent for a high school team: a six-member structure-guided PETase panel, an eleven-member RBS library screened by GFP in the chassis itself, a conjugation pipeline into a non-model halophile, an LCA workbook, a cost model, a CAD shell inside a national standard envelope, 31 HP engagements and nine teaching kits, all pointed at one well-defined object (Description, Engineering, Model, Hardware). What stops it short of GreatBay level is that the chain delivers selections and models rather than a finished working thing: no PET was degraded, no polymer was identified, no shell was moulded. The team says all of this itself in Description section 11 (Limitations), which I credit, but a1 rewards what was achieved, and the achievement is a platform in progress.
justification.a2: The main function is not demonstrated. Measured and real: LA5 growth curves (Results Fig 1-2), PCR screens (Fig 4, 9), and a quantitative GFP screen where RBS7 gives 50,077 RFU/OD600 against wild-type 103 (Results Table 2) - a genuine 484-fold result, but from three technical wells in one run, with fluorescence and OD600 acquired separately and no matched non-fluorescent control. Everything downstream is tentative: the LC-MS signals are relative peak areas with ME0143144 only a Level 3 'tentative BHET-derived or MHET candidate' (Results, section on candidate profiles), the six-flask recovered masses of 0.02-0.08 g are unidentified material (Table 3), and Proof of Concept admits the lead V3 plasmid design 'carries TGA at insert codon 19' and that assayed clones are not sequence-confirmed. Scored on evidence, not candour: one quantitative screening result, no proof the route works.
justification.a3: This is the strongest argued impact case I have read from a high school team that has not yet built the product. The target is bounded and numerically defined by GB/T 44451-2024 (120 g instrument, 90x65x280 mm), the prices come from two named operators (¥5,000 for the Vaisala RS41 E-model from Q. Wang, ¥2,000 for the domestic instrument from W. Du), and the adoption path is a four-gate route ending in a licence and a year of parallel observation (Description Fig 9; Entrepreneurship). The acceptance test was defined by the user, not the team - paired same-balloon flights with the profiles differenced. It is not a 5 because nothing has been tested in a realistic setting: TAS Taipei actually ran its wastewater rig and found it insufficient, whereas here the MVP shell from purchased PHA is still future work.
justification.a4: Eight cycles are documented with a real Learn step, and at least two changed the next build: the 48-run temperature/salt MD factorial with two seeds and a stated two-SD screen prioritised dsPETase05 V3 (dd = -0.367 ± 0.145 Å, Model 1 section 5), and the GFP panel moved RBS7 into the phaCAB construct (Engineering cycles 6-7). The transformation and PCR iterations of cycle 3 and the failure log on the Contribution page, which marks each failure resolved, partly resolved or open, are the kind of engineering honesty I look for. It falls short of 4 because no cycle closes: the MD prediction was never tested against enzyme activity, and the team states that RBS7 'has not yet been compared with the baseline phaCAB in the same flask experiment' (Description, Limitations), so the central design decision is still unvalidated and several cycles are workflow troubleshooting rather than redesign driven by functional data.
justification.a5: HP is this project's best aspect and meets the p.21-23 criteria properly. Thirty-one engagements are scored by the team against five published criteria, and the 4S cycle forces a 'Shift' step in which they do their own work in response. Concrete design changes are traceable: expert concerns produced the M1/M2/M3 module architecture, Lehan Li's advice set the mutation strategy (stable scaffold first, surface charge last) and capped the library at two digits, which is exactly the six-design panel that was built, and the questionnaire self-audit led them to withdraw their own '6-12 months in seawater' claim as inconsistent with Dilkes-Hoffman et al. (2019). The whole project frame, 'designed to be lost', came out of these conversations. I withhold the last half point because the engagement set leans heavily on academics and other iGEM teams, and the station operators who would actually handle the shell are represented by two interviews.
justification.a6: Attribution is detailed and candid. Students are credited with the fermentations, PCR, conjugation, plating and notebook keeping in per-person CRediT-style entries, and the instructor and advisor entries are specific rather than decorative. Two declared dependencies pull this down from 4: instructor Yueqi Zeng 'independently conducted part of the experimental work after students returned to school', and the entire wiki was built by advisor Weisi Wang with OpenAI Codex, with a 16-entry AI-assisted visual register listing the comic and flag artwork. Nothing here is concealed - the Wiki Credits page is more forthcoming than most - but core execution partly sits with adults and the site itself is an advisor's build, which is what a6 asks about.
justification.a7: The project sits on standard components and adds to them: existing phaC/phaA (BBa_K089003, BBa_K089001), B0034, the K2800031-34 RBS series and K3137001 are reused, and the RBS collection with its defining primers is designed for another team to rebuild (Contribution, Parts). RBS7 (BBa_K2800034) is genuinely characterised in LA5 and carried into a composite, which is real modular work. Two things hold it at 3.5. The 53-entry collection is padded with primers and one-off plasmid-construct records, which is inventory rather than modularity. And I could not open any Registry page to check compatibility or depth - parts.igem.org served a CAPTCHA, which I will not work around - so the Registry side of this aspect is unverified rather than credited.
justification.a8: On-wiki documentation is excellent and would let another team rebuild the work: the Measurement page states the unit and the limit of every readout and refuses to over-claim (no OD600-to-cell calibration, a transcription error retained and flagged, a conflicting dilution record left unresolved), Experiments maps modules to protocols P01-P20, the Parts table gives each entry's function and flags the two cassettes carrying an internal stop codon, and the notebooks are on-wiki PDFs. The handbook makes me judge parts on the Registry itself, which I could not reach (CAPTCHA), so I cannot confirm that the 38 new entries carry annotation, host, rationale and characterisation. On wiki evidence this would be a 4.5; with the Registry unverified I hold it at 3.5.
justification.w1: The home page states the project in one line - a Halomonas-based PHA platform for radiosonde shells from waste PET - and then walks the reader through what a radiosonde is, why its shell is abandoned by design, and why PHA rather than PLA. After the home and Description pages I could state the aim, the chassis, the three modules and the success criterion without hunting. The staged animations and the figure-per-idea discipline are close to the Lambert_GA standard; the only cost is that the home page asks for some scrolling before the science arrives.
justification.w2: Documentation of the evidence is strong, but the evidence is thin where it matters most. Real data are shown for growth (Fig 1-2), screening gels (Fig 4, 9), the RBS panel (Fig 11, Table 2) and the fermentation endpoints (Table 3), with units, replicate structure and processing stated. Against that, the headline claims of the project rest on models - the carbon footprint, the ¥35.3/kg cost, the 30 g shell mass and the 4-10 month skin lifetime are all calculations, labelled as such but still not measurements. The team marks the gap honestly rather than papering over it, which is why this is 3.5 and not 2.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly into Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Engagement and Team, every page carries a numbered on-page contents, figures are numbered and captioned consistently, and an image viewer lets you open gels and plates at full size. I could move from a claim in Description to its evidence in Results or Model in one hop each time. Not quite Patras level only because the Engagement section is very large and a first-time visitor could lose the thread between Human Practices, Education, Entrepreneurship, Sustainability and Collaboration.
justification.w4: The Contribution page is written for the next team rather than for the judges: media recipes named by total NaCl, the S17-1 to LA5 conjugation workflow, a failure log classified resolved / partly / open (including the still-open chloramphenicol selection problem), the LCA workbook, and a two-step method for estimating foam mass and seawater lifetime from a CAD model. Notebooks from both sites are on the wiki. The mark against it is sprawl - 21,000 words of Human Practices and 13,000 of Education against 3,000 of Results - which is the imbalance the handbook warns about in 'complete but not sprawling'.
justification.w5: Referencing is among the best I have seen at this level. Claims carry dated APA citations with DOIs (Song et al. 2020 for EPS fragmentation, Royer et al. 2023 for PLA in seawater, Dilkes-Hoffman et al. 2019 for marine PHA erosion, Zhang et al. 2022 for foaming), personal communications are named and dated, the national standard is cited by clause, and the Wiki Credits page documents fonts, map data, software licences and a register of AI-assisted images. The spot-checks I made resolve to real papers that say what the wiki says. Half a point off because a few figure sources sit only in the credits page rather than in the caption.

J2.one_line: An unusually well-framed and honestly documented platform project with outstanding human practices, held back from finalist contention by the fact that the central biology - PET to PHA - is screened and modelled but never demonstrated.
strengths: Human Practices genuinely drives the project: 31 engagements scored against published criteria, a 4S cycle with a self-investigation step, and traceable design changes (the M1/M2/M3 module split, the two-digit library cap from Lehan Li, withdrawal of their own overstated degradation claim)

The application is bounded by a real national standard (GB/T 44451-2024: 120 g, 90x65x280 mm) and priced from named operators, with a four-gate adoption route whose acceptance test - paired same-balloon flights - was specified by the user, not the team

A properly designed dry-lab experiment: a 48-run temperature x salt MD factorial with two seeds per cell and a stated two-SD screening threshold, reporting that only one of seven readouts passed (Model 1, Fig 2)

Measurement discipline well above the field: the Measurement page states what each readout can and cannot support, retains a transcription error as a flagged error, and refuses to apply one batch's dilution factor retrospectively

A failure log on the Contribution page classifying each problem resolved, partly resolved or open, including the unsolved chloramphenicol selection behaviour - the kind of openness about failure the handbook credits in GreatBay_SZ

Documentation built for reuse: media recipes, conjugation workflow, LCA workbook, a foam mass-and-lifetime method, and a parts table that flags which of its own cassette designs contain an internal stop codon
weaknesses: The core conversion is unproven: no PET degradation assay, no identified polymer, no titre. The six-flask endpoint is 0.02-0.08 g of unidentified recovered material weighed against a shared tare (Results Table 3)

The lead enzyme design is not validated - the team states the V3 plasmid design carries TGA at insert codon 19, and that assayed clones lack full sequence confirmation, so the MD-driven selection has no functional test behind it
The key engineering decision is still open: RBS7 has not been compared with the baseline phaCAB in the same flask experiment, so the one cycle that reached a production construct does not close

The GFP ranking rests on three technical wells in a single run, with fluorescence and OD600 acquired separately and no matched non-fluorescent control; LC-MS comparisons are n = 2 relative peak areas within one batch

No hardware was built. The shell mass, skin lifetime and foaming route are arithmetic from a CAD model and published rates - by the handbook's measurement standard, nothing about the shell has been measured
Sprawl: 21,000 words of Human Practices and 13,000 of Education against roughly 3,000 of Results, so the volume of the wiki does not track the weight of the evidence
red_flags: Registry pages could not be checked: parts.igem.org returned a CAPTCHA, which I did not attempt to bypass. Aspects 7 and 8 are therefore scored on wiki evidence with the Registry depth of the 38 claimed new entries unverified - another judge with Registry access should confirm.

Extensive AI involvement is declared rather than hidden: the wiki was built by advisor Weisi Wang with OpenAI Codex, three animations were made with Claude Code, the team flag was enhanced with image generation, and a 16-entry visual register lists AI-generated comic artwork. I found no indication that any evidence figure (gel, plot, plate photo) was AI-produced, and the register explicitly says absence from it does not certify an image was made without AI. I record this as a disclosure to note, not an integrity concern.

Instructor Yueqi Zeng is declared as having 'independently conducted part of the experimental work after students returned to school'. Declared, so no integrity issue, but it is part of why I did not score a6 above 3.5.

The chassis is Halomonas sp. LA5. The Safety page describes the White List and Check-In framework in its training module but I did not find an explicit statement that a Check-In was filed or approved for this organism. A question for the team rather than an accusation; worth the panel confirming against the team's safety form.

calibrated.changed: a1 4.0->3.5: a1 asks what was achieved, and here the chain delivers selections and models with no PET degraded and no polymer identified (consistent with my own a2 of 2.5). Keystone, which built and tested an integrated system on a real sample, got 3.5; scoring this team above it rewarded planned scope over delivered scope.

justification.a1: BioSonde covers a lot of ground within one season: a conjugation workflow for a non-model halophile (Halomonas sp. LA5), six designed PETase variants, an eleven-member RBS-GFP library measured in the target host, a phaCAB pathway build, a 48-run MD panel, a Monte Carlo LCA, and a foam-shell geometry study (Description; Engineering; Model; Hardware; Contribution). What keeps it below the GreatBay/TAS level is that the climb stops short of a demonstrated function: no sequence-confirmed clone, no PETase activity on PET, and no chemically identified PHB. The scope and the honesty are impressive; the completed arc is not yet there.
justification.a2: The measured outcomes are growth curves, PCR screening gels, relative LC-MS peak areas and one quantitative reporter assay; the two core functions of the project are not shown to work. The LC-MS comparisons are within-batch relative responses from n=2 A/B samples on cultures the team itself calls 'labelled', with no sequence-confirmed inserts and no matched empty-vector control in the assayed set (Results, 'PETase construction and substrate screening'; Measurement). The six-flask fermentation reports 0.02-0.08 g of 'recovered material' with no polymer identification and a shared tare mass (Results, Table 3), and the Proof of Concept states that a 4,724 bp V3 plasmid design carries TGA at insert codon 19. The team says all of this plainly, which I credit, but under the evidence rules a2 cannot exceed the mid-range.
justification.a3: The need was tested with the people who run the system, not asserted: a senior engineer at the Institute of Atmospheric Physics and a Beijing observation-operations director both questioned the premise, and the team's own arithmetic (60-80 t/yr of radiosonde material against 1-2 Mt/yr of ocean plastic) led them to delete the claim that the shell would measurably reduce marine plastic (Human Practices, Chapter I). What replaced it - a deliberately released, never-retrieved object whose material is chosen in advance - is a defensible impact argument, and Wang Qian's procurement account became four explicit qualification gates (HP Chapter VI). No shell has been built or flown, so the route remains a plan with named limits.
justification.a4: Eight DBTL cycles are documented with real failures driving redesign: blank TOP10 plates on 13 July led to a revised SOC-recovery workflow that gave colonies on 16 July; a PCR iteration on 5 August changed mix and cycling rather than discarding a construct; and candidate colonies that grew on chloramphenicol plates but stayed clear in liquid chloramphenicol were recorded as an open problem with a concrete next test (Engineering, Cycles 3-4; Contribution, failure log). Both models fed design decisions - the 48-run factorial MD prioritised V3 on a stated two-SD screen (Model, Section 5), and the GFP panel chose RBS7 for the phaCAB build (Engineering, Cycles 6-7). The main gap is that success criteria are descriptive screens rather than calibrated thresholds.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the project. Thirty-one engagements are each run through a Set/Sound/Shift/Steer loop and scored on a published five-criterion rubric, and the Shift step is the team's own checking, not a summary of praise (Human Practices, Table 1 and Chapters I-VI). Concrete, traceable changes: the application was bounded to shell plus insulation and the tonnage claim dropped after Xu Xiaojuan's challenge; the PET feedstock itself came from her question; procurement advice from Wang Qian became the four gates; and Sun Haixi and the research-design review stopped the team equating reporter brightness with PHA production. They also audited their own 64-response questionnaire, withdrew a degradation statement that contradicted Dilkes-Hoffman et al. (2019), named the leading wording as a flaw and recorded that respondents were mostly their own community. A BGI science-ethics director reviewed the project; what is missing for a 5 is any statement of consent procedure for the questionnaire respondents.
justification.a6: Attribution is unusually specific: every student and instructor has a task-by-task entry, including that an instructor, Yueqi Zeng, independently continued experiments after students returned to school, and that the wet-lab head supplied vectors, the S17-1 donor and the LA5 strain (Attributions, 'Project contributions'). The host-lab relationship with BGI is named rather than hidden, as is a two-month student placement there. The wiki also carries an AI-assisted visual register and states that OpenAI Codex built the site and that three animations were made with an AI coding tool. I would still ask in session which students personally ran the LC-MS and MD work, since those entries are phrased at a higher level than the bench entries.
justification.a7: The project is built in standard form: pSEVA321/341 contexts, a shared promoter-RBS-CDS architecture, six designed PETase coding sequences, ten primer-defined RBS elements and a composite RBS-phaCAB construct, with 53 Registry entries claimed (38 new) across five groups (Parts; Contribution). The design logic is genuinely synthetic-biology shaped - one junction varied, everything else held constant, which is what made the RBS comparison interpretable. It falls short of the top because only the reporter composite has measured function; the PETase and phaCAB parts are designed and built but not yet characterised, and at least two cassette designs carry internal stop codons.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation itself is excellent: numbered figures with full captions stating n, correction factors and instrument, three tables of raw per-flask values, a Measurement page that re-derives dilution factors and flags a contradictory notebook entry, and a Contribution page that lists media recipes and failures for reuse. On the Registry side the Parts page gives an ID, class, new/existing status and project role for all 53 entries, and the team notes sequence defects inside those entries. I could not reach parts.igem.org from this session (CloudFront 403), so I cannot confirm how much characterisation data actually sits on the Registry pages rather than only on the wiki; I have scored conservatively and would check this before the session.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the mechanism and the goal in a few lines - a Halomonas-based PHA platform for biodegradable radiosonde shells from waste PET - and uses a labelled schematic that separates instrument, shell and balloon so a reader knows exactly which component is being replaced (home). The staged radiosonde flight explainer is a genuinely good piece of science communication for a lay reader, and each section hands off to the right page.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently tied to figures with units, n and the correction applied, and the wiki repeatedly separates what was measured from what was modelled or planned: the Proof of Concept labels itself component-level, the Results page ends with 'Scope and next validation steps', and Measurement states outright that no polymer assay has been done (Results; Proof of Concept; Measurement). That discipline is rare and I credit it. It is not a 5 because the evidence that exists is thin where it matters most - n=2 chemical samples, technical-well-only reporter replication, and recovered mass standing in for polymer.
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly (Project / Wet Lab / Dry Lab / Engagement), standard pages are kept, and each long page carries an on-page contents list. Three content pages sit outside the standard set (alternative-platform, protocol, collaboration) but are reachable from the main menu. The cost is sprawl: Human Practices runs to about 21,000 words and Education to about 13,000, so a judge with limited time has to work to find the design-changing moments inside the HP narrative.
justification.w4: A future team could pick this up: the Contribution page hands over media recipes named by total NaCl, the full S17-1 to LA5 conjugation workflow, a classified failure log with resolved/partly/open status, a recalculating LCA workbook with a seeded Monte Carlo, and a foam mass-and-lifetime calculation (Contribution; Hardware). Both site notebooks are provided, and the Shenzhen page explains honestly why handwritten records were transcribed. The notebooks being PDFs rather than browsable entries is the one friction point.
justification.w5: Referencing is thorough and unusually scrupulous: full reference lists on HP, Hardware and Model; prior work by MammothEdu-South 2025 explicitly credited as the project's starting point; fonts, map data (frykit_data, Tianditu branch), WMO OSCAR and NOAA IGRA station metadata all credited with licences; and an AI-assisted visual register naming which images were AI-made (Attributions). The team also distinguishes a secondary relay (Amateur Radio Newsline) from the original ABC report. I spot-checked the claim attributions rather than every DOI, so I leave a half point for unverified links.

J3.one_line: An exceptionally honest, well-documented high school project with outstanding human practices and engineering records, held back by core biology that is screened and built but not yet shown to work.
strengths: Human Practices is genuinely integrated: 31 engagements run through a Set/Sound/Shift/Steer loop, with traceable design changes including dropping their own marine-plastic claim after doing the tonnage arithmetic themselves (HP Chapters I and VI)

Eight DBTL cycles with real failures on record - blank transformation plates, a PCR redesign, and an unresolved chloramphenicol selection anomaly kept open rather than buried (Engineering; Contribution failure log)

One clean quantitative dataset in the target chassis: the RBS-GFP panel in LA5, with RBS7 at 50,077 RFU/OD600 versus wild type, which then actually changed the next build (Results; Engineering Cycle 6)
Attribution is model-quality - per-student and per-instructor task breakdowns, the host-lab relationship with BGI named, and an AI-assisted visual register (Attributions)
A Measurement page that audits its own arithmetic, flags a contradictory dilution record and states what each readout cannot show - rarer and more valuable than another figure
weaknesses: No construct is sequence-confirmed, so the LC-MS comparisons describe 'labelled' cultures rather than verified strains; the team says so, but it caps what the data can support (Results; Proof of Concept)
The project's two headline functions are unproven: no PETase activity on intact PET, and the 0.02-0.08 g of fermentation 'recovered material' has no polymer identification (Results, Table 3)
Replication is thin where the conclusions lean hardest - n=2 A/B chemical samples and technical wells only for the reporter assay, with no independent biological repeats
Human Practices and Education together run to roughly 34,000 words; the design-changing moments are excellent but a reader has to dig for them
The questionnaire reflection is admirably self-critical about wording and sampling, but says nothing about consent or ethics oversight for respondents, many of whom were students
red_flags: Could not reach parts.igem.org from this session (CloudFront 403), so the depth of the 53 claimed Registry entries is unverified; the a8 score is conservative pending that check

The Proof of Concept discloses that the 4,724 bp V3 plasmid design carries TGA at insert codon 19, and the Contribution page says two cassette designs contain internal stop codons - disclosed by the team, not concealed, but it means the lead PETase design as built may not express

An unresolved selection anomaly (colonies growing on chloramphenicol plates but staying clear in liquid chloramphenicol, Engineering Cycle 4) leaves open whether the assayed LA5 cultures carried the plasmid at all

Extensive disclosed AI use: the website was built with OpenAI Codex, three animations with an AI coding tool, and a 15-page education comic is AI-illustrated. This is declared in a register, which meets the disclosure expectation; the experimental prose reads as the team's own and no figure looked generated, but the volume of AI-assisted production is worth a session question
Notebooks are supplied only as PDF downloads rather than browsable wiki entries

calibrated.changed: none. a2 of 2.5 follows my own rule that a team with no measured functional data cannot exceed 2.5 whatever the narrative says: n=2 relative LC-MS peak areas on unsequenced clones, recovered mass with no polymer identification, and a disclosed internal stop codon in the lead design. The high a4, a5 and a6 are genuinely earned and I have not trimmed them; the ranking, not the scores, carries the rule that outstanding practice cannot outrank working biology.

one_line.en: Exceptionally well-framed and honestly documented, with grand-prize-calibre human practices and record-keeping, but the central conversion is screened and built rather than demonstrated.
one_line.zh: 框架設定與文件誠實度極佳，人文實踐與紀錄保存達大獎水準，但核心轉化只做到篩選與建構，未獲實證。

strengths: 31 engagements in a consistent format, each with a traceable design change, plus a self-audit of the team's own survey wording
The problem is bounded by a real national standard and priced from named operators rather than pitched as saving the world
One clean quantitative dataset in the target chassis that then changed the next build
Unusual metrological honesty: the Measurement page separates correction from calibration, flags a contradictory record and refuses to call relative peak areas concentrations
weaknesses: No activity assay for the degradation branch; ranking rests on n = 2 relative peak areas with no abiotic control
No clone used in a functional assay HAS been sequence-confirmed
No polymer was identified — small recovered masses weighed at coarse precision with no purification procedure or biomass normalisation
No hardware was built, and Human Practices and Education together dwarf the Results page
red_flags: The team discloses that a lead plasmid design carries an internal stop codon early in the insert and that two cassette designs contain internal stop codons
An unresolved selection anomaly leaves open whether assayed cultures carried the plasmid
An instructor is declared as having independently conducted part of the experimental work
Extensive declared AI use in wiki, animation and illustration production

screen.project_title: Engineered E. coli for colorimetric sensing and biotransformation of chlorpyrifos and glyphosate
screen.what_they_built: They built two independent whole-cell colour sensors (ChpR-P_chpA driving eforRed for chlorpyrifos, PhnF-P_phnG driving amilCP for glyphosate) and two detoxification strains expressing organophosphate hydrolase OPD and glyphosate N-acetyltransferase GAT. The sensing and biotransformation modules were coupled and tested against pesticide and phosphate gradients.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a cloning host and BL21(DE3) expression host; pETDuet-1 for the sensing plasmids and pET28a for the enzyme plasmids, with a pelB signal peptide directing GAT to the periplasm; new basic parts for ChpR-P_chpA (BBa_26F401B7), PhnF-P_phnG (BBa_265YGEQY), OPD (BBa_26MN9CN6) and gat (BBa_26O2WI43) plus four composites, with reused eforRed and AmilCP parts.
screen.best_evidence: /results 4.1-4.5: ELISA and HPLC independently tracked pesticide removal over 0, 4, 8 and 24 h across six starting concentrations (100% removal at 0.1 and 1 uM; 58.45% / 60.60% for chlorpyrifos and 76.13% / 70.97% for glyphosate at 10 uM), and a phosphate gradient showed degradation collapsing from 57.20% at 0 mM to 5.47% at 50 mM phosphate; the specificity assay reports a 3.43-fold glyphosate response versus phosphate control for PhnF and only 2.46-fold for ChpR, below the team's own 3-fold criterion.
screen.hp_integration: Large human practices and entrepreneurship sections are present but the crawled pack does not show a specific design change traced to stakeholder input, so integration is asserted rather than demonstrated in the part of the wiki screened.
screen.reason: Two orthogonal detection-plus-detoxification modules with genuinely good quantitative work: dose-response curves, cross-validation of degradation by two independent analytical methods (ELISA and HPLC), a specificity control against inorganic phosphate, and a phosphate-tolerance limitation the team reports against its own pre-registered 3-fold threshold rather than hiding. It needs a full read to check attribution for the HPLC and ELISA work, replicate structure, and whether human practices actually changed anything.
screen.field_notes: MCA-SWIS (Bioremediation village, China) addressed chlorpyrifos and glyphosate residues in farmland with a two-module system in E. coli. The sensing module couples substrate-specific transcriptional regulators to chromoproteins: ChpR from Sinorhizobium meliloti activates P_chpA in response to TCP (the hydrolysis product of chlorpyrifos) driving eforRed, while PhnF from Agrobacterium tumefaciens CHLDO de-represses P_phnG in response to glyphosate driving amilCP. The biotransformation module expresses organophosphate hydrolase OPD (41.4 kDa) and periplasm-targeted pelB-GAT (16.6 kDa) from pET28a, confirmed soluble by SDS-PAGE across an IPTG gradient. Degradation was quantified by both ELISA and HPLC at 0, 4, 8 and 24 h over 0.1-100 uM: complete removal at 0.1 and 1 uM, partial at higher loads, with efficiency falling as substrate rose and the two methods agreeing in trend. A phosphate-tolerance assay fixed pesticide at 10 uM and varied phosphate 0-50 mM, showing chlorpyrifos degradation dropping from 57.20% to 5.47% and glyphosate from 72.24% to 4.50%, which the team names as the main barrier to use in phosphorus-rich soil. The glyphosate sensor met their 3-fold specificity threshold (3.43x) while the chlorpyrifos sensor did not (2.46x), attributed to insufficient TCP accumulation in a 6 h co-culture incubation. Sixteen parts listed, large education and entrepreneurship pages, no attributions page in the crawl.

screen.project_title: Waste to Watt — one-pot saccharification and fermentation of plastic-coated paper containers to ethanol
screen.what_they_built: A one-pot simultaneous saccharification and fermentation system: cenA cellulase plus a newly cloned thermophilic β-glucosidase (TmBglA) release glucose from laminated paper-container fibre while Zymomonas mobilis ferments it to ethanol, with a coupled ODE model and a benchtop integrated fermentor-distiller.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5α for cloning and BL21(DE3) for expression in pET-24a(+) (T7lac, ZYM-5052 autoinduction); Zymomonas mobilis as the fermenting microbe. New basic part BBa_26U9WJTK (codon-optimised T. maritima bglA) plus new characterisation added to the existing cenA part BBa_K118023 (Edinburgh 2008).
screen.best_evidence: /engineering Task 4: one-pot SSF of ~8 g alkali-pretreated ramen-bowl paper with both crude lysates and Z. mobilis for 48 h at 34 C gave ~1.0% ethanol in the distillate by refractometer against a 1% glucose control at ~1.5%, implying roughly 1.3 g glucose released per bottle (~16% of paper mass). Supporting: /engineering Task 1 saccharification of untreated tissue at 0.077-0.111 g glucose per g paper (n=3, mean ± SE) with a stall after 16 h, and the measured glucose inhibition constant Ki = 121 mM feeding the ODE model.
screen.hp_integration: Yes and traceably — they followed their own waste from the campus bin to the collector, the city cleaning team, a paper mill and a reuse specialist, then took the concept to a microbiologist, an enzymologist, ITRI and a paper-industry professor; the HP form has an explicit "What we changed" field per stakeholder and the conversations shaped the SSF framing and the scale-up assessment.
screen.reason: The strongest team in this batch: a complete characterisation programme on a part they chose and registered themselves (temperature, pH, glucose inhibition, ethanol tolerance, coculture stability, combined ethanol+heat), nearly all with n=3 and error bars, a model parameterised from their own measured Ki rather than literature, and an end-to-end demonstration that real paper waste becomes measurable ethanol, plus a built fermentor. Reads like a top-2 candidate for high school.
screen.field_notes: Taiwanese high school team (Mingdao, Biomanufacturing village) addressing plastic-laminated paper food containers that no mill will take. They surveyed GH1/GH3 β-glucosidases against criteria set by their one-pot design, chose TmBglA from Thermotoga maritima, codon-optimised and cloned it into pET-24a(+), verified clones by colony PCR (1024 bp) and screened eight clones by pNPG assay. Characterisation was run at fermentation-compatible conditions (34 C, pH ~6.4) far from the enzyme's thermophilic optimum: activity across 30-45 C, pH range, ethanol tolerance to 15% v/v over 24 h (90-105% residual activity), heat and distillation-simulating stress, and glucose product inhibition giving Ki = 121 mM. Three models follow: enzyme inhibition kinetics, Monod growth for Z. mobilis, and a coupled ODE showing the closed system reaching 500 mM glucose and 80.5% inhibition with 43.7% conversion versus an open system where the microbe acts as a glucose sink. The cenA cellulase is an extension of Edinburgh's BBa_K118023 with new kinetics added to the original part page. Hardware is a 45x45x60 cm laser-cut frame carrying shredder, reaction vessel on a rail, distillation and condensation so the mixture is never transferred. The final SSF run used their entire remaining enzyme stock and was not optimised, and ethanol was measured by refractometer rather than GC — the main evidential weakness. No separate results or parts page on the wiki; results live inside Engineering and Contribution.

justification.a1: The chain is unusually complete for a high school team: a cellulase BioBrick re-cloned and assayed, a new codon-optimised BglA beta-glucosidase cloned and characterised across temperature, pH, ethanol, heat and coculture, a three-part kinetic/ODE model built on their own measured constants, a benchtop one-frame fermentor, and a final one-pot run on a real ramen-bowl container (Engineering Tasks 1-4; Model; Hardware). Results build on each other rather than sitting side by side, which is what separates this from a single-result project. It falls short of the Grand Prize anchors because the final conversion is a single low-yield demonstration rather than an optimised or iterated proof of concept.
justification.a2: Enzyme function is genuinely demonstrated: pNPG and pNPC assays against empty-vector lysate controls, means with SE from n = 3, a pNP standard curve converting absorbance to product, and colony PCR gels with a named ladder and an explained false-positive control lane (Contribution Figures 1-3; Engineering Figures 2-4). Paper-to-glucose conversion is measured (0.077-0.111 g/g, n = 3, Engineering Figure 5) and the plateau is honestly read as product inhibition. The weak link is the capstone claim: the one-pot SSF run (Engineering Figure 13) compares paper+enzymes+Z. mobilis against a glucose-fed Z. mobilis standard, with no paper-plus-microbe-without-enzyme or no-microbe negative control, and ethanol is read by refractometer on a distillate, which responds to any solute; the derived 'roughly 1.3 g glucose from 8 g paper' is an inference, not a measurement.
justification.a3: The use case is anchored in real numbers the team collected themselves: NT$1.6/kg gate price for paper containers, the national Recycling Fund subsidy that certified processors receive and ordinary mills do not, mill rejection of PE-laminated loads, and ITRI's threshold of several tonnes a day or 100-500 kg on site (Human Practices, Acts I and II). Prof. Perng and Mr. Chen independently identified pulper reject as a feedstock the mill would pay to have removed, which is a credible route. But nothing was tested on real dirty or greasy feedstock, no mass balance or energy balance exists, and the team itself concedes it could not answer whether the process leaves the laboratory.
justification.a4: The DBTL cycles are real rather than decorative and at least two test results changed a design. The 80 degree ethanol-plus-heat experiment (Engineering Figure 12, Task 3-5) killed the team's own plan to recover and reuse the enzyme after conventional distillation and redirected them to low-temperature vacuum distillation, and the failed motorised rail led to the hand-pushed carriage and a documented assembly check (Hardware, Limitations). Screening criteria for the beta-glucosidase were written before candidate selection (Engineering Task 1-1, Table 1), which is the stated-measure-of-success behaviour the handbook asks for. It is a 4 rather than 5 because the redesigns are mostly process or hardware level; no construct was re-engineered in response to data.
justification.a5: Ten stakeholders along one traced waste stream, each written up on the same six-section form, with an explicit 'what we changed' and a section that keeps disagreements visible (Human Practices). Two changes are concrete and traceable into the bench work: adopting NCKU-Tainan's optical refractometer for ethanol measurement, and Prof. Ng's crude-lysate-with-empty-vector-control method, which is exactly the control scheme used in Contribution and Engineering. The team also documents where it went against expert advice (keeping one-pot SSF, skipping structure-prediction tools) and gives its reasoning, which is more honest than most. It is not a 5 because several 'what we changed' claims are softer than they sound (the safety-handbook addition and the emissions profile are asserted without evidence on the wiki), and the stakeholder answers are all rendered in one uniform polished voice, so it is hard to tell paraphrase from quotation.
justification.a6: The team page gives task-level roles for all fifteen students (wet lab experiments and first-pass analysis, hardware fabrication by named members, wiki coding, HP interviews), which is close to the attribution style the handbook rewards. Outsourcing is declared where it happened: gene synthesis by IDT, the Z. mobilis strain gifted by Prof. Hsieh's laboratory at NCYU, AI-assisted coding taught by a school teacher named in the Model page. Marked down because there is no attributions page at the standard URL, so the division between students, the instructor ('Ariel assisted our instructor') and any host-lab support is never stated in one place, and the wet-lab supervision arrangement is left implicit.
justification.a7: This is a genetic-device project built from Registry-compatible parts: an existing BioBrick (cenA, BBa_K118023) re-cloned and re-characterised, plus a new codon-optimised basic part, BglA BBa_26U9WJTK, registered as a tag-free CDS with host, topology, source and full sequence on the Registry. The design reasoning for choosing a GH1 over GH3 family enzyme, and for codon optimisation for E. coli expression, is explicit (Engineering Task 1-1 and 1-2). It is short of a 5 because the engineering stops at expressing two enzymes in BL21; there is no engineered circuit, no modular assembly standard discussion, and Z. mobilis itself was used wild type.
justification.a8: The Registry entry for BBa_26U9WJTK is the strongest documentation on offer: separate design, experiment, characterisation, application and summary records, figures with alt text and legends, a key-parameter table with conditions, and an explicit limitations list (crude lysate, pNPG not cellobiose, Km from three points). The contribution to BBa_K118023 was also posted to the Registry page, not only to the wiki. The wiki side costs them: parts, results, measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, notebook, safety-and-security and attributions all return 404 and are absent from the navigation, so a judge must find the results inside Engineering and Contribution without being told to, and the new part number appears only in running text on one page.
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem (7,000 students, plastic-lined containers no mill will take), the approach (cellulase plus beta-glucosidase plus Z. mobilis in one pot) and what was actually done, inside one abstract paragraph, with five labelled section cards beneath it. A captioned video transcript is provided in text, so the argument survives without playing the video. The Project page then restates motivation, research and aims clearly; the only drift is that 'Waste-to-Watt' promises electricity generation that the wiki never demonstrates.
justification.w2: Most key claims carry a figure with a legend naming the instrument, the buffer, the control and the replicate count (Contribution Figures 1-3; Engineering Figures 2-12; Model Figures 1-8 with linked raw CSVs). Modelled output is consistently labelled as simulation and the Model page states its own limitation that pNPG-derived kinetics are being applied to a cellobiose feed. Two gaps keep it off 5: the glucose-gradient kinetics were single measurements per condition, acknowledged on the Model page, and the final ethanol result lacks a negative control and rests on a refractometer reading of a distillate.
justification.w3: Navigation is short and clean, every page has an in-page section menu, and cross-page pointers to Contribution and Model are given as full URLs. Against that, seven standard pages that judges go to first (results, parts, measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, notebook, safety-and-security, attributions) return 404 and are not linked anywhere, so the experimental results live under Engineering and Contribution and the new part has no parts page. The Human Practices page is also very long for a single scroll.
justification.w4: A future team gets a good deal here: raw data CSVs and the named Python scripts for each model, a pNP standard curve, an OD-to-dry-cell-weight calibration, a full bill of materials with prices, laser-cutting drawings and 24 STLs plus editable CAD on the team's iGEM GitLab, and a user test of the documentation by eight students. What is missing is the ordinary laboratory record: there is no protocols page and no notebook, so the cloning, autoinduction and assay steps must be reconstructed from prose in Contribution and Engineering, and no failures timeline is kept.
justification.w5: Every page carries a numbered reference list with resolvable DOIs or URLs, including the Chinese-language municipal and industry sources, and literature values are attributed where they are compared with the team's own numbers (Ma et al. for g/g conversion, Mehmood for the 238 IU/mg benchmark, Rogers for the 97% ethanol yield). Prior iGEM work is properly credited: Edinburgh 2008, XMU-China 2019, CAU_China 2019 and SYSU-CHINA 2021 are each named for their specific contribution to the cenA lineage, and St_Andrews' GST-tagged BglA is distinguished from the new part on the Registry entry. Small gap: figures and photographs carry no individual source lines, and the stakeholder quotations are given without a date or recording reference on the page itself.

J1.one_line: A coherent waste-to-ethanol project with a genuinely new, well-characterised Registry part and honest controls on the enzyme work, let down by a final SSF demonstration without a negative control and by seven missing standard wiki pages.
strengths: New basic part BBa_26U9WJTK (BglA from T. maritima) is registered with host, topology, source, sequence and five separate documentation records including an explicit limitations list, which is well above the usual high school Registry entry

Enzyme activity claims are tested against empty-vector lysate controls with n = 3 and SE throughout, and absorbance is converted to product via a pNP standard curve rather than reported as raw OD (Contribution Figures 2-3, Engineering Figures 3-4, Model Figure 4)
A real DBTL loop: the combined 80 degree and ethanol stress test (Engineering Figure 12) disproved the team's own enzyme-reuse plan and redirected the hardware toward vacuum distillation

Characterisation is matched to the application rather than to the assay optimum: a thermophilic enzyme deliberately measured at 34 degrees and pH 6.4, plus a coculture experiment showing BglA survives alongside growing Z. mobilis while the microbe grows normally (Engineering Figure 10)

The model is built entirely on the team's own measured constants (Ki = 121 mM, mu-max = 0.55 per h, Ks = 0.16 mM, Yxs = 0.064 g/g) with raw CSVs and Python scripts linked, and it states where it is an approximation

Human Practices follows one physical object through ten stakeholders, records where they disagreed, and names two advice items that changed bench practice (refractometer, crude lysate plus empty-vector controls)

Hardware is fully reproducible: bill of materials at about US$90, laser-cut drawings, 24 STLs and editable CAD on iGEM GitLab, plus a documentation usability test with eight student testers and the low scores reported honestly
weaknesses: The capstone SSF experiment (Engineering Figure 13) has no negative control: no paper-plus-microbe-without-enzyme arm and no uninoculated arm, so the 1.0 percent distillate reading is not isolated to the enzyme cascade

Ethanol is quantified by refractometer on a distillate, an index-of-refraction method that responds to any dissolved solute; the derived figure of about 1.3 g glucose from 8 g paper is an inference chained through an assumed 97 percent literature yield, not a measurement

Seven standard pages (results, parts, measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, notebook, safety-and-security, attributions) return 404; results must be hunted for inside Engineering and Contribution, and the new part has no wiki parts page
No protocols or notebook page, so methods exist only as prose inside results narratives and the work could not be repeated step by step
The glucose-gradient kinetics underlying Ki, Km and Vmax were single measurements per condition (n = 1), acknowledged on the Model page but still the foundation of the whole coupled ODE result

Hardware validation (Table 1) is entirely qualitative: 'temperature was well controlled' and 'ethanol was successfully distilled and collected' with no logged values, set point, recovery percentage or input concentration
No attributions page; the role of the instructor who the team says students assisted, and of any host laboratory, is never stated in one place

The Z. mobilis growth and glucose data use a household blood-glucose meter whose stated range (20-600 mg/dL) sits above several of the tested concentrations, which the team notes but still uses for the depletion-time table
red_flags: Eight standard wiki URLs return 404 (results, parts, measurement, proof-of-concept, protocols, notebook, safety-and-security, attributions); under p.29 judges should not have to hunt, and key evidence sits on non-standard pages

No safety page at all, for a project involving NaOH pretreatment at 80 degrees, ethanol vapour near a heat source and a recombinant E. coli expression host; safety is mentioned only in a paragraph on the Hardware page
The one-pot SSF result, which the team calls the central achievement of the project, is reported without a negative control and with an indirect measurement method

Human Practices stakeholder answers are presented as full expandable quotations but are all rendered in a single uniform register, with no interview dates, recordings or language notes on the page; the supporting forms are offered as PDFs. This is a transparency gap I would ask about in Q&A, not an integrity allegation

Some 'what we changed' claims have no supporting evidence on the wiki, specifically the full safety and emissions profile said to have been prioritised for the prototype and the safety protocol said to have been added to the school's laboratory safety handbook
pages_read: https://2026.igem.wiki/mingdao/hardware (full, incl. validation, user testing, BOM, limitations)
Registry BBa_26U9WJTK (part record plus all five documentation entries: design, experiment, characterisation, application, summary)
Registry BBa_K118023 (documentation list; Mingdao 2026 characterisation entry 'CenA retains activity at 34C and pH 6.4')

calibrated.changed: a8 3.5 -> 4.0 and w3 3.5 -> 3.0. a8: p.18 says parts are judged on the Registry entry, and Mingdao is the one team whose Registry entry I actually verified as carrying separate design, experiment, characterisation, application and summary records with a key-parameter table and a limitations list, plus a contribution posted to BBa_K118023. I gave 4.0 to PLKLFC and HK League on unverified Registry entries with good wiki tables, so capping Mingdao at 3.5 for wiki-side 404s double-counted a navigation fault. w3: eight missing standard pages, including results and parts, is the worst set on this ballot; I gave 3.0 to Hangzhou No.14 for seven and to Cataverse for six, so 3.5 here was inconsistent.

justification.a1: For a high school team the scope is wide and the pieces connect. They selected a new beta-glucosidase (BglA from T. maritima) from the literature against stated criteria, cloned it and characterised it at 34 C (Engineering Fig 3-12). They re-characterised the cenA part at fermentation conditions (Contribution Fig 1-3), built a three-stage model from their own measurements (Model Fig 1-9), and finished with a paper-to-ethanol proof of concept on a real ramen-bowl container (Engineering Fig 13). They also built a benchtop prototype and ran a user test. It falls short of a 5 for three reasons: the final SSF demonstration is thin, the hardware never ran the biology, and nothing was tested on real dirty waste.
justification.a2: Measured: BglA activity against an empty-vector control (Fig 3, n=3), a temperature series (Fig 4), glucose inhibition (Fig 6), heat half-life of about 5 h at 80 C (Fig 8), a pH panel (Fig 9), coculture stability with Z. mobilis plus single-component controls (Fig 10), and ethanol tolerance to 15% (Fig 11). The cenA lysate gives about 7-fold signal over the control (Contribution Fig 2). The weak point is the SSF result (Fig 13c, 1.0% vs 1.5% ethanol in distillate by refractometer). It has no paper-free or enzyme-free control, so carry-over sugar from the lysate cannot be ruled out. No sequencing or SDS-PAGE is shown for the BglA clone.
justification.a3: Impact is argued from a well-traced waste chain: school, recycling yard, city EPB, paper mill, Jing Si, ITRI and an NCHU pulp lab, with concrete constraints such as NT$1.6/kg, the subsidy structure and pulper reject as feedstock (Human Practices). The team says plainly that the process has not been run on real dirty containers or at high solids loading, and that question 5, whether it can leave the lab, is unanswered. Deployment is plausible and checked with stakeholders, but nothing was tested in a realistic setting.
justification.a4: The project runs as a logical chain. The glucose plateau in Task 1 (Fig 5) prompted the inhibition study and the model in Task 2. The model's warning about real conditions prompted the stability tests in Task 3. The heat-plus-ethanol result (Fig 12) produced a real new requirement: conventional 80 C distillation destroys BglA, so vacuum distillation is needed. That requirement was not acted on, though, because the hardware still distils at 80 C. The model is fitted to their own data (Ki 121 mM, mumax 0.55/h, Y 0.064, with OD-to-DCW calibration) but is not validated against an SSF run. It also ignores ethanol inhibition of Z. mobilis, which inflates the predicted 13 g/L biomass and 12% ethanol. Overall this is mostly sequential characterisation rather than build-test-redesign cycles. The hardware motor failure and user-test feedback did drive small revisions.
justification.a5: The HP is structured and reflective. It uses the same six-section form for ten stakeholders across two 'acts', has an outward 'what it would do to them' section, and has an explicit agreed/disagreed section. The team kept one-pot SSF against Prof. Ng's advice and explains why. Documented changes are real but modest: adopting the refractometer, crude lysate with empty-vector controls, shredding and alkaline pretreatment, and reframing the model toward enzyme cost after Dr. Liao. Some 'what we changed' entries are weak links. For example, the recycling-yard visit is said to have led to characterising cenA at 34 C. The very polished 'full answers' make me want to ask how interviews were recorded and translated.
justification.a6: The wiki has no Attributions page (404). The team page gives task-based bios for 15 students: wet lab done in lunch breaks, hardware students did the CAD, laser cutting and assembly, and a student built the wiki. The instructor's role in the wet lab is not described ('Ariel assisted our instructor'). Outside help is named in the text: IDT gene synthesis, the Z. mobilis strain from Prof. Hsieh (NCYU), NCKU guidance, and a school IT teacher who taught AI-assisted coding. Execution looks student-led, but I could not check the official form fields from the wiki, so I hold this at 3.
justification.a7: There is one new basic part, BBa_26U9WJTK: a codon-optimised BglA CDS, linear, chassis E. coli BL21. I checked the sequence: it has no EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI, NotI, BsaI or SapI sites, so it is RFC10/RFC1000 compatible. There is also a contribution to the existing BBa_K118023 (cenA). Synthetic biology is central but simple: heterologous enzyme expression in pET-24a, dosed as crude lysate, with no engineered organism or genetic circuit. The part is a reusable enzyme for one-pot SSF.
justification.a8: Registry documentation is the strongest I would expect from a HS team. BBa_26U9WJTK has design rationale, a cloning/expression/pNPG protocol, a characterisation entry of about 20k characters with all the stability data, an application entry, and a summary table of key parameters and limitations. BBa_K118023 has a new dated entry, 'CenA retains activity at 34 C and pH 6.4'. The Model page adds raw CSVs and Python scripts. The only gap is no sequence verification for the part.
justification.w1: The home page states the concept in one line ('unrecyclable paper lunch boxes into ethanol, in a single pot'), and the abstract names enzymes, chassis and SSF. The Description page explains the motivation, prior iGEM parts and the approach clearly. But its 'Aims' and 'Expected Results' are still in planning tense ('we will', 'we anticipate'). It never states a quantified success criterion or summarises what was achieved.
justification.w2: Engineering and Model give methods, figure captions with n=3 and SE, empty-vector controls, a pNP standard curve, and downloadable raw data and scripts. That is convincing evidence for the enzyme claims. Evidence is weaker for the SSF ethanol result (missing controls; refractometer at about 1%) and for the hardware. Hardware Table 1 is entirely qualitative ('temperature was well controlled', 'ethanol was successfully distilled'), with no logged temperatures or recovery percentage.
justification.w3: There are eight clear tabs, in-page section menus, and good cross-links (Engineering to Model and Contribution). Many standard pages return 404: Results, Parts, Notebook, Protocols, Safety, Attributions and Measurement. Results live inside Engineering, parts are only reachable through text links, and a judge looking for the standard pages finds nothing. Long pages such as HP (~12.7k words) and Model (~8.4k words, including tutorial ODE examples) are bigger than they need to be.
justification.w4: This is a good record for future teams. It has raw CSVs and Python scripts for every model, an ODE tutorial, a hardware bill of materials (NT$2,868), laser-cut PDFs, 24 STL files and CAD on iGEM GitLab, assembly steps and pitfalls, a blank HP stakeholder template and an engagement log, plus detailed Registry protocols. There is no notebook or protocols page.
justification.w5: Every page has numbered references with DOIs and prior iGEM parts credited by team and year. I spot-checked nine DOIs on Crossref and all resolve to the stated papers. One has wrong metadata: Annamalai is cited as 9(11):2185-2194 (2018), but Crossref gives vol 11, pp 121-131. Some HP references are Facebook or Google Sites pages, and reference support is uneven in places (e.g. the 97% ethanol yield is attributed to a transcriptomics paper).

J2.one_line: A strong HS enzyme-engineering project: a new, well-characterised BglA part with exemplary Registry documentation and a model fitted to the team's own data. It is held back by an uncontrolled final SSF ethanol result, qualitative-only hardware validation, and missing standard pages, including Attributions.
strengths: New basic part BBa_26U9WJTK (BglA). It is RFC10/RFC1000 compatible, and its Registry documentation covers design, protocol, characterisation, application and summary.
Systematic characterisation under SSF-relevant conditions (temperature, pH, glucose inhibition, ethanol, coculture, heat plus ethanol) with empty-vector controls and n=3 (Engineering Fig 3-12).
Model parameters are all fitted from their own measurements (Ki, Km, mumax, Ks, Yx/s, OD-to-DCW), with raw CSVs and Python scripts downloadable.
The heat-plus-ethanol test produced a genuine design insight: conventional distillation is incompatible with enzyme reuse, so vacuum distillation is needed.
Contribution to the existing cenA part BBa_K118023, with a new dated characterisation entry on the Registry.
HP is reflective and structured: ten stakeholders, an explicit agreed/disagreed section, honest unanswered questions, and a reusable stakeholder form.
Open hardware package: BOM, laser-cut PDFs, STL and CAD on iGEM GitLab, and a user test with 8 testers and documented responses.
weaknesses: The final SSF result (Fig 13c, about 1.0% vs 1.5% ethanol in distillate) lacks paper-free and enzyme-free controls. The refractometer has limited resolution at this level, and the yield is back-calculated through assumptions.
The hardware never ran the biological process (Task 4 used a household fragrance-oil distiller), and its validation table has no numbers: no temperature log, no distillation recovery.
The vacuum-distillation requirement found in Task 3 was not carried into the hardware, which still distils at 80 C.

The model is not validated against an SSF experiment. It uses pNPG rates as a proxy for cellobiose, omits ethanol inhibition of Z. mobilis, and has no cellulase step. Its predicted 13 g/L biomass and 12% ethanol are optimistic.
No sequencing or SDS-PAGE verification of the BglA clone; the Km/Vmax estimate rests on three substrate concentrations at n=1.
Standard pages return 404 (Results, Parts, Notebook, Protocols, Safety, Attributions, Measurement).
The Description page still reads as a plan ('we will', 'Expected Results') with no stated quantified success criterion.
Several HP 'what we changed' links are tenuous (e.g. a yard visit is said to have led to cenA characterisation at 34 C).
red_flags: The Attributions page is missing from the wiki (404) and the instructor's wet-lab role is undescribed. Not an integrity concern by itself. Q&A question: who performed the cloning and assays, and how much did the instructor do?
No Safety page. Q&A/safety question, not an accusation: confirm Zymomonas mobilis is on the iGEM White List or was cleared through a check-in for a HS team.

HP stakeholder 'full answers' are rendered as fluent, polished English paragraphs with no note on recording or translation. Worth asking whether these are transcripts, translations or reconstructions (digital handbook academic-integrity guidance on quotes). Not scored down on suspicion.
Minor citation metadata error: Annamalai et al. is cited as Waste Biomass Valor 9(11):2185-2194 (2018); Crossref gives vol 11, pp 121-131.
pages_read: Registry BBa_K118023 (documentation list incl. Mingdao 2026 entry)

calibrated.changed: none — a4 3.5 for sequential characterisation with one unacted-on requirement matches keystone's single-cycle 3.5; a8 4.5 is the one case where I read full Registry characterisation entries of real depth.

justification.a1: The project climbs logically within one season: a stated screening spec for a β-glucosidase, a literature screen (Table 1, Engineering Task 1-1), a new codon-optimised BglA part cloned and assayed, characterisation against four fermentation stresses, a model fitted to the team's own kinetics, and finally a one-pot SSF run on a real ramen-bowl container plus a US$90 integrated fermentor with user testing (Hardware). That is a lot of ground for a high school team and it hangs together as one argument. It falls short of a 5 because the end-to-end demonstration is a single crude run with semi-quantitative ethanol measurement rather than an optimised, replicated process.
justification.a2: The enzyme work is genuinely demonstrated: pNPG assays with empty-vector lysate controls and n=3 (Engineering Figs 3, 4), glucose-inhibition series at three substrate levels (Model Figs 1-3), a coculture experiment with three arms showing BglA activity above 80% and Z. mobilis-only background around 12% (Engineering Fig 10), and paper tissue converted to glucose at 0.077-0.111 g/g (Fig 5). The final SSF claim is weaker: ethanol in the distillate was read by refractometer (not an ethanol-specific method) against a 1% glucose fermentation standard, with no paper-plus-no-enzyme or no-microbe vessel, and the glucose figure is back-calculated through an assumed 97% conversion (Engineering Task 4).
justification.a3: The need is confirmed from inside the waste chain rather than asserted: the yard prices containers at NT$1.6/kg and says it cannot wash them, the city explains that only certified processors get the subsidy, and Ta Chang Paper says it would give away or pay to offload its pulper reject (Human Practices, Act I). Jing Si's director confirmed the tissue route cannot take greasy post-consumer boxes, which is the gap the project fills. Deployment limits are named honestly — the team states on the same page that it never tested real dirty containers or the pulper-reject feedstock, and could not answer whether the process could leave the lab.
justification.a4: Each of the four Engineering tasks carries a real Learn step, and two of them changed the design. Discovering that 80°C plus 6% or more ethanol inactivates BglA within an hour (Fig 12) killed the planned enzyme reuse after conventional distillation and set a new requirement for low-temperature vacuum recovery; on Hardware, the motorised rail binding under load led to a hand-pushed carriage and an explicit pre-heat travel check in the assembly steps. The model was fitted to the team's own Ki, mu_max and Y_X/S and then used to ask how much inoculum a fermentor needs. It is not a 5 because the vacuum-distillation redesign was never built or tested, and only one inoculum and one feed rate were simulated.
justification.a5: Ten stakeholders were chosen by following one container along the actual waste chain, each written up in the same six-section form including 'What we changed', and the team keeps an 'Agreement and Disagreement' section and admits one of its five questions went unanswered (Human Practices).
