Real consequences are traceable: the mill and city findings that PE cannot be cleanly removed led to shred-and-alkali-pretreat rather than delaminate, and Jing Si's hygiene limit confirmed the pivot from paper-to-paper to fuel. It is not higher because several 'What we changed' entries restate work already planned — after the mill visit the team honestly writes that the visit matched the design it had already built rather than changing it — and neither the stakeholder interviews nor the eight-student hardware questionnaire mentions consent or any ethics oversight.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page at all (https://2026.igem.wiki/mingdao/attributions returns 404), which is the page I rely on for this aspect. The Team page gives each of the fifteen students a role, and outside help is named in the prose — the Z. mobilis strain and protocols from Prof. Hsieh's lab at NCYU, enzyme-design and measurement advice from Prof. Ng's lab and NCKU-Tainan, a school IT teacher who taught the AI-assisted coding used for the Python fits, gene synthesis by IDT, a borrowed hotplate stirrer. But no figure caption names who ran the experiment, there is no who-did-what chart, and the Registry entry for BBa_26U9WJTK lists three contributors including one credited with 'Supervision', so I cannot tell from the wiki how much of the bench work and the modelling the students did themselves.
justification.a7: The design is standard-parts synthetic biology: one new basic part contributed — the codon-optimised T. maritima BglA CDS, BBa_26U9WJTK, 1,344 bp, exportable in RFC10 and RFC1000, biosafety cleared — built in pET-24a(+)/E. coli BL21(DE3), together with reuse and re-characterisation of an existing BioBrick, Edinburgh's cenA (BBa_K118023). The hardware is a genuine engineered component of the system. It stops short of 5 because no composite part was designed, there is no regulatory or circuit design, and the biology is heterologous expression of two known enzymes.
justification.a8: The new part is documented on the Registry itself, not only on the wiki: the BBa_26U9WJTK page carries sequence, CDS role, linear topology, host (E. coli BL21), GC content and five authored sections — Design, Experiment, Characterisation, Application and Discussion. The team also added its 34°C/pH 6.4 characterisation to the original BBa_K118023 page, as described on the Contribution page. On the wiki side, figure captions give buffer, temperature, instrument, replicate number and error type, and raw CSVs and named Python scripts are referenced. Short of 5 because there is no Parts page on the wiki (404) to index the parts, and no protocols or notebook page.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem (7,000 students, plastic-lined containers no mill will take), the approach (cellulase plus β-glucosidase plus Z. mobilis in one pot) and the goal in a few lines, then hands the reader five short section teasers that each link onward. The video transcript is given as text, so the opening argument survives without watching the film. Minor digressions in the Project page's long motivation section keep it just below a 5.
justification.w2: Most claims are carried by a figure whose caption gives the buffer, temperature, instrument, replicate number and error type, and the team separates measurement from simulation consistently — the Model page labels every ODE output as a simulation and states the pNPG-versus-cellobiose limitation itself. The gaps are the semi-quantitative ethanol endpoint in Engineering Task 4, the single measurement per condition behind the Model 1 kinetics, and clone identity resting on colony PCR alone.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and fast — eight pages, each with its own anchor rail, and cross-page links that actually point to where the evidence is. But Results, Parts, Safety, Attributions, Protocols and Notebook all return 404, so results are buried inside Engineering and Contribution and a judge has to hunt for material the handbook says should be reachable from the standard pages.
justification.w4: A future team gets a long way from this wiki: assay conditions and media recipes are written into the Engineering and Model text, the Model page names each Python script and raw CSV, and Hardware publishes a priced bill of materials, 1:1 laser-cutting drawings, 24 STL files and assembly steps, plus a reusable blank stakeholder form. What is missing is a notebook or dated protocol page and any record of who did what, which is part of what makes a project rebuildable.
justification.w5: Every page carries a numbered reference list with DOIs, and prior iGEM work is credited generously and specifically — Edinburgh 2008, XMU-China 2019, CAU_China 2019 and SYSU-CHINA 2021 are each named with their part numbers and what they contributed, and the Contribution page explains how this team's addition differs. The references I sampled resolve and support the claims made. Image credit is not stated anywhere, though the figures all appear to be the team's own.

J3.one_line: A disciplined, honest high-school project: one new Registry-documented beta-glucosidase part characterised under real fermentation stresses, a model fitted to the team's own data, a one-pot SSF run on a real lunch box and a US$90 integrated fermentor — let down by a missing Attributions page and a semi-quantitative final ethanol measurement.
strengths: Defined the enzyme it needed before searching for one, then characterised BglA against the four stresses its own process imposes — heat, pH, ethanol, and co-incubation with living Z. mobilis — each with vector-only controls and n=3 (Engineering Figs 8-11)
The coupled ODE model is built from the team's own measured Ki, mu_max, Ks and Y_X/S rather than literature values, and is clearly labelled as simulation throughout (Model, Models 1-3)
Reports what went wrong and acts on it: the ethanol-plus-80C synergy (Fig 12) ended the enzyme-reuse plan, and the motor failure ended the automated rail (Hardware, Limitations)
Human Practices follows one container through five links of the real waste chain and keeps a section on where stakeholders disagreed, plus a frank list of the questions it could not answer

Hardware is reproducible by another team: bill of materials with prices, laser-cut drawings, 24 STL files, assembly steps, and eight students who ran the machine from the page alone and whose criticisms are printed with the team's response
Honest about limits in its own voice — pNPG kinetics are not cellobiose kinetics, the crude lysate Vmax is not a specific activity, and the enzyme loading in the final run was whatever stock remained
weaknesses: No Attributions page (404), and no figure caption or chart says which student ran which experiment, so the division between student work and the help from the NCYU and NCKU labs cannot be checked from the wiki

The final ethanol result rests on a refractometer reading of a distillate, which is not ethanol-specific, with a 1% glucose fermentation as the only comparator — a paper-plus-enzyme-no-microbe and a no-enzyme vessel would have made the claim much stronger
Results, Parts, Safety, Protocols and Notebook pages are all 404; the actual results live inside Engineering and Contribution, which makes a judge hunt
cenA and BglA clones were confirmed by colony PCR only — no sequencing and no SDS-PAGE of the expressed protein is shown, so clone identity rests on band size
Model 1's kinetics come from one measurement per condition (n=1), acknowledged but still the foundation of Ki = 121 mM and of Model 3
Neither the stakeholder interviews nor the eight-student hardware questionnaire mentions consent or any ethics oversight
red_flags: Attributions page missing entirely (404) while the project used a university strain, university enzyme-design advice and AI-assisted coding taught by a school staff member — a session question about who did the bench work and the Python fitting, not an accusation
Safety page missing (404); biosafety is only discussed inside a Human Practices answer (Z. mobilis as BSL-1) and in a Hardware paragraph

Stakeholder answers are quoted at length in uniformly fluent, similarly-voiced English although the meetings were in Chinese, and unlike the hardware testers' comments these are not marked as translations — worth asking how the quotes were produced and whether speakers approved them

The claim of roughly 1.3 g of glucose, about 16% of the starting paper mass (Engineering Task 4), is a back-calculation from a refractometer ratio and an assumed 97% conversion; it is presented with its assumptions, but it is an inference, not a measurement
pages_read: 404 checked: results, parts, attributions, safety-and-security, notebook, protocols, proof-of-concept, measurement, education, software

calibrated.changed: none. a6 of 3 is the band I use for a missing Attributions page plus per-student roles plus named outside help, and the a8 of 4 is one of the few I could actually verify on the Registry rather than infer.

one_line.en: A coherent waste-to-ethanol project with a genuinely new, well-documented Registry part and a model built on its own measured constants, let down by an uncontrolled final demonstration and seven missing standard pages.
one_line.zh: 從廢棄物到乙醇的連貫專案，有真正新穎且文件完整的 Registry 零件，模型全部建立在自家量測常數上，但最終示範缺對照、七個標準頁缺失。

strengths: A new basic part registered with host, topology, source, sequence and five documentation records including an explicit limitations list
Enzyme activity tested against empty-vector lysate controls with replicates and standard-curve conversion rather than raw absorbance
A real loop where a combined stress test disproved the team's own reuse plan and redirected the hardware
Fully reproducible open hardware with a costed bill of materials, drawings, CAD files and a usability test whose low scores are reported honestly
weaknesses: The capstone demonstration HAS no negative control arms, so the result is not isolated to the enzyme cascade
Ethanol is quantified by a method that responds to any dissolved solute, and the derived yield is chained through an assumed literature conversion
Seven standard pages return 404, including results, parts, protocols, notebook and attributions
Kinetic constants underlying the model come from single measurements per condition, and hardware validation is entirely qualitative
red_flags: No attributions page and no description of the instructor's wet-lab role
No safety page at all for work involving hot alkali, ethanol vapour near a heat source and a recombinant host
Stakeholder quotations rendered in a single uniform register with no interview dates, recordings or translation notes
A citation's volume and page metadata do not match the record

screen.project_title: MPA-DNT-Safe / "DNT Detonators": sensing, degradation and cold-gated containment of 2,4-dinitrotoluene
screen.what_they_built: A two-strain E. coli system for 2,4-DNT: a YhaJ-PyqjF-GFP whole-cell biosensor and a BL21(DE3) strain carrying an eight-gene Burkholderia dnt degradation operon, both fitted with a pCspA-MazF cold-inducible kill switch and silicate-gel immobilisation. They also built three generations of a 3D-printed portable fluorescence spectrometer to read the sensor in the field.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli (pET-28a(+) backbone, BL21(DE3) for degradation). 10 new basic parts registered: PyqjF (BBa_26PFC87Q), YhaJ (BBa_260ZJI3G) and dntAa/Ab/Ac/Ad/B/D/G/E; standard RBS BBa_B0034, terminator BBa_B0015 and Anderson promoters J23100/J23106/J23114; new characterisation of existing part BBa_K2817006 (pCspA-MazF).
screen.best_evidence: /results: HPLC-UV time course of degradation at 50 ug/mL 2,4-DNT - engineered MPA-DNT falls to 11.88 +/- 2.65 ug/mL at 10 h (76.2% apparent removal) against 45.87 ug/mL (8.3%) for the WT BL21 control; a concentration series gives 90.26 +/- 6.57% at 20 ug/mL down to 56.16 +/- 4.96% at 200 ug/mL. Sensor data on the same page: J23114 gives the best 8.67-fold induction and SNR rises to 22.16 at 8 h with 200 ug/mL DNT.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - /human-practices records six stages in which synthetic biologists argued them out of a single super-bacterium into a two-strain split, a soil expert pushed them past bottle-culture conditions, and four rounds of hardware stakeholder feedback (an ecologist, an instrument maker, an engineer, a final field tester) drove the spectrometer from a rejected wooden box to a sealed quantitative Generation 3.
screen.reason: Three modules each backed by quantitative data with controls and error bars, a genuinely iterated open-hardware reader with BOM and print files, 10 new parts plus new characterisation of an existing one, and HP that visibly changed the design. The one serious hole is attribution: the /attributions page serves duplicated 'case file' project-overview text rather than any statement of who did what (the /collaborations page serves the same duplicated content), and /model is unedited iGEM template boilerplate. Worth a full read, with the panel pressing on attribution and on how the eight-gene operon was verified beyond PCR gels.
screen.field_notes: MPAYF-USA (Bioremediation, USA) targeted 2,4-dinitrotoluene, a carcinogenic nitroaromatic from polyurethane and TNT manufacture with a 9-17 year natural half-life, and split detection from degradation across two E. coli strains rather than building one super-bacterium. The biosensor is YhaJ driving the DNT-responsive PyqjF promoter onto GFP; comparing J23100/J23106/J23114 for yhaJ expression showed J23114 gave the lowest background and the best 8.67-fold induction, with a dose response over 20-200 ug/mL and SNR reaching 22.16 at 8 h. The degradation strain carries eight Burkholderia dnt genes under T7 and removed 76.2% of 50 ug/mL DNT in 10 h by HPLC-UV against 8.3% for wild-type BL21, with triplicate means and SDs across a 20-200 ug/mL load series. A pCspA-MazF cold kill switch (existing part BBa_K2817006) was re-characterised at 6.2x reporter output at 15 C versus 37 C plus 48 h growth inhibition, with the team noting honestly that CFU and escape-frequency assays are still needed to claim killing. Hardware is a strength: three generations of a 3D-printed portable fluorescence spectrometer with slit and filter design history, cross-scenario sample testing, printing parameters, BOM and source code, driven by named stakeholder feedback. The wiki is large and polished but has housekeeping failures - the attributions and collaborations pages both serve duplicated project-overview text, and the model page is unedited iGEM template text.

screen.project_title: MelanoShield — melanin-shielded Bt biopesticide co-produced in one E. coli chassis
screen.what_they_built: An engineered E. coli that co-produces the Bt insecticidal protein Cry1A(c) and UV-absorbing melanin from glucose in a single chassis, so the pigment shields the toxin from sunlight, plus a model-guided MelA tyrosinase variant, a chitinase-Cry fusion to breach the insect peritrophic matrix, and two hardware devices.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) for module building and W3110(DE3) (selected for phenolic-stress tolerance) as the production chassis, with melA integrated at the chromosomal poxB locus by CRISPR-Cas9; pET-24a(+) and pET-28a(+). Around twenty new Registry parts including BBa_26RAI01L (PT7-lacO-cry1A(c)), BBa_26C847O2, BBa_26YJQ7UU (melA cassette), BBa_26OJUQDJ, BBa_26EZQ4CF (pTargetF-poxB) and BBa_26JNDBJ7.
screen.best_evidence: /wet-lab/results and /engineering: melanin extracted from the recombinant fermentation blocked ~95.4% of 200-400 nm UV at 0.05 g/L and near 100% above 0.1 g/L (T = 10^-A conversion, solvent blank); the melA-integrated W3110(DE3) strain reached 1.91 ± 0.02 g/L melanin with 2.0 g/L tyrosine (0.18 ± 0.05 g/L without), and the co-producing strain still made 1.80 g/L melanin alongside a strong insoluble ~69 kDa Cry1A(c) band on SDS-PAGE. The liposome Cy5-release assay gave 45.4 ± 1.4% to 52.1 ± 1.7% release for Bt at 5-100 µg/mL and separated the two fusion linkers, (EAAAK)3 at 49.6 ± 3.0% vs (GGGGS)2 at 43.0 ± 1.5% at 90 min (P = 0.028, n = 3).
screen.hp_integration: Yes and decisively — a Jiangnan University industrial-biotech professor argued that fermenting and mixing two strains would raise equipment, labour and material costs, which turned the project from "two strains, two fermentations" into "one chassis, two functions" and then prompted the phenolic-stress chassis comparison; farmer and distributor interviews reshaped the monitoring hardware and questioned the usefulness of traps.
screen.reason: Five engineering cycles each closed with data, including a CRISPR chromosomal integration, a measured production trade-off when functions were combined, a computationally prioritised MelA variant that was actually built and tested, and an informative negative on fusion expression. The epistemic discipline is unusual — the team repeatedly separates what the model predicts from what the data show. Weak points a full read must check: the attributions page is effectively empty (54 words), there is no insect bioassay, and the W144K improvement (0.55 to 0.63 g/L) is not shown to be significant.
screen.field_notes: Shanghai high school team (NACIS, Agriculture village) that started from caterpillar damage in their own pesticide-free school garden and identified Plutella xylostella. Module 1 expressed Cry1A(c) in BL21(DE3) (SDS-PAGE ~69 kDa, mostly insoluble, which they argue aids enrichment and is compatible with alkaline midgut solubilisation). Module 2 expressed MelA tyrosinase from Rhizobium mulingense and measured UV blocking of extracted melanin across 0.05-1 g/L. Module 3 moved to W3110(DE3) after comparing BL21, MG1655 and W3110 growth in tyrosol, used CHOPCHOP-designed sgRNA and pTargetF to integrate melA at poxB (chosen to cut acetate accumulation), then added pET24a-cry1A(c) for co-production. Module 4 used an ESM-2 zero-shot screen revised after a failed first round, then structure confidence plus L-tyrosine docking plus 100 ns apo MD to shortlist W144K, W153P and T248L; W144K was built and gave a 14.5% mean titer increase. Module 5 fused SmChiA to Cry1A(c) with (GGGGS)2 or (EAAAK)3 linkers chosen by Chai Discovery RMSD; neither fusion gave a visible ~131 kDa band but both retained membrane-permeabilising activity in a Cy5-liposome assay. Hardware: a UV photostability demonstration box with cloud monitoring and a LoRa/K230 field insect-counting terminal with heatmaps, both documented at length (8.8k words) with explicit verification boundaries. HP uses a PARE framework across eleven logged stakeholders. Wiki navigation is duplicated on every page and there are frequent typos; the attributions page has no content.

screen.project_title: AI de novo redesign of terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase for thermostable enzymatic DNA synthesis
screen.what_they_built: A de novo protein design pipeline that rebuilt the flexible DNA-binding region of TdT to improve thermostability and accommodate bulky oxyamino-modified nucleotides, aimed at enzymatic DNA writing for DNA data storage.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with pET-28a(+); genes fully synthesised by GenScript. Parts: BBa_263ET0E5, BBa_266N6QG1, BBa_26BMB5EM, BBa_26DIWVPI, BBa_26NOOCP1, BBa_26YHUEKK, plus BBa_B0034.
screen.best_evidence: /results: of 85 designed sequences, 25 expressed (SDS-PAGE, Figure 8), and in urea-PAGE incorporation assays designed variant 7_813_83 retained normal activity on oxyamino-modified dNTPs after 30 min at both 45 C and 50 C where wild-type TdT lost activity, and still showed residual natural-dNTP activity after 5 min at 55 C (Tables 2-9).
screen.hp_integration: Partly: an explicit ASK-LISTEN-REFLECT-INTEGRATE-EVALUATE framework with four milestones, and interviews on IP ownership of AI-designed proteins and on the sustainability of enzymatic synthesis; the pack shows these shaping framing and commercialisation thinking more than the enzyme design itself.
screen.reason: This is the rarest thing in a high school pack: a de novo designed protein that measurably outperforms wild type at the bench. Seven named DBTL cycles run computation into experiment and back, 85 designs were synthesised and 25 expressed, and the lead variant beats WT on the hardest substrate at 50 C with MD giving a coherent mechanism. Worth a full read, with two things for the panel to probe: the activity data are reported as active/weak/normal categories rather than quantified kinetics, and there is no Attributions page at all, so the student-versus-outsourced split (GenScript synthesis, large compute) cannot be checked from the wiki.
screen.field_notes: NBJF (USA, Biomanufacturing village) tackled DNA data storage by redesigning terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase for thermostability and tolerance of bulky oxyamino-modified nucleotides. The pipeline ran RFdiffusion (7,000 backbones) through ProteinMPNN and ESMFold (82 backbones at pLDDT > 80, RMSD < 2 A), LigandMPNN inverse folding (8,200 sequences, 2,250 retained), then TemStaPro (1,609 predicted stable above 80 C) and Foldseek/SaProt (85 finalists), using a carbon-atom placeholder strategy to preserve DNA and modified-nucleotide space while retaining ~150 catalytic residues. GenScript synthesised all 85 plus WT; 25 expressed in BL21(DE3) by SDS-PAGE, and urea-PAGE incorporation assays across 30-55 C identified 7_813_83 as the lead, retaining normal oxyamino-dNTP activity after 30 min at 45 and 50 C where WT failed, and residual natural-dNTP activity after 5 min at 55 C. Long-timescale MD at 300/350/400 K supports the mechanism: lower RMSD and RMSF, stable DSSP content, more internal hydrogen bonds and a tighter free-energy landscape for the designed protein, with the flexible loop replaced by a compact multi-helix bundle. Seven explicit DBTL cycles, six TdT parts submitted, a 17,589-word engineering page, and an HP programme covering IP in AI-designed proteins and sustainability of enzymatic synthesis. No attributions page exists on the wiki, and the functional data are categorical rather than kinetic.

screen.project_title: From bottle, back to bottle — FAST-PETase engineering plus EnzAdapt enzyme-property prediction and photoprotective PET copolyesters
screen.what_they_built: Two mutation-discovery routes into FAST-PETase (a GVP-GNN structure-aware screen giving Y87Q and docking-based active-site design giving S187Y), validated on PET films, plus a deep-learning model (EnzAdapt) predicting Tm, Topt and pHopt, plus synthesis of pyrrolidone-aromatic copolyesters for UV/blue-light shielding.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with pET-22b(+)-FAST-PETase, Ni-NTA purification; no BBa part IDs appear anywhere on the wiki and there is no parts page.
screen.best_evidence: /results-wet-lab §1-2: purified Y87Q releases about 1.9-fold more soluble product than parental FAST-PETase at 60 C and 4.9-fold more at 70 C with 120 h time courses, and S187Y gives 2.18-fold higher PET-film hydrolysis (3.44-fold in the ThermoStable-PETase scaffold), both confirmed by UPLC quantification of MHET and TPA rather than A260 alone.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — an AREA-framework programme (11,442 words) with recycling firms and scientists in Shanghai reframed enzymatic hydrolysis as a complement to mechanical recycling rather than a universal solution, and the team states plainly that it has not processed contaminated real-world waste.
screen.reason: The data are the strongest in this batch on paper — product-verified multi-fold activity gains in two scaffolds, a benchmarked ML model, and MD/PRS/DFT/DIAS mechanistic analysis. But the work is at published-paper level (melt polycondensation, GPC, 2D HSQC, HRMS, DFT) with an attributions page that is only a link to the iGEM form, and there are no Registry parts at all. Worth a full read mainly so the panel can test aspect 6 (who did this) and aspect 7/8 (no standard components documented); if attribution does not hold up, the score collapses.
screen.field_notes: NEBS-VCA (Software & AI, CHN) ran a PET-recycling project with three strands. Wet lab: site-directed mutants of FAST-PETase expressed in BL21(DE3) and Ni-NTA purified, assayed on amorphous PET films at 40-70 C with A260 screening and UPLC quantification of MHET and TPA; Y87Q (found by a GVP-GNN second-shell screen on PDB 7SH6) gave about 1.9-fold more soluble product at 60 C and 4.9-fold at 70 C, and S187Y (found by docking of active-site variants among nine screened) gave 2.18-fold in FAST-PETase and 3.44-fold in a ThermoStable-PETase scaffold. Dry lab: EnzAdapt, a CG-MoE/ESM-2 hybrid predicting Tm, Topt and pHopt, reported on deduplicated benchmarks as R2 0.823 / RMSE 5.30 C for Tm, R2 0.615 / 11.58 C for Topt and R2 0.536 / 0.789 pH units for pHopt across three seeds, with residual, sequence-identity and EC-class robustness analyses. A third strand synthesised P-BPDA pyrrolidone-benzene monomer into PEPT and PETGP copolyesters (NMR, FT-IR, GPC Mn >32 kDa) achieving 98.2% UV and 87.6% blue-light blocking at 10 mol% while keeping 81.2% visible transmittance, with DFT HOMO-LUMO gaps rationalising the effect. Engineering is organised as three DBTL cycles with an explicit Diagnose phase using MD, pre-reaction-state geometry, DFT cluster models and DIAS decomposition. Human practices follows an AREA cycle with recycling companies in Shanghai. Red flags for judging: no BBa parts anywhere, an attributions page that is only an external link, and material-science work far beyond normal high-school lab access.

screen.project_title: Crocetin cell factory: de novo crocetin biosynthesis in E. coli with semi-rational CCD engineering
screen.what_they_built: An eight-gene crocetin pathway (idi, CrtE, CrtB, CrtI, CrtY, CrtZ, CCD, ALD) reconstructed in E. coli BL21(DE3), first as two plasmids and then consolidated onto one pETDuet backbone, followed by three point mutants of the rate-limiting cleavage dioxygenase CsCCD2.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); pACCAR25-deltacrtX (provided by a professor) plus pET-CCD-ALD, consolidated into pET-Ds-Cro. 12 new BBa entries plus reused parts; all plasmids and the three mutants were synthesised by GenScript.
screen.best_evidence: /results: HPLC chromatograms show crocetin plus residual zeaxanthin in the two-plasmid strain and reduced zeaxanthin in the single-plasmid strain, with a calibration-curve yield of 2.37 µg/g DCW; mutant comparison at two induction temperatures gives N366G at 113% of wild-type (2.68 µg/g) at 20 C, with D253G and Q283P at 63% and 66%.
screen.hp_integration: Some. Human practices (3.5k words) and an iHP page are present and the project narrative links saffron scarcity and student stress to the product concept, but no specific design change is clearly traced back to a stakeholder in the screening pack.
screen.reason: A clean, logical three-step engineering story (two-plasmid proof, single-plasmid consolidation, mutant screen) with HPLC quantification, but the attribution picture is the problem: the attributions page is empty, plasmid 1 came from a named professor and every construct including all three mutants was synthesised commercially by GenScript, so very little of the build was done by the students. Yields are also minute (2.37 µg/g DCW) and the mutant improvement (113% of wild type) is reported only in relative terms without replicates or error bars. Several standard pages (team, education, experiments, attributions) are empty and jQuery code leaks into the rendered text.
screen.field_notes: NFLSHS-China (Biomanufacturing, China) engineers E. coli into a crocetin cell factory to replace saffron harvesting. The full route from endogenous IPP through DMAPP, GGPP, phytoene, lycopene, beta-carotene and zeaxanthin to crocetin dialdehyde and crocetin uses idi, CrtE, CrtB, CrtI, CrtY, CrtZ, a Crocus sativus cleavage dioxygenase CsCCD2 and an aldehyde dehydrogenase. A two-plasmid system (pACCAR25-deltacrtX, provided by Professor Wang, plus a GenScript-synthesised pET-CCD-ALD) produced crocetin by HPLC but left a large zeaxanthin peak; the eight genes were then consolidated onto pETDuet-1 as pET-Ds-Cro under two T7 promoters, which reduced residual zeaxanthin and gave 2.37 µg/g DCW. Identifying CCD as rate-limiting, the team docked mutants against zeaxanthin and picked D253G, Q283P and N366G (Vina scores -10.2 to -10.7 kcal/mol); N366G reached 113% of wild-type crocetin (2.68 µg/g) at 20 C induction, while the other two fell to 63-66%, and all strains did better at 20 C than 25 C. Twelve BBa entries are listed and a detailed notebook (5.1k words) and 6.7k-word entrepreneurship section exist. Serious documentation gaps: the attributions page renders empty, the team, education, experiments and protocol standard pages are empty or thin, every plasmid and mutant was commercially synthesised, and raw jQuery handlers appear in the page text.

screen.project_title: MiRVOX: Pulmora (miRNA toehold switch) + OncoNose (breath e-nose)
screen.what_they_built: A cell-free toehold-switch assay for a microRNA lung-cancer biomarker (retargeted to C. elegans cel-miR-39-3p for whitelist reasons) with sfGFP readout, plus an exploratory low-cost MOS-sensor electronic nose for breath VOCs. Seven synthetic oligos registered as parts and a Python stem-loop RT-PCR primer designer.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Cell-free (PURExpress) rather than a living chassis; 7 registered synthetic oligonucleotide parts (BBa_260MKHLC target, BBa_26IZFICR stem-loop RT primer, BBa_26PRKBLC T7 forward primer, BBa_263U40RB reverse, plus three controls) and BBa_J23100 referenced.
screen.best_evidence: There is none. /results states plainly: "No experimental results have been produced yet. This page is built and empty, not padded." with all four hypotheses marked "No data yet"; /contribution confirms "Two practical iterations completed and failed; iteration 3 pending. The PURExpress run has NOT been performed." The strongest real finding is the computational one on /model: 69 accepted primer pairs with T7 on the forward primer, none with T7 on the reverse, benchmarked on 20 C. elegans miRNAs.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in part and honestly logged: a table on /human-practices records that Prof. Keith Pardee proposed EXPAR and the team compared it with PCR and kept PCR, and that UTokyo's challenge on detecting up- and down-regulated miRNAs set three follow-up directions; but much of the page is prospective ("who we need to hear from", questions published before the conversations).
screen.reason: Exemplary honesty and an unusually well-referenced, well-navigated wiki (judging guide page, per-source citation map), but aspect 2 is near zero: no wet-lab result exists, the cell-free run was never performed, and two attempted iterations failed. Finalists are chosen largely on whether the project worked; a team with an explicitly empty results page cannot be top-2 however good the writing.
screen.field_notes: Kazakh high-school team (Oncology village) tackling lung-cancer triage in a TB-endemic country, where imaging cannot separate malignant from benign lesions. Two arms: Pulmora, a cell-free reverse-logic toehold switch reading a miRNA via stem-loop RT-PCR with sfGFP output, and OncoNose, a MOS-sensor breath e-nose at prototype v0.1. Target swapped from human miR-21 to C. elegans cel-miR-39-3p because iGEM's White List bars human-gene miRNAs without a Check-In a high-school team cannot file. No experimental data at all: NASBA plateaued at every concentration and a T7 promoter carrying only one initiating G gave almost no transcript, and the PURExpress run was never done; the team says so explicitly rather than padding. Real dry-lab output: a Python stem-loop RT-PCR primer designer that enforces complete-target preservation, benchmarked on 20 miRNAs, open source in the team GitLab. Notably strong reference discipline, including two self-corrections of their own literature reading (a five-miRNA panel paper whose stated list and results disagree).

screen.project_title: ChemoGuard: seven-locus DPYD qPCR panel for fluoropyrimidine toxicity risk
screen.what_they_built: A modular TaqMan qPCR panel covering the seven Tier 1 DPYD loci (rs75017182, rs3918290, rs55886062, rs67376798, rs115232898, rs146356975, rs112766203), with 14 primers and 22 allele-specific probes, intended as a pre-chemotherapy pharmacogenetic test in Kazakhstan.
screen.chassis_and_parts: No living chassis; the project is oligonucleotide and assay design. 56 basic parts registered: primers, single-stranded hydrolysis probes and double-stranded DPYD allele control templates.
screen.best_evidence: /results: final run at 63 C, 30 uL reactions, three technical replicates plus NTC per locus - 66/66 expected positive fluorescence signals across 22 probes, 7/7 NTCs with no Cq, and per-channel Cq means with SD (only rs75017182 HEX exceeded 1 cycle SD at 1.68). /engineering records the ROX probe titration that cut end-point background from 330 to 13.4 RFU for rs3918290.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, strongly on implementation rather than on the molecular design: Karen Merritt of Advocates for Universal DPD/DPYD Testing argued the test must be built into the standard patient pathway rather than requested by patients, which changed the team's deployment model, and her advice on interactive materials drove the VR and board games.
screen.reason: Honest, well-controlled work, but the team states plainly that the run used pooled allelic templates and therefore demonstrates assay functionality only - not allelic specificity, genotyping accuracy, LOD or reproducibility - so the diagnostic claim itself is unvalidated. Synthetic biology content is thin: the parts are primers, probes and control templates rather than designed biological systems, and there is no model, software or circuit. The wiki is one of the best-designed in the batch and the HP is genuinely moving, but Project is the main determinant and it sits around a strong medal rather than top-2.
screen.field_notes: NIS-Kazakhstan (KAZ, Diagnostics) built ChemoGuard, a seven-locus TaqMan qPCR panel for DPYD variants that predict severe 5-fluorouracil and capecitabine toxicity, motivated by the absence of routine pre-chemotherapy pharmacogenetic testing in Kazakhstan. They designed and synthesised 36 oligonucleotides (14 flanking primers, 22 allele-specific probes across FAM/ROX/HEX/Cy5) and 22 synthetic double-stranded allele control templates, all registered as 56 basic parts. Four test runs: an early run that showed spurious ROX signal on reference DNA, a 61-64.2 C annealing gradient, a ROX probe titration that cut background roughly 25-fold, and a final run at 63 C giving 66/66 positive signals in triplicate with 7/7 clean NTCs and per-channel Cq SDs listed. The team explicitly scopes out allelic specificity, LOD, between-run reproducibility and Kazakh variant frequencies as future work. HP is built around an interview with Karen Merritt (AUDT co-founder, who lost her mother to fluoropyrimidine toxicity) and reframed the product from an optional test to one embedded in the standard patient pathway; education includes a VR game and a board game. The attributions page credits a secondary PI with securing the lab, supervising all experiments and guiding protocols, which is worth weighing on aspect 6. Strong front-end wiki design with an interactive 'Try it' playground; no model page.

screen.project_title: ProbioRegulon / Mordilac - probiotic delivery of a modified mcIRBP-19 bitter-gourd peptide
screen.what_they_built: A design for Lactobacillus paracasei (validated first in E. coli) secreting a modified 18-residue mcIRBP-19 insulin-receptor-binding peptide from bitter gourd via a Usp45 signal, intended as a probiotic drink for early-stage type 2 diabetes.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli (NEB Stable) as the test host, L. paracasei as the intended chassis; Usp45 signal peptide, GST fusion, three GenScript-synthesised constructs; only three new BBa IDs appear and none is experimentally characterised.
screen.best_evidence: /results: a pre-project alpha-amylase inhibition assay on bitter gourd extract is the only real wet-lab dataset (flesh extract R2 = 0.995, one-way ANOVA p < 0.001, F = 491.2, matching acarbose at 60% and exceeding it at 80-100%, p < 0.001). The project's own constructs got as far as transformation with clean no-DNA controls and a miniprep gel matching vendor QC bands; the Cycle 3 expression SDS-PAGE is explicitly labelled 'Proposed; not yet performed'.
screen.hp_integration: Stakeholder work is described and the product concept (a probiotic drink rather than an injectable) is shaped by it, but no documented conversation visibly changed a construct or an experiment.
screen.reason: Intellectually the most self-critical wiki in the batch - scramble controls in docking, an ipTM separation they refuse to call binding, a COPASI model cross-checked in SciPy to four significant figures - but the engineered system was never shown to work. Expression was not performed, no part was characterised, and the only strong experimental dataset is a plant-extract assay predating the project. Aspect 2 cannot be scored above 'planned', so it cannot reach top-2 on the Project section.
screen.field_notes: NPSI Singapore (Food & Nutrition) designed 'Mordilac', an engineered Lactobacillus paracasei to secrete a modified mcIRBP-19 peptide from bitter gourd for blood-glucose regulation, prototyping the coding sequence in E. coli first. The dry lab is unusually rigorous for a high school team: SignalP 6.0 cleavage prediction for a direct Usp45 fusion versus a LEISSTCDA propeptide variant, ColabFold structures with per-residue pLDDT and MSA-depth caveats (only 2 homologues for the invented 18-mer), Kabsch backbone superposition (RMSD 2.98 A overall, 0.91 A over GIVAR, with an explicit warning that the 0.91 A figure proves nothing), HPEPDOCK docking with composition-matched scrambles that interleave with the designed peptides, AlphaFold3 ipTM giving the first clean designed-versus-scramble separation (0.38-0.43 vs 0.31-0.36) while still below the 0.6 reliability threshold, and a COPASI two-branch insulin-signalling model (peak 2.51-fold early uptake, decaying to ~1% by 100 s) re-integrated independently in SciPy. Wet lab, by contrast, stops early: a strong pre-project alpha-amylase inhibition study on bitter gourd extract (flesh R2 = 0.995, ANOVA p < 0.001, exceeding acarbose at 80-100%), then transformation of three synthesised constructs with clean no-DNA controls and a miniprep gel, with a suspected plasmid dimer in Gene 2 and an untested ScaI digest planned. Expression, secretion and any functional assay are marked proposed. The wiki is an excellent model of honest reporting and would be a useful record for future teams, but there is no working part.

screen.project_title: BioChronos - a DNA memory recorder for intermittent water contamination
screen.what_they_built: A planned two-module recording biosensor: a CueR copper-responsive promoter driving sfGFP (M1) and a Bxb1 integrase cassette that latches by inverting DNA (M2U untagged, M2L with LVA tag); the module joining the copper sensor to the integrase was designed but never built.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a, pTwist Amp Medium Copy backbone, Gibson assembly from Twist fragments; parts include M1 BBa_26QKL23N, M2U BBa_26LANJSF, M2L BBa_26HJC5Z5 built on BBa_K190017, BBa_B0032 and BBa_B0015. None of the clones was sequence-verified.
screen.best_evidence: /results, the single assay of 14 October 2026: M1 fluorescence rose 2.08-fold at 1000 uM CuSO4 over 183 min across three independent colonies (118.7 vs 57.1 RFU), with no increase detected from 1 to 200 uM against a stated 1.22-fold detection limit, and the team records that there was no plasmid-free control, no pre-induction baseline, no technical replicates and no sequence confirmation. The M2 inversion modules were never characterised.
screen.hp_integration: Limited - the team set out to ask water managers whether a did-it-happen record is useful, but records that the water authority they approached never replied, and the sampling-interval rationale comes from statute rather than a stakeholder conversation.
screen.reason: The most intellectually honest wiki in the batch - provenance for every number, limitations written harder than the results, five closed DBTL cycles including two that cancelled experiments, and a serious accessibility system - but the project itself produced one preliminary, uncontrolled, unsequenced reporter assay responding only at 1000 uM, and the memory modules that define the project were never tested. Project is the main determinant for finalists, so no. Flag instead for Best Wiki, Best Model and Best Education consideration.
screen.field_notes: Oakridge-HYD (India/multi-country, Bioremediation village) proposed BioChronos, a recording rather than reporting water sensor: copper exposure would drive Bxb1 integrase to invert a DNA cassette, latching a one-bit record readable at the next scheduled site visit. Three modules were assembled from Twist fragments by Gibson into a pTwist Amp backbone after the planned Kan backbone was unavailable; none was sequence-confirmed. Only one assay was run (14 Oct 2026): M1 reporter fluorescence rose 2.08-fold at 1000 uM CuSO4 across three colonies, flat from 1 to 200 uM, with the team itself listing the missing plasmid-free control, missing pre-induction read, single blank wells, plate-edge light leakage and out-of-range OD values. The inversion modules M2U and M2L were never characterised, and Module 3 (copper sensor to integrase) exists only as a design. Five DBTL cycles are documented, three of them dry-lab, including one where the team's own data broke a literature K = 5 uM parameter (re-grounded to a 492-2724 uM bound) and one that withdrew a planned readout. Dry lab is substantial: model design, inference and history pages total ~15k words, plus a rederivation script and downloadable data tables. The wiki has a per-page documentation-status banner, full citation of primary sources including Bonnet et al. 2012, and a built-in accessibility panel (dyslexia, low vision, epilepsy, ADHD modes). Exemplary record-keeping, very thin bench result.

screen.project_title: Four-promoter whole-cell biosensor for early warning of Aspergillus flavus in stored maize and peanuts
screen.what_they_built: Four E. coli whole-cell biosensors in which VOC-responsive promoters (hipB, dkgB, evgA, elfA) drive the luxCDABE autoluminescence operon, immobilised in calcium-alginate microbeads and read out by a smartphone long-exposure dark box, giving staged warnings for early infection versus toxigenic stage in maize and peanuts.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli K-12 MG1655 (promoter source), DH5alpha (cloning), Rosetta (expression); pGEN-luxCDABE backbone (Addgene #44918). Parts: BBa_267CCUUV hipB, BBa_26W1GDJQ dkgB, BBa_26E0Z... evgA, BBa_26M2OFZE elfA promoters, plus a blue-light suicide system (BBa_26TDUTC0 OptoLacI-LW220F, BBa_265NC3H5 AsLOV2) using BBa_K5363015 PhiX174E; reuses BBa_K3769103 luxCDABE.
screen.best_evidence: /results §4: microplate-reader induction factors with triplicates and p-values — hipB 9.1x (SD 3.82, p=0.017), dkgB 27.9x (p=0.0017), evgA 25.0x (p=0.00098), elfA 14.8x (p=0.0018) against a 2.1-fold positive threshold. §5: smartphone grayscale induction factor versus plate-reader RLU across seven VOC concentrations (0-200 ug/L), linear regression R²=0.9717 with 100% concordant positive/negative calls. §7: microbead activity retention 91-94% at 1 d, 82-87% at 3 d, 70-76% at 7 d at -20 C.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, repeatedly — a synthetic biology expert's biosafety concern added the blue-light-inducible suicide plasmid, grain-depot field visits and an optics expert drove three hardware generations ending in the smartphone long-exposure dark box, and customs/agronomy input split the product into a fixed warehouse array and a portable version.
screen.reason: Strongest pack in this batch and the clearest candidate for a full read. Four functioning parts with replicated, significant induction data; a second orthogonal readout (chemiluminescence imaging) agreeing with the plate reader; a low-cost hardware route validated against the lab instrument with R²=0.9717; honest negative real-sample results (natto and clean depot grain all below threshold, with natto cross-reactivity discussed rather than hidden); storage stability; a modelled three-tier warning rule; a biocontainment part added because of stakeholder input; and an unusually complete page set. Two caveats for the panel: no positive real sample was ever tested (chemically simulated VOCs stand in for live A. flavus), and the attributions page is missing, so aspect 6 is unverified.
screen.field_notes: OTIA-Hangzhou (Agriculture, China) built four whole-cell biosensors that detect Aspergillus flavus infection of stored maize and peanuts by sensing stage-specific volatile organic compounds rather than the fungus itself. Four E. coli K-12 promoters screened from transcriptomic data (hipB and evgA for early infection, dkgB and elfA for the toxigenic stage) were cloned upstream of luxCDABE in pGEN-luxCDABE, sequence-verified at 100% identity, expressed in E. coli Rosetta and immobilised as ~2 mm calcium-alginate microbeads. Under headspace challenge with defined VOC mixtures, all four gave significant induction (9.1x to 27.9x, n=3, p<0.02) above a 2.1-fold threshold, corroborated by SDS-PAGE intensification of Lux subunit bands and by chemiluminescence imaging that scaled with VOC dose. A custom light-tight smartphone dark box reproduced plate-reader RLU with R²=0.9717 over seven concentrations and 100% concordant calls, after three hardware generations (photoresistor, photodiode, smartphone long exposure) and a GrainLens Android app. Real samples (natto as a VOC-rich source, plus wheat, peanut and maize from grain depots) all fell below the positive threshold, reported honestly as partial VOC overlap and clean grain. Microbeads retained 70-76% activity after 7 days at -20 C. Parts also include a blue-light-inducible OptoLacI/AsLOV2-PhiX174E suicide system added after biosafety advice. Extensive four-stage IHP (196-response consumer survey, depot staff, farmers, mycology, optics, 3D-printing and customs experts) and a modelling page converting luminescence into three-tier AFB1 warnings. No attributions page.

screen.project_title: COLOPRINT — tumour-microenvironment-triggered probiotic therapy for colorectal cancer, delivered by 3D-bioprinted pills
screen.what_they_built: An E. coli Nissle-targeted three-module system (hypoxia/formate-gated therapeutic payloads, Lpp-OmpA nanobody adhesion, essential-gene kill switch plus barcoded reporters), characterized in DH5a, alongside COLOPrinter — a low-cost open-source four-material bioprinter with an aseptic isolator and G-code translator — and an erosion/release simulation of the printed pill.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for characterization, E. coli Nissle 1917 as the intended therapeutic chassis. ~24 new 2026 BBa parts (basic: yCD-M100H BBa_26599PUP, tilS BBa_26GLV9ZI, three FNR hypoxia promoters, two anti-PD-L1 nanobodies; plus composite generators and kill switches), built on registry standards J23100/J23118/B0034/B0015 and reusing BBa_K811000, BBa_K3482035, BBa_K2120006.
screen.best_evidence: /results 1.2: the three FNR hypoxia promoters driving yCD-M100H give hypoxia/normoxia ON-OFF ratios of 5.7 (PfbsrhaB-42, p<0.01), 3.6 and 1.8 against a 0.22 control baseline, with 30-min kinetics; /results 1.7: LDH assay on CT26 cells gives 54.80% cytotoxicity for ClyA (n=3) against PBS 0% and lysis buffer 100%.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — the team's own 'ECOLI' loop is tied to specific design changes, e.g. cancer-survivor consultations about systemic 5-FU toxicity drove the switch to a localized 5-FC prodrug system, and a specialist consultation drove the 3xGS linker choice in the nanobody display.
screen.reason: Large set of genuinely new, quantitatively characterized parts with statistics, controls and honestly reported failures (flat GFP reporter, dead formate promoter, anomalous LDH values, contaminated MC38 line), plus real hardware and modelling. This is the profile the handbook rewards; it deserves a full panel read.
screen.field_notes: PLKLFC (Oncology, HKG) built COLOPRINT: tumour-gated therapeutic E. coli Nissle delivered in a 3D-bioprinted hydrogel pill. They contributed about 24 new parts including yCD-M100H (BBa_26599PUP), three FNR-dependent hypoxia promoters, two Lpp-OmpA anti-PD-L1 nanobodies and tyrS/tilS essential-gene kill switches. Key quantitative results: yCD-M100H gave a statistically significant 29.71% activity gain over wild-type yCD in vivo by phenol-red assay (vs a 2-fold claim for purified enzyme in the source paper); PfbsrhaB(-42) gave the best hypoxia ON-OFF ratio of 5.7 (p<0.01); ClyA produced 54.80% LDH cytotoxicity on CT26 cells (n=3); and amilCP/sfGFP reporters carried a Sanger-verified 24-base ASCII-to-DNA 'PLKLFC' barcode. Negative and anomalous results are reported honestly: no hypoxia response from the sfGFP reporter (attributed to oxygen-dependent chromophore maturation, with a mandatory post-induction aeration recommendation for future teams), no formate response from PfdhF (attributed to NarL/NarP repression in LB), negative LDH values for Azurin and yCD attributed to poor His-tag yield, adhesion imaging that is explicitly observational only, and an MC38 line lost to contamination. Hardware is COLOPrinter, a modified budget printer co-extruding four hydrogels with a custom aseptic isolator, open CAD and a setup guide; the model couples AlphaFold2 linker analysis to an EDT/marching-cubes pill-erosion simulation claiming a 38.8% higher colon delivery score for a gyroid geometry. Human practices run through the team's own ECOLI framework. Weak spots: no attributions page, no measurement or education page, and human cell lines barred by institutional policy.

justification.a1: The scope is unusually large for a high school team and the results build on one another: a new prodrug enzyme characterised against a wild-type control, then placed under three new hypoxia promoters, then re-reported with sfGFP, then extended to a formate AND-gate (Results 1.1-1.4), alongside two novel essential-gene kill switches, barcoded reporters, three printer prototypes and two software tools. What keeps it off a 5 is that the capstone claim - engineered bacteria binding and killing colorectal cancer cells - is the weakest link: adhesion is observational only (Results 2.1) and only ClyA produced measurable cytotoxicity (Results 1.7).
justification.a2: Several modules are shown to work against real controls: yCD-M100H vs wild-type yCD vs native DH5-alpha, 29.71% higher activity at p<0.05 (Results 1.1); three hypoxia promoters with normoxic controls, ON/OFF ratios of 5.7, 3.6 and 1.8 against a 0.22 baseline and a 30-minute kinetic series (Results 1.2); kill switches benchmarked against BBa_K2120006 and a plasmid-free control over 12 h with an arabinose dose series (Results 3.2); ClyA at 54.8% cytotoxicity with PBS and max-lysis controls, n=3 (Results 1.7). Against that, the integrated therapeutic is not demonstrated: 5-FC/5-FU killing of CT26 failed, four treatment groups returned negative cytotoxicity that the team cannot explain, and replicate numbers and error-bar definitions are stated only for the LDH table.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and genuinely stakeholder-shaped - oncology nurses drove pill ergonomics, gastroenterologists drove a non-lytic containment choice, and sewage engineers produced a stool disinfection protocol (Human Practices cycles 8, 9, 12). The open-source COLOPrinter and setup guides are a concrete accessibility contribution for low-resource labs (Hardware, Setup Guides). Impact remains projected rather than tested, though: the cost figures are from literature (Description) and the delivery performance comes from simulation, not from a dissolution experiment (Model II).
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Test results repeatedly change the next design: the live co-culture collapsed on growth-rate mismatch and was redesigned into purified-protein treatment (Engineering, Payload Cycle III); the GFP null result produced a mandatory aeration step (Biosensor Cycle II); the formate null result produced a reasoned conclusion that an orthogonal synthetic promoter is needed (Biosensor Cycle III); printer V2's quantified failures - wiring fatigue, swap latency, calibration drift - drove the V3 rotary turret (Hardware, Prototypes 2 and 3). Measures of success are stated before testing (ON/OFF ratio, offset distance, extrusion multiplier, Colon Delivery Score), which is what separates this from troubleshooting.
justification.a5: Seventeen documented cycles under the team's own ECOLI framework, each naming a stakeholder and a resulting design change: Dr Wang's critique produced the formate AND-gate, Dr Ma's advice produced the AlphaFold-guided linker and the dual-promoter cassette, Dr Tang produced amilCP then sfGFP for endoscopy, Dr Tse produced the tyrS/tilS switches, and Prof Ngo's freedom-to-operate warning led the team to abandon the NB4 nanobody and withhold it from the Registry (Human Practices, cycles 2-7 and 12-15). This is two-way dialogue shaping both biology and hardware, at the level the handbook describes for a Grand Prize team. The only reservation is that the underlying survey and interview materials sit on Google Drive, off the team namespace.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page - https://2026.igem.wiki/plklfc/attributions returns 404 - so the only attribution is the role list on the Team page, which is per-person but not task-level for the experiments. Outsourcing that is declared is handled well: Twist synthesised all constructs and Tech Dragon did the Sanger sequencing (Experiments 1.1, 2.2). What is not stated is who actually performed the murine cell culture, the His-tag purification and the Leica THUNDER confocal imaging, which for a secondary school raises the question of host-lab or instructor execution; the Safety page says only that students work under teacher supervision.
justification.a7: The project is built squarely on Registry-compatible standard components: Anderson promoters J23100/J23114/J23118, RBS B0034, terminators B0015 and B1002, with reuse of BBa_K811000, BBa_K3482035, BBa_K2120006, BBa_K808000, BBa_K592009 and BBa_I746916, combined with around twenty new basic and composite parts of the team's own design (Parts). The modular Lpp-OmpA-3xGS backbone is explicitly offered as a swappable scaffold for future teams (Contribution I.1). It falls a half point short of 5 because assembly standards and RFC compatibility are never discussed - every construct was ordered as synthetic DNA rather than assembled.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is thorough and well cross-linked: the Parts page tabulates every new basic and composite part with a functional rationale, and Results and Engineering reference part numbers inline throughout. However, the handbook judges parts on the Registry entry alone, and every parts.igem.org request from here returned a CloudFront 403, so I could not confirm that the Registry entries carry the sequence features, controls and characterisation claimed on the wiki - I score what I could verify and would check this before the Jamboree. The notebook is only an embedded PDF with 119 words of page text, and several standard pages (attributions, measurement, proof-of-concept, implementation) are absent.
justification.w1: The Home page states the problem (colorectal cancer, with three named hurdles), the solution (COLOPRINT: engineered E. coli in bioprinted hydrogel pills) and the architecture (adhesion, killing, safety modules plus hardware and HP) within roughly one screen, each with a link onward. The Description page then repeats it as a four-step clinical pipeline. Some hedged phrasing ('aims to', 'is expected to') blurs what was achieved against what is proposed, which costs it a half point.
justification.w2: Most key claims are tied to a figure with controls - the WT-yCD comparison, the normoxia/hypoxia promoter pairs, the mazF benchmark, the before/after sterilisation plates with positive and negative controls. The gaps are real, though: replicate number is given only for the LDH table, error bars and statistical tests are asserted (p<0.05, p<0.01) but not defined anywhere, the adhesion result is a four-row table of microscope impressions, and the negative cytotoxicity values are reported without an assay-validity check. The team is commendably honest that the adhesion findings 'are purely observational and not quantitative' (Results 2.1).
justification.w3: Navigation is grouped sensibly into Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab and Parts, standard URLs are preserved for the pages that exist, and cross-links between Results, Engineering and Human Practices work well. Friction comes from the missing standard pages a judge goes looking for - attributions, measurement, proof-of-concept and implementation all 404 - and from the Engineering page running to nearly 10,000 words in one scroll with no in-page contents.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way: Experiments gives transformation, miniprep, LDH, phenol red, promoter characterisation, purification and SDS-PAGE protocols with concentrations and timings, the printer STLs and setup guides are published, the simulation code sits on iGEM GitLab, and failures (MC38 contamination, co-culture collapse, printer V2) are documented rather than hidden. What is missing is raw data - no plate-reader exports or numeric tables behind the curves - and a notebook that is only an embedded PDF rather than a dated record on the page.
justification.w5: Most pages carry numbered reference lists with resolvable DOIs and inline citation. But the Engineering page tags six references '(See audit note below)' or '(Corrected from composite entry; see audit note below)' and no audit note appears anywhere on that page, live or crawled. Checking those entries against PubMed, the coordinates given resolve to unrelated papers - Front Immunol 2019;10:1455 is a brain-endothelial microparticle study (https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2019.01455), Cell Death Dis 2020;11:592 is a miR-3622a-3p colorectal study (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41419-020-02789-z), Oncol Rep 2018;39:1235-1244 is a pituitary miR-16 study (https://doi.org/10.3892/or.2018.6227) - and the Follrich 2022 and Zhang 2021 entries do not resolve at all. I give no evidential weight to the claims resting on them and would raise the specific concern with rcc@igem.org; the RCC, not me, decides what it means.

J1.one_line: An exceptionally ambitious and largely well-controlled high school project - real promoter, enzyme and kill-switch characterisation plus three printer iterations and outstanding integrated HP - held back by an unproven targeting module and a reference list with several citations that do not resolve.
strengths: Genuine controlled characterisation across several modules: yCD-M100H against a wild-type and a native-strain control at p<0.05 (Results 1.1); three new hypoxia promoters with normoxic controls, ON/OFF ratios and 30-minute kinetics (Results 1.2); tyrS/tilS kill switches benchmarked against the Registry mazF part and a plasmid-free control over 12 h (Results 3.2).

Negative and failed results are reported and used: the GFP assay showing no hypoxia response with a reasoned maturation explanation, the formate AND-gate null attributed to NarL/NarP repression, the catastrophic live co-culture, and the MC38 contamination (Results 1.2-1.6, Engineering Payload Cycle III).

Hardware engineering with quantified measures of success: extrusion multiplier swept 0.5x to 7x to fix 300 um filament and optimal mechanical integrity, printer V2's failure modes itemised and answered by the V3 rotary turret (Hardware, Prototypes 1-3), with the 300 um value then feeding the dissolution model.

Integrated Human Practices of finalist quality: seventeen cycles each naming a stakeholder and a concrete design change, including abandoning the NB4 nanobody on freedom-to-operate grounds and switching from a bactericidal to a bacteriostatic switch on gastroenterologists' advice.

A coherent, reusable parts contribution - around twenty new basic and composite parts built on Anderson promoters, B0034 and B0015, with a swappable Lpp-OmpA-3xGS display backbone offered to future teams (Parts, Contribution I).
weaknesses: The central targeting claim is unproven. Adhesion rests on a four-row table of microscope impressions in which the two anti-PD-L1 constructs were 'similar to control' (Results 2.1); the team says so honestly, but the personalised-targeting platform therefore has no quantitative support.

The therapeutic system was never shown to work end to end: only ClyA killed CT26 cells, and the yCD-M100H/5-FC prodrug route - the part most tied to the patient-driven design - produced negative cytotoxicity values (-4.0%) that are explained by hypothesis rather than tested (Results 1.7).

Statistics are asserted rather than documented: p values appear for the promoter and enzyme work but replicate number, error-bar definition and the test used are given nowhere except the LDH table's n=3.

No Attributions page (404), so beyond the Team page role list there is no task-level account of who ran the mammalian cell culture, the His-tag purification or the confocal imaging - the pieces least typical of a secondary school lab.

Six Engineering references are tagged '(See audit note below)' with no audit note on the page, and PubMed lookups show several of those journal/volume/page coordinates belong to entirely different papers while two others do not resolve.
Supporting material sits off the iGEM namespace - all HP survey and interview materials on Google Drive, printer STLs on Thingiverse - which under the handbook's evidence rule cannot be judged.
red_flags: Six references on the Engineering page are flagged '(See audit note below)' or '(Corrected from composite entry)' but no audit note exists on the page. Verified against PubMed: Front Immunol 2019;10:1455 is a brain-endothelial microparticle paper (10.3389/fimmu.2019.01455), not the cited nanobody checkpoint study; Cell Death Dis 2020;11:592 is a miR-3622a-3p colorectal paper (10.1038/s41419-020-02789-z), not the cited IFN-gamma PD-L1 study; Oncol Rep 2018;39:1235-1244 is a pituitary miR-16 paper (10.3892/or.2018.6227), not the cited CXCR7 study; the Follrich 2022 Appl Environ Microbiol and Zhang 2021 Clin Colorectal Cancer entries do not resolve. I would email rcc@igem.org with these specifics and give no evidential credit to claims resting on them; the RCC decides, not me.

Every page footer carries a blanket statement that 'Some images on this website were generated by Google Gemini' with no indication of which images. Declaring AI image use is good practice, but as written it does not distinguish schematic artwork from the gels, plots and micrographs used as evidence, and the digital handbook treats AI-made or cleaned evidentiary figures as misconduct. A Q&A question rather than a finding.

Whitelist question for safety@igem.org, not for me to decide: the team cultured murine colorectal carcinoma lines CT26 and MC38, used Class II biosafety cabinets and refers to 'BSL-1 and BSL-2 protocols' on its Safety page. They state they avoided human cell lines and all in vivo work, but whether continuous animal cell lines fall inside the High School Whitelist needs a determination.
Parts could not be verified at source: every parts.igem.org request returned a CloudFront 403 from this environment, so the Registry entries behind the a8 score are unconfirmed.

The GFP protocol on the Experiments page (3.3) includes a one-hour post-incubation aeration step, while Results 1.3 says the protocol lacked one and blames the null result on its absence. Worth asking which version produced the reported data.
Notebook is a single embedded PDF (119 words of page text) and no raw numeric data are posted anywhere on the wiki.
pages_read: parts.igem.org Registry pages for BBa_26599PUP, BBa_26JHMPW8, BBa_26IS8VW3, BBa_26SLMCX1 (all returned HTTP 403, not readable)

calibrated.changed: none. w5 2.5 is the lowest on this ballot and stays there: six Engineering references point to papers that are not the cited work and two do not resolve, which is a different order of problem from the thin-citation cases (ZQT at 2.5 for whole pages with no references, SHSID at 3.0). The specifics go to rcc@igem.org; I give the dependent claims no evidential weight and do not score a penalty beyond the aspect.

justification.a1: The scope here is at the top of the high school field: six new basic parts and roughly sixteen composite parts across three modules, three generations of a self-built bioprinter with quantified characterisation, two open-source software tools, an AlphaFold2 display pipeline and seventeen human practices cycles (Parts, Hardware, Engineering, Human Practices pages). Like GreatBay_SZ it is told as one chain of increasingly hard steps, from enzyme characterisation to promoter control to printing live cells in hydrogel. It falls short of a 5 because the adhesion arm never got past qualitative microscopy, two of three payloads failed their cytotoxicity test, and the delivery pill was never measured dissolving.
justification.a2: Real measured evidence exists for several claims: the phenol red assay gives yCD-M100H a 29.71% activity gain over wild type against a DH5a negative control (Results 1.1); three new hypoxia promoters have endpoint absorbances, leakage values and ON/OFF ratios of 5.7, 3.6 and 1.8 with a control baseline of ~0.22 (Results 1.2); the kill switches are compared to BBa_K2120006 over 12 h growth curves and distinguished as bacteriostatic versus bactericidal (Results 3.2); ClyA gives 54.8% cytotoxicity, n=3, against PBS and lysis-buffer controls (Results 1.7). Negatives are reported honestly: the formate AND gate showed no formate response, the GFP reporter showed no hypoxia difference, Azurin and yCD-M100H gave negative cytotoxicity. Against that, adhesion is explicitly observational only (Results 2.1), all work was in DH5a rather than the proposed Nissle 1917 chassis, and the pill delivery claims are modelled, not measured.
justification.a3: The route to use is argued carefully and shaped by real constraints: a stool bleach protocol after the sewage plant visit, a bacteriostatic rather than lytic switch after the gastroenterologists warned about LPS release, an endoscopy-visible sfGFP reporter after the imaging specialists, and a nanobody dropped on patent advice (Human Practices cycles 4, 6, 8, 9). The cost argument for bacterial manufacture and a benchtop printer is plausible for low-resource settings. It stays at 3.5 because nothing was tested in a realistic setting: GI transit, release and dose are simulation outputs only, there is no implementation page, and no costed deployment figures beyond literature comparisons.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Test data repeatedly changed the next build: the live co-culture LDH assay gave absorbances above the maximum-release control, was diagnosed as bacterial overgrowth and acidification, and was redesigned into a purified-protein assay (Engineering, Therapeutic Payload Cycle III); the null GFP result was traced to oxygen-dependent chromophore maturation and turned into a mandatory aeration step for future users; the formate circuit's null result produced a reasoned conclusion to use insulated synthetic promoters instead of a native one. Hardware shows the same discipline with quantified criteria: corner offset distance measured by microscopy, filament width tuned from 150 to 400 um, shaker testing at 37 C selecting a 4x multiplier and 300 um filament, then V2's four named failure modes driving the V3 turret and a Geneva mechanism after beta-tester feedback. Short of 5 because the erosion model, the centrepiece of the delivery claim, takes only one parameter from their own bench (the 300 um filament) and its "validation" section is a simulation-versus-simulation comparison, never checked against a measured dissolution curve.
justification.a5: Seventeen cycles under their ECOLI framework, each with a named stakeholder and a documented consequence: cancer survivors steering the design toward a localised prodrug system, Dr Tang prompting the amilCP visual marker and DNA barcode, gastroenterologists Wong and Lai causing the switch from a lytic toxin to essential-gene bacteriostatic containment, sewage engineers producing the stool disinfection protocol, Professor Ngo's patent warning retiring the NB4 nanobody, and Dr Ma's advice producing the dual-promoter display cassettes. This is reflective, responsible and responsive in the handbook's sense, with a 170-respondent survey giving baseline public data rather than decoration. Not a 5 only because a few cycles (education, nursing ergonomics) are reported more as outreach than as exchange that changed the design.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page at all - the URL returns 404 - which is where the handbook says to read who did what. The Team page partly compensates with a per-student role list and names four teacher PIs, and outsourcing is declared where it matters (DNA synthesis by Twist Bioscience, Sanger sequencing by Tech Dragon, Experiments 1.1 and 2.2). What is missing is any statement of where the mammalian work was done or by whom: CT26/MC38 culture, a Class II cabinet and a Leica THUNDER confocal are well beyond a typical school lab, and no host institution or technician is credited anywhere I could find. I raise that as a question, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is built squarely on standard components - J23100/J23114/J23118, B0034, B0015, B1002, araC-pBAD, K811000, K3482035, K592009 - and adds a substantial new set: yCD-M100H, tilS, three FNR-dependent hypoxia promoters and two Lpp-OmpA nanobody coding parts as basic parts, plus payload generators, hypoxia- and formate-regulated devices, promoter::sfGFP test devices, kill switches and barcoded reporters (Parts page). The Lpp-OmpA-3xGS backbone and the sfGFP test devices are explicitly designed for reuse by other teams, and the two open-source software tools also count under p.18. I could not load parts.igem.org during review (403 from the CDN), so Registry-side compatibility and depth are asserted from the wiki rather than verified by me.
justification.a8: On the wiki the documentation is genuinely good: a Parts page with typed tables and functional descriptions for every part, a Biological Principles page giving the mechanism behind each BioBrick, and an Experiments page with workable protocols, plate layouts, instrument models and buffer concentrations. Two things hold it to 3.5. First, the handbook judges parts on the Registry and I could not reach the Registry to confirm that the characterisation data on the Results page is mirrored there. Second, several standard pages are empty 404s (Measurement, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Protocols, Attributions) and the Notebook is only an embedded PDF with no on-page content, so a reader is steered around gaps rather than through a complete record.
justification.w1: The Home page states the disease, the three hurdles, the COLOPRINT concept and the three biological modules with links onward, and the Description page lays out a four-step clinical pipeline that I could restate after one reading. The aim, chassis and parts are all findable. Marks come off for heavy hedging language ("aims to", "hopes to") that occasionally obscures what was actually done, and for visible copy errors such as a duplicated phrase on the Home page and "week" for "weak" in the adhesion section.
justification.w2: The Results and Engineering pages carry figures, tables and numbers for the main claims - promoter ON/OFF ratios, the 29.71% enzyme improvement, an LDH table with n=3 and explicit baseline and maximum controls, growth curves against a Registry kill-switch control, and before/after sterilisation plates with positive and negative controls. Failures are shown rather than hidden. It is not a 5 because statistical claims ("statistically significant", "p<0.01") appear without the test used, replicate counts or error values for most figures, and the whole delivery story rests on simulation outputs presented alongside measured data.
justification.w3: The sidebar is grouped sensibly into Project, Wet Lab and Dry Lab and the page-to-page flow follows the project's own logic. But several standard pages return 404 (Measurement, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Attributions, Protocols, Education, Inclusivity, Sustainability), so a judge looking in the expected place finds nothing and has to hunt - exactly what p.29 says should not be necessary. Individual pages are also very long, with Engineering near 10,000 words, which makes specific results slow to locate.
justification.w4: A future team gets a lot: open-source STL files for the printer and isolator, four-part setup guides, the G-code translator, the simulation repository on iGEM GitLab, detailed protocols, and - most valuable - candid accounts of what failed and why (co-culture overgrowth, GFP maturation, V2 wiring fatigue and calibration drift). The gap is the Notebook, which is an embedded PDF rather than a readable record, and some repository references phrased as "GitHub" on the Contribution page, which points readers off iGEM servers.
justification.w5: Every page ends with a numbered reference list carrying DOIs and PMIDs, prior iGEM parts are cited by number, and the site discloses that some images were generated by Google Gemini, which is the right instinct. Short of 4 because in-text citation is uneven: the Yang et al. hypoxia promoter work is called "Yang et al. (2016)" in the Results and Engineering text while the reference entry gives a 2025 ACS Synthetic Biology paper, figures and microscopy images generally carry no source or credit line, and citation numbering style changes between pages.

J2.one_line: An unusually broad and well-engineered high school project - new characterised parts, three printer generations and seventeen stakeholder cycles - held back by an absent attributions page, a delivery model never checked against measured dissolution, and an adhesion module that stayed qualitative.
strengths: Genuine DBTL iterations where data forced redesign: the failed live co-culture LDH assay was diagnosed (bacterial overgrowth, medium acidification) and replaced with a purified-protein assay; the null GFP hypoxia result was traced to oxygen-dependent chromophore maturation and turned into guidance for other teams (Engineering, Results 1.3).

Quantitative promoter characterisation with a control baseline: three new FNR-dependent hypoxia promoters compared on absolute induction, leakage and ON/OFF ratio (5.7, 3.6, 1.8) against a ~0.22 control, leading to a reasoned choice of PfbsrhaB(-42) (Results 1.2).

Hardware judged by measurement, not assertion: corner offset distance by microscopy, filament width tuned 150-400 um, shaker integrity testing at 37 C selecting a 4x multiplier and 300 um filament, and three printer generations with named failure modes for V2 (Hardware sections 2A-2C).

Human practices that visibly changed the build - bacteriostatic essential-gene switches after the gastroenterologists' LPS warning, a stool disinfection protocol after the sewage plant visit, a nanobody dropped on patent advice, dual-promoter display cassettes after Dr Ma (Human Practices cycles 3, 4, 8, 9).
Honest reporting of negative results, including the formate AND gate showing no formate response and Azurin and yCD-M100H giving no measurable cytotoxicity, each with a stated hypothesis for why.
weaknesses: No Attributions page exists (404), and no page states where the mammalian cell culture and confocal imaging were carried out or by whom, although the instruments named are well beyond a school lab.

The pill delivery claim - the project's whole route to the patient - is modelled only. The 'Model Validation' section compares two simulations against each other; no dissolution, release or CFU measurement was made on a printed pill, and only the 300 um filament diameter comes from their own bench.

The adhesion module, one of the three core modules, produced qualitative microscopy only; the team says so plainly, but it means tumour targeting is unevidenced and the anti-PD-L1 C3 construct performed at background.
All wet lab work was done in E. coli DH5a, while the proposed therapeutic chassis throughout is Nissle 1917 - no data in the intended host.

Several standard pages are empty (Measurement, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Protocols, Attributions) and the Notebook is only an embedded PDF, so the record has holes where judges are told to look.
Statistical claims ('statistically significant', 'p<0.01') appear without the test, replicate number or error values for most figures.
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404; panel should ask who performed the CT26/MC38 culture, the Leica THUNDER confocal imaging and the plate-reader assays, and at which facility. Raised as a question, not an allegation.

A high school team reports mammalian cancer cell culture in Class II biosafety cabinets and safety training referencing BSL-2 protocols (Safety and Security page). Worth a check with the safety committee that this was approved for a high school team, though no whitelist organism issue is apparent (DH5a and Nissle 1917 only).

Site footer discloses that some images were generated by Google Gemini. Disclosure is the right practice; I saw no sign that any evidence figure (gels, plate photos, growth curves, microscopy) is AI-generated, but the panel may wish to confirm the boundary with the team.

Citation inconsistency: the hypoxia promoter source is cited in text as 'Yang et al. (2016)' on both the Results and Engineering pages while the reference entry is a 2025 ACS Synthetic Biology paper (PMID 40542734). Looks like a dating error rather than a fabricated reference.

parts.igem.org returned 403 to me throughout this review, so Registry-side documentation depth and RFC compatibility for the ~22 new parts could not be verified; aspects 7 and 8 rest on the wiki's own account of them.
pages_read: attempted parts.igem.org pages for BBa_26599PUP, BBa_26JHMPW8, BBa_26IS8VW3, BBa_26QAL0X0 (403, not readable)

calibrated.changed: none — a6 3.0 (404 page but per-student roles and declared synthesis/sequencing outsourcing) is now level with squirrel-beijing and keystone; w3 3.5 with eight missing standard pages is consistent with the bar I applied elsewhere.

justification.a1: COLOPRINT climbs through genuinely harder steps inside one season: a new prodrug-converting enzyme characterised against a wild-type control, three new FNR hypoxia promoters characterised for strength and leakage, two essential-gene kill switches benchmarked against the Registry's mazF part, barcoded reporters verified by Sanger sequencing, three generations of a $55-base bioprinter, and an in-silico erosion simulator (Results; Engineering; Hardware; Model). Breadth is matched by honesty: the formate AND-gate, the GFP reporter assay and the live co-culture LDH assay are all reported as failures with analysis. It falls short of a 5 only because the headline claim of the platform - tumour-targeted adhesion and killing - is still unproven.
