justification.a2: Measured, controlled data support several core claims: yCD-M100H gave a 29.71% activity increase over wild-type yCD with a DH5a negative control (p<0.05, Results 1.1); the three hypoxia promoters showed hypoxic absorbances of 0.65-0.78 against a 0.22 control baseline with ON/OFF ratios of 5.7, 3.6 and 1.8 plus 30-minute kinetics (Results 1.2); kill switches were run as 12-hour growth curves against both a plasmid-free control and BBa_K2120006, distinguishing bacteriostatic from bactericidal (Results 3.2). The LDH assay with PBS and lysis-buffer controls, n=3, gave ClyA 54.8% cytotoxicity but negative values for Azurin and yCD-M100H, which the team attributes to poor His-tag yield (Results 1.7). The Adhesion Module - the part that makes the therapy targeted - is explicitly qualitative and near-background, and the formate AND-gate did not respond, so the integrated device is not shown to work.
justification.a3: The need is real and confirmed by users rather than only by literature: colorectal cancer survivors through the Hong Kong Cancer Fund, gastroenterologists Dr Wong and Dr Lai on endotoxin risk, an oncology nurse on dysphagia, and Shatin Sewage Treatment engineers on environmental escape (Human Practices Cycles 1, 8, 9, 12). The team also names its own limits and a route to deployment (EcN chassis, bioprinted pill, hospital-sited printing). But everything downstream of the bench is proposal: no in vivo work, no gastric-transit test of a loaded pill beyond a 5-hour shaker trial (Hardware V1 test C), and the point-of-excretion bleach protocol (Cycle 9) is asserted, never tested.
justification.a4: This is the team's strongest aspect. Failures drive redesigns that are then built and tested: the live co-culture LDH assay failed because E. coli doubles in 20 min against CT26's 16-22 h, so the team moved to purified-protein treatment (Engineering 1.2 Cycle III); the hypoxic sfGFP assay showed no induction, the team traced it to oxygen-dependent chromophore maturation and wrote a one-hour aeration step into the protocol (Engineering 1.3 Cycle II; Experiments 3.3); the PfdhF null result was explained through NarL/NarP repression and led to a stated conclusion that an orthogonal synthetic promoter is needed. Hardware shows the same discipline across V1-V3, with quantified failure modes (wiring fatigue, calibration drift) and a pivot to a Geneva mechanism after external user testing. The AlphaFold2 linker study genuinely preceded and chose the build (3xGS, pLDDT 88.6 for OmpA), and the erosion simulator was calibrated on the team's own measured 300 um filament.
justification.a5: Sixteen documented ECOLI cycles each name a stakeholder, their challenge and the resulting build. Dr Wang Boxiang's question about the microaerobic healthy gut produced the formate AND-gate BBa_263FCA00; Dr Tang's diagnostic-workflow question produced the amilCP barcode reporter, and Mr Tang's endoscopy critique replaced it with sfGFP; Dr Wong and Dr Lai's LPS warning turned the kill switch from lytic mazF to bacteriostatic tyrS/tilS; Prof Ngo's Freedom-to-Operate challenge led the team to abandon the NB4 nanobody and withhold it from the Registry; Ms Tong's dysphagia observations fixed the 12.00 x 6.25 x 4.24 mm pill envelope used in the model. Critical voices and misuse are genuinely anticipated. Two gaps keep it off 5: the 170-respondent survey with 43.7% under-18 participants is reported with no mention of consent or ethics oversight (Human Practices Cycle 0), and the supporting interview logs and survey instruments sit on Google Drive, which judges cannot assess.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page: /plklfc/attributions returns 404 and the navigation contains no equivalent. The Team page gives each of the 25 students a short role list, which is useful, but no figure caption, results section or table says who ran which experiment, and no outside lab, instructor or facility is acknowledged anywhere. That matters here because the work includes murine cell culture, His-tag affinity chromatography, SDS-PAGE and Leica THUNDER confocal imaging (Experiments 3.1, 4.1) - plausible for a well-equipped school, but unverifiable as written. Named outsourcing is limited to Twist gene synthesis and Tech Dragon Sanger sequencing, which is good practice. I record this as a question for the session, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is built squarely from standard parts: Anderson promoters J23100/J23114/J23118 chosen deliberately by export pathway, B0034, B0015 and B1002 terminators, and existing Registry parts K811000, K3482035, K592009, I746916, K808000 and K2120006 used as both payloads and benchmarks (Parts; Engineering 1.2). The team contributes roughly two dozen new basic and composite parts, several of them shown to function, and the Lpp-OmpA-3xGS display backbone plus the hypoxia promoter set are designed for reuse by other teams (Contribution). The G-code translator and the erosion simulator count as standard components too.
justification.a8: The wiki-side documentation is genuinely good: the Parts page tables every new basic and composite part with type, name and a real functional rationale, and the Results and Engineering pages carry the characterisation behind them. I could not reach parts.igem.org to confirm what is actually on the Registry entries (requests returned 403), so Registry depth is unverified from my side. Two concrete defects pull this down: the Engineering and Contribution pages repeatedly give composite part IDs where the basic promoter is meant - Pfbslac(-41) is called BBa_26B4FM0X on Engineering 1.3 but BBa_26F6JGAV on the Parts page - and the Notebook page is a single embedded PDF with no raw data files.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem (1.9M cases, 900k deaths), the three obstacles it targets and the COLOPRINT solution in a few readable lines, then routes the reader to Description, Hardware and Human Practices. The Description page lays out the four-step clinical pipeline clearly, and the three-module architecture (Adhesion, Killing, Safety) is used consistently as the organising spine across every page.
justification.w2: Most central claims carry a figure, a table or numbers with controls, and the team is unusually careful to flag what did not work (GFP null, formate null, negative LDH values). Modelled output is kept separate and labelled as simulation on the Model page. Against that, several assays report means and p-values without stating n or replicate structure (hypoxia endpoint data, Results 1.2), the adhesion evidence is a four-row table of microscope impressions, and the prose across Description and Parts leans heavily on 'aims to', 'is expected to' and 'is projected to' for functions never tested.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and maps onto the judging criteria, with Wet Lab and Dry Lab groupings and a separate Biological Principles page that keeps the Results page uncluttered. Standard pages are missing, though: no Attributions, Education, Inclusivity, Implementation or Proof-of-Concept pages exist (all 404), and the Human Practices page at ~7,300 words is a long scroll with no in-page index. Some material judges would want - interview logs, survey instruments, lesson plans - lives on Google Drive.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way: the Experiments and Protocol page gives step-level protocols with instruments, concentrations and plate layouts; Hardware gives costs, part sources, STL IDs and the measured extrusion-multiplier-to-filament-width relationship; the simulator is on iGEM GitLab with a README. What is missing is the record of the season itself - the Notebook is one embedded PDF rather than a dated log, there are no raw data files behind any figure, and with no Attributions page there is no record of who to ask.
justification.w5: Citations are present on every page and mostly carry DOIs, image generation by Google Gemini is disclosed in the footer, and prior Registry parts are credited. But the Engineering reference list is in a visibly unfinished state: six entries end with '(See audit note below)' and one with '(Corrected from composite entry; see audit note below)', and no audit note appears anywhere on the published page. Several of those flagged entries carry no DOI and I could not verify them (Wang S 2018 Oncol Rep; Zhang Y 2021; Deng R 2020; Follrich S 2022 Appl Environ Microbiol; Krasniqi A 2019 Front Immunol). Reference 7 is marked a duplicate of reference 2, and Yang et al. is cited in text as 2016 while the list gives a 2025 ACS Synth Biol paper.

J3.one_line: An unusually complete high school project - characterised new parts with real controls, honest failures, a three-generation DIY bioprinter and sixteen traceable stakeholder loops - held back by a missing Attributions page and a reference list left in a visibly unaudited state.
strengths: Measured characterisation with proper controls on three independent systems: yCD-M100H vs wild-type vs untransformed DH5a (29.71% increase, p<0.05), hypoxia promoters against a 0.22 absorbance baseline with ON/OFF ratios, and tyrS/tilS kill switches benchmarked against both a plasmid-free control and Registry part BBa_K2120006 (Results 1.1, 1.2, 3.2)

Failures are reported and acted on rather than buried: the live co-culture LDH assay, the hypoxic sfGFP assay and the PfdhF formate AND-gate all failed, each is analysed mechanistically, and two of the three produced a concrete protocol or design change (Engineering 1.2 Cycle III, 1.3 Cycles II-III)

Human Practices that visibly changed the build - the formate AND-gate from Dr Wang, the amilCP-to-sfGFP reporter switch from the OptoMedic imaging specialist, the bacteriostatic tyrS/tilS switch from gastroenterologists' LPS warning, and the abandonment of the patented NB4 nanobody on Prof Ngo's Freedom-to-Operate challenge (Human Practices Cycles 2, 6, 8, 4)

Hardware engineering with quantified iteration: a $55 FDM printer converted to a bioprinter, V2's wiring fatigue and calibration drift documented as failures, V3's rotary turret, and a Geneva-mechanism pivot after external beta-testing by the CUHK team, with STLs and a $200 aseptic isolator costed out (Hardware)

A model that genuinely fed the design: AlphaFold2 linker failure analysis (1xGS steric clash, 4xGS entropic collapse, topological inversion) chose the 3xGS linker actually built, and the erosion simulator was calibrated on the team's own measured 300 um filament width (Model I; Hardware V1 test C)
weaknesses: No Attributions page exists (404), no figure or results section says which student ran which experiment, and no host lab, technician or equipment provider is acknowledged - despite mammalian cell culture, affinity chromatography and confocal imaging appearing in the protocols

The Adhesion Module, which is what makes the therapy targeted rather than generic, rests on a four-row table of qualitative microscope impressions with C3 at background; the team says so plainly, but the platform's central claim is therefore unsupported

Six references on the Engineering page end with '(See audit note below)' and no audit note is published; several of those lack DOIs and could not be verified, one reference is marked a duplicate, and Yang et al. is dated 2016 in text and 2025 in the list

Part IDs are inconsistent between pages - the basic hypoxia promoters are given their composite IDs on the Engineering and Contribution pages, contradicting the Parts page - which would mislead a future team ordering from the Registry

The Notebook is one embedded PDF with no dated log or raw data files, and key Human Practices material (interview logs, survey instruments, lesson plans) sits on Google Drive where it cannot be judged
red_flags: Six Engineering references carry an unresolved editorial marker '(See audit note below)' with no audit note anywhere on the page; of these, Wang S 2018 (Oncol Rep), Zhang Y 2021 (Clin Colorectal Cancer), Deng R 2020 (Cell Death Dis), Follrich S 2022 (Appl Environ Microbiol 88(12):e01254-22) and Krasniqi A 2019 (Front Immunol 10:1455) carry no DOI and I could not verify that they exist or support the cited claims. Specific evidence recorded; ask the team at the session and refer to the RCC only if the citations prove unresolvable.

Work with murine colorectal carcinoma cell lines CT26 and MC38 in Class II biosafety cabinets, with the Safety page stating training to 'BSL-1 and BSL-2 protocols' (Safety and Security; Experiments 3.1, 4.1). Mammalian cell lines sit outside the usual high school whitelist, so I would verify that a safety check-in was filed and, if not, raise it with safety@igem.org rather than score it.
Required Attributions page is absent from the wiki entirely (404 on /attributions and every variant I tried), which is a ballot requirement, not just a gap in the record.

The Human Practices page directs judges to Google Drive for all survey questions, interview questions, interview logs and lesson materials; none of that can be judged, and the 170-respondent survey with 43.7% under-18 participants carries no statement of consent or ethics oversight.

Registry part pages could not be reached from this session (parts.igem.org returned 403), so the depth of the ~24 claimed new Registry entries is unverified in either direction; worth a direct check before the ballot is final.
pages_read: parts.igem.org pages for BBa_26599PUP, BBa_26JHMPW8, BBa_26SLMCX1 (403, unreachable)

calibrated.changed: a6 2.5 to 3.0. Each of the 25 students has a role list and the outsourcing that did happen (Twist synthesis, Tech Dragon sequencing) is named, which is the same evidence as Mingdao, Hongwen and Keystone at 3.0; I had pushed this to the 2.5 band occupied by teams offering only generic bios or nothing. The unacknowledged cell-culture and confocal facilities keep it at 3.0 rather than higher, and remain a session question.

one_line.en: The broadest project outside the top five — characterised promoters, kill switches and three printer generations with outstanding Human Practices — held down by no attributions page at all and an unproven targeting module.
one_line.zh: 前五名以外最廣的專案——已表徵的啟動子、自殺開關與三代列印機，人文實踐出色——但完全沒有歸屬頁，標靶模組也未獲證實。

strengths: Controlled characterisation across several modules, including an enzyme variant against wild-type and native-strain controls and three new hypoxia promoters with ON/OFF ratios
Negative and failed results reported and used, including a null reporter assay traced to a mechanistic cause and a failed co-culture
Hardware engineering with quantified measures of success across three printer generations, feeding a measured filament width into the model
Seventeen Human Practices cycles each naming a stakeholder and a concrete design change, including abandoning a patented nanobody
weaknesses: The central targeting claim rests on qualitative microscope impressions in which the key constructs were similar to control
The therapeutic system was never shown to work end to end, and the prodrug route produced negative cytotoxicity values explained by hypothesis only
Statistics are asserted without replicate number, error-bar definition or stated test in most figures
All wet lab was in a laboratory strain while the proposed chassis is a probiotic; several standard pages are empty
red_flags: No Attributions page exists anywhere, while the work includes mammalian cancer cell culture and confocal imaging of unstated provenance
Six Engineering references carry an unresolved audit marker with no audit note; several do not resolve or point to different papers, which two judges verified independently
Mammalian cancer cell lines and references to BSL-2 protocols need a whitelist determination from the safety committee
Blanket AI-image disclosure in the footer that does not distinguish schematics from evidentiary figures

screen.project_title: Furflouris: biosynthesised allantoin, vanillin and a PepG-EGF module for pet skin and coat care
screen.what_they_built: Three engineered E. coli BL21 platforms: de novo allantoin from glucose via xdhABC + pucLM, heterologous vanillin via quiC-BsSfp-SrOMT-NiCAR, and a decapeptide-thrombin site-hEGF fusion for hair repair, all aimed at a pet-grooming product line.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3)/DH5alpha; 12 new BioBrick parts (9 enzyme CDSs, hEGF, 2 composite pathway parts) plus added documentation for existing part BBa_K258010 (hEGF). Anderson promoter library (J23114/J23106/J23100/J23119) used for module balancing.
screen.best_evidence: /results: HPLC time-courses with three biological replicates - allantoin undetectable in wild-type BL21 but 6.24 +/- 1.40 mg/L at 12 h rising to 9.82 +/- 0.82 mg/L at 48 h in BL21-Allantoin; a full 16-combination promoter matrix spanning 1.92 +/- 0.19 to 14.03 +/- 0.86 mg/L with J23100-xdhABC / J23119-pucLM best; vanillin reaching 93.88 +/- 12.96 mg/L at 20 h and 127.05 +/- 3.17 mg/L after initial-pH optimisation to pH 6.0.
screen.hp_integration: Yes. A synthetic biology expert consultation prompted the molybdenum cofactor (molybdate) optimisation after allantoin yields stalled; pet-store and street interviews introduced the fragrance requirement that became the vanillin module; veterinary dermatology input and store-chain exchanges set the daily-care positioning and product format; the agricultural bureau conversation fixed the regulatory product category.
screen.reason: The largest body of replicated quantitative wet-lab data in this batch: three pathways, HPLC quantification against standard curves, a 16-member promoter combination screen, and molybdate, temperature and pH optimisation, plus ELISA and a double-blind ex vivo hair trial. Worth a full read, but two things could sink it: the attributions page is empty and the team page is 227 words, so the division between students and any host lab is undocumented, and every results figure is captioned 'Fig. X'. Titres are also very low in absolute terms (14 mg/L allantoin).
screen.field_notes: PROFUTURE-CHINA (Fashion & Cosmetics, China) built Furflouris, a pet skin-and-coat care concept resting on three engineered E. coli BL21 platforms. Allantoin is made de novo from glucose by introducing xdhABC from Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and pucLM from Candida utilis as two cassettes on one plasmid; wild-type BL21 produced none while the engineered strain reached 9.82 +/- 0.82 mg/L at 48 h by HPLC, and a 16-combination Anderson-promoter matrix balancing the upstream and downstream modules spanned 1.92 to 14.03 mg/L with J23100-xdhABC plus J23119-pucLM best. Molybdate supplementation and a fermentation-temperature series (30 C optimal) followed. A separate heterologous vanillin pathway (quiC, BsSfp, SrOMT, NiCAR) gave 93.88 +/- 12.96 mg/L at 20 h, improved to 127.05 +/- 3.17 mg/L at initial pH 6.0, where the team notes explicitly that peak biomass (pH 6.5) did not give peak product. A 213 bp hair-repair decapeptide-thrombin site-hEGF fusion in pET28a was expressed, cleaved with thrombin, confirmed by ELISA, and tested in a double-blind ex vivo cat-hair gloss trial. Twelve new parts were registered and extra documentation was added to the existing hEGF part BBa_K258010. Human practices is very large (12k words) with a Python-assisted stakeholder map and a five-stage PAWS cycle, and several design changes trace to it. Weak points: no attributions page, a near-empty team page, generic 'Fig. X' captions throughout results, and no modelling page.

screen.project_title: Bio Color ID: PHB tags dyed with biosynthetic halogenated indigoids for product authentication
screen.what_they_built: One engineered E. coli making both a bioplastic (PHB from a phaCAB operon) and a halogenated indigoid pigment, cast together into small tags whose optical response under five LEDs and four backgrounds acts as an authentication fingerprint, read by a purpose-built 60-component Bio Color ID Reader.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21-AI and BL21(DE3), plus a lambda-Red tnaA deletion derivative. ~45 new parts in a structured collection: phaCAB operons from C. necator and A. lata, native and codon-optimised MaFMO, a seven-allele tnaA series (BBa_26I40MCD wild type through BBa_26QYYVV5 T465A), six Fre-L3 halogenase fusions (SttH, PyrH, RebH, Thal, PrnA, SnFDHal), a P43-creRBS cassette, and two co-resident plasmid devices on pBR322/amp and p15A/cam.
screen.best_evidence: /results Part 1: PHB yield of 0.105 vs 0.088 g per g wet cell mass for the C. necator against the A. lata operon (unpaired two-tailed t-test, p<0.05, mean +/- SEM, n=3), with the host/temperature screen giving a 135% induced increase for BL21-AI at 30 C against 62% for BL21(DE3), and the polymer's identity confirmed independently by Nile red confocal imaging (cytoplasmic granules vs membrane-only control) and FTIR (ester carbonyl at 1719.71 cm-1). Part 2 adds native vs codon-optimised MaFMO at 0.86 vs 0.23 g/L indigo and 6,6'-dihalogenated spectra at 560/562 nm against indigo's 618 nm.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - /human-practices traces a banknote-security museum visit, Seoul Beauty Week, K-Beauty Expo, a consultation with Prof. Kang Sungsoo and public testing at Maker Faire into a three-part evaluation table (can the same sample be re-recognised, can imitations be separated, can it be read on a product), which became the structure of the Part 3 optical work; a collaboration agreement with IEUM&Co. opened a route to real cosmetic packaging.
screen.reason: The strongest project in this batch and a credible finalist candidate: replicated statistics, orthogonal confirmation of the product (gravimetry + Nile red + FTIR), a chromosomal knockout, a graded allele series used as an engineering knob, a large and genuinely reusable part collection, a validated instrument, and five engineering cycles that report failures (three of six halogenases dead, codon optimisation backwards) as the thing that steered each next step. The single glaring gap is the /attributions page, which is 68 words of boilerplate with no content - for a high school team doing lambda-Red recombineering, confocal and FTIR, the panel must establish what was student work and what the host lab did.
screen.field_notes: PSI Korea (Biomanufacturing, KOR) built Bio Color ID, an anti-counterfeiting tag combining bacterial PHB with biosynthetic indigoid dyes, read optically rather than scanned. Part 1 established PHB in E. coli: a host x temperature screen selected BL21-AI at 30 C (135% induced mass increase vs 62% for BL21(DE3); 37 C collapsed both), the C. necator phaCAB operon beat the A. lata one at 0.105 vs 0.088 g/g wet cells (p<0.05, n=3), and the recovered film was confirmed as PHB by Nile red confocal granules and an FTIR ester carbonyl at 1719.71 cm-1. Part 2 made a halogenated indigoid in a single cell, which published routes avoid by splitting the reactions: BL21(DE3) leaked and turned blue before induction so BL21-AI was adopted, native MaFMO outperformed the codon-optimised version 0.86 vs 0.23 g/L, chromosomal tnaA was deleted by lambda-Red (773 bp vs 1739 bp locus), a seven-allele tnaA series was screened from 3% to 92% of wild-type output leaving T465A as the usable knob, and of six Fre-L3 halogenase fusions only SttH (6-position) gave a clearly non-indigo colour at 560/562 nm against indigo's 618 nm. Part 3 fabricated tags and validated the self-built reader (hemispherical LED shell, fixed camera, locked white balance, 5 illuminations x 4 backgrounds x 3 channels = 60 components) for repeat readout, independently fabricated tags, and discrimination from paper imitations. Parts, contribution and engineering pages are written for reuse, including a 'what did not work' section. The attributions page is empty (68 words) and there is no model page.

justification.a1: Three workstreams build on each other in rising difficulty: a PHB module screened across hosts, temperatures and two operon sources (Results Part 1); a halogenated indigoid made in a single cell, which published routes split across two cells or two temperatures (Results Part 2); and a purpose-built reader, measurement study and matching software (Hardware, Measurement, Software). This is scale comparable to the TAS Taipei anchor. It falls short of a 5 because the integrating step was never built: Contribution states plainly "we have not run the double transformant ourselves", so the one-cell co-production shown on the Home page is a design, not a result.
justification.a2: The core function claims are supported against controls with replicates. PHB: gravimetric yield with induced/uninduced pairs, n = 3, mean ± SEM, Student's t-test (p < 0.01 host comparison; p < 0.05 operon comparison), Nile red confocal against an empty-vector control under identical acquisition settings, and FTIR with the 1719.71 cm-1 ester carbonyl assigned (Results Part 1, Figures 3-6). Indigoids: titer against an indigo standard curve (0.86 vs 0.23 g/L, n = 3), a tnaA series spanning 3-92% with K270A as a catalytic-null control, and DMSO absorption spectra showing 560/562 nm against indigo's 618 nm (Results Part 2, Figures 2, 4, 6). It is a 4 rather than 5 because the decisive halogenase comparison is by eye with no replicates, product identity is admitted as tentative without LC-MS, residual 618 nm absorbance shows conversion is partial, and the authentication claim itself rests on three tags and one imitation pair per colour.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and stakeholder-shaped rather than asserted: Seoul Beauty Week interviews, a packaging supplier (Pinsheng) raising placement and attachment questions, two incumbent providers reviewed, and IEUM&Co. agreeing to supply real cosmetics for attachment trials (Human Practices 07-08, Description 15). Counterfeit figures are cited to OECD/EUIPO and MOIP with their scope limits spelled out. It stays at 3.5 because nothing has yet been tested in a real setting: no tag has been read after attachment, the USD 0.10 target is labelled a development goal rather than a measured cost, and the only imitation challenge is watercolour on paper, one pair per colour (Results Part 3, Section 9).
justification.a4: Engineering Success documents five cycles in which a test result changed the next design, not troubleshooting: BL21(DE3) turning blue before induction forced the host change to BL21-AI; CgFMO giving no pigment with a halogenase forced the move to MaFMO; the codon-optimised sequence losing 3.7-fold forced the native sequence; the rate imbalance drove the chromosomal tnaA deletion and then the variant series; and the selection criterion was explicitly set to colour, not halogenase activity, before Cycle 5. Failures are recorded, including three halogenases that gave nothing. Half a point short of 5 because the chosen design (T465A plus Fre-L3-SttH) was validated against its own criterion only qualitatively, pale versus deep blue, which the team itself names as the first thing to quantify.
justification.a5: Four expert consultations produced traceable changes: Prof. Park's advice on repeatability and references set the validation agenda and contributed to replacing the smartphone with a fixed camera module; Prof. Cunningham's point about overlapping RGB channel sensitivity changed how the data are described; Dr Son's challenge on PHB turned a blanket sustainability claim into a conditional one, visible in Description section 2.2 and the Sustainability page. Maker Faire visitor questions are mapped item by item onto six development priorities (Human Practices Table 4), and the packaging and provider visits produced the before/after-attachment test plan. Not a 5 only because the HP work shaped the evaluation and application agenda more than it shaped the molecular design, and the industry conversations are explicitly described as non-representative.
justification.a6: The Attributions page is published but completely empty, on the live site as well as in the crawl, so the handbook's p.25-26 question of who did what is unanswered on the page meant to answer it. The Team page gives student role leads (experiment, measurement, hardware, software, HP) and Registry entries carry per-contributor CRediT-style roles, which is real task-level evidence, but those same entries list a PI (Chris Song) as a designer with Methodology, Supervision and Validation on parts including BBa_26QYYVV5 and BBa_26TZ7VWJ. Nothing states who ran the confocal microscope, FTIR, gene synthesis or the lambda-Red recombineering, or what the two PIs, three instructors and advisor contributed. For a workload this large, the silence has to count against the score rather than be read generously.
justification.a7: The project is genetic devices built from standard components throughout: 47 part numbers, including seven tnaA alleles, six Fre-L3 halogenase fusions, the P43-creRBS cassette and plasmid-level devices on deliberately compatible pBR322/Amp and p15A/Cm backbones (Parts page). The team reuses existing Registry entries (phaCAB flagged as duplicates of BBa_K089001-3) alongside new ones, exactly the TAS pattern. The tnaA series is framed as an interchangeable slot with reuse instructions for other tryptophan-competing pathways, which is genuine standard-component thinking rather than a parts dump. Hardware and software are substantial but sit on top of the biology, not in place of it.
justification.a8: Registry entries carry role, topology, host organism, composition, GC content, functional description and separate Design, Experiment, Characterisation, Application and Discussion documentation sections (checked on BBa_26QYYVV5 and BBa_26TZ7VWJ), and the wiki Parts and Contribution pages map each number to its characterisation location. Against that: the Attributions page is blank, the lab notebook is a single PDF link rather than a navigable record, BBa_26QYYVV5 shows a biosafety screening result of "Denied, published after review", and the Description says the phaCAB operons were amplified from C. necator and A. lata genomic DNA while the Safety page says no source organisms were cultured and the genes came as synthesised or cloned sequences.
justification.w1: The Home page moves from the counterfeiting problem to the Bio Color ID concept to the reader in a clear sequence, and the Description opens with the research question and a plain statement of what was evaluated. Most pages begin with a scoped summary and a contents list. It loses half a point for the Home page's "One cell, two products" and "Two plasmids go in" framing, which presents the co-production strain as built when the Contribution page says the double transformant was never run, and for the long scroll-animated preamble before any result appears.
justification.w2: This is the strongest part of the wiki. Nearly every claim carries a figure with a stated control, n, error definition and statistical test, and limits are written next to the result rather than buried: the gravimetric yield is explicitly flagged as not excluding co-extracted material, the tnaA screen as pathway output rather than specific activity, the three-tag agreement as insufficient to characterise batch variation, and the software's false-accept/false-reject rates as synthetic data only. Modelled and measured are consistently separated. Short of 5 because the halogenase comparison carries no replicates or numbers, and the pigment source used for the Part 3 tag series (biosynthesised versus standard indigo/indirubin) is not stated where the tags are characterised.
justification.w3: Standard URLs are intact, the nav groups pages sensibly (Project / Wet Lab / Dry Lab / Engagement), and every long page has an in-page contents list, so finding a given result is straightforward. Against that, the wiki is sprawling by the digital handbook's own test: Hardware runs to 12,310 words, Measurement 7,136 and Results 9,326, with substantial duplication between Description, Results, Measurement and Parts. The Attributions page renders as a heading with nothing under it, and the notebook is one external PDF.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this. The Experiments page carries 16 protocols including the lambda-Red and FLP excision procedure and the tag fabrication protocol with batch-record fields; Contribution lists working conditions with the reasoning, three documented failures and two ways the team misread its own data; the Parts collection page gives explicit reuse recipes including the non-optional delta-tnaA host requirement; Hardware gives 3D-printed parts, LED mounting coordinates and default settings. Short of 5 because the notebook is a single PDF rather than a dated record, and the underlying RGB feature tables and raw images are not posted.
justification.w5: Each page carries its own numbered reference list with resolvable DOIs (Lee 2021 Nat Chem Biol, Li & Young 2015, Choi 2003, Datsenko & Wanner 2000), figure sources are listed separately on the Description page, statistics are attributed to EUIPO, OECD and MOIP with their scope stated, and a PDB entry is cited for the K270A rationale. The gap that keeps it from 5: the codon-optimised MaFMO is credited only to "an earlier iGEM team" with no team named or linked, which is exactly the prior-iGEM credit the handbook asks for, and some engagement-photo figures carry no source line.

J1.one_line: An unusually complete high-school project: a tunable tryptophanase slot that lets one E. coli cell make a halogenated indigoid, backed by controlled, replicated data and a well-documented part collection, let down by a blank Attributions page and an integrated strain that was never built.
strengths: Controls and replicates are the norm, not the exception: empty-vector confocal control, catalytic-null K270A control in the tnaA series, induced/uninduced pairs, n = 3 with SEM and t-tests, and FTIR plus Nile red used together to prove the gravimetric material really is PHB (Results Parts 1-2).

A real engineering narrative with five data-driven redesigns and recorded failures, including the counter-intuitive finding that the codon-optimised MaFMO is 3.7-fold worse and gives nothing at all once a halogenase competes (Engineering Success, Cycles 2 and 5).

The tnaA allele series is a genuine contribution to the Registry rather than a parts list: seven graded settings, a stated working window of 24-45%, an explicit host requirement, and a frank account of why the values disagree with Li and Young (Parts collection, Contribution).

Limits are written beside the claims throughout - no LC-MS so the product is a mixture, three tags cannot establish batch reproducibility, the software's rates are synthetic, the USD 0.10 cost is a target - which makes the evidence that is presented easier to trust.

Human Practices changed things that can be pointed at: the move to a fixed camera module, the retreat from an unqualified PHB sustainability claim, and a six-item validation agenda built from Maker Faire visitors' questions.
weaknesses: The Attributions page is empty on the live site. Nothing says who ran the confocal, FTIR, recombineering or synthesis, or what the two PIs, three instructors and advisor did; Registry entries list a PI as a part designer with Supervision and Validation roles, which makes the gap more pressing rather than less.

The headline claim - one cell making both the bioplastic and the halogenated pigment - is a design. Contribution says the double transformant was never run, yet the Home page presents co-production as achieved.
The decisive halogenase choice rests on colour judged by eye, with no replicates and no numbers; the team identifies the 560/618 nm absorbance ratio as the obvious fix but did not compute it.

Authentication performance is not established: three tags from one condition, one imitation pair per colour, watercolour on paper only, and no reading after attachment. The wiki says this clearly, but the gap between the demonstrated measurement and the claimed application remains wide.

The wiki is long past 'complete but not sprawling' - Hardware alone is over 12,000 words, with heavy duplication across Description, Results and Measurement - and the lab notebook is a single PDF rather than a usable record.

A factual inconsistency between pages: Description says the phaCAB operons were amplified from C. necator and A. lata genomic DNA with KCTC/KACC strain numbers; the Safety page says no source organisms were cultured and the genes were obtained as synthesised or cloned sequences.
red_flags: Attributions page published but blank, so aspect 6 cannot be verified from the page the handbook designates for it (p.25-26).

Registry entry BBa_26QYYVV5 (tnaA T465A) shows biosafety screening 'Denied - published after review' with SecureDNA matches to regulated-organism lists. iGEM Safety reviewed and published it on 20 October 2026; I note it for the record and would not decide it myself.

Source-organism inconsistency between the Description (operons amplified from C. necator KCTC 22469 and A. lata KACC 15149 genomic DNA) and the Safety page (source organisms not cultured; genes obtained as synthesised or cloned sequences). Worth a Q&A question rather than an integrity concern.

The pigment used for the Part 3 indigo:indirubin tag series is not identified where the tags are characterised; Human Practices mentions considering commercial PHB and indigo in parallel with microbial production, so whether the characterised tags contain the team's own biosynthesised pigment is unresolved on the wiki.

No integrity concern found. Citations resolve, figures carry controls and stated n, and no modelled or synthetic result is presented as measured - the software page explicitly separates synthetic test rates from physical-sample performance.

calibrated.changed: a6 2.5 -> 3.0. The Attributions page is blank, but Registry entries carry per-contributor CRediT-style roles and the Team page names student leads for experiment, measurement, hardware, software and HP. That is task-level evidence the 2.5 teams (HK Joint School, BIST-China, Hongwen, Cataverse, GreatBay-SCIE) simply do not have, so the floor score was harsher than my own bar. The PI appearing as a designer on two part entries, and the silence on who ran the confocal, FTIR and recombineering, keep it below 3.5.

justification.a1: Three linked workstreams were actually executed: PHB production in E. coli with host/temperature screening, operon comparison, Nile red confocal and FTIR identification (Results Part 1, Figs 2-6); single-cell halogenated indigoid engineering including a chromosomal tnaA deletion, a seven-allele activity series and a six-halogenase screen (Results Part 2, Figs 2-6); and tag fabrication plus a purpose-built five-LED/four-background optical reader with its own validation (Hardware 8.2-8.5, Measurement). The chain of increasingly difficult steps and the openly reported dead ends (CgFMO, codon-optimised MaFMO, three silent halogenases, the odd A. lata band) read like the GreatBay pattern. It falls short of a 5 because the two modules were never run in one cell - the Contribution page states plainly "we have not run the double transformant ourselves" - and the authentication function itself was never demonstrated end to end.
justification.a2: The wet-lab claims are measured, not asserted: PHB yield 0.105 vs 0.088 g/g wet cell mass with n=3, SEM and a two-tailed t-test (Results Fig 4B), Nile red confocal against an empty-vector control (Fig 5), FTIR carbonyl at 1719.71 cm-1 (Fig 6B), colony PCR 773 bp vs 1739 bp for the tnaA deletion (Fig 3), native vs codon-optimised MaFMO at 0.86 vs 0.23 g/L against an indigo standard curve (Fig 2C), and absorption maxima at 560/562 nm against indigo's 618 nm (Fig 6). K270A serves as a declared catalytic-null control in the tnaA series. What has not been shown is the project's actual function: software decision performance was tested on synthetic data only (Software, Table 10 and the synthetic-test section), the team states no acceptance/rejection evaluation on physical tags exists, and no LC-MS confirms the product mixture.
justification.a3: The deployment route is specific and stakeholder-checked rather than generic: a B2B model argued from conversations with four cosmetics brands at Seoul Beauty Week, packaging placement constraints gathered from Pinsheng at K-Beauty Expo, a comparison with incumbent services (NEMOIN, HiddenTag), a priced build of about USD 100 for the reader (Hardware Table 27) and an agreement with IEUM&Co. to supply real cosmetic products for attachment trials (Human Practices 08). The team is careful not to overclaim. It is held below 4.5 because nothing has yet been tested on a product: attachment, reading after attachment, tamper evidence and false-acceptance/false-rejection rates are all listed as future work, so the impact case remains argued rather than demonstrated.
justification.a4: This is the strongest aspect. Five wet-lab cycles on the Engineering page each end with a test result that changed the next build - pre-induction blue cultures sent them from BL21(DE3) to BL21-AI, a halogenase-negative CgFMO sent them to MaFMO, measured 3.7-fold output chose the native sequence, the deletion plus a seven-allele screen produced the 24-45% working window, and colour (not titre) selected SttH. The hardware ran five further generations driven by measurements, not impressions: exposure tables with ceiling-pixel fractions (Table 7), white-balance |R-G| of 7.6 vs 58.5 (Table 8), repeatability over a week (MAE 1.280 DN, Table 17) and a separation index that justified four backgrounds over a sixth LED (Table 23). Four Hanyang University students rebuilt the reader from the documentation alone (Hardware 9.2), a reproducibility test almost no team runs. Short of 5 only because the final loop - does the tag authenticate - was never closed.
justification.a5: The engagement is broad and genuinely two-way: the Bank of Korea Money Museum on layered physical security, four cosmetics brands, four expert consultations (Prof. Kang, two rounds with Prof. Park, Dr. Son, Prof. Cunningham by email), about 100 Maker Faire visitors, three authentication providers at K-Beauty Expo and the IEUM&Co. agreement. Several consultations visibly changed the work: Dr. Son's challenge on PHB killed an unexamined sustainability claim, Prof. Cunningham's point on overlapping RGB sensitivities changed how the data are described, and visitor questions became the imitation experiment with CRETION and the move to a fixed camera. It sits at 4 rather than 5 because a large share of the recorded adaptations are future evaluation priorities (Tables 4 and 5) rather than changes already made to the design.
justification.a6: The Attributions page is empty - it renders only navigation and footer (68 words in the crawl, confirmed on the live page). The handbook reads attribution from that page, and here there is nothing to read: no who-did-what chart, no statement of which steps students performed, and no acknowledgement of the outside help that other pages mention (CRETION made the watercolour imitations, four Hanyang University students built the second reader, Prof. Park offered laboratory instruments, and confocal, FTIR and UV-Vis instrument access is never attributed). The Team page lists six students with role titles only. Nothing suggests the work was not student-led, and the role titles match the page structure, but with the required attribution absent I cannot verify the division of labour, and the score reflects that absence rather than any suspicion.
justification.a7: The project is built on standard components and contributes a well-designed, reusable collection: 45 parts submitted, including seven tnaA alleles spanning 3-100% of wild-type output as an interchangeable rate slot, six Fre-L3 halogenase fusions in one identical format so ring position is the only variable, the P43-creRBS cassette, and two plasmid backbones deliberately chosen with different origins and markers for co-residence (Parts page, Plasmid-level devices). Prior Registry parts are reused and declared as duplicates (BBa_K089001-3). The Part Collection page explains reuse concretely - take the whole system, swap the halogen, swap the position, or take the slot alone for any pathway competing with tryptophanase - which is exactly the modularity the handbook asks for.
justification.a8: Documentation is uneven across the two places it has to live. On the Registry, the collection's core parts are genuinely well documented: Fre-L3-SttH (BBa_26TZ7VWJ) carries design, experiment, application and discussion sections totalling about 7,800 characters, and all seven tnaA alleles plus native MaFMO and the P43 cassette carry experiment, characterisation and discussion entries. But I checked roughly 30 of the other submitted parts and found sequence and a one-line description only - including the plasmid-level devices the team says "actually ran in our experiments" (BBa_266WXW7Z, BBa_26MBNFQZ), the alternative fusions Fre-L3-PyrH and Fre-L3-RebH, and the PHB basic parts. The wiki itself is excellent and would let a team rebuild the work, but parts are judged on the Registry, so this lands at 3.5.
justification.w1: A reader can state the aim, chassis, parts and criterion after the home and description pages: the problem (surface labels can be copied), the idea (PHB plus biosynthesised indigoids giving a material-level optical fingerprint), the chassis (E. coli, two compatible plasmids), and how it is read (5 LEDs x 4 backgrounds x 3 channels = 60 values). The home page uses one schematic per idea in the Lambert_GA manner and the description opens with a stated research question. It is a long scroll and some of the home-page sections repeat the counterfeiting framing, which keeps it just below a 4.5.
justification.w2: Claims are supported with real numbers and figures throughout, and the team is unusually disciplined about labelling what each result is. Replicates and statistics are given (n=3, mean ± SEM, t-tests on Results Figs 3B and 4B), controls are named, tables carry units (DN, mm, g/L), and limits are stated next to the result rather than hidden - for example that three tags cannot establish batch reproducibility (Results Part 3, section 6) and that the software's synthetic rates "do not establish authentication performance on physical tags". The main reservation is provenance: the Measurement tag series is built on quantified indigo and indirubin standards whose source (own cultures vs purchased) is never stated.
justification.w3: Navigation is coherent - Project / Wet Lab / Dry Lab / Engagement, with a per-page table of contents and sensible cross-links between Engineering, Results, Parts and Contribution. Against that, several standard pages return nothing: Attributions renders empty, and Proof of Concept, Implementation, Model, Design, Protocols, Inclusivity and Entrepreneurship are all 404 in the crawl. Protocol content exists but lives under Experiments, and the lab notebook page is a single PDF link with no on-page content, so a judge following the standard menu hits dead ends where key material should be.
justification.w4: The Contribution page is written exactly for the next team: parts with reasons to use them, a table of conditions that worked, a list of what failed (three silent halogenases, codon optimisation, the A. lata construct) and two ways of misreading results that caught them out. The hardware page adds a bill of materials, print settings, STL file names, firmware settings and an assembly checklist - enough that four outside students rebuilt the instrument from it. Marks come off for the empty attributions page, the notebook existing only as a PDF link, and the open-hardware package being described as "to be released" rather than released.
justification.w5: Citations are numerous, numbered per page and carry DOIs; the description closes with a References and Figure Sources section, and the team repeatedly engages with its sources rather than name-dropping them - reconciling its own tnaA values against Li and Young 2015 and explaining why the two disagree, and attributing the Fre-L3 fusion format and SttH to Lee et al. 2021. Statistics quoted from OECD/EUIPO and the Korean MOIP are given with scope caveats. I did not verify every reference resolves, and a few figure-level image credits are implied rather than stated, which keeps this at 4.

J2.one_line: An unusually complete high-school engineering project - real DBTL in both wet lab and hardware, a thoughtfully modular parts collection, and candid limits - held back by an empty attributions page and by the fact that the system was never assembled or tested as an authentication device.
strengths: Five wet-lab DBTL cycles where a measured result changed the next build, plus five hardware generations driven by exposure, white-balance and repeatability data (Engineering page; Hardware Tables 7, 8, 15, 17)
Controls and replicates throughout: empty-vector and catalytic-null (K270A) controls, n=3 with SEM and t-tests, colony PCR at 773 vs 1739 bp, FTIR and Nile red confocal confirming the polymer is PHB
A genuinely reusable parts collection - seven tnaA alleles as a graded rate slot, six halogenase fusions in one format, two co-resident backbones - with explicit reuse instructions on the Parts page

A purpose-built reader that was measured, not just built: LED centre wavelengths verified against laboratory instruments, repeatability of 1.28 DN MAE over a week, and a separation index used to justify four backgrounds over a sixth LED
Four Hanyang University students rebuilt the instrument from the released documentation alone, with the developers taking no part (Hardware 9.2)

Human Practices that changed the project - Dr. Son's challenge removed an unexamined sustainability claim, Prof. Cunningham's advice changed how the RGB data are described, and visitor questions produced the imitation comparison
A Contribution page written for the next team, including what failed and two ways the team misread its own results
weaknesses: The Attributions page is empty, so the division of work between students, instructors and outside helpers cannot be checked at all
The two modules were never combined in one cell - the team states it has not run the double transformant - so the headline 'one cell, two products' claim is designed but unbuilt
No authentication performance exists: the classifier was evaluated on synthetic data only, and false acceptance and false rejection on physical tags are acknowledged as untested
Roughly 30 of the 45 submitted parts, including the plasmid devices that actually ran, are Registry stubs with sequence and a one-line description
Several standard pages (Proof of Concept, Implementation, Model, Design, Protocols) are 404, and the notebook page is only a PDF link
No LC-MS, so the pigment product is a tentatively assigned mixture and residual 618 nm absorbance shows halogenation is incomplete
Provenance of the indigo and indirubin used in the 60-feature tag series is never stated - if these were purchased standards, the optical characterisation is partly decoupled from the biology
red_flags: Attributions page renders empty on both the crawl and the live site (https://2026.igem.wiki/psi-korea/attributions/): no attribution form content, no who-did-what, and no acknowledgement of outside contributors the project pages do mention (CRETION for the imitation samples, four Hanyang University students for the second reader, Prof. Park's offer of laboratory instruments, and access to confocal, FTIR and UV-Vis instruments)

The Measurement tag series is built on quantified indigo and indirubin 'standards' whose source is never stated; the Human Practices page separately records a plan to use commercially available PHB and indigo. A Q&A question, not an accusation - but it matters for how much of the optical work rests on the team's own biology

Minor inconsistency to ask about: the Safety page says source organisms were not cultured and genes were obtained as synthesised or cloned sequences, while Results Part 1 says the phaCAB operons were amplified from genomic DNA of C. necator KCTC 22469 and A. lata KACC 15149. Both are RG1 organisms, so this is a documentation question rather than a safety concern

Several standard pages return not-found (proof-of-concept, implementation, model, design, protocols, inclusivity, entrepreneurship), which the handbook warns against since judges are not required to hunt for content
pages_read: Registry API records and documentation sections for BBa_26TZ7VWJ, BBa_26QYYVV5, BBa_26HR5VUJ, BBa_26OHLQJP, BBa_26I40MCD, BBa_26O85S4V, BBa_26OUEDU0, BBa_26PG9R5O, BBa_26RHWVOZ, BBa_26ZWI5MC, BBa_26UTMV8R, BBa_2656P61X, BBa_26LN3L31, BBa_263HP7BU, BBa_266WXW7Z, BBa_26MBNFQZ, BBa_26DEZI2K, BBa_26LWQ4YG, BBa_2600Z3PD and ~15 further submitted parts

calibrated.changed: a6 1.5->2.0: I scored other empty-attribution teams with role titles on the team page at 2.0 (labi-taiwan, hk-joint-school), and 1.5 was reserved in my head for a team with no role information anywhere — squirrel-guangzhou fits that better and still got 2.0. Correcting down to the common bar.

justification.a1: Two biosynthetic modules (PHB from phaCAB; indigo and 6,6'-halogenated indigoids from tryptophan) carried from construct to purified material, plus a 3D-printed multi-LED reader, a verification app and 45+ Registry parts, with the project climbing through genuinely harder steps (host choice, tnaA deletion, variant tuning, halogenase regioselectivity, film fabrication, optical readout) — the GreatBay-style ladder. It stops short of a 5 because the keystone was never built: Contribution states plainly "we have not run the double transformant ourselves", so the one-cell co-production that the whole concept rests on remains a design, and authentication accuracy is untested.
justification.a2: The core biology is demonstrated with controls and replicates: PHB yield gravimetric n=3 with SEM and t-tests (BL21-AI 30 C ~135% induced increase; C. necator 0.105 vs A. lata 0.088 g/g, p<0.05), Nile red confocal against an empty-vector control, and FTIR with the 1719.71 cm-1 ester carbonyl (Results Part 1). Part 2 adds a standard-curve titer (0.86 vs 0.23 g/L), colony PCR of the tnaA deletion (773 bp vs 1,739 bp), a K270A catalytic-null control, and absorption spectra shifting 618 to 560/562 nm. Held back from 5 because no LC-MS means the halogenated products stay tentative assignments, residual 618 nm absorbance shows halogenation is incomplete, and the Software page states that discrimination on physical tags "has not yet been measured".
justification.a3: The need is documented with sourced figures and unusually honest scoping on Human Practices (OECD/EUIPO USD 467 bn; EUIPO EUR 3 bn for EU cosmetics; MOIP blocked-listing counts explicitly labelled as an enforcement indicator, not prevalence), and four cosmetics companies plus two authentication providers were asked what blocks adoption. IEUM&Co. agreed to supply real cosmetic products for attachment studies, which gives a concrete route in. It is a 4 rather than a 5 because nothing has yet been tested in the real setting: no tag has been attached to packaging, the ~USD 0.10 target is flagged as an unverified goal, and the only imitation tested was watercolour on paper.
justification.a4: Five DBTL cycles on the Engineering page each turn on a specific failure: BL21(DE3) turning blue before induction, CgFMO giving no pigment with a halogenase, codon optimisation losing 3.7-fold, TnaA outrunning the halogenase, and three of six halogenases giving nothing. Each Learn changed the next Build, with quantitative criteria and a frank statement of what was not measured (variant protein levels). The hardware iterated too, moving from smartphone to fixed camera module after within-tag spread (20.4) exceeded between-specimen distances (3.81-6.62). Short of 5 only because no model fitted to their own data was then used to predict or design, the way TAS's dosing calculator was.
justification.a5: The 4A loop is applied consistently to named stakeholders — Prof. Kang Sungsoo, two consultations with Prof. Youngkyung Park, Dr. Jina Son, Prof. Brian Cunningham by email, four cosmetics companies, Pinsheng, NEMOIN and HiddenTag — and the integration table in section 09 states each input, its effect and the remaining evidence boundary. Real changes followed: a fixed camera module, LED characterisation, holding out whole specimens when setting thresholds, and a parallel commercial-material route after Dr. Son challenged the PHB rationale. It is a 4 rather than 5 because a large share of the Adaptation entries are deferred priorities rather than changes already made, and the ~100 Maker Faire visitors and the school sessions with minors carry no mention of consent or ethics oversight.
justification.a6: This is the project's weak point: https://2026.igem.wiki/psi-korea/attributions/ renders as "Not Found", so the wiki contains no account of who did what. The Team page gives role titles only (Experiment Leader, Hardware Leader and so on), and the only task-level attribution I could find is on the Registry entries themselves, where BBa_26TZ7VWJ credits Seongbin Cho and eunseo yoon with Investigation/Methodology and Chris Song with Supervision. Outside help is named where it occurs (CRETION made the watercolour imitations; four Hanyang mechanical engineering students rebuilt the reader as a reproducibility test), which is good practice, but with lambda-Red recombineering, confocal microscopy, FTIR, a custom PCB and firmware on the page and two PIs, three instructors and an advisor listed, I cannot tell from the wiki which hands did the bench and analysis work. I record this as a question for the session, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The collection is the strongest synthetic-biology argument here: basic CDSs (three PHB enzymes from two source organisms, two FMOs, seven tnaA alleles, six halogenases at ring positions 5, 6 and 7), composite Fre-L3 fusions in one identical format, the P43-creRBS constitutive cassette, and plasmid-level devices built as a compatible pair (pBR322/Amp with p15A/Cm) so both modules can sit in one cell. The tnaA series is explicitly designed as an interchangeable slot spanning 3-100% of wild-type output, which is reusable far beyond this project, and the three C. necator pha genes are honestly flagged as duplicates of BBa_K089001-3. Hardware and software add standard components.
justification.a8: Registry entries are real and substantive: BBa_26TZ7VWJ carries sequence with annotated sub-parts, topology, GC content, host, RFC10/RFC1000 export, biosafety screening and four documentation sections (Design, Experiment, Application, Discussion), so the part data do not live only on the wiki. The Parts and Contribution pages add collection-level documentation, a conditions table, a what-did-not-work section and two named pitfalls in reading one's own results. Marked down slightly because the Lab Notebook page is a bare link to a PDF (85 words of page text) and the hardware fabrication, executable and verification packages are described as being prepared rather than released.
justification.w1: The Description page opens with a clear statement of the system and the research question ("Do independently fabricated tags with the same composition show similar optical responses...?"), and the home page walks a reader from the counterfeiting problem to the two-plasmid design and the reader. The home page is a long scroll-driven narrative, though, and the actual mechanism (phaCAB plus FMO/tnaA, halogenase added) only arrives well down it, so a judge in a hurry reaches the science slowly.
justification.w2: Documentation of evidence is the wiki's best feature. Claims carry figures with controls, units, n and error bars; statistics are named (unpaired two-tailed t-test, p values, mean +/- SEM, n=3); and measured, modelled, synthetic and planned results are separated explicitly and repeatedly — the Software page states up front that acceptance of genuine tags and rejection of unregistered ones "have not yet been evaluated" and that synthetic rates do not establish performance, and Results Part 3 closes by saying the work "do[es] not establish authentication accuracy or resistance to replication". Not a 5 only because the central product claim still has no physical-tag evidence behind it.
justification.w3: Within a page the design works well: every long page has its own contents menu, and Parts, Contribution, Engineering and Results cross-link to each other. But eight standard URLs return Not Found (attributions, proof-of-concept, implementation, model, protocols, design, inclusivity, entrepreneurship), and the missing Attributions page is the one a judge is directed to. Several pages are also very long (Hardware ~12,300 words, Software ~7,500, Measurement ~7,100) with material repeated between Description, Results and Measurement, which is closer to sprawling than to "complete but not sprawling".
justification.w4: A future team is unusually well served: 16 protocols on the Experiments page, a Contribution page written explicitly as "what you can take" with a working-conditions table, three things that did not work, and two ways of misreading your own results; hardware print settings (Bambu Lab P1S, PLA, 0.4 mm nozzle, 0.20 mm layer, 15% infill), a priced parts list and a session data-record specification. The independent rebuild by four students working from the documentation alone is exactly the right test of reproducibility. Short of 5 because the notebook is a single PDF, no raw data files are posted, and the release packages are still in preparation.
justification.w5: Every page carries numbered references with DOIs, and the ones I checked resolve and support what is claimed (Lee et al. 2021 10.1038/s41589-020-00684-4; Li and Young 2015 10.1186/s12866-015-0346-3; Na et al. 2026 10.1038/s41467-025-67935-7; Li et al. 2024 10.1016/j.ymben.2023.11.003). The team also credits CRETION for the imitation samples, flags its own Registry duplicates, and lists figure sources. The clear lapse is on Results Part 2: "A codon-optimized MaFMO sequence had been used by an earlier iGEM team" — prior iGEM work is acknowledged in the abstract but the team is never named or linked.

J3.one_line: A deep, unusually honest two-module project (PHB plus halogenated indigoid) with five real DBTL cycles, a validated custom reader and 45+ documented Registry parts, let down by a missing Attributions page and an unbuilt one-cell capstone.
strengths: Five documented DBTL cycles on the Engineering page, each driven by a named failure (BL21(DE3) leaking blue before induction, CgFMO dead with a halogenase, codon optimisation losing 3.7-fold, three of six halogenases giving no pigment) and each changing the next build

Core biology shown with controls and replicates: Nile red confocal against empty vector, FTIR at 1719.71 cm-1, K270A as a catalytic-null control, n=3 with SEM and t-tests, and absorption maxima shifting from 618 nm to 560/562 nm against an authentic indigo standard

A genuinely reusable part collection: seven tnaA alleles spanning 3-100% of wild-type output as an interchangeable tuning slot, six halogenase fusions in one identical Fre-L3 format, and two plasmid backbones chosen as a compatible origin/marker pair

Measurement discipline that is rare at any level: 60 RGB features defined and ordered, MAE/RMSE/Pearson r reported for repeats (r >= 0.9977, pooled MAE 3.58 DN) and for imitations, with repeated explicit statements of what the numbers do not establish

Human Practices organised as traceable Aspiration-Action-Analysis-Adaptation loops with named experts and companies, and an integration table that distinguishes what changed from what is still only a priority

A Contribution page written for the next team, with working conditions, what did not work, and two specific ways the team was misled by its own results, plus a reader rebuilt from the documentation alone by four independent builders
weaknesses: The Attributions page returns Not Found, and no page on the wiki says which student did which experiment, analysis, build or figure; only the Registry entries carry per-part contributor roles

The one-cell co-production that the whole concept depends on was never demonstrated: Contribution states the double transformant was not run, and tags were made by mixing separately produced PHB with pigment

Authentication performance is unmeasured. The verification software was tested on synthetic data only, and the sole imitation tried was watercolour on paper, with substrate and pigment system both differing from the real tag
No LC-MS, so the halogenated indigoid identities and the proportions of mono-halogenated and unsubstituted species remain tentative assignments from spectra

Eight standard page URLs 404 (attributions, proof-of-concept, implementation, model, protocols, design, inclusivity, entrepreneurship), while Hardware, Software and Measurement run to 7,000-12,000 words each with substantial repetition of Results
No mention of consent or ethics oversight for the ~100 Maker Faire visitors or the school sessions, and the prior iGEM team whose codon-optimized MaFMO sequence is referenced is never named
red_flags: Attributions page is absent (renders as Not Found), so the division of work between students, two PIs, three instructors and an advisor cannot be assessed from the wiki — a question for the session, not an accusation
Lab Notebook page is a single PDF link with no browsable record on the wiki
Software performance figures come from synthetic data; the team labels this clearly and repeatedly, so I treat it as a limitation rather than an integrity issue
A prior iGEM team's codon-optimized MaFMO sequence is referenced without naming or linking that team (Results Part 2)

calibrated.changed: none. a8 of 4.5 is the only one at that level besides Hangzhou, and both rest on Registry pages I could actually open and read, which is the distinction I held to throughout.

one_line.en: A complete two-module project with five real DBTL cycles, a reusable graded part collection and a reader rebuilt by independent builders, held back by an empty attributions page and a one-cell capstone that was never built.
one_line.zh: 完整的雙模組專案，五個真實 DBTL 循環、可重用的分級零件集，讀取器還被獨立團隊依文件重建，但歸屬頁空白、單細胞共產目標從未建成。

strengths: Controls and replicates throughout, including empty-vector and catalytic-null controls, with FTIR and confocal staining used together to confirm the polymer
A genuinely reusable parts collection: seven alleles as a graded tuning slot with a stated working window and host requirement
A purpose-built reader that was measured rather than asserted, with verified LED wavelengths and week-long repeatability, rebuilt from documentation alone by four outside students
Limits written beside the claims throughout, and a Contribution page recording two ways the team misread its own results
weaknesses: The Attributions page is empty, so the division of work between students, two PIs, three instructors and an advisor cannot be checked
The headline one-cell co-production was never run; tags were made by mixing separately produced material
Authentication performance is untested: the classifier was evaluated on synthetic data and only one imitation pair was tried
No mass spectrometry, so the pigment product is a tentatively assigned mixture, and many submitted parts are Registry stubs
red_flags: Attributions page renders empty on the live site despite named outside contributors elsewhere on the wiki
Source-organism inconsistency between the Description and Safety pages
Provenance of the indigo and indirubin used in the tag series is never stated
One Registry entry shows a biosafety screening status that iGEM reviewed and published; noted for the record

screen.project_title: Butyrate-producing E. coli Nissle 1917 with a self-limiting feedback circuit for early Alzheimer's prevention
screen.what_they_built: EcN carrying a five-enzyme butyrate pathway (HBD-CRT-TER on one plasmid, PTB-BUK on another) plus a PpchA-LacI-Ptac negative-feedback circuit to cap butyrate, and pNorVb/PpchA-PLEE1 EGFP biosensors for nitric oxide and butyrate. Supported by a two-part gut-to-blood DDE model, a capsule-dispensing device and a cognitive-screening app.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli Nissle 1917 (and BL21 for some work); 9 new Registry parts (BBa_269U4PRD PTB-BUK, BBa_26NNM850 HBD-CRT-TER, BBa_26ZJNPZO LacI-PpchA-Ptac-HBD-CRT-TER, BBa_26ISJMG9, plus basic PTB/BUK/HBD/CRT/TER) and 4 existing parts reused (BBa_K4442001, BBa_K4387005, BBa_K4751009, BBa_K864400). Plasmids were synthesized by VectorBuilder.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /engineering: HPLC on co-transformed EcN showed ~5.0 mM butyrate over 24 h versus control, against a pre-set success criterion of >2 mM, with Western blots at the expected masses for PTB (32.23 kDa) and BUK (39.79 kDa) after the redesign and RT-qPCR confirming HBD/CRT/TER transcription. Cell work on /results: sodium butyrate restored viability to ~88-90% against 2 mM glutamate in dHT22 cells with EC50 = 88.84 uM, and Tau-EGFP-P301L aggregates fell dose-dependently from 100% to 72.74% (1 mM) and 11.47% (300 mM).
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and traceably: clinicians at Conde S. Januario explained that clearing late-stage biomarkers rarely stops decline, which moved the target population to cognitively healthy older adults; Prof. Ivy Cheng's advice drove the RAW264.7 to BV-2 to HT22 to Tau-P301L sequence of cell experiments; MUST's Prof. Zhu flagged moisture in powder dispensing, which turned hardware v2 into a capsule system.
screen.reason: The strongest experimental package in the batch: a multi-plasmid pathway that failed for a diagnosable reason (no T7 polymerase in EcN, incompatible pET origins), was rebuilt on Ptac/pSC101 and then produced measurable butyrate, with independent cell-level evidence and an honestly reported negative result (no M1-to-M2 switch). Deserves a full read. The panel should probe aspect 6 hard: plasmids were ordered from VectorBuilder, all four cell lines came from Prof. Cheng, and the HPLC was run at MUST, so how much the students executed is the open question. Also check the lorem-ipsum /experiments page and the empty /parts page.
screen.field_notes: Macau high-school team (Therapeutics) engineering E. coli Nissle 1917 to make butyrate in the gut lumen as an early, pre-diagnosis Alzheimer's intervention, with a PpchA-LacI-Ptac feedback loop to keep butyrate inside the 1-10 mM non-toxic window. Cycle 1 failed outright (T7 inactive in EcN; two pET plasmids sharing an origin cannot be co-maintained) and cycle 2 on Ptac/pSC101 succeeded, giving ~5.0 mM butyrate by HPLC plus Western and RT-qPCR confirmation. Independent cell data: EC50 88.84 uM for protection against glutamate excitotoxicity in dHT22, dose-dependent suppression of Tau-P301L aggregation to 11.47% at 300 mM, and a clean negative result ruling out M1-to-M2 macrophage/microglia polarization as the mechanism. Nine new Registry parts; a delay-differential gut-to-blood pharmacokinetic model; an ESP32-based capsule dispenser (v3) and a gamified cognitive screen field-tested in two Macau care settings. Heavy university support (University of Macau cell lines, MUST HPLC access after their own GC-FID failed) is disclosed; the wiki still carries a template /experiments page of placeholder text and an empty /parts page.

screen.project_title: Yeauty: hyaluronic acid production in engineered Komagataella pastoris
screen.what_they_built: Built an HA biosynthesis pathway in Pichia/Komagataella pastoris by heterologous UGD and HAS expression, screened three HAS sources, then balanced UDP-GlcA and UDP-GlcNAc precursor supply with a P2A-linked UGD-UAP cassette, and scaled to a 5 L fermenter with an automated methanol-feeding device.
screen.chassis_and_parts: K. pastoris X33, pPICZ A vectors, AOX1/ADH2 promoters; 18 parts registered (11 basic, 7 composite) including SzHAS, XlHAS, PmHAS, BsUGD, EcUAP and T2A/P2A/E2A peptides.
screen.best_evidence: /results: SzH-6 reached 0.96 +/- 0.12 g/L intracellular HA (38.10 mg/g CDW); HPLC-MS/MS of 2-AMAC-labelled ChABC digest confirmed HA disaccharide identity (m/z 572.19, B1 157.01); optimized HAT22 reached 1.71 +/- 0.08 g/L, ~78% higher, with qPCR showing balanced UGD/UAP; 5 L fermenter gave 3.97 +/- 0.15 g/L after 120 h.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — /human-practices tracks Idea V1 to V4 after a visit to HA manufacturer Freda, 38 consumer and 14 beautician interviews, which pushed the project towards endotoxin-free purity and molecular-weight control.
screen.reason: Strong, properly controlled quantitative chain: enzyme screen, structural confirmation by HPLC-MS/MS, model-guided precursor balancing with a 78% improvement, and 5 L scale-up to 3.97 g/L. Concerns for the panel: plasmids were commercially synthesized, HPLC-MS/MS was run by Ocean University of China's testing centre, and the wiki is short on raw data, so aspect 6 needs checking. Still worth a full read.
screen.field_notes: Qingdao-China (Fashion & Cosmetics, CHN) engineered Komagataella pastoris to make hyaluronic acid, arguing yeast avoids bacterial LPS endotoxin and allows molecular-weight control. They compared three HA synthases (SzHAS, XlHAS, PmHAS) each paired with BsUGD in pPICZ A dual cassettes; SzHAS clone SzH-6 gave the highest intracellular titer, 0.96 +/- 0.12 g/L (38.10 mg/g CDW), with no HA secreted. Product identity was confirmed by ChABC digestion, 2-AMAC derivatization and HPLC-MS/MS run by Ocean University of China's analysis centre. An FBA model on iMT1026 predicted a 1:1 UGD:UAP optimum, so they screened T2A, P2A and E2A with an mCherry/eGFP-NLS dual reporter by confocal microscopy, chose P2A, and co-expressed BsUGD-P2A-EcUAP with SzHAS: strain HAT22 reached 1.71 +/- 0.08 g/L, about 78% above SzH-6, with qPCR confirming balanced transcript levels, and 3.97 +/- 0.15 g/L after 120 h in a 5 L fermenter. Supporting work includes 18 Registry parts, an AureoFlow methanol fed-batch controller, and a per-member attribution page; several plasmids were commercially synthesized.

screen.project_title: UPKeep — converting Ulva prolifera green-tide biomass into ulvan oligosaccharide cosmetic ingredients
screen.what_they_built: A two-part enzymatic process: a free (non-cell-anchored) cellulosome built from screened cellulase modules plus scaffoldin to open the Ulva cell wall, and an INPNC-Uly1040 surface-display fusion for ulvan depolymerisation, with an iron-responsive safety switch and cosmetic functional testing of the resulting oligosaccharides.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3), Rosetta and endotoxin-free ClearColi; pET-22b(+)/pET-28a(+). Only two new BBa IDs appear (BBa_26MNB4WT, BBa_26420DD5) and the Parts page is empty in the crawl — a real documentation gap.
screen.best_evidence: /results PART 02: purified Cel9A specific activity 21.1 U/mg (DNS, 1% CMC, pH 5.5, 50 °C, 30 min, glucose standard curve) with pH, temperature and time optima mapped and activity retained after prolonged 50 °C incubation; purified Uly1040 11.22 U/mg by A235; whole-cell INPNC- vs PelB-Uly1040 activity comparison; PART 05 iron-responsive switch gives lower OD600 in iron-deficient than iron-replete medium over 24 h.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, explicitly tabulated: Seawin/Vland advice split the two reactions into separate steps (D02), CCiC peers and a cellulosome researcher pushed them off a cell-anchored cellulosome to a free one (D04), and stakeholders added desalting and endotoxin checks to sample assessment.
screen.reason: The only team in this batch besides GreatBay-SCIE with purified, quantified enzyme activity plus downstream product function (moisture uptake, water retention, hydroxyl-radical scavenging against HA and glycerol) and a tested containment switch, on a five-version design history driven by a documented stakeholder decision table. Worth a full read, but flag the gaps: Parts and Attributions pages are empty and only two new registry parts are traceable, so aspects 7-8 are weak for a top-2 claim.
screen.field_notes: QingdaoAcademy 2026 (UPKeep, Fashion & Cosmetics, CHN) valorises Ulva prolifera green-tide biomass into ulvan oligosaccharides for cosmetics. Seven candidate enzymes were screened by colony PCR and SDS-PAGE; only Cel9A and Uly1040 gave reliable soluble expression, and the results page documents the failures in detail (Cel6B and Cel9B-C never gave clean bands, cell-free expression produced fluorescent GFP controls but no resolvable product bands, BglC showed two overexpression bands until retransformation). Purified Cel9A: 21.1 U/mg on CMC by DNS, optima pH 5.5 and 60 °C, activity retained at 50 °C but lost at 60-70 °C over long incubation. Purified Uly1040: 11.22 U/mg by A235, with substrate-specificity comparison against alginate and chondroitin sulfate. INPNC surface display gave whole-cell activity similar to PelB in both ClearColi and Rosetta; induction was optimised down to 0.05 mM IPTG. An iron-responsive safety switch suppressed growth in EDTA medium relative to iron-replete over 24 h, with viable counts named as the missing next measurement. Oligosaccharide product testing followed patent CN103767888A for water retention and compared against hyaluronic acid and glycerol. Design went through five versions driven by a published decision table (Seawin, Vland, Bright Moon, CCiC peers). Parts and Attributions pages are empty, the main documentation liability.

screen.project_title: GlacierGuard — engineered bacterial-cellulose composite membrane for localized glacier protection
screen.what_they_built: A biodegradable bacterial cellulose membrane to replace synthetic geotextiles on glaciers, built from three engineered systems: heterologous bcsABCD cellulose production in E. coli with a pgm-galU precursor boost, UreABC urease-driven CaCO3 biomineralization for whitening and reflectance, and CspA cold-shock expression for low-temperature fermentation. Membranes were then tested as a material.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli C41(DE3) (chosen over BL21(DE3)) and BL21(DE3); pET-28a, RFC#10-compatible codon-optimised synthesis. 10 BBa parts covering bcsABCD, pgm-galU, ureABC and cspA modules.
screen.best_evidence: /results: completing the cluster raised BC titre stepwise from 3.5 +/- 1.0 mg/L (empty vector) to 3.8 +/- 0.7 (bcsAB), 47.1 +/- 16.4 (bcsABC) and 230.6 +/- 15.3 mg/L (bcsABCD) — 65.9x, n = 3 biological replicates — with Western blots at the predicted masses for all four Bcs proteins; PGM activity 47.97 +/- 7.95 vs 4.58 +/- 1.24 (10.5x), GalU 17.2x, CaCO3 25.00 +/- 2.61 mM (7.0x control), CspA giving 1.86x GFP/OD600 at 15 C. At material level, BC membranes beat geotextile ice retention by 3.2 percentage points under simulated day-night cycling and gained 842.0% mass after 1 h immersion.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — 27 interviews, site visits to the LZU Chayu and CAS alpine stations, an Azha glacier field trip and 440 survey responses are run through an explicit Why-How-What-Adaptation loop whose fourth step records the design, safety and application changes each interaction produced.
screen.reason: The most complete package in the batch and the one that best matches the handbook's finalist anchors: replicated quantitative data on three independent engineered systems, a stepwise gene-cluster experiment that actually explains the 65.9x result, honest reporting of the two things that failed (thyme-oil hydrophobic coating, light attenuation), material-level testing against the real incumbent (geotextile), and HP that visits the actual deployment site and feeds back into design. Read in full.
