Two things to check: there is no /attributions page at all, and the AI-screened BcsD variants (1,855 candidates, W19R + G113E top-scoring) were never built or tested, so that work is prediction only.
screen.field_notes: RDFZ-China (Conservation village, China) built GlacierGuard, a bacterial-cellulose composite membrane as a biodegradable alternative to the synthetic geotextiles currently laid on melting glaciers. System 1 moved the bcsABCD cellulose synthase cluster into E. coli, found C41(DE3) beats BL21(DE3) (183.7 +/- 18.6 vs 58.4 +/- 14.5 mg/L) and attributed it to gentler T7 drive easing membrane-protein insertion load, then showed BC titre climbing with cluster completeness to 230.6 +/- 15.3 mg/L (65.9x empty vector, n = 3), with all four Bcs proteins detected by anti-His Western. A pgm-galU module raised PGM and GalU activity 10.5x and 17.2x to strengthen UDP-glucose supply, not yet integrated into the producing strain. An AI screen (ESM-C plus MuZero/MCTS over AlphaFold structures, scored against Rosetta) generated 1,855 BcsD variants with a 24% in-silico hit rate against genetic algorithms at 10%, but none were built. System 2 (UreABC urease, Ni2+-boosted) gave 25.00 +/- 2.61 mM CaCO3, 7x control, for whitening. System 3 (CspA) gave 1.86x GFP/OD600 at 15 C. Material tests compared membranes against geotextile for ice retention, measured 842% water uptake, and reported honestly that the thyme-oil hydrophobic coating did not work and light attenuation is insufficient. Human practices ran 27 interviews plus 440 surveys through a documented adaptation loop including alpine research stations and an Azha glacier field trip. No attributions page is published.

screen.project_title: FusionDrive: anti-TIGIT–IL-2v fusion protein for gastric cancer immunotherapy
screen.what_they_built: A full-length anti-TIGIT antibody fused via a (G4S)4 linker to an engineered IL-2 variant (lowα/highβ: F42A/Y45A/L72G + L80F/R81D/L85V/I86V/I92F), expressed in CHO cells. Three molecular formats (antibody, WT-IL-2 fusion, IL-2v fusion) were built and compared.
screen.chassis_and_parts: CHO cells for expression (chosen after iGEM Safety Committee advice), Jurkat E6-1 for functional testing, E. coli DH5α for cloning; pEE6.4 vector, Gibson assembly. 11 registry parts: 7 basic (VH, CH1, Fc, VL, CL, IL-2-WT, IL-2v) and 4 composite CMV-driven expression cassettes (BBa_26LQJFHQ, BBa_26Q5QY6M, BBa_269JOVIU etc.).
screen.best_evidence: TIGIT-binding ELISA EC50 values of 0.6317 nM (antibody), 1.335 nM (WT fusion) and 1.155 nM (IL-2v fusion), plus flow cytometry showing 99.4% pSTAT5-positive Jurkat cells at 100 nM WT fusion versus no pSTAT5 response to antibody alone (/alternative-platform §3.2–3.3 and /engineering Cycles 1–2). In the PHA-induced CD25 model (5 µg/mL, 24 h, ~50% CD25+, ~80% viability) the IL-2v fusion showed a greater signalling reduction in CD25+ than CD25− cells (/alternative-platform §4).
screen.hp_integration: Yes — Prof. Liu Zhifang (antibody engineering) told them to re-test binding after adding modules, which is why TIGIT ELISA was run separately on all three formats; the iGEM Safety Committee's advice drove the choice of CHO over other hosts and the Jurkat quality documentation.
screen.reason: Genuinely ambitious mammalian antibody engineering for a high school team, with real binding curves and flow data across five cycles. Held back from finalist calibre by three things: the Attributions page is empty (62 words of boilerplate) so the student/host-lab boundary cannot be judged, there is no Results page at all (data is scattered across Engineering and a non-standard Alternative Platform page), and no replicate counts, error bars or statistics are reported for any of the key numbers. The central selectivity claim rests on a PHA-induced Jurkat surrogate that the team itself says does not establish Treg-versus-effector selectivity.
screen.field_notes: SEHS (Shandong, CHN, Oncology village) built FusionDrive, an anti-TIGIT antibody–IL-2v fusion aimed at gastric cancer, motivated by the high regional gastric cancer burden and framed as a 'local people, local problems' project. Three formats (anti-TIGIT, anti-TIGIT–IL-2, anti-TIGIT–IL-2v) were expressed in CHO cells and compared across five DBTL cycles; TIGIT-binding ELISA gave EC50s of 0.6317, 1.335 and 1.155 nM, and 100 nM WT fusion drove 99.4% pSTAT5-positive Jurkat cells where the bare antibody drove none. A notable assay-debugging episode: the first ELISA saturated because TIGIT-Fc coating was recognised by the anti-human-IgG1-HRP detector, fixed by switching to His-tagged TIGIT. Because the iGEM white list barred primary T cells and tumour lines, they used PHA (5 µg/mL, 24 h) to upregulate CD25 in Jurkat cells as a stand-in for the high-CD25 Treg phenotype — a reusable workaround they document as a contribution. They registered 11 parts (7 basic, 4 composite CMV cassettes) and built a compact organoid-chip optical detection device as hardware. Safety work is unusually thorough: documented correspondence with the iGEM Safety and Security Committee, an ATCC Certificate of Analysis for the Jurkat lot, and a dual-use forum with Shandong University experts. The wiki has no Results page and an empty Attributions page.

screen.project_title: Multi-wavelength optogenetic living biosensor for light pollution and avian ecological risk
screen.what_they_built: Three light-sensing reporter circuits in E. coli - red (PhyA/FHY1 split RNAP with HO1-PcyA chromophore synthesis), green (CcaS/CcaR) and blue (AsLOV2) - all reporting through firefly luciferase, intended as a low-cost biological front-end screen for artificial light at night translated into bird risk levels.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5alpha and BL21(DE3); pETDuet, pCDFDuet and pET28a three-plasmid co-transformation with separate origins and resistances. 15 new BBa parts plus reused Registry parts (BBa_B0034, BBa_K3521000/2/4, BBa_K566021, BBa_K613000, BBa_R0051 and others); a part-collection page is present.
screen.best_evidence: /results 3.2: Fluc assay of the red circuit across a red-light power gradient and a duty-cycle gradient, mean +/- SD with n = 3 independent runs, significance marks to p < 0.001, dose-response fits (duty cycle linear fit R2 = 0.83, p = 0.0002; Spearman rho = +0.93) and fold-induction curves against dark and natural-light controls, plus a 140-minute time course showing activation building after ~60 min. Green channel characterised over power, pulse frequency (optimum 60 Hz) and duty cycle (optimum ~20%); blue channel only preliminary.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, in five documented cycles: a public questionnaire, an urban lighting specialist asking what decision a measurement should support, an avian ecologist warning against a human-centred interpretation of light, a Dongtan wetland field visit that reset the measurement requirements, and an optogenetics expert review on biosafety and product trade-offs, with an explicit record of changes adopted versus deferred.
screen.reason: The red and green modules are characterised to a standard rarely seen at high school level: independent biological replicates, dark and natural-light controls, statistics, and three orthogonal tuning axes (power, frequency, duty cycle). The team also report leaky uninduced expression honestly. Deserves a full read. Weak points the panel should probe: the blue channel is only a single preliminary reading, there is no model page and no hardware, and the jump from RLU to an 'avian ecological risk level' is still literature mapping rather than a demonstrated instrument.
screen.field_notes: Shanghai-city (Conservation, China) built a multi-wavelength optogenetic E. coli biosensor for artificial light at night, arguing that photometers measure physical irradiance but not biological effect, and framing the output as a bird collision and circadian-risk screen. Six recombinant plasmids were constructed by homologous recombination and Sanger-verified: pETDuet-lambdac-PhyA(1-617)-FHY1-RNAPalpha, pCDFDuet-HO1-PcyA for phycocyanobilin synthesis, pET28a-Fluc, pET28a-CcaR-Fluc, pET28a-CcaS and pET28a-AsLOV2-Fluc, deployed as three-plasmid co-transformations in BL21(DE3). SDS-PAGE across eight plasmid combinations (P1-P8) showed all components expressed at expected masses. Luciferase assays characterised the red 660 nm circuit across light power and duty cycle with n = 3 independent runs, mean +/- SD, significance testing and fold-induction analysis, plus a 140-minute time course, and the green 525 nm CcaS/CcaR circuit across power, pulse frequency (peak 60 Hz) and duty cycle (peak ~20%); the blue 470 nm module gave only a detectable RLU signal before time ran out. Leaky uninduced expression is reported rather than hidden. Human practices runs as five iterative cycles including a Dongtan field visit and expert reviews; there is no model or hardware page and no attributions page in the crawl.

screen.project_title: Brazzein production via an active inclusion body platform in E. coli and yeast
screen.what_they_built: A self-assembling-peptide active inclusion body platform (L6KD-PEP-MtuI) that lets brazzein be recovered by centrifugation and acid-triggered intein cleavage without a column, plus plasmid-based and genome-integrated brazzein expression in S. cerevisiae and computationally designed variants.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli SHuffle T7 Express on pET30a; S. cerevisiae CEN.PK2-1C, plasmid and CRISPR-Cas9 integration at the 106 locus. 16 registered BBa parts including BBa_26IBLFC4 (brazzein CDS), BBa_262Z076W (L6KD), BBa_26K5F1YM (L6KD-PT-PEP-Mtu-scar-BRZ) and three mutant CDSs.
screen.best_evidence: /results: five DBTL cycles with gels at each step. Cycle 1 SDS-PAGE shows the SUMO route failing (faint band only); the MtuI platform is reported as giving recovered brazzein confirmed by LC-MS; yeast plasmid expression is confirmed by SDS-PAGE plus anti-His Western blot (blot outsourced to a company); genome integration verified by colony PCR (2,095 bp, colonies 9-11 and 13) with an SDS-PAGE band at 10-18 kDa.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in a specific, traceable way: HP feedback that a His-tag suppresses sweetness led the team to remove it from future designs and drove the shift from plasmid to genome-integrated yeast expression for stability and biosafety.
screen.reason: Five genuine DBTL cycles with a documented failure that redirected the design (SUMO to MtuI), a column-free purification platform demonstrated on a second cargo (EGFP), both prokaryotic and eukaryotic hosts plus CRISPR genome integration, 16 registered parts and LC-MS identity confirmation. Borderline rather than clear: everything is gel-level, no yield was quantified, no sweetness or thermostability was ever measured, and the computational variants are untested, so a full read should check how much is confirmation versus characterisation.
screen.field_notes: SHSBNU-China (Food and Nutrition, China) worked on recombinant production of the sweet protein brazzein as a sugar substitute, through five DBTL cycles. Cycle 1 fused brazzein to an L6KD-SUMO self-assembling peptide to form active inclusion bodies in E. coli SHuffle T7 Express on pET30a; SDS-PAGE showed the fusion in the pellet but only a faint post-cleavage band, so the team switched to a pH-responsive MtuI intein (L6KD-PT-linker-PEP-MtuI-scar-brazzein), recovering brazzein by centrifugation and acid cleavage with LC-MS confirmation, and demonstrated the same platform with EGFP as cargo. Cycle 3 used ProteinMPNN, RosettaFold3 and GROMACS to generate roughly 1,000 variants and select RDA, GSM and E9K mutants for predicted thermostability or sweetness, all registered as parts but none tested functionally, and the team names the limitation that no taste test was possible. Cycles 4 and 5 moved to Saccharomyces cerevisiae CEN.PK2-1C: plasmid expression under pTDH3 verified by SDS-PAGE and an outsourced anti-His Western blot, then CRISPR-Cas9 integration of pTDH3-brazzein-tTDH1 at the 106 locus verified by colony PCR (2,095 bp) with an SDS-PAGE band at 10-18 kDa. The recurring 11 kDa band versus the expected 6.5 kDa is discussed against prior literature and prior iGEM teams (Harvard 2010, SZU-China 2024). Sixteen BBa parts were registered. No yield, purity, sweetness or stability measurement exists, the attributions page is only an embedded form, and safety and measurement standard pages are thin.

screen.project_title: Exploring a potential way to shorten the life cycle of rapeseed (BnDREB1C overexpression)
screen.what_they_built: They cloned the Brassica napus transcription factor BnDREB1C into pCAMBIA1300 under CaMV 35S and introduced it into Arabidopsis thaliana by Agrobacterium GV3101 floral dip. They then screened, molecularly confirmed and phenotyped transgenic plants for a shortened growth period.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Arabidopsis thaliana Col-0 as plant chassis (white-list justified, with a dedicated Alternative Platform page), E. coli DH5a cloning host, Agrobacterium GV3101; pCAMBIA1300 backbone with HPT plant marker and Kan bacterial marker; BnDREB1C basic part plus expression-cassette composite parts said to be registered (no BBa IDs appear in the crawled pages, which is a documentation gap).
screen.best_evidence: /results s6-7: RT-qPCR on five independent OV lines gave 7.2, 11.9, 8.0, 4.4 and 4.7-fold BnDREB1C over WT, all statistically significant (actin reference, 2^-ddCt), and those lines flowered roughly five days earlier than WT with taller main stems and more inflorescence branches; /alternative-platform Table 1 summarises vector (642/642 bp, 100% identity), hygromycin selection, genomic PCR, qPCR and phenotype in one chain.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in a modest way: interviews with Chongqing rapeseed growers, oil producers, retailers, consumers, a rapeseed researcher and a legal/policy expert are each followed by a Reflection and Response, and the stated integration is mainly confirmation of the short-growth-period need plus safety/consumer framing rather than a change of molecular target.
screen.reason: A complete and honest plant-synbio chain from vector to phenotype with replicated quantitative qPCR and a frank limitations list, which is a substantial high-school achievement; it sits just below the strongest teams because the headline phenotype (about five days earlier flowering) is reported qualitatively without n, statistics or a flowering-time table, the parts are not visible as BBa IDs on the crawled pages, and there is no attributions page in the crawl.
screen.field_notes: SHSD (Shanghai/Chongqing, Agriculture village) asked whether the rapeseed CBF/DREB1-type transcription factor BnDREB1C can shorten a plant's growth period, motivated by the 220-230 day winter rapeseed cycle that blocks rice-rapeseed rotation. Because Brassica napus is off the iGEM white list they used Arabidopsis thaliana as a surrogate chassis and documented that choice on a dedicated Alternative Platform page. They built pCAMBIA1300-35S-BnDREB1C by BglII/XbaI digestion plus homologous recombination, verified it by colony PCR and Sanger sequencing (642/642 bp, no mutations), transformed GV3101 and floral-dipped Col-0, then selected T0 seed on 50 mg/L hygromycin and confirmed integration by genomic PCR. RT-qPCR on five independent lines gave 4.4-11.9 fold overexpression over WT with significance stars, and those lines flowered about five days earlier with taller stems and more branches. A second engineering case compared 0.03% and 0.15% Silwet L-77 floral-dip formulations and showed that the high concentration wilted the plants, and a third case is a growth-chamber lighting/layout model run over two rounds. Human practices covered growers, oil producers, retailers, consumers, a rapeseed expert and a policy expert, and the team also got iGEM HQ to add Arabidopsis to the Registry host list and a reverse-orientation option for composite parts.

screen.project_title: PlantGuard-Dual: engineered yeast gel beads for visual drought alerting and soil water retention
screen.what_they_built: Two yeast modules in gel beads: a drought-alert bead where an osmotic-stress promoter drives the blue chromoprotein Y amilCP, and a soil-improvement bead where GPD1 drives secreted cellulose synthase (α-factor–dcsA) and hyaluronic acid synthesis (hasA–hasB). Paired with a three-level hardware system (ADRS) that reads bead colour, logs environmental data and triggers watering via an app.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. cerevisiae INVSc1 on pYES2 (URA3, 2µ, CYC1 terminator, 6×His), E. coli DH5α for cloning, Gibson/homologous assembly. 25-part collection, 17 of them new: a seven-promoter library (STL1, DDR2, PST2, GRE1, TPS1, ALD2, GPD1), Y amilCP, dcsA, hasA-hasB, and nine pYES2 composites (BBa_2671N89S, BBa_26GY2R3L, BBa_26UTIYW8, BBa_26XS36DC, etc.).
screen.best_evidence: Quantified effector output under osmotic stress: hyaluronic acid rising 0.476 → 5.436 → 7.366 → 20.973 ng/mL across 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6 Osm/L and dcsA activity 114.07 → 1306.64 → 1438.80 → 1924.04 U/L, both with p<0.001 (/results, Figures 16–17). Plant-level validation in Nicotiana benthamiana after four days' drought gave total chlorophyll of 3.629 ± 0.11 (watered), 2.328 ± 0.022 (drought) and 3.121 ± 0.0014 mg/g (yeast-treated drought), n=3 per group (/results, Figure 20 and Table 1).
screen.hp_integration: Yes, documented as five numbered pathways from stakeholder to decision: Hefeng Farm pushed them from smallholders to standardised farms; Chongming repositioned the system alongside existing irrigation; Qiu Xinyuan and Wu Shengbo prompted the promoter comparison and the co-culture test; Tian Shiyu and Zhou Feng forced a retrievable bead housing; Liu Tianle's demand for measurable evidence made them drop SDG 13 from their impact framework.
screen.reason: The strongest candidate in this batch and a credible top-2 contender. It is the only team here that closes the loop from genetic circuit to quantified effector output to a measured plant phenotype, and it backs that with a 25-part collection, a transcriptomic promoter-selection model built on public GEO data with cross-strain validation, a built hardware system with its own test results and cost list, and an IHP section where five stakeholder conversations are traced to specific design changes. Cycle 1 is a genuine documented failure (tnaA-ndoI did not express in yeast, consistent with an expert's warning about indole toxicity) that drove the redesign to Y amilCP. The one thing a full read must settle is attribution: the Attributions page is empty on the wiki, and the scale of the work across wet lab, hardware, software and model needs the student/instructor boundary made explicit.
screen.field_notes: SHSID (Agriculture village, CHN) built PlantGuard-Dual, a two-bead drought management system in S. cerevisiae INVSc1. A seven-promoter osmotic-stress library (STL1, DDR2, PST2, GRE1, TPS1, ALD2, GPD1) was screened on pYES2 against mannitol gradients with OD588 colorimetry and a sensitivity heat map, giving the order GPD1>TPS1>GRE1>PST2>DDR2>STL1>ALD2; they then deliberately assigned the high-sensitivity GPD1 to the early-acting soil-improvement module and the glucose-repression-free DDR2 to the last-resort alert module. Crucially, colour change occurred under mannitol but not NaCl at matched osmolarity, which they read as drought-specific rather than generic osmotic response. The soil module (GPD1–α-factor–dcsA and GPD1–hasA–hasB) gave dose-dependent hyaluronic acid up to 20.97 ng/mL and dcsA activity up to 1924 U/L (p<0.001). Co-culture of both modules delayed colour development from 12–15 h to beyond 48 h, and a four-day N. benthamiana drought trial (n=3 per group) showed yeast-treated plants retaining 3.121 mg/g total chlorophyll versus 2.328 for drought controls. Cycle 1 failed outright — a tnaA-ndoI two-enzyme indigo cascade gave no ~100 kDa band and no colour — and was replaced with Y amilCP, an amilCP variant codon-optimised for yeast by iGEM19_SCU-China. Supporting work is unusually broad: a promoter-selection model built from GEO GSE312455 with YEASTRACT regulatory analysis and an independent GSE274661 validation set, the ADRS hardware (sensors, ESP32-CAM, data fitting, watering control, app, parts list and costing), a 25-part collection page, and 15.5k words of education. The Attributions page is empty.

justification.a1: Two genetic modules were built and verified in S. cerevisiae, a seven-promoter library was screened, polymer output was quantified, a three-version hardware prototype was tested, and a four-day plant trial was run (Results; Engineering; Hardware). The results build on each other in rising difficulty, which is the GreatBay/TAS pattern, but the top of the scale is not reached because the two modules did not work together (Results, Dual-Module Validation: no colour at 48 h once the retention strain was added) and soil water retention itself was never measured.
justification.a2: The alert module is genuinely demonstrated: a mannitol gradient (0.1/0.3/0.6 Osm/L) against a matched-osmolarity NaCl control and an uninduced control, repeated in liquid, on SD-URA plates and in alginate beads, with OD588 quantification at the amilCP peak and a promoter heat map (Results). The soil module is weaker: SDS-PAGE bands were 'relatively faint', cellulose appeared as visible material in all samples including the control, and the triplicate ELISA values are implausibly tight (1306.813 / 1306.396 / 1306.708 U/L) to carry the stated p<0.001. The plant trial (n=3 per group; chlorophyll 3.12 vs 2.33 vs 3.63 mg/g) lacks a wild-type-yeast control, so the effect cannot be attributed to the engineered polymers rather than to added yeast; the team itself notes colour was scored at one 24 h point 'without replicates or proper controls' (Engineering, Learn 1.2).
justification.a3: The use case is grounded in stakeholder data: a 242-respondent survey gives a price ceiling (71.07% below 100 RMB/m2/yr) and an application-method constraint, and farm and plant-base visits set the deployment context (Human Practices; Entrepreneurship). A hardware cost list and deployment strategy exist (Hardware 6.2). But nothing was tested in a field-like setting and no water saving or yield effect is quantified from the team's own data, which is what TAS's wastewater run supplied.
justification.a4: The team's strongest aspect. Cycle 1.1 (tnaA-ndoI) failed outright, with no protein near 100 kDa and no colour at any mannitol level; the team diagnosed fusion size, codon bias and indole toxicity (the last raised by an interviewed expert) and redesigned around Y amilCP (Engineering, Learn 1.1). The DESeq2 analysis of GSE312455 fed candidate promoter selection, screening then assigned DDR2 to the alarm and GPD1 to the retention module on a stated threshold rationale, and three hardware versions were revised after the Hefeng and Chongming visits (Model; Engineering; Hardware 2.1-2.3).
justification.a5: Human Practices is reflective and responsive rather than outreach. A quantitative public survey (242 responses, biosafety and cost findings), field trips to Hefeng Farm, Chongming Dongtan base and Jincang Bioscience, and interviews with plant-microbe, root-development and environmental-economics specialists are each tied to a named decision: target users refocused, the device became a networked array, validation priorities and a retrievable housing added, and SDG 13 dropped from the impact framework (Human Practices, 'Five key decisions'). What keeps it below 5 is that several listed changes remain 'next evaluation' rather than executed.
justification.a6: The /attributions page returns 404, so the attribution record the handbook requires (p.25-26) is absent. The Members page lists each student's division (wet lab, outreach, art, hardware) but gives no task-level account of who ran which experiment, and nothing states what instructors, the PI or outside providers did, although Sanger sequencing was clearly outsourced ('submitted for sequencing', Results). The notebook, bead work and protocols read as student-run and the scale is plausible for a school lab, so I score this as shared and undeclared rather than outsourced.
justification.a7: Squarely synthetic biology with standard components: seven native yeast stress promoters, a reused chromoprotein (Y amilCP, credited to SCU-China 2019), the pYES2 backbone, CYC1 terminator, His tag and alpha-factor secretion signal, assembled into nine composite plasmids and registered as 25 parts, 17 of them new (Part Collection; Contribution). Like TAS, novelty is modest, but the architecture is genuinely part-based and modular, with the promoter treated as an interchangeable module.
justification.a8: Wiki-side part documentation is good: each basic part carries origin, length, biology, its own amplification gel and references (Contribution), and the Part Collection table maps every BBa ID to its module. Against that, the standard /parts URL is 404 with the content at /part-collection and /contribution, /attributions and /proof-of-concept are 404, and /measurement and /inclusivity are still unfilled template pages showing '1.1.1 xxxxx' and font-specimen filler. I could not load any Registry entry (parts.igem.org returned 403 to me), so under p.18 no Registry-side credit can be given.
justification.w1: The homepage states the problem, the shortcomings of mulch, SAPs and FDR/TDR sensors, and the dual-bead solution within about one screen, with a clear one-line framing of each module. Description then restates the goals cleanly in three engineering levels. A little drift comes from the hype-leaning opening sequence and the repeated 'both names refer to the same module' disclaimer pasted at the top of five pages.
justification.w2: Most key claims carry a figure: colony PCR gels with stated expected sizes (1921 bp, 702 bp, 3508 bp, 2594 bp), OD600 growth curves, OD588 absorbance series, ELISA standard curves with R2 values, raw chlorophyll tables, and plant photographs by group (Results). What is missing is consistent rigour: n and replicate type are rarely defined, error bars are not described, the SDS-PAGE evidence is admitted to be faint, and the plant experiment lacks the wild-type-yeast control needed to support its conclusion.
justification.w3: Navigation follows the ballot closely (Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab, Outreach), each page has a working side menu, and the Part Collection is easy to find. But two standard URLs are 404 (/parts, /attributions) and two more serve unfinished template text (/measurement, /inclusivity), which is exactly the friction p.29 warns about. Large blocks of Results are duplicated verbatim inside Engineering and again inside Hardware section 8, so the site is more sprawling than it needs to be.
justification.w4: Experiments gives real protocols with reagent volumes, thermocycler steps and supplier catalogue numbers, failures are recorded rather than hidden, and raw ELISA and chlorophyll numbers are tabulated, so much of the work could be repeated. Against that, the Notebook is a four-paragraph narrative summary with no dated entries, there is no link to the DESeq2 analysis code, and no sequencing traces or raw plate-reader files are deposited.
justification.w5: Human Practices, Model, Sustainability and Contribution cite properly, with per-part primary references and a credited prior iGEM team (SCU-China 2019 for Y amilCP). Results and Engineering, the two pages carrying the experimental claims, have no reference list at all, and Description sources its headline drought statistics to non-scholarly pages (a Voronoi infographic, 'pactimes'), which is thin support for the numbers that motivate the project.

J1.one_line: A real two-module yeast project with an honestly documented failure-and-redesign cycle and strong stakeholder-driven engineering, let down by missing controls behind the soil-improvement claims and by absent attribution and placeholder standard pages.
strengths: Cycle 1 failed and is reported as a failure: no tnaA-ndoI protein near 100 kDa and no colour at any mannitol concentration, with causes analysed and the design replaced by Y amilCP (Engineering, Test/Learn 1.1)

The drought alert module is shown against the right controls: a mannitol gradient versus matched-osmolarity NaCl and an uninduced control, repeated in liquid, on solid medium and in alginate beads, with OD588 quantification at the chromoprotein peak (Results)

Human Practices runs both ways: a 242-response survey with cost and biosafety numbers plus farm, plant-base and company visits, each tied to a named design change including dropping SDG 13 from the impact framework (Human Practices)

A DESeq2 analysis of public yeast osmotic-stress RNA-seq (GSE312455, three strain backgrounds, design ~ strain + stress) shortlisted promoters before bench screening, with the control/treatment time-point confound stated openly (Model)
Hardware went through three versions driven by what the team saw at Chongming and Hefeng, with component tests, a cost list and a user manual (Hardware 2.1-2.3, 4.1-4.7, 6.2)
Cloning is properly verified throughout: colony PCR at stated expected sizes in both E. coli and INVSc1, plus Sanger sequencing of every construct (Results; Engineering Build sections)
weaknesses: The plant trial has no wild-type-yeast control, so the higher chlorophyll in the treated group (3.12 vs 2.33 mg/g) cannot be attributed to the engineered cellulose and hyaluronic acid rather than to added yeast biomass (Results, Plant Experiment Verification)

Cellulose production is not demonstrated: SDS-PAGE bands were 'relatively faint' and the visual assay found material in all samples including the control, leaving only a kit enzyme-activity readout to separate the groups (Engineering, Test 2)

The ELISA triplicates are far too tight for biological replicates (1306.813 / 1306.396 / 1306.708 U/L), so the p<0.001 claim is not supported by the data shown; n and the nature of the replicates are never defined anywhere on the wiki
The central promise of the project, that the beads improve soil water retention, is never measured in soil; the team acknowledges this as future work
The two modules do not yet work together: adding the retention strain suppressed the alarm entirely for 48 h, possibly through nutrient competition (Results, Dual-Module Validation)
No attributions page exists (404), and the Members page gives divisions but no task-level account of who did what or what was outsourced
Results and Engineering, which carry the experimental claims, have no reference lists, and large passages are duplicated across Results, Engineering and Hardware
red_flags: /attributions returns 404; no attribution record anywhere on the wiki (handbook p.25-26)
/parts and /proof-of-concept return 404; part content lives only at /part-collection and /contribution
/measurement and /inclusivity are unfilled design templates still showing '1.1.1 xxxxx' headings and font-specimen filler text
ELISA 'triplicate' values differ by less than 0.05% yet carry p<0.001 significance claims (Results; Engineering Test 2) - a rigour problem, not an integrity finding on this evidence
Description sources headline drought statistics to non-scholarly pages (a Voronoi map, 'pactimes'); Results and Engineering cite nothing

Registry entries for the 17 claimed new parts could not be loaded by me (parts.igem.org returned 403), so no Registry-side credit could be given; this is a limit of my access, not evidence of a problem with the entries
pages_read: attempted Registry pages for BBa_26UYPPLI, BBa_26GY2R3L, BBa_26XS36DC, BBa_26QD5JVR (403 blocked)

calibrated.changed: none. a6 3.0 matches Hangzhou No.14 (404 attributions, division/role-level listing only, student-looking notebook); a8 3.0 matches the other teams whose standard parts URL is missing and whose remaining award pages are unfilled template text.

justification.a1: The scope is near the top of what I expect from a high school team: a seven-promoter drought-responsive library in S. cerevisiae, a chromoprotein alarm construct, two biopolymer effector constructs, alginate bead encapsulation, a co-culture test, a potted Nicotiana benthamiana trial, three hardware generations with working firmware and dashboard, and an RNA-seq promoter screen (Results, Engineering, Hardware, Model). The chain of increasingly hard steps and the openly reported first-design failure (tnaA-ndoI, Engineering Learn 1.1) read like the GreatBay pattern. It falls short of a 5 because the central product claim, that the beads retain soil water, is never measured in soil.
justification.a2: Construction is verified for every construct by colony PCR and Sanger sequencing in both E. coli and INVSc1 (Results Fig. 3-5, 11-14), and function is quantified: OD588 pigment versus mannitol dose, a no-colour NaCl isotonic set and uninduced controls (Fig. 7, 8, 22-24), HA by competitive ELISA with a 4PL standard curve and triplicates rising 0.48 to 20.97 ng/mL (Table 1, Fig. 44), dcsA activity 114 to 1924 U/L on a linear standard (R2 = 0.9952, Fig. 46-47), and plant chlorophyll 2.33 vs 3.12 mg/g for drought vs yeast-treated (Table 1 on Results). Weaknesses that keep it off 4.5: no soil-moisture measurement anywhere, dcsA secretion never shown (SDS-PAGE bands described as faint, Engineering Test 2), the dual-module result is an absence of colour that could equally be competition or shading, and the NaCl-negative result is interpreted as drought specificity when at equal osmolarity it argues the sensor is not purely osmotic.
justification.a3: The route to use is concrete and stakeholder-checked: the Chongming and Hefeng visits moved the target user to standardised farms and placed the device alongside existing drip irrigation, the Jincang and landscaping interviews cover distribution, and the Hardware page carries a parts list, cost estimate and user manual (Hardware 6.1-7.2, IHP Stage 1-2). Against that, nothing has been tested in soil or in a field: the only efficacy data are four days of potted plants in the lab, and the HA yields measured (tens of ng/mL) are far from a dose argument for rhizosphere water holding.
justification.a4: There is one genuine cycle in the handbook sense: the tnaA-ndoI module showed no protein near 100 kDa and no colour, the team diagnosed size, codon bias and indole toxicity, and rebuilt with Y amilCP, which then worked (Engineering Build/Test/Learn 1.1 to 1.2). Promoter screening fed a design decision rather than a report, with GPD1 for early retention and DDR2 as the late alarm, justified by glucose repression and HOG independence (Engineering, Promoter Sensitivity Screening). Hardware iterated v1 to v2 to final against farm and expert feedback, and the fitted relation drought = 0.001*lux - 0.004*blue + 4e-5*blue_pixels + 0.42 was derived from their own sensor readings and used in the control loop (Hardware 4.3, 5.2). Held at 4 because success criteria are rarely stated as numbers in advance and the camera metric is never calibrated against the OD588 reference they already own.
justification.a5: This is the strongest section. The IHP page opens with five explicit stakeholder-to-decision pathways, each naming the input, the change and the evidence page, and the changes are traceable elsewhere on the wiki: the expert criticism that warning and retention were disjointed produced the dual-threshold promoter architecture, Researcher Zhou's warning on alginate fragility and root-depth dynamics produced the perforated retrievable tube housing and multi-depth placement (Hardware 2.2), and Dr Liu's push for measurable evidence led them to drop SDG 13 from the framework. A 242-response public survey with cost ceilings and trust sources backs the deployment thinking rather than being outreach dressed up as HP.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page: https://2026.igem.wiki/shsid/attributions/ returns 404, as do /parts/ and /proof-of-concept/. The Team page gives divisions and a one-line role per member plus advisors and the PI, which is something, but there is no who-did-what record of the kind the handbook asks for, so I cannot tell which steps the students executed and which the host lab, sequencing service or instructors did. I raise this as a gap, not an accusation; it caps the aspect near 2.5.
justification.a7: The project is built on standard components and adds to them: a 25-part collection of 16 basic and 9 composite parts with 17 new, reusing pYES2, the CYC1 terminator, the His/T7 tag and the SCU-China-optimised Y amilCP (Part collection, Contribution). The promoter library is exactly the sort of reusable collection the handbook rewards, and the firmware and HTTP API on the Software page are a second, usable contribution. I could not open parts.igem.org from here (403 from CloudFront on all four part numbers I tried), and the wiki has no working Parts page, so I am scoring the collection as presented and leaving room for a Registry check by another judge.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is good: the Contribution page gives per-part origin, biology, a gel and references, the Experiments page carries 26 protocols with reagent catalogue numbers and cycling conditions, and the Software page publishes the firmware in full. But the Parts page is a 404, I could not verify the Registry entries themselves (the handbook judges parts there), and two standard pages, Measurement and Inclusivity, are still unedited template filler with headings reading 1.1.1 xxxxx and repeated font-specification boilerplate. Those defects pull an otherwise 4+ aspect down.
justification.w1: The home page tells the problem, the shortcomings of mulch, SAPs and FDR/TDR sensors, and the two-bead solution in a sequence I could follow, and the Description page states chassis, promoters, reporter, effectors and the mannitol test regime clearly. After home plus description I can state the aim, the organism and the success criterion. It is not Lambert_GA tight: the same module-naming disclaimer is repeated verbatim at the top of six pages, and the home page gives no quantitative result.
justification.w2: Main claims are carried by real figures and tables rather than assertion: gels for every construct, OD600 growth curves, OD588 dose curves, a heat map of promoter sensitivity, two ELISA standard curves with triplicate tables, and the chlorophyll table with three plants per group (Results, Engineering). Hardware claims are backed by recorded test videos and a seven-trial blue-value series (Hardware 8.3). Short of 4.5 because the water-retention claim at the heart of the product has no soil data, and the Notebook promises soil mass and moisture monitoring that appears nowhere in the Results.
justification.w3: Navigation is logical, with Project, Wet Lab, Dry Lab and Outreach groups and a per-page side table of contents that maps onto the judging criteria. Against that, four standard pages return 404, two are placeholder templates, and the Hardware page reproduces the whole of the Results wet-lab section almost word for word, which makes a long wiki longer without adding evidence. It is usable but sprawling rather than Patras-tidy.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: 26 protocols with reagents and catalogue numbers, plasmid maps and primer positions, the complete ESP32-CAM and controller source with the HTTP API documented, the model's datasets (GSE312455, GSE274661), filtering thresholds and DESeq2 design formula, and a part collection table. What is missing is a dated notebook (the Notebook page is 1,700 words of phase summaries) and any attribution record, both of which matter for reproducing how the work was actually done.
justification.w5: Citation practice is uneven. The Description's long background rests on four web sources, several of them popular or secondary (Voronoi, a blog post), and the Hardware page cites unanswered.io and maweb.org for engineering claims. Some Model references are incomplete enough that I could not resolve them as given, for example a Callister 2009 entry with no journal and a Pelet 2020 entry titled only Promoter dynamics and HOG/TF mechanisms. The Contribution page does better, citing PMC articles per part, and prior iGEM work (SCU-China's Y amilCP) is credited.

J2.one_line: An unusually complete high school project: a screened yeast promoter library driving a chromoprotein drought alarm and two biopolymer retention constructs, taken through a failed first design, quantitative assays, a plant trial and three stakeholder-driven hardware builds, but let down by a missing Attributions page, two placeholder standard pages and no soil-level measurement of the water retention it claims.
strengths: A real failure-driven redesign: tnaA-ndoI showed no protein near 100 kDa and no colour, and was replaced by Y amilCP, which then worked (Engineering, Build/Test/Learn 1.1 to 1.2)

Quantitative dose-response with proper standard curves: HA by competitive ELISA (4PL fit, 0.48 to 20.97 ng/mL across 0 to 0.6 Osm/L, triplicates) and dcsA activity 114 to 1924 U/L on a linear standard with R2 = 0.9952 (Engineering Test 2, Figs 43-47)

A seven-promoter library screened under a mannitol gradient with NaCl isotonic and uninduced controls, in liquid, on solid medium and in alginate beads, with the ranking used to assign GPD1 to retention and DDR2 to the alarm (Results, Promoter Selection)

Human Practices with five explicit stakeholder-to-decision pathways whose consequences show up in the engineering: the dual-threshold promoter architecture, the retrievable perforated tube housing and multi-depth bead placement, and the removal of SDG 13 from the impact framework (IHP; Hardware 2.2)

Hardware iterated three times against farm visits and expert interviews, with bench tests of the pump, wireless link and dashboard, and a drought estimate fitted from their own lux and blue-value data and used in the control loop (Hardware 4.1-4.7, 5.2, 8.3)

A record a future team could work from: 26 protocols with reagent catalogue numbers, full firmware source with a documented HTTP API, plasmid maps with primer positions, and a stated-limitations RNA-seq model (Experiments, Software, Model)
weaknesses: No Attributions page at all (/attributions/ returns 404), so who did which step cannot be checked; the Team page only gives division-level roles
The product's core claim, that the beads improve soil water retention, is never measured in soil; the Notebook mentions monitoring soil mass and moisture, but no such data appear in Results

The dual-module result is an absence of colour after 48 h in co-culture, which could be competition, shading or metabolic load rather than relief of osmotic stress; no independent measurement distinguishes these

NaCl at matched osmolarity gives no colour while mannitol does, which the team reads as drought specificity; at equal osmolarity this argues the sensor is not responding to osmotic pressure alone, and the wiki does not address that
dcsA secretion is not demonstrated: the SDS-PAGE bands are described as faint and indistinguishable across conditions, yet the α-factor secretion design is treated as validated downstream
Measurement and Inclusivity are unedited template pages (headings reading 1.1.1 xxxxx and repeated font boilerplate), and /parts/ and /proof-of-concept/ are 404
The Hardware page duplicates the entire wet-lab Results section verbatim, and several pages repeat the same module-naming disclaimer, making the wiki longer without adding evidence
Citations are uneven: blog-level web sources for engineering claims, and at least two Model references too incomplete to resolve as written
red_flags: Attributions page missing (404) - I cannot verify the student-versus-instructor split; I raise this as a question for the team, not as an accusation
Parts and Proof of Concept standard pages return 404; parts.igem.org was unreachable from my machine (403 CloudFront) so the Registry entries behind the 17 claimed new parts remain unverified by me
Measurement and Inclusivity pages are unfinished template placeholders containing filler text such as 1.1.1 xxxxx
Two Model references (a Callister 2009 entry and a Pelet 2020 entry) are given without journal or identifier and I could not resolve them; worth a direct question rather than any inference
Hardware cites unanswered.io and a commercial blog as evidence for engineering claims; a GitHub repository is linked, and content off iGEM servers cannot be judged

calibrated.changed: none — a6 2.5 (404 page, but a team page with a one-line role per member, more than bios alone) and w5 3.0 (popular/secondary sources and two unresolvable references) both hold against the field.

justification.a1: PlantGuard carries a two-module yeast system (DDR2-YamilCP drought alarm, GPD1-driven dcsA and hasA-hasB water retention) from a seven-promoter screen through quantitative characterisation, a four-day Nicotiana benthamiana pot trial, an RNA-seq promoter model and a three-version ESP32 hardware/app prototype (Description, Results, Model, Hardware). The climb through harder steps is real, including an abandoned first design. It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS level because the headline property, soil water retention, was never measured, and the one experiment that put both modules together suppressed the alarm rather than coordinating with it (Results, Dual-Module Validation).
justification.a2: The alert module is genuinely shown to work: colony PCR (~1921 bp in E. coli, ~702 bp in yeast), OD600 growth curves against untransformed control, visible blue under 0.1-0.6 Osm/L mannitol but none under iso-osmolar NaCl, OD588 quantification, solid-medium halos and alginate beads (Results, Engineering Test 1.2). The effector module is quantified by ELISA with triplicates (HA 0.48 to 20.97 ng/mL; dcsA 114 to 1924 U/L, p<0.001) and the plant trial gives chlorophyll numbers for three groups of three (3.63, 2.33, 3.12 mg/g). Against that, SDS-PAGE bands were faint and not resolved by condition, cellulose was only "visible material" in all samples including control, colour was scored at single timepoints without stated replicates, and no soil moisture was ever measured.
justification.a3: The need is argued from drought data and, more persuasively, confirmed by named users: Hefeng Farm, the Chongming planting base, a landscaping director, a retail seller and the Tianshui Water Resources Utilization Center (Human Practices, Stages 1-3). The team names a deployment route, a hardware cost estimate and a parts list (Hardware, Constructive Parts and Cost). It stays at 3.5 because nothing was tested outside the lab: the pot trial ran four days indoors, and the claimed rhizosphere benefit has no field or soil-column evidence.
justification.a4: Cycle 1.1 is a real failure honestly reported: the tnaA-ndoI fusion gave no band near 100 kDa and no colour in any of seven promoters, and the team redesigned to YamilCP after an expert flagged indole toxicity (Engineering, Learn 1.1). Cycle 2 and the promoter heat map feed a reasoned choice of DDR2 for the alarm and GPD1 for retention, and the hardware went through three versions, dropping a bead dispenser and adding a retrievable housing after Researcher Zhou's warning about alginate fragility (Hardware, Design Motivation). The Learn steps are honest about what is missing but success criteria are mostly qualitative, and the co-culture result is read as consistent with the design when it actually shows the two modules interfering.
justification.a5: The IHP page opens with five decisions, each tied to a named stakeholder, the resulting change and the page where it shows: refocusing target users after Hefeng Farm, positioning alongside existing irrigation after Chongming, module and promoter testing after Qiu Xinyuan and Wu Shengbo, a retrievable housing and revised validation priorities after Tian Shiyu and Zhou Feng, and dropping SDG 13 from the impact framework after Dr Liu Tianle. Those are traceable design consequences, not a contact list. It is not a 5 because the 242-respondent questionnaire, with 34.3% of respondents under 18, is reported with no mention of consent, anonymity or any ethics oversight, and critical or opposing voices are summarised rather than engaged.
justification.a6: This is the weak point. The Attributions page returns 404, so the only on-wiki account of who did what is the Team page's one-line bios ("wet lab member", "outreach team") plus named advisors, instructors and the PI with no description of their role. The Awards page states that "Our standardized Attributions Form covers team members' responsibilities", but that form is not on the wiki for a judge to read. With DESeq2 analysis of public RNA-seq, competitive ELISA and Sanger sequencing in the record and no statement of who ran them or what the host lab supplied, I cannot tell how much is student work; this is a question for the session, not an accusation.
justification.a7: The project is built squarely from standard components: a 25-part collection with 17 new parts, including a seven-member drought-responsive yeast promoter library and nine composite pYES2 plasmids, reusing registry parts such as BBa_K3221205 YamilCP (credited to iGEM19_SCU-China), pYES2 and the CYC1 terminator (Part collection, Contribution). Hardware and the MicroPython/ESP32 firmware, with full source listed on the Software page, count as standard components too. Short of 5 because the constructs are yeast expression plasmids rather than RFC-compatible assemblies, and the two effector composites are documented but not yet shown to deliver their intended function in soil.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is good: each part gets origin, length, properties, biology, a gel image and references on the Contribution page, and the Part collection page groups them into three functional modules. But the standard /parts URL 404s, so a judge must find the collection under "Part collection", and the Registry pages themselves could not be reached from here to confirm sequence features, host and characterisation data. Under the rule that part documentation must live on the Registry, wiki-only evidence caps this at 3; if the Registry entries carry the same depth as the Contribution page, this would rise.
justification.w1: The home page lands the problem, the shortcomings of mulch, SAPs and FDR/TDR sensors, and then the dual-bead solution in a few lines, with a logo schematic and links onward to Project, Engineering, Human Practices, Hardware and Education. The Description page repeats the three-level architecture clearly. A little of the framing is padded with global water-crisis background before the project itself appears.
justification.w2: The core claims carry figures and numbers: gels for every construct, OD600 and OD588 curves, a promoter heat map, ELISA standard curves with R2 of 0.99 and 0.9952, triplicate concentration tables, and a chlorophyll table with the kit equation and the dilution factor stated (Results). Model outputs are kept clearly separate from wet-lab results and the Model page states its own limitations, including the 0 vs 45 minute control confound. Marked down because replicates and error bars are absent from the colorimetric work, cellulose production rests on "visible material" with no control difference, and the water-retention claim at the heart of the project is asserted rather than measured.
justification.w3: Navigation is sensible and the side menu maps onto the criteria, but a judge has to hunt: /parts, /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /design and /protocols all 404, with the content sitting under "Part collection" and "Experiments" instead. The Measurement and Inclusivity pages are byte-identical unfinished templates still showing "1.1.1 xxxxx" and font-specimen filler text. The wiki also sprawls, with Human Practices at ~17.9k, Education ~15.5k and Entrepreneurship ~13.9k words against ~4k on Results.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: the Experiments page gives 22 protocol tables down to reagent volumes, the Software page lists complete firmware source, and the Contribution page documents each part with its gel. What is missing is a dated notebook (the Notebook page is ~1.7k words of narrative around a timeline figure), downloadable raw data behind the ELISA and OD plots, and any attribution record, all of which a rebuilding team would want.
justification.w5: Citation practice is uneven. The Contribution page cites primary literature per part and the team credits iGEM19_SCU-China for the YamilCP optimisation, but Results, Engineering and Software carry no reference lists at all, and the Description page's four references are informal web pages given without resolvable links. In the Model reference list, "Callister, S. J., McCue, L. A., & Smith, R. D. (2009). W303 yeast strain multi-concentration time-course response" and "Pelet, S. (2020). Promoter dynamics and HOG/TF mechanisms" have no journal, volume or DOI and I could not resolve them; I would ask the team at the session rather than assume anything.

J3.one_line: A genuinely broad high-school project with a working, well-controlled yeast drought alarm and honest iteration on a failed first design, let down by a missing Attributions page, unfinished standard pages, and citations that thin out exactly where the science is.
strengths: Drought alarm module is demonstrated, not just claimed: dose-dependent blue under 0.1-0.6 Osm/L mannitol with a matched NaCl iso-osmolar control showing no response, confirmed in liquid, on solid medium and in alginate beads, and quantified at OD588 (Results; Engineering Test 1.2)

A real failure was reported and acted on: the tnaA-ndoI fusion expressed no protein and gave no colour in any promoter, and the team redesigned around YamilCP after an expert raised indole toxicity (Engineering, Learn 1.1)

Five human-practices decisions are each traced from a named stakeholder to a specific change and to the page that records it, including dropping the bead dispenser and adding a retrievable housing after Researcher Zhou Feng's warning about alginate fragility (Human Practices; Hardware)

Quantitative effector characterisation with controls and triplicates: HA rising from 0.48 to 20.97 ng/mL and dcsA activity from 114 to 1924 U/L across the osmotic gradient, with standard curves shown (Results; Engineering Test 2)

A 25-part collection with 17 new parts, each documented on the wiki with origin, biology, gel and references, and prior iGEM work (SCU-China's YamilCP) properly credited (Contribution; Part collection)
Reproducibility material a future team could use: 22 detailed protocol tables on Experiments and complete ESP32/MicroPython firmware source on the Software page
weaknesses: No Attributions page on the wiki (the URL 404s); the Awards page says a form exists but a judge cannot see who did the cloning, the ELISA or the DESeq2 analysis, and advisors, instructors and the PI are named without roles

The project's central promise, improved soil water retention, is never measured; no soil moisture, water-holding or evaporation data appear anywhere, so the retention module's benefit rests on enzyme activity plus a four-day pot trial

The one experiment combining both modules showed the retention strains suppressing the alarm entirely for 48 hours; this is written up as consistent with the design when it is an unresolved integration problem the team itself flags as future work

Measurement and Inclusivity are byte-identical unfinished template pages carrying "1.1.1 xxxxx" and font-specimen filler, and /parts, /proof-of-concept, /design and /protocols all 404, so judges must hunt for content
Results and Engineering, the two pages carrying the science, contain no citations at all, and two entries in the Model reference list could not be resolved
The 242-respondent public questionnaire, with 34.3% of respondents under 18, is reported with no mention of consent, anonymity or ethics oversight
Colorimetric results are reported from single timepoints with no stated replicates or error bars, and SDS-PAGE bands for dcsA and hasA-hasB were too faint to distinguish between conditions
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404 while the Awards page asserts a completed Attributions Form; combined with DESeq2 RNA-seq analysis, competitive ELISA and Sanger sequencing in the record, who performed the essential work cannot be established from the wiki. A session question, not an accusation.

Two Model references give no journal, volume or DOI and did not resolve for me: "Callister, S. J., McCue, L. A., & Smith, R. D. (2009). W303 yeast strain multi-concentration time-course response" and "Pelet, S. (2020). Promoter dynamics and HOG/TF mechanisms". Worth asking the team to supply the sources.
Public questionnaire of 242 people, a third of them minors, with no statement of consent or ethics oversight (Human Practices).
Measurement and Inclusivity pages are unfinished placeholder templates containing literal "xxxxx" headings and design-specimen filler text.

Registry part pages could not be fetched (403 from the Registry host) during this review, so Registry-side documentation depth for the 17 new parts is unverified; a8 reflects what is verifiable on the wiki.

calibrated.changed: a8 3.0 to 3.5. I applied the wiki-only cap of 3 to this team alone, when eleven other teams in this section were equally unverifiable (parts.igem.org refused every request from my environment) and I scored them 3.5 to 4.0 on their wiki-side documentation. Re-reading shsid/contribution.txt, it carries per-part origin, length, properties, biology, a gel image and references across 25 Registry IDs, which is the same evidence class as GCGS and Hongwen. It stays below 4.0 because the standard /parts URL 404s and the Model page's unresolvable references make me less confident in the page's bookkeeping.

one_line.en: A broad two-module yeast project with a working, well-controlled drought alarm and an honestly reported failed first design, let down by a missing attributions page, placeholder pages and no soil measurement of the retention it claims.
one_line.zh: 範圍寬廣的雙模組酵母專案，乾旱警示模組運作良好且對照嚴謹，第一版失敗也誠實呈報，但缺歸屬頁、有未完成頁面，且從未在土壤中量測其宣稱的保水效果。

strengths: The first design failed and is reported as a failure, with causes analysed and the design replaced
The alarm module shown against the right controls — an osmolarity gradient versus a matched salt control and an uninduced control — in liquid, on solid medium and in beads
Human Practices running both ways, with a large survey plus site visits each tied to a named design change
Hardware iterated three times against field visits, with component tests, a cost list and a user manual
weaknesses: The central promise, improved soil water retention, is never measured in soil
The plant trial HAS no wild-type-yeast control, so the effect cannot be attributed to the engineered products
Replicate counts are undefined and one set of triplicates is far too tight to be biological, undercutting its significance claim
The two modules suppress each other when combined, which is written up as consistent with the design rather than as an open problem
red_flags: No attributions page; the Members page gives divisions but no task-level account
Measurement and Inclusivity are unfilled design templates still showing filler headings and specimen text
Parts and proof-of-concept return 404; Results and Engineering carry no reference lists
Public questionnaire with a third of respondents under 18 and no consent or ethics statement

screen.project_title: kisMET - bringing binding sites to cellulose
screen.what_they_built: Komagataeibacter rhaeticus engineered to secrete an SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP fusion protein that anchors to its own bacterial cellulose, turning the pellicle into a biosorbent that captures Li+, Ni2+, Co2+ and Mn2+ from dilute battery-recycling wastewater and releases them by mild cellulase digestion.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for construction, K. rhaeticus as production chassis; pSEVA331-Prha modular scaffold with signal peptides SP4/SP10, CBM64/CBM3a, HiBiT reporter and eight ion-binding peptides (LiBP1/2, NiBP1/2, CoBP1/2, MnBP1/2); 27 Registry entries plus eleven downloadable construct design files with checksums.
screen.best_evidence: /results Cycle 4: ICP-OES across 8 strains x 4 concentrations (10-200 mg/L) - e.g. NiBP2 cut residual Ni2+ from 10 to 3.22 mg/L (67.8% removal), CoBP2 to 2.39 mg/L (76.1%), with cellulase-released fractions closing mass balance to 98-99% (LiBP2 at 200 mg/L: 174.50 + 21.86 = 196.36 mg/L). Cycle 1 HiBiT gave ~2,500-fold extracellular luminescence on rhamnose induction with matching SDS-PAGE bands.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - stakeholder interviews in the battery-recycling industry redefined the target from bulk recovery to the dilute residual stream left after hydrometallurgy, which set the 10-200 mg/L test range.
screen.reason: Four genuinely closed DBTL cycles ending in instrument-grade ICP-OES data for eight strains across four concentrations, a systematic 2x2 scaffold screen that produced a reusable plug-and-play display platform, 27 documented parts, and an unusually disciplined Limits section that states what was not tested (mixed-metal selectivity, reuse). This is the strongest evidence in the batch after GEMS-Taiwan and deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: SMS-Shenzhen (Shenzhen, Bioremediation village) built kisMET, a biosorption platform in the cellulose-producing bacterium Komagataeibacter rhaeticus for scavenging Li, Ni, Co and Mn from dilute battery-recycling effluent. The design is one modular fusion protein, SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP, secreted and anchored onto the bacterium's own cellulose; HiBiT split-luciferase gives a femtomolar handle on expression and display. Four DBTL cycles: expression and secretion in E. coli at 28 C (~2,500-fold extracellular luminescence), transfer to K. rhaeticus with fractionation showing matrix anchoring, a 2x2 SP4/SP10 x CBM64/CBM3a library that selected SP4-CBM64 as the standard scaffold, and an eight-strain metal panel. Cycle 4 is the strongest result: a two-stage equivolumetric adsorption plus cellulase-release assay read by ICP-OES over 10, 50, 100 and 200 mg/L, with removals up to 76% for Co and 68% for Ni and mass-balance closure of 98-99%. Contribution publishes 27 Registry entries, eleven FASTA design files with SHA-256 manifests, HiBiT CSVs, 21 protocols and 17 weekly records, with an explicit Limits section (design files are not sequencing reads, single metals only, mass balance is a measurement check not a specificity proof). Attributions page is nearly empty, which is the main gap for aspect 6.

justification.a1: Four linked DBTL cycles of increasing difficulty: a rhamnose-inducible SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP cassette built and expressed in E. coli (Engineering Cycle 1), moved into the non-model chassis K. rhaeticus with a working electroporation/selection pipeline at 340 ug/mL chloramphenicol (Cycle 2), a 2x2 SP-CBM scaffold screen (Cycle 3) and an eight-strain metal-binding panel measured by ICP-OES across 10-200 mg/L (Cycle 4). That is real scale for a high school team. It falls short of the GreatBay/TAS anchor because the final, headline function (metal capture attributable to the displayed peptide) is the one step without a biological control, and single-step removal for Li is only 12.75-19.14% (Results, Fig. 9A).
justification.a2: The expression half is genuinely well controlled: SDS-PAGE with uninduced S/P versus induced IS/IP lanes at two temperatures (Engineering Fig. 3A), HiBiT with -Rha, empty-vector and sterile-medium baselines and mean +/- SD (Figs 4, 7, 8), colony PCR at the stated amplicon sizes plus whole-plasmid nanopore alignment (Figs 2, 6). The metal assay is weaker: Fig. 11/Fig. 9 compares IBP1 and IBP2 only against the starting standard solution, with no wild-type or empty-vector K. rhaeticus biomass and no cellulose-only arm, and no n or error bars are given, so the data cannot separate peptide-mediated capture from native biosorption by cellulose and cells. The team says as much on Contribution -> Limits ("does not show that the peptide is the only thing binding it"), which is honest but does not supply the missing control.
justification.a3: The application target is unusually well defined for a HS project: twelve interviews walked the team from "battery recycling" to the specific low-concentration tail stream after hydrometallurgical solvent extraction, with GEM confirming residual Li/Ni/Co/Mn there and Yaoxinmiao describing the treatment context (Human Practices). Against that, nothing was tested in real or simulated leachate, selectivity under competing ions was not measured, and the sustainability case is literature-derived with an explicit note that it is "not a completed full-process LCA" (Sustainability, scope box). Credible use case, supported by stakeholders, but the impact numbers are not the team's own.
justification.a4: Each cycle's test changed the next design rather than just re-running a failed step: the 16 vs 28 C comparison fixed induction at 28 C because it also matches K. rhaeticus growth (Cycle 1 Learn); the fraction profiling in K. rhaeticus redirected measurement to the washed pellet and whole broth (Cycle 2 Learn); the 2x2 screen locked pSEVA331-Prha-SP4-CBM64-HiBiT as the universal scaffold and retired CBM3a/SP10 on measured grounds (Cycle 3 Learn); and the switch from unbuffered water to 10 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.2 was made to stop hydroxide precipitation of the divalent metals (Cycle 4 Learn). Modularity is used deliberately to skip redundant screening in Cycle 4. What is missing is a stated quantitative measure of success before testing, and a redesign driven by the metal data itself.
justification.a5: Twelve recorded conversations across the chain (Juhefeng, Meizhou Zhongrun, GEM, Yaoxinmiao, Lingzhu, Jiecheng, Defang Nano, Director Deng Yi, BIT-China 2024) organised on a Motivation/Mutual connection/Message/Move loop, with each entry naming what changed. Concrete consequences are visible: front-end recyclers were dropped as users after Meizhou Zhongrun; Prof. Meng's point that HiBiT cannot prove metal binding pushed the team to validate expression, immobilisation and adsorption separately; Li Zongjin's shear-force warning moved the intended mode of use to pre-made adsorbent added to wastewater rather than growing cells in it; and the team withdrew from the entrepreneurship track because the cost data would not stand up (Attributions, student leader entry). Two-way and responsive; it shapes scope and validation logic more than it changes a construct.
justification.a6: The Attributions page carries 30 entries with task-level detail, Registry parts name individual student designers with CRediT roles (e.g. BBa_26N7CE1M, jinyu Peng, Conceptualisation/Investigation), and the Team page sets out six workstreams. Outside help is declared rather than hidden: Link Spider provided the laboratory and funding, the instructor states she guided experimental design and raw data collection, and three AI tools are listed for literature synthesis, translation, drafting of the Description/HP/SDG text and wiki coding. The wet lab sits in a sponsor's facility and part of the English prose is AI-assisted, which is why this is a 4 rather than a 5, not a concern about honesty.
justification.a7: This is squarely synthetic biology with standard components: Golden Gate assembly into a broad-host-range pSEVA331 BsaI vector, a rhaSR-PrhaBAD cassette and RiboJ insulator reused from earlier iGEM parts (BBa_K4663024, BBa_K4216041), and a four-module fusion (SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP) in which only the C-terminal payload is swapped across eight variants. Sixteen basic and eleven composite parts are registered, and the Registry pages show RFC10/RFC1000 export and sub-part composition. Modularity is demonstrated in practice, not just asserted, when seven new strains were made by payload swap alone (Cycle 4 Build).
justification.a8: Judged on the Registry itself, the entries are well made: BBa_26N7CE1M gives role, circular topology, host K. rhaeticus, 5,624 bp, GC content, the seven constituent parts, biosafety screening cleared, and five documentation sections (Design, Characterisation, Discussion, Application, Experiment); the basic part BBa_26AMNFBN cites the phage-display paper it came from. The wiki matches the Registry part by part (Parts, Composite Part) and adds FASTA designs with SHA-256 checksums. Two things keep it off a 5: the characterisation on the metal-binding parts rests on the same uncontrolled ICP-OES panel, and the Registry documentation titles ("Ultra-High-Affinity", "Premier Cobalt Recovery", "Flagship") claim more than the data.
justification.w1: The Description abstract states the problem, the SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP design and the limits in one paragraph, and it is refreshingly candid ("Selectivity in mixed wastewater, downstream product purity, biosorbent reuse and a complete closed-loop process remain to be established"). The landing page itself, though, is a 188-word animated intro that asks the visitor to type a passphrase before anything is explained, so the goals are clear only after a click or two rather than within one screen.
justification.w2: Most claims are tied to a labelled figure with methods: gels with marker lanes and stated amplicon sizes, HiBiT bar charts with defined fractions, log10 axes, units in RLU and mean +/- SD, and a source-figure viewer for the ICP-OES data that preserves the original axis breaks and warns that "concentration is not a substitute for metal mass or recovery rate". The central adsorption figure still lacks a non-engineered control and any statement of n, and the Results and Engineering prose ("rigorously proves", "quantitatively validated platform") overshoots what Contribution -> Limits concedes on the same site.
justification.w3: Navigation follows the ballot (Project / Wet Lab / Human Practices / Team / Attributions), the standard URLs are intact, each page has an on-this-page index, and there are command-K search, high-contrast and readable-font toggles. Friction comes from the decorative layer: the passphrase intro screen, scrambled glyph strings in the page breadcrumbs, and a Team page where member profiles are reachable only by playing a claw-machine game, which is charming but hides information a judge is looking for.
justification.w4: The handover is one of the better ones I have seen at this level: 21 protocols with reagents, volumes and thermal programs (Experiments), a 91-page dated notebook, eleven FASTA design files with a checksum manifest, the HiBiT CSV, the ICP-OES source-figure PDF with its sample definitions (A = residual, B = post-cellulase), an 18-page safety manual, and a four-step "what a future team can start from" with an explicit Limits section. It is short of 5 only because the ICP-OES raw values are published as a figure PDF rather than a data table, and the records are PDFs rather than per-experiment data.
justification.w5: Claims carry numbered, resolvable references with DOIs on Description, Engineering, Results and Contribution, including the bioRxiv source for SP4/SP10 and the phage-display papers behind the Ni/Co peptides; figure captions state what is schematic rather than measured. Prior iGEM work is credited (BIT-China 2024, GreatBay-SCIE, Yucai-SZ, the reused BBa parts), third-party fonts and the UN SDG icons are licensed, and AI tool use is listed on Attributions. Minor gaps only: a few sustainability figures rest on paraphrased literature without an inline marker.

J1.one_line: A genuinely engineered, well-documented four-cycle project with strong expression data and exemplary honesty about its limits, held back from the top by a central metal-capture assay that has no non-engineered control and no stated replicates.
strengths: Four DBTL cycles where each test changed the next design: 28 C induction lock, fraction-based measurement in K. rhaeticus, scaffold lock from the 2x2 SP-CBM screen, and the switch to 10 mM Tris-HCl to stop hydroxide precipitation (Engineering, Learn sections).

Expression and secretion are shown against real controls: empty-vector and sterile-medium baselines, -Rha versus +Rha, two induction temperatures, colony PCR plus whole-plasmid nanopore verification, and HiBiT bar charts with units and mean +/- SD (Engineering Figs 2-8).

Registry work is substantial and student-attributed: 16 basic and 11 composite parts with host, topology, composition, biosafety clearance, source citations and Design/Characterisation/Discussion/Application/Experiment documentation (e.g. BBa_26N7CE1M, BBa_26AMNFBN).

Human Practices is two-way and consequential: twelve interviews narrowed the user from 'battery recyclers' to post-solvent-extraction tail streams, changed the validation logic (expression, immobilisation and adsorption validated separately) and the intended mode of use (pre-made adsorbent rather than cells grown in wastewater).

An unusually honest Limits section plus a reusable handover package: 21 protocols, a 91-page notebook, FASTA designs with SHA-256 checksums, the HiBiT CSV and the ICP-OES source figure with its sample definitions (Contribution).
weaknesses: The Cycle 4 ICP-OES panel has no wild-type or empty-vector K. rhaeticus arm and no cellulose-only arm, so removal of Li/Ni/Co/Mn cannot be attributed to the displayed peptide rather than to native biomass and cellulose sorption (Results, Fig. 9; Engineering, Fig. 11).
No n, replicates or error bars are reported for the metal data, unlike the HiBiT figures which do state mean +/- SD; single endpoint values per condition carry the project's main functional claim.

The protein is shown to be in the washed cell pellet, which contains both cells and cell-associated cellulose; nothing in the figures separates cellulose binding from cell-surface retention, so 'anchored on bacterial cellulose' is inferred rather than demonstrated (Cycle 2 Test/Learn).

Prose overclaims relative to the team's own Limits page: 'rigorously proves', 'quantitatively validated multi-metal bio-adsorption and recovery platform' and 'closed-loop' sit alongside 12-19% single-step Li removal, and the Registry documentation titles use 'Ultra-High-Affinity', 'Premier' and 'Flagship'.
Presentation choices hide content a reader needs: a passphrase intro gate on the landing page, scrambled glyph breadcrumbs, and team member profiles reachable only through a claw-machine game.
red_flags: Central functional assay (ICP-OES metal capture) run without a non-engineered biological control; the team acknowledges on Contribution -> Limits that the mass balance 'does not show that the peptide is the only thing binding it', so the headline capture claim is not evidentially supported.

Mass-balance closure of 89-99% is presented in Engineering/Results as proof that ions are 'specifically immobilized onto the bacterial cellulose matrix'; it is an accounting check only, as the Limits page itself states. The two pages disagree in tone.

AI tool use declared on the Attributions page (deepseek, Doubao, OpenAI Codex/GPT) covering literature synthesis, translation, drafting of the Description, Human Practices and SDG text, carbon-footprint workflow structuring, and wiki implementation. Disclosure is full and the team states it reviewed all outputs, so I treat this as transparent rather than as an integrity concern, but it means some wiki prose is not wholly in the students' own words, and I would ask about it in Q&A rather than report it.
Wet-lab work was carried out in a sponsor's (Link Spider) laboratory and the instructor records guiding 'raw data collection'; declared, not hidden, but it moderates aspect 6.

No model, measurement, hardware, software or proof-of-concept pages exist (voids). Not required, but the absence of a measurement page means the ICP-OES method's calibration, detection limits and dilution handling are described only in prose.
pages_read: engineering (all four DBTL cycles, in full)
attributions (rendered live with headless Chrome; the crawl captured it empty)

calibrated.changed: none. a8 4.5 rests on Registry entries I could actually open and read (role, topology, host, sub-part composition, five documentation sections), which is the p.18 basis; a2 3.5 is right because the headline metal-capture assay has no non-engineered control, the same fault that held Mingdao's capstone and SHSID's plant trial to 3.5.

justification.a1: Four linked DBTL cycles carry one idea from a prototype cassette in E. coli DH5a, through electroporation into Komagataeibacter rhaeticus, a 2x2 SP-CBM scaffold screen, to an eight-strain metal-binding panel measured by ICP-OES at four concentrations (Engineering, Results Fig. 9). That chain of increasingly harder steps, plus 27 Registry entries, 12 industry interviews and a published protocol/notebook set, is close to the GreatBay_SZ pattern of scale and scope. Held just below 5 because the hardest step, capture from anything resembling real wastewater, was not attempted.
justification.a2: Construction is properly verified (colony PCR at 2,768 bp and whole-plasmid nanopore alignment, Engineering Fig. 2 and Fig. 6) and expression/secretion is well demonstrated with real controls: Fig. 4 includes empty-vector K. rhaeticus and sterile-medium blanks, and induction raises medium supernatant luminescence ~2,500-fold over -Rha (Fig. 3B). The metal work is measured, not modelled: ICP-OES gives numbers for all 8 strains at 10-200 mg/L (Results Fig. 9). The gap is decisive for the headline claim, though: Cycle 4 carries no wild-type or empty-vector biomass arm, so capture cannot be attributed to the ion-binding peptide rather than to native cellulose and cell surface, and the team itself concedes on Contribution -> Limits that mass balance "does not show that the peptide is the only thing binding it"; no replicate n is given for the ICP panel.
justification.a3: The application was narrowed by evidence from stakeholders rather than asserted: Juhefeng and Meizhou Zhongrun ruled out front-end physical recyclers, GEM confirmed residual Li/Ni/Co/Mn in post-extraction tail streams, and Yaoxinmiao placed the entry point at park-level centralised or on-site end-of-pipe stations (Human Practices, Stages 1-2). Lingzhu Technology changed the product form to a pre-manufactured biosorbent supplied to treaters, which is a concrete deployment route. It stops short of TAS Taipei's standard because nothing was tested in a real or synthetic wastewater matrix, and the tested 10-200 mg/L range sits above the ppm tail stream the Description targets, with Li removal only 12.75-19.14%.
justification.a4: Each cycle's test result changes the next build, which is the real test: 16 vs 28 C comparison fixes the induction temperature at 28 C to match the K. rhaeticus growth optimum (Cycle 1 Learn); fractionation showing the PBS-washed pellet holds most signal redirects Cycle 3 to pellet and whole-broth readouts; the 2x2 screen retires CBM3a and SP10 and locks pSEVA331-Prha-SP4-CBM64-HiBiT as a reusable scaffold (Cycle 3 Learn); Cycle 4 then swaps only the C-terminal payload. Deductions: no quantified success criterion is set before testing, there is no model of any kind, Cycle 4 has no negative-strain control, and the Part Collection's account of a 37 C inclusion-body failure contradicts the Engineering page's own statement that no band appeared in either insoluble pellet fraction.
justification.a5: Twelve case studies across five stages, each written as Motivation / Mutual connection / Message / Move, with named industrial counterparts (Juhefeng, Meizhou Zhongrun, GEM, Yaoxinmiao, Lingzhu, Jiecheng, Defang Nano), a regulator, a protein expert and an exchange with BIT-China 2024.
