The changes are traceable: Prof. Meng's point that HiBiT cannot prove metal binding led the team to validate expression, immobilisation and adsorption as separate steps, which is the structure the experiments actually follow; Li Zongjin's shear-force warning moved the plan to supplying pre-made material. The attributions form also records the student lead cutting the entrepreneurship deliverable because the cost data would not stand up, which is the responsible half of the rubric done honestly rather than decoratively.
justification.a6: The attributions form is unusually complete: 30 named entries with role tags and itemised tasks, 6 external contributors (SnapGene licences, two external advisors, a writing advisor, a peer-team collaboration, and sponsor Link Spider who "provided laboratories for our wet lab activities"), explicit declarations for all five iGEM/partner offers, and a project timeline. Three AI tools are declared by name with the specific sections they touched. Against a 5: the instructor's own entry covers guiding raw data collection, troubleshooting, protocol optimisation and reviewing/archiving lab records, the lab and ICP-OES instrument are external, and AI assisted drafting of Description, Human Practices and SDG text and the wiki build. All declared, so this is a transparency credit with a real outside-help discount, not an integrity question.
justification.a7: This is the project's strongest engineering suit: a Type IIS BsaI Golden Gate cassette on the broad-host pSEVA331 backbone, two prior-team Registry parts reused (rhaSR-PrhaBAD BBa_K4663024 and RiboJ BBa_K4216041), and 16 basic plus 11 composite new entries organised into six functional tiers (Parts; Part Collection). The point of the collection is reuse: one validated SP4-CBM64-HiBiT scaffold with eight interchangeable C-terminal payloads, demonstrated by the fact that Cycle 4 skipped re-screening entirely. That is a collection designed to be reused, not a pile of submissions.
justification.a8: The Parts page tabulates all 27 entries with Registry ID, type, function, length and link, and Part Collection adds per-tier design rationale, the annotated device map for BBa_26N7CE1M, and the cycle-by-cycle characterisation. Contribution publishes 11 FASTA designs with SHA-256 checksums, the 8-value HiBiT CSV, the ICP-OES source figure with axis breaks retained, 21 protocols and a 91-page notebook. Two reasons it is not a 5: the handbook judges parts on the Registry and parts.igem.org returned an AWS WAF challenge from this environment, so Registry-side depth is unverified; and much of the primary record sits in downloadable PDFs rather than on the page.
justification.w1: Description states the aim, chassis, the SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP construct, the four target metals and the intended niche in one abstract, and that abstract ends by naming what is not established (mixed-metal selectivity, product purity, reuse, closed loop) - rare and valuable. The Project hub gives a one-paragraph orientation to each of the four pages. It falls short of Lambert_GA because the actual home page carries only 188 words and sits behind a typed-passphrase intro animation, so the clearest statement of the project is one click deeper than it should be.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is anchored to a figure or a number on the page: SDS-PAGE across induced/uninduced and soluble/insoluble fractions (Fig. 3A, Fig. 7), HiBiT bar charts plotted as mean +/- SD with empty-vector and sterile-medium baselines (Fig. 4), nanopore alignments, and the full ICP-OES table of residual and recovered concentrations for 8 strains at 4 inputs (Results Fig. 9), with the raw CSV and the original source-figure PDF downloadable. The Limits section flags where the evidence stops. Short of 5 only because replicate counts are not stated for the metal panel and the capture assay has no untransformed control.
justification.w3: Navigation is coherent and judge-aware: four labelled sections, an on-page table of contents everywhere, figures on Results that link back to the matching cycle on Engineering, a search box, and genuine accessibility toggles for high contrast and a readable font. Working against it: a passphrase gate on entry, team members hidden behind a claw-machine game with only a plain-text name list as fallback, decorative glyph noise in page headers, and large verbatim duplication of Cycle 3 and Cycle 4 text and captions between Engineering and Results, which makes the project read longer than it is.
justification.w4: Contribution is close to a model handover page: 11 construct FASTA files with a checksum manifest, 21 protocols, 17 weekly records in a searchable 91-page notebook, the HiBiT CSV with its sample definitions (A = residual liquid, B = post-cellulase liquid), an 18-page safety manual offered for adaptation, and a four-step guide telling the next team to verify the clone, follow that clone's own records and not mix protocol versions. The six-item Limits list tells a future team exactly which claims not to build on. Kept below 5 because the reusable material is mostly inside PDFs rather than structured on-wiki.
justification.w5: Fifteen numbered references on Description and ten on Engineering/Results, with DOIs or stable links, used in-text at the point of each claim rather than dumped at the end; part provenance is cited to the primary literature (Vannas et al. for SP4/SP10, Schiefner et al. for CBM64, Yaniv et al. for CBM3a, Bhargawa et al. and Sieber/Matys/Maruthamuthu for the metal peptides). Figure provenance, prior-team Registry parts, UN SVG icon sourcing, font licences and the CC-BY terms are all declared, and the further-reading block explicitly says those chassis modifications were not implemented here. Spot-checked citations are real and say what the wiki says they say.

J2.one_line: A genuinely engineered, modular biosorption platform with four real DBTL cycles, 27 Registry parts and quantitative ICP-OES data, let down mainly by the absence of a non-engineered control in the metal-capture assay and by never touching a realistic wastewater matrix.
strengths: Four DBTL cycles where each test result visibly changes the next build: 16 vs 28 C fixes induction, fractionation redirects the readout to the cell-cellulose pellet, the 2x2 SP-CBM screen retires CBM3a/SP10 and locks SP4-CBM64-HiBiT as a reusable scaffold, and Cycle 4 then swaps only the payload (Engineering, Cycles 1-4).

A parts collection built for reuse rather than for counting: Type IIS Golden Gate on broad-host pSEVA331, two prior-team Registry parts reused, 16 basic plus 11 composite entries in six functional tiers, one validated scaffold carrying eight interchangeable metal payloads (Parts; Part Collection).

Real controls on the reporter work: empty-vector K. rhaeticus and sterile-medium blanks near background, uninduced arms throughout, and a ~2,500-fold induced increase in medium supernatant luminescence (Engineering Fig. 3B, Fig. 4).

Quantitative, fully reported metal data: ICP-OES residual and cellulase-released concentrations for 8 strains at 10/50/100/200 mg/L, with the numbers in the text, the source figure preserved with its axis breaks, and the underlying CSV downloadable (Results Fig. 9; Contribution).

Human Practices that actually moved the project: GEM and Yaoxinmiao relocated the application to end-of-pipe polishing, Lingzhu changed the product form to pre-manufactured biosorbent, and Prof. Meng's warning that HiBiT cannot prove metal binding produced the staged expression/immobilisation/adsorption validation the experiments follow (Human Practices, Stages 1-5).

An attributions form of exemplary completeness: 30 itemised entries, 3 AI tools declared with the specific sections they touched, 6 external contributors including the sponsor who provided the laboratory, all five partner offers answered, and a project timeline (Attributions).

A handover page that tells future teams where the evidence stops: 11 FASTA designs with SHA-256 checksums, 21 protocols, a 91-page notebook, and a six-item Limits list stating that mass balance is a measurement check and not proof of specificity (Contribution).
weaknesses: The Cycle 4 capture assay has no wild-type, empty-vector or scaffold-without-IBP arm, so the central functional claim cannot be separated from non-specific sorption by native bacterial cellulose and cell surface; every number in Results Fig. 9 is a capture by engineered biomass, not a capture by the peptide.

No replicate count or error bars are reported for the ICP-OES panel, and the 'strict mass balance closure' wording is generous for cases like Co at 10 mg/L, where 2.39 + 6.51 = 8.90 against a 10 mg/L input.

Nothing was tested in a real or synthetic wastewater matrix, and the tested 10-200 mg/L range sits above the ppm tail stream the Description targets; single-step Li removal of 12.75-19.14% is modest for the stated application.

An internal contradiction between pages: Part Collection describes 37 C induction trapping protein in inclusion bodies and the Results conclusion refers to 'the inclusion-body-like band observed in early Cycle 1 trials', while the Engineering and Results Cycle 1 text states that no target band appeared in the insoluble pellet at either temperature.
No modelling of any kind: no isotherm, no binding constant, no capacity per gram of biomass, so the data cannot be extrapolated to a reactor or compared with conventional adsorbents.

Sprawl and friction in the wiki: a typed-passphrase gate before the home page, team members behind a claw-machine game, and long verbatim duplication of Cycle 3 and Cycle 4 text and captions across Engineering and Results.

Much of the primary record (notebook, protocols, construct sequences, the original ICP figure) lives in downloadable PDFs rather than on the page, and Registry-side documentation could not be checked from here.
red_flags: Specificity not controlled: the ICP-OES metal-capture panel (Results Fig. 9 / Engineering Cycle 4) includes no non-engineered biomass control, so adsorption attributed to the ion-binding peptides may be partly or wholly native cellulose sorption. The team concedes the point on Contribution -> Limits but the Results and Engineering conclusions still read as a validated multi-metal capture platform.

Internal inconsistency about Cycle 1: Part Collection states that 37 C induction trapped the fusion protein in insoluble inclusion bodies and the Results conclusion refers to an inclusion-body-like band in early Cycle 1 trials, whereas the Engineering and Results Cycle 1 text states no target band was observed in either insoluble pellet fraction. One account must be wrong; worth asking which.

Registry pages could not be opened from this environment (parts.igem.org returned an AWS WAF / CAPTCHA challenge, which I did not attempt to bypass), so a7 and a8 rest on the team's own wiki tables and the claimed BBa identifiers; Registry-side documentation depth is unverified by me and should be checked by a judge with access.

AI assistance is declared for substantive prose, not just translation: Doubao for drafting/revising the Description, Human Practices and SDG sections and for structuring the carbon-footprint workflow, and OpenAI Codex/GPT for drafting English page text and building the wiki (Attributions, AI Tool Use). Properly disclosed and not an integrity issue, but the panel should read the polished English prose as AI-assisted when weighing student voice.

Instructor footprint in the lab record: the mentor entry covers guiding raw data collection, troubleshooting, protocol optimisation and reviewing/revising/archiving laboratory records, and the sponsor provided the laboratory. Declared, so no integrity concern, but it tempers a6.

Routine check only, not an allegation: Komagataeibacter rhaeticus should be confirmed against the iGEM high-school organism white list. The team declares RG-1/BSL-1 containment and the Safety page is thorough, so I raise this as a question rather than a safety referral.

calibrated.changed: none — a2 3.5 for a capture assay with no non-engineered control is the same deduction I applied to squirrel-guangzhou's uncontrolled kill-switch work and keystone's confounded controls; a6 4.0 is earned by a 30-entry form with declared externals.

justification.a1: The project climbs through genuinely harder steps inside one season: a rhamnose-inducible SP-CBM-HiBiT-IBP cassette built and expressed in E. coli, moved into Komagataeibacter rhaeticus, then an orthogonal 2x2 SP-CBM scaffold screen, then an eight-strain metal-binding panel measured by ICP-OES across 10-200 mg/L for four metals (Engineering, Cycles 1-4). Twenty-seven Registry entries, a 91-page notebook, 21 protocols and twelve stakeholder case studies sit behind it. It falls short of the GreatBay anchor only because there is no model at all, no hardware, and the capture numbers themselves are modest (Li+ single-step removal 12.75-19.14%).
justification.a2: Expression and secretion are convincingly shown: SDS-PAGE bands at the predicted 16 kDa, HiBiT luminescence rising ~2,500-fold in the medium supernatant on induction, with uninduced and empty-pSEVA331 controls near background (Engineering Fig. 3, Fig. 4). Cellulose association is supported by fractionation of washed pellet versus supernatant (92.8% retention, Part Collection). The metal capture claim is weaker than the prose: the ICP-OES assay (Engineering Fig. 11) has no wild-type or empty-vector biomass arm, no stated replicate number, and the team's own Part Collection page recomputes closures of 83.6% and 110.04% against the Engineering page's "strict mass balance closure" and "rigorously proves that captured metal ions are specifically immobilized". Bare bacterial cellulose binds metal ions, so peptide-driven capture is not yet established.
justification.a3: The application was located by stakeholders rather than asserted: GEM confirmed that residual Li, Ni, Co and Mn remain after solvent extraction, Shenzhen Yaoxinmiao moved the entry point to park-level centralised wastewater stations and on-site enterprise stations, and Jiecheng New Energy benchmarked kisMET against back-washable reusable resins already in use (Human Practices, Stages 2 and 4). Li Zongjin's follow-up supplied industrial cost ranges and a 10-20% cost-margin threshold. What stops this short of the TAS anchor is that nothing has been tested in anything resembling a real stream: all measurements are single-metal standards in 10 mM Tris-HCl at pH 7.2, and the carrier is consumed by cellulase each cycle, which the Jiecheng interview identified as the key commercial weakness.
justification.a4: Four documented cycles in which the Learn step changed the next Build: the 16 vs 28 C comparison fixed induction at 28 C to match K. rhaeticus physiology; Cycle 2's finding that signal sits in the washed pellet redefined which fractions Cycle 3 measured; the 2x2 screen locked SP4-CBM64 and justified skipping redundant E. coli screening for the seven Cycle 4 constructs; and unbuffered water was replaced with 10 mM Tris-HCl after hydroxide precipitation of the divalent metals (Engineering, Cycle 4 Learn). Against the anchor this is one tier down: there is no model fitted to the team's own data and used for design, success criteria are stated after the fact rather than before, and the Cycle 1 account of inclusion bodies is internally inconsistent (Results Conclusion refers to "the inclusion-body-like band observed in early Cycle 1 trials" while the Test section reports none).
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the submission. Twelve interviews across five stages, each written as Motivation / Mutual Connection / Message / Move, and the Moves are real: the target user migrated from front-end recyclers (Meizhou Zhongrun, little wastewater) to the hydrometallurgy tail (GEM) to park-level wastewater stations (Yaoxinmiao); Prof. Meng's point that HiBiT cannot prove metal binding produced the step-wise expression / immobilisation / adsorption validation logic that the ICP-OES assay follows; Li Zongjin's follow-up made bead-yield measurement a wet-lab priority and added cost-per-use and a 5 L stirred-tank validation plan; BIT-China's advice restructured the SDG argument around SDG 6 and 12. Critical voices are kept in (Jiecheng: resins already do this), and the Safety page records informed consent forms and privacy agreements for interviewees. Short of 5 because the regulator conversation stays at SDG mapping rather than misuse or environmental-release analysis, and several Moves change framing rather than the bench.
justification.a6: The Attributions page (which needs JavaScript to render) gives 30 individual entries naming specific tasks per person, four former members marked as no contribution, three AI tools with the scope of each disclosed, and six external contributors including the sponsor Link Spider, which provided both the laboratory and funding, and advisors Zhao Xuanye, Mr Du and Zhou Sha. Student entries describe hands-on work (Golden Gate primer design, heat-shock transformation, colony PCR, SDS-PAGE, HiBiT assays, K. rhaeticus electroporation), and the student leader discloses that she drafted the form herself. Two things I would ask about rather than assume: instructors "supervised raw data collection" and "optimized corresponding operation protocols", and no one is credited with running the ICP-OES, which is unlikely to be a school instrument.
justification.a7: The project is standard-parts synthetic biology in the way the handbook describes. It builds on a pSEVA331 Golden Gate backbone and reuses two existing Registry parts with credit (RiboJ BBa_K4216041, rhaSR-PrhaBAD BBa_K4663024), and contributes 16 basic and 11 composite entries organised as a six-tier toolkit (Parts; Part Collection). Modularity is exercised, not just asserted: the same SP4-CBM64-HiBiT scaffold carries eight interchangeable 7-30 aa payloads, and the Part Collection sets out three explicit reuse modes for other teams. Several composite devices are shown to express, secrete and anchor, which is well beyond the "functioning Part" bar for a high school team.
justification.a8: The Parts page tabulates all 27 entries with Registry ID, type, function and length, the Part Collection carries per-part Design and Characterization records, and the Contribution page publishes eleven FASTA design files with SHA-256 checksums, the HiBiT CSV, the ICP-OES source figure, 21 protocols and a 91-page notebook, all with an explicit statement that design sequences are not sequencing reads. I could not open parts.igem.org from here (403 / bot check), so I cannot confirm how much of that characterisation actually sits on the Registry records rather than only on the wiki; the wiki itself says the Registry records "identify the designs" while the experiments are described on the wiki pages, which reads as thinner Registry content than the wiki implies.
justification.w1: Every section page opens with a one-line Summary, and the Description abstract states problem, approach and the four target ions in a few calibrated sentences. The home page, however, is an intro animation gated behind a passphrase prompt ("Type KisMET") and, once entered, offers only the tagline "Exploring metal fate in water with bacterial cellulose" plus navigation: no problem statement, no schematic, no route onward. Measured against the Lambert_GA and Patras home-page anchor, a judge arriving at the front door learns almost nothing and has to find the Description page unaided.
justification.w2: Claims are mostly attached to real figures with detailed captions: colony PCR at 2,768 bp and nanopore alignments (Fig. 2, Fig. 6), Coomassie gels with lane keys, HiBiT bar charts with mean +/- SD, and ICP-OES values quoted numerically for every strain and concentration. The Part Collection's "Proven vs. proposed - stated plainly" table is better practice than most teams manage. Against that, the Engineering and Results pages still say the data "rigorously proves that captured metal ions are specifically immobilized" and show "strict mass balance closure" while the team's own Part Collection arithmetic gives 83.6% and 110.04% and states that "Reporter controls do not replace a matched biomass or empty-vector comparison in a metal-adsorption assay". Replicate numbers for the ICP-OES panel are never given.
justification.w3: Navigation is competent: standard pages are present and grouped as Project / Wet Lab / Human Practices, each page has an on-page contents list, and figures cross-link to where the same figure is discussed on another page. Three things work against it. The landing page is a passphrase gate, the Team page's primary interface is a claw-machine game that hides member profiles behind play, and the content sprawls - the Results page largely repeats Engineering verbatim, Part Collection runs to roughly 18,700 words and Sustainability to 7,500. "Complete but not sprawling" is not met.
justification.w4: This is the wiki's best aspect. The Contribution page is written as an explicit handover: eleven construct design files with a checksum manifest, the HiBiT measurement CSV with its sample definitions (A = residual liquid, B = post-cellulase liquid), 21 protocols, 17 weekly records in a 91-page searchable notebook, an 18-page safety manual offered for adaptation, and a four-step "what a future team can start from" that warns against mixing protocol versions. The Limits section tells the next team exactly which claims not to build on. The only drawback is that the notebook and protocols arrive mainly as PDFs, with thin on-page content behind them.
justification.w5: Citation practice is consistently good: numbered references with DOIs or stable links on Description, Engineering, Results and Contribution; peptide choices traced to specific papers (Bhargawa 2024 for LiBP, Sieber 2025 and Matys 2020 for Ni/Co, Maruthamuthu 2018 for Mn/Co); reused Registry parts credited by BBa ID; prior iGEM work credited by name (BIT-China 2024 OUROBOROS, GreatBay-SCIE, Yucai-SZ); third-party fonts, the CC-BY licence and three AI tools all disclosed. Minor reservations only: SP4/SP10 rest on a bioRxiv preprint, and two market claims rest on Chinese-language newspaper items I could not open.

J3.one_line: A disciplined four-cycle engineering story on an unusual cellulose-producing chassis, with outstanding human practices, attribution and handover documentation, let down by a metal-adsorption assay that has no biomass control and by overclaiming prose the team's own Part Collection page quietly refutes.
strengths: Four DBTL cycles in which the Learn step demonstrably changed the next Build: 28 C induction, fraction-based measurement after the Cycle 2 anchoring finding, SP4-CBM64 locked by a 2x2 screen, Tris buffering introduced after hydroxide precipitation (Engineering)

Human Practices that moved the project: the target user shifted from front-end recyclers to the hydrometallurgy tail to park-level wastewater stations across three named interviews, and Prof. Meng's warning that HiBiT cannot prove metal binding produced the step-wise validation logic the team then followed

Expression and secretion backed by proper controls - uninduced cultures, empty-pSEVA331 strain and sterile medium blanks near background against a ~2,500-fold induced signal (Engineering Fig. 3, Fig. 4)

A genuinely reusable 27-part toolkit with one swappable payload slot, exercised across eight peptides, plus FASTA designs with SHA-256 checksums, 21 protocols and a 91-page notebook on the Contribution page

Attribution of unusual quality: 30 named entries with specific tasks, three AI tools with their scope disclosed, six external contributors including the sponsor that supplied the laboratory, and informed consent forms recorded for interviewees
A Part Collection page that recomputes its own mass balances, names the missing control, and tabulates proven against proposed applications
weaknesses: The ICP-OES adsorption panel has no wild-type or empty-vector biomass arm, so metal capture cannot be attributed to the ion-binding peptides rather than to bare bacterial cellulose; no replicate number is given for any ICP-OES condition

Engineering and Results claim "strict mass balance closure" and that the data "rigorously proves" specific immobilisation, while the team's own Part Collection page shows closures of 83.6% and 110.04% and says the fractions do not establish specificity - the pages contradict each other
The home page is a passphrase gate with no statement of problem, approach or goal and no schematic, so a judge landing there is given nothing to orient on
Heavy duplication and sprawl: Results restates Engineering almost verbatim, and Part Collection (~18,700 words) and Sustainability (~7,500) are far past "complete but not sprawling"
No model of any kind, and no test in anything resembling a real leachate - all capture data are single-metal standards in Tris buffer
Registry records could not be opened from here, so the depth of on-Registry documentation behind the 27 IDs is unverified
red_flags: Overclaiming in the Engineering and Results prose ("rigorously proves", "strict mass balance closure", "quantitatively validated") that the team's own Part Collection page refutes with its own arithmetic (NiBP2 at 10 mg/L = 83.6%; CoBP2 at 50 mg/L = 110.04%). Not misconduct - the correction is published on the team's own wiki - but a judging-session question about which page the team stands behind.
Metal-adsorption assay lacks a matched biomass / empty-vector control, which the team states openly on the Part Collection page but not on Engineering or Results, where the claim is made.

parts.igem.org returned 403 / a bot check for every part I tried (BBa_26N7CE1M, BBa_26E50YQ1, BBa_2690BGT5), so Registry documentation depth is unverified rather than judged absent. I did not attempt the CAPTCHA.

Three AI tools are disclosed as having drafted and translated English page text and built the wiki; the prose voice is noticeably uniform across pages. Disclosure is acceptable under the Responsible AI guidance, so this is a question for the session about the reasoning behind project choices, not an allegation.
The wet lab was hosted in a laboratory provided by the sponsor Link Spider, and no one is credited with operating the ICP-OES. Worth clarifying who ran the instrument and prepared the dilutions.

screen.project_title: BioScyde — scytonemin as a biologically produced UV filter in E. coli
screen.what_they_built: Heterologous transfer of the Nostoc punctiforme scytonemin pathway into E. coli, split into a cytoplasmic monomer arm (ScyA/B/C plus AroG-tyrA precursor boost) and a periplasmic arm (ScyE with pelB/ssdsbA signal peptides for oxidative dimerisation). Supported by a large in-silico redesign pipeline, a DNA/primer design suite, and an unusually deep iHP programme.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli TOP10 / BLR(DE3) / BL21-AI; 30 BBa parts deposited (scyA, scyB, scyC, scyE native and three pelB variants, ssdsbA-scyE, emrD, tyrA-fbr, EboA/B/C/E/F, pBad). Several parts are design-only, uploaded without wet-lab characterisation.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /engineering: gel electrophoresis confirmed ScyACB and AroG-tyrA plasmids at expected size (with a documented Twist synthesis error giving ~8 kb and ~10 kb bands); SDS-PAGE bands at ~130 kDa (AroG tetramer, unconfirmed) and ~65 kDa consistent with ScyA/TyrA; His-tag ELISA gave ~600 ng/mL after proteinase-K lysis. TLC detected no scytonemin monomer; no ScyE band was ever obtained; antibiotics failed after August so untransformed controls grew like transformed cells.
screen.hp_integration: Yes and traceably — Prof. Tanya Soule's interview revealed the unremoved native cyanobacterial signal peptide, which produced ScyE-pelB V2 and V3 (BBa_263NY899, BBa_26M9O8N7), and stakeholder work forced the team to drop 'reef-safe'/SPF claims in favour of an evidence-based claims register.
screen.reason: Exemplary honesty, iHP and modelling discipline, but on aspect 2 almost nothing worked: no ScyE detected across four build-test cycles, no monomer by TLC, and an acknowledged antibiotic-selection failure that invalidates the later expression work. The /attributions page is effectively empty (209 words, heading only), so aspect 6 cannot be checked at all. Finalist calibre needs a working part; this wiki documents, very well, that none was obtained.
screen.field_notes: SPC (St. Paul's College, Hong Kong; Fashion & Cosmetics village) attacked oxybenzone-linked reef toxicity by making scytonemin, a cyanobacterial UVA pigment, in E. coli. Two arms: ScyA/B/C monomer synthesis boosted with AroG-tyrA, and periplasmic export of ScyE for the final oxidative dimerisation, since only the monomer has previously been made in E. coli. Four DBTL cycles produced SDS-PAGE bands consistent with ScyA and AroG/TyrA, a His-ELISA signal near 600 ng/mL, but no ScyE band, no TLC-detectable monomer, and an August antibiotic-selection failure that the team reports openly. Thirty BBa parts were deposited including a signal-peptide series (native, pelB V1-V3, ssdsbA) and the Ebo transport complex, many design-only. Dry lab is large: redox MD showing the Cys62-Cys74 disulfide is permanent (SG-SG 2.04 A oxidised vs 4.82 A reduced), pocket-conserving redesign where Rosetta and RFdiffusion strategies were killed by the team's own evidence, docking against a native control (-9.55 vs -7.86 to -8.18 kcal/mol), a VEGA toxicity screen declared uninformative (60 of 85 predictions outside applicability domain), and a public GitHub repo. iHP ran ten expert consultations plus a 102-response consumer survey and demonstrably changed both the construct design and the claims register.

screen.project_title: PNPeeker: p-nitrophenol detection, degradation and containment for agricultural soil
screen.what_they_built: A three-part E. coli system - a PobR/PpobA/RFP whole-cell biosensor for p-nitrophenol improved by a computationally selected S120T mutation, a five-gene hydroquinone-pathway degradation strain (pnpA-pnpB-pnpC-pnpE-pnpD), and a cold-inducible lysis kill switch - plus three generations each of field sampling hardware and spraying hardware, ending in a retrofitted consumer drone.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning, BL21(DE3) for sensing; pSB1A3 backbone with J23100, B0034 and T0015 standard elements. 9 new BBa_26* parts alongside BBa_B0015, BBa_B0034, BBa_J23100 and BBa_K5083099.
screen.best_evidence: /results 1.6: the PobR-S120T sensor beat wild type at every concentration from 0.001 to 10 mg/L (about 11.2 vs 7.5 A.U. at 0.1 mg/L; about 20.0 vs 15.5 A.U. at 10 mg/L, roughly +29%), n = 3, fluorescence normalised to OD600. /results System 2: the degradation strain removed about 92%, 95%, 94%, 87% and 54% of pNP at 10, 50, 100, 500 and 1000 ug/L after 24 h. /results 1.8: the sensor discriminated certified blank soil spiked at 10, 50, 100 and 500 ug/kg.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and it is the backbone of the project: five HP stages each tied to a decision, which narrowed the claim from a detector to a presumptive screening tool whose positives must be confirmed by HPLC/LC-MS/GC-MS, drove the insulated box to pocket-sized sampling redesign, and turned a failed manual spraying trial into the modular drone spraying platform.
screen.reason: Broadest competent project in the batch: sensing, remediation, containment and two independent hardware lines, with docking and MD used prospectively to pick S120T and then validated wet-lab, a standard curve, soil-matrix testing against a certified reference soil, and a kill switch with real OD data at 16 C versus 37 C. Human practices is unusually disciplined - each stage named around a decision, and the team narrowed its own claim rather than overselling. Caveats for the panel: the team itself lists specificity, LOD, LOQ and recovery as not yet done, the degradation percentages are reported without an explicit non-engineered control in the summary, and there is no attributions page for a project of this scope. Deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: Squirrel-Beijing (CHN, Bioremediation) built PNPeeker, an engineered E. coli platform for detecting and removing p-nitrophenol in agricultural soil. System 1 is a whole-cell biosensor, J23100-B0034-PobR-T0015-PpobA-B0034-RFP-T0015 assembled by overlap-extension PCR into pSB1A3, giving a dose-dependent Fluorescence/OD600 response over 0.001-10 mg/L; AutoDock Vina docking identified S68, S120 and H124 in the PobR pocket, 10 ns MD ranked S120T most stable (RMSD 1.7-2.0 versus 2.0-2.4 for wild type), and the S120T sensor outperformed wild type at every concentration, about +29% at 10 mg/L. A log-linear standard curve (Y = 3.674X + 1.208) supports back-calculation, and the sensor discriminated pNP spiked at 10-500 ug/kg into a gamma-irradiated certified blank soil reference material (Tanmo TMQC4390), which the team states openly is not field soil. System 2 expresses the five-gene hydroquinone pathway pnpA-pnpB-pnpC-pnpE-pnpD and removed roughly 92-95% of pNP at 10-100 ug/L in 24 h, falling to 54% at 1000 ug/L. A cold-inducible lysis circuit fires strongest at 15-20 C and collapsed OD600 at 16 C while the 37 C culture kept growing. Hardware runs to 8.8k words: three detection generations (insulated box with lyophilised bacteria, then phone-based fluorescence recognition with GPS heatmaps, then a pocket kit using cold-induced bacteria developed with RDFZ-China), three remediation generations ending in a DJI Air 3S retrofitted with symmetric ultrasonic-atomiser spray pods triggered optically from the heatmap, plus BOM, build manual, troubleshooting PDF and a drone-compliance overview. 24.5k-word IHP in five decision-linked stages; the team explicitly scopes the device as a presumptive screening tool requiring lab confirmation. Specificity, LOD, LOQ and recovery are acknowledged as not yet measured; no attributions page.

justification.a1: Three modules all carried to measured data, not just design: a PobR-PpobA-RFP sensor with a dose-response, a structure-guided S120T mutant with a measured ~29% output gain, a soil-extract test over four spiking levels, a five-gene hydroquinone pathway with HPLC removal kinetics at five concentrations, and a two-step cold-inducible containment circuit (Results, Engineering). Three generations of detection and remediation hardware add a prototyping arm, including an honest failure (the DIY drone could not lift its payload, Hardware). That is the TAS Taipei pattern of results building on each other; it falls short of a 5 because the sensor lacks specificity and LOD work and the claimed integrated sense-and-degrade strain has no data behind it.
justification.a2: The sensor dose-response uses a 0 mg/L negative control, medium-blank subtraction, Fluorescence/OD600 normalisation, n = 3 biological replicates and mean +/- SD (Results 1.2, 1.6), and the degradation assay is quantified by HPLC against an empty-vector BL21-Control and an abiotic control, giving 92/95/94/87/54% removal across 10-1000 ug/L (Results System 2; Experiments 7.6-7.7). Two of three modules are therefore shown to work against proper controls with replicates. The containment module is weaker: the lysis conclusion rests on OD600 alone at 16/25/37 C with no lysis-gene-free control strain, which the team itself flags, and the whole project lacks specificity testing against other phenols, LOD/LOQ and spiked recovery.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and was narrowed by stakeholders into screening rather than confirmation, with an explicit boundary that positives must go to HPLC/LC-MS labs (Human Practices overview), and the cost case is from their own build: about Y400 per kit and roughly Y1 per test (Description, Hardware Cost). But the biology has never met a real contaminated sample - the soil was a certified gamma-irradiated blank reference material spiked in the lab (Results, Main Results), and the field hardware demonstrations used empty tubes or substitute materials. The drone spraying of live engineered bacteria remains an aspiration with no release-risk assessment.
justification.a4: Six labelled DBTL cycles each close properly: A1 identifies poor low-concentration discrimination, A2 answers it with docking plus 10 ns MD across four candidate mutants and validates S120T in the wet lab with every other circuit element held constant, and A3 turns the readout into a calibration curve and a soil workflow (Engineering, Cycles A1-A3). C1 deliberately characterises PcspA with GFP before attaching cytotoxic effectors in C2 - good engineering discipline. The hardware arm iterates on measured failure and on stakeholder review rather than on troubleshooting, and the summary table states the next measurement for each bottleneck.
justification.a5: Engagements are with named institutions across stages - Beijing Beikong sewage treatment centre, Zhejiang Institute of Geological Survey, Beijing Water Science and Technology Institute, Prof. Shen Xiantao at Tongji Medical College HUST, Zhangzhou Emergency Medical Center, Liantuo agricultural base, Jiangsu Environmental Protection Group and Suzhou Yisibei - each written as a design/build/test/learn loop with a stated consequence. Two consequences are substantive: the farm base's concern about engineered cells persisting in open soil is what drove the cold-inducible containment module, and the emergency-medicine exchange forced the repositioning from minute-level response to planned screening. A summary table maps each exchange to the change it caused; this is HP shaping the project, not outreach.
justification.a6: This is the project's weakest point. The standard Attributions URL returns 404, and the Team page carries only 29 personal bios, several written in the future tense, so nothing on the wiki states what the instructors, the host laboratory or any external group contributed. The Notebook does name three students per task block, which is real evidence of student involvement, but it reads as an allocation grid, several names in it do not appear on the Team page, and nobody is credited with the HPLC runs, plate-reader work or supervision. Gene synthesis, sequencing (Tsingke) and competent cells (Beyotime) are properly declared in Experiments, but without an attributions page I cannot judge how much of the execution was the students'.
justification.a7: The project is built from standard components throughout: J23100, B0034, J0034, T0015 and B0015 in pSB1A3, with all coding sequences codon-optimised and EcoRI/XbaI/SpeI/PstI sites removed for RFC#10 compliance (Experiments 2.2; Engineering Cycle B1). Nine new parts were registered, spanning a regulator, an inducible promoter, five pathway enzymes and two composites, alongside reuse of the existing BBa_K5083099 with new characterisation. The dual-operon split of pnpABCDE to avoid downstream attenuation is a genuine standard-parts design decision rather than a label.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation of components is unusually good: a Parts page with codes, types and per-part rationale, a Contribution page tying each part to data, and full construction records. Against that, five standard URLs are broken or empty - /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design all 404 - and the Model, Measurement, Software and Inclusivity pages are still unedited iGEM template text, so the docking and MD work is nowhere on the Model page. I also could not open any of the Registry entries (parts.igem.org returned 403 throughout), so the handbook's rule of judging parts on the Registry alone could not be applied; I score the wiki-side documentation and note this limit.
justification.w1: The home page carries the project in one pass: the pollutant, why GC-MS is not available to the people affected, the three modules, and the headline numbers (+29% with PobR-MUT, four soil spiking levels, ~95% removal at 24 h) before the reader leaves the first screen or two. Every page then opens with a four-card overview that says what is in it. The only drift is the hardware page's platform framing, which promises a general-purpose pocket microplate reader rather more than the evidence supports.
justification.w2: Nearly every claim is attached to a numbered figure with stated conditions, replicate number and normalisation, and the methods sit beside the result on Results and Engineering; the degradation and sensor sections both describe their controls explicitly. Two things pull it down: the Contribution page states that an integrated strain simultaneously sensing and degrading pNP was built, and no construction record, part or figure for such a strain exists anywhere on the wiki; and at least one caption is wrong (Description Figure 10, under the degradation pathway, repeats Figure 9's PobR docking caption). I could read captions but not the figures themselves.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and ballot-aligned, with a working search, a 28-term glossary, per-page overview cards and prev/next links. The defect is the one the handbook names directly: five standard pages do not resolve, Attributions among them, and the footer still links to Attributions. Content that belongs at /protocols and /design lives on Experiments and Description instead, which works for a reader who explores but breaks the standard URLs a judge is told to rely on.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild this. Experiments gives media recipes, antibiotic and pNP stock preparation, every cloning step, instrument settings and the full HPLC method (C18, methanol:water 50:50, 0.5 mL/min, 318 nm), plus the docking and MD protocols. The Notebook gives dated blocks with named students and three downloadable lab-notebook PDFs, and Hardware adds a BOM, a build manual and a troubleshooting guide. Failures are kept on the page - the 54% removal at 1000 ug/L, the unflyable DIY drone - which is what makes a record useful.
justification.w5: Description carries 23 numbered references with DOIs that resolve, Engineering has its own list, the chassis micrograph is attributed to its Frontiers source, and prior iGEM work is credited properly (GEC-Guangzhou 2025 as the sampling-tube inspiration, RDFZ-China for the cold-induced strain exchange). The gaps are on the longer applied pages: Hardware and much of Human Practices make factual claims about monitoring practice and costs with no inline citation, and the stakeholder accounts are paraphrased without dates.

J1.one_line: A genuinely three-module wet-lab project - sensor, engineered mutant, HPLC-quantified degradation pathway and a cold-inducible kill switch - with excellent protocols, stakeholder-driven engineering and good controls, undermined by a missing Attributions page and several broken standard URLs.
strengths: Two of three modules are demonstrated against proper controls: sensor dose-response with a pNP-free control, n = 3 and SD, and degradation quantified by HPLC against an empty-vector and an abiotic control across five initial concentrations.

A real data-driven redesign: the wild-type sensor's poor low-concentration discrimination led to docking plus 10 ns MD screening of four mutants, and the chosen S120T gave a measured ~29% higher normalised fluorescence under otherwise identical circuit conditions.

Human Practices with named institutions at every stage and consequences that are visible in the biology - the cold-inducible containment module exists because an agricultural base raised persistence in open soil.
Reproducibility: complete media, cloning, plate-reader and HPLC protocols, dated notebook with downloadable lab-notebook PDFs, hardware BOM and build manual, and failures left on the page.
Honest limitation statements throughout - OD600 cannot establish lysis, the extracted fraction is not shown to equal the bioavailable fraction, LOD/LOQ and recovery still outstanding.
weaknesses: No Attributions page (the standard URL 404s) and no statement anywhere of instructor, host-lab or mentor roles; the Team page is bios only, so the division of labour between students and adults cannot be judged.
The cold-inducible lysis claim rests on OD600 at three temperatures with no lysis-gene-free control strain, no CFU counts, live/dead staining or escape rate.
No specificity testing against other phenols or soil organics, and no LOD, LOQ or spiked recovery, so the sensor's analytical performance is undefined.
Contribution claims an integrated strain that senses and degrades pNP simultaneously, with no construction record, part or data anywhere on the wiki.
Model, Measurement, Software and Inclusivity pages are still unedited iGEM template text, and /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design all 404.
Soil work used a certified gamma-irradiated blank reference soil spiked in the lab; no field sample has ever been through the biosensor.
red_flags: Standard page /attributions returns 404; /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design also 404 (handbook p.26, p.29).
Contribution page asserts an integrated sensing-plus-degrading strain was built; no supporting data exists on the wiki - a claim outrunning the evidence, not an integrity finding.
Caption error on Description Figure 10 (degradation pathway figure carries the PobR docking caption from Figure 9).

Several students named in the Notebook task grid (e.g. Mijia Xia, Alexander Yang, Yihan Zhang, Hanyu Xiao, Xiyue Zhang) do not appear on the Team page; one Team bio describes the project as detecting acetaminophen.
I could not open any Registry part page - parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403 for all four parts I tried - so the handbook's rule of judging parts on the Registry entry alone could not be applied here.
Proposed drone spraying of live engineered bacteria over farmland is described without a release risk assessment on the Safety page, which covers only general lab training.

calibrated.changed: a6 2.5 -> 3.0 and a8 3.0 -> 3.5. a6: I gave Keystone 3.5 because its notebook names a lead student per activity; this notebook also names students per task block, which is more than the 2.5 teams have, so 2.5 was too harsh - the name mismatches against the Team page keep it below Keystone. a8: Squirrel Guangzhou has the identical profile (Registry 403, five 404 standard pages, several untouched template pages, a good wiki parts table) and I scored it 3.5; this team additionally has a Contribution page tying each part to its data, so 3.0 was inconsistent.

justification.a1: PNPeeker delivers three built-and-tested modules (PobR-PpobA-RFP sensor, a five-gene pnpABCDE hydroquinone pathway, a PcspA-T4 Holin/Lysozyme cold switch), a docking/MD-guided S120T sensor variant with a measured ~29% signal gain, soil-extract testing, and three hardware generations on both detection and remediation sides (Hardware page). That is a genuinely large body of work for a high school team and it is told as one story. It falls short of GreatBay level because the modules were never integrated into one working strain or device, and the field-facing claims (phone fluorescence reading, pocket-sized Gen 3) rest on an unvalidated algorithm and on another team's unfinished cold-induction work.
justification.a2: Measured, not merely claimed: dose-response over 0-10 mg/L with a pNP-free strain control, medium blank subtraction and n=3 (Results 1.2); a log-linear standard curve Y = 3.674X + 1.208 (1.7); graded responses to soil extracts at 10/50/100/500 ug/kg (1.8); HPLC time-course degradation at five initial concentrations with an empty-pSB1A3 BL21 control to exclude adsorption and abiotic loss, giving 87-95% removal at 10-500 ug/L and a documented failure at 1000 ug/L (54%); PcspA GFP/OD600 across five temperatures and a lysis strain whose OD600 falls to ~0.11 at 16 C while growing at 37 C. Held back from 5 by no specificity, LOD/LOQ or recovery data (the team says so itself), lysis supported by OD600 alone with no viable-count control, no enzyme-expression check for the five pnp genes, and soil that was certified blank reference material rather than field soil.
justification.a3: The use case is sharply bounded by stakeholder input: Description and Human Practices state the tool is preliminary screening and never replaces HPLC/LC-MS confirmation, with costs given (~Y400 fixed, ~Y1 per test) and a five-direction implementation roadmap that names what is still unvalidated. The Zhejiang Institute of Geological Survey exchange narrowed the target users from residents to pollution-clue sites and professionals, and the law-firm consultation produced an explicit no-open-release position. It is not a 5 because nothing was tested on a real contaminated sample or site: all soil was spiked certified blank material, and the spraying demonstrations deliberately used LB powder rather than cells, so real-world performance is still argued rather than shown.
justification.a4: The Engineering page runs five labelled cycles and at least two change the design on evidence. Cycle A2 is the strongest: docking identified S68/S120/H124, 10-ns MD across four mutants selected S120T, the mutant was built and then beat the wild type across 0.001-10 mg/L (~29% at 10 mg/L) - a model used to pick a build and then checked against measurement. The degradation module's dual-operon split (pnpAB and pnpCDE, each J23100-B0034...T0015) is a stated design response to transcription attenuation, and hardware Remediation Gen 2 reports an honest build failure (full payload exceeded the DIY airframe) that killed the DIY-airframe route in favour of a consumer-drone retrofit. Short of 5: no success criteria were quantified in advance, the kinetics were not fitted to a model, and the central hardware claim - phone-camera fluorescence as a substitute for a plate reader - has no calibration against the reference instrument, which p.20 makes the test of working hardware.
justification.a5: The Human Practices page documents seventeen engagements with named institutions (Beijing Beikong sewage treatment centre, Zhejiang Institute of Geological Survey, Prof. Shen Xiantao at HUST Tongji, Beijing Water Science and Technology Institute, Beijing Chaoyang Hospital occupational diseases, Zhangzhou Emergency Medical Center, Jiangsu Environmental Protection Group and Suzhou Yisibei, Lvhaineng, Wanshang Tianqin Law Firm, HSBC) plus a 592-response survey, and closes with a summary table pairing each exchange to a concrete change. Several changes are real and checkable: paper records to QR/GPS digital records after Beikong, the scope cut from emergency use to planned screening after Zhangzhou, the cold-inducible containment module after the agricultural-base visit, the refusal to release live cells after the legal consultation, and a result interface that forbids a green 'safe' reading without validated thresholds. This is reflective, responsible and responsive in the p.21-23 sense, near the GreatBay standard; I withhold the final half point because a few links are looser than claimed (specificity feedback is credited with motivating PobR-MUT, which raises output, not selectivity).
justification.a6: The notebook is the team's best attribution evidence: every dated block in all three systems lists the members who did it, and outside help is declared (Beyotime competent cells, commercial gene synthesis, Tsingke Sanger sequencing, certified blank soil from Tanmo). Against that, the Attributions page is linked in the footer of every page but returns 404, so the form the handbook tells me to read (p.25-26) is simply absent, and the Team page is aspirational bios ('I will take my tasks seriously') rather than roles. HPLC quantification, AutoDock/MD runs and the plate-reader work are nowhere credited to a host lab or instructor, so I cannot tell who operated them. No accusation is implied; the missing page and unstated instrument support are what hold this to 3.
justification.a7: Nine new parts were registered - PobR (BBa_26Z6M53T), PpobA (BBa_2676Z2RC), pnpA/B/C/E/D (BBa_2655T92N, BBa_26LCCKVY, BBa_26O6RF9K, BBa_26LCJT59, BBa_26IP85GF), the composite sensor BBa_26BFFCJG and the composite degradation module BBa_26URBFN2 - plus new characterization added to the existing BBa_K5083099. Everything is built from standard elements (J23100, B0034, T0015/B0015, J0034, pSB1A3), codon-optimized with EcoRI/XbaI/SpeI/PstI sites removed for RFC#10 compatibility, and the Parts page sets out how the sensor, pathway and containment parts can be recombined. This is a well-designed reusable collection rather than a one-off construct; it is not a 5 only because the component parts' individual characterization is light next to the composites.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is detailed - the Parts page gives a table plus a rationale for each part, Results gives construction architecture, verification sizes (534 bp PobR, 134 bp PpobA, GFP 717 bp, Holin 657 bp, Lysozyme 492 bp) and functional data, and the Notebook attaches per-system lab notebook PDFs hosted on the wiki. The handbook scores parts on the Registry, not the wiki, and parts.igem.org returned 403 to me throughout, so the depth of the ten Registry entries is unverified from here; I score what I can see and flag the gap rather than credit or penalise it. Documentation is also uneven across the site: the Model, Measurement and Software pages are untouched iGEM template boilerplate even though the docking/MD work would have filled the Model page.
justification.w1: The home page states the aim, the chassis (E. coli BL21), the three modules and the headline numbers (~29% higher normalized fluorescence with PobR-MUT, ~95% removal at 24 h) in a scrolling story that a non-specialist can follow, and the Description page then lays out problem, methods comparison, each module and the intended users in order. A 28-term glossary is linked from every page and is unusually honest (it notes that an OD600 drop alone does not establish lysis). I can state the project's goal and success criterion after the first two pages, which is the Lambert_GA test; a half point off for a home page that leads with mood before substance.
justification.w2: The Results page gives objective, methods, results and conclusion for each experiment, with replicate counts, normalization formulas, controls and numeric values, and figures are referenced throughout (35 images on that page). The Notebook's dated tables and downloadable PDFs back it up. Two things keep it off 4.5: the Contribution page claims the team 'integrated standardized modules to build an engineered strain that simultaneously senses and degrades pNP' with no supporting experiment anywhere on the wiki, and the hardware's central reading claim has no measurement behind it, so parts of the site assert more than the evidence pages show.
justification.w3: Navigation is good - a persistent menu grouped by Project/Wet Lab/Human Practices/Team, a per-page contents list, page-overview jump cards, previous/next links and a site search. Two concrete defects: the Attributions link in the footer of every page 404s, and the Model, Measurement and Software pages are empty iGEM boilerplate, so a judge following the standard page list lands on three dead ends. The 24,000-word Human Practices page is also heavy going, though its summary table rescues it.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this: construct architectures are written out element by element, the extraction protocol is given (1 g soil, 10 mL 0.1 M EDTA, 30 min, 8000 rpm), the Notebook covers June 9 to August 31 with daily entries and per-system PDFs on iGEM servers, and the Contribution page states what is reusable and how. Reproduction would stall on the missing Attributions page, the absent protocols page, and hardware that is described in prose and video rather than with build files or a parts list with dimensions.
justification.w5: The Description page carries 23 numbered references with DOIs and uses them in text; spot-checked entries resolve to real work that says what is claimed (Zhang et al. 2009 J Bacteriol on PnpA/PnpB from Pseudomonas sp. WBC-3; Ma et al. 2023 Chemosphere on a biosensor for pNP in agricultural soil), and the borrowed SEM image of BL21 is credited to its source. Prior iGEM work is credited where used (GEC-Guangzhou 2025 hardware, RDFZ-China collaboration). The Hardware and Human Practices pages carry far fewer citations than their claims warrant, and several captions are still placeholders reading 'Fig. x'.

J2.one_line: A large, genuinely measured three-module project (sensor with a model-guided mutant, HPLC-verified degradation with an empty-vector control, cold-triggered lysis) wrapped in outstanding human practices, let down by a 404 attributions page, three boilerplate standard pages and hardware whose key reading step was never calibrated.
strengths: Model-to-bench cycle that closes: AutoDock Vina docking plus 10-ns MD over four candidate mutants picked S120T, the mutant was built and then measurably outperformed the wild type across 0.001-10 mg/L (~29% at 10 mg/L) - Results 1.3-1.6, Engineering Cycle A2.

Degradation data with a proper negative control: BL21 carrying empty pSB1A3 was run alongside the pathway strain and residual pNP quantified by HPLC at five initial concentrations, giving 87-95% removal at 10-500 ug/L and an openly reported drop to 54% at 1000 ug/L (Results, System 2).

Human Practices that changed the project and can be audited: seventeen named engagements summarised in a table pairing each one to a design change - digital QR/GPS records after Beijing Beikong, scope cut to planned screening after Zhangzhou Emergency Medical Center, the PcspA containment module after the agricultural-base visit, no open release after the Wanshang Tianqin legal consultation.

A reusable, standards-compliant parts collection: nine new parts plus new characterization of BBa_K5083099, all codon-optimized with RFC#10 illegal sites removed and built from J23100/B0034/T0015 in pSB1A3, with a Parts page explaining how future teams can recombine them.

Honest reporting of limits and failures: the team states that specificity, LOD/LOQ and recovery are still missing, that the soil was certified blank reference material rather than field soil, that the DIY drone could not lift its own payload, and that an OD600 drop does not by itself prove lysis.
Per-task attribution inside the Notebook, where every dated experiment block names the members who performed it, and purchased reagents, synthesis and Sanger sequencing are declared.
weaknesses: The Attributions page is linked in the footer of every page but returns 404, so the attribution form the handbook asks judges to read does not exist; the Team page is aspirational bios rather than roles.
Model, Measurement and Software are untouched iGEM template pages - the docking and MD work that would have filled the Model page sits only inside Results.

The hardware's central claim, a phone camera and colour algorithm replacing a plate reader ('a microplate reader in your pocket'), has no calibration against the reference instrument and no reported agreement, units or error; the insulated box is described as 'approximately 30-37 C' with temperature monitoring admitted as future work.
The Contribution page states the team built an engineered strain that simultaneously senses and degrades pNP; no construction or data for such a strain appears anywhere on the wiki.

No specificity testing despite Prof. Shen's explicit warning about nitrophenol isomers and heavy metals, and no LOD/LOQ or recovery in a soil matrix, so the screening tool's analytical performance is undefined.
Detection Gen 3 (the pocket-sized, box-free form) rests on RDFZ-China's cold-induction work that the page says is still in progress, so the final hardware generation is a plan rather than a build.

No expression evidence for the five degradation enzymes (no SDS-PAGE or activity assay) and no intermediate or product measurement, so removal of pNP is shown but the proposed hydroquinone route is not.
Placeholder captions ('Fig. x') remain on the Hardware page, and Hardware and Human Practices are thinly cited next to the Description page.
red_flags: Attributions page 404 (https://2026.igem.wiki/squirrel-beijing/attributions) while linked from every page footer - the handbook's attribution form is therefore unavailable; a6 scored on the Notebook's per-task credits instead.
Contribution page claims an integrated sensing-and-degrading strain was built, with no experimental evidence on the wiki - an overclaim, not an integrity matter, but it should be put to the team.

Registry part pages (e.g. BBa_26BFFCJG, BBa_26URBFN2, BBa_K5083099) returned HTTP 403 to me on every attempt, so Registry documentation depth could not be verified; a8 reflects wiki-visible documentation with this caveat, not a judgement that the entries are thin.

HPLC quantification, AutoDock Vina/MD simulations and plate-reader measurements are reported without naming the facility or supervising lab; combined with the missing attributions page, who executed these steps is unclear. Raised as a question only, no accusation intended.

Drone-based spraying of engineered bacteria appears as a long-term concept; the team states demonstrations used LB powder and no live cells, and the legal consultation led them to rule out open release - no safety referral warranted, but the panel should confirm this boundary in Q&A.

calibrated.changed: w3 4.0->3.5: a 404 attributions page plus three untouched boilerplate standard pages and a 24,000-word HP page is the same defect profile I scored 3.5 for basis-china and bist-china after this pass.

justification.a1: PNPeeker carries three biological modules plus hardware through to data in one season: a PobR-PpobA-RFP whole-cell pNP sensor, a structure-guided S120T variant that raised output ~29%, a five-gene hydroquinone degradation pathway with HPLC kinetics, and a PcspA-driven cold lysis switch (results.txt, engineering.txt). Three generations each of detection and remediation hardware, costed at ~¥400 fixed and ~¥1 per test, sit on top of that (hardware.txt). It climbs logically (Cycles A1-A3, B1, C1-C2) rather than piling up modules, although specificity, LOD and any field soil remain untested.
justification.a2: The core sensing claim is measured, not asserted: dose-response over 0.001-10 mg/L with a pNP-free strain control and medium blank, n=3 and SD, giving 12.8 and 15.4 A.U. at 1 and 10 mg/L, and a controlled WT-vs-MUT comparison with every circuit element held constant (results.txt 1.2, 1.6). Degradation used an empty-vector BL21-Control and time-course HPLC across five loads, 92/95/94/87/54% removal at 10-1000 ug/L (results.txt System 2). Two gaps hold this below 4.5: the lysis circuit has no lysis-gene-free control strain at the same temperatures (the team says so itself in Cycle C2 Learn), and no specificity test against other nitrophenols or phenols exists even though public health advisers raised isomer interference (human-practices.txt Stage 2.3).
justification.a3: The need is real and externally confirmed, not asserted: EPA priority pollutant status plus exchanges with the Beijing Beikong Sewage Treatment Center, the Zhejiang Institute of Geological Survey ecological restoration division and the Beijing Water Science and Technology Institute, which together pushed the team to target plots with existing pollution clues rather than every household (human-practices.txt Stages 1.3, 2.2, 3.1). Costs are worked out (~¥400 kit, ~¥1 per test versus ~¥20,000-30,000 for a plate reader, hardware.txt) and the scope limit "screening is not confirmation" is stated repeatedly. It stops short of 5 because every soil test used a sterilised certified blank soil spiked in the lab (results.txt Main Results) and all field demonstrations deliberately used no live cells.
justification.a4: Six documented DBTL cycles each hand something concrete to the next: the flat 0.001-0.01 mg/L response in Cycle A1 motivated PobR engineering in A2; docking plus 10 ns MD picked S120T on RMSD grounds and the built mutant then measured ~11.2 versus 7.5 A.U. at 0.1 mg/L (engineering.txt A2). Characterising PcspA with GFP before attaching the lysis genes, precisely so promoter activity and cytotoxicity would not be confounded, is a genuinely good engineering decision (Cycle C1). On hardware, the DIY drone exceeded the frame payload and the route was abandoned for a retrofit on a consumer platform (hardware.txt Remediation Gen 2-3). The summary table even names the next measurements (LOD/LOQ, CFU counts, escape rate), though success criteria were mostly qualitative rather than set in advance.
justification.a5: The summary table on human-practices.txt traces eighteen engagements from stakeholder to feedback to a named change, and several changes are real design moves, not paperwork: the Liantuo agricultural base's worry about bacteria surviving in open farmland led to building and testing the PcspA-T4 Holin/Lysozyme module; equipment firms killed the drone-release route; the Wanshang Tianqin law firm consultation produced the detection-versus-transformation split; and Beijing Luhaineng's point that colour is misread removed any green "safe" status from the result interface. Critical and commercial voices (HSBC on willingness to pay) were sought, not only friendly ones. Two reservations: a 592-response public questionnaire is reported with percentages but no word on consent, anonymity or ethical oversight, and attributing the S120T engineering to a public health exchange overlaps with the team's own Cycle A1 Learn, so that link reads looser than the others.
justification.a6: The notebook is the strength here: dated task tables with a "Completed by" column naming the students on each step (for example Mijia Xia, Zhihan Guo and Tianqing Shen on the PobR and PpobA amplifications; Nuoqian Zhang, Michael Zheng and Alexander Yang on cloning and BL21 transformation), plus disclosed suppliers for synthesis and sequencing (Tsingke), competent cells (Beyotime) and the soil reference material. Against that, the Attributions page the footer links to returns 404 on the live wiki, so no instructor, advisor or host laboratory is named anywhere, and the Team page gives bios largely written in the future tense ("I will take my tasks seriously") rather than what each person did. For roughly thirty students drawn from many different schools, running HPLC, MD simulations and a summer bench programme, the wiki never explains whose laboratory this was; that is a question for the session, not an accusation, and it holds a6 at 3.
justification.a7: The project is built from standard parts throughout: J23100, B0034, J0034, T0015 and B0015 in pSB1A3, with illegal EcoRI/XbaI/SpeI/PstI sites removed for RFC#10 compatibility (engineering.txt Cycle B1). The team contributes seven basic and two composite parts, including the PobR-based reporter circuit and the dual-operon pnpABCDE module, and adds characterisation to the existing BBa_K5083099 (parts.txt, contribution.txt). The dual-operon split to avoid attenuation in a five-gene pathway is a deliberate standard-parts design choice rather than a copy of a published construct.
justification.a8: The wiki documentation is genuinely good (parts.txt lists all ten parts with IDs, types and reuse suggestions; results.txt carries the matching data), but the Parts page contains no hyperlink to a single Registry entry, no sequences and no per-part characterisation, so a judge must search the Registry by hand. I tried to open BBa_26BFFCJG, BBa_26URBFN2, BBa_26Z6M53T and BBa_K5083099 on parts.igem.org and was blocked (HTTP 403), so I could not verify that the Registry entries carry the data the wiki claims. On the handbook rule that part data living only on the wiki does not meet the parts requirement, this sits at 3.5 pending a session check of the Registry pages.
justification.w1: The home page tells the problem, the gap in GC-MS access, the three modules and the headline numbers (29% higher normalised fluorescence, ~95% removal at 24 h) in one scrolling story, then signposts six next pages with one-line reasons to visit each (home.txt). The Description opens with four orientation cards (Context, Need, Design, Application) before any detail, and a 28-term glossary is reachable from every page. A reader who knows nothing about nitrophenols understands the goal within a minute; the only cost is a heavy animated intro that must load before the text appears.
justification.w2: Most claims carry a figure with controls, replicates and units, and the team is unusually careful about what its data do not show: docking and MD results are labelled as in-silico throughout, Cycle B1 Learn notes that HPLC shows only parent pNP loss and that the intermediates still need targeted analysis, and the glossary itself warns that a drop in OD600 does not establish lysis. Two things pull this down from 4.5. The Contribution page states that "we integrated standardized modules to build an engineered strain that simultaneously senses and degrades pNP" (contribution.txt, An Integrated Strain for Simultaneous Sensing and Degradation), and no such strain appears anywhere in results.txt; and Figure 10 on description.txt reuses the caption of Figure 9 ("Predicted binding mode of PobR with pNP") where a degradation-pathway caption belongs.
justification.w3: Navigation is strong: a grouped side menu, per-page contents, orientation cards, previous/next links, a working site search and a shared glossary. Two faults cost it. The footer link to Attributions 404s on the live site, which is exactly the page a judge is told to look for. And the Model, Measurement, Software and Inclusivity pages are still unedited iGEM boilerplate ("Visit the Special Awards page for more information", lists of 2025 inspiration teams), so the docking and MD work that genuinely is modelling is nowhere near the Model page.
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this wiki: the notebook gives dated task-by-task records for all three systems with downloadable lab-notebook PDFs, the Results methods sections give concrete conditions (1 g soil to 10 mL of 0.1 M EDTA, 30 min shaking, 8000 rpm for 10 min; induction at 37 C for 8 h), hardware gives a full bill of materials with prices and sources, and the Contribution page spells out what to reuse. What is missing is raw data files, the phone app's source (the Software page is untouched boilerplate although the wiki says the app was team-written), and the attribution record that would tell a future team who to ask.
justification.w5: The Description carries 23 properly formatted references and I verified four DOIs resolve and match the claims made (Ma et al., Chemosphere 2023, 137306 for whole-cell pNP sensing in agricultural soil; Jha et al., NAR 2016 for the engineered transcription-factor sensor; Xu et al., AMB Express 2021; Tang et al., Nat Chem Biol 2021). Prior work by other teams is credited by name, including the GEC-Guangzhou 2025 hardware the sampling tube builds on and the RDFZ-China collaboration, and the external SEM image of BL21 carries its source URL. The deduction is coverage: the 24,000-word Human Practices page, the Hardware page and the Contribution page carry no reference list at all, so several factual statements there stand uncited.

J3.one_line: A disciplined three-module pNP project with real controlled data, six genuine DBTL cycles and human practices that visibly changed the design, let down by a missing Attributions page, untested specificity and Registry entries I could not verify.
strengths: Measured, controlled core data: dose-response with n=3 and a pNP-free control, a WT-versus-S120T comparison with all other circuit elements held constant, and HPLC degradation kinetics against an empty-vector BL21-Control (results.txt)
Computation actually drove a build: docking plus 10 ns MD selected S120T, the mutant was made and measured, and the ~29% output gain at 10 mg/L closes the loop (engineering.txt Cycle A2)
Characterising PcspA with GFP before attaching the lysis genes, to separate promoter activity from cytotoxicity, is mature experimental reasoning for a high school team (Cycle C1)

Human practices with traceable consequences: the farmland visit produced the biocontainment module, equipment firms killed the drone-release route, and the public communication consultancy removed any green 'safe' reading from the result interface (human-practices.txt summary table)
Honest about limits throughout: OD600 cannot prove lysis, HPLC shows only parent compound loss, the soil was a certified blank spiked in the lab, and no live cells were ever taken into the field
Hardware iterated through a documented failure (the DIY drone exceeded the frame payload) to a cheaper retrofit, with a full costed bill of materials (hardware.txt)
weaknesses: The Attributions page returns 404 although the footer links to it, so no instructor, advisor or host laboratory is named anywhere on the wiki; the Team page bios are mostly written in the future tense

No specificity testing against other nitrophenols or phenols, and no LOD/LOQ or recovery, even though advisers raised isomer and matrix interference; the sensor claim rests on spiked certified blank soil
The cold-lysis experiment has no lysis-gene-free control strain at the same temperatures, so growth slowdown cannot be separated from lysis (the team acknowledges this)
The Contribution page claims a strain that simultaneously senses and degrades pNP; no data for such a strain appears on any results page
Model, Measurement, Software and Inclusivity pages are unedited iGEM boilerplate, and the Parts page gives no Registry hyperlinks, sequences or per-part characterisation
The 592-response public questionnaire is reported without any mention of consent, anonymity or ethical oversight
red_flags: Attributions page 404 on the live wiki (https://2026.igem.wiki/squirrel-beijing/attributions) while the footer links to it; no external help, instructor or host lab named - a question for the session, not an accusation
Contribution page asserts an integrated sense-and-degrade strain was built, with no supporting data anywhere on the wiki
Could not verify Registry entries: parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403 for BBa_26BFFCJG, BBa_26URBFN2, BBa_26Z6M53T and BBa_K5083099 from this environment, so a8 is scored on wiki documentation only
Caption copy-paste error: description.txt Figure 10 repeats the Figure 9 caption about PobR-pNP binding where a degradation-pathway caption belongs
One team bio describes a different project (acetaminophen residues in water) than the rest of the wiki, suggesting reused template text on the Team page
Public questionnaire (592 respondents) reported with no consent or ethics statement

calibrated.changed: none.

one_line.en: A three-module project with model-guided mutant selection, HPLC-verified degradation against an empty-vector control and strong Human Practices, let down by a 404 attributions page and boilerplate standard pages.
one_line.zh: 三模組專案，模型導向的突變體選擇、以空載體對照驗證的 HPLC 降解數據與紮實的人文實踐，但歸屬頁 404、多個標準頁仍是範本文字。

strengths: A closed computation-to-bench loop: docking plus simulation selected a mutant that then measurably outperformed wild type under identical conditions
Degradation quantified by HPLC against empty-vector and abiotic controls across five initial concentrations
Human Practices with named institutions at every stage and a containment module that exists because a field visit raised persistence
Complete protocols, a dated notebook with per-task student credits, and honest limitation statements
weaknesses: No attributions page and no statement of instructor, host-lab or mentor roles
The cold-inducible lysis claim rests on optical density with no lysis-gene-free control, no colony counts and no escape rate
No specificity, detection limit or recovery testing, so analytical performance is undefined
Model, Measurement, Software and Inclusivity pages are unedited template text

Caption copy-paste error on a key pathway figure, and one team bio describes a different project

screen.project_title: SalvGen / Cardivit: salvianic acid A production in E. coli with a dual kill switch
screen.what_they_built: A three-generation metabolically engineered E. coli BL21 producing salvianic acid A (SAA, the Danshen cardiovascular compound) from endogenous 4HPP, plus two independent containment circuits: an arabinose-inducible pBAD-MazF and an oxygen-responsive phyB-MazE/MazF.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) / DH5-alpha, pSB1A3 RFC10. Nine basic and five composite parts, including BlFldH (BBa_263ORDZN), HpaB (BBa_265UMLHE), HpaC (BBa_262URU68), aroG-fbr (BBa_26FOGVIZ), tyrA-fbr (BBa_267UMI3X), laaD (BBa_26K7FZE8), phyB (BBa_26W5JO2P), SAA1/2/3 composites (BBa_26XG50YG, BBa_26JK2UH1, BBa_26UW0W4F) and re-characterized pBAD (BBa_I0500).
screen.best_evidence: /results Part 1: HPLC against an SAA standard curve, three biological replicates - WT BL21 1.64 +/- 0.61 mg/L, BL21/SAA1 155.38 +/- 11.57 mg/L, BL21/SAA2 (aroG-fbr + tyrA-fbr) 1066.87 +/- 54.27 mg/L, BL21/SAA3 (HpaB E63S/E216G/E294I) 1366.87 +/- 57.09 mg/L at 24 h and 3503.33 +/- 201.08 mg/L at 40 h, with parallel glucose depletion (19.04 to 0.96 g/L) and the DOPA by-product tracked to 125.56 mg/L. /contribution: pBAD-mRFP 4.68x/7.38x/8.55x induction at 0.02/0.05/0.2% arabinose, and pBAD-MazF cutting OD600 by 53.6% and 89.2%.
screen.hp_integration: Yes: a RARE (Reason-Approach-Response-Evolution) framework documents public surveys, patients, clinicians, Danshen industry and company visits feeding the choice of SAA, the four rounds of production optimisation, the biosafety design and the product form; the wiki claims specific revisions at each step, which a full read should verify rather than take on trust.
screen.reason: The strongest experimental package in this batch: six DBTL cycles, replicated HPLC titres rising ~22-fold across three rationally justified strain generations to 3.5 g/L, by-product and carbon-source tracking that exposes the remaining flux problem, docking/MD/CAVER used to explain the enzyme mutant, and two containment circuits characterized with real numbers including a re-characterization contribution to an existing Registry part. Two things a full read must probe: the attributions page is empty and all genes were vendor-synthesised, so how much was done by a host university lab is unknown (aspect 6), and gram-per-litre shake-flask titres from a high-school team warrant checking the raw chromatograms.
screen.field_notes: Squirrel-Guangzhou (Biomanufacturing village) built Cardivit/SalvGen, an E. coli BL21 chassis producing salvianic acid A, the cardiovascular compound from Danshen (Salvia miltiorrhiza). Three strain generations were built on pSB1A3 under lacI-placUV5 (chosen over T7 to avoid inclusion bodies): SAA1 (BlFldH + HpaB + HpaC) gave 155.38 +/- 11.57 mg/L against 1.64 mg/L for wild type; SAA2 added feedback-resistant aroG and tyrA for 1066.87 +/- 54.27 mg/L; SAA3 swapped in HpaB(E63S/E216G/E294I) for 1366.87 +/- 57.09 mg/L at 24 h and 3503.33 +/- 201.08 mg/L at 40 h, quantified by Agilent 1260 HPLC against an SAA standard curve with glucose (GOD-POD) and the DOPA by-product (to 125.56 mg/L) tracked in parallel; a LaaD-based SAA4 is design-stage only. AutoDock Vina docking on EcHpaB 6QYI with MD and CAVER tunnel analysis rationalises the mutant. Biosafety has two circuits: pBAD-mRFP characterized at 4.68x/7.38x/8.55x induction across 0.02-0.2% arabinose and pBAD-MazF reducing OD600 by 53.6% and 89.2% (viable counts still missing), plus an oxygen-responsive phyB-MazE/MazF for gut-versus-environment containment.
