Nine basic and five composite parts, RFC10-compatible, with a Bronze re-characterization of pBAD (BBa_I0500). The /model and /hardware pages are left as iGEM template text and the attributions page is empty.

justification.a1: Results shows four successive engineered strains with measured SAA titers (WT 1.64 mg/L; SAA1 155.38 ± 11.57; SAA2 1066.87 ± 54.27; SAA3 1366.87 ± 57.09 mg/L), a 40 h fermentation time course with glucose and DOPA by-product tracking, plus two separately characterised containment circuits (pBAD-MazF, phyB-MazE/MazF). That is several linked results of increasing difficulty, close to the GreatBay/TAS pattern. It falls short of a 5 because the probiotic chassis EcN, which the whole Cardivit story rests on, was never actually built or tested (Results, SAA4 section: 'In future work, we will transfer the optimized pathway into EcN'), and no cardioprotective activity of the product was shown.
justification.a2: The core function is demonstrated against controls with replicates: SAA1 vs wild-type BL21 (94.9-fold), HPLC quantified against a calibration curve the notebook shows them having to redo for linearity, three biological replicates per group with SD stated (Results and Experiments). The safety systems are tested too: pBAD-mRFP gives a time- and dose-dependent normalised fluorescence response with matched growth curves showing 0-0.2% arabinose does not itself affect growth, and pBAD-MazF shows 53.6% and 89.2% lower final OD600 versus an uninduced control; phyB-MazE/MazF grows anaerobically but is restricted aerobically, with a colony-formation figure. Held back from 5 because the kill switches are scored as growth inhibition rather than CFU killing, no statistical tests are reported, and everything is in BL21(DE3) rather than the intended EcN.
justification.a3: The problem framing (CVD burden, Danshen supply chain) is well sourced and the Entrepreneurship page works through MVP, market, SWOT and risk, but nothing links the team's own data to a health outcome: no dose calculation for gut delivery, no bioactivity assay, no real-world-like test comparable to TAS Taipei's wastewater setup. Impact numbers are literature-derived (WHO, GBD) rather than from their measurements. Credible use case with stakeholder input, but the chain from 1.4 g/L in a shake flask to cardiovascular protection is asserted, not quantified.
justification.a4: Engineering lays out six DBTL cycles and at least three are genuinely data-driven: the SAA1 titer and precursor reasoning led to aroG^fbr/tyrA^fbr (SAA2), the plateau led to the HpaB triple mutant (SAA3), and the continued DOPA accumulation measured in the SAA3 time course motivated the LaaD design (SAA4). Standard parts (pSB1A3, B0034, B0015, J23100) and modular generations are used throughout. Cycle 4 is design-only with no test, measures of success are not stated before testing, and the computational docking/MD/CAVER work explains a mutant taken from Tian et al. 2025 rather than generating a tested redesign of their own, so this sits at 4 rather than 5.
justification.a5: Human Practices runs 17 RARE cycles with a real range of interlocutors (family interviews, a 177-respondent survey with the analysis PDF attached, a TCM hospital clinician, Qingping herb market, a Danshen grower, Daosheng Biotechnology, the Shenzhen synthetic biology facility, patients, packaging and commercial advisers), and several visibly changed the project. The Daosheng conversation about precursor bottlenecks redirected the second generation to 4HPP supply, and community safety concerns plus a comparison with BSDFZ-China 2025 led them to drop a temperature-triggered switch for the oxygen-responsive phyB design (cycles 13-14). This is dialogue feeding design, not outreach, and it is tied to specific pages of the wet lab story.
justification.a6: This is the weakest part of the dossier. The /attributions standard page returns 404, and I found no statement anywhere of which laboratory hosted the work, who the advisors or PI were, or who ran the HPLC, plate reader and 100 ns GROMACS simulation. The Team page gives 20+ student bios with broad roles, the notebook is dated and student-voiced, the Contribution page has a named wet lab leader's account of task allocation, and gene synthesis and sequencing are declared as outsourced, so there is real evidence students did bench work; but with no attributions page I cannot tell how much of the instrumentation and computation was mentor- or facility-run, which the handbook asks me to judge (p.25-26). I am scoring the documentation gap, not alleging anything.
justification.a7: The project is squarely synthetic biology on standard components: pSB1A3 backbone, BBa_B0034 RBS, BBa_B0015 terminators, J23100, the reused pBAD (BBa_I0500) and placUV5 (BBa_K3040120), and nine new basic plus five composite parts covering the SAA pathway and both toxin-antitoxin circuits (Parts page table). Two engineered devices were actually built and tested, and existing parts are reused alongside new ones, which is the TAS pattern. Short of 5 only because I could not open the Registry entries themselves (parts.igem.org returned 403 throughout this session) to confirm the sequences and annotation behind the IDs.
justification.a8: The wiki side is good: the Parts page tabulates every BBa ID with length, type, award mark and function, and Results/Experiments give media, induction, HPLC and plate-reader conditions. But the handbook judges parts on the Registry alone and I could not reach it, and several standard pages are missing or empty: /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design all 404, while Model, Measurement, Hardware, Software, Education, Inclusivity and Sustainability are still the unedited iGEM template text with 'Inspirations' lists. Notably the team's own modelling (docking, 100 ns MD, CAVER) sits on Results while the Model page is boilerplate, which is exactly the kind of thing a judge should not have to hunt for.
justification.w1: The homepage runs a clear eight-panel scroll from CVD burden to Danshen to SAA to the engineered pathway and the dual kill switch, with a signposted set of entry points into the project. A reader knows the problem and the approach within a screen or two. It loses half a point because the outcome is never stated up front: nothing on the homepage says they reached ~1.4 g/L SAA or that the production work was done in BL21 rather than the EcN the page foregrounds.
justification.w2: Most key claims on Results and Engineering carry a figure, a control and a number with SD from three biological replicates, and the methods (MR medium, 0.1 mM IPTG, 24 h shake flask, HPLC conditions, Varioskan at 584/610 nm, GOD-POD glucose kit) are given in enough detail to follow. Gel figures are captioned per fragment. It is not a 5 because the crawl text does not let me confirm ladder size marks or lane labels inside the gel images, no statistical comparison is reported, and the language occasionally outruns the assay, for example describing OD reduction as 'self-elimination'.
justification.w3: Navigation is sensible (Project / Wet Lab / Human Practices / Entrepreneurship / Team), each page has a contents rail, an 'at a glance' set of jump links, a working search and a 28-term glossary, which genuinely helps a non-specialist. The problem is the standard URLs: /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design are 404, and seven award pages are untouched template text, so a judge following the ballot lands on empty or missing pages. That is the friction the handbook explicitly warns about.
justification.w4: The Notebook is dated June-August 2026 with objectives, steps and results per entry, including the failures a future team needs (0/12 positive clones on the first SAA1 colony PCR, a first HPLC calibration with poor linearity that had to be redone), and Notebook PDFs are downloadable from the wiki. Experiments gives reusable methods and Contribution adds a transformation-troubleshooting write-up and a reusable pBAD characterisation. Short of 5 because there is no protocols page and no raw data tables or chromatograms, so the numbers could be repeated in spirit but not re-derived.
justification.w5: Inline author-year citations are used throughout Description, Results and Safety, each page carries a reference list with full journal citations that look resolvable, figure sources are credited (the Salvia photographs are attributed to named photographers), and prior iGEM work is properly acknowledged: BUCT 2021 for the MazE/MazF design, BSDFZ-China 2025 for the dual-control idea, RDFZ-CHINA 2022 and SZU-China 2023 in the safety comparison. Small gaps only: a few schematic figures have no stated source and the BUCT reference is a bare 2021 wiki URL with tracking parameters.

J1.one_line: A genuinely strong high school wet-lab project: four generations of metabolic engineering taking SAA from 1.6 to ~1370 mg/L with controls and triplicates, plus two tested containment circuits, let down by a missing attributions page, several 404 standard pages, and the fact that the probiotic chassis the whole story rests on was never built.
strengths: Stepwise production data with a real negative control: WT BL21 1.64 ± 0.61 mg/L vs BL21/SAA1 155.38 ± 11.57 mg/L (94.9-fold), rising to 1066.87 ± 54.27 (SAA2) and 1366.87 ± 57.09 mg/L (SAA3), all HPLC-quantified with three biological replicates and SD (Results, Part 1).

Both safety circuits were actually characterised, not just drawn: pBAD-mRFP gives dose- and time-dependent normalised fluorescence with matched growth curves showing arabinose alone does not perturb growth, pBAD-MazF drops final OD600 by 53.6% and 89.2% versus uninduced, and phyB-MazE/MazF grows anaerobically but is restricted aerobically with a colony-plate figure (Results, Parts 2-3).

Honest reporting of limits and failures: SAA4 is labelled a future strategy with only the LaaD fragment verified, the 0 h SAA baseline of 146 mg/L is explained rather than hidden, DOPA by-product accumulation is reported as evidence of flux loss, and the Notebook records 0/12 positive clones and a failed first HPLC calibration.

Human Practices is tightly coupled to the bench: the Daosheng precursor-bottleneck conversation drove the SAA2 redesign, and community safety concerns plus a comparison with BSDFZ-China 2025 led them to replace a temperature-triggered kill switch with the oxygen-responsive phyB design (HP cycles 9, 13-14).

Clean use of standard components and a coherent part series: pSB1A3, BBa_B0034, BBa_B0015, J23100, reuse of pBAD (BBa_I0500) and placUV5, nine new basic and five composite parts tabulated with function and award mark (Parts).
weaknesses: No attributions anywhere: /attributions is a 404 and no page names the host laboratory, advisors or who operated the HPLC, plate reader and the 100 ns MD run, so I cannot judge how much of the execution was the students' (handbook p.25-26).

The probiotic chassis is unbuilt. Every production and containment experiment is in E. coli BL21(DE3) or DH5-alpha, while the homepage, Description, Safety and Entrepreneurship pages all frame Cardivit as an EcN probiotic; transfer to EcN is deferred to future work.

Standard pages are missing or boilerplate: /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /protocols and /design 404, and Model, Measurement, Hardware, Software, Education, Inclusivity and Sustainability are untouched iGEM template text. The team's own docking/MD/CAVER work sits on Results while the Model page is empty template.

The kill switches are validated as growth inhibition by OD, not as killing: no CFU/mL survival ratios, no escape-frequency estimate, and no test of the switches in the SAA-producing strain, yet the text speaks of 'self-elimination' and 'precise clearance'.

No statistics beyond mean and SD, and the HpaB computational work explains a mutant taken from Tian et al. 2025 rather than predicting and then testing a variant of the team's own, so the dry lab informs rather than drives the design.
Nothing connects the measured titer to the claimed cardiovascular benefit: no dose estimate for gut delivery, no bioactivity assay, and the impact numbers are all from the literature.
red_flags: Attributions page absent (404) - this is a handbook-required standard page and the basis for scoring aspect 6; I score the gap, I do not infer misconduct.

Four further standard URLs (proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols, design) return 404 and seven award pages are unedited iGEM template text, which conflicts with the p.29 expectation that judges are guided from the standard pages.

parts.igem.org returned HTTP 403 for every part I tried (BBa_26UW0W4F, BBa_26W5JO2P, BBa_263ORDZN), so the Registry entries behind the 14 claimed parts could not be verified in this session. This is a limit of my access, not a finding against the team; aspects 7 and 8 are capped accordingly and should be re-checked.

Framing drift between the application claim (EcN probiotic for human use) and the evidence base (BL21(DE3) shake flasks). Clearly flagged by the team in the SAA4 section and the glossary, so this is a scope caveat rather than an integrity concern.

No academic-integrity concerns found: references are specific and conventionally formatted, prior iGEM teams are credited by name and year, figure photographers are named, and modelled results are explicitly labelled as docking/MD/CAVER output.
pages_read: attempted Registry: BBa_26UW0W4F, BBa_26W5JO2P, BBa_263ORDZN (all HTTP 403)

calibrated.changed: a2 4.5 -> 4.0. I held Hangzhou No.14 and HongKong-JSS to 4.5 only where statistics were reported, and I marked Cataverse and HK Joint School down to 4.0 for exactly the gaps present here: no statistical test anywhere, containment scored by OD600 alone with no lysis-gene-free control, and all work in BL21 rather than the EcN the claim rests on. The production data are genuinely well controlled, which keeps it at 4.0 rather than lower.

justification.a1: Large, coherent scope for a high school team: three engineered strains built and measured (SAA1 155.38 +/- 11.57 mg/L, SAA2 1066.87 +/- 54.27, SAA3 1366.87 +/- 57.09 at 24 h; 3503.33 +/- 201.08 mg/L at 40 h, Results Figs 6, 9, 12, 15), a 40 h fermentation time-course with glucose and DOPA by-product, two working safety circuits, docking/MD/CAVER analysis, 17 documented stakeholder cycles and a full entrepreneurship plan. It falls short of GreatBay-level because the chain stops before the chassis that the product actually needs: nothing was ever built or tested in E. coli Nissle 1917, SAA4 is design-only, and the production and containment modules were never combined in one strain.
justification.a2: The main function is demonstrated with quantitative data and a real control: WT BL21 gives 1.64 +/- 0.61 mg/L against 155.38 +/- 11.57 mg/L for SAA1, three biological replicates and two technical HPLC replicates against an external SAA standard curve (Results, SAA 1 section; Experiments, HPLC method). The arabinose switch is well controlled in one respect - pBAD-mRFP shows 0-0.2% arabinose does not itself slow growth, then pBAD-MazF drops OD600 by 53.6% and 89.2% (Results Figs 22, 25). Weaker points: no empty-vector or parent-strain control in either kill-switch experiment, 1% arabinose was never checked for a growth effect on its own, growth inhibition is not killing (the team says so and promises viable counts), and the aerobic/anaerobic comparison (Fig 27) also differs in shaking versus static culture.
justification.a3: The deployment route is argued carefully and is stakeholder-checked: patient interviews on long-term adherence, a packaging consultation that led to the freeze-dried capsule format, a pharmacy and Qingping market survey of the existing Danshen trade, and a Danshen grower who argued that microbial production complements rather than replaces cultivation (Human Practices cycles 06, 07, 12, 15). Safety is taken seriously, with SAA toxicology and warfarin/aspirin interaction literature reviewed honestly as not transferable to oral delivery (Safety page). But nothing was tested in anything resembling the intended setting - no gut-like condition, no EcN, no dose linking titer to a physiological effect - so the impact remains argued rather than demonstrated.
justification.a4: Six labelled cycles, and at least three of them are genuine: the Daosheng conversation about precursor bottlenecks led to aroG-fbr/tyrA-fbr and a 6.87-fold titer gain; the continuing DOPA accumulation measured in the 40 h run (125.56 +/- 8.72 mg/L at 40 h) is the stated reason for the LaaD design in Cycle 4; and pBAD was characterised with mRFP before mazF was put behind it, which is the right order. Standards are respected - RFC10 sites removed, BioBrick adaptors, pSB1A3, BBa_B0034/BBa_B0015, codon optimisation (Experiments). Held back because the docking/MD/CAVER work explains a mutant taken from Tian et al. 2025 after the fact rather than predicting the team's own design, Cycle 4 was never built, and success criteria are essentially titer alone.
justification.a5: The strongest aspect. Seventeen RARE cycles span public, clinical, science, industry, market and legal stakeholders, and the design consequences are traceable, not decorative: Dr Wang Guoliang on the first pathway, Daosheng on precursor supply (SAA2), Dr Zhang Jingyu on enzyme engineering (SAA3), the Shenzhen Synthetic Biology Infrastructure visit on flux (SAA4), patient interviews that turned a production platform into a delivery concept, and BUCT 2021 displacing the team's original temperature-based kill switch with an oxygen-based one (Safety page). Feedback that cut against them is reported - the clinician separating public trust in TCM from clinical evidence, and the Danshen grower rejecting the replacement framing. Short of 5 only because the 177-response survey stays descriptive and a few 'Evolution' steps are really literature decisions.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page at all: /attributions returns 404, as do /design, /implementation, /protocols and /proof-of-concept, and no Attributions link appears in the navigation. I could find no acknowledgement anywhere on the wiki of a host laboratory, instructor, PI or advisor, and no who-did-what breakdown; the Team page carries only self-written bios with broad role labels. The project includes 100 ns GROMACS simulations, CAVER channel analysis, Agilent HPLC quantification and seamless cloning, which a high school team may well have done with support, but the handbook (p.25-26) asks for that to be stated and here nothing is. I am recording this as a question for the team and the panel, not as an allegation.
justification.a7: Synthetic biology is the core of the project, not an accessory. The team registered 9 basic and 5 composite parts (Parts page), built as a deliberate modular series - SAA1 to SAA4 for metabolism, pBAD-MazF and phyB-MazE/MazF for containment - reusing standard parts (BBa_B0034, BBa_B0015, BBa_I0500, BBa_K1096002, BBa_K3040120) and designed for RFC10 compatibility in pSB1A3. They also add real characterisation data to the existing part BBa_I0500 (Contribution page: 4.68/7.38/8.55-fold normalised mRFP induction). I could not open parts.igem.org to check the Registry entries themselves (the Registry served a bot-verification page and I did not attempt to get past it), so this score rests on the wiki's part list and on documented construction.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is genuinely good: media recipes, kit catalogue numbers, HPLC column, mobile phase and wavelength, induction and sampling schedule, a dated day-by-day notebook from 1 June to 31 August including a failed transformation and a rejected calibration curve (R2 = 0.9808), and a parts table giving length and function for every part. Two things pull it down. The handbook judges parts on the Registry, and I could not reach those pages to confirm annotation, host, rationale and characterisation. And several standard pages (Model, Hardware, Measurement, Software, Education, Inclusivity, Sustainability) are still unedited iGEM boilerplate, while Attributions and Protocols are missing entirely.
justification.w1: The home page states the aim in one pass - engineered E. coli producing salvianic acid A for cardiovascular protection, with a dual kill switch - and the Description page carries the reader from the cardiovascular burden through chassis choice to the four production generations and the two containment modules. The 'at a glance' cards at the top of each page and the 28-entry Terminology A-Z are a real service to a non-specialist reader, and the glossary is careful enough to distinguish salvianic acid A from salvianolic acid A. A reader knows the aim and the success measure after two pages.
justification.w2: Claims are backed by numbers nearly everywhere: titers with standard deviations and replicate counts, glucose and DOPA time-courses, normalised fluorescence values, OD600 growth curves, and figures for plasmid maps and verification gels. Limitations are marked rather than hidden - SAA4 is labelled a future strategy, the kill-switch section states that OD600 cannot establish killing and that viable counts are needed, and the 0 h SAA baseline is explained rather than glossed over. Short of 5 because the kill-switch experiments lack vector-only controls, no raw data or numerical tables accompany the figures, and Figure 28 (colony formation) is described without any counts.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean and purposeful: a grouped side menu, per-page contents, a working search, and 'continue the story' links that carry a reader from Description to Engineering to Results to Parts. Against that, Attributions is absent from both the menu and the site, four standard URLs 404, and the award template pages that are still boilerplate are reachable even though unlinked. The home page's slow scroll-story also means the substance begins some way down.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of this. The notebook gives dates, objectives, steps and outcomes including the failures (0/12 positive clones on the first SAA1 colony PCR, the repeated HPLC calibration), the Experiments page gives protocols with supplier catalogue numbers, and the Contribution page passes on transformation troubleshooting and wet-lab coordination lessons. Everything sits on iGEM servers. Missing: a protocols page, raw datasets behind the figures, and any record of who did which part of the work.
justification.w5: Each substantial page closes with a reference list, in-text citation is author-year and used where it matters (Tian et al. 2025 for the pathway and the HpaB mutations, Chen et al. 2019, Yao et al. 2013, Szeliova et al. 2016), prior iGEM work is credited by name and year (BUCT 2021, RDFZ-CHINA 2022, SZU-China 2023), and image credits are given for the Salvia photographs in Description Figure 7. One citation I could not check - a 2026 Nature Medicine GBD paper with volume 32(4) - which I note only as something to confirm, not as a finding.

J2.one_line: A data-rich, genuinely iterative metabolic engineering project with outstanding human practices, held back by the fact that nothing was ever built in the probiotic chassis the product depends on, and by a completely missing attributions page.
strengths: Measured, controlled production data across three successive strains: WT BL21 1.64 +/- 0.61 mg/L vs SAA1 155.38 +/- 11.57, SAA2 1066.87 +/- 54.27, SAA3 1366.87 +/- 57.09 mg/L at 24 h, with three biological and two technical replicates and an external SAA calibration curve (Results Figs 6, 9, 12)

A real learn-to-design link: DOPA measured rising to 125.56 +/- 8.72 mg/L over 40 h is the stated reason for the LaaD/SAA4 strategy, and the Daosheng precursor-bottleneck conversation is the stated reason for aroG-fbr/tyrA-fbr in SAA2

Human practices that genuinely steered the project across 17 documented cycles, including feedback that contradicted the team (the Danshen grower rejecting the replacement framing; BUCT 2021 displacing their original temperature-based kill switch with an oxygen-responsive one)

Promoter characterised before it was trusted: pBAD-mRFP shows arabinose alone does not slow growth, then pBAD-MazF gives 53.6% and 89.2% OD600 reductions (Results Figs 22, 23, 25) - plus added characterisation contributed for existing part BBa_I0500

A modular, standard-compliant part collection (9 basic, 5 composite) in pSB1A3 with RFC10 sites removed and BBa_B0034/BBa_B0015 reused, designed as a reusable SAA1-SAA4 series plus two containment modules
Honest, reproducible record keeping: dated notebook including failures (0/12 positive clones, a rejected calibration at R2 = 0.9808) and methods with supplier catalogue numbers
weaknesses: No Attributions page exists (404), no host laboratory, instructor or advisor is acknowledged anywhere on the wiki, and there is no who-did-what breakdown for work that includes 100 ns MD simulations, CAVER analysis and HPLC quantification

The product chassis was never used: all production work is in BL21(DE3), E. coli Nissle 1917 appears only as an intention, and the SAA pathway and the two kill switches were never combined in a single strain

Kill-switch experiments lack a vector-only or parent-strain control; growth inhibition by OD600 is not killing (the team acknowledges this), 1% arabinose was never tested for an intrinsic growth effect, and the aerobic/anaerobic comparison also differs in shaking versus static culture

The computational work explains a mutant taken from the literature after the fact rather than predicting the team's own design, and Cycle 4 (LaaD) was never built, so the sixth 'cycle' stops at design

Several standard pages (Model, Hardware, Measurement, Software, Education, Inclusivity, Sustainability) remain unedited iGEM boilerplate, and Protocols, Design, Implementation and Proof of Concept all 404
red_flags: No attributions page and no acknowledgement of any mentor, supervising laboratory or institution anywhere on the wiki, despite advanced instrumentation and simulation work. Raise as a question for the team; not an accusation.
Registry part pages could not be opened to verify documentation depth - parts.igem.org returned a bot-verification page and I did not attempt to get past it, so a7/a8 rest on wiki evidence only.
One reference could not be checked and should be spot-checked by the panel: 'GBD 2023 IHD & Dietary Risk Factors Collaborators (2026), Nature Medicine, 32(4), 1454-1478' on the Description page.
The Entrepreneurship page quotes the 40 h titer (3503.33 mg/L) as evidence of feasibility for a product that would run in EcN, a strain in which no production was ever measured.

calibrated.changed: none — a6 2.0 despite no mentor or host lab acknowledged anywhere; after lowering psi-korea to 2.0 this is level with the other no-form, bios-only teams, which I am satisfied is the right floor given I make no accusation about who did the work.

justification.a1: SalvGen (Cardivit) carries one mechanism — a four-step engineered route to salvianic acid A — from literature design through three built and measured strain generations, and adds a second layer in two containment circuits plus a computational enzyme study (Results: Part 1, Part 2, Part 3). The climb is real and quantitative: 155.38 ± 11.57 → 1066.87 ± 54.27 → 1366.87 ± 57.09 mg/L at 24 h, and 3503.33 ± 201.08 mg/L at 40 h for SAA3. It stops short of a 5 because the fourth generation (SAA4/LaaD) exists only as a design with a verified fragment, and the probiotic chassis EcN on which the whole application rests was never used in any experiment (Results, end of Part 1: the pathway will be transferred to EcN in future work).
justification.a2: The core biology demonstrably works and is measured against controls: BL21/SAA1 versus wild-type BL21 (1.64 ± 0.61 mg/L), three biological and two technical replicates, HPLC against an external SAA standard curve (0-800 mg/L), and a 40 h time course of glucose, SAA and the DOPA by-product (Results, Fermentation characteristics of SAA3). The arabinose switch is shown twice: pBAD-mRFP gives a concentration-dependent 4.68/7.38/8.55-fold fluorescence rise with matched growth curves, then pBAD-MazF lowers 24 h OD600 by 53.6% and 89.2% against an uninduced control (Results, Part 2). Two gaps hold this at 4: the team itself notes OD600 cannot show killing and viable counts are still needed, and the oxygen circuit (Figure 27, 5.77-fold anaerobic/aerobic difference) has no circuit-free control strain, so part of that difference could be oxygen's own effect on growth.
justification.a3: The need is well evidenced (WHO 2022 figures on Description and HP) and confirmed by users rather than only by literature: a family interview, 177 survey respondents, cardiovascular patients, a TCM clinician and a retired head nurse all appear on the Human Practices page, and Danshen grower Mr. Wang Yanfeng framed microbial SAA as complementary to cultivation rather than a replacement. Implementation is concrete about form (freeze-dried powder in capsules, blister packaging) and honest about limits (Description, Implement; Safety, on SAA toxicology being intravenous and therefore not transferable to intestinal delivery). It is not higher because nothing was tested in or near the real setting: no gut-like condition, no EcN, no delivery or dose data.
justification.a4: Six labelled DBTL cycles each state a central question, a build, a quantitative test and a Learn step that visibly sets the next Design (Engineering page). The chain is genuine: DOPA accumulating to 125.56 ± 8.72 mg/L at 40 h motivates the LaaD strategy of Cycle 4; the admission that OD600 cannot prove killing and that induction cannot cover accidental release motivates Cycle 6's oxygen-responsive switch. The notebook records real setbacks (4 Jun HPLC calibration R2 = 0.9808 repeated; 10 Jun 0/12 positive clones) and the Contribution page writes up the no-colony troubleshooting. Short of 5 because most Learn steps confirm a success rather than redesign around a failure, Cycle 4 never reaches Build or Test, and success criteria are titer comparisons rather than pre-declared thresholds.
justification.a5: This is the strongest part of the wiki. The RARE framework (Reason, Approach, Response, Evolution) runs across eighteen documented engagements and several produce traceable design changes: Daosheng Biotechnology researchers' point about upstream precursor bottlenecks led directly to aroG^fbr/tyrA^fbr in SAA2; Dr. Zhang Jingyu's advice on AI-assisted protein design led to the HpaB triple mutant in SAA3; park outreach with middle-aged and older residents, where safety dominated, led to the dual kill switch; comparing BSDFZ-China 2025 led the team to reject a cold-triggered switch because released bacteria would not reliably meet temperatures below 16 C, and to adopt an oxygen trigger instead; a packaging company pushed them to capsules; Mr. Liu, Ms. Yu and Ms. Li moved positioning from medicine to supportive health management. Critical voices are kept rather than filtered. I withhold the 5 because the survey of 177 respondents and the patient interviews carry no statement of consent, anonymity or ethical oversight, and stakeholder views are paraphrased with no indication of how they were recorded.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page at all: /attributions, /attribution and /team/attributions all return 404, and the navigation never offers one. The Team page lists over twenty students with self-written bios, but the task statements are generic (experimental work, project research, data analysis) and nothing maps a person to a construct, a fermentation run or a simulation. Partial credit is earned where attribution does appear: the Contribution page names wet-lab leader Yao Xinyi for coordination and Wang Yujia for the biosafety literature review, the HP page names every external adviser (Dr. Wang Guoliang, Dr. Zhang Jingyu, the companies visited), and Experiments states plainly that genes were synthesised and sequenced by Tsingke. But 100 ns molecular dynamics, CAVER channel analysis, AutoDock Vina docking and a full HPLC metabolic-engineering campaign are presented with no statement of who ran them or whose laboratory hosted the work. That is a question for the session, not an accusation, and it holds a6 at 3 until answered.
justification.a7: The project is built squarely on standard parts and standard assembly. Experiments records global codon optimisation for BL21, manual removal of EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI and XhoI sites to meet RFC10, BioBrick homologous adaptors on every fragment and assembly into pSB1A3, with BBa_B0034 as RBS and BBa_B0015 as terminator. The Parts page lists nine basic and five composite parts, and several composites (SAA1, SAA2, SAA3, pBAD-MazF, phyB-MazE/MazF) carry their own functional data on the Results page rather than being named only. Short of 5 because the registered new parts are largely literature-derived coding sequences recoded to standard, and nothing was characterised in the intended EcN host.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is excellent: every part is tabulated with ID, type, length and function; the Parts page states candidly that experimental work supports SAA1-SAA3 while SAA4 remains a future strategy; Experiments gives full protocols with catalogue numbers, media recipes and chromatographic conditions; the notebook is dated day by day. Registry-side I could verify nothing — parts.igem.org returned a 403/CAPTCHA wall for BBa_26UW0W4F and I will not work around it — so the only part documentation I can actually judge is the wiki's, which by itself does not satisfy the Parts requirement. Medal marks asserted on the wiki (SAA3 Gold, pBAD Bronze, phyB Silver) remain unconfirmed, and no raw data files accompany the figures beyond two PDFs.
justification.w1: The home page states the problem, the inspiration, the approach and the boundary in eight short numbered steps, each a few lines with a schematic, and ends with six signposted routes into the project (The big picture, How we built it, What we found, and so on). The Description abstract then restates the whole arc in one paragraph with the key numbers. A judge knows within a minute what SAA is, why E. coli Nissle was chosen and what the kill switches are for. Marginally short of 5 only because the scrollytelling home page makes a reader scroll through eight panels to reach information a single schematic could carry.
justification.w2: The main claims are each tied to a figure with units, standard deviations and replicate counts, and the separation between measured, modelled and planned is unusually disciplined for a high school wiki: SAA4 is labelled a future strategy on three different pages, and the docking/MD/CAVER work is consistently described as a structural explanation of a literature mutant rather than as a result of its own. Gaps that keep it at 4: no control strain in the oxygen-switch test, no viable counts behind either kill switch, and Figure 28 (colony formation) is shown without any quantification in the text.
justification.w3: Navigation is clean — a persistent menu, a per-page contents list, an at-a-glance block, a searchable 28-term glossary and next/previous links — and the standard pages are kept. But seven pages (Model, Measurement, Hardware, Software, Education, Inclusivity, Sustainability) are unedited iGEM template boilerplate listing 2025 inspiration teams, Attributions returns 404, and the team's real computational work sits inside Results where a judge looking for a Model will not find it. That is the opposite of complete but not sprawling, and it is the clearest place where this wiki loses ground.
justification.w4: A future team could rebuild most of this. Experiments carries full protocols (media recipes, catalogue numbers, HPLC column, mobile phase, flow rate, wavelength, induction conditions), the notebook is a dated table from 1 June to late August including failed steps, the Parts page lists every construct, and Safety and Contribution pass on reusable lessons. Short of 5 because no raw data are downloadable beyond a survey PDF and a kit insert, the fermentation and fluorescence figures come without underlying numbers, and the missing Attributions page removes the record of who to ask.
justification.w5: Each content page ends with a numbered reference list, in-text citations are consistent (Tian et al. 2025, Chen et al. 2019, Yao et al. 2013, GBD 2023, WHO), prior iGEM work is credited where it was used (BUCT 2021 for MazE/MazF, BSDFZ-China 2025 for the dual-control idea), and even the Danshen photographs are credited to named photographers (Description, Figure 7). The lapses are small but real: a garbled 'Ting et al.m 2020', bare URLs standing in for the two iGEM references, and an incomplete market citation rendered as '(Desale)' on Entrepreneurship.

J3.one_line: A genuinely strong high school metabolic-engineering project — three built strains, measured titers with controls, two validated containment circuits and eighteen documented stakeholder cycles that visibly changed the design — held back by a missing Attributions page, untouched template pages, and a chassis and fourth generation that exist only on paper.
strengths: Measured, replicated production data with a wild-type control and an external standard curve: 155.38 ± 11.57 mg/L (SAA1) versus 1.64 ± 0.61 mg/L (WT BL21), rising to 1366.87 ± 57.09 mg/L (SAA3) at 24 h and 3503.33 ± 201.08 mg/L at 40 h, with glucose and DOPA tracked in the same time course (Results).

Human Practices that changed the project rather than decorating it: the Daosheng visit redirected the team to precursor supply (SAA2), Dr. Zhang Jingyu's input produced the HpaB triple mutant (SAA3), and park conversations about safety plus a critique of BSDFZ-China's cold-triggered switch produced the oxygen-responsive design (Human Practices, RARE cycles 09, 10, 13, 14).

Honest reporting of limits in the team's own voice: Results states that OD600 cannot establish killing and viable counts are still required, and that the 40 h run starts from a non-zero 146.00 ± 14.73 mg/L baseline; Safety notes that SAA toxicology comes from intravenous studies that cannot be transferred to intestinal delivery.

Clean standard-parts practice — RFC10 site removal, BioBrick adaptors, pSB1A3, BBa_B0034/B0015 — and a Parts page that explicitly separates what was tested (SAA1-SAA3) from what is only designed (SAA4).

A dated notebook that records setbacks, including a failed HPLC calibration (R2 = 0.9808) and 0/12 positive clones on the first SAA1 colony PCR, plus a Contribution page that turns the no-colony episode into reusable advice for other teams.
weaknesses: No Attributions page exists (404 on /attributions and every variant) and no figure caption or chart says which student ran which experiment, leaving sophisticated methods — HPLC metabolic engineering, 100 ns MD, CAVER, docking — without a stated owner or host laboratory.

The oxygen-responsive kill switch is tested only as circuit-bearing cells aerobic versus anaerobic, with no empty-vector or circuit-free strain in parallel, so the 5.77-fold difference cannot be separated from oxygen's own effect on growth; neither switch has viable-count data.
Everything was done in E. coli BL21(DE3) while the entire product concept rests on E. coli Nissle 1917, which never appears in an experiment — the central application claim is untested.

The Model, Measurement, Hardware, Software, Education, Inclusivity and Sustainability pages are unedited iGEM template text; the team's real computational work (docking, MD, CAVER) is buried inside Results where a judge looking for a Model would not find it.

The 177-respondent survey, the park outreach and the interviews with cardiovascular patients carry no mention of consent, anonymity or ethical oversight, and stakeholder responses are paraphrased with no note of how they were recorded.

Citation lapses: a mangled in-text reference (Ting et al.m 2020), bare URLs standing in for the BUCT 2021 and BSDFZ-China 2025 references, and an incomplete market source rendered as (Desale) on the Entrepreneurship page.
red_flags: Required Attributions page missing entirely (HTTP 404 on https://2026.igem.wiki/squirrel-guangzhou/attributions and on /attribution and /team/attributions); the Team page offers only generic role statements, so who did the bench and computational work cannot be established from the wiki. This is a session question, not an allegation.

No consent, anonymity or ethics/oversight statement anywhere for the 177-respondent public survey, the park outreach or the interviews with cardiovascular patients (Human Practices, RARE cycles 02, 12, 13).

Registry part entries could not be verified: parts.igem.org returned a 403 CAPTCHA wall for BBa_26UW0W4F and I did not attempt to bypass it, so the medal marks claimed on the Parts page (SAA3 Gold, phyB Silver, pBAD Bronze) and all Registry-side documentation are unconfirmed by me rather than judged absent.
Kill-switch functional claims rest on OD600 with no circuit-free control strain for the oxygen system; Figure 28 shows colony formation but no counts are reported in the text.

Some notebook rows for 21-27 July carry the annotation 'Planned sequence from earlier notebook draft', blurring what was recorded on the day against what was reconstructed later — worth one clarifying question.

calibrated.changed: none.

one_line.en: Four generations of metabolic engineering with real titres, controls and two tested containment circuits, undermined by a missing attributions page and a probiotic chassis that was never built.
one_line.zh: 四代代謝工程，具真實效價、對照與兩套經測試的圍阻電路，但缺少歸屬頁，且作為產品核心的益生菌底盤從未建成。

strengths: Stepwise production data with a wild-type negative control and an external calibration curve, across three biological replicates
Both safety circuits characterised rather than drawn, with dose- and time-dependent reporter data and matched growth curves
Honest reporting of limits and failures, including a non-zero baseline explained rather than hidden and failed cloning rounds recorded
Human Practices tightly coupled to the bench, with a supplier conversation driving a redesign and peer comparison replacing one kill-switch design
weaknesses: No attributions anywhere and no acknowledgement of host laboratory, advisors or who operated the instruments
The probiotic chassis the whole product depends on never appears in an experiment
Kill switches are validated as growth inhibition rather than killing, with no viable counts and no circuit-free control
Several standard pages 404 and seven award pages are untouched template text
red_flags: Attributions page absent and no mentor or supervising institution named anywhere despite advanced instrumentation and simulation
Framing drift between a probiotic product claim and a laboratory-strain evidence base
One reference could not be verified and several citations are malformed or bare URLs
Public survey, park outreach and patient interviews with no consent or ethics statement

screen.project_title: Layered biosynthetic perfume: cis-abienol base note and linalool middle note in E. coli
screen.what_they_built: Two independent terpenoid modules in E. coli BL21(DE3): a cis-abienol pathway (IDI, Erg20, GGPPS, CAS) boosted by an isopentenol utilisation pathway (ScCK, SfPhoN, MjIPK) fed with exogenous DMAOH, and a linalool pathway (IDI, Erg20, LIS) optimised by engineering Erg20 to shift GPP/FPP flux.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); all genes codon-optimised with EcoRI, XbaI, SpeI, PstI and NotI sites removed for RFC#10 BioBrick compatibility. 8 new BBa parts plus BBa_J23100.
screen.best_evidence: /results: BL21-Abienol-DMAPP reached 52.14 mg/L cis-abienol at 48 h versus 4.39 mg/L for the same-batch BL21-Abienol control (about 12-fold), with wild-type BL21 showing no detectable product and DMAOH consumption tracked by GC-FID from 10 to 1.29 g/L. The Erg20 F96W/N127W double mutant reached 39.15 mg/L linalool at 48 h, a 79.3% increase over the same-batch wild-type Erg20 control. Three biological replicates throughout.
screen.hp_integration: Partly: 5.4k words of human practices exist and entrepreneurship is extensive (7.4k words), but the pack does not show a stakeholder conversation changing a design parameter the way the engineering pages change in response to titre data.
screen.reason: Genuinely good metabolic engineering for a high school team - real titres, wild-type negative controls, same-batch comparisons, biological replicates, and two complementary strategies (precursor supply versus flux redistribution) with MD and CAVER analysis used to pick the Erg20 sites before testing them. But linalool and cis-abienol, both volatile terpenoids, were quantified by HPLC with UV detection rather than GC-MS, which is a real methodological weakness a panel will press on, and the basal cis-abienol titre is 2.88 mg/L in one experiment and 4.39 mg/L in another without reconciliation. No model, education, inclusivity, sustainability or attributions pages, HP integration is thin, and only 8 parts. Strong medal, not top-2.
screen.field_notes: Squirrel-Shanghai (CHN, Fashion & Cosmetics) built a modular 'layered perfume' in E. coli BL21(DE3), treating a fragrance as separately engineerable notes rather than producing an ambergris substitute. Base note: cis-abienol (an Ambrox precursor) via IDI, Erg20, GGPPS and cis-abienol synthase, all codon-optimised and stripped of RFC#10 restriction sites; the basal strain made 2.88 mg/L at 48 h with nothing detectable in wild type, and adding an isopentenol utilisation pathway (ScCK, SfPhoN, MjIPK) fed with 10 g/L exogenous DMAOH raised this to 52.14 mg/L at 48 h, about 12-fold over the same-batch control, with DMAOH consumption confirmed by GC-FID and growth curves showing the gain was not from biomass. Middle note: linalool via LIS, 19.39 mg/L at 48 h basally, then Erg20 protein engineering - 100 ns molecular dynamics (backbone RMSD stabilising at 0.25-0.35 nm), RMSF and CAVER channel analysis identified F96 (chain-elongation cavity) and N127 (dimer interface), and the F96W/N127W double mutant reached 39.15 mg/L, +79.3% over wild-type Erg20. Five DBTL cycles claimed. Quantification was by HPLC-UV on a C18 column for both volatile terpenoids rather than GC-MS, the clearest methodological gap. Wiki has a strong search/glossary navigation layer; pages for model, education, inclusivity, sustainability and attributions are absent.

screen.project_title: Prometheus Fire: one-pot thermally gated E-RCA + CRISPR-Cas12a miR-21 assay
screen.what_they_built: A single-tube, extraction-free microRNA assay that runs exponential rolling-circle amplification at 30 C and then ignites CRISPR-Cas12a readout at 60 C, using a temperature-responsive ssRNA blocker as a molecular safety valve and a Zn2+-dependent DNAzyme embedded in the padlock probe as a kinetic accelerator.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5alpha and BL21(DE3) with pET28a-enAsCas12a for protein production; the functional parts are nucleic acids (two miR-21 padlock recognition halves, I-R3 DNAzyme complementary sequence, enAsCas12a sgRNA, ssRNA blocker). No BBa part numbers appear anywhere in the crawl — Registry documentation looks absent or unlinked.
screen.best_evidence: /results: SDS-PAGE showing Ni-NTA purification at pH 8.0 giving a single major enAsCas12a band versus multiple impurity bands at pH 7.5 (Figs 8-10); Fig 11 real-time fluorescence kinetics showing the ssRNA blocker suppressing 30 C background leakage; Fig 12 a concentration-dependent response across a miR-21 dilution series from 10 fM to 100 nM with specificity against homologous non-targets.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — oncologist interviews redirected the device from definitive single-disease diagnosis to graded risk triage (absolute concentration plus low/medium/high strata, multiplexing interface reserved), and clinicians' warnings on whole-blood lysis and false positives pushed repositioning towards post-operative recurrence monitoring and nodule triage.
screen.reason: Technically the most ambitious project in this batch and the DBTL structure (five engineering questions with nested subcycles, each with a stated success criterion) is genuinely good. Expression, purification optimisation, DNAzyme cleavage by PAGE, blocker gating and a dilution series are all shown as figures. Two things a full read must resolve and which could sink it: aspect 6 — expressing and purifying enAsCas12a with SEC and running 20 ns GROMACS MD is unusual for a high school team and the /attributions page is empty, so who did what is undocumented; and aspect 7/8 — no BBa IDs are visible anywhere, so Registry documentation may be missing. Quantified claims like 'LoD markedly improved compared with NBE' are asserted without a stated LoD number.
screen.field_notes: SRE-China (Diagnostics, Shanghai) built Prometheus Fire, a closed-tube extraction-free assay for circulating miR-21 that combines exponential rolling-circle amplification with CRISPR-Cas12a. The innovation is temporal separation by temperature: at 30 C a padlock probe circularises on target miR-21, phi29 polymerase generates concatemers and an embedded Zn2+-dependent I-R3 DNAzyme cleaves them into short activators, while a programmable ssRNA blocker hybridised to the sgRNA keeps enAsCas12a asleep; ramping to 60 C melts the blocker and ignites collateral cleavage of FRET reporters. Wet-lab evidence on /results includes agarose gel confirmation of target-dependent RCA, PAGE of Zn2+-dose-dependent DNAzyme self-cleavage, IVT sgRNA production, plasmid NanoDrop purity (A260/280 ~1.85), SDS-PAGE optimisation of enAsCas12a expression (0.3 mM IPTG at 16 C) and purification, and fluorescence kinetics from 10 fM to 100 nM miR-21. Dry lab adds 20 ns GROMACS MD of the E177R/S545R/K551R enAsCas12a triple mutant (global RMSF down 35%, local residues down 55-59%) and OptNet, a small PyTorch feed-forward model for reaction-parameter optimisation. Human practices used stakeholder quadrant analysis, WeChat surveys (n>100 each) and oncologist interviews, which moved the product from mass screening to post-operative monitoring and grassroots triage with graded rather than binary output. No BBa part IDs are visible in the crawl and the attributions page is empty.

screen.project_title: FishFriend: yeast-biosynthesised 1,8-cineole as an antibiotic alternative in aquaculture
screen.what_they_built: S. cerevisiae BY4741 engineered with a progressively expanded single plasmid (pHS1 → pHS3 → pHS4) carrying the fungal cineole synthase Hyp3 plus tHMG1 and an IDI1–GGGS–ERG20(F96W/N127W) fusion, to divert mevalonate flux to GPP and produce 1,8-cineole for pathogen control in fish ponds.
screen.chassis_and_parts: S. cerevisiae BY4741 (ura3Δ0) on pRS426 (2µ, URA3), SD–URA selection, PEG/LiAc transformation; E. coli DH5α for propagation and as the Gram-negative assay target. Promoters/terminators pTEF1, pTDH3, pADH1, tCYC1, tENO2, tTDH1. Only one BBa ID appears anywhere (BBa_26Z5VW1Z); parts content lives on a non-standard /new-composite-part page.
screen.best_evidence: GC titres against a 0–500 mg/L calibration curve rising 20.46 → 31.87 → 100.54 mg/L across pHS1, pHS3 and pHS4, with chromatograms at 6.164/6.163/6.162 min (/results, Figures 6–7, 12, 18); separately, triplicate antibacterial growth curves giving an inhibition threshold between 0.10% and 0.20% (v/v) and 42% inhibition of overnight OD600 at 5% (2.07 vs 3.55 control).
screen.hp_integration: Yes, specifically — Prof. Zhu advised strengthening the upstream MVA pathway and relieving HMGR feedback inhibition, which became Cycle 2's tHMG1 addition, and advised conserving the IPP/DMAPP pool against ergosterol drain, which became Cycle 3's ERG20^WW. Prof. Cheng's warning about volatilisation justified the 10% dodecane overlay.
screen.reason: The cleanest DBTL narrative in this batch: four cycles where each design decision is justified by the previous cycle's quantitative GC data, including a documented assembly failure (the 12 kb three-way join) solved by decomposing into the intermediate pHS5 — and a five-fold titre improvement to show for it. Aspects 2 and 4 are plausibly at 4–4.5. Worth a full read mainly to resolve whether the weak Registry footprint (one BBa ID, empty Parts slot) is a crawl artefact of their non-standard /new-composite-part page, and whether the empty Attributions page hides significant outside execution. Titres appear to be single measurements with no replicates or SD, which the panel should check.
screen.field_notes: SRE-Shanghai (Agriculture village, CHN) built FishFriend, engineering S. cerevisiae BY4741 to make 1,8-cineole as a biodegradable replacement for aquaculture antibiotics. Across four DBTL cycles they expanded one pRS426 plasmid from Hyp3 alone (pHS1) to Hyp3 + tHMG1 (pHS3) to Hyp3 + tHMG1 + IDI1–ERG20^WW (pHS4), lifting GC-quantified titre from 20.46 to 31.87 to 100.54 mg/L against a 0–500 mg/L standard curve, with 10% dodecane overlay for in-situ extraction of the volatile product. Cycle 3's direct three-fragment assembly into a 12 kb circle failed; they recovered by first building the IDI1–ERG20^WW cassette as the 6,468 bp intermediate pHS5, and they publish that strategy as a contribution alongside a rapid yeast colony-PCR lysis protocol and a tsPurple visual reporter. Cycle 4 tested 1,8-cineole against E. coli DH5α (the white list barred Vibrio/Aeromonas), finding dose-dependent inhibition with a threshold between 0.10% and 0.20% v/v and 42% overnight inhibition at 5%, in triplicate with SDs. Human Practices ran six stages from Shanghai fish vendors and aquarium sellers up to international figures (a Miami mayor, a former Canadian DG of Aquaculture), and two professors' advice maps directly onto the Cycle 2 and Cycle 3 constructs. Weak points: one Registry part, an empty Attributions page, no model page, no education page, and no replicate data behind the headline titres.

screen.project_title: Starch Reaver: a three-enzyme system converting corn starch into low-GI resistant starch
screen.what_they_built: Cloned, expressed and purified alpha-amylase, 4-alpha-glucanotransferase and pullulanase in E. coli, determined each enzyme's optimal reaction conditions, then treated gelatinized and non-gelatinized corn starch with single, double and triple enzyme combinations and measured resistant starch content.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5-alpha for cloning and BL21(DE3) for expression; pET28a(+) constructs pET28a-AM, pET28a-GT and pET28a-PUL with His tags. Six new BBa parts plus four reused; genes from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens, Bacteroides finegoldii and Neobacillus ginsengisoli.
screen.best_evidence: /results section 4: resistant starch content by Solarbio kit (GOD-POD colorimetry against a standard curve) showing the gelatinized AM-GT-PUL triple-enzyme group significantly above all single and double combinations and above the untreated control, corroborated by SEM at x5.00k showing progressive surface erosion, pore formation and a dense collapsed matrix only in the triple gelatinized group. DNS maltose standard curve R-squared above 0.99.
screen.hp_integration: Partial: a 605-respondent survey identified taste and texture (39.34%) as the main purchase barrier and is cited as shaping future work on food incorporation, but no change to the enzyme design or assay plan is traced to stakeholders.
screen.reason: A clean, complete and well-controlled pipeline from cloning through purification to a functional food-relevant endpoint with two independent readouts (RS assay and SEM), which is a solid gold-medal standard. But it is explicitly one DBTL cycle, the enzymes are known wild-type sequences simply expressed rather than engineered, no absolute RS percentages or statistics are given in the text, and the human practices did not steer the science. Strong team, not top-2.
screen.field_notes: SSBS (Food and Nutrition, China) built Starch Reaver, a three-enzyme system to convert ordinary corn starch into low-GI resistant starch by changing type C crystals into digestion-resistant type B. Alpha-amylase (Bacillus amyloliquefaciens), 4-alpha-glucanotransferase (Bacteroides finegoldii) and pullulanase (Neobacillus ginsengisoli) were cloned into pET28a(+) by homologous recombination, verified by PCR (1989, 2691 and 2577 bp), colony PCR and full sequencing, expressed in BL21(DE3) with IPTG and purified by Ni-NTA with SDS-PAGE of crude, purified and solubility fractions. Each enzyme's optimum was determined separately (GT at 37 C, 0.5 mg/mL, 30 min; PUL at 42 C, 2.0 mg/mL, 30 min, quantified by DNS against a maltose standard curve with R-squared above 0.99). Starch was then processed in gelatinized and non-gelatinized form through all enzyme combinations, retrograded, ethanol-washed, dried and assayed with a Solarbio resistant starch kit: gelatinization was necessary, every enzyme group beat the control, and the AM-GT-PUL triple group was highest, matched by SEM at x5.00k showing the most collapsed, densified granule structure. The team describes this as one full DBTL cycle. Six new parts were registered alongside four reused ones, and a 605-person survey found 39.34% cite coarse taste as the barrier to sugar-control staples. The wiki is long (10.7k-word contribution page, 7.9k entrepreneurship) with no hardware, measurement or attributions pages.

screen.project_title: FRESHOMA: temperature-controlled isovaleric acid degradation for odour removal
screen.what_they_built: Engineered E. coli carrying an isovaleric-acid degradation module (fadD, fadL, aidB, mccAB) plus a pTRIP temperature/AHL-regulated suicide module, combined into one co-transformed strain. A conceptual deodorising appliance (6 design versions) wraps the biology.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a/EPI400/BL21(DE3); pETDuet-1, pCDFDuet-1, pTRIP backbones. ~13 new BBa parts in a nominated Part Collection (e.g. BBa_26QD0KRB pETDuet-fadD, BBa_26IJT41D fadD-fadL, BBa_269PASI5 aidB-mccAB, BBa_269PYXP5 pTRIP-holin-lysozyme) plus reused BBa_K4942010.
screen.best_evidence: /results 3.2-3.6: residual isovaleric acid quantified by competitive ELISA and HPLC over 24 h (pCDFDuet-aidB-mccAB lowest residual); /results 3.4 nearly 90% fatality at 20 C after 36 h for pTRIP-holin-lysozyme with negligible killing at 37 C; /results 3.6 combined strain degrades at 37 C then kills at 20 C across 1/3/5 g/L IVA.
screen.hp_integration: Four-phase HP (221-response survey, three expert interviews) is well organised and claims design responses, but the recorded changes are mostly framing, pricing and 'retained the primary circuit' rather than demonstrable redesign of the biology.
screen.reason: Competent, genuinely quantitative three-cycle project with a coherent part collection and an unusually clear awards/navigation page, but the hardware is untested (its own page labels module testing 'future development'), replication is not shown, HP changes are shallow, and the attributions page is empty (0 words), so student-vs-outside work cannot be judged. Strong medal team, not top-2 calibre.
screen.field_notes: SSES (Shanghai Shangde Experimental School, CHN, Fashion & Cosmetics village) built FRESHOMA, an engineered E. coli that degrades isovaleric acid, the main foot-odour compound, and carries a temperature/AHL-gated suicide switch so escaped cells die in cool environments. Three DBTL cycles: degradation module comparison (fadD, fadD-fadL, aidB-mccAB), killing module comparison (ccdB, MazF, holin-lysozyme), then a co-transformed combined strain in EPI400. Key data: HPLC and competitive ELISA show falling residual isovaleric acid over 24 h with aidB-mccAB best; sandwich ELISA quantifies FadD (163-220 ng/L) against an under-LOQ control; the holin-lysozyme killing strain reaches close to 90% fatality at 20 C after 36 h and stays quiet at 37 C; the combined strain degrades then kills in a two-stage 37 C/20 C run at 1, 3 and 5 g/L substrate. About 13 new parts are nominated as a Part Collection. A six-version deodorising appliance is designed but its modules are only slated for future testing, and the attributions page is empty. Wiki navigation (interactive home scene, awards page mapping claims to evidence) is a strength.

screen.project_title: Tyrofix — immobilized tyrosinase for producing DOPA-rich mussel foot protein biomaterials
screen.what_they_built: Three recombinant tyrosinases screened and the best (BmTyr) immobilized on carboxyl magnetic beads as a recoverable 'Tyrofix' platform, used to hydroxylate engineered Mfp3-Mfp6 fusion proteins with varied domain order and linker length, then evaluated on NIH/3T3 fibroblasts.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a and BL21(DE3), pET21a backbone. 14 parts listed: Mfp3, Mfp6, BmTyr, SaTyr, mTyr coding sequences, GGSG and double-GGGGS linkers, the vector, and composite expression constructs including three Mfp fusion arrangements.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /engineering Cycle 1: BCA plus protein-normalized activity across wash and elution fractions (mTyr highest recovery at ~0.34 mg/mL but BmTyr highest activity), activity retained after magnetic-bead immobilization with a 24-hour second time point showing BmTyr ahead; ABTS antioxidant assay favouring the two short-linker fusions; NIH/3T3 proliferation strongest at 25 ug/mL with greater scratch closure.
screen.hp_integration: Human practices (4,080 words) and a large entrepreneurship section are present and the application framing shifted toward wound care, but the pack does not evidence a specific stakeholder conversation changing a specific construct or parameter.
screen.reason: Three coherent DBTL cycles and a sensible screen-then-select logic, but most results are described qualitatively ('strong activity', 'favourable cytocompatibility') with few hard numbers, the mammalian cell work sits against an empty attributions page and a 111-word team page, and reuse cycles — the whole point of an immobilized platform — were never tested.
screen.field_notes: SUIS-SFLS (Therapeutics, CHN) built Tyrofix, a magnetic-bead-immobilized tyrosinase platform for producing DOPA-rich mussel foot protein biomaterials. Cycle 1 cloned BmTyr (891 bp), SaTyr (822 bp) and mTyr (909 bp) into pET21a (5363 bp) by homology assembly with gel, colony-PCR and sequencing verification; mTyr gave the best soluble recovery at about 0.34 mg/mL by BCA, but BmTyr had the strongest protein-normalized activity and retained more activity after bead immobilization at a 24-hour re-measurement, so BmTyr was selected. Cycle 2 compared Mfp3-Mfp6 fusion domain order and linker length (GGSG short vs double GGGGS long); ABTS antioxidant assays favoured the two short-linker constructs. Cycle 3 ran Tyrofix hydroxylation and cellular evaluation in NIH/3T3 fibroblasts, reporting cytocompatibility across tested concentrations, strongest proliferation at 25 ug/mL and greater scratch closure. Fourteen parts are listed on the contribution page (no dedicated parts page). Results are written largely as qualitative figure descriptions rather than tabulated values with replicates, repeated reaction-recovery-reuse cycles are explicitly left as future work, and there is no attributions page, no hardware page and only a 111-word team page against a 9,670-word entrepreneurship section and a 5,923-word model page.

screen.project_title: S.A.F.E. Crops: Smart Anti-Freeze Endophytes for Crops
screen.what_they_built: Bacillus subtilis 168Δ4 engineered to secrete three antifreeze/ice-binding proteins (DcAFP, ScGlu, ffIBP) under a cold-responsive AND-gate circuit, with a T4 holin/lysozyme kill switch, applied to plants as a protective endophyte.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) for expression screening and B. subtilis 168Δ4 with Pgrac100-amyQ secretion vector; 8 new Registry parts (DcAFP BBa_26Y0B452, ScGlu BBa_26QON142, ffIBP BBa_26S9P1BL, NmlgtB, LacIinv, AsbBgs, AND-gate composite BBa_26S5IFQU, SUMO BBa_26XCJA9O) plus documentation added to reused parts BBa_K112000/K112012.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering: purified proteins raised tobacco protoplast survival after 30 min at -5 C and lowered the cell-leakage factor of 7-day seedlings after 6 h at 0 C (bar charts with blank and untreated controls); A280 showed SUMO fusion raised ffIBP from ~0.2 to 0.619 mg/mL; Western blot confirmed secretion of all three fusions in B. subtilis; /contribution shows OD600 falling hourly for 7 h after holin-lysozyme induction.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in part - farmer and climate-expert interviews chose frost over pest control as the target, and Dr Tianyu Gong's advice on endophytes drove the switch to B. subtilis 168Δ4 as chassis.
screen.reason: Real functional data on three antifreeze proteins and a working lysis switch, with genuine iteration (SUMO rescue of insoluble expression), so a solid medal team. But the Results, Model, Hardware, Proof-of-Concept and Attributions pages are empty iGEM templates, so the evidence is scattered on the Engineering page, assays are single runs with weak controls, and nothing shows the integrated strain protecting a plant. Not top-2 material.
screen.field_notes: SZ-SHD (Suzhou, Agriculture village) targeted early-spring frost on tea and small-fruit crops identified in farmer interviews. They engineered B. subtilis 168Δ4 to secrete DcAFP, ScGlu and ffIBP under a two-stage cold AND-gate (NmlgtB/LacIinv/AsbBgs) with a T4 holin-lysozyme kill switch for containment. Key results: SUMO fusion rescued soluble expression in E. coli (ffIBP ~3x higher by A280), purified proteins improved tobacco protoplast survival at -5 C and reduced seedling cell leakage after 6 h at 0 C, Western blot confirmed secretion in B. subtilis, and induction of the holin-lysozyme pair dropped OD600 over 7 h. Eight new Registry parts plus added documentation on two 2008-era T4 parts and the SUMO tag. Human practices are extensive (5.2k words, field trips, a climate expert, a return interview with tea farmers) and changed the chassis choice. Weaknesses: Results, Model, Hardware and Attributions pages are unedited iGEM boilerplate, no modelling at all, and the full circuit was never tested on a plant.

screen.project_title: Recombinant multi-enzyme system against Streptococcus mutans dental plaque biofilm
screen.what_they_built: Six pET28a constructs expressing four single enzymes (dextranase, mutanase, lysozyme G, Dispersin B) and two bifunctional fusions (DEX-MUT, LYS-DSB) intended to dismantle the glucan matrix of cariogenic biofilm while lysing embedded bacteria.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5α for cloning and BL21(DE3) for expression; pET28a (T7 promoter, N-terminal T7 tag, C-terminal 6×His, KanR); homologous recombination assembly. 12 new registry parts (6 basic CDSs plus 6 pET28a composites: BBa_26WXGQ7C, BBa_26D4OIWK, BBa_26C23MGB, BBa_263XTF3V, BBa_26MTOK74, BBa_26FIAWUW and matching composites).
screen.best_evidence: DNS reducing-sugar assay on dextran giving 0.42 mg/mL (DEX), 1.33 mg/mL (MUT) and 0.81 mg/mL (DEX-MUT), backed by TLC showing all three produce glucose-like Rf products (/results §2.1–2.2); Dispersin B activity of 11,778 U/L for DSB with LYS-DSB retaining ~50%; dose-dependent crystal violet biofilm suppression and growth curves for both fusions up to 1000 µg/mL, with LYS-DSB near-complete growth suppression at 50 µg/mL (/results §2.5, Figure 13).
screen.hp_integration: Partly — eight stakeholder interviews (industry R&D, dentists, enzyme engineering Prof. Qin Zhen, a policy/investment analyst) plus a 534-response survey shaped the product framing, pricing and launch strategy, but the wiki does not show a stakeholder comment changing a construct or an assay.
screen.reason: Competent, honest cloning-and-expression work with a reasonable spread of activity assays, but the project never tested its actual target: every biofilm experiment was run on E. coli, a Gram-negative the team itself notes is a poor model for S. mutans, and the mature-biofilm degradation assay showed essentially no effect (OD570 ~2.76–2.85 versus 2.90 control). Both fusion proteins — the novel contribution — expressed poorly, and activities were measured on unnormalised crude lysates, which the team concedes prevents any specific-activity conclusion. There is also a substrate-specificity error in the Results text (mutanase described as preferring α-1,6 bonds). No Attributions page, no Parts page, no model.
screen.field_notes: SZA-Union (Therapeutics village, Shanghai, CHN) targeted dental caries with a two-pronged recombinant enzyme toolbox against S. mutans biofilm: a matrix-degrading pair (dextranase for α-1,6 dextran, mutanase for α-1,3 mutan) and a cell-attacking pair (lysozyme G, Dispersin B), each also built as a bifunctional fusion (DEX-MUT 3946 bp, LYS-DSB 2142 bp) in pET28a and expressed in BL21(DE3). All six constructs were PCR-verified and Sanger-sequenced correct. Induction was optimised across 16/37 °C, 0.1–1.0 mM IPTG and 4/16 h; LYS (26 kDa) and DSB (50 kDa) expressed well, DEX (74 kDa) and MUT (76 kDa) gave prominent bands, but secreted yield of both fusions was poor. Functional data: TLC showed all three glucanase constructs release glucose-like products; DNS gave 0.42, 1.33 and 0.81 mg/mL reducing sugar for DEX, MUT and DEX-MUT; a kit assay gave 11,778 U/L for DSB with LYS-DSB at ~50%; a lysozyme kit showed a 112-fold gap between LYS and LYS-DSB that the team correctly refuses to interpret because the samples were never normalised to equal total protein. Crystal violet and growth-curve assays showed dose-dependent biofilm inhibition up to 1000 µg/mL and near-complete growth suppression by LYS-DSB at 50 µg/mL — but all biofilm work used E. coli, and against mature E. coli biofilm the enzymes did essentially nothing (OD570 2.76–2.85 vs 2.90 control), which they attribute to the Gram-negative outer membrane. They contributed 12 parts, ran eight stakeholder interviews with a four-quadrant stakeholder map, and produced large education (5.5k words) and entrepreneurship (8.8k words) sections. No Attributions page, no Parts page, no model, and a substrate-specificity error in the Results text.

screen.project_title: GreenErgo: engineered E. coli producing ergothioneine for oxidation control in refrigerated ready meals
screen.what_they_built: The fungal Trichoderma reesei Egt1/Egt2 ergothioneine pathway rebuilt in E. coli BW25113, boosted by screening four SAM/methyl-cycle genes, then by six literature- and AI-predicted single-point Egt1 variants, with an FBA model choosing the pathway and naming the bottleneck first.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BW25113 (pTrc99a and pBBR1-MCS backbones). 18 parts, all coding sequences: egt1 (BBa_26ZQSMXP), egt2, egtE, the methyl-cycle set ADO1/BHMT/SAH1/SAM2, and five Egt1 point variants including the improved egt1-K406S (BBa_26U7ANMM).
screen.best_evidence: /engineering Cycles 1-3, quantified by HPLC against an authentic EGT standard on one calibration curve, n=3 biological replicates, mean +/- SD: baseline Egt1/Egt2 23.37 mg/L; adding EgtE dropped it to 16.36 mg/L (a reported negative result); ADO1 co-expression raised it to 39.1 mg/L (+67.3%); and of six Egt1 variants only K406S improved output, to 35.6 mg/L (+52.3%), with the other five falling as low as 9.6 mg/L.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - 13 engagements across four stages; a campus kitchen visit killed the original school-cafeteria premise (meals are cooked same-day), food scientists set the oxidation indicators they would have to measure, and a factory visit redirected the application to discoloration in peeled shrimp, which then framed the entrepreneurship plan.
screen.reason: Borderline but worth a full read. Real replicated HPLC titers, an honest negative result (EgtE, and five of six variants), and a genuine model-to-bench loop: an iML1515 FBA comparison of three EGT routes picked the fungal pathway and named methyl supply and Egt1 capacity as the bottlenecks, which is exactly what Cycles 2 and 3 then attacked. The attribution page is one of the best in the batch, naming per-member tasks, PI/advisor roles and AI tools. Against that: the standard /results page is empty (all data sits inside /engineering), the food-application half of the project - dosing a chilled food model, the 25-60 C stability work - is described but not shown as data in the pack, and the 'approximately 2.5-fold better than previously reported Egt1 mutants' claim on /achievement needs checking against the source.
screen.field_notes: SZSAIS-BaoAn (Biomanufacturing, CHN) produced ergothioneine, a thermostable sulphur antioxidant, in E. coli BW25113 as a candidate ingredient against lipid and protein oxidation in chilled ready meals. Modelling came first: iML1515 in COBRApy compared the prokaryotic EgtABCDE, fungal Egt1/Egt2 and anaerobic EanA/EanB routes under identical uptake and growth constraints, selected the two-enzyme fungal route, and identified methyl-donor supply and Egt1 catalytic capacity as the two bottlenecks. Three DBTL cycles followed, all quantified by HPLC against an authentic standard with n=3: baseline 23.37 mg/L; adding M. smegmatis EgtE made it worse at 16.36 mg/L; of four methyl-cycle genes ADO1 gave 39.1 mg/L (+67.3%) while BHMT did nothing; and of six Egt1 point mutants (two from literature, four from AI prediction with three models ranked by conservation, stability and active-site distance) only K406S helped, at 35.6 mg/L (+52.3%), submitted as an improved part. Cycle 4 addresses EGT thermal stability from 25-60 C, and the shrimp food-model application is a plan rather than a result. Human practices is well organised and genuinely redirected scope twice. Attribution is detailed per member and discloses AI tools (ChatGPT, WorkBuddy, Claude Code, Fusion PLM). Wiki weakness: the Results page is empty and all evidence lives inside the Engineering narrative; the Parts page lists descriptions with almost no characterisation data.

screen.project_title: FAAH-expressing E. coli Nissle probiotic for appetite support in childhood undernutrition
screen.what_they_built: A six-construct localisation panel expressing Faecalibacterium prausnitzii fatty acid amide hydrolase in E. coli, asking where the enzyme must sit to reach gut-lumen oleoylethanolamide, plus a from-scratch reanalysis of a published MDCF-2 microbiome trial.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) for expression and E. coli Nissle 1917 as the target chassis; pEM106.2 backbone with in vivo assembly cloning; variants with wild-type FAAH, dTm, YebF, OmpX, OmpA and a GFP control. Only one BBa part (BBa_26OGKKLT) found anywhere on the wiki.
screen.best_evidence: /results: four constructs sequence-verified and three (GFP, WT-FAAH, dTm-FAAH) show induced SDS-PAGE bands of expected mass absent from their own uninduced controls; the YebF variant is transformed into EcN and banked. The page states plainly '0 activity assays run so far'.
screen.hp_integration: Yes and crisply documented: eight experts across three countries forced a four-field record per engagement and narrowed the framework, including the correction that the end user is the caregiver/clinician, not the malnourished child.
screen.reason: The best-written and most scrupulously honest wiki in this batch, with a substantial independent reanalysis of a 939-sample published dataset and an exemplary attributions and AI-use record. But the Project section is the main determinant and nothing functional was demonstrated: expression bands only, no enzyme activity, no OEA measurement, and a single registered part. It cannot outrank teams with working systems.
screen.field_notes: Texas (USA, Food & Nutrition village) set out to express Faecalibacterium prausnitzii fatty acid amide hydrolase in E. coli Nissle 1917 to lower the satiety signal oleoylethanolamide and support appetite in childhood undernutrition. The wet lab is a six-variant localisation panel (WT, transmembrane-deleted, YebF secretion, OmpX and OmpA display, GFP control, plus an unbuilt catalytic mutant) cloned into pEM106.2 by in vivo assembly. Four constructs are sequence-verified, three show induced bands of the expected mass by SDS-PAGE, and the YebF-dTm-FAAH variant is banked in EcN as five glycerol stocks; the team states that zero activity assays have been run. The results page is unusually disciplined: 21 chronological figures, each with what it shows and what it concludes, including troubleshooting stories (satellite colonies on ampicillin resolved by switching to chloramphenicol; a single-nucleotide insertion fixed after eight weeks by moving ligation out of the cell). Dry lab reanalyses Chen et al. 2021 NEJM MDCF-2 16S data (ENA PRJEB38494, 939 samples, 118 children) in QIIME 2/R/Python with MICOM metabolic modelling, and is explicit that the growth-linkage analysis cannot be reproduced because child growth data was never released. Attributions (2.7k words) and a dedicated AI-use page are among the most transparent in the batch. Only one Registry part.

screen.project_title: BetterSweet: reconstructing the mogroside V pathway in Nicotiana benthamiana
screen.what_they_built: They designed a six-enzyme mogroside V biosynthetic pathway from Siraitia grosvenorii in pCAMBIA1302 using P2A self-cleaving linkers, and used Tobacco Rattle Virus virus-induced gene silencing to knock down the native squalene brake NbHISE1. Silencing was achieved in part; downstream mogroside production was not demonstrated.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Nicotiana benthamiana as the plant chassis with Agrobacterium tumefaciens delivery; pCAMBIA1302 binary vector with CaMV 35S, pTRV2 VIGS vector, pDONR207 Gateway entry vector; new composite parts for SgSQE1-P2A-SgCS (BBa_26YT57XV), SgEPH2-P2A-SgP450 (BBa_26V79NSZ), SgUGT269-1 (BBa_2651L0RT) and SgUGT289-3 (BBa_26HVH99B) plus their standalone coding sequences.
screen.best_evidence: /results Figure 1: qRT-PCR of NbHISE1 in ten pTRV2-HISE lines against a pTRV2-GFP control set to 1 shows seven lines below control and three above (1.1 the highest in the whole set), so silencing is explicitly partial; GC-MS sterol profiling (Figure 3) detected all four major phytosterols in both groups but the team states the profiles looked similar and that they cannot yet say silencing changed sterol levels.
screen.hp_integration: Extensive and well organised: a colour-coded stakeholder table covering sugar producers (TRR Group/Lin Sugar, Mitrphol), school canteen vendors, teachers and the public, with the Mitrphol interview on monk fruit export restrictions and the TRR interview on consumer acceptance reported as shaping the framing and the product work, though the molecular design appears driven by literature rather than by stakeholders.
screen.reason: Ambitious and unusually scrupulous about what the data do and do not show (the team refuses to read an end-point PCR gel as evidence of pathway activation and calls the sterol comparison inconclusive), with a genuine DBTL turn after the first silencing attempt failed on reused primers and plant age. But the central claim stops at partial knockdown of one native gene: no mogrol, no mogroside V, no squalene quantification, no demonstration that any of the four pathway plasmids expressed, and stable transformation is still waiting on flowers as of 16 October.
screen.field_notes: Thailand-RIS (Food & Nutrition village, Thailand) aimed to produce the monk fruit sweetener mogroside V in Nicotiana benthamiana rather than relying on slow-growing Siraitia grosvenorii, motivated by Thai sugar intake of about 22 teaspoons per day and a rise from 1.5 to 6.6 million diabetics.
