They cloned a six-enzyme pathway (SgSQE1, SgCS, SgEPH2, SgP450, SgUGT269-1, SgUGT289-3) into pCAMBIA1302 under CaMV 35S, using P2A self-cleaving peptides for the SQE-CS and EPH-P450 pairs that lose activity when directly fused, and keeping the UGTs separate so each could be assessed alone. To free up squalene they silenced NbHISE1 by Gateway cloning two fragments (277 bp and 223 bp amplicons) into pTRV2 and agroinfiltrating. Colony PCR confirmed all eight colonies for both fragments; the first silencing round failed, which the team attributed to reused primers and plant age, and after redesigning primers and infiltrating plants under five weeks old the second round gave qRT-PCR knockdown in seven of ten lines. Silenced plants grew shorter than pTRV2-GFP controls, read as a sterol-stress effect. GC-MS sterol profiling and an end-point NbHMGR1 PCR were both explicitly treated as inconclusive or as cDNA quality checks only. Stable transformation is unfinished pending seed. The wiki includes a lab handbook for future teams, a vision model page, inclusivity and sustainability pages, and a gummy and syrup product line.

screen.project_title: MELANIFY — converting post-consumer PET waste into allomelanin UV-protective pigment
screen.what_they_built: A two-host enzymatic cascade taking PET to allomelanin: Pichia pastoris secretes glycosylated HotPETase to depolymerise PET, and E. coli surface-displays MHETase and carries the TphA1/A2/A3/B and AroY/EcdB/EcdD operons to route terephthalic acid through protocatechuate to catechol.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Pichia pastoris KM71 with pPIC9K (AOX1, alpha-factor secretion signal, G418 selection, SacI-linearised genomic integration) and E. coli BL21(DE3) with pETDuet-1 dual-cassette constructs. Around fourteen new Registry IDs (e.g. BBa_26E50ZXU, BBa_26NRZB2D, BBa_26PUX4TB) plus BBa_K3317002, though there is no parts page on the wiki.
screen.best_evidence: /results Figure 24: HPLC at 280 nm of PCA decarboxylation by AroY-EcdB-EcdD lysate showing a peak coincident with the catechol standard at ~5.9 min, absent in the no-enzyme control, with concurrent depletion of the PCA substrate peak at ~4.9 min. Paired with Figure 15, HotPETase + InaVN-MHETase producing a peak matching the TPA standard at ~11.3 min and absent from the negative control, and Figure 14, Western blot after sarkosyl fractionation placing the fusion only in the outer-membrane pellet.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in direction-setting — a four-stage I.D.E.A. cycle running from professor consultations (including NUS) and community surveys through recycling-industry stakeholders to a UNIDO consultation and national media, with the stakeholder stage described as driving experimental adaptation; how specific conversations changed specific constructs is less sharply traceable than the wet-lab narrative.
screen.reason: Two independent steps of a five-step cascade confirmed by HPLC against authentic standards with negative controls, surface display confirmed by fractionation and Western blot, a successful Pichia genomic integration, and an explicitly reported failure (no PCA detected from TPA despite all four Tph subunits expressing) rather than a glossed-over gap. The scope and the honesty are both unusual for a high school team; the cascade is incomplete and no allomelanin was ever made, which caps aspect 2, but it merits the full read.
screen.field_notes: Thai high school team (XCL American School of Bangkok, Biomanufacturing village) framing PET waste and Thailand's UV index of 11-14 as one problem, and targeting allomelanin as a nitrogen-free, catechol-derived pigment that sidesteps oxybenzone's coral toxicity and Thailand's marine-park ban. The design splits work across hosts: Pichia secretes HotPETase (codon-optimised, alpha-factor signal, pPIC9K SacI-linearised at ~99% efficiency giving 16.8 µg linear DNA, G418-resistant clonal transformants) while E. coli handles the downstream monomers. The dry lab is substantive: NetNGlyc/NetOGlyc site prediction then 10 ns OpenMM MD at 70 C comparing glycosylated and wild-type PETase (RMSD spike to 1.7 Å at ~7 ns in the control, damped RMSF in loops 30-50 and 200-250, SASA collapse tracking the unfolding), carried over to HotPETase where the unglycosylated form diverges past 4.0 Å after ~2 ns; the team explicitly notes 10 ns is far too short to prove thermal unfolding. MHETase was displayed via an InaV-N fusion with a (GGGGS)3 linker, validated in silico by AlphaFold3 (pTM 0.73) and TMHMM, then by SDS-PAGE and outer-membrane Western. The cascade is confirmed at entry (PET to TPA) and exit (PCA to catechol); the middle TPA-to-PCA step failed, with a 2.4 min peak not matching the 5.0 min PCA standard. The design also omits the TphC transporter, so substrate access needs lysate or permeabilised cells — stated plainly on the description page. Notebook is 5,750 words and attributions 3,031; there is no model page and no parts page, so part documentation sits in Registry entries rather than on the wiki.

screen.project_title: ArtemiSilence — MSN-delivered siRNA to silence the mugwort allergen Art v 1
screen.what_they_built: Six siRNAs against ArtV1 screened in a Nicotiana benthamiana transient-expression system, then the best two loaded onto amino-functionalised mesoporous silica nanoparticles and applied by infiltration or foliar spray.
screen.chassis_and_parts: Agrobacterium tumefaciens GV3101 / N. benthamiana transient expression with pEG100-artV1-mNeonGreen; parts cited inline (e.g. ArtV1 BBA_264WQYOV, pEG100-artV1-mNeonGreen BBA_26VMH4LF, six siRNA parts) but the /parts page is empty.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering Cycle 2 table and /results Figure D: RT-qPCR normalised to NbPP2A by 2^-ddCt gives mean relative ArtV1 expression of 0.28 for siRNA154 and 0.58 for siRNA114 versus 1.54-1.92 for the non-working candidates; Cycle 3 spray delivery of MSN/siRNA154 reaches about 0.20, with >=3 leaves per group.
screen.hp_integration: Barely — /human-practices (471 words) reports two RedNote expert interviews that the team explicitly says did not change the protocol, plus a 9 September meeting with teachers and parents that prompted the switch to co-infiltration of Agrobacterium and siRNA.
screen.reason: Honest, well-scoped and genuinely iterative (three cycles with documented mistakes), and the qPCR knockdown is real. But the whole project is a tobacco proxy — nothing was tested in mugwort or on pollen — the results page is only 493 words with single-round qPCR, Models 0-4 are openly built on synthetic and hypothetical parameters, human practices is a 471-word page the team itself says did not change the design, and the parts page is empty. Clearly below the top-2 bar.
screen.field_notes: THIS-China (Bioremediation, CHN) targeted Artemisia pollen allergy by silencing the immunodominant allergen Art v 1 with siRNA delivered on amino-functionalised mesoporous silica nanoparticles. Cycle 1 built an ArtV1-mNeonGreen fusion expressed transiently in N. benthamiana via Agrobacterium GV3101 and established that MES rather than PEG buffer kept leaves intact; Cycle 2 screened six siRNAs by RT-qPCR (NbPP2A reference, 2^-ddCt), identifying siRNA154 at 0.28 and siRNA114 at 0.58 relative expression; Cycle 3 characterised NH2-MSN by SEM, TEM, DLS and zeta potential and found a 10:1 MSN:siRNA mass ratio optimal, with spray delivery of siRNA154 reaching roughly 0.20 relative expression. All work is in tobacco as a proxy; no mugwort plant or pollen was treated. Dry lab is six chained models, of which Models 0-4 are flagged by the team as using literature-derived, synthetic and hypothetical values, with Model 5 a deployment-cost scenario. Human practices is thin: two RedNote expert interviews that the team says did not alter the protocol, and one parent/teacher meeting that produced the co-infiltration fix. Attributions is 118 words pointing at the iGEM form; the parts page is empty although part IDs appear inline. The wiki is honest about failures (plant killed in transit, mislabelled RNA/protein samples).

screen.project_title: CPS Cycle — citrus waste, CotA laccase and soil for post-fire restoration
screen.what_they_built: A three-part system: citrus processing waste washed and milled into a plant-compatible soil component, Bacillus subtilis CotA laccase produced recombinantly in E. coli as a crude copper-loaded lysate, and the two combined into a dried CPS material tested against a burned-biomass phenolic model and lettuce growth.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with His-CotA in pET28a(+); backup constructs in pET21a and pFastBac1 (insect-cell route). Registry toolkit of three basic parts (e.g. BBa_2674Y1KG, BBa_266HUZUO), five composite parts and three collections, all CotA expression architectures.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /engineering: a six-condition induction screen (37 C 3 h, 30 C 6 h, 16 C overnight at 0.1 or 0.25 mM IPTG) with soluble/pellet SDS-PAGE showing 16 C overnight rescues soluble CotA; anti-His Western confirming a 60-65 kDa product; ABTS and guaiacol assays showing copper-dependent, dose-responsive activity with crude lysate comparable to purified enzyme and near-abolition at pH 2.5; raw citrus gave 0% lettuce germination while the CPS material gave 100% germination with improved stem and whole-plant length versus burnt soil across three independent seven-condition experiments of five seeds; ABTS activity still detectable in stored CPS at 72 h and guaiacol to 8 days.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — Korea Forest Service and a soil restoration company shaped field applicability and safety, a citrus by-product factory and a microbial production plant informed feedstock and scale-up, a patent attorney and an investor meeting shaped IP and commercialisation; the team also states openly that no landowner, resident or critical-perspective interview was recorded and warns against claiming representation.
screen.reason: Genuinely strong failure-driven protein engineering with replicated plant data, and an unusually scrupulous attributions page. But the synthetic biology is heterologous overexpression of one wild-type enzyme — no circuit, no characterised regulatory parts, and the Registry toolkit is mostly tag and vector variants, several explicitly uncharacterised; that caps aspect 7. The attributions page also shows the secondary PI designing, running and supervising most of the troubleshooting experiments and training students, which pulls aspect 6 down. Solid gold-medal shape rather than top-2.
screen.field_notes: TJI-Seoul (KOR, Bioremediation) linked two waste and damage problems into the CPS Cycle: citrus-processing residue, recombinant CotA laccase, and post-fire soil. Six engineering cycles are each anchored on a failure: CotA expressed strongly at 37 C but almost entirely as inclusion bodies, rescued by 16 C overnight induction at 0.25 mM IPTG with 0.5 mM CuSO4, which let them abandon four backup constructs (pET21a and pFastBac1, full-length and residues 45-514); activity proved copper-dependent rather than purification-dependent, so crude lysate was carried forward, validated by ABTS dose and pH series plus a guaiacol time-course and empty-vector controls; raw citrus waste blocked lettuce germination completely and hardened on drying, fixed by three ethanol and three distilled-water washes, drying, pulverisation and 1:1 soil mixing; the active lysate itself inhibited lettuce until component-by-component screening identified 10% glycerol in the storage buffer; a burned-leaf phenolic model gave only 0.4-0.6 ppm and was replaced by incompletely burned sawdust at 4-6 ppm; and the final dried CPS matrix retained ABTS activity to 72 h and guaiacol activity to 8 days while supporting 100% lettuce germination and better growth than burnt soil across three independent runs. Human practices covered the Korea Forest Service, a restoration company, a citrus by-product factory, a microbial production facility, a patent firm and a VC pitch, and the page itself names the stakeholder gap it did not fill. The wiki carries a separate, detailed AI-use page naming six tools and their roles, and an attributions page describing each person's contribution in the words submitted on the form — which also makes visible how much of the experimental design and supervision came from the secondary PI.

screen.project_title: You NAILed it — protein-coloured biodegradable nail material with bioadhesive
screen.what_they_built: A press-on nail material made from colour proteins (gfasPurple variants, fluorescent proteins, LvWSCP-chlorophyll a and smURFP-biliverdin) fused to hydroxyapatite-binding peptide and spider-silk NT/2Rep modules, cast with sodium alginate and hydroxyapatite by calcium crosslinking, plus a mussel-foot-protein adhesive (Mfp5-NT-2Rep-CT-Mfp5).
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli expression with Ni-NTA purification and laboratory-prepared tyrosinase. 80 BBa parts — the largest collection in this batch — covering the gfasPurple variant library, 16 fluorescent-protein candidates, two pigment-binding routes, HABP fusions, NT/2Rep material fusions and the adhesive, including an improved-part record.
screen.best_evidence: /results: three-group tensile comparison (n = 3 specimens each) giving 2.80 MPa / 96.18% strain for FM without HABP, 6.03 MPa / 67.02% for FM-HABP and 12.12 MPa / 20.92% for NT-2Rep-FM-HABP; SD values and statistics are not supplied. The adhesive gave a maximum separation load of 0.0068 N (0.085 kPa) on a PCR tube bonded to a Petri dish, with no untreated control.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in one traceable instance — a biodegradable-materials expert's follow-up prompted a soil-burial test of the composite nail, which showed no visible degradation after a month and led the team to withdraw its biodegradability claims.
screen.reason: Six DBTL cycles, a genuinely large characterised part collection and an unusually self-critical results page that refuses to overclaim. But the evidence is predominantly photographic colour-retention panels rather than measurement: no model page, no normalized colour quantification, tensile means without SD or statistics, and an adhesive at 0.085 kPa with no control group and a self-admitted failure to show DOPA conversion or attachment to a real nail. Scope and parts are impressive; demonstrated function is not yet at finalist level. Recommend a parts-only look rather than a full panel read.
screen.field_notes: Tsinglan (Fashion & Cosmetics village, China) made a protein-coloured, biodegradable press-on nail material across six DBTL cycles. Cycle 1 expanded gfasPurple into 15 colour variants; Cycle 2 screened 16 fluorescent proteins and established that emission colour does not predict the visible colour of the material; Cycle 3 added two pigment-binding routes, LvWSCP-chlorophyll a (leaf green, visibly stable after 100 C) and smURFP-biliverdin (pale blue, fades); Cycle 4 fused hydroxyapatite-binding peptide, finding candidate-dependent colour loss and precipitation; Cycle 5 added spider-silk NT/2Rep modules and cast specimens in sodium alginate with hydroxyapatite by calcium crosslinking; Cycle 6 built a mussel-foot adhesive Mfp5-NT-2Rep-CT-Mfp5, tyrosinase-treated and Ni-NTA purified. The headline quantitative result is a three-group tensile comparison showing strength rising 2.80 to 6.03 to 12.12 MPa as HABP then NT-2Rep are added, with strain at break falling 96.18% to 20.92%, n = 3, no SD given. Adhesion was 0.0068 N (0.085 kPa) with no untreated control. Stability work is extensive but photographic: 20-minute heat series to 100 C, pH 3-14 and ethanol 25-50% panels across all cycles. The results page is notable for how carefully it separates what each image can and cannot support, keeps conflicting notebook conditions distinct rather than harmonising them, and preserves failed batches including a September 16 mfp sequencing failure. 80 BBa parts and a 143-page original notebook PDF are published; there is no model page.

screen.project_title: Turning waste tea residue into PHB bioplastic
screen.what_they_built: A two-part biomanufacturing route: a physical-chemical-biological pretreatment that converts milk-tea shop tea residue into a fermentable hydrolysate, and three generations of engineered E. coli (phaABC, +pntAB, +acs) that make PHB from it.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a/BL21(DE3) with pCDF-Duet-1 and pET-Duet-1; new parts for phaABC (BBa_2656DDFI), pntAB (BBa_26P3XLFU), backbones and composites pCDFDuet-phaABC (BBa_26YDLXRH), pETDuet-pntAB (BBa_26Z5N7XB), pETDuet-acs-pntAB (BBa_261MMZBN), plus reused acs BBa_K4284020 and T7/lac promoters.
screen.best_evidence: /results section 1.4-1.5: HPLC quantification of glucose, xylose, acetate, furfural and 5-HMF across four acid-hydrolysis conditions (Group D highest glucose at 12.26 g/L but toxic; Group C selected), backed by plate inhibition tests and 24 h OD600 growth curves; section 3: Nile Red RFU rising with strain generation at 24 and 36 h, SDS-PAGE of PhaA/PhaB/PhaC, and NADPH/NADP+ ratios with strain 2 significantly above strain 1 at 36 h.
screen.hp_integration: Partly - a 441-response survey and street interviews plus expert and company interviews shaped the business model, safety-certification plan and downstream purification thinking more than the genetic design itself.
screen.reason: Four clean DBTL cycles, real HPLC feedstock characterisation and three-generation strain comparison with cofactor and acetyl-CoA measurements, written with unusual honesty about what the data cannot show. But PHB itself is only ever a relative Nile Red fluorescence - no titer, no yield, no gravimetric or GC confirmation that the polymer was made - the glucose normalisation is admitted to be unverified, and the Attributions page is empty. Strong gold territory, short of top-2.
screen.field_notes: UCS-A (Shanghai, Biomanufacturing village) converts spent milk-tea residue into PHB bioplastic. Module 1 is a sequential pretreatment (milling, dilute H2SO4 at 115 C, Cellic CTec3 cellulase for 36 h, CaO detoxification) screened across four acid conditions by HPLC for glucose, xylose, acetate, furfural and 5-HMF plus plate-inhibition and growth-curve assays; the selected condition (10% solids, 0.5% H2SO4, 115 C, 120 min, used at 50% dilution) became the standardised substrate for all later work. Module 2 built three E. coli strains stepwise: phaABC on pCDF-Duet-1, then pET-Duet pntAB for NADPH regeneration, then a pntAB-acs tandem for acetate salvage, each verified by colony PCR and full Sanger sequencing and expressed as shown by SDS-PAGE. Characterisation covers growth, Nile Red fluorescence (strains 2 and 3 highest at 36 h), residual glucose, NADPH/NADP+ and acetyl-CoA. The write-up flags its own weaknesses: RFU is not a titer, and the residual-glucose normalisation needs verifying. Human practices ran five stages from a 441-person survey to a company visit, mainly shaping commercialisation; Entrepreneurship is 8.2k words. No modelling, no hardware, empty Attributions page.

screen.project_title: Asprout — engineered Bacillus subtilis L-asparaginase II for paediatric acute lymphoblastic leukaemia
screen.what_they_built: A rationally mutated type II L-asparaginase (BsAII) from B. subtilis: ten single-point mutants plus wild type, all purified and characterised, followed by a three-way signal-peptide screen (PelB, OmpA, FedA) and fermentation optimisation of the best variant.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning and BL21(DE3) for expression, pET28a(+) with N-terminal 6xHis; 30 BBa IDs appear across the wiki, but the parts page itself is empty.
screen.best_evidence: /results: Michaelis-Menten kinetics by non-linear regression for all 11 variants (variant 214 best kcat/Km, lowest Km), indophenol-blue specific activities against an NH4Cl standard curve, and 30 C half-lives in which variant 224 is 21.6% longer-lived than wild type; the signal-peptide screen gives FedA the best kcat/Km and the longest half-life at 16.5 h versus PelB 14.5 h and OmpA 12.0 h, with triplicate means and standard deviations on the activity assay.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — a 9,735-word staged IHP built on 'Safety, Effectiveness, Protection' leads with a stakeholder map, running from problem identification through design to implementation, alongside a 5,453-word entrepreneurship plan; the strongest design link is the focus on half-life and immunogenicity-reducing surface residues drawn from clinical limitations of existing ASNase formulations.
screen.reason: The most complete protein-engineering package in the batch: eleven constructs sequence-verified, purified and compared head to head on activity, full Michaelis-Menten kinetics and thermal half-life, then a second design round on secretion signal peptides with fermentation optimisation and ELISA, plus a 6,890-word measurement page. Honest about failures (two of ten mutants did not sequence cleanly; first-round amplification of three sites failed). Needs a full read; the gaps to probe are the empty parts page, the absent attributions page, and whether the gains translate to anything beyond in vitro enzymology.
screen.field_notes: UCS-B (Therapeutics, CHN) engineered BsAII, a type II L-asparaginase from Bacillus subtilis, as an alternative to current E. coli and PEG-asparaginase formulations used against paediatric acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, targeting their immunogenicity, instability and short half-life. The 1128 bp gene was cloned into pET28a(+) by homologous recombination; ten computationally chosen single-point mutants (positions 125, 178, 191, 194, 214, 224, 254, 269, 299, 348) were made by site-directed mutagenesis, with eight of ten sequence-verified clean on the first pass. All eleven proteins were expressed in BL21(DE3) at 16 C and Ni-NTA purified to a single 42 kDa band. Characterisation covered indophenol-blue specific activity against an NH4Cl standard curve (variant 299 highest), Nessler-based Michaelis-Menten kinetics with Km, Vmax and kcat for all eleven (variant 214 best kcat/Km), and 30 C half-life decay fits (variant 224 +21.6% over wild type). A second cycle swapped the signal peptide on the 214 background: FedA gave the best catalytic efficiency and a 16.5 h half-life versus PelB 14.5 h and OmpA 12.0 h, after which fermentation conditions were optimised for BsAII-214-FedA and an ELISA run. The wiki carries a substantial measurement page (6,890 words), a 9,735-word staged IHP with stakeholder map, a 5,453-word entrepreneurship section and an awards page. Thirty BBa IDs appear across the site, but the parts page and the attributions page are both empty, so part documentation and the student-versus-outside split cannot be checked from the wiki.

screen.project_title: Enzymatic conversion of shrimp and crab shell chitin into N-acetylglucosamine for joint health
screen.what_they_built: Expression engineering and directed/ancestral redesign of a marine LPMO (LPMO3706) in E. coli BL21(DE3), combined with chitinases to raise GlcNAc yield from crustacean shell waste, supported by docking, molecular dynamics and ancestral sequence reconstruction.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3); 11 basic and 15 composite parts registered — wild-type LPMO3706, five point mutants, five reconstructed ancestral enzymes, across pET-22b/pET-28a/pACYC and T7/J23119/AraC-pBAD configurations.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering and /contribution: soluble fraction of LPMO3706 raised from 54.1% to 81.3% by ImageJ densitometry of SDS-PAGE across vector, chaperone and promoter comparisons, and ancestral variant Anc77 giving 1.923 mg/mL NAG by HPLC, a 47.8% increase over the same-batch enzyme mixture without LPMO.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — conversations with an aquaculture and restaurant operator, a doctor, patients and regulators are reported along with questionnaires, and shaped sourcing and product framing, but the link from a specific conversation to a specific design change is weaker than in the strongest teams.
screen.reason: Real experimental gains with HPLC and densitometry, but the attributions page is empty while the work leans on a host lab's previously isolated marine strain and heavy ASR/MD computation, the results page is empty with all evidence buried in the engineering narrative, and a stray reference to 'caffeine-degradation gene cassettes' on the contribution page signals unreviewed boilerplate. Not top-2 calibre.
screen.field_notes: Ulink-SZ (Biomanufacturing, CHN) engineered LPMO3706, a lytic polysaccharide monooxygenase from a marine bacterium their host laboratory had previously isolated from East China Sea sediment, to work synergistically with chitinases converting shrimp and crab shell chitin into N-acetylglucosamine for osteoarthritis-related use. Five DBTL cycles compared pET-22b, pET-28a and pACYC backbones (soluble fractions 54.1%, 70.7% and 63.2% by ImageJ densitometry at the expected 38.5 kDa), then chaperone co-expression and T7 / J23119 / AraC-pBAD promoters, reaching 81.3% soluble fraction with a pET-22b plus pKJE7 system. Sequence engineering used rational point mutation and ancestral sequence reconstruction; Anc77 produced 1.923 mg/mL NAG by HPLC, 47.8% above the no-LPMO enzyme-mixture control, and the team reports honestly that better docking scores and MD contact persistence did not predict NAG yield. Parts: 11 basic and 15 composite (BBa_26XGWOJA wild type through the Anc120 constructs). The wiki has no results page (all data sits inside the engineering narrative), an empty attributions page, a 110-word hardware page, and a contribution page that mentions caffeine-degradation cassettes unrelated to the project. Human practices covered aquaculture operators, a doctor, patients, regulators and questionnaires; sustainability (6,110 words) and entrepreneurship (4,298 words) pages are substantial.

screen.project_title: SulFlux — engineered BtSULT sulfotransferase to sulfate lithocholic acid for post-cholecystectomy syndrome
screen.what_they_built: A computationally redesigned Bacteroides sulfotransferase (BtSULT variants F147S and F147S/E144D) expressed from pET-28a(+) in E. coli BL21, intended as a probiotic that sulfates lithocholic acid in the gut.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3), pET-28a(+) (KanR, T7, 6xHis, lacI). One Registry part, BBa_26TR5LM8.
screen.best_evidence: /wet-lab.html and notebook: colony PCR bands at ~2 kb for WT and both variants, BCA average purified concentration 238.8 ug/mL (sigma 32.6, standard curve R2~0.95), and SDS-PAGE bands. The 19 Oct entry records visible SDS-PAGE bands and inconclusive TLC; no LCA sulfation or activity was ever measured.
screen.hp_integration: Stakeholder input (gastroenterologist Dr Singh, two patients, Facebook outreach) set convenience and tolerability as priorities and pushed a prebiotic-probiotic delivery idea, but the team's own page states no specific protein-design change came from it.
screen.reason: No engineering, results, parts, experiments or safety pages at all; the functional claim (LCA sulfation) is never demonstrated, the record is a month of failed transformations and failed pUC19 controls, and content is buried in non-standard pages and embedded PDFs. Clearly below finalist calibre.
screen.field_notes: ULP-CA (Renata, USA, Therapeutics) proposed SulFlux, an engineered Bacteroides sulfotransferase (BtSULT, variants F147S and F147S/E144D) delivered as a probiotic to sulfate lithocholic acid and relieve post-cholecystectomy syndrome. The wiki has no engineering, results, experiments, parts or safety page; the lab record lives on non-standard /wet-lab.html and /wet-lab-notebook.html pages plus embedded 19- and 74-page PDFs. Experimental evidence stops at colony PCR bands around 2 kb, BCA protein of ~239 ug/mL and SDS-PAGE bands after His-tag purification; the final 19 October entry reports inconclusive TLC and the team states no LCA sulfation or improved catalysis was established. The June-October chronology is unusually candid about failure: a documented 10-21 August pause, repeated September transformation failures including failed pUC19 controls, unresolved sample-label conflicts and BCA readings described as low or negative. Modelling (3,050 words) covers enzyme redesign and docking comparisons but is not tied to any bench readout. Human Practices is six qualitative engagements (SABPA forum, gastroenterologist Dr Singh, two patients, Facebook outreach, MedChem symposium) that shaped priorities but no documented design change; one Registry part, BBa_26TR5LM8, and an 11-page beginner research guide as the contribution.

screen.project_title: AstraEV — Astragalus-derived nanovesicles carrying quercetin and siKeap1 for UV oxidative skin damage
screen.what_they_built: Plant exosome-like vesicles isolated from Astragalus membranaceus root, loaded with quercetin, paired with an shRNA/siRNA arm targeting Keap1 to de-repress NRF2. Tested in HaCaT keratinocytes (H2O2 challenge) and NIH/3T3 fibroblasts (knockdown).
screen.chassis_and_parts: Mammalian cells (human HaCaT, mouse NIH/3T3) plus plant-derived vesicles — an alternative platform, not E. coli. One Registry part: BBa_26E3H2A3 (pLKO.1-puro-shKeap1, 7,080 bp composite), synthesised and sequence-verified by Sangon Biotech.
screen.best_evidence: /results: siRNA screen in NIH/3T3 at 48 h gave Keap1 remaining expression 0.11 / 0.20 / 0.19 vs 0.92 negative-control siRNA (88.5%, 78.5%, 79.3% knockdown), with ACTB positive-control siRNA at 0.08; the shRNA plasmid gave Keap1 0.34 vs 0.85 lipid-only and HO-1 ~3.5x untreated vs ~1.5x lipid-only. Each is one experiment with 2-3 wells and no biological replicates, and the team says so.
screen.hp_integration: An SJTU-BioX seminar moved them from engineering Astragalus cultivation to post-extraction vesicle engineering and suggested the TCM small-molecule + siKEAP1 pairing, and dermatologist input fixed quercetin as the native molecule; an iGEM white-list rule also pushed the siRNA arm from human to murine Keap1.
screen.reason: Outstanding engineering discipline and the most honest evidence labelling in this batch (H2O2 dose-response recalibration from 400 to 200 uM; candidate siRNA screen with both controls; explicit 'what we are not claiming' boxes). But the central claim — that the Astragalus vesicle delivers either payload — is never demonstrated: siRNA was delivered with Lipofectamine, not vesicles, siRNA was never loaded into vesicles at all, ROS readouts are one image per condition, CCK-8 is raw uncorrected OD from one plate, and the only part is a supplier-made, supplier-verified commercial plasmid. Aspect 2 and aspect 7 are too weak for a top-2 slot.
screen.field_notes: VGA-Pinion (USA, Biomanufacturing village) built AstraEV: exosome-like nanovesicles extracted from Astragalus membranaceus root, loaded with quercetin by sonication, intended as a topical dual-payload treatment for UV-driven oxidative skin damage, with an siRNA against KEAP1 to lift the brake on NRF2. Vesicles were confirmed only by TEM morphology (200 nm scale bars); the team states TEM does not establish identity, loading or size distribution, and that time ran out before siRNA was loaded into vesicles. The strongest data are RT-qPCR: three Keap1 siRNAs in NIH/3T3 at 48 h left 0.11, 0.20 and 0.19 relative expression against 0.92 for the negative control, an ACTB positive control fell to 0.08, and the pLKO.1-puro-shKeap1 plasmid (BBa_26E3H2A3, their only Registry part, synthesised and sequence-verified by Sangon) left Keap1 at 0.34 while raising HO-1 to ~3.5x. An engineering cycle recalibrated the H2O2 challenge from a literature 400 uM to 200 uM using their own gradient (0/200/400/800 uM giving 100%, 59.3%, 49.9%, 37.4% viability), after which free quercetin went from 94.1% to 10.7% of the H2O2-only ROS signal — a textbook demonstration of an uninformative result versus a negative one. Everything is single-run with no biological replicates, no Western blot and no statistics, all stated plainly on the wiki. Human practices is thin but traceable (SJTU-BioX seminar reshaped the design; an iGEM white-list ruling moved the siRNA target to murine Keap1). Two models (an ODE-style Model 1 and a 3D PhysiCell/BioFVM tissue model labelled 'conceptual instrument, no calibrated model') and a sources page reproducing team transcripts; AI writing assistance is disclosed on the attributions page.

screen.project_title: Cadture — metallothionein-augmented cadmium biosensor/bioaccumulator
screen.what_they_built: Eight constructs built on the existing pMH45 CadR.10 cadmium-responsive GFP biosensor, adding four metallothioneins either surface-displayed via Lpp-OmpA (pVIS1-4) or expressed cytoplasmically (pVIS5-8), on the hypothesis that MT binding lowers free Cd2+ and therefore lowers GFP output.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli EK317; pMH45 backbone modified by inverse PCR, DpnI, digestion and ligation. Metallothioneins IaMT2 (water spinach), SmtA (S. elongatus PCC 7942), EGR_09832 and OsMTI-1b (rice, from a 2024 iGEM design). Only one BBa ID found anywhere on the wiki (BBa_26KDUZNI) and the parts page is empty.
screen.best_evidence: /results: baseline-corrected GFP per OD600 across 0, 8, 40, 200, 300 and 400 nM Cd2+ plus ~11 h time courses, with working positive (pYC08, ~5,800) and negative (pTK03) controls. At 400 nM the parent pMH45 reads ~1,550 while pVIS1-4 read ~680, 470, 600 and 830 and stay concentration-dependent; the cytoplasmic pVIS5-8 all stay below ~100. The team states clearly that this is an indirect proxy — no cadmium was ever measured directly and ICP-MS is listed as future work.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, modestly — Professor Hung-Yu Lai's advice added the surface-versus-cytoplasm localisation comparison that became cycle 2, set the cadmium concentration range, and added bacterial viability as an evaluation metric; water-treatment and industry visits repositioned the system as complementary to existing treatment rather than a replacement.
screen.reason: A clean, well-controlled two-cycle experiment with real dose-response and time-course data and a genuinely interesting finding — that the capture and detection functions antagonise each other, which the team identifies as a design flaw rather than a win. But the central claim (cadmium removal) is never measured: lower GFP is consistent with MT binding and with several other explanations, including burden from expressing a second protein, and no empty-anchor or non-binding-MT control rules those out. Only one registered part and an empty parts page also sink aspect 8.
screen.field_notes: VIS (Taipei, Bioremediation) built Cadture, adding metallothioneins to the existing pMH45 CadR.10 cadmium-responsive GFP biosensor in E. coli EK317 to turn a sensor into a sensor-plus-bioaccumulator. Cycle 1 surface-displayed four MTs (IaMT2, SmtA, EGR_09832, OsMTI-1b) on Lpp-OmpA as pVIS1-4; cycle 2 moved the same four into the cytoplasm as pVIS5-8. Readout is GFP per OD600 across 0-400 nM Cd2+ with ~11 h time courses and working positive/negative controls. At 400 nM the parent pMH45 gives ~1,550 while surface constructs give ~470-830 and stay dose-responsive, and cytoplasmic constructs collapse below ~100 — from which the team draws the honest conclusion that bioaccumulation and detection interfere, since binding cadmium removes the very signal the sensor needs. They state explicitly that reduced fluorescence is an indirect proxy and that ICP-MS is required to show actual capture; the description page also flags that only steps 1-2 of the five-step design were implemented and direct Cd binding was never measured. Dry lab contributes a 5.8k-word Cd-removal model and a 1.4k-word measurement page. Human practices spans a water treatment plant, the farmers' association, Zhao Lian Industry and Professor Hung-Yu Lai, whose advice generated the localisation comparison. Documentation gap: parts page is empty and only one BBa ID (BBa_26KDUZNI) appears anywhere; attributions defer entirely to the embedded iGEM form.

screen.project_title: An ultrasound-reporting probiotic AND gate for early colorectal cancer screening
screen.what_they_built: An engineered E. coli designed to express acoustic reporter gas vesicles only when it senses both lactate (tumour metabolism) and nitrate (host inflammation), via a sigma-54 hrpR/hrpS to PhrpL AND gate, so a tumour becomes visible on a clinical ultrasound scan. Everything built and tested this year is in vitro.
screen.chassis_and_parts: MG1655 as device chassis, DH5a as assay host, BL21(DE3) for the Phase 0 gas vesicle control; pTwist Chlor medium copy and pTwist Kan backbones, pSC101 for the output module; bARGSer operon from Addgene #192473, first-generation ARG1 from #106473. Registry: BBa_26TCX3UM (trimmed PyeaR, 146 bp, characterisation published), BBa_26CQNUIL (RBS_sfGFP_med) and composite BBa_26BQEN31; two further parts withdrawn as duplicates of BBa_K3425031 and BBa_I2054.
screen.best_evidence: /results P2: a nine-point KNO3 ladder (0-16 mM) on pSense-Nit-dual in DH5a under anaerobic induction, read by ONPG/Miller, giving means of 42.6 MU at 0 mM rising to 162.7 MU at 2 mM (3.82-fold) and 311-340 MU at 8-16 mM, with the page stating exactly which six of twenty-seven tubes were never assayed and why n is 2 at most points. Phase 0 on /results shows 1.8-2.7-fold dose-dependent contrast-enhanced ultrasound signal from ARG1 gas vesicles across two independent gel phantoms on a Philips Affiniti 70 — but on a superseded construct, with collapse-based difference imaging explicitly not demonstrated. The lactate arm was flat at every dose and the two-input gate ran twice (13 and 18 October) with no call either time.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, decisively: Dr. Luo Shao-Chiao redefined the output as a binary triage call and killed the tumour-adhesion and spatial-localisation scope, then secured the Philips Affiniti 70 that made any imaging possible; Dr. Huang Yi-Lin's scepticism that the colon lumen is already anoxic, acidic and lactate-rich forced the specificity argument; a biosecurity flag replaced a deoxycholate sensor with host-native nitrate sensing, which also shrank the circuit; and public plus staff surveys tested the willingness-to-use premise.
screen.reason: Engineering discipline and documentation at a level rarely seen from a high school team: eighteen numbered cycles including ones that rejected the team's own hypothesis, pre-registered acceptance criteria, an explicit Done/Planned/Inconclusive/Superseded label on every claim, retracted claims named as retracted, and a parts-provenance rule drawn from five concrete labelling failures. The integrated device does not work — one of two sensor arms is flat and the gate returned no call — so aspect 2 is weak, and the panel must decide whether exemplary aspects 4, 5, 7 and 8 plus a near-exemplary wiki outweigh that. Worth the full read precisely because that trade-off is the judgement call.
screen.field_notes: WIST (TWN, Diagnostics) proposed an ingestible engineered E. coli that expresses acoustic reporter gas vesicles only when a sigma-54 AND gate (hrpR/hrpS to PhrpL) sees lactate and nitrate together, giving an ultrasound-visible early colorectal cancer prescreen aimed at the three groups Taiwan's FIT programme loses: non-collectors, positives who skip colonoscopy, and adults under 45, in whom incidence rose 3.5% a year from 1994-2018. Of eighteen DBTL cycles, seven are written in full: Cycle 7 killed an already-synthesised three-input pH/hypoxia/lactate gate found default-ON in healthy tissue and established the standing rule that no input may leave the output default-ON; Cycle 11 swapped an off-White-List deoxycholate sensor for a host-native PyeaR nitrate sensor; Cycle 14 blamed a flat lactate arm on an under-expressed lldR and redesigned its RBS; Cycle 15 tested that redesign, found the arm still flat, and concluded the gate's fold change is bounded by its own OFF state — the team flags this as the one cycle where their own hypothesis was specific enough to be rejected. The nitrate arm passes a pre-set acceptance criterion with a nine-point Miller-unit ladder (42.6 MU at 0 mM to 162.7 MU at 2 mM, 3.82-fold; 311-340 MU at 8-16 mM) and the page itself documents the six unassayed tubes and the reduced n. Phase 0 obtained 1.8-2.7-fold ultrasound contrast from first-generation ARG1 gas vesicles in agarose phantoms on a clinical Philips Affiniti 70 brought to the school by Philips, but on a superseded construct and without demonstrating collapse-based specificity. Three Registry parts cleared, two withdrawn as exact duplicates of existing entries, and the composite is reported as RFC 10 and RFC 1000 incompatible because of inherited EcoRI and SapI sites. The standout contribution is a downloadable parts-verification tool plus the primary-source rule behind it, distilled from five real labelling failures including a B0032 label on a B0034 sequence across ten places in six files. The wiki is scrupulous about what is Done, Planned, Inconclusive or Superseded, names retracted claims, and states that no integrated-device data exists.

screen.project_title: ReLeaf: five Pichia pastoris strains converting garden and agricultural waste to bioethanol
screen.what_they_built: Secreted five lignocellulose enzymes (laccase LccPo1, endoglucanase Cel5A, cellobiohydrolase CBH2, beta-glucosidase Bgl1, xylanase Xyn10A) from Pichia pastoris GS115, with a his4 auxotrophy strategy, plus a solar-powered Arduino fermentation monitor logging temperature, humidity, specific gravity and pH.
screen.chassis_and_parts: P. pastoris GS115, pPIC9K with AOX1 promoter, alpha-factor secretion signal and C-terminal 6xHis; seven Registry records for the five enzyme CDSs, the shared expression cassette and the his4 modification.
screen.best_evidence: /results and /proof-of-concept: colony PCR at expected sizes, anti-His Western blots at 57.7, 48.9, 51.4, 95 and 33.7 kDa, and laccase activity of 1.66 U/mL by ABTS at pH 4.5, 50 C after 10 days induction; xylan and Avicel hydrolysis assays with pooled supernatants. Many figures render as 'Media unavailable'.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — three-phase HP with documented pivots after expert criticism, but the engineering page does not show how any of it changed a build.
screen.reason: Five secreted enzymes verified by Western blot with one real activity number is respectable medal work, but the engineering page is a 360-word template reading 'Awaiting evidence', the model page is entirely placeholder, attributions is a link to an external form, and the key gel and blot figures do not load. The full process from garden waste to ethanol is unproven by the team's own admission.
screen.field_notes: WLSA-ShanghaiAcademy (Bioremediation, CHN) proposed ReLeaf, converting fallen leaves, branches and straw into bioethanol instead of burning or landfilling them. Five enzyme genes (lccpo1, cel5a, cbh2, bgl1, xyn10a) were expressed separately in Pichia pastoris GS115 from pPIC9K with the AOX1 promoter, alpha-factor signal and 6xHis tag; colony PCR hit expected sizes (1630, 1819, 1480, 1195, 2866 bp) and anti-His Western blots detected secreted protein at 57.7, 48.9, 51.4, 95 and 33.7 kDa, with clone-to-clone differences kept visible (CEL5A-2 and bgl1-2 failed). The one firm activity figure is laccase at 1.66 U/mL on ABTS, pH 4.5, 50 C after 10 days of 0.5% methanol induction at 20 C; xylan and Avicel assays used pooled supernatants from the three separately produced cellulases. The team states the full waste-to-ethanol process remains unproven. Dry lab contributes a solar-powered Arduino Mega fermentation monitor (temperature, humidity, specific gravity to ABV, pH) with wiring, bill of materials and a 48-hour dataset, plus open firmware and an interactive temperature-control demo. Serious documentation gaps: the engineering and model pages are unfilled templates saying 'Awaiting evidence', attributions is only a link to the official iGEM form, and many result figures show as 'Media unavailable'.

screen.project_title: AirNova: engineered multi-enzyme deodorising spray with smart atomiser
screen.what_they_built: E. coli-expressed enzyme cocktail (carboxylesterase BioH, laccase CotA, manganese catalase MCat) formulated at pH 7.2 as a cell-free spray that degrades malodour molecules on textiles, paired with an ESP32-S3 sensor-driven atomiser.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and SHuffle T7 Express lysY, pET-28a; 10 enzyme CDS parts listed on /parts (BBa_2656LJ24 BioH, BBa_267SX8YQ CotA, BBa_26M4ZK3J MCat, BBa_26VFK36H AoSOX1, BBa_26Q4CRJK QSOX1, BBa_26VBPDCN MAO-B, BBa_2668O85P MAO-N-D5, BBa_26NO2QHC HdMto, BBa_26ZRUZMT TynA) plus characterisation of existing BBa_K137000 KatE; Best Part Collection = BioH+CotA+MCat mixture.
screen.best_evidence: /parts: sensory deodorisation to ISO 17299/GB-T 33610 with a blinded panel — malodour scores down 44% organic decay (Wilcoxon p=0.0068), 61% cigarette smoke (p=0.004), 49% mixed (p=0.0029), with corresponding estimated odorant reductions 73/68/70%. /engineering and /contribution: KatE activity 2592.7 U/mL vs 4.31 U/mL empty-vector control by titanium sulfate OD410, standard curves R²>0.997.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — a biosafety expert's warning about E. coli endotoxin inhalation forced the pivot from a live-bacterial spray to a cell-free enzyme formulation, and a protein-expression expert's advice drove the switch to prokaryotic enzymes and lower induction temperature after two failed cycles.
screen.reason: Three genuine DBTL cycles in which two failed (eukaryotic SOX/MAO enzymes inactive in BL21 and SHuffle, with the negative assay data shown) before a successful prokaryotic redesign, then a composite enzyme product tested against national/international deodorisation standards with p-values. Quantitative part characterisation, hardware, and strong stakeholder-driven redesign. Weaknesses a full read must check: the /attributions page is empty (aspect 6 unverifiable), /results and /measurement are empty so evidence is scattered on /engineering and /parts, the product table mixes TynA and CotA in the described mixture, and 'estimated chemical odorant reduction' is inferred from sensory scores rather than measured by GC. Still plausibly top-of-field for HS.
screen.field_notes: Worldshaper-Hangzhou (Bioremediation, China) built AirNova, a cell-free enzymatic deodorising spray for enclosed public spaces such as nursing homes, hotels, transit and pet clinics. They expressed candidate enzymes in E. coli and documented two failed DBTL cycles: eukaryotic sulfhydryl oxidases (AoSOX1, QSOX1) and monoamine oxidases (MAO-B, MAO-N-D5) expressed but showed no activity in BL21 or in the oxidising SHuffle T7 cytoplasm, shown by DTNB (OD412) and titanium-sulfate (OD410) assays with linear standard curves. Cycle 3 switched to prokaryotic enzymes and obtained active BioH carboxylesterase, CotA laccase and MCat manganese catalase; existing BioBrick KatE (BBa_K137000) was quantitatively characterised at 2592.7 U/mL against 4.31 U/mL background. The BioH/CotA/MCat mixture in pH 7.2 buffer gave blinded sensory deodorisation of 44-61% across organic decay, cigarette smoke and mixed odours (Wilcoxon p=0.003-0.007) using ISO 17299:2014 and GB/T 33610-2019 methods. Hardware is an ESP32-S3 ultrasonic atomiser with air-quality, climate and IMU sensors and five operating modes, developed over three design iterations. Human practices (342-respondent survey, respiratory physicians, a biosafety expert, an OEM manufacturer) drove the live-cell-to-cell-free pivot and the sensor-triggered misting design; the wiki has a large entrepreneurship section but an empty attributions page.

screen.project_title: BlackNova — polydopamine biological hair dye from engineered E. coli
screen.what_they_built: Engineered E. coli producing dopamine from L-DOPA (and attempted from L-tyrosine), with a designed keratin-binding peptide PepACS and laccase-driven in situ polymerisation of polydopamine on hair, formulated as a three-part zero-live-organism dye kit.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) / pET-28a. Ten parts listed: new basics DmDDC (BBa_266O3UZY), SsDDC (BBa_26MJWS8Z), PepACS (BBa_263FLW0N); composites HpaBC, DmDDC-HpaBC, SsDDC-HpaBC, sfGFP-PepACS; existing HpaB, HpaC and sfGFP (BBa_I746916, re-characterised).
screen.best_evidence: /engineering and /parts: whole-cell biocatalysis with DmDDC converted 25.74–102.96 g/L L-DOPA to 18.44, 39.33, 60.88 and 78.37 g/L dopamine (92.2–101.5% molar conversion), quantified by a TLC-densitometry method they built (ImageJ, non-linear curve, R2 = 0.9992, 1.25–100 g/L). Yak hair dyed with CotA laccase at 0.9 U/mL matched a commercial dye visually and showed no visible fading after 5 and 10 detergent washes.
screen.hp_integration: Yes. Prof. Xufen Zhu diagnosed the failed one-step in vivo synthesis as metabolic resource competition and recommended decoupling growth from catalysis; the team rebuilt the process as two-stage whole-cell biocatalysis, which is what produced the 78.37 g/L titer. Biomanufacturing input also replaced all-in-one lyophilisation with the three-part kit.
screen.reason: A high-school team that made a functioning new part and showed it working quantitatively: near-complete molar conversion to 78.37 g/L dopamine, a novel assay developed to get around a real measurement problem, and a product-level demonstration (dyed hair, wash fastness, commercial comparator). Five DBTL cycles including two honest failures. Worth a full read, with two things for the panel to probe: the results, experiments, measurement and attributions pages are all empty, so every result lives inside the engineering narrative, and conversions above 100% suggest the TLC quantification needs scrutiny.
screen.field_notes: Worldshaper-HZ (CHN, Fashion & Cosmetics village) built BlackNova, a polydopamine hair dye intended to replace p-phenylenediamine chemistry. E. coli BL21(DE3)/pET-28a expresses DOPA decarboxylase from Drosophila (DmDDC) or pig (SsDDC); hpaBC was added to try to start from cheap L-tyrosine. Cycle 1 (in-culture conversion) failed because growing cells consumed L-DOPA and precipitating polydopamine broke NanoDrop reads. Cycle 2 fixed both: resting whole-cell biocatalysis plus a TLC-densitometry assay (FeCl3 stain, ImageJ lane profiles, non-linear fit with R2 = 0.9992) quantifying dopamine from 1.25 to 100 g/L. DmDDC then gave 18.44/39.33/60.88/78.37 g/L dopamine from 25.74/51.48/77.22/102.96 g/L L-DOPA — 92.2%, 98.3%, 101.5% and 98.0% molar conversion, the top titer near the solubility limit of dopamine HCl; SsDDC was poor. Cycle 3 added hpaBC and produced nothing from L-tyrosine, and SDS-PAGE could not resolve the problem because HpaB and DDC differ by under 3 kDa. Application data: white yak hair compared across water control, tyrosinase at 100 and 10 U/mL, CotA laccase at 0.9 U/mL and a commercial dye, with no visible fading after 5 or 10 detergent washes; an sfGFP-PepACS fusion anchors the dye to keratin and gave A510 = 0.93 as a characterisation of the existing part BBa_I746916. Human practices is genuinely integrated: a molecular biology professor's advice produced the whole-cell switch, a dermatologist shaped the safety and labelling roadmap, and toxicologists set an NMPA non-animal RHE/Franz-cell testing route; survey of 501 dye consumers. Caveats for a full read: no results, experiments, measurement or attributions page exists (word counts are zero), replicate structure for the titers is not stated, >100% conversion is unexplained, and quantification rests on TLC densitometry rather than HPLC.

screen.project_title: Whole-cell biosynthesis of L-carnosine for sarcopenia
screen.what_they_built: An engineered E. coli BL21(DE3) whole-cell catalyst converting beta-alanine and L-histidine to L-carnosine, improved through marine-enzyme homology mining, ancestral sequence reconstruction, structure-guided double mutation, a yeaS efflux knockout, and vector swap — plus a pharmacokinetic model of a four-layer oral nanocarrier.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and BL21(DE3) delta-yeaS; pET-28a and pET-22b. 11 parts: five natural PepD candidates (hypepd2/8/19/23/24), the reconstructed AncSE, single mutants I218H and L430H, the I218H/L430H double mutant, a yeaS sgRNA cassette and a yeaS repair donor (CRISPR via pEcCas/pEcgRNA).
screen.best_evidence: /part and /model: HPLC time courses at 0/1/2/4/6 h across five matched DBTL cycles — the I218H/L430H double mutant reached ~2.16x wild-type carnosine in the same cycle, yeaS deletion was verified by amplicon shift (1,782 to 1,143 bp), and the final pET-22b / double mutant / delta-yeaS strain reached 1.42 g/L at 6 h versus 1.15 g/L for pET-28a (+23.5%), with SDS-PAGE showing a stronger recombinant band.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — Ms. Liu (Boji Biotechnology) raised carnosinase degradation and delivery, which opened the multilayer-carrier research direction and the PK model, and a pharma professional's point that adult children are the buyers reshaped the business plan; the core enzyme engineering was not redirected by stakeholders.
screen.reason: The wet-lab science is the cleanest kind in this batch — five matched-control cycles with HPLC titres, a real knockout verified by amplicon size, and models that each hand a decision to the bench. But the wiki is half-finished: /engineering, /results and /contribution are empty, and /experiments and /attributions are still filled with placeholder passages from The Winter's Tale plus 'Team entry pending', with a line crediting Codex/OpenAI for wiki tooling. Worth a full read only to see whether the panel can establish what the students actually did; as published, aspect 6 is unverifiable and the wiki would drag the weighted average down hard.
screen.field_notes: Worldshaper-Nanjing (Biomanufacturing, China) made L-carnosine for age-related sarcopenia by whole-cell reverse hydrolysis in E. coli BL21(DE3). Five PepD-family candidates were mined from a marine-microorganism protein database supplied by Nanjing Tech University; hypepd23 won on titre, an ancestral reconstruction (AncSE) was built and lost to it, and structure-guided mutagenesis gave I218H/L430H at ~2.16x WT. Deleting the yeaS amino-acid exporter with pEcCas/pEcgRNA and switching pET-28a to pET-22b brought the final strain to 1.42 g/L at 6 h, all measured by same-cycle HPLC with matched controls. The model page is unusually disciplined about what each module can and cannot claim, and includes MD of the dual-substrate complex plus a compartmental PK model with sensitivity analysis for a four-layer oral nanocarrier (no animal work, per iGEM policy). HP covered 225 questionnaires from adults 60+, an eldercare home, and peer teams. The published wiki is incomplete: results, engineering and contribution pages are blank, and the experiments and attributions pages still carry Shakespeare placeholder text, so student-versus-supervisor attribution cannot be judged.

screen.project_title: SweetCycle: engineered glycosyltransferases for Rebaudioside M in Stevia hairy roots
screen.what_they_built: Rationally designed variants of the Stevia glycosyltransferases SrUGT76G1 and SrUGT91D2 (AlphaFold3/Boltz-2 ternary complexes, LigandMPNN redesign, chalcogen-bond screen), expressed first transiently in Nicotiana benthamiana and then in Stevia rebaudiana hairy roots, scored by HPLC for Reb M content.
screen.chassis_and_parts: N. benthamiana transient (A. tumefaciens GV3101) and S. rebaudiana hairy roots (A. rhizogenes K599), pCAMBIA1300-AtUBQ10-UGT-NOS. Ten basic parts: two parental CDSs plus eight variants, nominated part SrUGT76G T284I (BBa_26YB81CQ).
screen.best_evidence: /parts and /contribution: in Stevia hairy roots, SrUGT76G1 T284I gave 21.96 ug/g FW Reb M and T284S 19.65 ug/g versus 15.44 ug/g for wild type (1.42x and 1.27x). The earlier tobacco screen is reported as a null result (T284I 21.09 vs WT 18.52 ug/g) and the team states the displayed statistics use an assumed CV of 5% rather than independent biological replicates.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, strongly: the iGEM high-school whitelist forced abandonment of their intended plant chassis for a contained hairy-root system; a baking-sector visit showed sucrose supplies bulk/browning/water retention and permanently removed baking as an application and changed the goal from 'sweeter' to raising the Reb D + Reb M share; a stevia grower's economics made 'yield must not fall' a hard requirement and killed a straw-hydrolysis module; a plant synthetic biologist's reading of their null tobacco result is why hairy roots are presented as the answer rather than a fallback.
screen.reason: Outstanding Human Practices - genuinely decision-changing, including letting a competition rule improve the design - plus a clean two-cycle story with an honestly reported null first cycle and ten well-documented parts with a nominated best part. The reason it is only borderline is aspect 2: the headline 1.42x is a single hairy-root panel with no independent clones or biological replicates (the team says so itself and shows statistics computed from an assumed 5% CV), so 'it worked' is not yet established. Worth a full read for HP and Parts; the finalist case rests on whether judges accept the Reb M data.
screen.field_notes: Worldshaper-Shanghai (Agriculture village) ran SweetCycle, engineering the late Stevia glycosyltransferases SrUGT91D2 (Reb A to Reb D) and SrUGT76G1 (Reb D to Reb M) to raise the share of the sucrose-like sweetener Reb M. Design used AlphaFold3/Boltz-2 ternary complexes with explicit glycosidic connectivity, LigandMPNN redesign at T=0.1 around the acceptor pocket, and a sulfur chalcogen-bond geometry filter, giving six designed plus two literature variants. Cycle 1 in Nicotiana benthamiana detected transcripts by qPCR but gave no significant Reb M gain (T284I 21.09 vs WT 18.52 ug/g FW) - reported as a null result. Cycle 2 in Stevia hairy roots (A. rhizogenes K599, hygromycin marker confirmed by PCR) gave T284S 19.65 and T284I 21.96 ug/g FW against WT 15.44 (1.27x, 1.42x); the SrUGT91D2 variants showed no improvement. The team flags that there are no independent clones or biological replicates and that error bars come from an assumed 5% CV. Ten basic parts are registered with design, experiment, characterization, application and discussion documents; BBa_26YB81CQ (T284I) is the nominated new basic part. HP is exceptional: a 503-person survey, clinicians, an industry association head, a stevia grower, a fermentation engineer and beverage R&D, plus the whitelist rule that forced the chassis change. The standard /results page is left as unedited iGEM template text.

screen.project_title: AdipoSense — dual-metabolite-sensing engineered probiotic for obesity
screen.what_they_built: An E. coli Nissle 1917 circuit that senses gut succinate (PcaR/PcaO) and butyrate (HpdR/pHpdH inverted through a cI-LVA NOT gate) and fires an AND gate driving GFP and the Arabidopsis acyltransferase At1g78690p intended to make NAPE-related lipids.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5α for cloning, E. coli Nissle 1917 as chassis, pSB1C3 backbone (7228 bp, 5158 bp insert, four transcription units) by Gibson assembly. Eleven new parts including BBa_26LR3FRM (PcaR), BBa_26JDWRHF (HpdR R18C), BBa_26II0PJK (At1g78690) and composite BBa_2644WFNC, built on BNDS-China 2024's BBa_K5127014 and standard BBa_J23105/B0034/B0015/R0051.
screen.best_evidence: /results: succinate dose-response in EcN fitted to bottom 50.0 ± 4.2, top 665.0 ± 25.1 a.u., EC50 0.15 g/L, Hill 2.15 ± 0.12, 13.3-fold maximum induction; inverted butyrate response IC50 0.50 mM with 12.7-fold repression; the four-condition AND table (A 51.2 ± 3.7, B 58.5 ± 4.5, C 62.1 ± 4.1, D 612.4 ± 28.3) giving ~10-fold ON/OFF; and a 12.6% lower final OD600 for induced engineered EcN.
screen.hp_integration: Partly — public consultation and Dr Qijin Wang's questions about weight regain and misuse by healthy people pushed them from a constitutive therapeutic to conditional sensing, and the iGEM Safety and Security Committee forced removal of the Edwardsiella EseO/EseP effectors, after which they adopted the literature NAPE route.
screen.reason: The sensor and logic data are real and respectably quantified for a high school team, but the wiki is unfinished in ways that matter: the Model page and the Experiments page are both literal template placeholder text ("Reserved for the first subtopic in this page"), the attributions page is empty, and the home page displays Silver/Gold/Bronze award labels for criteria the team has not been awarded. The therapeutic output is unvalidated — no NAPE was identified, only candidate SDS-PAGE bands — and nothing was tested in any physiological model. Not a top-2 profile.
screen.field_notes: Shanghai high school team (WorldShaper-SHMed, Therapeutics village) building a conditional obesity probiotic on E. coli Nissle 1917. The circuit is four transcription units in pSB1C3: constitutive PcaR, constitutive HpdR, an HpdR-responsive cI-LVA inverter, and a tandem PpPcaO/pLam output driving At1g78690 and GFP. They switched from T4 ligation to Gibson after low efficiency, and raised EcN electroporation yield from three colonies to ~50 by five washes and 2.5 kV. Characterisation is GFP/OD600 on a plate reader: succinate EC50 0.15 g/L with Hill 2.15 and 13.3-fold induction, inverted butyrate IC50 0.50 mM with 12.7-fold repression, cross-reactivity tested against acetate, propionate, malate and fumarate at 2 mM, a four-condition AND truth table at ~10-fold ON/OFF, a time course plateauing at 650-670 a.u. between 8 and 12 h, and a 12.6% growth cost. The butyrate branch extends BNDS-China 2024's BBa_K5127014 into a new chassis, which is a legitimate contribution. The output module is the weak link: only candidate 31.35 kDa and 27 kDa SDS-PAGE bands, with the team itself stating that NAPE identification and quantification remain next steps. Safety work is thorough and includes the Safety and Security Committee's required removal of the Edwardsiella piscicida effectors. The Model and Experiments pages were never filled in.

screen.project_title: ReNovo: whole-cell urinary gentisic acid biosensor for renal cell carcinoma screening
screen.what_they_built: A gentisic-acid-responsive E. coli biosensor based on the Cupriavidus necator gtd system (GtdR regulator, GtdA dioxygenase, PgtdA promoter) driving mCherry, paired with a colorimetric Jaffe creatinine assay for dilution normalisation, and a single-use microfluidic chip plus reusable optical enclosure to run both assays outside a lab.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a for cloning, Rosetta (DE3) for expression; pUC57-mini backbone, Gibson assembly. Only 5 BBa parts registered (BBa_26746FMZ, 26MVH8SY, 26NDGDFL, 26Q6L5TL, 26RWRRI3).
screen.best_evidence: /results Part 2: the second-generation PG2 sensor (gtdT deleted) gave a linear mCherry response over 0-12 uM gentisic acid, R2 = 0.9764, replacing the first-generation pGM's non-monotonic curve that peaked near 2 uM. /results Part 3: no matrix effect in artificial urine (two-way ANOVA, concentration p < 0.0001, matrix p = 0.639), no reciprocal interference between the two assays (p = 0.4463 and p = 0.9837), and specificity against 2-HBA, 3-HBA, 4-HBA and salicyluric acid.
screen.hp_integration: Yes, and traceably: 19 stakeholders mapped to specific sections. Dr Gu recommended creatinine correction, which created the normalisation module; Dr Tengfei Hu proposed excising gtdT to remove transporter-driven burden, which is exactly the Cycle 2 redesign that produced the linear response; Dr Christina Feng's cold-chain objection drove freeze-drying in the hardware plan.
screen.reason: The cleanest failure-diagnosis-redesign story in the batch: a non-monotonic first-generation sensor, BCA and SDS-PAGE diagnostics, an expert-suggested hypothesis about transporter burden, gtdT excision, and a linear response as the result. Specificity, matrix tolerance and cross-assay interference are all tested with stated statistics, and the hardware is worked through to BOM level. Held back by only five Registry parts, no patient urine, and an unclear match between the 0-12 uM working range and clinically relevant urinary gentisic acid. Worth a full read, probably just below the top.
screen.field_notes: WUXI-DSAS (CHN, Diagnostics) built ReNovo, a whole-cell E. coli biosensor for urinary gentisic acid as a non-invasive renal cell carcinoma pre-screen. The circuit adapts the maleylpyruvate-responsive gtd system of Cupriavidus necator: GtdA converts gentisic acid to 3-maleylpyruvate, which activates GtdR and drives mCherry from PgtdA; mCherry was chosen over GFP because urine autofluoresces green. The first-generation pGM (gtdR-gtdA-gtdT-mCherry, 6223 bp, Gibson-assembled into pUC57-mini, verified by colony PCR, EcoRI/BamHI digest and long-read sequencing) responded but peaked near 2 uM and then declined; BCA and SDS-PAGE diagnostics plus two expert consultations pointed to GtdT-mediated uptake and metabolic burden, so gtdT was excised with XhoI to give PG2 (4876 bp), which is linear over 0-12 uM with R2 = 0.9764. Further cycles established a Jaffe creatinine assay for dilution normalisation (R2 = 0.98), showed no reciprocal interference between the biological and chemical assays, matched slopes in artificial urine versus control (two-way ANOVA matrix p = 0.639), demonstrated specificity against three hydroxybenzoic acid isomers and salicyluric acid, and used fluorescence microscopy to show that bulk signal tracks the fraction of responding cells (exponential fit R2 = 0.9954) - an honest caveat about the readout. Hardware is a 9.4k-word design for a single-use microfluidic chip plus reusable enclosure covering metering, dilution, thermal control, dual-channel optics, normalisation, a risk-report mini-program, biosafety containment and costed BOM. 19 stakeholder interviews mapped section by section; a dedicated AI Usage page. Only five BBa parts; no patient samples tested.

screen.project_title: Light-activated engineered subtilisin E for degrading the cat allergen Fel d 1
screen.what_they_built: An optogenetically gated protease: subtilisin E engineered for better Fel d 1 cleavage and caged with an AsLOV2 domain plus an inhibitory pseudo-substrate peptide, so the enzyme stays off in the dark and switches on under 450 nm blue light, delivered as a spray with an LED reaction kit.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with pET28a and pACYCDuet; pelB secretion signal, SUMO solubility tag; ~26 new BBa parts in a part collection (SubE WT, N218S, G166S, Q103E, N155D, the N155D/G166S/N218S triple mutant, and SubE-LOV2 fusions with varied insertion site and G4S linker length).
screen.best_evidence: /results Parts 3-5: Fel d 1 ELISA with a validated standard curve (R2 >= 0.99) shows all SubE variants significantly reduce residual Fel d 1 versus control, with N155D the strongest; the light-controlled fusion pelB-SUMO-SubE48-LOV2-(G4S)3-LVPFARGEST-(G4S)3-SubE shows a marked drop in residual Fel d 1 after 10 min of 450 nm light versus both the no-enzyme and dark controls; a fabric model with Fel d 1 deposited, sprayed and extracted quantifies residual allergen.
screen.hp_integration: Yes - Prof. Qin Zhen's advice to use a solubility tag rather than dialysis refolding produced the SUMO construct that rescued the inclusion-body failure, and Dr. Zhou Yang's advice drove the AlphaFold3 insertion-site/linker screen; a five-stage HP programme (allergist, vet, cat cafe, pet-service firms, manufacturers, VC) shaped the spray format and market plan.
screen.reason: The clearest working system in this batch: a measured functional output (ELISA-quantified Fel d 1 degradation) with negative, dark and scramble-equivalent controls, a mutant panel that picked a winner, a working dark-off/light-on switch, and an application test on fabric with hardware. Failure (inclusion bodies) is documented and fixed through a named expert's advice. Deserves a full read; check statistics, replication and the missing Attributions page.
screen.field_notes: YHA-HWFLA (Biomanufacturing village, China) engineered subtilisin E to degrade the cat allergen Fel d 1 under blue-light control, motivated by a teammate's cat allergy. Cycle 1 failed - pelB-SubE-WT went into inclusion bodies - and after interviewing Prof. Qin Zhen they added a SUMO tag, recovering soluble 41.9 kDa protein (BCA 1.83 mg/mL, confirmed by SDS-PAGE and Ni-NTA elution). Cycle 2 screened literature-guided mutants N218S, G166S, Q103E, N155D and a triple mutant, each checked for fold disruption by AlphaFold3 and assayed against Fel d 1 by ELISA, with N155D giving the largest reduction. Cycle 3 inserted AsLOV2 plus the inhibitory peptide LVPFARGEST at residue 48 or 160 with G4Sx1 or G4Sx3 linkers; the chosen fusion showed significantly lower residual Fel d 1 after 10 min at 450 nm than either the no-enzyme or dark controls, i.e. a working dark-off/light-on protease. They then built an LED blue-light reaction kit and tested the sprayed, pre-activated enzyme on Fel d 1-coated fabric with extraction and quantification. Roughly 26 new parts are collected on a part-collection page; HP ran five structured stages from allergist and veterinarian through manufacturing and VC interviews. There is no Attributions page in the crawl, so student-versus-outside execution cannot be checked from the wiki.

screen.project_title: MirUro: cell-free toehold-switch biosensor for urinary miRNA detection in bladder cancer
screen.what_they_built: Toehold-switch RNA biosensors (one-, two- and three-input cascaded AND gates) driving EGFP, triggered by miR-21-5p, miR-146a-5p and miR-205-5p, validated in E. coli and in a cell-free TXTL reaction as a step toward a paper strip.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli DH5a/BL21(DE3); pET28a-miTH-EGFP switches, pET15b-miR-1 and pCDFDuet-miR-2 trigger plasmids (synthesised by Wuhan Miaoling). ~12 new BBa parts plus reused BBa_K3577000, BBa_K4611011, BBa_K5038020, BBa_K5106007.
screen.best_evidence: /engineering Cycle 1: miTH-1 + trigger + IPTG gives ~25.7M RFU vs ~2.4M for switch alone (10.6-fold), with no-IPTG and single-plasmid controls; cell-free tubes fluoresce only in positive control and matched pair; standard curve y=2e6x-1e7, R2=0.9804 over 0-200 ng trigger plasmid. Trigger plasmids validated by miRNA-qPCR (80-150-fold overexpression).
screen.hp_integration: Very extensive HP (11.8k words, ~10 clinician/industry interviews, care-home and patient visits, feedback-to-design matrix), but from the screening pack the recorded effects are mostly on framing, usability and roadmap rather than on circuit design.
screen.reason: The engineering page carries real, controlled fluorescence data for a cascaded multi-input toehold AND gate in both cells and cell-free reaction, which is ambitious for a high school team and could in principle reach the top. But the wiki is badly let down: /results is unedited iGEM template boilerplate including Lorem ipsum and placeholder contact details, /attributions is empty, /experiments is 234 words. Worth a full read mainly to confirm Cycles 2-3 data and resolve the attribution gap, which is currently unjudgeable.
screen.field_notes: YiYe Academy (CHN, Diagnostics village) built MirUro, a toehold-switch biosensor reading three bladder-cancer urinary miRNAs (miR-21-5p, miR-146a-5p, miR-205-5p) with EGFP output, intended as a cell-free paper strip. Because patient samples are not allowed, they made two trigger plasmids that overexpress the three miRNAs in E. coli, verified by qPCR at 80-150-fold over control. Three cycles escalate from a single-input switch (miTH-1) to two- and three-input cascaded AND gates. Cycle 1 shows a 10.6-fold fluorescence increase in the induced co-transformed group with single-plasmid and no-IPTG controls, cell-free TXTL fluorescence only in the matched pair, and a linear dose-response (R2=0.9804) against trigger plasmid mass. A six-module modelling page covers LOD from 3 sigma/slope, AND-gate logic stringency, cascade attenuation, a hand-written RK4 strand-displacement ODE solver, RNA thermodynamics and a ROC/AUC clinical performance simulation. HP is large and clinically engaged. Serious wiki defects: the Results page is unmodified iGEM template text with Lorem ipsum, and the Attributions page has no content, so outside contributions (plasmid synthesis was contracted to Wuhan Miaoling) cannot be apportioned.

screen.project_title: META COVE: self-floating, recoverable heavy-metal bioremediation bacteria with electrochemical metal recovery
screen.what_they_built: E. coli carrying a zinc-responsive surface-display/auto-aggregation plasmid (Pznt-smtA-LPP-OmpA-Ag43-zntR) and a Pznt-driven gas-vesicle plasmid, so metal-loaded cells clump and float for collection; plus a two-chamber electrolysis reactor that strips the bound metals back out as separate deposits.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) and DH5a; pET21a and pET28a constructs, EGFP reporter variant, T7-driven positive controls; CRISPR-Cas9 asd/dapA knockout for a DAP-auxotroph containment chassis. ~19 new BBa parts in a part collection.
screen.best_evidence: /results 4.4: dual-plasmid strain drops residual metal to 5.8 uM at 10 h, close to the T7 positive control (5.6 uM) and significantly better than negative control (p<0.001); flotation rises 28% to 35.8% over 10 h (p<0.001 vs control) while sedimentation stays at baseline; TEM shows 100-200 nm cylindrical gas vesicles and SEM shows intercellular contacts in aggregates.
screen.hp_integration: Yes in part: experts' challenge about competition between modules led to rebuilding the mathematical model and refining the strain, and biosafety pressure drove the kill-switch/auxotroph work and a recover-rather-than-release stance. Framed by a ROOT (Realism, Optimization, Ownership, Trust) scheme over three engagement phases.
screen.reason: An integrated multi-module system (sensing, surface chelation, aggregation, buoyancy) that actually works together in one strain with statistics against both positive and negative controls, plus TEM/SEM ultrastructure, a CRISPR containment chassis and a genuinely engineered electrochemical recovery reactor. That scale and scope is in the finalist conversation for a high school team. Full read needed to check replication, to see the engineering page's cycles, and because the attributions page is empty, which currently leaves aspect 6 unverifiable.
screen.field_notes: YK Pao School (Shanghai, CHN, Bioremediation village) built META COVE, a self-floating recoverable bioremediation platform for heavy metals in water. Two plasmids in E. coli BL21(DE3): a zinc-responsive polycistron (Pznt-smtA-LPP-OmpA-Ag43-zntR-his) giving surface metal chelation plus Ag43 auto-aggregation, and Pznt-driven gas vesicle protein cluster giving buoyancy, with T7-driven versions as positive controls and an EGFP reporter version to characterise the Pznt promoter. Reported results include SDS-PAGE bands matching GVP (146.7 kDa), Ag43 (106.8 kDa), LPP-OmpA and ZntR; promoter dose and time kinetics; and for the dual-plasmid strain, residual metal of 5.8 uM at 10 h versus a 5.6 uM T7 control and p<0.001 against negative control, flotation rising from 28% to 35.8% while sedimentation stays flat. TEM shows 100-200 nm cylindrical gas vesicles; time-series fluorescence microscopy tracks aggregation from monodisperse cells at 2 h to interconnected clusters at 10 h. A CRISPR-Cas9 asd/dapA knockout for DAP auxotrophy is partly done and honestly reported as chimeric in 22 of 23 screened clones. Hardware is a two-chamber UF-membrane reactor with stainless cathode, graphite felt anode and Ag/AgCl reference that recovers lead, cadmium and zinc separately by stepped cathode potentials, with Arduino code and calibration appendices. The attributions page is empty.

screen.project_title: SpotAway: de novo designed pigment binders and a lipase fusion for an emergency stain patch
screen.what_they_built: De novo capsanthin-binding proteins (RFdiffusion3 backbones, LigandMPNN sequences, RoseTTAFold3 scoring, AutoDock Vina docking) fused to a cellulose-binding module, plus a triolein-binding-domain–lipase fusion, intended for a dry xerogel patch that is rehydrated with 1–2 drops of water to treat fresh chili-oil stains.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with IPTG induction and Ni-NTA purification for the binders; Pichia pastoris GS115 with Zeocin multicopy selection and BMGY/BMMY methanol induction for the secreted lipase fusion. Four BBa parts (BBa_268Z8SNK, BBa_26XO0X6Q, BBa_26SRS8UL, BBa_26DLVSHD), sodium alginate–gelatin xerogel carrier with trehalose–mannitol lyoprotectant.
screen.best_evidence: Docking-guided redesign confirmed in the wet lab: Binder-5 (Vina −10.9 kcal/mol) gave ΔOD275 ≈ 0.081 versus its parent Binder-1 (−7.3 kcal/mol, ΔOD ≈ 0.058), a ~40% improvement measured in the same batch with Binder-2 (≈0.102) as positive reference (/results §5, Figures 5.4–5.6). Binder-2 showed a linear dose response, ΔOD = 0.108·C − 0.006, R² = 0.993 over 0–1.5 mg/mL, with an egg-white protein negative control showing no comparable shift (/results §2–4, n=3, t-tests). The lipase fusion retained 87.8% activity on a mass basis (3.68 vs 4.19 U/mL) by copper-soap assay at 37 °C, pH 7.0 (/results §8).
screen.hp_integration: Yes — expert advice moved them off peroxide-based chemical decolorisation toward de novo pigment binders, and pushed them to hydrogel carriers and fusion expression; the dry/wet discrepancy flagged by advisors added docking pre-screening to the pipeline. 21 interviews and 719 survey responses defined the target users and the pigment-first priority.
screen.reason: De novo protein design executed end-to-end by a high school team, with the wet lab actually falsifying the computational ranking (pTM/ipTM could not distinguish Binder-1 from Binder-2) and the team responding by inserting docking pre-screening, which then predicted a real measured improvement — that is textbook engineering and the most epistemically careful results writing in the batch, with replicates, negative controls, calibration curves and explicit statements of what each assay cannot establish. Two things need a full read before any finalist judgement: the wiki states that wet-lab execution for the lipase arm 'was commissioned' while the Attributions page is empty, which goes straight to aspect 6; and the binding evidence is a ΔOD proxy with no Kd, with Binder-2's signal actually decreasing, so a panel should test whether the headline binding claim holds.
screen.field_notes: Yucai-SZ (Biomanufacturing village, CHN) built SpotAway, a dry-activated emergency stain patch for chili-oil stains combining a de novo capsanthin binder with a lipase fusion in a sodium alginate–gelatin xerogel. The dry-lab pipeline ran RFdiffusion3 (1,000 backbones) → LigandMPNN (2 sequences each) → RoseTTAFold3 (pTM>0.9, ipTM>0.75) → RMSD → AutoDock Vina. Four of five Round-1 candidates expressed solubly in BL21(DE3) at 24–27 kDa; a UV assay at 275 nm (after a 5 nm blue shift on petroleum ether addition) with an egg-white negative control distinguished binder-specific from generic protein response, and Binder-2 led with ΔOD ≈ 0.102 and a linear dose response R²=0.993 over 0–1.5 mg/mL. The decisive engineering moment was that pTM/ipTM were near-identical across Binder-1–4 while wet-lab performance differed sharply, so Cycle 2 added docking pre-screening; the redesigned Binder-5 (−10.9 kcal/mol) beat its parent by ~40% in ΔOD. Cycle 3 is an honest measurement-failure audit: the lycopene route was discontinued not because Binder-6 failed — it expressed and purified fine — but because lycopene's OD474.5 decayed with a ~2.5 h half-life under illumination, making the readout uninterpretable.
