Cycle 4 secreted a Lipase–Binder fusion from P. pastoris GS115 at a reported ~1 g/L, verified by anti-His Western blot with no truncation bands, retaining 87.8% lipase activity at equal mass (~143% per catalytic centre after molar correction) in a copper-soap assay on olive oil. One construct (ID 283) failed because of an internal PstI site in the CDS. Only four Registry parts, the patch itself was never assembled or tested on fabric, and the Attributions page is empty despite the wiki noting that some wet-lab execution was commissioned.

screen.project_title: Aegis / RGD-xES — pH-responsive integrin-targeted protein assembly around lung cancer cells
screen.what_they_built: A family of fusion proteins joining a multivalent RGD integrin-targeting module to 2-24 elastin-like ES repeats, designed to bind A549 lung-cancer cells and then phase-assemble into a physical layer in the mildly acidic tumour microenvironment. Five connected DBTL cycles from scaffold choice through stability to cell effects and normal-cell selectivity.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21 for expression (pET-28a, T7, SUMO solubility tag, His purification); A549 and BEAS-2B human cell lines for testing. 22 BBa parts plus BBa_B0015/B0034. Plasmids synthesised by GenScript.
screen.best_evidence: /results: DLS peak diameters at pH 6.0 of 11.26 and 12.33 um for RGD-6ES and RGD-8ES versus 2.89 and 3.01 um at pH 4.2 (~4x), matched by FITC fluorescence droplet imaging; CCK8 A549 viability fell to ~68% and 52% at 24 h and ~33% and 9% at 48 h; a matched-mass comparison gave 89% (RGD alone), 78% (ES alone), 61% (non-covalent mixture) versus 43% and 27% for the fusions, showing covalent fusion matters; BEAS-2B retained viability at twice the A549 dose.
screen.hp_integration: Stated but weakly traced — the human-practices and research pages shape framing and the NSCLC indication, but no cycle on the engineering page names a stakeholder input as the reason a construct or assay changed.
screen.reason: The deepest experimental dataset in the batch and written with real evidential discipline — every figure is followed by what it does not establish (DLS cannot prove a liquid condensed phase; CCK8 retention is not intact protein; scratch closure cannot be separated from cell loss). Worth a full read on aspects 2 and 4. The panel must probe aspect 6 hard: Western blots, DLS, FITC labelling, two mammalian cell lines and a GenScript synthesis bill are far beyond a typical high-school bench, the engineering page admits two figures are 'schematic placeholders for the layout and not raw experimental data', and the 270-word /attributions page lists 42 people with no task-level split.
screen.field_notes: Zhulu-China (Oncology village, China) built RGD-xES, fusion proteins pairing a (GRGDNPTGRGDSPA)9 integrin-targeting module with a variable number of elastin-like ES repeats, intended to recognise a lung-cancer cell and then assemble a physical layer around it in the acidic tumour microenvironment, attacking the cell mechanically rather than chemically. Cycle 1 compared KS and ES behind a SUMO solubility tag as a deliberately hard test, finding ES droplets of 7.55-8.59 um at pH 6.0 against 3.43-3.51 um for KS. Cycle 2 found the solubility ceiling: RGD-2ES to RGD-8ES expressed solubly, RGD-10ES upward went to the pellet, and RGD-6ES was chosen as lead over the larger but broader-distribution RGD-8ES. Cycle 3 ran thermal, pH, 7-day refrigerated storage and vibration stability, showing cell-adhesion retention degrades before the size metric does. Cycle 4 gave CCK8 time courses, live/dead staining, a scratch assay (closure 0.63 control vs 0.48 and 0.40) and a Western panel (Ki67 down, cleaved caspase-3 up from near zero, N-cadherin/Snail/MMP-2 down, E-cadherin up, YAP down with p-YAP up). Cycle 5 showed BEAS-2B normal bronchial cells tolerated twice the A549 dose. Caveats the team itself prints: no direct membrane imaging of the proposed layer, no invasion assay, no causality for the YAP signal. Plasmids were synthesised by GenScript and the attributions page carries no task-level breakdown.

screen.project_title: Persephone — a sprayable multi-enzyme and inhibitory-peptide coating against postharvest fruit loss
screen.what_they_built: Four functional modules in one chitosan-based spray: ACC deaminase (cuts ethylene biosynthesis), designed ethylene-receptor inhibitory peptides (block ethylene signalling), MnSOD (scavenges ROS) and chitinase (antifungal), each fused where useful to the cell-penetrating peptide BP100 and applied to real fruit.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3) with pET28a-His constructs (ACCD, SAMase, MnSOD, each with N- and C-terminal BP100 variants); 19 BBa part IDs registered, with a 4,011-word parts page.
screen.best_evidence: /proof-of-concept §4.1.1: headspace GC-MS on banana pieces after 5 days at 20 C gives 0.9749 mg/L ethylene in the blank, 0.6588 mg/L with ACC deaminase, and none detected with ACC-BP100 deaminase, matched by a roughly one-day delay in peel yellowing; §4.1.4 blueberries show a 3-4-fold lower decay rate and 2.2 g versus 3.1 g weight loss over 15 days for chitosan+chitinase versus water.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — a GROW/RIPE framework along the fruit supply chain (consumers, retailers, growers, processors, logistics) plus postharvest and synthetic-biology experts, credited with setting the module combination, the fruit types tested and the evaluation metrics, and with pushing the product to a cell-free sprayed formulation.
screen.reason: Four modules actually expressed, purified, assayed for specific activity and then tested on real bananas, apples and blueberries with instrument-backed numbers (GC-MS ethylene, Fiji browning quantification, decay and weight-loss rates), plus 19 Registry parts and a documented N- versus C-terminal BP100 fusion iteration with honest negatives. Worth a full read; the weak points to probe are the near-empty attributions page, a thin 1,334-word main human-practices page, and the DNA-nanoswitch binding assay stopping at method validation rather than measured affinities.
screen.field_notes: Zhulu-Union (Food & Nutrition, CHN) built Persephone, a sprayable postharvest preservation system attacking ethylene, ROS and fungal decay at once. ACC deaminase (P. putida UW4), SAM lyase (phage T3) and MnSOD (E. coli) were cloned into pET28a and expressed in BL21(DE3); N-terminal BP100 fusions failed or went to inclusion bodies, so C-terminal fusions were adopted, with purified yields tabulated (e.g. ACC deaminase 1004.37 mg/L, ACC-BP100 326.65 mg/L). Specific activities were measured by alpha-ketobutyrate-DNPH (1.63 U/mg wild-type versus 0.31 U/mg for ACC-BP100, a deliberate trade of activity for penetration). Fruit trials: headspace GC-MS showed ethylene at 0.9749 mg/L (blank), 0.6588 mg/L (ACC deaminase) and undetected (ACC-BP100) after 5 days; apple-slice browning quantified in Fiji increased 16.06% (control), 8.34% (MnSOD-BP100) and 12.70% (MnSOD) over 8 h; chitosan+chitinase delayed banana mould about a day and cut blueberry decay 3-4-fold with the lowest weight loss over 15 days. Four ethylene-receptor inhibitory peptides (BOP, EBOP, G01, B03) were designed and tested on bananas by firmness, soluble solids, titratable acidity and weight loss, with B03 best; an M13 DNA-nanoswitch assay was validated by disulfide and oligonucleotide bridging but affinities were not yet measured. Nineteen BBa parts, a 7,383-word model page and a 5,983-word safety page. The attributions page carries only schools and sponsors.

screen.project_title: EctoBloom: low-salt ectoine production with in-house bacterial cellulose mask carrier
screen.what_they_built: Engineered E. coli BL21(DE3) carrying the halophile ectABC operon to make ectoine without high-salt fermentation, plus a LysC T352I feedback-desensitized aspartokinase and an acsAB/acsCD bacterial cellulose module so the same chassis makes the mask membrane. Product concept is a BC-silk-ectoine facial mask.
screen.chassis_and_parts: E. coli BL21(DE3), pET-28a backbone with B0034 RBS and B0015 terminator; six parts documented (five new: ectABC composite, LysC T352I BBa_26XUR2FA, acsAB-acsCD BBa_K5481012 and others).
screen.best_evidence: /results: engineered strain 4.425 +/- 0.380 g/L ectoine by HPLC vs same-batch wild type 0.503 +/- 0.288 g/L (n=3, ~8.8x); LysC T352I strain 6.852 g/L vs same-batch parent 5.439 g/L; straw hydrolysate gave 4.295 g/L (97% of glucose); acsAB+acsCD strain gave 148.2 mg/L extracellular cellulose and a collectable surface membrane.
screen.hp_integration: Yes — /human-practices records five stages in which expert advice (Nanjing Tech fermentation researchers, a mask industry director, a dermatologist) drove carbon/nitrogen source choices, the upstream LysC precursor work and the product form.
screen.reason: Replicated HPLC quantification with same-batch controls, a clean five-step validation chain, honest caveats about cross-batch comparison and LOQ, five new parts, six DBTL cycles and HP that visibly changed the design. Weak spots: no real modelling page, empty attributions page, hydrolysate purchased. Clearly deserves a full read.
screen.field_notes: ZQT-Nanjing (Fashion & Cosmetics, CHN) attacked the high-salt 'bacterial milking' route to ectoine, which needs ~100 g/L NaCl and makes saline wastewater. They moved the ectB-ectA-ectC operon into E. coli BL21(DE3) under an IPTG-inducible promoter with B0034/B0015, reaching 4.425 g/L versus 0.503 g/L for same-batch wild type by HPLC (n=3), then raised it to 6.852 g/L with a LysC T352I feedback-desensitized aspartokinase against a same-batch parent at 5.439 g/L. Single-factor medium screening (carbon source, glucose level, nitrogen source, NH4Cl) gave 5.344 g/L, and purchased wheat-straw hydrolysate supported 4.295 g/L, 97% of glucose, supporting a renewable feedstock. A second module (acsAB plus acsCD) made 148.2 mg/L extracellular and 299.1 mg/L intracellular cellulose and a collectable surface membrane as the mask carrier. Six DBTL cycles, five new parts, 10k-word IHP with industry and dermatology input; the model and hardware pages are placeholder text and the attributions page is empty.

justification.a1: EctoBloom runs two linked engineering lines that build in difficulty: ectABC moved into a low-salt BL21(DE3) chassis (0.503 to 4.425 g/L vs same-batch WT), then medium screens, then a LysC T352I precursor modification (6.852 vs 5.439 g/L same-batch), plus a second line in which acsAB then acsCD give a collectable cellulose membrane (Results 1-6, Engineering Cycles 1-5.2). That is more than a single working construct and is close to the GreatBay pattern of stacked results. It stops short of a 5 because there is no model at all (the Model page is untouched iGEM template text) and the two lines are never integrated: no ectoine was ever loaded into a membrane, so the BC-Silk-Ectoine mask stays a concept (Results 6.5).
justification.a2: Function is shown against proper controls throughout: WT vs Ect in the same batch, parent vs T352I in the same batch, and WT vs AcsAB vs AcsAB-AcsCD with a clean ~3.8 mg/L background (Results 2.3, 5.3, 6.3). Figures give units, n = 3, SD and individual replicate dots (Fig. 4, verified in the rendered image), gels carry a size-marked ladder and named lanes (Fig. 3), and the team is unusually honest about the WT background peak near the limit of quantification. Short of 5 because the statistics are thin where they matter most: the headline +26.0% T352I gain has overlapping SDs (5.439 +/- 0.896 vs 6.852 +/- 0.367) and no P value, ANOVA is mentioned but only one P < 0.05 is reported (xylose), and no chromatogram, standard curve, spike-recovery result or expression-level check (SDS-PAGE/activity) is shown on the wiki.
justification.a3: The use case is credible and grounded in the team's own data rather than slogans: wheat straw hydrolysate reached 97.0% of the same-batch glucose titer (Results 4.1), and low-salt operation is argued against the bacterial-milking route they describe in Description 2. Stage 5 of Human Practices is the strongest part, with farmers raising seasonality, transport, moisture and pesticide/heavy-metal contamination, and an environment-bureau researcher (Fu Yiwei) leading them to drop "green alternative" framing and accept that low-salt effluent still needs treatment. It is not a 5 because nothing is tested in a real-world-like setting (contrast TAS Taipei's wastewater rig), there is no cost or LCA calculation of the team's own, and the home-page cost table ($385.46/kg ectoine, etc.) is uncited.
justification.a4: Six DBTL cycles each open with an explicit, quantitatively answerable engineering question and change one variable (Engineering, Cycles 1-5.2). The best cycle is genuinely data-driven redesign rather than troubleshooting: acsAB alone gave 445.5 mg/L intracellular but only 10.9 mg/L extracellular, which identified export as the bottleneck and dictated stacking acsCD, after which extracellular rose to 148.2 mg/L with similar totals (~456 vs ~447 mg/L) - the team correctly reads this as redistribution, not more synthesis. Cycles 2 and 3 are parameter screens rather than redesign, measures of success are only ever titer, and the Engineering Fig. 1 caption contradicts the page by calling hydrolysate "37% of glucose" where every other statement says 97.0%.
justification.a5: Human Practices is the strongest section: five stages with an Aspiration-Action-Analysis-Adaptation frame, a 397-response survey, consumer/parent interviews, beauty retail staff, a mask industry director (Jin Jingqi), a dermatologist, a cosmetic formulator, farmers, an environment-bureau researcher, and academics at Nanjing Tech and the Institute of Microbiology, CAS. Several changes are traceable into the bench work: Huang/Fu pushed systematic medium optimization, Fu's point about upstream precursor supply led to the LysC T352I cycle, Tian advised keeping LysC modular and not claiming industrial readiness, and Director Jin's substrate/functional-layer/active distinction produced the BC module. It also changed what they claim: the dermatologist set cosmetic-not-medical boundaries and the environmental researcher ended the "zero pollution" language. Short of 5 only because the exchanges are reported as summaries, with no dated records, quotes or materials for most interviews.
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page: 2026.igem.wiki/zqt-nanjing/attributions returns 404 and the Team page carries only member cards, roles and quotes, with no task-level breakdown of who designed, built, fermented or ran HPLC. The Notebook page does state that every cultivation, assay and observation was planned, executed and recorded by the student wet team with instructors supervising only, and the Experiments page declares bought-in items (Vazyme kits with catalog numbers, synthesised genes, purchased wheat straw hydrolysate). But that is a blanket statement, not the specific attribution the handbook asks for on the team page (p.25-26), and the project leans on advice from two university labs, so I cannot tell who ran the HPLC and mutagenesis. I would ask this directly in Q&A and the score could move either way.
justification.a7: This is a genuine synthetic-biology build: the halophile ectB-ectA-ectC operon as a single co-transcribed unit in BL21(DE3) on pET-28a(+), a site-directed LysC T352I basic part, and a stacked acsAB/acsCD cellulose module, with standard components reused (RBS BBa_B0034, terminator BBa_B0015) and internal EcoRI/XbaI/SpeI/PstI sites removed by synonymous mutation for RFC10 (Contribution, Bronze section). Five new coding parts plus reuse of registry parts matches the TAS Taipei pattern where novelty is not the point. Marked down slightly because the regulatory design is described inconsistently: Contribution says the composite uses the constitutive BBa_J23100, while Results, Engineering and Experiments all describe an IPTG-inducible T7/pET-28a(+) system induced at 5 h with 0.1 mM IPTG.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is good and self-critical, but the Registry side is what p.18 tells me to judge and I could not verify it (parts.igem.org returned 403 to me), so the claim that every part page carries full data and protocols is unconfirmed. On the wiki itself the Parts page carries no figures or data at all, only tables; it applies "Gold/Silver/Bronze medal" labels to its own parts, which is not how medals work; and the Gold composite is listed as BBa_26F6NIJF on the Parts page but as "ID assigned at registration" in the Contribution table. Several standard pages are missing or empty: attributions, proof-of-concept, implementation, design and protocols all 404, and Model, Measurement, Hardware and Software are unedited iGEM template text with "Inspirations" lists, so a judge looking for Proof of Concept or Implementation has to hunt across Results and Description.
justification.w1: The home page lands the problem quickly: the skincare framing, the cost-per-kilogram comparison table putting ectoine at $385.46/kg against glycerin and hyaluronic acid, the 100 g/L NaCl high-salt route, and then the two modules. The Description abstract states the chassis, the route, the renewable feedstock and the product in one paragraph, and the Results overview gives the six-step validation chain plus headline titers before any detail. It is a little diluted by marketing-styled copy on the home and team pages ("Small team. Big bloom.") and by the mask prototype being presented up front when it was never built.
justification.w2: Most key claims are tied to a figure with a same-batch control, n = 3, SD and units, and the Summary table on Results explicitly names the control basis for every comparison and warns that cross-batch titers must not be subtracted as cumulative gain - better discipline than I usually see at any level. Membrane formation is supported by three photographs including parallel flasks and a spread sheet. Against that: no HPLC chromatograms, standard curve or spike-recovery data are shown, the raw gels, chromatograms and spreadsheets are said to be "archived in the team's shared project space" rather than on the wiki, the Parts page carries no evidence, and in Fig. 3A the band annotated 1266 bp sits above the 1500 bp ladder mark.
justification.w3: The side navigation maps cleanly onto the ballot (Project, Wet Lab, Human Practice, Team), every content page has a sectioned table of contents, a 28-term glossary and a working search, and the previous/next links make the wet-lab chain readable in order. Friction: five standard URLs 404 (attributions, proof-of-concept, implementation, design, protocols), four standard pages are untouched template text, Collaboration sits at the non-standard path collaborations.html, and the Human Practices and Education pages run to about 10,000 words each, which pushes against "complete but not sprawling".
justification.w4: A future team could get a long way from this: the Experiments page gives strains, kits with catalog numbers, enzymes, media and stock recipes, seamless assembly, site-directed mutagenesis, fermentation and HPLC conditions (C18, acetonitrile-water 20:80, 0.6 mL/min, 40 C, 210 nm); the Notebook attaches two dated PDF records that it says retain failed PCRs, truncated long-gene amplification and incomplete digests; and the Contribution page adds a six-row troubleshooting table and names the next experiments (DGC co-expression, cellulase/Congo red/SEM confirmation). Two gaps stop it short of 5: the basal salt medium of the main fermentation is never specified ("the laboratory's standard basal salt medium"), and no raw data or attribution of who did what is on the wiki.
justification.w5: Referencing is uneven. Description is properly done, with 18 numbered inline citations anchored to specific claims (Galinski 1985 for ectoine isolation, Sauer and Galinski 1998 for bacterial milking, market size to [17], raw-material prices to [18]). But Results and Contribution give end-of-page reference lists with no inline markers, and Engineering, Experiments, Human Practices, Safety and Education carry no references at all - including factual claims that need one, such as the C. glutamicum Cys324Tyr/Cys311Phe precedent for single-point desensitization, the statement that BL21(DE3) is urease-negative, and the home-page production-cost table. Prior iGEM parts are credited (BBa_K3520004, BBa_K5002345) which is good practice, but the overall gap is wide.

J1.one_line: A disciplined, control-led wet-lab project with real same-batch evidence for ectoine production, a precursor-supply mutation and a self-made cellulose membrane, backed by genuinely integrated Human Practices, but held back by a missing Attributions page, four boilerplate standard pages, thin statistics and patchy citation.
strengths: Every performance claim is paired with a same-batch control and the team refuses to subtract across batches: WT 0.503 vs Ect 4.425 g/L, parent 5.439 vs T352I 6.852 g/L, and a Summary table on Results that names the control basis for each comparison.

Figures meet a real bench standard for a high school team: units, n = 3, SD, individual replicate dots on the bar charts, and gels with a size-marked ladder and named lanes (Results Fig. 3 and Fig. 4, checked in the rendered images).

The acsAB-then-acsCD two-step build is a genuine DBTL decision: 445.5 mg/L intracellular but 10.9 mg/L extracellular identified export as the bottleneck, and after stacking acsCD extracellular rose to 148.2 mg/L with totals unchanged, which the team correctly reads as redistribution rather than extra synthesis.

Unusual intellectual honesty: the WT background peak near the limit of quantification, the refusal to claim a death phase from a declining OD600, the explicit statement that dry weight cannot prove secretion, and the statement that only unloaded membranes exist so far.

Human Practices changed both the biology and the claims - Dr Fu's point on precursor supply produced the LysC T352I cycle, Director Jin's substrate/functional-layer distinction produced the cellulose module, and the environment-bureau researcher ended the 'zero pollution' language.

The Contribution page is written for reuse: protocols, a six-row troubleshooting table, named follow-up assays (DGC co-expression, cellulase hydrolysis, Congo red/calcofluor, SEM) and credit to prior Registry parts BBa_K3520004 and BBa_K5002345.
weaknesses: No Attributions page (the standard URL 404s) and no task-level account anywhere of who designed, cloned, fermented or ran the HPLC; the Team page gives roles and quotes only.
Statistics are thin where the headline claims sit: the +26.0% T352I result has overlapping SDs and no P value, ANOVA is mentioned but only the xylose comparison reports P < 0.05.

No analytical evidence for the HPLC method is shown - no chromatogram, no standard curve, no spike-recovery result - even though the method is the basis of every titer, and raw data are said to be held in a shared project space off the wiki.

Model, Measurement, Hardware and Software are unedited iGEM template text with 'Inspirations' lists, and proof-of-concept, implementation, design and protocols all 404, so standard pages are either empty or absent.
Engineering, Experiments, Human Practices, Safety and Education carry no references at all, and the home-page production-cost table is uncited.

Internal inconsistencies a reader has to resolve: Engineering Fig. 1 says hydrolysate reached 37% of glucose while the text says 97.0%; Contribution describes the composite as using constitutive BBa_J23100 while every other page describes IPTG-induced T7 on pET-28a(+); the Gold composite is BBa_26F6NIJF on the Parts page but 'ID assigned at registration' in the Contribution table.
The two engineering lines are never joined - no ectoine was loaded into a membrane - so the BC-Silk-Ectoine mask remains a concept with no physical prototype or efficacy data.

Cellulose identity rests on alkali-resistant dry weight alone, with the specific confirmations (cellulase hydrolysis, staining, SEM) listed as planned; the team says this itself, but it limits what the 148.2 mg/L figure can support.
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404 at the standard URL and no task-level attribution appears on the Team page (handbook p.25-26); this lowers aspect 6 and is a Q&A question, not an integrity matter.

Registry entries could not be verified: parts.igem.org returned 403 to my requests, so the Parts and Contribution claim that each part page carries full data, controls and protocols is unconfirmed, and p.18 tells me to judge parts on the Registry entry alone.

In Results Fig. 3A the band annotated 1266 bp migrates above the 1500 bp ladder mark, which does not match the ladder as labelled; the gels also have no no-template control lane. I would ask the team to walk me through that gel rather than draw a conclusion from it.
The Parts page assigns 'Gold Medal', 'Silver Medal' and 'Bronze Medal' labels to the team's own parts, which is not how iGEM medals work and could mislead a reader.

Home-page market and cost figures ($385.46/kg ectoine, EUR 3,000/m3 reactor cost, 100 g/L NaCl) carry no citation on that page; the comparable Description figures are cited, so this reads as an omission rather than anything more.

No safety concern: the work is BL21(DE3) and Komagataeibacter-derived genes, RG1 and whitelist-compliant, with a clear safety page; nothing here needs referral to safety@igem.org, and I found nothing I would take to the RCC.
pages_read: live figures: results/img3 (gels), results/img4 (WT vs Ect bar chart)
Registry part pages BBa_26XUR2FA, BBa_26F6NIJF, BBa_26D12J9H, BBa_266X7U1Y, BBa_26ILC68O, BBa_K5481012 - all returned HTTP 403, not readable

calibrated.changed: none. a6 3.0 rather than 2.5 because the Notebook page does state that the student wet team planned, executed and recorded every cultivation and assay with instructors supervising only - a blanket statement, but more than the 2.5 teams offer; a2 4.0 matches Hongwen on same-batch controls with n=3 and SD but no inferential statistics on the headline gain.

justification.a1: EctoBloom (Results, Engineering) runs a genuine chain of increasingly hard steps for a high school team: build ectABC in BL21(DE3) (4.425 g/L vs same-batch WT 0.503 g/L), screen carbon and nitrogen sources, add LysC T352I (+26.0% same-batch), then a second strain making its own bacterial cellulose membrane (acsAB then acsAB-acsCD, 148.2 mg/L extracellular, photographed sheet). It falls short of GreatBay scope because the end product, the BC-Silk-Ectoine mask, was never built: no loading, no membrane characterisation, no efficacy data (Results s6.5 and Future Work say so plainly), and there is no model, hardware or measurement work at all.
justification.a2: The core function is measured, not asserted: HPLC quantification with n=3 biological replicates, same-batch wild-type control, SDs plotted as error bars, a 48 h time course (0.102 g/L at 6 h rising to 4.425 g/L at 48 h) and ANOVA on the carbon-source screen (Results s2-s5). The cellulose arm has a clean wild-type background and an informative intracellular/extracellular split (445.5/10.9 for AcsAB vs 299.1/148.2 for AcsAB-AcsCD, Results s6.3). I hold it at 4 rather than higher because the quantitative evidence on the wiki is tabulated numbers and captioned bar charts, no chromatograms or standard curve are shown, and the team's own unexplained 0.503 g/L wild-type signal (Results s2.3) shows the HPLC method is not yet fully validated.
justification.a3: The deployment route is argued and stakeholder-checked rather than generic: farmers on straw seasonality, collection cost and pesticide/heavy-metal contamination, an environmental researcher on saline and fermentation effluent, a dermatologist on claim boundaries, and a formulator who pushed them to call it a prototype concept (Human Practices Stages 4-5). Against that, nothing was tested in a realistic setting: no bioreactor, no fed-batch, no cost model, and the product itself does not exist, so the impact case stops at a well-reasoned argument from shake-flask data.
justification.a4: Six labelled DBTL cycles on Engineering each ask one quantitative question and change one variable, and at least two cycles are real cycles rather than troubleshooting: the glucose inverted-U (peak 4.425 g/L at 20 g/L, falling to 3.034 g/L at 50 g/L) fixed the baseline for every later experiment, and the acsAB result (product stuck intracellularly, 10.9 mg/L outside) directly caused the acsCD redesign that moved 148.2 mg/L outside. Cycles 2-3 are nonetheless medium screening rather than design change, there is no model predicting or explaining any of the data, and the team honestly notes titre alone cannot attribute the T352I gain to precursor supply (Results s5.3).
justification.a5: This is the strongest aspect. A 397-response survey, then consumers, retail staff, a mask industry director, two Nanjing Tech academics, a CAS researcher, a dermatologist, a formulator, farmers and an environmental researcher, each written up as Aspiration-Action-Analysis-Adaptation. Design changes are traceable: expert advice drove the carbon/nitrogen optimisation and the LysC T352I route, industry feedback added the bacterial cellulose module, the dermatologist moved them off medical claims, and farmer input made them downgrade straw hydrolysate from 'green alternative' to a feedstock with contamination and logistics caveats (HP Stage 5, Adaptation 1).
justification.a6: There is no Attributions page: /attributions and /team/attributions both return 404, so the required form that tells me what students did versus advisors, instructors and outside labs is simply absent. What I can see is partial: the Notebook states the student wet team planned, executed and recorded every cultivation and assay, gene synthesis and the straw hydrolysate are declared as purchased, and Human Practices names the academics who advised on pathway, media and the T352I choice. With key design input coming from university researchers and no who-did-what chart, I cannot verify execution the way the handbook asks, and the missing form is itself a deduction.
justification.a7: The project is standard-parts synthetic biology: five new parts (EctB BBa_26D12J9H, EctA BBa_26ILC68O, EctC BBa_266X7U1Y, LysC T352I BBa_26XUR2FA, composite EctABC+LysC T352I BBa_26F6NIJF) plus the existing BBa_K5481012, codon-optimised, built on pET-28a(+) with B0034 RBS and B0015 terminator, and arranged basic-then-composite so each piece is separately reusable (Parts, Contribution). LysC T352I is a genuinely reusable node for any ASA-derived pathway. I cannot confirm RFC compatibility independently because parts.igem.org returned 403 to me throughout.
justification.a8: On the wiki the documentation is well above average: construction verified by colony PCR and Sanger sequencing, a full Experiments page with media, kits, assembly and HPLC conditions, a Notebook with weekly Gantt charts, daily plan tables and downloadable per-system PDF records, and a Contribution page written for reuse. The Registry side I could not check (403 on every part page), and the handbook judges parts on the Registry, so the depth of those six entries stays unverified; the wiki also leaves the Model, Hardware, Measurement and Software pages as unedited iGEM template text, which is poor documentation hygiene.
justification.w1: The home page states problem, cost driver and the two modules in a few sentences, and the Description abstract lets a reader say exactly what the chassis, the pathway, the feedstock and the product form are. The 28-term glossary and the per-page overview cards help a non-specialist. It is a little marketing-heavy at the top (skincare scene-setting before the science) and the eight-stage platform framing is more than the evidence supports, which is why it is not a 5.
justification.w2: Claims are consistently tied to numbers with controls, replicate counts and SDs, and every section ends with an explicit boundary note saying what the data cannot show (for example that the optimised medium cannot be called higher-yielding than LB without a parallel titre measurement, Results s4.5.4). The summary table even warns that cross-batch titres must not be subtracted as cumulative gains. It stops short of 5 because raw evidence (gels, chromatograms) sits in captions and PDFs rather than being shown and read on the page.
justification.w3: Navigation is clear and criterion-shaped: a persistent menu grouped Project / Wet Lab / Human Practices / Team, in-page tables of contents, site search, prev/next links and a glossary. The failures are structural: the Attributions, Proof of Concept, Implementation, Protocols and Design URLs are all 404, and Model, Hardware, Measurement and Software are live but still carry iGEM's template boilerplate about award criteria, so a judge following the standard page set hits dead or empty pages.
justification.w4: A future team could re-run most of this: full materials and methods on Experiments, two daily notebooks as on-wiki PDFs, part-by-part build rationale with sequence lengths on Contribution, and an explicit Future Work list (ppc/aspC overexpression, thrA weakening, fed-batch, 60-72 h harvest study, DGC co-expression for c-di-GMP). The two-step acsAB then acsCD finding, with the warning that the same operon failed in BL21 in an earlier report, is exactly the kind of reusable lesson the handbook rewards. Held at 4 because the attribution and protocol pages are missing and the Registry entries are unverified.
justification.w5: Both Description and Results carry numbered reference lists and the ones I spot-checked resolve correctly and say what is claimed (Galinski 1985 Eur J Biochem 149:135-139; Sauer and Galinski 1998 Biotechnol Bioeng 57:306-313 for bacterial milking). Use is uneven: the numbering schemes differ between Description and Results for the same sources, Human Practices and Education carry essentially no in-text citations, and figure and image credits are not given.

J2.one_line: A disciplined two-module wet-lab project with real same-batch controls, replicates and honest limits, let down by a missing attributions page, unverifiable Registry entries and four template-boilerplate standard pages.
strengths: Measured, controlled core result: 4.425 +/- 0.380 g/L ectoine vs same-batch wild type 0.503 +/- 0.288 g/L by HPLC, n=3, with a full 48 h time course and growth curves (Results s2-s3)

A genuine design change driven by test data: acsAB alone retained cellulose intracellularly (10.9 mg/L outside), adding acsCD moved 148.2 mg/L outside and produced a collectable membrane at the air-liquid interface (Results s6)

Unusually honest boundary statements after almost every result, including refusing to call the urea group evidence of urea utilisation in a urease-negative strain and warning that cross-batch titres must not be summed

Human Practices that actually changed the project: 397-response survey, then experts, industry, dermatologist, formulator, farmers and an environmental researcher, with the straw-hydrolysate claim downgraded and medical claims removed as a result
Renewable-feedstock evidence that is measured rather than asserted: wheat straw hydrolysate reached 97.0% of the same-batch glucose titre (4.295 vs 4.425 g/L)
Reusable part design and a Contribution page written for the next team, with LysC T352I kept as a separable basic part for any ASA-derived pathway
weaknesses: No Attributions page at all (404), so who did what, and how much advisors and outside labs contributed, cannot be judged
The headline product, the BC-Silk-Ectoine mask, was never made: no ectoine loading, no membrane characterisation, no safety or hydration data, so the integration claim rests on two separate strains
No modelling of any kind, and the Model, Hardware, Measurement and Software pages are still unedited iGEM template text
Cycles 2 and 3 of the DBTL narrative are single-factor medium screening rather than design iteration; only the acsAB to acsCD step is a full redesign driven by a failure
The anomalous 0.503 g/L wild-type HPLC signal is flagged but unresolved, which leaves the analytical method only partly validated
Reference numbering is inconsistent between Description and Results, and Human Practices and Education carry almost no in-text citations or image credits
red_flags: Required Attributions page returns 404 (both /attributions and /team/attributions); Proof of Concept, Implementation, Protocols and Design also 404

I could not open any Registry part page (parts.igem.org returned 403 on BBa_26F6NIJF, BBa_26XUR2FA, BBa_26D12J9H, BBa_K5481012), so a7 and a8 rest on wiki claims and should be re-checked by a judge with Registry access before the panel settles those scores

Question for the team, not an accusation: 4.4 g/L ectoine from 20 g/L glucose in an unoptimised shake flask is a high carbon conversion for a first-generation construct, and the 0.503 g/L signal in a wild type that lacks ectABC is not explained; I would ask to see the chromatograms and calibration curve

Key engineering choices (carbon/nitrogen optimisation, the T352I site) were suggested by university and CAS researchers per Human Practices; with no attribution form I cannot tell how far that advice extended into execution

calibrated.changed: none — a6 2.5 (404 form, but the notebook does state the student team executed the work) sits correctly between the bios-only 2.0 group and the per-task-credit 3.0 group.

justification.a1: EctoBloom carries two engineering lines through to data in one season: a low-salt ectoine strain in BL21(DE3) taken from pathway construction through carbon/nitrogen screening to a LysC point mutation (6.852 g/L, Results §5), and a second strain that builds its own bacterial cellulose membrane (Results §6, photographs Figs 17-19). That is more ground than most high school teams cover, and the steps genuinely build on one another. It falls short of a 5 because the headline deliverable, the BC-Silk-Ectoine mask, exists only as a concept: no loaded membrane, no release data, no model (the Model page is untouched iGEM template text).
justification.a2: The central claim is properly controlled: engineered strain 4.425 +/- 0.380 g/L against a same-batch wild type at 0.503 +/- 0.288 g/L, n = 3, HPLC against a standard curve (Results §2.2-2.3), plus a time course, growth curves showing a ~12.5% burden, dose-response curves for glucose and NH4Cl, and a same-batch parent/T352I comparison (+26.0%, §5.3). The cellulose work has a wild-type background control and a clean intracellular-to-extracellular redistribution with AcsCD (§6.3) backed by membrane photographs. Held at 4 because the wild-type ectoine signal is unexplained, the blank-matrix, spike-recovery and peak-purity checks are still described as pending, and everything downstream of crude extract is unmeasured.
justification.a3: The need is not asserted but checked: a 397-response survey, beauty-retail interviews, a mask industry director, a dermatologist, a formulator and a factory manager (Human Practices Stages 1-5), and the team states plainly that it has no MVP and no pilot-scale data. Ectoine is already an industrial product, so a low-salt route has an obvious place to land. It is not a 4+ because nothing was tested in or near a real setting, the straw supply chain was only discussed with farmers rather than sampled, and the cost advantage over the high-salt route is argued from literature prices rather than measured.
justification.a4: Six cycles are each framed around one quantitatively answerable question with one variable changed, and the Learn step visibly chooses the next Build: medium work is stopped when marginal gains shrink, which leads to the LysC node (Engineering Cycle 3 to 4), and the acs operon is deliberately split so a negative result could be localised, which it was (AcsAB synthesises but retains product, so AcsCD is added; Cycles 5.1-5.2). The boundaries of each conclusion are stated honestly. It stops short of 5 because no failure forced a redesign, no abandoned construct is reported, there is no model fitted to the team's own data, and Fig. 1 of the Engineering page states the hydrolysate reached 37% of glucose where every other page says 97.0%.
justification.a5: The Aspiration-Action-Analysis-Adaptation loop produces design changes I can trace to named people: Director Jin Jingqi's feedback turned a vague ectoine mask into the three-layer substrate/functional layer/active design; Dr Fu Yangkai redirected the team upstream to precursor supply, which became the LysC T352I work; Dr Tian Xiaodong argued for keeping LysC and ectABC as separate modules; the dermatologist narrowed the claims to cosmetic rather than medical; and Fu Yiwei of the Nanjing environment bureau made the team drop absolute green claims and reframe wheat straw as conditional (Stage 5, Adaptation 1-2). Not a 5: no genuinely critical or opposing stakeholder appears, quotes are paraphrased with no dates or transcripts, several adaptations are wording changes rather than design changes, and the 397-person survey and the interviews with students carry no consent, anonymity or oversight statement.
justification.a6: The /attributions page returns 404 and is absent from the navigation, so the standard record of who did what is missing. The Notebook carries one blanket sentence that the student wet team planned, executed and recorded every cultivation and assay while instructors and advisors gave supervision and safety guidance only, and the team does disclose that genes were synthesised commercially and the wheat straw hydrolysate purchased externally (Results §4.1.1), which is honest. But there is no task chart, no per-figure or per-experiment attribution, and the Team page gives only broad lane labels, so I cannot tell which student ran the HPLC or the mutagenesis. Capped at 3 until the session clarifies; this is a question, not an allegation.
justification.a7: The design is standard-parts work: ectB-ectA-ectC as one operon with B0034 and B0015 in pET-28a(+), internal EcoRI/XbaI/SpeI/PstI sites removed by synonymous mutation for RFC10 compliance (Contribution, construction and validation), five new parts claimed (EctA/EctB/EctC, LysC T352I, ectABC-lysC*) and existing Registry parts BBa_K3520004 and BBa_K5002345 credited as prior cellulose documentation. The composite module has real functional evidence behind it. Not a 5 because the new parts are a published pathway and a literature-established mutation rather than new design, which the team says plainly.
justification.a8: Wiki-side documentation is a strength: full protocols on the Experiments page, a Notebook with weekly Gantt, a daily table and downloadable PDFs, captioned figures and explicit statements of what each dataset cannot show. Registry-side I could not verify: parts.igem.org returned 403 from my environment, the Parts page itself shows no sequences, lengths or part-level characterisation figures, and the Contribution table lists the Gold composite as 'ID assigned at registration' while the Parts table gives it as BBa_26F6NIJF. Because the characterisation data I can see live on the wiki rather than demonstrably on the part pages, and the Attributions page is missing, this sits at 3.5 pending a look at the Registry entries.
justification.w1: The home page tells the problem in a few screens (why ectoine, why high-salt fermentation is costly, a per-kilogram cost table against glycerin, urea and hyaluronic acid) and then names the two modules and the vision before handing the reader six labelled entry cards. The Description abstract states the problem, the approach and the product in one paragraph with a system schematic (Fig. 1). A little marketing framing at the top, but a judge knows the goal within a minute.
justification.w2: Claims and evidence are kept apart with unusual discipline for a high school wiki: every titer carries n = 3 and SD, each comparison names its same-batch control, and the Summary warns in bold that figures from different batches must not be subtracted as a cumulative improvement. Unsupported inferences are refused explicitly (the urea group is not taken as evidence of urea utilisation; no death phase is asserted from the OD decline). Short of 5 because figure images cannot be checked from the crawl, raw values beyond means and SDs are not posted, and the analytical QC checks promised in the notebook schedule are written up as still to be done.
justification.w3: The side menu is short and the page-to-page 'previous/next' trail and glossary are genuinely helpful. But /attributions, /proof-of-concept, /implementation, /design and /protocols all 404, and the Model, Hardware, Measurement, Software, Entrepreneurship, Inclusivity, Sustainability and Alternative Platform pages are unedited iGEM template boilerplate with 'Inspirations' lists. A judge looking for a model or a measurement contribution finds placeholder text, which is exactly the hunt the handbook tells teams to spare us.
justification.w4: A future team could repeat most of this: the Experiments page gives media recipes, assembly, mutagenesis, HPLC conditions and the alkaline-purification dry-weight method; the Notebook gives a dated day-by-day record with PDF daily logs; and the Contribution page is written deliberately as a handover, including the two-step acsAB then acsCD construction template and the limits of the dry-weight conclusion. Missing for a 5: raw datasets, part sequences on the wiki, and any record of who did which task.
justification.w5: Description and Results carry numbered reference lists with DOIs for the key literature, and prior Registry parts are credited by ID (Contribution). Against that, the Human Practices, Education and Safety pages carry no citations at all although they make factual claims about salinity effects, skin biology and biosafety classifications; the market size and price figures rest on a market-blog entry and a wholesale quotation platform; and I found no image credits anywhere. I could not verify that individual references resolve from this environment, so this is scored on consistency of citation practice rather than on a resolution check.

J3.one_line: A disciplined two-module wet-lab project with properly controlled, honestly bounded fermentation data and HP that visibly reshaped the product design, let down by a missing Attributions page, boilerplate award pages and unverifiable Registry documentation.
strengths: Same-batch controls everywhere that matters: WT vs Ect (0.503 vs 4.425 g/L, n=3, HPLC), parent vs T352I (5.439 vs 6.852 g/L), and a wild-type background control for the cellulose dry-weight assay

Unusually honest reporting: the Results Summary states in bold that cross-batch titers must not be subtracted, refuses to call the urea result utilisation, and refuses to call the OD decline a death phase

Six DBTL cycles each driven by one quantitative question, including a deliberate two-step acsAB then acsCD build so that a negative result could be localised - and the AcsAB-only result (product retained intracellularly) really did set the next Build

Human Practices with traceable consequences: the three-layer mask structure from Director Jin, the LysC precursor work from Dr Fu, modular separation of LysC and ectABC from Dr Tian, and the withdrawal of absolute green claims after the environment bureau interview
A physical result a reader can see: a collectable bacterial cellulose membrane formed at the air-liquid interface, reproduced across parallel flasks (Results Figs 17-19)
Protocols, a dated notebook with downloadable daily logs, and a Contribution page written explicitly as a handover to future teams
weaknesses: No Attributions page (/attributions 404s) and no per-task or per-figure record of which student did which experiment; only one blanket sentence in the Notebook
The product that gives the project its name is unbuilt: no ectoine loading, no release curve, no membrane characterisation, no mask prototype data
Model, Hardware, Measurement, Software, Entrepreneurship, Inclusivity, Sustainability and Alternative Platform pages are untouched iGEM template boilerplate

Registry documentation cannot be confirmed from the wiki: the Parts page shows no sequences or part-level characterisation figures, and the Gold composite's ID is given inconsistently (BBa_26F6NIJF vs 'ID assigned at registration')
The 397-response survey and the interviews with students carry no mention of consent, anonymity or any ethics oversight
No failure-driven redesign is reported anywhere; the cycles read as a planned optimisation ladder, which makes the engineering narrative less convincing than it could be
Engineering page Fig. 1 caption states wheat straw hydrolysate reached 37% of glucose; every other page says 97.0%
Human Practices, Education and Safety pages make factual claims with no citations, and no image sources are credited
red_flags: Required standard page missing: /attributions returns 404 and does not appear in the navigation, so aspect 6 cannot be settled from the wiki
Survey of 397 respondents and interviews with students and parents, with no consent, anonymity or ethics-oversight statement (handbook p.23-24) - a reflective gap, not an integrity allegation
Internal inconsistency: 37% vs 97.0% for the wheat straw hydrolysate group between the Engineering Fig. 1 caption and all other reports of the same experiment

Notebook daily table lists blank-matrix, spike-recovery and peak-purity QC, a supernatant-vs-lysate localisation check and a plasmid stability check as performed (2026-08-28, 08-31, 09-01), while the Results page describes the same checks as still to be done - worth asking about in session

Ectoine reported in the fermentation supernatant at g/L levels although it is normally an intracellular compatible solute, with no stated export mechanism; and the wild-type signal of 0.503 g/L is unexplained
Registry part pages could not be reached from this environment (HTTP 403), so sequence features and part characterisation remain unverified; aspect 8 is scored accordingly and should be rechecked

calibrated.changed: none.

one_line.en: A disciplined two-module project with same-batch controls, replicates and honest limits, let down by a missing attributions page, four template standard pages and an unbuilt final product.
one_line.zh: 嚴謹的雙模組專案，具同批次對照、重複與誠實的限制說明，但缺歸屬頁、四個標準頁仍是範本，最終產品從未製作。

strengths: Every performance claim paired with a same-batch control, with the team refusing to subtract across batches
Figures meeting a real bench standard: units, replicates, individual data points and gels with a marked ladder and named lanes
A genuine two-step build where an export bottleneck was identified and then addressed, with the result correctly read as redistribution rather than extra synthesis
Human Practices that changed both the biology and the claims, including ending absolute environmental language
weaknesses: No attributions page and no task-level account of who designed, cloned, fermented or ran the analysis
The named final product was never made: no loading, no membrane characterisation, no prototype data
No analytical evidence for the quantification method — no chromatogram, standard curve or recovery result
Thin statistics on the headline improvement, and four standard pages are unedited template text
red_flags: Attributions page returns 404, as do proof-of-concept, implementation, protocols and design
A gel band annotation migrates inconsistently with the labelled ladder, and no no-template control lane is shown
The Parts page assigns medal labels to the team's own parts, which is not how iGEM medals work
Internal inconsistency on the hydrolysate result between a figure caption and every other page
